docs.title: Home
docs.text:
LibreFolio Free to understand, free to act.

Bring all your investments together, in a secure dashboard. Your data comes to life through analytics tools designed for you. Everything clear, everything under control — because good decisions start with good information.

  • Private, by design
  • 100% Open, open source
  • Multi-broker, one portfolio
Ready to tryLibreFolio? Recommended Install with Docker

The standard path to run LibreFolio privately and reliably.

Read Docker guide → Run on Host?

Set up the Python + Pipenv environment to run LibreFolio directly on your host machine.

Host installation → Stay updated?

Follow our progress and get notified of new features:

  • Click Watch at the top of the GitHub repository.
  • Select Custom in the notifications dropdown.
  • Check Releases and click Apply.
Watch - Star - Dashboard

A unified view of your entire portfolio. Track your net worth, allocation, and daily changes in one secure place.

Explore dashboard → Brokers Integration

Import data directly from your broker's report files using dedicated plugins.

See all supported brokers → Transactions

Full transparency over every single movement. Filter, search, and edit transactions across all your portfolios effortlessly.

View transaction types → Deep Dive Insights

Uncover market trends with precision. Powerful technical analysis, trading signals, and historical performance metrics for every single asset in your portfolio.

Explore technical analysis → Asset & Forex

Track asset valuations and exchange rates automatically. Manage multi-currency portfolios with live data fetched straight from financial providers and central banks.

Asset types → Forex management → Tools

LibreFolio comes with a set of tools, one for each useful job! Each one starts from your real portfolio and shows you the numbers before you act. From now on, crunching numbers and making decisions is child's play!

Explore tools → A Modular Ecosystem

Free yourself from spreadsheets. LibreFolio is engineered to connect seamlessly with the financial tools you already use, extending its capabilities through a growing ecosystem of community-driven plugins.

Broker Imports

Upload and process your broker export files in seconds using smart community-driven parsers.

Asset Prices & Quotes

Automatically update the values of stocks, ETFs, and crypto by connecting to real-time data providers.

Exchange Rates & Forex

Sync exchange rates (FX) to precisely calculate and balance your multi-currency portfolios.

Technical Signal Plugins

Add new indicators as isolated Python plugins with schema-driven parameters, outputs, thresholds, and documentation.

Tools

Plan and calculate with tool plugins, one for each job, starting from your own portfolio.

Built for thoughtful investors

Track. Understand. Decide.

Better with dedicated products

Different needs deserve different tools.

LibreFolio fit Complete portfolio workspace

Bring brokers, assets, currencies, and portfolios into one structured view.

Portfolio complexity Specialized tools Minimal tracking without analysis

If you only need a simple list of holdings, a lightweight tracker may be enough.

LibreFolio fit Portfolio analytics

Analyze allocation, returns, risk, performance, and portfolio structure.

If you only need current values and totals, a simpler dashboard may be enough.

LibreFolio fit Code-guaranteed privacy

100% free and viewable code gives you absolute control over your financial data, with the certainty that no backdoors exist.

Privacy & ownership Specialized tools Privacy not a priority

If you prefer to rely on the security promises written in the Terms of Service of private companies without being able to verify them.

LibreFolio fit Long-term portfolio clarity

Focus on structure, performance, allocation, and informed decisions over time.

Trading style Specialized tools Automated intraday trading

If you need automated intraday execution, use tools built specifically for trading automation.

LibreFolio fit Open, expandable architecture

Add brokers, providers, currencies, and workflows as the project grows.

Extensibility model Specialized tools Fixed ready-made experience

If you want a closed product with no customization path, a simpler app may fit better.

docs.title: 🏠 Backups: Moving and Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page of the backup guide covers moving LibreFolio from one installation to another (from a hosting to a server of your own, or the other way round) and what to do when something goes wrong with a backup or a restore.

The rest of the guide starts on Backup, Restore and Moving Your Instance.

docs.title: 🏠 Bring Your LibreFolio Home
docs.text:
An archive moves your LibreFolio from one installation to another. Two ways:

Way When Where Restore The restore checks the archive on a copy before anything changes; with Docker it takes a secure backup (.lfbk) as it is, and it is the simplest way Settings › Administration › Backup, or backup restore (Restore on This Installation) By hand The data folder of the destination is empty, or does not exist yet: unzip the zip there before the first start Terminal of the destination server, below

In both cases the destination runs the same version of LibreFolio or a newer one (Never Backwards).

docs.title: ✋ By Hand: Unzip Before the First Start
docs.text:
Know this before you start:

  • 🔎 Nothing checks the archive first. A damaged archive, or one from a newer LibreFolio, shows when the start fails, and some damage only later, when a page reads the data it touches. A restore checks it on a copy before anything changes. To check an archive before you unzip it by hand, use an installation of LibreFolio that already runs: backup inspect <archive> compares each file with the manifest and, for a zip, writes nothing; backup restore <archive> --dry-run makes the whole check of a restore, on a copy («Check an Archive» and «Try a Restore on a Copy» in CLI Admin Tools). The dry run works in that installation's data folder: never point it at the empty folder you are about to fill.
  • 📖 The steps for any installation, the host one included: «Use an Archive on Another Installation» in CLI Admin Tools.

The steps, with Docker Compose:

  1. Source server — Settings › Administration › Backup, or terminal. Make a backup and bring it to the destination server (Make a Backup). If it is a clear backup, bring the secrets/ folder of its data folder too: the archive does not hold it.

    Result: the archive (.zip or .lfbk) is on the destination server.

  2. Destination server — terminal, folder of docker-compose.yml. The data folder LibreFolio-data must be empty, or not exist yet. If LibreFolio has already started on it, stop it (docker compose down) and move LibreFolio-data aside first.

    Result: no other data mixes with the archive's.

  3. Only for a secure backup (.lfbk) — terminal of an installation where LibreFolio's command line is available. An .lfbk is not a zip: turn it into its zip with backup decrypt.

    # Host installation
pipenv run ./dev.py backup decrypt librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.lfbk -o librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip

# Docker, in a running LibreFolio container: the paths inside it, and the zip where the container's user can write
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup decrypt /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.lfbk -o /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip

    Result: the zip to unzip at step 4. Know this:

    • 🔓 The password is asked at the terminal, or read with --password-file or --password-stdin.
    • 🚫 An -o that already exists is refused, and nothing is written: the command never replaces a file.
    • 🔒 Only the owner reads the zip (0600): the user who ran the command, or with Docker the container's user.
    • 🗑️ The zip holds every user's data in clear: delete it once unzipped.
    • 🔑 If the backup holds the instance key, the command adds 🔑 It also holds the instance key: with it, every saved provider key can be read.: whoever has that zip also reads the saved keys of the data providers.

  4. Destination server — terminal, folder of docker-compose.yml. Unzip the zip into the data folder.

    # In the folder of docker-compose.yml, before the first start
unzip librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip -d LibreFolio-data

    Result: LibreFolio-data/ holds the archive's data. The manifest.json left there is harmless: you can delete it.

  5. Destination server — folder LibreFolio-data/secrets/. Before the first start:

    • 🗝️ Clear backup: put the secrets/ of the source server back into LibreFolio-data/, and the saved secrets stay readable. Without it, LibreFolio creates a new instance key the first time it needs one.
    • 🔐 Secure backup that carries the key: the zip already holds secrets/instance.key, and the saved keys of the data providers stay readable. Make the folder and the file private, or the start log has a warning («Startup Checks» in Environment Variables):
    chmod 700 LibreFolio-data/secrets
chmod 600 LibreFolio-data/secrets/instance.key

    Result: the instance key is in place, and nothing in the start log is about it.

    ⛔ The key of a backup, only on an empty data folder

    Use the key of a backup only this way: on an empty data folder, on an installation that sets neither LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY nor LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY_FILE. A key set there wins over secrets/instance.key, and the saved keys of the data providers would stay unreadable. Never put it in place of a key already in use: what was saved with that key would become unreadable. To bring a secure backup to an installation that has its own key, restore it: the restore encrypts the saved keys again with that installation's key.

  6. Destination server — terminal, folder of docker-compose.yml. First start, with the same image as the source or a newer one.

    docker compose up -d

    Result: the start applies the pending migrations by itself.

docs.title: ⛔ Never Backwards
docs.text:
LibreFolio never takes a database back to an older version: use the version that made the archive, or a newer one. An older LibreFolio refuses an archive whose database holds a migration it does not know.

  • 🏷️ backup inspect shows which version made the archive (Made by LibreFolio <version>); Settings › About shows the version of an instance.
  • ❌ backup restore refuses such an archive with revision_unknown, before anything changes.
  • 🛑 By hand, an older LibreFolio does not start on such data: the log has Failed to apply database migrations, and Docker keeps restarting the container. Stop it with docker compose down.

Update the receiving LibreFolio first (Updating LibreFolio), then restore. With Docker, the latest image is the newest release.

docs.title: 🔐 Making a Secure Backup
docs.text: What you see Why What to do ❌ A password is needed: give it with --password-file or --password-stdin, or run the command at a terminal (password_required) backup create --encrypt without a terminal to ask on, such as in cron Give the password with --password-file or --password-stdin (From the Command Line) ❌ The password of a backup needs at least 12 characters, with an uppercase and a lowercase letter, a digit and a symbol (password_too_weak: …), or in Settings › Administration › Backup The password does not meet the rules of a backup's password. The rules are listed after password_too_weak:. In Settings, Create backup stays disabled until every rule is met; if the rules of a backup did not come from the server (GET /api/v1/backup/instance/options), the meter applies those of an account's password (8 characters), and the server still refuses fewer than 12 Choose a longer password that meets every rule. Nothing was written ❌ The two passwords differ (password_mismatch) The second password typed at the terminal is not the first Run the command again ❌ password file: <path> does not exist (password_unreadable), or cannot be read, is empty or blank, is not UTF-8 text --password-file cannot give the password Fix the file: the password alone, in UTF-8. With Docker, the path inside the container, such as /run/secrets/backup_password ⚠️ The instance key cannot be used: the secure backup was made without it, so saved provider keys must be entered again after a restore, or in Settings › Administration › Backup The instance key cannot be used: the backup was made without it, so the keys of the data providers must be entered again after a restore. secrets/instance.key is there, but damaged or out of reach, or longer than the 4096 bytes a restore can read back (the key LibreFolio generates has 43 characters). The backup is complete, without the key If the start log says what is wrong with the key, fix it («Startup Checks» in Environment Variables), then make a new secure backup. If it says nothing, the key is too long to travel: keep a copy of secrets/ with the backup, as for a clear backup

docs.title: 🧾 The Check Refuses the Archive
docs.text:
backup restore, with or without --dry-run, ends with a refusal and its code in parentheses, without changing anything. Settings › Administration › Backup refuses the same archives and says why on the card, without the code: The archive is damaged. for archive_damaged, for instance.

Code Why What to do revision_unknown The archive comes from a newer LibreFolio Update this installation (Never Backwards), then run the command again manifest_newer_format The archive format is newer than the one this LibreFolio reads Update LibreFolio first checksum_mismatch, archive_damaged, missing_entry The archive is damaged, cut short or changed backup inspect names the entries that differ. Copy the archive again from where you keep it, or use another one database_damaged The database fails SQLite's integrity check, SQLite cannot read its schema, or it holds text that is not UTF-8. Settings › Administration › Backup: The backup's database is damaged: it cannot be restored. Copy the archive again from where you keep it, or use another one. Text that is not UTF-8 means another program wrote to the database (LibreFolio never writes it), or the archive was changed database_foreign_objects The database holds a trigger, a view or a virtual table, which LibreFolio never creates. Settings › Administration › Backup: The backup's database holds triggers, views or other objects LibreFolio never creates: it was not made by LibreFolio, or it was changed, and it cannot be restored. The archive was not made by LibreFolio, or was changed after: use another backup not_a_backup Not an archive LibreFolio wrote, such as a data folder zipped by hand Put such a copy back by hand, into an empty data folder sealed_backup_needs_key A sealed nightly backup (.tar): its password is inside, encrypted for a key the check does not have. Settings › Administration › Backup: This is a sealed backup of a hosting panel: its password is encrypted for the provider's key. Extract backup.lfbk, open password.age with age, then restore backup.lfbk with that password. Restore it where its private key is: backup restore <archive>.tar --identity-file <key file> (Sealed Backups) sealed_no_identity, sealed_identity_invalid, sealed_tar_invalid, sealed_manifest_invalid, sealed_password_invalid A sealed backup given with --identity-file that does not open See Making or Opening a Sealed Backup no_space The copy needs more free space than the disk of the data folder has Free some space: the archive unpacked, plus twice its database, plus 64 MB, and for a secure backup the size of its .lfbk too archive_unreadable The archive cannot be opened, most often because the server's user cannot read it With Docker and the official image, sudo chown 1000:1000 <archive> on the host gives it to that user restore_already_pending Another restore waits for the next start Restart LibreFolio to apply it, or cancel it with backup pending --cancel or Cancel the restore in Settings › Administration › Backup wrong_password The password does not open the secure backup: not the one it was made with, or the start of the file was changed. Settings › Administration › Backup asks for it again: Wrong password, or the file was changed: type the password again. Type it again as it was chosen, upper and lower case included. If it is right, copy the file again from where you keep it password_required A secure backup, and no password: the command had no terminal to ask on, and neither --password-file nor --password-stdin Run the command at a terminal, or give the password with one of the two options envelope_damaged The secure backup is damaged, cut short, or changed after it was made Copy it again from where you keep it, or use another one: LibreFolio reads no part of a damaged .lfbk envelope_unsupported The secure backup comes from a newer LibreFolio, or asks for settings this one does not accept Update this installation first (Never Backwards), then run the command again

Two more messages:

  • ❌ No file at <path>: with Docker, give the path inside the container, /app/backend/data/prod-docker/….
  • ❌ The backup has no active administrator: after a restore nobody could manage the instance, or the same in the report of Settings › Administration › Backup, whose confirmation stays disabled: on the installation the backup comes from, make an active account administrator, then make a new backup.

Every code: «Refusals — what the codes mean» in CLI Admin Tools.

Two notices let the restore go on, but read them before you confirm:

  • 🔑 Your account is not among the administrators of this backup: after the restart you cannot sign in with it. Only in the report of Settings › Administration › Backup, in red. After the restore you sign in with an account of the backup, with the password it had then: the account you use now is not in it. Before you confirm, make sure you know the password of one of the administrators the report names; if you do not know it, use another backup.
  • ⚠️ Ledger totals differ from the backup's (<n> lines):, or Ledger totals differ from the backup's on 2 lines: in the report of Settings › Administration › Backup: the cash of a broker or the quantity of a position in the copy, once up to date, is not the one the backup recorded, because transactions were lost, added or changed between the two (by a migration that corrects data, for instance). Each line that follows gives a broker's number, then a currency or an asset's number, with the backup's amount before the arrow and the copy's after it: the numbers are those of the addresses /brokers/<id> and /assets/<id> in the app. Compare these lines with the instance the backup comes from. The notice never blocks the restore: whether you confirm is up to you.

docs.title: 🔏 Making or Opening a Sealed Backup
docs.text:
To make one, with backup create --sealed or --recipient: nothing is written, and the command exits with 1.

What you see Why What to do ❌ LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS is not set: give the recipients there, or with --recipient age1… --sealed did not find the variable: not in .env, or the container was not recreated after it was added Set it (Seal Every Backup), then docker compose up -d, or run the command from the project folder with pipenv run, which reads .env ❌ LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS: item 2 is not an age recipient: expected age1… as age-keygen prints it (BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_INVALID), or expected at most 2 recipients, comma-separated (BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_TOO_MANY), or item 2 repeats an earlier recipient (BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_DUPLICATE) The variable holds something other than one or two distinct age1… keys: a private key, an SSH key, a comma too many Write the public keys only, as keygen or age-keygen -y prints them. The Security tab says the same (backup.recipients) ❌ A --recipient is not an age recipient: expected age1…, as keygen or age-keygen prints it, ❌ The same recipient is given twice, ❌ At most 2 recipients: --recipient twice, while a key is being changed The same rules, for --recipient Give one or two different public keys ❌ A sealed backup draws a password of its own: --sealed and --recipient go without --encrypt, --password-file or --password-stdin A sealed backup has no password to give Drop the password options ❌ --sealed reads the recipients from LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS: give them there or with --recipient, not both --sealed and --recipient together Keep one of the two ❌ <path> already exists: a key file is never written over backup keygen never replaces a key: the old one may still open backups Choose another file name, or move the old file away first if you are sure no backup needs it

To open one, with --identity-file: the command changes nothing and exits with 1. It reads the key file first, then the .tar.

What you see Why What to do (sealed_backup_needs_key) A .tar given without --identity-file, on the command line or in Settings › Administration › Backup Give the key file, or open it by hand and restore backup.lfbk with its password ❌ --identity-file opens a sealed backup (.tar) only: <path> is not one A .zip or an .lfbk given with --identity-file Drop --identity-file: those archives open as usual ❌ The key file cannot be read (sealed_identity_invalid), Line 3 of the key file is not an age key, The key file holds no age key The file is not a private key: the public key alone, a key copied with a missing character, or a file the command cannot read Give the file written by keygen or age-keygen, with its AGE-SECRET-KEY-1… line. Comments (#) and blank lines may stay ❌ None of the keys given opens the password of this backup (sealed_no_identity) The backup was sealed for another key: an older one, before a change of key Compare its recipients (tar xOf <archive>.tar manifest.json) with the # public key: line of your key files, and give the matching one (sealed_tar_invalid), such as The archive is cut short or The archive does not hold manifest.json, password.age and backup.lfbk, in this order Not the .tar LibreFolio wrote: cut short by a copy, rebuilt by hand with tar cf, or not a sealed backup Copy the original again from where you keep it, or use another night's backup (sealed_manifest_invalid), such as The manifest does not describe backup.lfbk: its size or SHA-256 differs manifest.json or backup.lfbk was changed The copy is damaged: use another one (sealed_password_invalid) The key opened password.age, but what it holds is not a password LibreFolio wrote Not a LibreFolio backup, or changed: use another copy ❌ The password does not open this backup (wrong_password) The key opened the password, but that password does not open backup.lfbk: the two files come from different backups, or one was changed Use another copy, kept whole as LibreFolio wrote it (envelope_damaged), during the check or the restore A byte of backup.lfbk was changed after the backup was made: the password was right Use another copy: LibreFolio reads no part of a damaged .lfbk

docs.title: 🔁 The Restore Does Not Go Through
docs.text: What you see Why What to do backup pending says The state of the restore cannot be read, (restore_state_unreadable: <reason>) .restore/restore.json cannot be used: permissions (io), a link or a folder in its place (not_a_file), or content LibreFolio did not write (invalid). A restore may have stopped half way. Meanwhile no checked copy is removed For io, give .restore/ back to the user that runs LibreFolio and check again. Otherwise stop LibreFolio and run backup pending --recover previous: the data of before comes back from .restore/previous/. Then start it, or restore a backup again («An Unreadable Restore State» in CLI Admin Tools) backup pending ends with (server_running) At the last start, another server process served the data folder: a worker restarted on its own, or a second server Restart the whole server, never one worker, and run one server per data folder backup pending ends with (other_data_directory) The server found its data folder under a path other than the one the restore was confirmed for, such as a copy of the data folder backup pending --cancel, or Cancel the restore in Settings › Administration › Backup, then restore the archive again: with backup restore, where the server runs backup pending ends with (backup_running) A backup was running at the last start Nothing: the next start applies the restore backup pending says the restore was rolled back, (first_start_failed) The first start on the restored data did not complete The data is as it was. The log of that start has the cause: fix it, then restore the archive again … rolled back, (swap_interrupted) The start that applied the restore was interrupted, and the next one undid it Restore the archive again … rolled back, (swap_failed) The folders could not be moved into place Make sqlite/, custom-uploads/, broker_reports/ and scenario_catalog/ real folders of the data folder, neither links nor separate mounts, then restore the archive again … rolled back, (stage_missing) The checked copy was gone or changed Restore the archive again A start stops, and its log says another server applied the restore or serves the data folder Two LibreFolio servers use the same data folder Stop the other one, then start LibreFolio again: backup pending will tell whether the restore was kept LibreFolio does not start, and its log has The data directory is half restored Putting the former data back failed too, on a disk or permission error for instance Fix the cause the log gives: every start tries again Failed to apply database migrations after an unzip by hand An archive from a newer LibreFolio, or a migration that fails: the log has the error For a newer archive, docker compose down, then use the version that made it or a newer one (Never Backwards)

docs.title: 🖱️ What Settings › Administration › Backup Says
docs.text:
The restart window gives in words the reason that backup pending gives as a code: the table says which one, and the row of that code in The Restore Does Not Go Through says what to do. On the card, Try again reads the state of the restore again; to send an archive again, choose it again.

What you see Why What to do After Restore and restart, the sign-in page, with no message The restore worked and ended every session. Only in the case of the next row does the sign-in page come although the restore did not go through Sign in with an administrator of the backup, with the password the account had when the backup was made. If nobody remembers it: After a Restore The sign-in page appeared, but once signed in the data is as before The page did not read the outcome with its ticket (a reload of the page, more than an hour of waiting, or LibreFolio restarted from the command line rather than from the page), and LibreFolio runs without JWT_SECRET (Keep Users Signed In After a Restart): every start signs everyone out, even if the restore did not go through. The accounts and passwords of before still sign in Open Settings › Administration › Backup: the card says The last restore was rolled back on …, or shows the restore waiting, with the reason; then see the row of that reason below LibreFolio has not come back yet. If nothing starts it again by itself, start it yourself: the restore is applied at that start. LibreFolio has not answered for a minute: nothing restarted it (no supervisor, or one that starts it only after a failure, Who Starts LibreFolio Again), or its start is slow If it is stopped, start it: docker compose up -d with Docker, or start the server on a host installation. The page goes on by itself once LibreFolio answers LibreFolio has not stopped. If it does not restart by itself, restart it yourself: the restore is applied at that start., a minute after Restore and restart, with Back to Backup The request did not stop the server: the restore still waits for the next start, and backup pending shows it waiting Restart LibreFolio yourself: docker compose restart librefolio with Docker, or stop the whole server and start it again. Its start applies the restore, and the page goes on by itself. Or Back to Backup: the card shows the restore waiting, to restart (Restart now and restore) or cancel (Cancel the restore) The restore did not go through, with The data is as it was before: … The restore was rolled back: the first start after it did not complete (first_start_failed), the start that applied it was interrupted (swap_interrupted), its folders could not be moved into place (swap_failed) or its checked copy was gone (stage_missing) What the row of that code says. Back to Backup returns to the card, which says when the last restore was rolled back and why The restore did not go through, with LibreFolio restarted, but the restore was not applied. and the reason A start left the restore waiting: At the last start a backup was running… (backup_running), It was confirmed for another data directory… (other_data_directory) or At the last start another LibreFolio process was serving the data… (server_running) What the row of that code says. Back to Backup shows the restore waiting, with Restart now and restore and Cancel the restore The archive is larger than this LibreFolio accepts (500 MB). The installation limits the archives uploaded for a restore with LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (backup_too_large) There is no limit unless someone set one: raise it, or set it to 0, then restart (The Upload Limit of a Restore). Or restore from the command line, which has no upload limit Unpacked, the archive is larger than this LibreFolio accepts for a restore. The sizes the manifest declares, added up, exceed LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB (unpacked_too_large). The check refused the archive before unpacking anything There is no limit unless someone set one: raise it, set it to 0 or remove it, then restart (The Upload Limit of a Restore). Or restore from the command line with LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB=0 in front of backup restore LibreFolio cannot read its restore limit right now: try again later. LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB is not a whole number of megabytes (backup_restore_unavailable): no check starts, and the archive stays on the server. The log has an error, from the start already Write a whole number of megabytes, 0 for no limit, or remove the variable, then restart; the Security tab of Settings › Administration names it (backup.restore_limit). Then choose the archive again Sending stops with A proxy in front of LibreFolio refused an archive this large: ask whoever runs it to accept larger uploads, or restore from the command line., or with The server does not answer: check the connection and try again. or The server answered with an error: the server's log has the cause., and the log of LibreFolio has nothing about it A proxy in front of LibreFolio refused the archive: Nginx takes only 1 MB by default. The first message: the proxy answers too large (HTTP 413); the others: it drops the connection or answers otherwise Let the proxy take archives as large as yours, with client_max_body_size in Nginx (The Upload Limit of a Restore), or restore from the command line Not enough free space on the server for this archive. The disk of the data folder, or a quota, is full (backup_no_space): while sending, and then nothing of the archive is kept (a network file system or a quota may report it only at the end of the file), or at the confirmation with Restore and restart, and then nothing is confirmed and the checked copy stays; the log has A restore could not be confirmed: not enough free space Free some space on the disk of the data folder, then choose the archive again. After a confirmation, Try again: the report comes back, and Restore and restart confirms again Not enough free space on the server to check the archive. docs.title: 🔑 After a Restore
docs.text: What happens What to do Nobody remembers the password an administrator had in the backup Whoever runs the server sets a new one with user reset, or creates a reset link with user reset-link (Reset a Password or Lock an Account) The sign-in page answers that an account is disabled: it was waiting for its email verification An administrator clicks Reactivate on its row (What Each Action Does), or deletes it so that its owner signs up again (Delete an Account) A link sent before the restore no longer works Send a new invitation or a new password-reset link (Users & Invitations) A secret plugin setting is reported as set but unreadable, as the report of the check announced (… cannot be read with this instance's key: enter them again after the restore.) The backup had no key able to read it: a clear backup, or a secure one whose instance had a key set in its environment, or could not use its own. If you still have the old key, put it back in place before anyone enters a secret again; only otherwise enter the setting again in Settings › Plugins, where each user enters their own (What Follows). If the start log says that the key of this installation cannot be used, fix that first («Startup Checks» in Environment Variables) After a move, no email is sent Set the email variables on this installation, then restart (Email)

docs.title: 💾 Backup, Restore and Moving Your Instance
docs.text:
A backup is one archive with your whole LibreFolio in it: the database and the files of every user. It is a plain zip or, for a secure backup, an .lfbk encrypted with a password you choose.

Here you find:

  • what the archive holds and what follows;
  • how to make one, from the app or from the command line, and how to keep copies off the server;
  • how to check it and how to restore it, from the app or from the command line.

Every option and message of the commands: «Back Up the Instance», in CLI Admin Tools.

🗓️ Make one before every update

LibreFolio never takes a database back to an older version. A backup made before an update is your way back to the version you had: see Updating LibreFolio.

📚 This guide is in several pages

Besides this page: Backups: Sealed Backups, Backups: Moving and Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 📦 What a Backup Holds
docs.text:
The archive is a zip with the layout of the data directory: unpacked into an empty data directory, it is your instance again. A secure backup is the same zip, encrypted with a password, in an .lfbk file. A sealed backup is a secure backup whose password opens only with a private key of yours, in a .tar.

In the archive What it is sqlite/app.db The database: users, brokers, transactions, assets, prices, exchange rates and settings. A consistent copy, taken while LibreFolio keeps running custom-uploads/ The files uploaded in the app broker_reports/ The broker reports scenario_catalog/ Your stress scenarios, if you added any secrets/instance.key Only in a secure backup, and only if LibreFolio generated the instance key: the key that encrypts the saved keys of the data providers. A restore only reads it: the installation that receives the backup keeps its own manifest.json The description of the archive: LibreFolio version and creation date, migration revision of the database, rows per table, control totals of the ledger (the cash of every broker per currency and the quantity of every position), size and SHA-256 checksum of every file, and whether the archive carries the instance key

Never in the archive:

  • 🔑 secrets/: a secure backup carries only the key LibreFolio generated, secrets/instance.key, never a key you set yourself with LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY or LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY_FILE («The Instance Key» in Environment Variables);
  • 📝 logs/ and scheduler_state.json (the last run of the scheduled syncs);
  • 💾 backups/, where LibreFolio keeps the backups it makes, and .restore/, the work folder of a restore;
  • ⚙️ the configuration: .env and the environment variables, the email settings included, which live only in the environment.

docs.title: 🧭 What Follows
docs.text:
• 🔒 Keep it private. A clear archive holds every user's data, not encrypted: keep it, with every copy, as private as the server. A secure one opens only with its password: keep the password apart from the archive.
  • ⚙️ Bring your configuration with you. Keep a copy of your .env with the archives: on another installation, set again the options you need, the email ones included (Where the Configuration Lives).
  • 🏠 Any installation can take it, from Settings or from the command line, if it runs the same version of LibreFolio or a newer one, whoever made the archive.
  • 🗝️ Saved secrets and the instance key. What LibreFolio encrypted with the instance key, such as the API key of a data source saved in the app, can be read only with that key:
Backup The instance key Restored on an installation with another key Secure, key generated by LibreFolio Travels with the data The secrets are re-encrypted with the key of the installation that receives it: nothing to do Clear; sealed; secure with a key from the environment (LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY, LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY_FILE) or not usable Stays out The secrets stay saved but unreadable; LibreFolio never uses a wrong value. Settings › Plugins says under each one Saved, but this instance's key cannot read it: enter it again.

If you still have the old key, put it back before anyone enters a secret again: a secret entered under the new key would become unreadable once the old one is back. Enter the secrets again only if the old key is lost.

  1. Stop LibreFolio.
  2. On the server, in secrets/ of the data directory: put your copy of secrets/instance.key in place of the generated one. Or, in .env, set the old value of the variable again («The Instance Key» in Environment Variables).
  3. Start LibreFolio again.

If the installation keeps its own key, or its secrets are already encrypted with its key, it takes the old key at the restore: from the command line, restore with --instance-key-file and your copy of the old key; the check re-encrypts those secrets with this installation's key («The Instance Key of Another Installation» in CLI Admin Tools).

For the settings of the whole instance, every start logs the error Stored plugin secrets that the instance key cannot read: …, with their count, until they are entered again or the old key is back. No plugin shipped with LibreFolio keeps one today.

docs.title: ⬇️ Make a Backup
docs.text:
Two ways give the same archive:

Where What you get Settings › Administration › Backup, in the app (administrators) The archive downloaded to your computer, and a copy kept on the server Terminal on the server: backup create The archive on the server, or where you say with --output

From both, the backup can be secure: the same zip, encrypted with a password you choose. Only from the command line can it be sealed: encrypted with a random password that only a private key of yours opens, for backups made without anyone at the keyboard.

LibreFolio keeps working during the backup. One backup runs at a time, whoever started it.

docs.title: 🖱️ From Settings › Administration › Backup
docs.text:
1. Open Settings › Administration › Backup (only administrators have the tab), section Back up the instance.
  2. Choose the kind:
    • Clear (default): A plain .zip: whoever has the file sees all the data, and on another instance the keys of the data providers must be entered again.
    • Secure: An .lfbk encrypted with a password you choose: only that password opens it, and a lost password cannot be recovered. It also carries the keys of the data providers. See Secure Backups.
  3. For a secure backup, type the password in Password of the backup and again in The same password again. The rules of an account password apply, given by the server: the meter under the first field lists them as you type (At least 12 characters, One uppercase letter, One lowercase letter, One number, One special character) and shows how strong it is. While the two fields differ, The two passwords differ. shows and Create backup stays disabled.
  4. Click Create backup. The password fields empty at once; the card follows the backup phase by phase (a secure backup ends with Encrypting with your password).
  5. At Backup ready, click Download. The browser saves librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip (date and time of start, in UTC), or .lfbk for a secure backup, which the card marks Encrypted with your password: keep it safe, LibreFolio cannot recover it.

Good to know:

  • 🔑 Keep the password of a secure backup in a password manager, apart from the archive: LibreFolio keeps no copy of it, and without it nobody opens the archive, you included.
  • 💾 A copy stays on the server, in the list of Backups Kept on the Server, until you delete it or the automatic clean-up removes it: download it from there later, too. A copy on the same disk as the data is not a real backup: keep it elsewhere (Keep Copies Off the Server). Delete from the server removes it at once; Create a new backup starts another one.
  • ⚠️ The backup is complete, with warnings: the database failed its integrity check or has broken references and was archived as it is; or some files were left out; or, for a secure backup, the instance key could not be used and was left out (Making a Secure Backup). The archive is written all the same: read the warnings before you rely on it.
  • 🚦 Another backup is running (from the app or the command line): the card says so, try again when it ends.

What the card does with a backup already in progress:

Backup in progress The card Clear, started from this or another tab of the app, whose answer never arrived (connection dropped at the start) Not lost: the next Create backup finds it, follows it and offers its download Secure, not started from this tab Never followed: only its password opens the archive. The card says that another backup is running Any, while the card already offers an archive It keeps offering its own and only says that another backup is running Started from the command line Not followed: its archive goes elsewhere

The card never says which backup is running: the browser's console does (id and origin).

docs.title: ⌨️ From the Command Line
docs.text:
In the server's terminal, from the folder with docker-compose.yml (Docker) or from the LibreFolio folder (host installation):

# Docker: the archive appears in its own folder of ./LibreFolio-data/backups/ on the host
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup create

# Host installation: the archive goes into its own folder of backups/ in the data directory
pipenv run ./dev.py backup create

# A secure backup (.lfbk): the password is asked twice
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup create --encrypt

The command prints the path of the archive and its SHA-256:.

  • 🗃️ Without --output, the archive stays on the server, in a folder of its own inside backups/ (Backups Kept on the Server).
  • 📁 --output (-o) copies the archive into another folder that already exists, or under a name of your own; nothing stays in backups/. With Docker the path is inside the container: use a folder mounted from the host.
  • 🔒 Only the owner of the archive can read it (0600): with Docker, the container's user.
  • 🔐 --encrypt makes a secure backup, librefolio-backup-<date>-<time>.lfbk, and asks the password twice at the terminal. Instead: --password-file FILE, a file with the password alone (the line breaks at its end do not count), such as a Docker secret; or --password-stdin, one line of the standard input from a pipe (at a terminal, the command asks it without showing it). Either one makes the backup secure by itself, with or without --encrypt; they are not used together.
  • 🙈 There is no --password: every user of the server reads the commands that run (ps), and the shell keeps them in its history.
  • 📏 Password rules, as in Settings › Administration › Backup: at least 12 characters, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a symbol. Otherwise the command stops before writing anything: ❌ The password of a backup needs at least 12 characters, with an uppercase and a lowercase letter, a digit and a symbol (password_too_weak: min_length, digit).
  • 🤖 Without a terminal (cron, script), --encrypt alone stops: ❌ A password is needed: give it with --password-file or --password-stdin, or run the command at a terminal (password_required).
  • 📖 Every option, warning and error: «Back Up the Instance» and «Back Up with Docker» in CLI Admin Tools.
🐳 The password of the backups as a Docker secret
  1. Next to docker-compose.yml, write the password alone in a file, such as backup_password.txt, never in LibreFolio-data/ (whoever had the data would have the password too). Then chmod 600 backup_password.txt, and keep a copy of the password elsewhere: lost, it cannot be recovered.

  2. In docker-compose.yml, add the marked lines and leave the rest of the service as it is. If the file already has secrets: lists, such as for JWT_SECRET_FILE («Secrets in Files» in Environment Variables), add the lines to them.

    services:
  librefolio:
    secrets:                              # added
      - backup_password                   # added
secrets:                                  # added
  backup_password:                        # added
    file: ./backup_password.txt           # added

    Run docker compose up -d: the container is recreated with the secret.

  3. In the server's terminal, make the backup with the path of the secret in the container:

    docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup create --password-file /run/secrets/backup_password

docs.title: 🗃️ Backups Kept on the Server
docs.text:
A backup made from the app or the command line is no longer deleted after an hour: it stays on the server until you delete it, or until the automatic clean-up removes it. Each one has a folder of its own in backups/ of the data directory: moment of creation (UTC), origin (ui app, cli command line) and a short code that tells two backups of the same second apart. The archive inside keeps its usual name, .zip, .lfbk or .tar:

backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500-ui-1a2b3c4d/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip

backups/.jobs/ holds only a backup in progress or one that failed, removed after an hour.

Where you see them: Settings › Administration › Backup, under Backups on this server, or Files › Backups, the same list; administrators only. Refresh, at the top of the list, reads it again: a backup made from the command line appears only then. For each backup:

  • 📅 date and time of creation, and origin: app or command line;
  • 🔐 type: plain, with password (secure) or sealed;
  • 📏 size and SHA-256: click to copy the whole checksum and compare it with the one of the downloaded file;
  • 📦 Once restored: the space its contents take once restored, not compressed, that is what a restore will take; point at it for its parts: the database, the uploaded files, the broker reports and the other files. A backup made before LibreFolio recorded it shows «—»;
  • ⬇️ Download and 🗑️ Delete, which removes the backup from the server at once.

💽 Download it and keep it elsewhere

A backup that stays on the same disk as your data is not a real backup: when the disk is lost, the data and its backups go together. Download the archive and keep it on another disk, a NAS or off-site (Keep Copies Off the Server).

The list shows only the backups made by this version of LibreFolio. The loose librefolio-backup-*.zip files of earlier versions in backups/ are not listed and LibreFolio never removes them: delete them yourself when you no longer need them.

docs.title: 🧹 Automatic Clean-up
docs.text:
In the closed Automatic clean-up panel, in the Backups on this server section of Settings › Administration › Backup or of Files › Backups, you set two limits, both optional:

Limit What it does Off Total size, in MB When the kept backups weigh more, the oldest are deleted until the rest fits 0 Maximum age, in days An older backup is deleted 0
  • 🛡️ The latest backup is always kept, whatever the limits say.
  • ⏰ The clean-up runs after each backup and when LibreFolio starts, at most once an hour: a saved change applies within an hour.
  • 🏠 Self-hosted: both limits are off until you set them.
  • 🔍 Only the backups of the list are cleaned: never the older loose archives in backups/, a backup in progress or a failed one.
  • ⌨️ The backups of the command line stay in the same place and follow the same limits: Where the Backups Stay.

docs.title: 📊 The Space Bar
docs.text:
In Files, above the tabs, administrators see the Space used bar: how much room your instance takes. It updates with Refresh and whenever the list of kept backups changes. The legend gives the size of each part:

Part What it counts Database The database and the files it keeps beside it Uploaded files The files uploaded in the app, such as those of the Files page Broker reports The statements uploaded to import transactions Backups Everything in backups/: the backups kept on the server, a backup in progress and a failed one Pending restore A restore not finished or dropped yet: the uploaded archive and its unpacked version Other LibreFolio files The rest of the data directory: logs, state and the like

Three looks of the bar:

Situation The bar The line under it 💽 No limit (self-hosted default) The whole disk of the data: LibreFolio's parts coloured, Other on the disk grey, Free empty How much LibreFolio uses of the disk 📏 With a limit The limit, filled as far as the data goes used of limit 📁 No limit and the disk unknown (LibreFolio cannot ask it) LibreFolio's folder alone, split into its parts, with no free space —

Set the limit in Files › Advanced (closed panel under the bar), field LibreFolio total space (MB): a whole number of megabytes, 0 for no limit, then Save; a green notice confirms. It is the most space LibreFolio may take in all. The same field is in Settings › Administration › Global Settings, category Memory: either place changes it.

  • 🚧 Past the limit, LibreFolio refuses what would add data: an uploaded file, a broker report, a backup started by hand (after trying the automatic clean-up) and a restore whose result would pass it. The message says what to raise the total space to and, if the disk lacks room, how much more it needs free. Never stopped: transactions, prices and database, the backups of a hosting panel and of the command line (the clean-up follows them) and a restore already confirmed. The limit deletes nothing by itself.
  • ⚠️ The bar warns that the limit is exceeded and suggests deleting backups or files, or raising the limit. It then becomes your data, so that no part is left out: a Limit 20 MB tick shows where the limit falls, the red lines after it by how much you pass it.
  • 💬 A refusal is told where you are: in the upload or import window, or on the backup card. An administrator finds Open the settings, which opens Settings › Administration › Global Settings with the LibreFolio total space (MB) row in view and highlighted: unlock the tab to change it; a user reads how much space to free, or to ask an administrator. With a limit set by whoever hosts the instance, the message says to ask them.
  • 🔒 Set in the server's configuration: with LIBREFOLIO_STORAGE_LIMIT_MB in the environment, its value is the limit, the field is read-only, here and in Global Settings, and a note says it is set by whoever hosts the instance (Environment Variables). A value that is not a whole number is ignored and the field works as above.
  • 🧹 Clean-up and bar work together. Usually the backups grow: the automatic clean-up keeps them in check, and every backup deleted in Settings › Administration › Backup or in Files › Backups shortens Backups in the bar. Near the limit, start there.

docs.title: 🗄️ Keep Copies Off the Server
docs.text:
backups/ is in the data directory, on the same disk: a backup there does not survive the loss of the disk. An archive downloaded from Settings is already off the server. From the command line, write the archives to another disk, a NAS or off-site with --output, on a schedule.

In the crontab of the user that runs LibreFolio (crontab -e), host installation, every night at 03:30:

30 3 * * * cd /path/to/LibreFolio && pipenv run ./dev.py backup create --output /mnt/nas/librefolio/

With Docker, add -T (cron gives the command no terminal). The archive lands in a folder of its own in LibreFolio-data/backups/, where the automatic clean-up, once set, keeps the disk from filling up: copy it elsewhere with your usual tool.

30 3 * * * cd /path/to/librefolio && docker compose exec -T librefolio python dev.py backup create

Secure archives: add --password-file with a file that holds the password (cron has no terminal to ask on). With Docker, the secret of the example above:

30 3 * * * cd /path/to/librefolio && docker compose exec -T librefolio python dev.py backup create --password-file /run/secrets/backup_password
  • 📁 The folder of --output must exist when the command runs: mount the NAS first. A path that is not an existing folder becomes the name of the archive.
  • 🔢 The command prints what it did and exits with 1 when the archive is not where you asked: keep the output, or have cron mail it to you.
  • 🧭 cron has a short PATH: if it does not find pipenv or docker, write the full path (command -v pipenv prints it).
  • 🗑️ LibreFolio deletes none of these archives: remove the old ones yourself. Keep several, and the last one made before each update.
  • 🔑 Keep a copy of .env too, as private as the archives: no archive holds it. And a copy of secrets/, unless your archives are secure: a clear or sealed one leaves the instance key out (What Follows).
  • 🔏 Nightly archives that the server itself cannot open, without a password file on its disk: Every Night with cron, in Sealed Backups.

docs.title: 🧰 Backups with restic or Backrest
docs.text:
LibreFolio writes the archive; a backup tool takes it off-site and keeps a history of it. restic copies a folder, encrypted, to S3, Backblaze B2, SFTP and more, and forgets the old copies by a rule of yours. Backrest is a web interface for restic, with its own scheduler. LibreFolio needs neither: they only read the folder of its archives.

Nightly recipe, host installation. In a private file (chmod 600), restic's variables:

# /etc/librefolio-restic.env: where the copies go, and the file with restic's password
RESTIC_REPOSITORY=sftp:backup@nas.example:/srv/restic/librefolio
RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE=/root/.restic-librefolio-password

In the crontab:

30 3 * * * cd /path/to/LibreFolio && pipenv run ./dev.py backup create --output /var/backups/librefolio/ && . /etc/librefolio-restic.env && restic backup /var/backups/librefolio/ && restic forget --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4 --prune && find /var/backups/librefolio/ -name 'librefolio-backup-*' -mtime +2 -delete

The line makes the archive, sends the folder, keeps seven daily and four weekly copies in the repository and removes the local archives older than two days. With Docker, make the archive with the command of Keep Copies Off the Server and give restic the host folder LibreFolio-data/backups/. With Backrest, add a plan on that folder, with its schedule and retention, and leave backup create in cron.

  • 🔐 restic's password is a key to all your data: whoever holds it reads every copy. As private as the password of a secure backup, with a copy elsewhere: lost, the repository cannot be read any more.
  • 🔑 No public key. restic uses its password to write as well as to read: the server that sends the copies can also read them. If that is a problem, send sealed backups (--sealed): only your private key opens them, neither the server nor restic's password. Secure backups (--password-file) work too, but their password sits in a file on the same server.
  • 📦 Little to deduplicate. Every archive is compressed, a secure one is encrypted: restic stores each archive almost whole. Plan the repository's space for the copies you keep.
  • 🧪 Try a restore before you need one. restic restore latest --target /tmp/librefolio-check, then check the archive with backup restore --dry-run.

docs.title: 🔐 Secure Backups
docs.text:
A secure backup is the archive of a clear backup, encrypted with a password you choose, in a file of LibreFolio's own: .lfbk. You make it from Settings › Administration › Backup or with backup create --encrypt on the command line; every check and restore of this page takes it, given its password.

  • 🛡️ It protects the file at rest. Lost disk, stolen laptop, copy on a cloud or a NAS: without the password nothing can be read, neither the data nor the names of the files. A changed or truncated file is detected when opened and refused.
  • 👁️ It does not protect from whoever knows the password: they read everything, the data of every user and the keys of the data providers. Give it only to whoever may restore the backup, never together with the file.
  • 🗝️ It carries the instance key, if LibreFolio generated it (secrets/instance.key): the saved keys of the data providers travel with the backup, and the restore re-encrypts them with the key of the installation that receives it, which keeps its own. A key you set yourself (LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY, LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY_FILE) never leaves.
  • 🆘 A lost password cannot be recovered. LibreFolio keeps no copy of it, and nothing else opens the file.
  • ⏳ Slow to guess. The key of the file comes from the password through scrypt: 32 MiB of memory and about a tenth of a second per try, nothing for one backup, slow for whoever tries passwords one after another. Hence the rules: at least 12 characters, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a symbol.
  • 💽 On the server, while it is made, the clear archive is written first, in the work folder of the backup inside backups/, which only the server's user can open; it is removed as soon as the .lfbk is written, and when the backup fails. After an abrupt interruption (power cut, kill -9), the next start of LibreFolio removes what was left in clear, and the backup must be made again. A check decrypts the backup the same way: Check a Backup.

The design, for developers: Secure Backups (.lfbk).

docs.title: 🔎 Check a Backup
docs.text:
Two commands check an archive without changing anything. In the server's terminal, inside the container with Docker: an archive in LibreFolio-data/backups/ is there in /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/, and a kept backup is in its own folder, such as /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500-cli-1a2b3c4d/.

# Is the archive whole, and what does it hold?
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup inspect /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500-cli-1a2b3c4d/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip

# Can this installation restore it? A restore tried on a copy
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup restore /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500-cli-1a2b3c4d/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip --dry-run

# A secure backup: the same commands ask its password first
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup inspect /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500-cli-1a2b3c4d/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.lfbk

Host installation: pipenv run ./dev.py backup … with the path of the archive on the host.

backup inspect backup restore --dry-run It answers Whether the archive is whole: size and SHA-256 of every entry, compared with the manifest Whether this installation can restore it: archive unpacked into a copy, brought up to date and checked It shows Who made the archive and when, revision of the database, rows and tables, files, whether the instance key is included The same, plus: the migrations a restore would apply, the ledger totals of the copy compared with those of the archive, the provider keys re-encrypted with this installation's key or to enter again, the administrators you would sign in with It needs Any LibreFolio, server running or stopped; no data directory, except for a secure backup, which it decrypts there The installation that would receive the archive (the server may keep running) and free space in its data directory: archive unpacked + twice its database + 64 MB It ends with ✅ Every entry matches the manifest ✅ The archive can be restored. Dry run: the instance was left as it is, and the copy removed.
  • 🔐 Secure backup (.lfbk): both ask the password first, at the terminal or with --password-file FILE / --password-stdin, as backup create. They decrypt it into a private folder of the data directory, which only the server's user can open, and remove the decrypted archive at the end: room is needed for that too, about the size of the .lfbk. After an abrupt interruption (power cut, kill -9), the next start of LibreFolio removes what was left in clear: the archive of --dry-run at once, the folder of inspect after an hour, which the next inspect also removes. The report adds Secure backup: decrypted with its password. Wrong password: ❌ The password does not open this backup (wrong_password). A .zip ignores the two options.
  • 🗝️ --dry-run says what becomes of the saved keys of the data providers, for any archive: Saved provider keys: 2 re-encrypted with this instance's key if the backup carries the key that encrypted them, ⚠️ 1 saved provider key cannot be read with this instance's key: enter it again after the restore for those it cannot read (What Follows).
  • 🔁 Run inspect now and then on the copies you keep, and --dry-run before a move, on the installation that will receive the archive.
  • 🖱️ Restore an archive, in Settings › Administration › Backup, runs the same check as --dry-run on an archive from your computer: read the report, then Drop this archive, and nothing changes (Restore from Settings › Administration › Backup).
  • ❌ A refusal ends with a code in parentheses: When Something Goes Wrong. Full lists in «Check an Archive» and «Try a Restore on a Copy», in CLI Admin Tools.

docs.title: ♻️ Restore on This Installation
docs.text:
A restore replaces the data of the installation with the archive's: database and files, for every user. Two ways, which check the archive on a copy first and change nothing until you confirm; the next start of LibreFolio applies the restore:

Where Who After confirming Settings › Administration › Backup, in the app Administrators LibreFolio stops at once, for that start Terminal on the server: backup restore Whoever has access to the server You restart it when it suits you

On an instance someone hosts for you, the command line is on their server: use Settings › Administration › Backup, or ask them.

docs.title: 🖱️ Restore from Settings › Administration › Backup
docs.text:
1. Choose the archive. In Settings › Administration › Backup, under Back up the instance, the Restore an archive card reminds you that a restore replaces the data of every user: if you may want them back, make a backup first. Choose an archive… → a .zip or a secure .lfbk made by LibreFolio, here or elsewhere. The Restore an archive window opens, and the next steps go on in it: a .zip goes to the server at once, with a progress bar: Stop sending stops it, nothing is kept.

    Or take a backup the server keeps: Restore on its row in the list of backups kept on the server, here or in Files › Backups, opens the Restore a backup window, with no further confirmation: the server takes that backup as the archive, with no download or upload, and the next steps, report included, happen in that window. Close it, or choose I'll decide later in the report: the check waits on the Restore an archive card, with Resume and Discard. A sealed backup of a hosting panel opens only with the private key of its recipients: it is not restored here.

  2. Type the password, for a secure backup: the window asks for it before sending anything (A secure backup: type the password it was made with.). Fill in Password of the backup and click Check the backup: the archive is sent, and the password goes with the request that starts the check, which tries it at once. Wrong password → Wrong password, or the file was changed: type the password again.; the archive stays on the server and the next try does not send it again. Cancel forgets the file.

  3. Let it be checked. The server checks the archive on a copy, as backup restore --dry-run does (Check a Backup): Decrypting the backup (secure only), Checking the archive, Unpacking it on a copy, Updating the copy's database, Verifying the copy. Nothing changes until you confirm. Stop the check drops it (a check still running is dropped as soon as it ends).
  4. Read the report, in the What this restore would do window: closing it keeps the check for later, as I'll decide later does. Closing the window during the check keeps it too: the check goes on, and Resume follows it again. What it says: below.
  5. Type the word. The window shows a real word, picked at random, of 6 to 10 letters in the language of the interface. Type it by hand in the field below: the field refuses pasted and dropped text. The word guards against a hasty click, not against an administrator: the API and the command line do without it. For an archive that cannot be restored, neither the word nor Restore and restart appears: only the button that drops it.
  6. Restore and restart. It confirms the restore and stops LibreFolio at once, for everyone. A window covers the page, LibreFolio is restarting: Its start applies the restore. This page waits for it to come back. LibreFolio does not restart by itself: whatever supervises it does (Who Starts LibreFolio Again), and that start applies the restore (What the Next Start Does).

docs.title: 📋 What the Report Says
docs.text:
• who made the archive, with which version of LibreFolio and when;
  • the database: at the version of this LibreFolio, or brought to it on the copy, with the migrations listed and the fixes applied to the copy;
  • the files and their size, the size of the database and the tables whose rows the update changed; and a bar of what the backup holds: the database, the uploaded files, the broker reports and the other files;
  • whether the backup carries the key of the instance it comes from: either way, this LibreFolio keeps its own;
  • the saved keys of the data providers: how many re-encrypted with this LibreFolio's key (2 saved keys of data providers are re-encrypted with this instance's key.) and how many unreadable, to enter again after the restore (1 saved key of a data provider cannot be read with this instance's key: enter it again after the restore.) (What Follows);
  • the ledger totals: the same as when the backup was made, different on the lines listed (how to read them), not recorded, recorded by another version of the method or unreadable;
  • the administrators of the backup, with After the restore you sign in with one of them, with the password of then; every session open now ends.
  • Invitations and links sent before the restore will have expired: send them again if needed.
  • every administrator with the picture of their account in the backup, and Verify a password before restoring: pick one, type their password and click Verify. Answer: You will sign in with this password after the restore., or That is not their password. The password is compared with the backup only: never stored, written to the log or sent back;
  • the warnings, which let it go on, and the blockers, which forbid the restore: a backup without an active administrator, and a restore that would pass the space limit, with the size to raise it to; such a check gives its space back at once, and the report stays on screen until you close it;
  • until when the uploaded archive is kept: 24 hours after the check.

Under the report: Drop this archive drops the check and its copy, nothing is restored. I'll decide later closes the window and keeps the check: the Restore an archive card shows A restore waits for your decision until …, with Resume, which opens the same report again, and Discard, from any tab or device of an administrator.

docs.title: 🏁 How It Went
docs.text:
When LibreFolio answers again, the page shows the outcome:

Outcome What you see What to do ✅ It worked The sign-in page, with no message: every session has ended. A restore that worked leaves no line on the card Sign in with an administrator of the backup, with the password it had when the backup was made: the first page shows the restored data ↩️ It did not go through The restore did not go through, with the reason. The data is as it was before: … = rolled back, the card says when and why. LibreFolio restarted, but the restore was not applied. = a start left it waiting, for the reason that follows Back to Backup returns to the card (after the sign-in page if the restart ended your session, or to the block page on an instance blocked meanwhile). Then What Settings › Administration › Backup Says ⏳ It takes long After a minute without the server: LibreFolio has not come back yet. If nothing starts it again by itself, start it yourself: the restore is applied at that start. If LibreFolio does not stop at all, after a minute: LibreFolio has not stopped. If it does not restart by itself, restart it yourself: the restore is applied at that start., with Back to Backup What Settings › Administration › Backup Says

The page reads the outcome with a one-time ticket received from the restart request, valid one hour and kept only in the memory of the tab: no session is needed. Without the ticket (page reloaded, more than an hour of waiting, restart from the command line instead of from here) the page goes by its session: without JWT_SECRET, which signs everyone out at every start (Keep Users Signed In After a Restart), it goes to the sign-in page whatever the outcome, and Settings › Administration › Backup says, once you are in, whether the restore went through.

docs.title: ⏳ A Restore Waiting
docs.text:
A restore confirmed and not applied yet takes the place of Choose an archive…: one confirmed from the command line, or here when LibreFolio did not stop or a start left it waiting. The card says A restore waits for the next start of LibreFolio, with the backup, who confirmed it (cli from the command line) and when, the reason if a start left it waiting, and Restarting stops LibreFolio for everyone; its next start applies the restore and ends every session.

Button What it does Restart now and restore Stops LibreFolio, as Restore and restart does; the page waits for it the same way Cancel the restore Drops it with its checked copy, as backup pending --cancel does: the data stays as it is

While a start applies the restore, the card says A start of LibreFolio is applying the restore.

Good to know:

  • 👑 Only administrators have the tab. One restore at a time: one archive is checked at a time, wherever the check started, here, in another tab or on the command line (Another archive is being checked: try again when it ends.).
  • 📏 If the installation limits the size of the archives (LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB, none by default), the card says so (Archives up to 500 MB.) and refuses a larger file before sending anything: The Upload Limit of a Restore.
  • 💽 The disk of the data directory needs room for the archive, for its copy during the check and, for a secure backup, for the decrypted archive: how much, in Check a Backup.
  • 📦 During the check, the archive takes its size on the server, which the card says while it is uploaded, plus its unpacked version; both count towards the space limit until the restore ends or is dropped.
  • 🔑 The password of a secure backup goes to the server only with the request that starts the check, which tries it at once: never stored, written to the log or sent back. The field empties as soon as you send it.
  • 🔄 A reload of the page keeps following the check and the report, and any other tab or device of an administrator picks it up from the Backup tab. The uploaded archive is kept 24 hours: after that, the confirmation answers The check is too old: check the archive again.
  • 🚪 The restore ends every session, everyone signs in again with an account of the backup, and the links sent before stop working: What the Next Start Does.
  • ❌ A refused upload, check or confirmation, or a server that does not answer, shows on the card with the reason. Try again reads the state of the restore again; to send an archive again, Choose an archive…. The check refuses the same archives as the command line: The Check Refuses the Archive.
  • 🖥️ If nothing restarts LibreFolio, such as a host installation started by hand, start the server yourself once it has stopped: the page waits for it.

docs.title: 📤 The Upload Limit of a Restore
docs.text:
An administrator uploads the archive from Settings › Administration › Backup (Restore from Settings › Administration › Backup), through PUT /api/v1/backup/restore/upload, and the instance checks it on a copy, as backup restore --dry-run does on the command line. Two variables limit how large it can be.

LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB limits the archive as it is sent, compressed:

Value Largest archive accepted Not set, or empty No limit 0 No limit A whole number, such as 2048 That many megabytes, of 1024 × 1024 bytes each

  1. In .env, or in the container's environment:

    LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=2048

  2. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

  3. In the configuration of the proxy in front of LibreFolio, let at least as much through: Nginx with client_max_body_size, default only 1 MB (client_max_body_size 2048m; matches the example), and your CDN, if it limits the size of a request.

The limit in force is read in upload_limit_mb of GET /api/v1/backup/restore/status: 0 no limit, null unreadable value. Settings › Administration › Backup shows it on the restore card (Archives up to 500 MB.) and refuses a larger file before sending it.

The upload answers Code When 413 backup_too_large, with the limit in limit_mb Archive over the limit: before writing anything if the request announces its size, otherwise as soon as the upload goes past the limit. Nothing is kept 413 without backup_too_large — It comes from the proxy, not from LibreFolio 503 backup_upload_unavailable Value that is not a whole number (500MB, -1): the server does not stop, but the start log already has LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB cannot be used: … (check is backup.upload_limit) and every upload adds to the log an error that names the variable: The upload limit of a restore cannot be read 507 backup_no_space The disk of the data directory has no room for the archive and, during the check, for its unpacked copy (how much: «Try a Restore on a Copy» in CLI Admin Tools); also when the disk reports itself full only at the end of the file, as a network file system or a quota may. The check has a code of its own, no_space: 507 if it cannot even start, refusal of the archive once it runs 500 backup_upload_failed The upload cannot be written for another reason; the log has the cause

LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB limits the unpacked size, from the sizes the manifest declares, before the check unpacks anything: a zip can unpack to far more than its size, on the disk of the data directory.

Value Largest unpacked size of an archive Not set, or empty No limit 0 No limit A whole number, such as 16384 That many megabytes, of 1024 × 1024 bytes each
  • An archive over the limit is refused before anything is unpacked: the check fails with the code unpacked_too_large, nothing of the copy is left. A secure archive is decrypted first (about its size), then measured the same way.
  • A value you set always wins, 0 included. backup restore on the command line follows the same limit; whoever runs the server lifts it for one command with LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB=0 in front of it («Try a Restore on a Copy» in CLI Admin Tools).
  • A value that is not a whole number does not stop the server: the start log already has LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB cannot be used: … (check is backup.restore_limit), then every check, POST /api/v1/backup/restore/stage, answers 503 with the code backup_restore_unavailable, the archive is kept and the log has an error.

docs.title: ⌨️ Restore from the Command Line
docs.text:
In the server's terminal, where LibreFolio runs: in the container with Docker.

# 1. Check the archive on a copy, read the report, then type "restore" to confirm
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup restore /app/backend/data/prod-docker/backups/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500-cli-1a2b3c4d/librefolio-backup-20261015-121500.zip

# 2. Restart LibreFolio: its next start applies the restore
docker compose restart librefolio

# 3. See how it went
docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup pending
  • 🧪 Step 1 runs the same check as --dry-run, shows the same report, then asks you to type restore. Nothing changes yet: LibreFolio keeps running on its data, the restore waits for the next start.
  • 🖥️ Host installation: pipenv run ./dev.py backup restore <archive>, then stop the whole server and start it again: never one worker alone.
  • ⏳ With LibreFolio up again, backup pending says ✅ The last restore was applied on …. Before the restart, backup pending --cancel drops the restore waiting, with its checked copy.
  • 🤖 In a script, --yes confirms without asking.
  • 🔐 Secure backup (.lfbk): backup restore asks the password before the check, or reads it with --password-file or --password-stdin, as inspect does (Check a Backup): in a script, one of the two together with --yes.
  • 📖 More: «Restore an Archive» and «Follow or Cancel a Restore» in CLI Admin Tools.

docs.title: 🔄 What the Next Start Does
docs.text:
• 🔀 The swap. The database and the three folders of files change places with the checked copy, in an instant whatever the size. secrets/, logs/, scheduler_state.json and backups/ stay as they are: the installation keeps its own instance key. The key a secure backup carries is never put in its place: the check already re-encrypted the keys of the data providers on the copy, with this installation's key.
  • 🚪 Every session ends. Everyone signs in again, on every device, with an account of the backup and the password it had then.
  • 🔗 One-time links are revoked. No invitation, password-reset or email-verification link sent before works any more, not even those in the backup: send new ones. An account still waiting for its email verification stops waiting: when its owner asks the sign-in page for a new link, the page answers that the account is disabled. An administrator reactivates it with Reactivate (What Each Action Does) or deletes it (Delete an Account) so that its owner signs up again.
  • ✅ The first start must complete. Only then is the restore kept and the former data removed. If it fails (failed migration, damaged file), the next start puts the former data back by itself, and backup pending, like the card in Settings › Administration › Backup, says that the rollback was done, with the reason.

docs.title: 🔌 Who Starts LibreFolio Again
docs.text:
You start the restore: with the restart of the command line, or with Restore and restart in Settings › Administration › Backup, which stops LibreFolio. Nothing in LibreFolio restarts the server: whatever supervises it does, after that stop and after a first start that fails, so that the next start brings the data back.

Supervisor Restarts LibreFolio by itself Docker Compose With restart: unless-stopped, in both compose files LibreFolio ships systemd With Restart=always None No: start LibreFolio yourself, and the restore, or the way back, happens at that start

Restore and restart stops LibreFolio cleanly: a policy that restarts only after a failure, such as on-failure, does not start it after that stop.
