To open one in the container, give --identity-file a path inside it; better, open it on your computer, where the private key is (Open a Sealed Backup).
  • 🔁 After a first start that fails on the restored data, the container restarts by itself (restart: unless-stopped, in both compose files LibreFolio ships), and that start puts the data back as it was.
  • 🔒 On the host, the archives belong to the container's user, and only that user reads them: with another host user, copy them with sudo cp -a.
  • 💻 From a source checkout, ./dev.py docker exec backup create does the same.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text: • 📄 Command-Line Tools — Start the Server, Manage Users, Maintain the Database, …

docs.title: 🛠️ Command-Line Tools
docs.text:
dev.py runs the administration tasks: starting the server, managing users and invitations, maintaining the database, backing up the instance. Each section says where to run the command and when it needs the server stopped.

Where to run the commands

Installation Where Command form On the host Terminal on the server, in the LibreFolio folder (the project root), Pipenv environment pipenv run ./dev.py <command> — or ./dev.py <command> after pipenv shell Docker, server running Terminal on the host, in the folder of docker-compose.yml docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py <command> Docker, server stopped Same terminal docker compose stop librefolio, then docker compose run --rm librefolio python dev.py <command> (one-off container), then docker compose start librefolio
  • There is no pipenv run in the container: the image installs the dependencies globally.
  • docker compose exec runs the command as root. From a source checkout, ./dev.py docker exec <command> runs it as the server's user instead (details).
  • The commands user, db current, db check, db currencies, backup create, backup inspect, backup restore, backup decrypt and backup pending work in the image (Back Up with Docker). db upgrade and db downgrade need the server stopped, so the third form (Apply Migrations). Development commands such as test are not part of the image.

📚 This guide is in several pages

Besides this page: CLI Admin Tools: Backups.

docs.title: 🖥️ Start the Server
docs.text:
On the host, in the server's terminal, LibreFolio folder. In Docker the server is the container's main process: docker compose up -d starts it.

# Standard start, one worker
pipenv run ./dev.py server

# Size the workers to the CPUs (`auto` and `0` do the same)
pipenv run ./dev.py server --workers auto

# Or set the number of workers
pipenv run ./dev.py server --workers 4

# Listen on another port (default: PORT from .env, else 6040)
pipenv run ./dev.py server --port 8080

# Kill whatever already holds the port, then start
pipenv run ./dev.py server --force

The server answers on the chosen port (PORT from .env, else 6040).

  • 🧮 More workers serve more requests at once: use them on any machine with more than one CPU. auto starts \(\max(1,\ 2\,(n-1))\) workers on \(n\) CPUs.
  • ⏳ At the first start, or when they are out of date, the server builds the web interface and this documentation: it takes a few minutes. If the interface does not build, the server does not start.
  • 🔑 A restart signs everybody out, unless JWT_SECRET is set in .env (Configuration).
  • ⏹️ Ctrl+C stops the server cleanly: dev.py gives it the shutdown budget plus 2 seconds (10 seconds by default), then ends it; a second Ctrl+C ends it at once. A SIGTERM sent to dev.py alone, by a process supervisor for example, gets the same wait: dev.py passes it on to the server.
⚙️ Other server options — rarely needed Option What it does --host HOST Address to listen on (default: HOST from the environment or .env, else 0.0.0.0) --data-dir PATH Another data directory for this run, instead of LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR --no-scheduler Start without the scheduled price and FX rate syncs --rebuild, -r Rebuild the web interface even when it looks up to date --debug, -d DEBUG logs, a debug build of the web interface and the API documentation pages (/api/v1/docs, /api/v1/redoc), otherwise off

Short forms: -w for --workers, -p for --port, -f for --force. --test, --coverage and --no-reload are development options: pipenv run ./dev.py server --help lists them all.

docs.title: 👤 Manage Users
docs.text:
On the host or in Docker with the server running (first or second form of the table above): these commands write straight to the database, so they also work while the server is running.

In the app, administrators manage accounts and invitations in Settings › Administration › Users (Users & Invitations). The command line is for a server without a browser, or to go past the user limit.

docs.title: ➕ Create and List Users
docs.text:
# Create an administrator account
pipenv run ./dev.py user create <username> <email> <password>

# Create a regular account
pipenv run ./dev.py user create <username> <email> <password> --role user

# List all users: ID, username, email, active, administrator
pipenv run ./dev.py user list

user list prints, for each account: ID, username, email, active, administrator.

  • 👑 user create creates an administrator; with --role user, a regular account. People can also sign up on their own: Register here on the login page while Registration is Open (on a new instance, also until the first account exists), or with an invitation link (Who Can Sign Up).
  • 🔒 Password: same rules as in the app and the API. At least 8 characters, with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter, a digit and a symbol. Letters and digits of any alphabet count (É, é); a symbol is any character that is neither a letter, a number nor a space (!, _, €). An invalid password changes nothing: the command prints Password does not meet security requirements: and one line per rule missed, starting with the rule's code (digit: the password must contain a digit), then exits with 1.
  • 🔤 Username: 3 to 50 characters, without @ (at sign-in, anything containing @ is read as an email address). Spaces, accented letters, ., _, -, + are fine. Errors, each with exit 1 and changing nothing: A username cannot contain @: the sign-in reads it as an email address; A username must be 3 to 50 characters long; Username already taken; Email already registered if another account has that address, or the address is another account's username (user set-email), in any capitals.
  • 📏 At the user limit, user create warns The instance is at its limit (LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS: 5 of 5 places taken): the command line creates the account anyway, then creates the account: the command line is how you go past the limit.

docs.title: ✉️ Invite Someone
docs.text:
# An invitation link for a regular account
pipenv run ./dev.py user invite

# An invitation for an administrator, with a note of whom it is for
pipenv run ./dev.py user invite --admin --email anna@example.com

The command prints a link that works once, for 7 days: send it to the person, who opens it and creates their own account with the username, email and password they choose (what they see).

  • 👑 --admin: the new account is an administrator; without it, a regular one.
  • ✉️ --email: only a note of whom the invitation is for; the person can sign up with another address.
  • 🌐 With LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL set, the link is complete (https://librefolio.example.com/invite#token=…). Without it, the command prints the path only, /invite#token=…, and reminds you to put the address of the server in front of it (http://192.168.1.10:6040). If the variable is set but is not an http:// or https:// address, the reminder says LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not valid (…), with the reason. This holds for every link on this page.
  • 🔒 The secret part comes after #: browsers never send it to the server, so it does not end up in the server or proxy logs. Send the link whole.
  • 🚪 Invitations work with Registration Open or By invitation. With Closed, the command stops with Registration is disabled: invitations cannot be created and exits with 1; the links already sent do not work either.
  • 📏 An invitation takes a place of the user limit until it is used, revoked or expired. At the limit, the command warns, then creates the invitation anyway.
  • ⏳ No command cancels an invitation: a link nobody used expires after 7 days. Sooner, Revoke in the Users tab, or through the API: GET /api/v1/users/account-links lists every account link with its state, DELETE /api/v1/users/account-links/<id> revokes an open one.

docs.title: 🔑 Reset a Password or Lock an Account
docs.text:
# Set a new password (same rules as above)
pipenv run ./dev.py user reset <username> <new_password>

# Lock an account out, then let it back in
pipenv run ./dev.py user deactivate <username>
pipenv run ./dev.py user activate <username>

reset changes the password at once; deactivate refuses the account from its next request.

  • ⏱️ reset ends the open sessions: every device is signed out at its next request. To lock someone out for good, deactivate: activating the account again does not bring its old sessions back.
  • 🔗 reset also cancels any reset link still open for the account, whoever created it.
  • 👑 deactivate refuses the last active administrator: User '<username>' is the last active administrator: promote or activate another administrator first, exit 1.
  • 📏 At the user limit, activate of a deactivated account warns … the command line reactivates the account anyway, then reactivates it. No warning for an account that already holds its place: one waiting for its email with a live link, or the initial administrator waiting for its setup link.
  • 📬 With email verification on, activate lets an account waiting for its email in at once and deactivate ends the wait: either way its verification links stop working (Email Verification in Email).
  • 🏁 On the initial administrator still waiting for its setup link, reset and activate set it up without the link and end the wait for good: its setup links are invalidated, the one of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN included, and neither user setup-link nor a new LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN gives it another one. activate alone leaves an active account whose password nobody knows, until reset or a reset link gives it one; reset alone leaves it inactive, until you step in with activate.
  • 🚫 On that same waiting administrator, deactivate sets nothing up: it cancels the setup link, as Cancel setup link does in Users & Invitations. It prints ✅ User '<username>' deactivated; every setup link of the account is invalidated, the one of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN included, and the account keeps waiting: user setup-link gives it a new one, and so does a new LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN at the next start. The same token, at a restart, does not: the instance has already seen it.
  • 💬 The app's Forgot Password? screen shows this command for both installations: for Docker the line docker compose exec librefolio sh -c 'exec gosu …' sh user reset … (the one of docker exec, run as the server's user, not root); for the host ./dev.py user reset …, after pipenv shell or with pipenv run in front. When the instance can email a reset link, the screen shows only the email form, without the commands (Forgotten Passwords).

docs.title: 🔗 Send a Password-Reset Link
docs.text:
pipenv run ./dev.py user reset-link <username>

The command prints a link: the person opens it and chooses the new password themselves, instead of receiving the one you chose with user reset (what they see).

  • ⏱️ The link works once, for 30 minutes. A new link for the same account cancels the earlier ones; a change of the account's password or email — in the user's Profile, or with user reset or user set-email — cancels them all.
  • 🚪 Once the new password is set, every signed-in device is signed out, as with user reset. Creating the link signs nobody out.
  • 🌐 Complete link with LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, the path only (/reset-password#token=…) without it (as for invitations).

docs.title: 🔁 A New Setup Link for the Initial Administrator
docs.text:
pipenv run ./dev.py user setup-link

The command prints a new setup link for the administrator created from LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL at the first start (The Initial Administrator), as long as nobody has used theirs: they open it, choose the password and are signed in. Use it when the link has expired, got lost or was cancelled.

  • ⏱️ The link works once, for 72 hours. The earlier setup links are invalidated, the one of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN included.
  • 🚫 After a cancellation — Cancel setup link in Users & Invitations, or user deactivate on the waiting administrator — the administrator still waits: this command gives it a new link.
  • 📮 After a new address for the waiting administrator — LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL changed before a restart, or user set-email — its links, sent to the old address, are invalidated: this command gives it a link for the new one. The same address with other capitals of the letters A-Z is no change: the link keeps working.
  • 🔚 Set up another way — user activate, or a password from user reset or from a reset link — the administrator waits no more: its links are invalidated for good and the command stops with the error below.
  • 🌐 Complete link with LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, the path only (/setup#token=…) without it (as for invitations).
  • 📧 The command only prints the link: it sends no email.
  • ❌ Without a waiting administrator, the command stops with No administrator account is waiting for its setup link and exits with 1. The same if the administrator completes the setup while the command runs: the command checks again just before it issues the link and gives none to an account already set up.

docs.title: 📧 Change the Email Address of an Account
docs.text:
pipenv run ./dev.py user set-email <username> <new_email>

The same change as a new email in the user's Profile, without their password: for someone who cannot change their address themselves, or to separate two accounts that share one (below).

  • 🔤 An address belongs to one account only, whatever its capitals: Anna@example.com and anna@example.com are the same address. Only the letters A-Z are compared this way, not accented ones: Émile@example.com and émile@example.com are two different addresses.
  • 🚪 A new address signs the account out of every device, cancels every password-reset link and every pending email-change link, and is recorded as not verified; the account can still sign in. It does not touch the password. The same address with other capitals only changes how it is written: nobody is signed out and it stays verified.
  • 👑 On the initial administrator still waiting for its setup link, the new address also invalidates that link: the account still waits, and user setup-link gives it a new one. While LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL is set, each start of the server gives the waiting account that address again: change the variable as well, or the next start brings the old address back and invalidates the new link too.
  • ❌ Refused, with exit 1 and changing nothing: an address another account already has, in any capitals (Email already registered); an address that is another account's username, in any capitals (same error: an account created before version 1.3 may have an @ in its username, Usernames with an @, and if that name became someone's address, the sign-in, which reads an address first, would no longer find that account); an invalid address (Not an email address); an unknown username (User '<username>' not found). The account's own username is no obstacle: it can become its address.

docs.title: 👑 Grant or Remove Administrator Rights
docs.text:
pipenv run ./dev.py user promote <username>
pipenv run ./dev.py user demote <username>

A demotion signs the account out of every device.

  • 👑 demote refuses the last active administrator: User '<username>' is the last active administrator: promote another user first, exit 1.
  • 🏁 demote also refuses the initial administrator still waiting for its setup link, which keeps its role until then: User '<username>' is the initial administrator waiting for its setup: it keeps its role until then; deactivate it to cancel its setup link, or delete it from Settings › Administration › Users, exit 1, changing nothing. To cancel its link: user deactivate (above). To remove the account: delete it in Users & Invitations, with no demotion first. The command line deletes no account.

docs.title: 🧭 Restart the Guides of a User
docs.text:
# Every guide, the Welcome setup included
pipenv run ./dev.py user reset-onboarding <username>

# One guide only
pipenv run ./dev.py user reset-onboarding <username> --flow intro_tour

The next time the user opens LibreFolio, the Welcome setup and the guides start again, as on their first visit; the user's data and preferences stay. --flow restarts one guide only: pipenv run ./dev.py user reset-onboarding --help lists the names (welcome, intro_tour, import_guide…).

docs.title: ⬆️ Apply Migrations
docs.text:
Every start of the server applies the pending migrations by itself: you rarely need to do it by hand.

On the host, in the server's terminal, LibreFolio folder, with the server stopped: db upgrade refuses to run while the server answers on the configured port. db current, db check and db currencies change nothing and also run with the server up.

# Apply pending migrations
pipenv run ./dev.py db upgrade

# Show the migration the database is at
pipenv run ./dev.py db current

# Look for missing CHECK constraints: changes nothing, exits with 1 if any
pipenv run ./dev.py db check

# List the currency codes that are not ISO codes: changes nothing, exits with 1 if any
pipenv run ./dev.py db currencies

# Upgrade and check another database file, such as a copy
pipenv run ./dev.py db upgrade /path/to/copy/app.db
pipenv run ./dev.py db check /path/to/copy/app.db

db upgrade brings the database to the latest migration; db current prints the one it is at.

  • 📄 Without a path, the commands use the configured database. A path names another SQLite file: a relative one starts at the project root, whatever folder you run the command from. The file must exist, except for db upgrade, which creates it (folder included) and brings it up to date.
  • 🐳 In Docker, the path is inside the container: LibreFolio-data/ is /app/backend/data/prod-docker, the database is sqlite/app.db in it. db current, db check and db currencies: server running, docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py db current <path>. db upgrade and db downgrade: server stopped (docker compose stop librefolio), then a one-off container, docker compose run --rm librefolio python dev.py db upgrade <path> (details).

docs.title: 🔤 Two Accounts with the Same Email Address
docs.text:
From version 1.3, an email address belongs to one account only, whatever its capitals. If an earlier database has two accounts with addresses that differ only in capitals (Anna@example.com and anna@example.com), the upgrade stops at the migration that checks this and the server does not start. The earlier migrations stay applied, no account is changed, the next start picks up from there. The log (or the output of db upgrade) names the accounts by id and username, never by address; a ; separates one group from the next:

Email addresses must be unique regardless of case (release 1.3), and these accounts share one apart from upper and lower case: #3 'anna', #8 'anna_work'. Give all but one account of each group another address with …

LibreFolio never merges two accounts: give all but one account of each group another address, then start LibreFolio again.

On the hostDocker

In the server's terminal, LibreFolio folder:

pipenv run ./dev.py user set-email <username> <new_email>

In the folder of docker-compose.yml. The server is the container's main process, so the container does not stay up and docker compose exec is no use: use a one-off container.

docker compose stop librefolio
docker compose run --rm librefolio python dev.py user set-email <username> <new_email>
docker compose start librefolio

docs.title: 🩹 Post-Migration Fixes
docs.text:
Right after the migrations, every start runs the post-migration fixes: repairs that a migration cannot make. Usually there is nothing to do. In the log (the server output, also saved in logs/) you may read:

Log line Meaning ✅ Post-migration fixes applied and verified A repair was made. On a large database that start is slower, once. ⚠️ Post-migration fix failed Database left as it was, server started normally. The warning gives the error and the copy of the database kept next to the original until you delete it (app.db.pre-autoincrement-20261008T101500Z.bak). The fix is tried again at the next start. 🩺 Post-migration fixes skipped The copy could not be made, or the database fails SQLite's integrity check. Nothing changed. 🔗 Foreign key violations already in the database, left as they are The database holds references to rows that no longer exist, listed in the warning. The fixes leave them as they are and still run: a fix fails only on a broken reference it would add itself.

The empty file app.db.post-migration.lock, next to the database, makes the runs take turns when several workers start together: leave it in place.

The fixes:

  • autoincrement: the id of a deleted user, broker, asset, transaction, FX conversion route or asset event is never given out again. While converting, it deletes the report folders of brokers that no longer exist, so that a new broker does not inherit them.
  • orphan_pair_halves, once: repairs the transfers that a broker deletion left without their other half on the remaining brokers.
    • 📈 Securities received from the deleted broker → opening position at the transfer cost, from the transfer date. That broker's capital counts them at that cost, not at their market value on arrival, so its gain also includes what they gained before the transfer. Without a recorded cost they stay without one and the app reports an acquisition without a purchase value: enter the cost in the transaction.
    • 💶 Cash transfers with the deleted broker → deposits or withdrawals: capital and gain do not change.
    • 📤 Securities sent to the deleted broker: right after the fixes, at the same start, each transfer becomes an adjustment that takes the securities out of the sending broker, without a value: only the quantity goes down, and the cost counts as a realized loss on that broker. One log line each (Lone transfer leg converted to an ADJUSTMENT-out without a value). If the database fails SQLite's quick check, they stay as they were (Lone transfer legs left as they are: the database failed its quick check). If the whole step fails (Lone transfer legs could not be converted; starting normally), nothing is changed and the server starts anyway.
  • event_types, once: repairs the asset events with a type LibreFolio does not know, such as dividend or dividendo written by hand in a CSV. Until now such an event made the whole list of the asset's events fail to load, so none was shown.
    • ✅ A type that differs only in letter case or spaces (dividend, Split) is corrected.
    • 🗑️ An event whose type is still unknown is deleted. A linked transaction stays, without its event: link it again to the right event if you need to.
⌨️ Run the fixes by hand — to preview them or retry a failed one

On the host, in the server's terminal, LibreFolio folder, with the server stopped (the script does not check it). In Docker: Post-migration fixes with the server stopped.

# Preview: report what would be fixed, change nothing
pipenv run python -m backend.app.db.post_migration --dry-run

# Apply the fixes
pipenv run python -m backend.app.db.post_migration

The script prints each fix as clean (nothing to do), would_apply (dry run), applied or failed, with the orphan broker folders, a kept copy and any error, then one line for each transfer of securities sent to a deleted broker (Lone transfer leg …); it exits with 1 when something failed. --db PATH and --data-dir PATH point it at another database or another data directory.

To see what orphan_pair_halves will do on your database, run --dry-run before the first start of the new version: it prints Fix orphan_pair_halves: would_apply when there is something to repair, and a warning lists the transactions by id, grouped by conversion (TRANSFER->ADJUSTMENT), with those that will stay without a cost and the transfers of securities sent to a deleted broker; these get one line each after the fixes (would become an ADJUSTMENT-out without a value). The script prints on the console what the server would write to the log: the warning and, on a real run, one line per transaction changed (with LOG_LEVEL at INFO, the default). It writes no log file: keep its output if you want a record of the repair.

🔗 How the fixes work inside: Database Schema — Post-migration fixes.

docs.title: 💱 Currency Codes That Are Not ISO Codes
docs.text:
From version 1.3, LibreFolio saves a currency only as an ISO 4217 alphabetic code (EUR, USD). Earlier versions also accepted the name or the numeric code and saved it as written: Euro, 978. Such a value still reads, but an edit that saves its row again is refused until the code is corrected, and its amounts are not summed with those of the ISO code: 978 and EUR make two balances. A restored backup can bring such values back.

Shortly after every start, the log warns when the database holds some; LibreFolio does not change them by itself:

Stored currency codes that are not ISO 4217 codes: an edit of their rows is refused until they are corrected (./dev.py db currencies lists them)

On the host or in Docker with the server running (docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py db currencies):

# Where each value is stored, how many rows hold it, and the ISO code it stands for
pipenv run ./dev.py db currencies

# Another database file, such as a copy
pipenv run ./dev.py db currencies /path/to/copy/app.db

The command lists the values without changing anything.

  • 🔎 Each line names the place (transactions.currency, assets.currency, the steps of an FX route, a provider's settings, a user's base currency…), the value, how many rows hold it and the ISO code it stands for: 978 is EUR, US DOLLAR is USD.
  • ➖ A dash: no single code. A name two currencies share (Bolívar Soberano: VED or VES), a value that is not a currency, or a code that counts cents rather than units (GBX, ZAC, ILA), never to be simply renamed.
  • 🔤 A code in lower case or with spaces (eur) is listed too: the right currency, in a form that exact comparisons miss.
  • 🧱 A value saved as raw bytes or as text that is not valid UTF-8, which only a damaged or hand-made database holds, appears in SQLite's notation (X'455552') with a dash: it is never a code.
  • 🚦 Exit 0 when every code is ISO, 1 when it lists some, 2 when it cannot read the database.

docs.title: 🔧 Add Missing Global Settings
docs.text:
On the host or in Docker with the server running:

pipenv run ./dev.py user init-settings

Adds the missing Global Settings with their default values, as every start does, but without starting the server; it never changes a value already set.

docs.title: 🧹 Reset the Database
docs.text:
On the host, in the server's terminal, LibreFolio folder, with the server stopped:

pipenv run ./dev.py db create-clean

All data will be lost

db create-clean deletes the database and creates an empty one. Like db upgrade, it refuses to run while the server is up. Uploaded files and broker reports stay on disk: Database Initialization & Reset.

docs.title: 📋 Full Command Tree
docs.text:
# Every command, by category
pipenv run ./dev.py --help

# The options of one command
pipenv run ./dev.py server --help
👩‍💻 Developer and documentation commands
  • Frontend: pipenv run ./dev.py front build, front dev, front check — Frontend Development
  • Testing: pipenv run ./dev.py test all — Test Walkthrough
  • API Client: pipenv run ./dev.py api sync — API Overview
  • i18n: pipenv run ./dev.py i18n audit — Internationalization
  • Documentation: pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs deploy publishes this documentation to GitHub Pages; pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs gallery regenerates the screenshots with Playwright on a test server (--no-populate keeps the current test data).

The full developer toolkit: Developer Workflow Guide.

docs.title: 📝 Configuration
docs.text:
LibreFolio's startup options live in a .env file: ports, the data folder, logging, login sessions, sign-ups, secrets and a few optional features.

Where it goes: in the .env file in LibreFolio's folder (the root of the project; with Docker, the folder of docker-compose.yml). With Docker, the same variables also work in the environment: block of docker-compose.yml, which wins over .env. LibreFolio reads .env when it starts.

The options you change from inside the app are the Global Settings instead.

📚 This guide is in several pages

  • Configuration: Secrets and Plugin Settings: the options that are secrets, how to read them from files, the instance key and the settings of the plugins.
  • Configuration: Checks and Protections: what LibreFolio checks at startup, the browser protections (Content-Security-Policy, frame protection) and how it stops.
  • Configuration: Accounts and Asset Search: who can sign up, the limit on failed sign-ins, the initial administrator, the order of the price providers in the search and the web search.

docs.title: 🔧 Create the .env File
docs.text:
In LibreFolio's folder, from a terminal:

  1. Copy the sample file:

    cp .env.example .env

    You get a .env with every option, grouped by what they do. With the pre-built Docker image, the Docker installation guide downloads the same sample as .env.

  2. Edit the values you need. A commented option, such as # SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=auto, shows the default: remove the # only to change the value. Names are case-sensitive.

  3. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

docs.title: ✏️ Main Options
docs.text:
Where: in LibreFolio's .env, or in the container's environment (environment: block of docker-compose.yml). Then restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

In the main options and in the risk settings below, a value of the wrong type or out of range stops the server at startup with an error. The exceptions are in the details under each table, with what appears in the log.

Server, data and logs

Variable Default What it does PORT 6040 Port of the web server. With Docker Compose, the port opened on the host: the container always listens on 6040. TEST_PORT 6041 Port of the test server (./dev.py server --test). LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR ./backend/data/prod Folder of the database, the uploads, the broker reports and the logs; a relative path starts from the project folder. LOG_LEVEL INFO How much the server writes to the logs: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. PREVIEW_CACHE_MAX_MB 50 Memory, in MB, of the image-preview cache, for each server process.
  • LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR with Docker: fixed to /app/backend/data/prod-docker. To move the data on the host, in docker-compose.yml change the left side of the ./LibreFolio-data volume.
  • LOG_LEVEL: at DEBUG or TRACE, the web app also writes to the browser's console every failed call to the server, the refused ones included (a 4xx answer); at the other levels, only the server errors, the calls that got no answer and the answers it cannot read.

Login sessions and reverse proxies

Variable Default What it does JWT_SECRET not set Key that signs the login sessions. See Keep users signed in. SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE auto When the login session cookie is sent over HTTPS only: auto (if the browser uses HTTPS), always or never. See HTTPS and reverse proxies. LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER not set Behind a reverse proxy, the header in which it passes the visitor's address, such as Fly-Client-IP on Fly.io. See The Visitor's Address.
  • JWT_SECRET not set, empty or made of spaces only: a new key at every start, so everyone has to sign in again after a restart. JWT_SECRET_FILE reads it from a file instead: see Secrets.
  • LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER: set it only if every request crosses that proxy.

Browser protections and API documentation

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION false Leave it unset on an install of your own. true lets only LibreFolio's own pages show it in a frame. See Frame Protection. LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY false Leave it unset on an install of your own. true adds a second, wider Content-Security-Policy to the pages of the web app, in report-only mode. See The Report-Only Policy. LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS false Leave it unset. true serves the API's documentation pages: Swagger UI at /api/v1/docs, ReDoc at /api/v1/redoc, schema at /api/v1/openapi.json.
  • LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION not set: dashboards at another address, such as Home Assistant panels, can show LibreFolio in a frame. true adds X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' to every response. The three rules object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self' do not depend on this option: LibreFolio's pages always carry them (The Content-Security-Policy). Valid values: true or false; 1/0, yes/no and on/off too, in any case; any other value stops the server at startup.
  • LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY: only the pages of the web app, not the documentation or the API. It blocks nothing: the browser lists in its developer console what that policy would block, without sending a report anywhere. The enforced Content-Security-Policy always stays on. Same values as LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION.
  • LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS off: the pages answer 404, in every profile and with Docker too (an instance in use does not publish the map of its own API). A browser that opens one of these addresses, another address under /api/ or a documentation page that does not exist under /mkdocs/ is taken to the app (/); a program still gets 404 with {"detail": "Not Found"}. In the web app, a page that does not exist takes you back to the page you came from, or to the Dashboard. ./dev.py server --debug turns it on; LibreFolio's test runs keep it on. Valid values: true or false; 1 and 0 too. The pages' own policy: The Content-Security-Policy.

Instance links: support, terms of service, privacy

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_SUPPORT_URL not set Where the users of the instance ask for help: a page with http:// or https://, or an email address such as mailto:help@example.org. LIBREFOLIO_TOS_URL not set The terms of service of the instance: a page with http:// or https://, linked from the Terms of service link of the legal notice. LIBREFOLIO_PRIVACY_URL not set The privacy policy of the instance, linked as Privacy policy next to the terms of service: same rules as LIBREFOLIO_TOS_URL.
  • The three addresses are public: anyone who can reach the server can read them at /api/v1/system/instance.
  • LIBREFOLIO_SUPPORT_URL: for example for an asset the search does not find (Let us know, under the search results). With an email address, the user's email app opens a message with the details of the search. With a page, it opens in a new tab and receives the report in the title and body query parameters, like a prefilled GitHub issue, so that a support form can fill itself in; the details are copied too, to paste there. Not set: on an install of your own (the selfhosted profile), a new public issue on LibreFolio's GitHub opens with the details, for the user to review before sending it. Any other value is ignored, as if it were not set, and the server logs it once. A page whose address holds a user name or a password counts as not set too.
  • LIBREFOLIO_TOS_URL: the legal notice that every user sees (Settings › About, the Welcome page, under the card of every sign-in page, at the foot of the sidebar) points to the terms with the Terms of service link, opened in a new tab. Not set: no link, the notice alone. Unlike LIBREFOLIO_SUPPORT_URL, no mailto:.
  • A value that cannot be used in LIBREFOLIO_TOS_URL or LIBREFOLIO_PRIVACY_URL, an address with a user name or a password included: the server never stops; that link stays hidden and the legal notice is shown without it. The log has an error, Invalid instance link, the first time each server process answers /api/v1/system/instance (the app reads it as soon as it opens): the variable and its value in problem (a value with an @ is not shown: it may hold a user name or a password) and, in consequence, what it costs until you fix it, for example the terms of service link stays hidden until it is fixed: the legal notice shows without it. A LIBREFOLIO_SUPPORT_URL that cannot be used logs the same error too, with its own consequence. Fix the value, then restart.

Backup and space

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB not set: no limit Leave it unset. The largest size, in megabytes, of an archive an administrator may upload to check it for a restore; 0 means no limit. See The Upload Limit of a Restore. LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB not set: no limit Leave it unset. The largest size, in megabytes, an archive may unpack to while it is checked for a restore, from the sizes its manifest declares; 0 means no limit. LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS not set One or two age public keys (age1…), comma-separated: backup create --sealed then makes a sealed backup. Not a secret. LIBREFOLIO_STORAGE_LIMIT_MB not set Leave it unset on an install of your own: the limit is set in the space bar of the Files page. The space the instance may take, in megabytes; 0 means no limit. See The Space Bar.
  • All four are read from the environment only.
  • LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB with a value that is not a whole number: the server does not stop; the uploads answer 503 and the log has an error, from startup already (Startup Checks) and then each time the limit is read.
  • LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB: a value you set always wins, 0 included; backup restore on the command line follows it too. An archive over the limit is refused before anything is unpacked (unpacked_too_large). With a value that is not a whole number the server does not stop: the checks of a restore answer 503 (backup_restore_unavailable), the log has an error from startup already (Startup Checks) and then at each check, and the Security tab of Settings › Administration reports it (backup.restore_limit).
  • LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS: the keys as backup keygen or age-keygen print them; two only while a key is being changed. The sealed backup is a .tar that only the matching private keys open, never the instance key. A value that cannot be used (a key that is not age1…, more than two, the same one twice) does not stop the server: the log has an error and the Security tab of Settings › Administration reports it (backup.recipients).
  • LIBREFOLIO_STORAGE_LIMIT_MB set: it wins over the LibreFolio total space (MB) setting, whatever value an administrator saved, and locks it: the field in the space bar is disabled (greyed out) and a save is refused. Not set: the setting decides, 0 until an administrator saves another value. A value that is not a whole number is ignored and the setting applies. Past the limit, LibreFolio refuses an uploaded file, a broker report, a backup started by hand and a restore that would take the data beyond it; it deletes nothing. The administrator cannot raise it from here: the message asks whoever hosts the instance to do it.

Price providers and broker imports

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_BASE_SECONDS 60 The first pause of a price provider that answers «too many requests» (HTTP 429); each refusal in a row doubles the next pause. A whole number of seconds from 0 to 86400; 0 turns the pauses off. See Provider Pauses. LIBREFOLIO_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_MAX_SECONDS 3600 The longest pause the doubling reaches: a whole number of seconds from 1 to 86400, not below the first pause while the pauses are on. LIBREFOLIO_PROBE_RATE_LIMIT 30 How many times a minute one user may test the settings of a price provider (Test Configuration in the asset form; Ask Provider counts too). A whole number from 0 to 10000; 0 turns the limit off. LIBREFOLIO_BRIM_PREWARM false (true in test mode) Optional. true makes the workers for importing broker reports ready at startup, with the import plugins loaded. See BRIM Architecture → Preload and warm-up.
  • Provider pauses: during a pause no request reaches the provider. On by default: an exception to the rule that a new option leaves an install as it was. A provider's Retry-After may still ask for more, up to one day. A value that cannot be used in either variable does not stop the server: the log has an error and both defaults apply.
  • LIBREFOLIO_PROBE_RATE_LIMIT: the tests may call the provider; past the limit, the form tells the user when to try again. 0 only for a test instance (./dev.py server --test does it): the log has a warning at every start. Read at every test: a change applies without a restart. A value that cannot be used does not stop the server: the log has an error and 30 applies.
  • LIBREFOLIO_BRIM_PREWARM: the first broker import after a start is about 4 seconds faster, for about 80 MB of memory from startup and about 1.4 seconds of CPU at every start; on a small cloud machine they cost more than the seconds they save, so it is off. Valid values: true or false; 1/0, yes/no and on/off too, in any case. Any other value does not stop the server, unlike the main options: the log has a warning at startup and the option stays off.

Email

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST not set: email off Optional. The SMTP server that sends LibreFolio's emails, such as smtp.example.com. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS starttls How the connection to the SMTP server is encrypted: starttls, tls or none. See Encryption Modes. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT 587 with starttls, 465 with tls, 25 with none The port of the SMTP server, only when it is not the usual one of its encryption mode. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER not set: no login The user for the login on the SMTP server, set together with LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD (Secrets). LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM not set The sender of the emails, required as soon as a server is set. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_REPLY_TO not set: replies go to the sender Where the replies to LibreFolio's emails go. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR 50 How many emails the instance may send in an hour, per server process. LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS 20 How many registration emails one client address may trigger in an hour, per server process: a whole number, at least 1. See Limits on Activation and Password-Reset Emails.
  • LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* variables: all explained in Email.
  • LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS: one single count for the registrations, Send the link again and Forgot Password?. Past the limit, a new account is created and waits, and its email is held.

Older .env files may still contain PORTFOLIO_BASE_CURRENCY: LibreFolio ignores it and new users start from the Default Currency in Global Settings.

🔒 HTTPS and reverse proxies — the session cookie

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE decides when the cookie that keeps users signed in is Secure: the browser then sends it over HTTPS only. Case and spaces around the value do not matter; any other value stops the server at startup with an error.

Value When to use it auto (default) Secure when the browser reached LibreFolio over HTTPS, that is when the reverse proxy says so with the X-Forwarded-Proto: https header (only the first value counts). No list of trusted proxies to set up: the header can only turn Secure on, never off. Over plain HTTP (http://localhost:6040, a LAN IP, the Tailscale IP of Levels 1 and 2 in Exposing Securely) the cookie is not Secure and signing in works. always Always Secure: an install reached over HTTPS only. Over plain HTTP the browser drops the cookie and the sign-in does not stick: the next page sends you back to the login. never Never Secure. The way out when a proxy sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https to a browser that uses plain HTTP, such as Nginx with a hard-coded proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https; in a plain-HTTP server block: with auto, that browser would be sent back to the login after every sign-in. Better fix the proxy ($scheme instead of https); never is the fallback.

With auto, behind an HTTPS reverse proxy the proxy must send X-Forwarded-Proto:

  • Tailscale Serve and Funnel (Levels 3 and 4 in Exposing Securely), Caddy and Traefik send it on their own: nothing to configure.

  • Nginx does not. In Nginx's configuration, in the location block that proxies LibreFolio, add:

    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

  • Any other proxy: make it send the header. Or, if LibreFolio is reachable only through it, in .env:

    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=always

To check in your browser whether the session cookie is Secure: Checking Connection Security.

🧮 Risk engine workers — advanced tuning

Risk simulations and portfolio optimizations run in separate worker processes, started on first use. The defaults suit most installs: add a variable to .env only to change them.

Variable Default What it does RISK_SIMULATION_WORKERS, RISK_OPTIMIZATION_WORKERS 1 (1–8) Worker processes per kind of job: more processes run more jobs at once. RISK_SIMULATION_QUEUE_CAPACITY, RISK_OPTIMIZATION_QUEUE_CAPACITY 2 (0–64) Jobs that can wait for a worker; beyond that limit, new requests are refused. RISK_SIMULATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, RISK_OPTIMIZATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 120 / 60 Time limit of one job, in seconds. RISK_SIMULATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, RISK_OPTIMIZATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 600 Idle workers stop after this many seconds and start again with the next job; 0 keeps them running.

docs.title: 💻 Parameters Set by the Tools
docs.text:
./dev.py and Docker Compose set them for you: change them only if you know why.

Variable Default What it does HOST 0.0.0.0 Address ./dev.py server listens on; 127.0.0.1 accepts local connections only. Docker Compose always uses 0.0.0.0. LIBREFOLIO_LOG_LEVEL — Replaces LOG_LEVEL when set; ./dev.py server --debug and ./dev.py server --test set it to DEBUG. LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS — Set to 1 by ./dev.py server --debug, which turns on the API's documentation pages (the variable of the same name, above). LIBREFOLIO_NO_SCHEDULER — Any non-empty value, 0 included, turns the scheduled price and FX rate syncs off. Set by ./dev.py server --no-scheduler. LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE — 1, true or yes, in any case, switches to the test data folder. For LibreFolio's test runs only: ./dev.py server --test and the test runners set it, ./dev.py server turns it off. A server started without ./dev.py (uvicorn directly, a service unit) takes it from its own environment. On an instance in use, outside the test runner, the startup checks report it as an error. LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR ./backend/data/test Folder of the test data; it cannot overlap the production one.

docs.title: 🔝 Which Value Wins
docs.text:
From the highest priority to the lowest:

  1. The --host, --port and --data-dir options of ./dev.py server.
  2. The variables set in the shell.
  3. The .env file.
  4. The defaults listed on this page.

With Docker Compose, the environment: block of docker-compose.yml wins over .env: it fixes HOST, LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR and, inside the container, PORT=6040 (your PORT still sets the port on the host). See Advanced Docker.

For a plugin setting, from the highest priority to the lowest:

  1. Its variable: LIBREFOLIO_PLUGIN_… before the plugin's older name for it, and each before its _FILE form.
  2. The value saved inside LibreFolio.
  3. The plugin's default.

A variable with a wrong value still wins and leaves the plugin not configured. A personal setting has no variable: the value saved by the user, then the default.

docs.title: 📂 Where the Data Goes
docs.text:
• Production: backend/data/prod/, or LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR. It holds the database (sqlite/app.db), custom-uploads/, broker_reports/, logs/ and, once LibreFolio has created the instance key, secrets/.
  • Test: backend/data/test/, or LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR. Same layout, kept apart.

Filesystem Structure details each folder and how to back it up.

docs.title: 👥 Configuration: Accounts and Asset Search
docs.text:
Who can sign up to your LibreFolio, how many accounts it may hold, the limit on failed sign-ins and the initial administrator; then two options of the asset search: the order of the price providers in the results and the optional web search.

  • Where to write it: in LibreFolio's .env file (Configuration, the guide's first page, explains the file and its other options). Then restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.
  • From inside the app: the matching choices are in the Global Settings (Settings › Administration). A set variable wins: each line below says how.

docs.title: 👥 Accounts and Sign-ups
docs.text:
Where: in LibreFolio's .env, Accounts section of .env.example: uncomment a line to set it. All optional; an empty value counts as not set. Without them, the Global Settings decide; three more variables, for installs made with a script and Docker Compose, create the initial administrator of a new instance.

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION not set Who may create an account: open (anyone), invite (only with an invitation link) or disabled (nobody). Not set: the Registration setting decides. LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS not set (no limit) The most accounts the instance may hold: a whole number, at least 1; any other value (0, abc, -3, 1.5) stops the server at startup. See When the Instance Is Full. LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE not set The language of the accounts that have not chosen one, and of the emails to people who have no account yet: en, it, fr or es. Not set: the Default Language setting decides; on a new instance, English. LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_CURRENCY not set The currency new accounts start with: an ISO 4217 code that LibreFolio knows, such as EUR, USD or CHF. Not set: the Default Currency setting decides; on a new instance, EUR. LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE not set The timezone of the app, the one the times of the market data scheduler are read in: an IANA name such as Europe/Rome or America/New_York. Not set: the Timezone setting decides; on a new instance, UTC. LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL not set The address your users open LibreFolio at, with http:// or https://, such as https://librefolio.example.com: the start of the invitation and password-reset links, and of the links in the emails. LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT on The limit on failed sign-ins: on or off, in any case, spaces around the value included. off for a test instance only. Any other value, true, 1 and yes included, stops the server at startup. See Failed Sign-ins.
  • LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION — in the app: Registration, in the Global Settings. Not set: on a new instance it is By invitation, unless an administrator changed it; an instance upgraded from an earlier version keeps the mode it had. Set: this value wins, and the global setting cannot be changed from the app. Case and spaces around the value do not matter. Whatever the value, the first account of a new instance can be created from the login page, with Register here, and becomes the administrator (Who Can Sign Up); with LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL, LibreFolio creates that administrator directly instead (The Initial Administrator). open also shows the administrators who open the app from an address outside the local network a warning that names this variable (The Open-Registration Warning).
  • LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS — active accounts count, and so does each invitation until it is used, revoked or expires, each account waiting for its email verification while its link is live, and the initial administrator while it waits for its setup; deactivated accounts do not.
  • LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE, LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_CURRENCY, LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE — in the app: Default Language and Default Currency of the Global Settings, Timezone of the scheduler's configuration. The variable holds until an administrator saves that setting for the first time; from that first save the administrator's value wins, even when it goes back to the default (English, EUR, UTC). Language and currency in any case. The server itself always works in UTC.

  • LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL — who uses it:

    • the Users tab of Settings › Administration: the invitation and password-reset dialogs fill in their Server address field with it; without it, with the address the administrator's browser is using. The administrator can change it, and the browser then checks that this LibreFolio answers there;
    • the command line: it puts it in front of the invitation and password-reset links it prints; without it, it prints the path only (/invite#token=…) and you add the address yourself;
    • the emails with a link, with no fallback to the browser's address: without it, no invitation email, no email with the password-reset link and no forgotten-password email (Email).

    An address that holds a user name or a password is refused: LibreFolio works as if it were not set.

Wrong value, two behaviours:

  • LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL do not stop the server, unlike the main options: LibreFolio stays on the safe side and writes an error to the log the first time each server process needs the value: Invalid account configuration, with the variable and its value in problem (an address that holds an @ is not shown: it may carry a user name or a password) and in consequence what it costs until you fix it:

    Wrong value What LibreFolio does consequence in the log LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION other than the three modes Registration is closed and the global setting stays locked registration stays closed until it is fixed LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL without http:// or https://, or with a user name or a password Ignored, as if it were not set: the command line prints the path only and says why under each link; the dialogs of the Users tab start from the browser's address; no email with a link and, while email works, the start log has a warning too (Email) links show the bare path until it is fixed

  • The other five stop the server at startup with a value other than those allowed in the table above (as an unusable value of the initial administrator does). The error is in the server's console output (docker compose logs librefolio with Docker) and names the variable and the value: LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT='yes': expected on or off, LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS='abc': expected a whole number of at least 1.

Fix the value, then restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

docs.title: 📏 When the Instance Is Full
docs.text:
When the active accounts, the pending invitations, the accounts waiting for their email verification and an initial administrator waiting for its setup reach LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS:

  • nobody can sign up without an invitation, whatever the Registration mode;
  • an invitation link already sent still works: its place was counted when it was created;
  • administrators cannot create invitations or reactivate accounts, except from the command line: user create, user invite and user activate print a warning, then go ahead. user activate prints none for an account that already holds its place: one waiting for its email verification while its link is live, or the initial administrator waiting for its setup.

A place frees up when an account is deactivated or deleted, when an invitation is revoked or expires, or when the link of an account waiting for its email verification expires (see Email Verification in Email). The first account of a new instance can always be created.

docs.title: 📉 When the Plan Gets Smaller
docs.text:
If the active accounts outnumber LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS — you lowered the limit and restarted, or you restored a backup with more users than the limit allows — the instance is over the limit. LibreFolio does not delete anybody: it asks an administrator to choose.

  • Who is concerned: only active > limit. With exactly as many active accounts as the limit, nothing happens. Invitations and accounts waiting for their verification take places but never start this state.
  • What everybody else sees until the choice is made: a message that an administrator has to choose who keeps the access. Nobody but an administrator enters, and the administrators see nothing but this choice.
  • A limit LibreFolio cannot read (LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS=abc, 0) never starts this state: the server does not start until you fix the value, so a typo cannot lock everybody out.

Where: in the app, as an administrator.

  1. Sign in. Before any other page, the list of the active accounts appears: you are checked and cannot be unchecked; each row says how many brokers the account owns alone (those brokers stay, but nobody else can reach them until the account is reactivated); a counter shows how many accounts are chosen against how many the limit allows.
  2. First of all, make the full backup: the same page offers it, so the data can be taken away before anybody is deactivated.
  3. Choose who keeps the access, then Deactivate the others and continue. The page says how many invitations it will cancel before you confirm.

Result: the accounts not chosen are deactivated, not deleted: they are signed out, cannot sign in and keep all their data; you can reactivate one when a place frees up (When the Instance Is Full). Pending invitations are cancelled, newest first, only as far as the chosen accounts need their places.

No special step is needed after a restore: the restored accounts are counted the same way.

docs.title: 🚦 Failed Sign-ins
docs.text:
When sign-ins keep failing, LibreFolio stops checking passwords for a while: nobody can try password after password until one works. The limit is on unless you turn it off.

Limit Past it 10 failed sign-ins every 15 minutes with the same username or email address, whether an account has it or not Every sign-in with that username or email address is refused, the right password included, until the oldest failure is 15 minutes old. 50 failed sign-ins every 15 minutes from the same address, whatever username or email address they use; an IPv6 address counts by its /64, the block one subscriber usually holds. Not counted are the sign-ins that come through a proxy LibreFolio does not trust, on a local address: see Behind a reverse proxy below Every sign-in from that address is refused, for any account, until the oldest failure is 15 minutes old.

What the user sees: the login page says Too many login attempts: wait a few minutes and try again. The wait is 15 minutes at most. The answer is the same whether an account exists or not: the limit does not reveal which accounts exist.

What counts as a failure:

  • a wrong password, or a username or email address that no account has;
  • a wrong current password in Change Password, or when a user changes their own email address in the Profile tab (Profile): it counts as a failed sign-in with the account's username, from the same address. So 10 wrong current passwords also block signing in with that username, and failed sign-ins with the username block those two checks: Change Password and the Profile tab then say Too many wrong passwords: wait a few minutes and try again. Deleting one's own account asks for no password: nothing to limit there;
  • a wrong password in Send the link again: on the login page, an account waiting for its email verification gets Send the link again, which checks the username or email address and the password as a sign-in does (Email Verification). It counts as a failed sign-in with what was typed, from the same address; past the limit, it is refused before the password is checked, and the page says in how many minutes to try again. The right password clears the failures of what was typed, as a successful sign-in does. Its own limits still apply (Limits of the Verification Emails).

What does not count:

  • the right password of a deactivated account, or of one still waiting for its email verification: neither a failure nor a success;
  • a sign-in the limit refuses: it is not counted and its password is not even checked, so trying again does not make the wait longer;
  • the invitation and password-reset links: their tokens are long random values nobody can guess, and a limit per address could refuse them to every user behind the same router. Forgot Password? asks for no password and has limits of its own: see Forgotten Passwords.

How they are counted:

  • a successful sign-in clears the failures of the username or email address it used, not those of the address it came from;
  • the username and the email address count apart, even for one account: someone guessing its password gets 10 tries with the username and 10 with the email address every 15 minutes, still within the 50 of their own address. Capitals A to Z do not matter: Alice and alice share one count;
  • kept in memory, by each server process: a restart forgets every count, which also lets a user who cannot wait back in at once. With several server processes (./dev.py server --workers N), each keeps its own counts, so the limits are N times these; the Docker image runs one.

Behind a reverse proxy, the address that counts is the visitor's, as LibreFolio reads it. Tell LibreFolio about your proxy, by listing it in FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS or by naming the header it sets in LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER: where and how, in The Visitor's Address. Until then, LibreFolio sees every visitor with the proxy's address, and what happens depends on where the proxy is:

Proxy LibreFolio does not trust What happens On a local address (a Docker network, your own network or your VPN), such as a proxy container in front of the Docker image, the usual setup LibreFolio leaves the sign-ins through it out of the limit per address, so that 50 failed sign-ins from anyone cannot refuse every sign-in. The limit per username or email address still counts them. The log has one warning per server process, the first time a request through such a proxy meets a limit per address: Requests come through a reverse proxy that LibreFolio does not trust: the limits per client address skip them. List the proxy in FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, or name the header it sets in LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER On a public address, such as a CDN Every visitor shares the proxy's address and its count: 50 failed sign-ins from anyone refuse every sign-in through the proxy, the right passwords included, for up to 15 minutes

Turning it off, for a test instance only, whose automated tests sign in wrongly on purpose: anyone can then try passwords without pause.

Where: in LibreFolio's .env.

  1. Add the line (case does not matter):

    LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT=off

  2. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

    Nothing is counted any more and nothing is refused. Every start logs a warning, with accounts.login_limit in check: LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT=off: failed sign-ins are not limited; turn it back on unless this is a test instance. The same check, on demand, is in the Security tab of Settings › Administration: a warning, counted in the number on the tab, until the limit is back on («Security» in Global Settings).

  3. To turn the limit back on, remove the variable or set it to on, then restart: it holds from the next start. Any other value stops the server at startup (Accounts and Sign-ups).

docs.title: 👑 The Initial Administrator
docs.text:
LibreFolio can create the administrator of a new instance by itself, at its first start, for the address you give it: nobody can register first and take its place. It is meant for installs made with a script or Docker Compose. Without these variables nothing changes, and the first account registered becomes the administrator (Who Can Sign Up).

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL not set The email address of the administrator. Setting it turns the initial administrator on. LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_USERNAME admin The administrator's username: 3 to 50 characters, without @, as at registration. LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN not set Optional: the token of the setup link, for a script that delivers the link itself. 32 to 200 characters, only letters, digits and - . _ ~, since it travels in a link: the output of openssl rand -hex 32, for example. LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE reads it from a file instead: see Secrets. Not set: LibreFolio generates the token.

An empty value counts as not set. Spaces around the email and the username do not matter; the token is used exactly as written, so a space in it, even at the end, makes it unusable.

Where: in LibreFolio's .env, before the instance's first start.

  1. Set the administrator's address; the username and the token only if you do not want the generated ones:

    LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
# LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
# LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=

  2. Start LibreFolio. At the first start of an instance without any account, LibreFolio:

    1. creates the administrator, not yet active, with a random password nobody knows: nobody can sign in with it yet;
    2. sets the Registration global setting to By invitation; LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION, when set, still decides;
    3. issues a setup link, /setup#token=…, that works once, for 72 hours.

  3. Hand the link over to the administrator. Who hands it over depends on the token:

    • With LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN, whoever chose it: the link is the instance's address followed by /setup#token= and the token. LibreFolio neither logs it nor emails it.
    • Without it, LibreFolio generates the token and hands the link over itself:
      • it writes the link once in its log, as a warning: Setup link of the initial administrator, single use: open it to choose the password, with the link in link (with Docker: docker compose logs librefolio). The link is the full address when LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is set; otherwise it is the path, and note asks you to put the address of your server in front of it;
      • it emails the link to LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL when email works, that is with an SMTP server set up (Email) and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL set. The email is in the instance's default language and goes out once the server is up, so a slow mail server never delays the start. If it cannot be sent, the log has Setup link of the initial administrator not emailed, with the reason, and the link in the log still works.

  4. The administrator opens the link: the instance's setup page, where they choose the password and sign in. From then on the variables create nothing more: each start logs LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_* ignored: this instance already has accounts, as on an instance that already has accounts and no administrator waiting.

While the administrator waits: nobody can register as the first account, and the administrator takes a place of LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS. A restart issues nothing new and does not write the link in the log again.

When no link works any more, each start logs a warning:

Warning in the log When The initial administrator's setup link has expired: run ./dev.py user setup-link… The link has expired The initial administrator's setup link was withdrawn (cancelled, or its address changed): run ./dev.py user setup-link… The link was cancelled or the administrator's address changed

That command prints a new link (A New Setup Link). A new value of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN also gives a new link, at the next start.

Unusable value: stops the server at startup, on any instance, one that already has accounts included:

  • LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_USERNAME or LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN set without LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL;
  • an email that is not an address;
  • a username shorter than 3 or longer than 50 characters, or with an @ in it: the sign-in reads a name with @ as an email address, and the administrator signs in with the address of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL anyway;
  • a token shorter than 32 or longer than 200 characters, or with a character other than letters, digits and - . _ ~, a space included;
  • a LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE that cannot give the token (Secrets in Files).

The error is in the server's console output (docker compose logs librefolio with Docker): it names the variable, never the token. Fix the value, then start again.

docs.title: 🥇 The Order of the Price Providers in the Search
docs.text:
When you create an asset, the search asks every price provider at once and lists the results provider by provider. Each provider declares its tier, premium (a source an instance vouches for, such as licensed data) or community (the default), and its priority inside the tier. The results of the premium providers come first. None of the providers shipped with LibreFolio is premium, so without one the search keeps its order.

Where: in LibreFolio's .env. No restart: LibreFolio reads them at every search, and they apply to the next search.

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_ASSET_PROVIDERS_PREMIUM not set The providers to count as premium, by code, separated by commas, such as yfinance,justetf: exactly these, whatever they declare. Not set: what each provider declares. LIBREFOLIO_ASSET_PROVIDERS_ORDER not set The providers to list first, in this order, by code, separated by commas; the others follow in their declared order. Premium providers still come before the others. Not set: what each provider declares.
  • The codes of the providers shipped with LibreFolio are yfinance, justetf, borsa_italiana, css_scraper and scheduled_investment; a provider you add has its own. Case and spaces around the codes do not matter.
  • A code that no provider has is ignored, and the server logs it once.

docs.title: 🔎 Optional: Web Search for New Assets
docs.text:
When you create an asset, also from the broker import wizard, and a provider's own search finds nothing, LibreFolio can find the asset's page with a web search through the ddgs library. It is on by default and never used for price updates.

Where: in LibreFolio's .env: uncomment a line of .env.example to change one. All optional. Then restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

Variable Default What it does LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_ENABLED 1 0 turns the web search off; the providers' own search keeps working. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_ENGINE ddgs ddgs needs no setup. apikey is reserved for a paid search service and returns no results yet. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_DDGS_REGION wt-wt Search region. wt-wt (worldwide) keeps national sites such as Borsa Italiana from being pushed down. Examples: it-it, us-en. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_DDGS_BACKEND auto Engines that ddgs queries: auto rotates them for the widest coverage; a list such as google,bing,duckduckgo gives steadier results. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_TIMEOUT 6 Time limit of one search, in seconds: at least 1. Any other value means the default. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_MAX 5 Most links returned by one search: a whole number, at least 1. Any other value means the default. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_API_KEY empty Key for the apikey engine. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_API_KEY_FILE reads it from a file instead: see Secrets. 🔁 Results change between attempts — when a known asset is sometimes not found

With auto, each search may reach different engines, so the same query can do better or worse from one try to the next. Retry once, or set LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_DDGS_BACKEND=google,bing,duckduckgo.
