docs.title: 🐳 Advanced Docker Guide
docs.text:
For those who customize the Docker deployment, build their own image or run maintenance on the container. For a first installation, start from the Installation guide.

Two Compose files:

File Image it runs docker-compose.prod.yml The official image from GHCR. The installation guide saves it as docker-compose.yml. docker-compose.yml, in the repository An image you build yourself with ./dev.py docker build.

Where the commands of this page are run:

Command Where docker compose … On the host, in the folder that holds docker-compose.yml and .env. No checkout needed. ./dev.py docker … On the host, in the root of a checkout of the repository. ./dev.py docker exec <cmd> From the checkout; the command runs inside the running container (details). docker compose run --rm librefolio … In the folder of docker-compose.yml, with the server stopped: a one-off container (fixes).

docs.title: ⚠️ Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Docker group (Linux), to use Docker without sudo. On the host:

    sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

    Then log out and back in, or run newgrp docker. Without it, every docker and docker compose fails with a permission error.

  2. .env file, next to the Compose file. ./dev.py docker build refuses to proceed without it. In a checkout:

    cp .env.example .env
$EDITOR .env          # review and customize parameters

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text: The image is runtime-only: the web app (SvelteKit) and the documentation (MkDocs) are built on the host and copied into it; ./dev.py docker build does it for you. Build stages, contents and startup: Architecture overview → Docker image.

docs.title: 📄 docker-compose.yml
docs.text: It defines the librefolio service and its persistent data directory.

docs.title: 🔝 Resolution Priority
docs.text:
From lowest to highest:

graph LR
    CodeDefaults[1. Code Defaults] --> EnvFile[2. .env File]
    HostShell[3. Host Env Variables]
    DockerCompose[4. docker-compose.yml environment block]

    EnvFile --> HostShell
    HostShell --> DockerCompose

.env reaches the container through env_file; the environment: block overrides it. For the ${…} placeholders of the Compose file, such as ${PORT:-6040}, a variable of your shell wins over .env.

docs.title: 🔧 Service: librefolio
docs.text:
Key Value Good to know 🏷️ image ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:latest (production file) or your local librefolio:latest (repository file) LIBREFOLIO_IMAGE in .env picks another tag 🏗️ build Repository file only: builds the Dockerfile in the root Arguments UID, GID and DOCS_VARIANT 🔌 ports host ${PORT:-6040} → container 6040 PORT chooses the host side; inside the container the server always listens on 6040, the only port of the image 📂 volumes bind mount ./LibreFolio-data → /app/backend/data/prod-docker 📝 env_file: .env Your configuration (copied from .env.example) 🌍 environment LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR (path in the container), HOST=0.0.0.0, PORT=6040 Leave them as they are. PORT=6040 replaces the host port of your .env: the dev.py commands in the container (docker exec) look for the server on the right port, and db upgrade sees it running and refuses to start 🩺 healthcheck GET /api/v1/system/health every 30 seconds It only tells Docker that the server answers

📈 Monitoring LibreFolio: /api/v1/system/ready

Point a monitor such as Uptime Kuma or an orchestrator at GET /api/v1/system/ready, for example http://your-server:6040/api/v1/system/ready (with your PORT). No sign-in needed; the status code is enough:

  • 200: ready. {"status": "ready", "checks": {"database": "ok", "migrations": "ok"}, "database_revision": "…", "mode": "normal", "app_version": "…"}. database_revision: the migration of the database; app_version: the running version, the same as the public GET /api/v1/system/info, so a monitor checks the version after an update.

  • 503: not ready. status is not_ready; checks shows what is not ok:

    Check Value Meaning database unreachable The database does not answer migrations behind The database is at an older migration: one was not applied, or failed migrations ahead The database is at a migration this version does not know: the data comes from a newer LibreFolio. Use that version or a newer one: Never Backwards migrations unknown It cannot tell, for example while the database is unreachable

The answer never includes details or paths: LibreFolio writes them to its own log (docker compose logs librefolio) as Instance not ready, once for each change of state. db current shows the migration of the database (Apply Migrations).

docs.title: 💾 Data Directory: LibreFolio-data/
docs.text: Bind mount next to the Compose file: SQLite database, custom uploads, broker reports, logs. It survives container stop, restart and removal; you back it up straight from the host.

docs.title: 👤 User and Permissions
docs.text:
The container starts as root only to hand all of LibreFolio-data/ over to the LibreFolio user, at every start; then it runs the server as that non-root user: on the host the files belong to its UID/GID. ./dev.py docker exec uses the same UID/GID (details).

The UID/GID comes from the build arguments UID and GID, kept in the image as LIBREFOLIO_UID and LIBREFOLIO_GID and read by the entrypoint at every start.

Image UID/GID Official on GHCR 1000:1000. The two .env lines below have no effect. ./dev.py docker build The ids of the user who runs it, whatever .env says. docker compose build UID and GID read from .env (default 1000).

To match the ids to the host user, or the dedicated user, that must own the data, in .env:

UID=1000
GID=1000

They take effect only when docker compose build rebuilds the image: .env also reaches the container through env_file, but a restart does not change the ids.

  • On the host, ls -l LibreFolio-data/ shows the user and group of that UID/GID according to the host's /etc/passwd and /etc/group.
  • Inside the container, the same files usually show as librefolio:librefolio: the same numeric UID/GID, resolved with the container's /etc/passwd and /etc/group.
Linux reminder: users, groups and IDs

All commands: on the host.

Your UID and GID:

id -u              # your user ID (e.g. 1000)
id -g              # your primary group ID (e.g. 1000)
id                 # full info: uid, gid, groups

UID/GID of another user:

id -u username     # UID of 'username'
id -g username     # primary GID of 'username'

A new group:

sudo groupadd librefolio          # create group (auto-assigns GID)
sudo groupadd -g 1500 librefolio  # create group with specific GID

A new user:

# System user (no home, no login — ideal for services)
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --gid librefolio --shell /usr/sbin/nologin librefolio

# Regular user with home directory
sudo useradd -m -g librefolio librefolio

The assigned ids:

id librefolio
# → uid=998(librefolio) gid=998(librefolio) groups=998(librefolio)

Your user in a group:

sudo usermod -aG librefolio $USER
newgrp librefolio    # activate in current session (or log out/in)

Checking membership:

groups $USER         # list all groups for your user

Ownership of the data directory:

sudo chown -R librefolio:librefolio ./LibreFolio-data

Then put the matching UID/GID in .env and rebuild with docker compose build: at every start the container hands the directory back to the image's UID/GID.

docs.title: 🛠️ CLI Commands
docs.text:
Where: root of a checkout of the repository. dev.py wraps the Docker operations:

./dev.py docker build          # Build image (auto-builds frontend + docs)
./dev.py docker build --light  # Light variant: no documentation screenshots (tagged *-light)
./dev.py docker build --no-cache  # Full rebuild without Docker cache
./dev.py docker rebuild        # Build → stop → restart (one-step deploy)
./dev.py docker up             # Start containers
./dev.py docker down           # Stop containers
./dev.py docker logs -f        # Follow container logs
./dev.py docker status         # Show container status
./dev.py docker exec <cmd>     # Run a dev.py command inside the container

Without a checkout, in the folder of docker-compose.yml, the day-to-day work:

Action Command Start docker compose up -d Stop docker compose down Follow the log docker compose logs -f Container status docker compose ps

Image variants:

  • --light builds the image without the documentation screenshots, which then load from the online site (Image Variants).
  • Local tags: librefolio:<version> and librefolio:latest for the full image, librefolio:<version>-light and librefolio:latest-light for the light one; <version> is the git version of the checkout. On the registry, instead, latest is the light variant and latest-light does not exist.
  • To run your light build with the repository's Compose file, in .env: LIBREFOLIO_IMAGE=librefolio:latest-light.
🧱 When ./dev.py docker build stops

A resource cannot be downloaded. The build caches external resources (the Noto Color Emoji font for flags on Windows, MathJax for formulas, Mermaid for diagrams) so that the image works offline. If one is missing and there is no cached copy, the build stops:

❌ Resource cache incomplete — the build would ship without these:
   - noto-color-emoji: ...

The first build requires internet (or a pre-warmed cache). With the network back, run the build again; ./dev.py cache js refreshes the cache by hand (--force re-downloads everything).

The frontend is a debug build. The image must contain the production build of the web app. ./dev.py docker build rebuilds frontend/build/ in production when the last build was a debug one (./dev.py server --test, ./dev.py server --debug, test runner), when the sources have changed or when it was not built for this version (details). docker build or docker compose build skip that step: with frontend/build/ in debug or instrumented for coverage, the build stops:

ERROR: /build is not a production frontend build: it is a debug build (.build-debug = 1)
Rebuild it with './dev.py front build', then build the image again.

Run ./dev.py front build, then build the image again; or build with ./dev.py docker build.

🖼️ Building a full image with the documentation screenshots

A full image contains the screenshots only if they were generated, and the documentation rebuilt with them, before the build: otherwise a local full image and a light one are the same apart from the tag. In the checkout:

./dev.py mkdocs gallery   # generate the screenshots
./dev.py mkdocs build     # rebuild the documentation with the screenshots
./dev.py docker build     # build the full image; it rebuilds for production the debug frontend the gallery leaves

./dev.py mkdocs gallery requires a complete environment (pipenv) and the Playwright browsers. It starts its own test server and populates the test database (--no-populate skips reseeding). It takes a few minutes.

docs.title: 📡 docker exec — Running Commands Inside the Container
docs.text:
Where: from the checkout; the command runs in the running container, as the server's user: the numeric LIBREFOLIO_UID:LIBREFOLIO_GID of the image (User and Permissions, above), not root. Files created in LibreFolio-data/ belong to that user straight away. For example:

./dev.py docker exec user create admin admin@example.com Pass123!
./dev.py docker exec user list

Without a checkout, in the folder of docker-compose.yml, ./dev.py docker exec user list is the same as this line (gosu, also used by the entrypoint, switches to the image's ids before dev.py starts):

docker compose exec librefolio sh -c 'exec gosu "${LIBREFOLIO_UID:-1000}:${LIBREFOLIO_GID:-1000}" python dev.py "$@"' sh user list

A plain docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py <cmd> runs as root: what it creates in LibreFolio-data/ belongs to root until the next start, when the entrypoint hands the directory back to the image's user.

Command In the image user, db, info, backup They work (Back Up with Docker) test, i18n, mkdocs translate, mkdocs translate-validate Listed, but they only answer that they are not available in this installation: the image contains the application, not the development tree ./dev.py docker exec test db populate The same not available answer as every test command ./dev.py docker exec server --test Stops with Frontend build failed. Server not started.: test mode rebuilds the web app in debug, which needs Node.js and the sources; the image has only the production build, without Node.js. Like ./dev.py mkdocs gallery, it belongs to a development checkout

Database migrations need no command. The server applies the pending ones at every start: after docker compose pull and docker compose up -d there is nothing else to do; docker compose restart librefolio retries them after a failure. The restart does not help when the upgrade to 1.3 stops because two accounts have the same email address apart from capitals: separate the two accounts first, as «Two Accounts with the Same Email Address» in Command-Line Tools explains. Do not use ./dev.py docker exec db upgrade: db upgrade needs the server stopped, and in the container the server is the main process, always running.

docs.title: 🩹 Post-Migration Fixes
docs.text:
At every start, right after the pending migrations, the server runs the post-migration fixes: repairs that a migration cannot make. What they repair and what the log says: Command-Line Tools → Post-Migration Fixes. In Docker:

  • the log is the container output (./dev.py docker logs or docker compose logs), also saved in LibreFolio-data/logs/;
  • the copy kept by a failed fix sits next to the database, in LibreFolio-data/sqlite/, for example app.db.pre-autoincrement-20261008T101500Z.bak.

docs.title: ⏹️ Running the Fixes with the Server Stopped
docs.text:
To preview the fixes, or to retry one that failed at startup and read its error. docker exec needs the running container: docker compose run replaces the server with your command instead, in a one-off container.

Where: folder of docker-compose.yml. Always preview with --dry-run first:

docker compose stop librefolio
docker compose run --rm librefolio python -m backend.app.db.post_migration --dry-run   # preview: changes nothing
docker compose run --rm librefolio python -m backend.app.db.post_migration             # apply the fixes
docker compose start librefolio

Result: the script works on the same database and data directory as the server and reports what it finds:

Database: /app/backend/data/prod-docker/sqlite/app.db
Integrity check: ok
Fix autoincrement: would_apply
Orphan broker folder: broker_reports/uploaded/broker_7

Each fix is clean (nothing to do), would_apply (dry run), applied or failed; it also lists a kept backup, the errors and each transfer of securities sent to a deleted broker, with the cost it takes or the reason it stays as it is (details). Exit code 0 when nothing failed, dry run included; 1 if a fix, the integrity check or the conversion of those transfers failed.

docs.title: 🧪 Test Mode
docs.text:
The image has no test mode: it listens only on 6040, the production server, and both Compose files publish only that port. The test server (./dev.py server --test, port 6041 by default) is a developer tool: on the host, from a source checkout. Its database, backend/data/test/sqlite/app.db by default, is separate from LibreFolio-data/; ./dev.py test db populate --force deletes and recreates it with mock data.

How to start it, and why it does not start in the container: Developer Workflow.

docs.title: 🎮 1. Customizing docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
The most common changes. After (2)–(5), restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

# What Where and how (1) Match the host UID/GID Rebuild the image with them: ./dev.py docker build as the user who must own the files, or UID=1001 and GID=1001 in .env and then docker compose build (2) Change the production port In .env: PORT=3000 (3) Custom data path In docker-compose.yml, the bind mount: ./my-data:/app/backend/data/prod-docker (4) All configuration In .env (copied from .env.example) (5) Run another image tag In .env: LIBREFOLIO_IMAGE, for example LIBREFOLIO_IMAGE=ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:1.1.0

The first account created in the browser becomes the administrator: no command. To have LibreFolio create it at the first start, from LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL: The Initial Administrator.

📄 The repository's docker-compose.yml, annotated 
services:
  librefolio:
    image: ${LIBREFOLIO_IMAGE:-librefolio:latest}  # (5) Built by ./dev.py docker build
    build:
      context: .
      args:
        UID: ${UID:-1000}              # (1) UID owning the data files (build time only)
        GID: ${GID:-1000}              # (1) GID owning the data files (build time only)
        DOCS_VARIANT: ${DOCS_VARIANT:-full}  # light = no documentation screenshots
    container_name: librefolio
    # No 'user:' directive — entrypoint starts as root, fixes permissions,
    # then drops to the numeric LIBREFOLIO_UID:LIBREFOLIO_GID via gosu, like ./dev.py docker exec.
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-6040}:6040"           # (2) Production port — change via PORT in .env
    volumes:
      - ./LibreFolio-data:/app/backend/data/prod-docker  # (3) Persistent data (bind mount)
    env_file: .env                     # (4) All config from .env file
    environment:
      - LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR=/app/backend/data/prod-docker  # Docker-specific override
      - HOST=0.0.0.0
      - PORT=6040                      # The container's port; (2) sets the host side
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:6040/api/v1/system/health')"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      start_period: 15s
      retries: 3

docker-compose.prod.yml has the same service without build:; its default image is ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:latest.

docs.title: 🔒 2. Security and Exposure (Tailscale and Reverse Proxy)
docs.text:
Way When Guide Tailscale (recommended, the simplest) Automatic HTTPS, without router ports or public DNS Tailscale Exposure Guide Classic reverse proxy (Nginx, Traefik) You already have a web infrastructure, SSL/TLS certificates of your own, several applications on one server, custom security headers or rate limiting Below

Once exposed, Checking Connection Security shows how to check that users connect securely and, behind a reverse proxy, that the session cookie is Secure.

Behind a classic reverse proxy, in .env also say which proxy to trust (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS) or which header holds the visitor's address (LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER): otherwise LibreFolio sees every visitor with the proxy's address, and reports it in the log and in the security checks. See The Visitor's Address.

In the proxy configuration, do not compress again: LibreFolio already compresses with gzip (API JSON, JavaScript and CSS, documentation pages) and sends images and the live stream of the asset search as they are.

docs.title: 💾 3. Database Backup
docs.text:
The database is in LibreFolio-data/ next to docker-compose.yml: a bind mount readable from the host, no docker cp.

Do not copy app.db from a running container

SQLite runs in WAL mode (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL): recent transactions are in app.db-wal, so a cp of app.db alone with the server up can give an inconsistent or stale backup. Use one of the procedures below.

Where: on the host, folder of docker-compose.yml.

Option A — Stop the container, then copy (the simplest):

#!/bin/bash
docker compose stop librefolio
cp ./LibreFolio-data/sqlite/app.db /path/to/backups/app.db-$(date +%F)
docker compose start librefolio

Option B — Online backup with the SQLite CLI (no downtime; requires sqlite3 on the host):

#!/bin/bash
sqlite3 ./LibreFolio-data/sqlite/app.db ".backup '/path/to/backups/app.db-$(date +%F)'"

.backup uses SQLite's online backup API, safe with a live WAL database.

Option C — backup create, without a stop or sqlite3 on the host. Inside the container, from the folder of docker-compose.yml:

docker compose exec librefolio python dev.py backup create

Result: a consistent copy of the database, uploaded files, broker reports and stress scenarios in one archive, in its own folder of LibreFolio-data/backups/, with the server running (Back Up with Docker). A clear archive leaves out secrets/, which holds the instance key: back that folder up as What to Back Up explains. A secure archive, with --encrypt, contains the key, encrypted with your password.

Full list of what is worth backing up (uploaded files, original broker reports): Filesystem Layout.

Files you may find next to the database:

File What to do app.db.pre-<fix>-<UTC time>.bak Copy kept by a failed post-migration fix: delete it when you no longer need it app.db.post-migration.lock Empty lock file of the post-migration fixes, reused at every start. Leave it: deleting it while the server starts could let two runs overlap

docs.title: 🔑 4. Environment Variables
docs.text:
All configuration is in .env (copied from .env.example); leave the Docker variables of the environment: block as they are. Every variable and its effect: Configuration Guide.

🔐 Users signed in across restarts. In .env, JWT_SECRET to a long random string, for example the output of openssl rand -hex 32:

JWT_SECRET=<output of openssl rand -hex 32>

Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d. Without it, LibreFolio generates a new key at every start: every restart or update of the container signs everyone out.

docs.title: ✅ 5. Verify the Image You Pull
docs.text:
Every image on GHCR (ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio, full and light) has a build attestation, signed by the release pipeline of the project's repository: this exact image was built there from this code. No key of ours to keep or lose (GitHub proves the identity of the run, Sigstore records it): anyone can verify it.

Where: where you have Docker and the GitHub CLI.

  1. Take the digest of the image you pulled:

    # The digest of a tag (the line "Digest: sha256:…")
docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:1.3.0

  2. Ask GitHub to verify it:

    # Verify the attestation of that digest
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio@sha256:<digest> --owner Librefolio

    Result: ✓ Verification succeeded! with the repository and the workflow that built it. Only an error → this digest does not come from LibreFolio's pipeline: do not run it.

The attestation covers every tag that points to the same digest (1.3.0, latest...). Releases before this check have none.

docs.title: 📧 Email
docs.text:
LibreFolio sends email through an SMTP server that you name in a few environment variables. Email is optional: without it nothing changes, nothing is sent, and the invitation and password-reset links are copied by hand.

What LibreFolio sends:

  • A test email, which an administrator sends to their own address from Settings › Administration › Email.
  • The invitation and password-reset links created by an administrator, with Send by email in their dialogs: Links Sent by an Administrator.
  • A reset link for a forgotten password, to whoever asks for one from the login page: Forgotten Passwords.
  • The setup link of the initial administrator, once, when LibreFolio creates that administrator from LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL and generates the link itself: The Initial Administrator.
  • A link to confirm the email address of a new account, when Require Email Verification is on: Email Verification.
  • A notice to the old address and a confirmation to the new one when someone changes the email address of their account: Email Address Changes.

The emails with a link also need LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL: Emails with a Link.

To set email up:

  1. In LibreFolio's .env, section # Email: write the LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* variables, at least the server and the sender, plus the login when the server asks for one. Copy the example of your case.
  2. In the same .env, for the emails with a link: LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (Emails with a Link).
  3. From a terminal: restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.
  4. In LibreFolio, Settings › Administration › Email: the state reads Ready. Send yourself a test email.

📚 This guide is split into several pages

This page sets email up: the variables, examples for the usual servers, the Email tab of Settings and its test email. The rest of the guide:

  • Email: Links and Messages: the emails with a link, forgotten passwords, their limits, email verification and the notice of an address change.
  • Email: When It Does Not Work: the errors, what the log says and the security notes of the SMTP setup.

docs.title: 🔐 Where the Configuration Lives
docs.text:
From environment variables only, written in .env like the other options: ./dev.py and Docker Compose (env_file: .env) pass them to the server. The password also in a secret file.

  • Never stored. It is not in the database, and a backup of LibreFolio does not contain it: keep your own copy of .env and of the password file.
  • Never shown. No page of the interface shows the server, the port, the user, the sender or the password. Settings › Administration › Email says whether email works and, if not, which variable to fix; of the LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* values, it shows only the hourly limit.
  • Public: only whether email is ready. /api/v1/system/instance, readable by anyone who reaches the server, says "available": true when the state is Ready and "links": true when, on top of that, the emails can carry a link (Emails with a Link). Nothing else.
  • Restart after a change. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

To turn email off: in .env remove LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST or leave it empty, then restart. The other variables can stay: without a server, LibreFolio ignores them.

docs.title: 📋 The Variables
docs.text:
In .env, section # Email. .env.example lists them, commented: copy the lines you need.

Variable Default Accepted values LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST not set: email off The SMTP server: a host name, such as smtp.example.com, or an IP address, and nothing else: no smtp://, no user@, no :587, no path. An IPv6 address without square brackets, such as fd00::25. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS starttls starttls, tls or none, in capitals or not: Encryption Modes. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT 587 with starttls, 465 with tls, 25 with none A whole number from 1 to 65535. Set it only if the server uses a port other than the one of its mode. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER not set: no login The login of your account on the SMTP server. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD not set The password of that login, used exactly as written, spaces included. Or LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE: the path of a file that holds it. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM required with a server The sender: an address, with or without a name, such as LibreFolio <noreply@example.com> or noreply@example.com. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_REPLY_TO not set: replies go to the sender The address replies go to. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR 50 How many emails LibreFolio may send in an hour, per server process: a whole number, at least 1. LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS 20 How many registration emails one client address may trigger in an hour, per server process: a whole number, at least 1. Past the limit, new accounts are created and wait, but their emails are held: Limits of the Verification Emails. Not an SMTP variable (its name does not start with LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_), but it is checked with them and read only when a server is set.
  • Empty is the same as not set: an empty value, or one of spaces only, counts as not set.
  • The login comes in pairs: LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER together with a password, or neither of them for a server that takes mail without a login.
  • The password in a file: LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE follows Secrets in Files. The password is the text of the file as it is, whatever characters it holds, without the line breaks at its end. Set only one of the two: if both are set, LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD wins, the file is ignored and the startup log has a warning. Unlike JWT_SECRET_FILE, a password file that cannot be read does not stop the server: email stays off until it is fixed.
  • The hourly limits count per server process, over the last 60 minutes, in memory: LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR and LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS alike. A restart starts again from zero. ./dev.py server --workers 4 runs four processes, each with its own count: the instance can send up to four times the limit (Start the Server). The Docker image runs a single process.

docs.title: 🔑 Encryption Modes
docs.text:
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS What it does Usual port starttls (default) Connects, then switches to encryption before sending anything. A server that does not offer it is refused: nothing goes out in clear. 587 tls Encrypted from the first byte, also called SSL/TLS or SMTPS. 465 none No encryption: messages, links and password travel in clear. Only for a relay on the same machine or on your local network. 25
  • With starttls and tls, LibreFolio checks the server's certificate: it must be valid and issued for the name in LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST. Write the name the certificate is issued for, usually not the IP address.
  • The port follows the mode, not the other way around: LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT=465 alone keeps starttls, which a server on port 465 does not expect. For port 465, set LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=tls.

docs.title: 💡 Examples
docs.text:
In LibreFolio's .env, in the section that starts with # Email: this version's .env.example has it. If your .env is old and has no such section, add the block of the example at its end. Replace smtp.example.com, the addresses and the password with your own, then restart LibreFolio.

Docker Compose + secret fileMail providerGmailLocal relay

The password stays out of .env and out of the container's environment, in a Docker secret.

  1. In a file next to docker-compose.yml, such as smtp_password.txt: save the password. A line break at its end does not count; spaces do.

  2. From a terminal, in the same folder: the container sees the file with the owner and permissions it has on the host, so make it readable by the user that runs LibreFolio. With the official image it is 1000:1000:

    sudo chown 1000:1000 smtp_password.txt
sudo chmod 600 smtp_password.txt

    An image you built yourself may use other ids: put them in the chown command (Advanced Docker).

  3. In docker-compose.yml: add the marked lines and leave the rest of the service as it is. If the file already has secrets: lists, such as the JWT_SECRET_FILE example of Secrets, add the new lines to those lists:

    services:
  librefolio:
    secrets:                         # added
      - smtp_password                # added
secrets:                             # added
  smtp_password:                     # added
    file: ./smtp_password.txt        # added

  4. In .env: add the variables. If there is a LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD line with a value, remove it: it would win over the file.

    LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER=noreply@example.com
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/smtp_password
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM=LibreFolio <noreply@example.com>

    No LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS and no port: starttls on port 587 is the default.

  5. From a terminal: run docker compose up -d. The state in Settings › Administration › Email reads Ready.

Your account on the SMTP server of a mail provider.

  1. In .env, section # Email:

    LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER=you@example.com
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD=your-app-password
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM=LibreFolio <you@example.com>
    • That is starttls on port 587, the defaults. If the provider gives port 465, add LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=tls: the port follows.
    • Use an app password, not the password you sign in with: the provider creates it for a single application and you can revoke it without touching your account.
    • The provider's help pages give the server name, the port and the encryption, and which sender addresses your account may use.
    • Better still, keep the password in a file, as in the Docker Compose tab.

  2. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d. The state in Settings › Administration › Email reads Ready.

Your Gmail account, or a Google Workspace one, through Gmail's SMTP server. LibreFolio signs in only with a user and a password, not with «Sign in with Google»: you need an app password, not the password of your Google Account.

  1. In your Google Account: turn on 2-Step Verification, if it is not on yet. App passwords exist only with it.
  2. On myaccount.google.com/apppasswords: create an app password, with a name such as LibreFolio. Google shows it as a code of 16 characters, in four groups of four: copy it. If the page offers no way to create one, Google's help page says why. A work or school account may need its administrator.

  3. In .env, section Email, or at its end if your .env has none:

    # =============================================================================
# Email config gmail
# =============================================================================
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER=you@gmail.com
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD=abcdefghijklmnop
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM=LibreFolio <you@gmail.com>
    • you@gmail.com stands for your full Gmail address, or your work one with Google Workspace.
    • abcdefghijklmnop stands for the app password: its 16 characters without the spaces, because LibreFolio uses the password exactly as written, spaces included. Better still, keep it in a password file as in the Docker Compose tab, without the spaces there too.
    • Spaces are fine in the sender, not in the password.
    • The sender is the same address, with or without a name in front. Gmail sends only from your address, or from one you added and confirmed under Send mail as in Gmail's settings.
    • No LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS and no port: starttls on port 587 is the default and one of Gmail's two modes. For the other, port 465, add LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=tls: the port follows.

  4. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

  5. In LibreFolio, Settings › Administration › Email: the state reads Ready. Click Send a test email: it goes to the address of your account (The Test Email).

To keep it working:

  • A personal Gmail account sends about 500 emails a day: past that, Gmail refuses for a period of 1 to 24 hours. A Google Workspace account has 2,000 a day through smtp.gmail.com. These are Google's limits, and Google can change them. When Gmail refuses, the test email and the log report the refusal (Sending Errors).
  • LibreFolio's limit is 50 emails an hour by default: up to 1,200 in a day. To stay under the personal limit, in .env add LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR=20, that is 480 a day, and restart. The count is per server process: The Variables.
  • Google revokes app passwords when you change the password of your Google Account: create a new one, write it in place of the old one in .env and restart. Removing the app password, on the page where you created it, also stops LibreFolio from sending.

A relay such as Postfix, on the same machine or on your network, takes mail without a login and delivers it for LibreFolio. Three cases; in each one the variables go in .env, section # Email, then restart.

LibreFolio on the host, relay on the same machine:

LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST=localhost
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=none
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM=LibreFolio <noreply@example.com>

LibreFolio in Docker, relay in another container on the same Docker network, here a Compose service called smtp-relay:

LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST=smtp-relay
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=none
LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM=LibreFolio <noreply@example.com>

LibreFolio in Docker, relay on the host: inside a container, localhost is the container, not the host.

  1. In docker-compose.yml: add the marked lines.

    services:
  librefolio:
    extra_hosts:                                # added
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"     # added

  2. In .env: LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST=host.docker.internal, with LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=none and the sender as above.

  3. In the relay: let it accept mail from the Docker network (in Postfix: inet_interfaces and mynetworks).

In every case:

  • Port 25 is the default with none: set LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT only if the relay listens on another one.
  • No user and no password: a relay without login does not ask for them.
  • The relay delivers the mail: it must be allowed to send for the domain of LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM.
  • none sends in clear: use it only towards your own machine or your own network. Towards any other server, Settings › Administration › Email and the startup log show a warning.

docs.title: 🖥️ Settings › Administration › Email
docs.text: In LibreFolio: Settings (gear icon in the sidebar) › Administration › the Email tab, after Backup (on a phone: the shield icon, then the envelope icon). Only administrators see it. The book icon at the top opens this page.

docs.title: 🚦 The State
docs.text:
State What it means What the tab shows Off LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST is not set: nothing is sent. This is the default. A short explanation and a pointer to this guide. Ready Every variable can be used. The emails left this hour, the notices that apply, the address the emailed links start with and its check, and Send a test email. Not working A variable cannot be used: email stays off until it is fixed. The problem, with the name of the variable at fault, and a reminder to restart after the fix.

✅ Ready does not mean an email has already been delivered

Ready means that every variable can be used. LibreFolio does not contact the server until it sends an email: only a test email proves that the server takes your mail.

  • Not working names one problem at a time, the first it finds: fix it in .env, restart, then check again. Configuration Problems says what to check for each one.
  • With Ready, the tab counts the emails left, for example 48 of 50 emails left this hour: the last 60 minutes, not the clock hour. When none is left, it says in how many minutes the next one can go. With several server processes, each one counts its own: the tab shows the count of the process that answered.
  • The encryption warning appears when LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=none points to a server outside your local network: Security Notes.
  • A notice about LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL appears when it is not set (information: emails work, but no email with a link can go out) or cannot be used as the base of a link (warning): Emails with a Link.

docs.title: 🧭 The Address in Emailed Links
docs.text:
With the state Ready and a usable LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, the tab shows Links in emails start with …, followed by that address, and checks from this browser that this instance answers there. It is the same signed check as the invitation and reset dialogs (The Server Address of a Link).

Message What it means Checking from this device that this instance answers there… The check is running. This instance answers there, from this device. Fine: the links reach this LibreFolio instance, at least from here. From this device, another server answers at that address, not this instance. … Something answers there, but not this LibreFolio instance. This device cannot reach this instance at that address. … No answer that this browser could read: a wrong or closed address, a name this device does not resolve, no answer within 8 seconds, a browser that blocks a public page from reaching a local address or asks your permission first, or an older version of LibreFolio that cannot answer the check. This page uses https:// while LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL starts with http:// … This browser cannot check an http:// address from an https:// page, and the links in emails would travel unencrypted: set the variable to the https:// address. This browser cannot read LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL as an address … The browser reads addresses a little more strictly than the server: the links may not open. Check the value.

📱 This device only

The check runs from the browser you are using, so it says what this device sees. A VPN, a direct IP address, its DNS or its network can differ from your users': after a warning, check from another device before changing the variable. Check again repeats the check, for example after you changed network.

  • The check runs once when the tab opens, not after each test email. Check again appears with a warning.
  • Nothing is checked with the state Off or Not working, nor when LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set or cannot be used, which the notice above reports.

docs.title: ✉️ The Test Email
docs.text:
In LibreFolio, Settings › Administration › Email, with the state Ready: Send a test email sends an email to yourself.

  • To your address: the email of your account, as in Profile. There is no field to type another one.
  • In your language: the one in your Preferences, otherwise the instance's Default Language (Global Settings), otherwise English.
  • What it says: the subject is LibreFolio test email in English. The message names your instance by the address the browser reached it at, not by LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, and says that, if you can read it, LibreFolio can send emails. It comes as plain text with an HTML version.
  • It counts against the hourly limit, even when the server refuses it.

The result appears below the button. Test email sent to your address: the SMTP server accepted the message; check your inbox and the spam folder. Otherwise the tab says what went wrong: Sending Errors. While LibreFolio talks to the server, the button reads Sending…: LibreFolio waits up to 20 seconds for each step, so a server that does not answer takes a while to fail.

docs.title: 📬 Email: Links and Messages
docs.text:
The messages LibreFolio sends once email works, flow by flow:

  • the links for invitations and password resets;
  • forgotten passwords;
  • the limits on those emails;
  • the verification of new addresses;
  • the notice of an address change.

Email has to work first: the SMTP variables, the Email tab and the test email are in Email. When a message does not go out: Email: When It Does Not Work.

docs.title: 🌐 Emails with a Link
docs.text:
An invitation or password-reset link sent by email is built only from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL. Never from the address the browser used, nor from anything else in a request.

flowchart TD
    REQ["Email with a link to send"] --> CHK{"LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL<br>set and valid?"}
    CHK -->|"no"| REF["Refused:<br>EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE"]
    CHK -->|"yes"| BUILD["Link = LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL<br>+ page + secret part"]
    BROWSER["Browser address,<br>request data"] -. "never used" .-> BUILD
    BUILD --> MAIL["Email sent,<br>link works once"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class REF no
    class MAIL ok

The email names the instance, by the host of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, and says how long the link is valid.

https://librefolio.example.com/reset-password#token=…

🛡️ Why

Anyone can send LibreFolio a request that names another address. If the link were built from the request, a stranger could have LibreFolio email one of your users a real link to a site of theirs, and catch its secret part when the user opens it.

Where to set it: LibreFolio's .env file. The address your users open LibreFolio at:

LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL=https://librefolio.example.com
Rule Value Scheme http:// or https://, then a host name Forbidden user name or password, ? or #, spaces

It is the same variable the command line puts in front of the links it prints: Accounts and Sign-ups.

The «no» branch of the diagram (variable missing, or an address that breaks these rules), besides the EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE refusal:

  • the test email still works;
  • Require Email Verification cannot be turned on (Email Verification);
  • the links you copy, from the command line for one, stay as they are.

How long the links are valid, written in the email:

Link Valid for New invitation 7 days Password reset 30 minutes Verification 24 hours Setup of the initial administrator 72 hours

The secret part of the link comes after #: browsers never send it to the server, so it stays out of server and proxy logs.

To check it:

  • With email Ready, Settings › Administration › Email shows a notice when LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set or cannot be used, and the start log has a line (What the Log Says).
  • Once it can be used, the tab shows the address and checks, from your browser, that this instance answers there: The Address in Emailed Links.
  • From anywhere, /api/v1/system/instance shows "links": true when both email and the address are fine.

docs.title: 📨 Links Sent by an Administrator
docs.text:
An invitation or password-reset link created by an administrator can be sent by email, instead of being copied by hand.

Condition: email Ready and a usable LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (Emails with a Link). Then the invitation and password-reset dialogs of Users & Invitations show Send by email under the link.

---
config:
  sequence:
    actorMargin: 20
    width: 120
    messageMargin: 20
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Administrator
    participant F as Dialog
    participant L as LibreFolio
    A->>F: Invite, or<br>Password-reset link
    F-->>A: Link + Send by email
    A->>F: Send by email
    F->>L: Only the secret part
    Note over L: Email: link from<br>LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL
    L-->>F: Outcome
    F-->>A: Outcome

The outcome, shown in the dialog:

flowchart TD
    S["Send by email"] --> V{"Link valid?"}
    V -->|"expired, used<br>or revoked"| NO["Refused:<br>create a new one"]
    V -->|"yes"| P{"Email left?"}
    P -->|"no"| ERR["The reason<br>(Sending Errors)"]
    P -->|"yes"| OK["Sent to …<br>address and language"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class NO,ERR no
    class OK ok
Invitation Password-reset link Send to Starts with the address written in the invitation; you can change it. No field: it goes to the address of its account. Language of the email Chosen in the dialog (table below); without a choice, the instance's Default Language. The language of its account. Content Names you as the person who invites and says, when it is the case, that the new account will be an administrator. — Condition — Only while the account is active. Language choice Effect The instance's language The email is in the instance's Default Language (Global Settings). English, Italiano, Français, Español For someone who reads another one.

The language of the email is the email's only: it does not become the language of the account the invitation creates.

To set the Default Language before an administrator has saved it, in the .env file (en, it, fr or es):

LIBREFOLIO_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=it

See Environment Variables.

  • The link in the email starts with LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, whatever Server address the dialog shows: only the secret part of the link travels from the dialog. The dialog says so above the button.
  • Why an email did not go out: Sending Errors.
  • Each email counts against the hourly limit.

docs.title: 🗝️ Forgotten Passwords
docs.text:
Someone who forgot their password can ask for a reset link by email, with their username or email address, without signing in.

Before the answer:

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    REQ["Forgot Password?<br>username or email address"] --> READY{"Email Ready and<br>LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL usable?"}
    READY -->|"no"| NOPE["Refused: short message,<br>the same for everyone"]
    READY -->|"yes"| ADDR{"Per-address<br>counter full?"}
    ADDR -->|"no"| NAME{"3 an hour for this<br>name or address?"}
    NAME -->|"no"| INST{"Hourly limit of<br>the instance spent?"}
    ADDR -->|"yes"| WAIT["Refused: the answer<br>says how long to wait"]
    NAME -->|"past"| WAIT
    INST -->|"yes"| WAIT
    INST -->|"no"| RESP["The same answer<br>for everyone"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    class NOPE,WAIT no

After the answer, silently:

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    RESP["Answer already given"] --> FIND{"An active account<br>matches?"}
    FIND -->|"no"| STOP1["Nothing"]
    FIND -->|"yes"| ADMIN{"An administrator's link<br>still valid?"}
    ADMIN -->|"yes"| STOP1
    ADMIN -->|"no"| ACC{"Per account: 1 every 5 minutes<br>and 3 an hour past?"}
    ACC -->|"yes"| STOP2["Nothing"]
    ACC -->|"no"| BOX{"Per mailbox:<br>3 an hour past?"}
    BOX -->|"yes"| STOP2
    BOX -->|"no"| SEND["Email with the link:<br>30 minutes, once"]
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class SEND ok

The email with the link is in the account's language.

The same answer for everyone, whether an account matches or not:

If an active account matches, its owner gets an email with a link to choose a new password

The search for the account and the sending come after the answer: nobody can use it to find out which accounts exist.

  • The account is found as the login finds it: username or email address. The email goes to its address.
  • The link replaces the reset links that earlier requests sent the account. A link created by an administrator, instead, is never cancelled by a request.

It is safe because changing an account's email address asks for the current password (Profile): see Security Notes.

The login page:

State of the instance What the page shows Email Ready and a usable LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL Forgot Password? opens the form for it, without the server commands (they stay in Command-Line Tools). After a request the form says Email sent: check your spam folder too., the same for everyone, and its button counts down 5 minutes, the interval for one account, before the next request; a reload of the page keeps the countdown. Otherwise That command, open, under the warning: Email recovery is not available on this instance. Reset your password from the server terminal, or ask your administrator for a password-reset link. The page cannot read the instance's configuration from the server Only the advice: Ask your administrator for a password-reset link: they can create one for your account.

An administrator creates that link in Settings › Administration › Users, even without email (Password-Reset Links).

The limits:

Limit Past it LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS requests an hour (20 by default) from the same address. A count shared with the registrations and with Send the link again (Limits on Activation and Password-Reset Emails). An IPv6 address counts by its /64, the block one subscriber usually holds. Refused until a place frees in that count, or in the hourly limit of the instance if that one waits longer. The answer says how long. 3 requests an hour for the same username or email address, whether an account matches or not Refused until the oldest of them is an hour old. The hourly limit of the instance, LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR Refused until an email fits again. 3 emails an hour to the same mailbox, whatever account they are for and however its address is written Nothing is sent; the answer stays the same. 1 email every 5 minutes, and 3 an hour, for the same account, the links created by an administrator included Nothing is sent; the answer stays the same. Two requests at the same moment cannot both be sent.

Where the counts live:

  • the limit per account counts the account's reset links in the database;
  • the others are kept in the memory of each server process: with several processes, each has its own count, and a restart forgets them;
  • a reset email that did not go out still counts, for the account and for the mailbox.

One mailbox, however its address is written. The limit per mailbox counts the aliases of an address as one mailbox:

Spelling Mailbox counted Capitals Do not count. name+news@example.com name@example.com: a +tag does not count, on any domain. first.last@googlemail.com firstlast@gmail.com: the dots of a Gmail address do not count, and googlemail.com is gmail.com.
  • The limits of the verification emails and of the notices of an email change count the same way.
  • Each email still goes to the address exactly as the account has it.
  • A mailbox that takes mail under any name, such as a catch-all domain or Fastmail's anything@user.fastmail.com, counts each name apart: only the hourly limit of the instance holds those back.

Behind a reverse proxy, the address that counts is the visitor's, as LibreFolio reads it (The Visitor's Address):

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    Q1{"LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER<br>set?"} -->|"yes"| HDR["Address in the proxy's header<br>(Fly-Client-IP, X-Real-IP)"]
    Q1 -->|"no"| Q2{"Proxy listed in<br>FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS?"}
    Q2 -->|"yes"| XFF["uvicorn reads<br>X-Forwarded-For"]
    Q2 -->|"no: untrusted proxy"| Q3{"Address<br>of the proxy"}
    Q3 -->|"local: Docker, LAN, VPN"| LOC["Per-address limits skipped;<br>the others count"]
    Q3 -->|"public: a CDN"| PUB["Everyone shares<br>the proxy's count"]

  • With LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER, in the .env file, LibreFolio reads the address in the header your proxy sets with the visitor's address (Fly-Client-IP on Fly.io, X-Real-IP from Nginx):

    LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER=X-Real-IP

    Set it only if every request crosses that proxy: a visitor who reaches LibreFolio directly could write the header.

  • Otherwise it is the address the server (uvicorn) sees. uvicorn takes the visitor's address from the proxy's X-Forwarded-For header only when the proxy's address is listed in FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (127.0.0.1 when not set). List your proxy's addresses or networks there, in the .env file:

    FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=172.18.0.0/16

    Never *: uvicorn would take the first address of the header, which the visitor can write.

  • An untrusted proxy on a local address, such as a proxy container in front of the Docker image, the usual setup: a visitor cannot use up the count of Forgot Password?, Send the link again and the registrations for everyone. The limits per username or email address, per account and per mailbox, and the hourly limit of the instance, still count. The log warns once per server process, and the security checks report it as a warning of platform.client_address (The Visitor's Address).

  • An untrusted proxy on a public address, such as a CDN: the first LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS requests of anyone use up the count through the proxy for everyone, for up to an hour. Tell LibreFolio about the proxy.

docs.title: 🚦 Limits on Activation and Password-Reset Emails
docs.text:
The emails that activate an account and the ones that reset a password are held back by two counters, the same for every way to ask for them. Each counts over the last 60 minutes, in the memory of each server process.

Counter Variable Default What it counts Per address LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS 20 an hour The emails that leave for one client address (an IPv6 address by its /64), in one count: the registrations, every Send the link again with the right password and every Forgot Password? for an account that exists. Tries are not counted (diagram below). Per instance LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR 50 an hour Every email the instance sends: activations, resets, invitations, notices.

The per-address counter counts the emails that leave, not the tries:

flowchart TD
    REQ["Registration, Send the link again,<br>Forgot Password?"] --> FULL{"Per-address<br>counter full?"}
    FULL -->|"yes, registration"| HELD["Account created,<br>email held"]
    FULL -->|"yes, the other two"| REJ["Refused at once,<br>before the password"]
    FULL -->|"no"| NEXT["The other checks<br>(diagram below)"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    class REJ no

When the counter is not full, the place is spent only if the other checks pass:

flowchart TD
    OTHER{"The other checks: password,<br>existing name, account, mailbox, instance"} -->|"refused"| FREE["No place spent"]
    OTHER -->|"passes"| SEND["Spends a place, now"]
    SEND --> SMTP{"Does the SMTP server<br>accept it?"}
    SMTP -->|"no"| CNT["Stays counted:<br>it was tried"]
    SMTP -->|"yes"| OK["Sent"]
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class OK ok

These cost it nothing:

  • a wrong password: it has its own limit;
  • a request for a name no account has (for Forgot Password?, the answer is the same whether an account matches or not);
  • a request refused by another limit, such as a Send the link again refused by the limit per account or per mailbox.

Three more limits stay as they are. They are not counters of activation emails, and they rarely matter for an account whose email was held: nothing has reached its mailbox yet.

Limit Applies to The sign-in's limit on wrong passwords (Failed Sign-ins) Send the link again, which shares it with the login page. 3 emails an hour to the same mailbox LibreFolio cannot be used to flood someone else's address. 1 email every 5 minutes, and 3 an hour, for the same account Send the link again.

How long to wait. The answer says how many seconds to wait, and that time is exact: the longest of the waits of the counters that held the request back. The same request made at that moment goes through, unless others from the same network used the place meanwhile: the answer then says the new time.

An example. An office with one internet address and a limit of 20.

Time What happens 9:00 – 9:40 Twenty colleagues register: their twenty emails leave. 9:45 The twenty-first, Mario, registers. His account is created, but his email is held: the page tells him to try again in about 15 minutes, the time until the 9:00 email leaves the count at 10:00. 9:46 Mario signs in and asks for the link again: the same counter refuses him, for 14 minutes. 10:00 He asks again with username and password: the link leaves.

The per-address counter is shared on purpose, with a consequence to know: when a network has used up its count with registrations, Forgot Password? from that network waits too, until a place frees.

For a network where many people sign up together, such as a school or an office, raise LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS in the .env file. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

docs.title: ✅ Email Verification
docs.text:
With Require Email Verification on, a new account cannot sign in until its owner confirms the address with a link that LibreFolio emails to the account.

Where: the switch is in Settings › Administration › Global Settings, Security category (Global Settings). It is off by default.

The registration:

flowchart TD
    REG["Registration,<br>with an invitation too"] --> SW{"Require Email<br>Verification on?"}
    SW -->|"no"| ACTIVE["Active account"]
    SW -->|"yes"| CAN{"Can an email with<br>a link go out?"}
    CAN -->|"no"| NOREG["No account created:<br>Sign-up is not possible right now…"]
    CAN -->|"yes"| CREATE["Account created,<br>waiting"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class NOREG no
    class ACTIVE ok

Then the verification email:

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    CREATE["Account created, waiting"] --> LIM{"Per-address counter or<br>hourly limit of the instance full?"}
    LIM -->|"yes"| HELD["Page: Try again in<br>about N minutes"]
    LIM -->|"no"| TEXT["Page: Account created.<br>We are sending you…"]
    TEXT --> BOX{"After the answer:<br>mailbox 3 an hour, SMTP error,<br>email broken?"}
    BOX -->|"held"| LOG["Only in the log:<br>not sent"]
    BOX -->|"restart"| NOLINE["No email,<br>no line"]
    BOX -->|"leaves"| MAIL["Email with the link:<br>24 hours, once"]
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class MAIL ok

Finally the click on the link:

flowchart TD
    MAIL["Link in the email"] --> OPEN["Page with the button<br>Confirm my email address"]
    OPEN -->|"only opened, no click"| NOTHING["Nothing:<br>the link stays valid"]
    OPEN -->|"click"| DONE["Active account: login<br>page, with a confirmation"]
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class DONE ok

Who waits: every account created from the registration page while the switch is on, the ones opened with an invitation included.

They never wait:

  • the first account of a new instance, its administrator;
  • the administrator LibreFolio creates from LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL, activated by its setup link;
  • the accounts created with user create on the command line;
  • the accounts that already exist.

The texts of the login page right after the registration:

Case Text The email can leave Account created. We are sending you an email with a link to activate it: open it within 24 hours, then sign in. No email after a few minutes? Check the spam folder, then sign in with your username and password: you will be offered a new link. The client address already had the emails of LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS registrations (20 by default) in the last hour, or the hourly limit of the instance is spent Account created, but the activation email could not leave now. Try again in about N minutes: sign in with your username and password, and you will be offered a new link.
  • N is exact: the time until both counters admit a new email (Limits on Activation and Password-Reset Emails).
  • Behind a reverse proxy LibreFolio does not trust, on a local address (the usual Docker setup), nothing is counted per address, so the second text never shows (Forgotten Passwords).
  • We are sending you an email means that the email is queued, not that it was delivered: it leaves after the answer, and it can still not go (Limits of the Verification Emails).

The email, Confirm your email address, is in the instance's Default Language: a new account has no language of its own yet. Its link starts with LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (Emails with a Link).

🔍 Why a click is needed

The mail filters that scan links, such as Microsoft Defender Safe Links, open the links of a message in a browser that runs scripts: if opening were enough, the filter would activate the account in place of its owner. Such an opening spends nothing; the link stays valid for its owner. Someone who opens a link without having signed up has only to close the page.

Until the address is confirmed, the account cannot sign in, but it can ask for a new link:

flowchart TD
    LOGIN["Sign-in with username<br>and password"] --> PW{"Password?"}
    PW -->|"wrong"| REF["The usual sign-in refusal:<br>nobody learns more"]
    PW -->|"right"| MSG["Address not verified yet:<br>Send the link again offered"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    class REF no

Send the link again, the first checks:

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    RS["Send the link again:<br>username and password"] --> L1{"Per-address<br>counter full?"}
    L1 -->|"yes"| W["Refused: the page says<br>in how many minutes to retry"]
    L1 -->|"no"| L2{"Wrong-password<br>limit reached?"}
    L2 -->|"yes"| W
    L2 -->|"no"| PW2{"Right password?"}
    PW2 -->|"no"| REF["The usual<br>sign-in refusal"]
    PW2 -->|"yes"| GO["Checks on the account<br>(diagram below)"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    class W,REF no

With the right password, the checks on the account:

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    GO["Right password"] --> L3{"Per account: 1 every 5 minutes<br>and 3 an hour past?"}
    L3 -->|"no"| L4{"Mailbox: 3 an hour<br>past?"}
    L4 -->|"no"| L5{"Hourly limit of<br>the instance spent?"}
    L3 -->|"yes"| W["Refused: the page says<br>in how many minutes to retry"]
    L4 -->|"yes"| W
    L5 -->|"yes"| W
    L5 -->|"no"| L6{"Link expired and<br>no free place?"}
    L6 -->|"yes"| ASK["The owner is told<br>to ask you"]
    L6 -->|"no"| NEW["New link: the earlier ones<br>stop working"]
    classDef no fill:#b71c1c,stroke:#7f0000,color:#ffffff
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class W,ASK no
    class NEW ok

What the person sees, step by step: If LibreFolio Asks You to Confirm Your Email in Getting Started.

docs.title: 🔀 Turning It On and Off
docs.text:
---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    OFF["Off"] -->|"turn on: only if an email<br>with a link can go out"| ON["On"]
    ON -->|"turn off: always works"| OFF
    ON -->|"email stops working"| BROKEN["On, no email leaves:<br>nobody can sign up"]
    BROKEN -->|"fix email"| ON
    BROKEN -->|"turn off"| OFF

«An email with a link can go out» = email Ready (Settings › Administration › Email) and a usable LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (Emails with a Link).

Step What LibreFolio says Turn on, but no email with a link can go out The switch is greyed out, with the hint: Needs an email with a link to go out: set up SMTP and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL first (Settings › Administration › Email). That changes between opening the tab and saving The save is refused and nothing of it is stored: Email verification needs an email with a link to go out, and none can go now: check Settings › Administration › Email. On: saving the other settings Always works, even when email has stopped working since. Turn off The accounts already waiting keep waiting: their links still work, and so does Send the link again. To let one in at once, activate it (Waiting Accounts). Email stops working while it is on (the server or a variable breaks) Nobody can sign up any more, not even with an invitation, which stays valid; no account is created. The registration page says: Sign-up is not possible right now: this instance cannot send the verification email. Try again later, or ask its administrator. Only the first account of a new instance is let through. Send the link again fails the same way. Fix email (When It Does Not Work) or turn the switch off.

docs.title: ⏳ Waiting Accounts
docs.text:
Towards Active:

flowchart TD
    W["Waiting, link valid<br>(place taken)"] -->|"click on Confirm"| A["Active"]
    W -->|"Reactivate, or user activate"| A
    W -->|"24 hours: the link expires"| E["Waiting, link expired<br>(place free)"]
    E -->|"Send the link again"| W
    E -->|"Reactivate, or user activate"| A
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class A ok

To turn it away:

flowchart TD
    W["Waiting, link valid<br>(place taken)"] -->|"Delete"| D["Deleted"]
    E["Waiting, link expired<br>(place free)"] -->|"Delete"| D
    W -->|"user deactivate, or<br>PATCH is_active false"| X["Deactivated:<br>links off, place free"]
    E -->|"user deactivate, or<br>PATCH is_active false"| X

Where: in Settings › Administration › Users, a waiting account shows the badge Waiting for verification, not Deactivated, even once its link has expired. Hover over the badge, or open the row, for the hint: the owner has not opened the link yet, signing in offers a new one, and Reactivate lets the account in at once.

Step Facts the diagram does not say The place of the user limit (LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS) Taken as by an open invitation. The place is free again when the last link sent expires, 24 hours later; on a full instance, Send the link again tells the owner to ask you. Reactivate (Accounts Waiting for Their Email), or user activate on the command line Lets the account in without the email: it can sign in at once, and the links already sent stop working. While the link is valid the place is already counted, so Reactivate works even on a full instance and user activate prints no limit warning. Once the link has expired, a free place is needed, as for any deactivated account. Delete (Delete an Account) To turn it away. The Users tab itself offers no Deactivate for an account that is not active: there, Delete is the way. user deactivate on the command line, or the administrator API with is_active: false To turn it away. Deactivated, it stops waiting: its links stop working, its place is free, its row reads Deactivated from then on, and signing in tells the owner that the account is disabled.

The administrator API endpoint:

PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}

docs.title: 📏 Limits of the Verification Emails
docs.text:
The checks of Send the link again are in the diagram of Email Verification; here the numbers, and what whoever passes them sees.

Limit Past it LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS emails an hour (20 by default) from the same address, counting the emails that leave: the registrations, Send the link again with the right password and Forgot Password? for an account that exists. An IPv6 address counts by its /64. The next new accounts are still created and wait, but their emails do not leave: the login page says so right after the registration, with how long to wait; the owners ask for the link again from the login page once that time has passed. Send the link again is refused for the same time. The sign-in's own limit on wrong passwords, shared with the login page: 10 every 15 minutes for the same username or email address, 50 from the same address (Failed Sign-ins) Refused before the password is checked: the page says in how many minutes to try again. The right password clears the failures of what was typed. 1 email every 5 minutes, and 3 an hour, for the same account, the email of the registration included Refused: the page says in how many minutes to try again. 3 emails an hour to the same mailbox, whatever account they are for and however its address is written (Forgotten Passwords): the email of a registration and the links sent again alike, and only the emails that left Send the link again is refused: the page says in how many minutes to try again. After a registration, the account is created and waits, but no email leaves, and nothing tells the owner: the page shows its usual text, which already says what to do (check the spam folder, then sign in to get a new link). The hourly limit of the instance, LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR Refused until an email fits again. A registration made while it is spent is held like one past the limit of its address. A free place, once the account's link has expired Refused: the owner is told to ask you.

What stays invisible after a registration. None of these reaches the page:

  • the mailbox limit of 3 verification emails an hour;
  • the hourly limit of the instance;
  • an SMTP error;
  • email or LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL that stopped working meanwhile;
  • a restart.

Only the log says it (What the Log Says):

Verification email: not sent
Verification email: the request failed

A restart before the email goes out leaves no line at all. The account stays waiting with its email held, and Send the link again recovers it: that is why the text of the page tells the person what to do when nothing arrives.

🔍 Why the mailbox limit is not checked before the answer

It is deliberate. A registration that answered differently when the mailbox had just received emails would tell anyone who signs up with someone else's address whether that mailbox is receiving them.

Besides:

  • a link whose email did not go out counts neither for the account nor for the mailbox;
  • if the account stops waiting in the meantime (address confirmed, or an administrator activated or deactivated it), no new link is sent;
  • the limits per address and per mailbox are kept in the memory of each server process (each has its own count; a restart forgets them), and behind a reverse proxy the address that counts follows the rules of Forgotten Passwords.

docs.title: 🔔 Email Address Changes
docs.text:
When the email address of an account has changed, in Profile, LibreFolio writes two short emails, in the account's language: a notice to the address the account had before, and a confirmation to the new address, which is now the account's.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    CH["Email address change<br>in Profile"] --> OK["The change goes through:<br>the answer never waits for the email"]
    OK --> CASE{"Only the capitals of the<br>letters A to Z changed?"}
    CASE -->|"yes: not a change"| SKIP["No notice"]
    CASE -->|"no"| LIM{"3 changes an hour<br>for the account past?"}
    LIM -->|"yes"| SKIP
    LIM -->|"no"| EN{"Email on?"}
    EN -->|"no"| LOG["Nothing: an information line<br>in the log, not a warning"]
    EN -->|"yes"| SEND["Notice to the old address,<br>in the account's language"]
    SEND --> NEW["Confirmation to the new address,<br>in the account's language"]
    classDef ok fill:#2e7d32,stroke:#1b5e20,color:#ffffff
    class SEND,NEW ok
The notice and the confirmation Recipients The notice to the old address, then the confirmation to the new one. Each goes on its own: if one cannot leave, the other still does, and neither undoes the change. What they do not say The notice shows nothing of the new address, not even the domain; the confirmation nothing of the old one. Neither has the username: both open with a plain «Hello,» (Security Notes). What the notice says That the address changed. If the owner did not make the change, someone may be using their account: they must change the password at once if they still can, and tell you. No link. What the confirmation says That this address is now the account's: it signs in with it and gets its emails there. Whoever has no account on the instance is told that someone typed the address by mistake, and to tell you. No link. Instance name The host of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, with its port if it has one, or «LibreFolio» when the variable is not set or cannot be used: with no link, the notice does not need it. Hourly limit Counts like any email. 3 an hour per account and per mailbox 3 changes with emails an hour per account, and 3 emails an hour per mailbox, however its address is written (Forgotten Passwords). A mailbox past its limit gets nothing, the other address still gets its email. Without these limits, an account could point its email at any address and change it again, to make your instance write there. Capitals Anna@example.com for anna@example.com is no change of address: no email goes. Accented letters count as different: Émile@example.com for émile@example.com is a change, with its notice.

docs.text:
