docs.title: 🔄 Developer Workflow & Tools
docs.text:
This guide covers developer-specific workflows, tools, and all CLI commands available in LibreFolio.

Prerequisite: Host Installation

Before using these developer tools, ensure you have set up your local Python, Node.js, and Pipenv environment. For step-by-step setup instructions, see the Host Installation Guide.

docs.title: 🖥️ SvelteKit Frontend Development
docs.text:
For active frontend development with Hot Module Replacement (HMR), start a second terminal and run:

./dev.py front dev

The Vite development server will run at http://localhost:5173 and automatically proxy all /api calls to the FastAPI backend.

Frontend Dependency

The SvelteKit frontend is heavily dependent on the data returned by the backend. You must keep the backend server running in parallel (via ./dev.py server in another terminal) to handle API requests.

docs.title: 🔄 Development Workflow CLI Commands
docs.text: LibreFolio includes a central orchestration script, dev.py, which is your single entry point for all development tasks. Run ./dev.py --help for the full command tree.

docs.title: ⏹️ Stopping the Server
docs.text:
./dev.py server runs uvicorn as its child process and waits for it (run_server_live() in scripts/cli_base.py). It lets the server finish its own shutdown, bounded by the shutdown budget (LIBREFOLIO_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 8 s by default; see Stopping the Server in Configuration):

  • Ctrl+C: the terminal sends SIGINT to the whole foreground process group, so the server already has it. dev.py sends nothing more, since a second SIGINT would make uvicorn force its exit: it prints Interrupted: waiting for the server to stop … and waits.
  • SIGTERM to dev.py, for example from a process supervisor that signals only the main process: dev.py forwards it to the server, prints SIGTERM: waiting for the server to stop … and waits the same way. A server that gets the SIGTERM from its process group as well (the test runner signals the whole group, scripts/test_runner/_server.py) gets it twice and stops once.
  • The wait (_server_stop_grace() in dev.py) is the budget plus 2 s: 10 s by default, 7 s with LIBREFOLIO_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5, 10 s with a value that cannot be used, and no limit with 0.
  • A second Ctrl+C or SIGTERM, or the end of the wait: dev.py kills the server (SIGKILL).

dev.py exits with 130 after a Ctrl+C and 143 after a SIGTERM. With --coverage no dev.py is left to wait: it replaces itself with coverage run, and the signals reach the server directly (see Frontend Coverage Architecture). The other dev.py commands still run through run_command_live(), whose subprocess.run kills the child 0.25 s after a Ctrl+C.

docs.title: 🖥️ Frontend Management
docs.text: Command Description Details ./dev.py front dev Start Vite dev server with HMR Run at http://localhost:5173 ./dev.py front build Compile frontend into production-ready static assets static files output to backend/static ./dev.py front build --debug Compile frontend with source maps Used for debugging frontend issues ./dev.py front check Run svelte-check type validator Checks Svelte components and TS types ./dev.py front preview Preview the compiled production build locally Run Vite preview server

docs.title: 🔗 API Client Synchronization
docs.text:
LibreFolio uses an OpenAPI-first workflow to keep types synchronized between Python (backend) and SvelteKit (frontend):

Command Description Details ./dev.py api schema Export OpenAPI JSON schema from FastAPI backend Generates openapi.json ./dev.py api client Generate TypeScript client from the exported schema Generates frontend API client ./dev.py api sync Export schema and generate client in one step Highly recommended after changing models/routes

docs.title: 🌍 Internationalization (i18n)
docs.text:
Manage translations across English, Italian, Spanish, and French. The catalogue the frontend loads, frontend/src/lib/i18n/<lang>.json, is generated and ignored by git: never edit it, the build stops on a hand edit. Its sources are frontend/src/lib/i18n/base/, one folder per subsystem with its prefixes.txt, and each plugin's i18n/ fragment (see Internationalization and A Plugin's Translations). Every command works on the sources, and the ones that change keys regenerate the catalogue.

Command Description ./dev.py i18n audit Audit missing or extra translation keys across languages, after a strict check of the sources ./dev.py i18n audit --duplicates Audit and report duplicate translation values ./dev.py i18n add KEY --en "…" --it "…" --fr "…" --es "…" [--into SOURCE] Add a key in the four languages, in the source that owns it; --into names the source: base, a subsystem, or a plugin as <family>/<plugin> ./dev.py i18n update KEY [--en "…"] [--it "…"] [--fr "…"] [--es "…"] Change a key's translations, in the source that holds it ./dev.py i18n remove KEY Remove a key from every source and language ./dev.py i18n where KEY The source file that holds a key, or the one add would write it to ./dev.py i18n search QUERY Search key names or translation values; shows the source of each key ./dev.py i18n tree [PREFIX] Print key tree structure starting with optional prefix ./dev.py i18n build [--strict] [--force] Regenerate the catalogue from the sources: a missing translation falls back to English with a warning (an error with --strict); --force overwrites a hand-edited generated file ./dev.py i18n check [--lenient] [--against REV] Validate the sources, strictly: every language complete (--lenient accepts a missing translation, as the build does); --against also proves the catalogue identical to the one at a git revision, key by key and language by language ./dev.py i18n move PREFIX --into SOURCE Move every key under a prefix, in every language, to another source ./dev.py i18n split Put every key of base and of the subsystems in the folder its declared prefix names (re-runnable) ./dev.py i18n absorb --base REV --theirs REV [--prefer {ours,theirs}] Replay the key changes a branch made on the old single-file layout, as a three-way merge per key and language; conflicts are listed and nothing is written unless --prefer settles them

The catalogue is regenerated by ./dev.py front build, by the npm hooks of dev, build, build:debug, check and check:watch (so also by ./dev.py front dev and ./dev.py front check; by hand, npm run i18n:build), before every Vitest run, by ./dev.py lint --dead-code before knip, and by the commands above. The development server generates it once, when it starts, and does not watch its sources: a source you edit by hand reaches the running server only after ./dev.py i18n build.

docs.title: 🗃️ Database Migrations (Alembic)
docs.text:
Create and apply database schema changes:

Command Description ./dev.py db upgrade Apply all pending migrations to the SQLite database ./dev.py db migrate "MESSAGE" Auto-generate a new Alembic migration based on SQLAlchemy models ./dev.py db downgrade Rollback the database schema by one migration step ./dev.py db create-clean Recreate a fresh database and apply all migrations ./dev.py db current Show the current database migration revision

db migrate, db upgrade, db downgrade and db create-clean refuse to run while a server listens on the port that serves the target database (PORT for the production database, TEST_PORT for the test one): stop that server first. The server itself applies pending migrations at startup (ensure_database_exists() in backend/app/services/platform/database_bootstrap.py, the database step of the lifespan).

docs.title: 🧪 Test Runner
docs.text:
Run backend unit/integration tests and frontend Playwright E2E tests:

Command Description ./dev.py test all Run all test categories in the optimal order ./dev.py test <category> all Run tests in a single category (e.g., api, e2e, front-fx) ./dev.py test <category> --help List the units (actions) of a category, each with its description ./dev.py test <category> <action> --list List the tests of one unit without running them; all lists the whole category

docs.title: 🧰 Linting, Formatting & Documentation
docs.text: Command Description ./dev.py format Format backend Python code with black ./dev.py lint Lint and auto-fix backend Python issues using ruff ./dev.py mkdocs serve Start the local MkDocs documentation development server ./dev.py mkdocs build Compile the documentation site into static HTML ./dev.py shell Open a subshell inside the active pipenv virtual environment

docs.title: 🐳 Docker Integration
docs.text:
Developers can build and run production-tagged containers locally using the dev CLI:

Command Description ./dev.py docker build Build production Docker image (compiles frontend + docs first) ./dev.py docker up Launch the containerized stack in detached mode ./dev.py docker down Stop and remove active Docker containers ./dev.py docker rebuild Build, stop, and restart containers with the new image ./dev.py docker exec <cmd> Execute a dev.py command inside the running container, as the server's user (through gosu), not root

For details on local Docker workflows, container settings, and how the host .env file integrates with docker-compose.yml, see the Advanced Docker Guide. How the image itself is built and started: Architecture overview → Docker image.

docs.title: 🏗️ What ./dev.py docker build Does
docs.text:
cmd_docker_build() checks that .env exists, then _docker_ensure_assets_built() prepares what the image copies from the host:

  1. Version: get_git_version(), asked once before any other step, so that a step writing a tracked file cannot turn it into -dirty: LF_APP_VERSION when it is set, git describe otherwise. The VERSION file of an earlier build is deleted first, so a checkout where git cannot answer gets unknown, not the old value. The frontend bundle and VERSION both carry this frozen version (see Version Stamps → Local image builds).
  2. Resource cache: scripts/update_js_cache.py, strict. It caches the flags subset of the Noto Color Emoji font (frontend/static/fonts/noto-color-emoji/, drawn by the 'LF Flags' face of frontend/static/lf-flags.css on every non-Apple device: Windows has no flag emoji of its own) MathJax and Mermaid (mkdocs_src/docs/javascripts/vendor/). Mermaid is mermaid.min.js at a version pinned in scripts/update_js_cache.py, with the SHA-256 of that file: a download that does not match fails the build and writes nothing, so a cached copy is never replaced by an unreviewed one. mkdocs_src/overrides/main.html writes it before Material's bundle on the pages that have a diagram, so none of them asks a third party once the cache is filled; javascripts/mermaid-early.js reads the same pinned file from the CDN when the cache is empty. The same lines write the full screen view of a diagram (javascripts/diagram-zoom.js, stylesheets/diagram-zoom.css): a click, or Enter or Space on the focused diagram, opens it over the page; the wheel or a pinch zooms around the pointer, a drag pans, a double click or 0 fits it, + and - zoom, and Esc or a click outside the diagram closes it and gives the focus back to the diagram. Its texts follow the page's language (en, it, fr, es). Material draws each diagram into a closed shadow root of div.mermaid, which no other script can reach, so diagram-zoom.js replaces Element.prototype.attachShadow to open those roots: it has to run before Material's bundle draws. Rule: a script that must see a diagram's SVG goes in the template's head, as a classic script before the bundle and only on pages that have a diagram, never in extra_javascript (those load after the bundle, when the shadow root is already closed). The ELK layout is not served: a diagram whose frontmatter says layout: elk is drawn with the default layout, so leave the key out of new diagrams. A resource that cannot be downloaded and has no cached copy fails the build (❌ Resource cache incomplete). ./dev.py front build fails only for the resources the frontend ships (--required-for frontend), and ./dev.py server only warns and falls back to the CDN. ./dev.py cache js (--force) refreshes the cache by hand.

  3. Frontend: _docker_ensure_frontend_built() rebuilds it in production mode, with LF_APP_VERSION set to the frozen version for that build only, when _docker_frontend_stale_reason() gives a reason, shown in the log:

    • missing or outdated: check_frontend_needs_build() finds sources newer than frontend/build/index.html, the files of frontend/static/ included, or a Tool codegen input, a frontend source or a static file added, removed or renamed since that build (what it watches: Frontend Tests Overview → Automated Setup);
    • not a production build: .build-debug says 1 (a debug build, for example from ./dev.py server --test) or is missing (mode unknown);
    • built for another version: frontend/build/.build-version does not hold the frozen version.

    After its build it writes the version into .build-version. Every frontend build empties frontend/build/, so the file exists only when the last build was made for an image: a build from ./dev.py front build, a server or the test runner is rebuilt once, and a new commit, even one that touched no frontend file, changes the version and rebuilds the bundle too. The Dockerfile's frontend stage still checks the result (scripts/docker/check_frontend_build.sh). 4. Documentation: mkdocs build when mkdocs_src/site/index.html is missing or older than any .md under mkdocs_src/docs/. 5. requirements.txt: regenerated with pipenv requirements when missing or older than Pipfile.lock. 6. VERSION: the frozen version, written into a file, since the image has no .git/. The sidebar (the bundle's version) and Settings → About (GET /api/v1/system/info, the backend's) show the same version in the image.

The build then runs docker build -t librefolio:<version> -t librefolio:latest --build-arg UID=<uid> --build-arg GID=<gid> .. <version> comes from _get_docker_tag(), which clears get_git_version()'s cache and asks again after the steps above: if one of them changed a tracked file, the tags end in -dirty while the version inside the image does not. The UID/GID are those of the user running the command (os.getuid(), os.getgid(); only docker compose build reads UID/GID from .env). --light adds -light to both tags and --build-arg DOCS_VARIANT=light; --no-cache is passed through. ./dev.py docker rebuild runs the same build, then docker compose down and docker compose up -d; a failed build leaves the running containers alone.

docs.title: 🧪 Test Mode in the Container
docs.text:
The image cannot run test mode, for the two reasons below, and it exposes only the production port 6040: neither Compose file publishes the test port. Run test mode from a source checkout on the host instead:

./dev.py test db populate --force --with-static   # mock data in the test database
./dev.py server --test                            # test server on :6041

Then open http://localhost:6041 and sign in as a test user, for example e2e_test_user / E2eTestPass123! or e2e_test_admin / E2eAdminPass123!.

The compose stack holds only the host's PORT (${PORT:-6040}), so the test server can run on the host while the stack is up.

Why the image cannot run test mode

  • test is not part of the image. dev.py registers a command group only when the directories it needs exist (_has() in dev.py): without backend/test_scripts/, which .dockerignore keeps out, test stays listed but answers 'test' is not available in this installation and exits with 2, so test db populate cannot seed the test database. i18n (frontend/scripts/) and mkdocs translate / translate-validate (mkdocs_src/aphra-pipeline/) behave the same way; ./dev.py test utils dev-cli-image pins this behaviour on a copy of the image's file set.
  • server --test forces a debug frontend build, while the image ships a production one: auto_build_frontend() sees the mode mismatch and rebuilds, and the rebuild stops at its first check. Before any npm or npx call, cmd_fe_build() looks in frontend/node_modules/.bin for the tools it runs, and the image has no node_modules and no Node.js: dev.py stops with Cannot run the frontend build: the frontend dependencies are not installed, names the missing tools (openapi-zod-client, svelte-check, vite) and the fix for a checkout, cd frontend && npm ci, which the image cannot run, and the server does not start.

The flow above runs on the host, so its test database is backend/data/test/sqlite/app.db in the source checkout (from LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR, default ./backend/data/test), and ./dev.py test db populate --force deletes and recreates it.

docs.title: 🚦 Lint Gates & Code Policy
docs.text:
LibreFolio's Python hygiene rules are enforced by gates, not by convention documents: everything listed here lives in [tool.ruff.lint] in the repo-root pyproject.toml and runs on every ./dev.py lint invocation. The audit lesson behind this setup (audit 08, P1-2): "level zero" cleanups do not hold without a gate that fails the build when the level regresses.

./dev.py lint            # ruff check --fix (auto-fixes what is safe)
./dev.py format          # black, line-length 300
./dev.py lint --dead-code  # vulture dead-code scan (config in pyproject.toml)

docs.title: 🧱 The gate list
docs.text:
Gate Rule family Why it is on E / W pycodestyle errors / warnings Baseline style (E501 line-length stays off — black owns it) F pyflakes Unused imports, undefined names I isort Import ordering B flake8-bugbear Real-bug patterns (B008 stays off — FastAPI Depends() needs call defaults) C4 flake8-comprehensions Unnecessary comprehension/list/dict calls UP pyupgrade Modern syntax — with UP006/UP007/UP035/UP045 off by choice: List[X], Union[X, Y], Optional[X] and typing imports are kept because they read more explicitly next to Pydantic PLC0415 import-outside-toplevel Imports belong at module top; the few legitimate function-local imports carry a justified # noqa: PLC0415 S110 try-except-pass No silent except: pass swallows — audit 08/P0-3 fixed the instances, the gate keeps them from coming back C901 cyclomatic complexity Gated at 10 ([tool.ruff.lint.mccabe] max-complexity = 10) — see the policy below RUF022 sorted __all__ Barrel modules keep __all__ sorted — with 3 deliberate exceptions, see below

ruff check backend/ is green under these gates; a regression is a lint failure, not a discussion.

docs.title: 📏 The C901 policy: flat packers vs real complexity
docs.text:
McCabe counts every decision point — including ternaries and boolean operators — so a flat "unpack-and-repack" data mapper with 12 ternaries scores 13 while being perfectly linear code. Cognitive complexity would be the honest metric for that shape, but ruff does not implement it. The threshold was therefore set low (10) and the resulting triage distinguishes two kinds of over-threshold function:

  1. Flat data shuffling (packers, CSV parsers, per-rule validators, bulk loops with early returns) → keeps a per-function justified noqa that says why it is flat:
def validate_chain_steps(  # noqa: C901 — flat numbered rule-chain validation
  1. Genuinely nested logic (orchestrators, state machines, nested closures) → marked TODO(P2-refactor) in the same comment and tracked in the audit backlog for real decomposition:
async def get_lots_analysis(  # noqa: C901 — TODO(P2-refactor): long orchestrator; extract per-analysis stage helpers

The transaction batch refactor demonstrates the preferred outcome: TransactionService.execute_batch() no longer has a C901 exemption or TODO(P2-refactor). Its former 637-line body is now an approximately 50-line orchestrator over TransactionBatchContext and ordered functions in the batch stage modules (transaction_batch_stages.py, batch_edits.py, batch_creates.py, batch_costs.py).

As of 2026-09-11, the current tree carries 201 # noqa: C901 sites and 24 TODO(P2-refactor) markers. Relative to the tracked pre-refactor tree, execute_batch() accounts for the one-site reduction in both totals (202 → 201 and 25 → 24). Recheck live counts instead of copying these numbers:

grep -rn "noqa: C901" backend/ scripts/ --include="*.py" | wc -l
grep -rn "TODO(P2-refactor)" backend/ scripts/ --include="*.py" | wc -l

Writing a new # noqa: C901

Read the whole function first. If its branches are flat format/error handling, write the noqa with the flat-shape justification. If you found real nesting, mark it TODO(P2-refactor) — or better, extract a helper and drop the noqa entirely.

docs.title: 🛢️ The 3 RUF022 exceptions
docs.text:
__all__ is kept sorted everywhere except three barrel modules that group their exports by domain with section comments — sorting would scatter related names away from their group:

  • backend/app/db/__init__.py
  • backend/app/db/base.py
  • backend/app/schemas/__init__.py

Each carries # noqa: RUF022 — grouped by domain with section comments; sorting would scatter related names.

docs.title: 🪵 Logging inside except (TRY400 convention)
docs.text: Inside an exception handler, use logger.exception(...) — never logger.error(...): the former attaches the active traceback, the latter silently drops it. Audit 08 converted all 55 logger.error-in-except sites (03/09) and the codebase is TRY400-clean today (ruff check --select TRY400 passes), although the rule is not yet part of the select list — treat it as mandatory style regardless.

docs.title: 🧪 Beyond the linter: JSON validator vs sanitizer
docs.text:
Two JSON-safety helpers coexist with opposite error policies, and they must not be merged (audit 08, report 03 §N-03-A):

  • ensure_json_safe (backend/app/utils/json_utils.py) — the validator: recursively checks a value is natively JSON-serializable and raises ValueError otherwise. Used by Pydantic field_validators on contract boundaries (signals, AI Export payloads), where a non-JSON value means the producer is broken and must be rejected.
  • _json_safe_details (defined in backend/app/services/assets/core.py) — the sanitizer: stringifies anything non-primitive and never raises. It exists for one field (AssetSourceError.details in provider diagnostics), preserves None/empty as "omit the field", and sanitizes one list level deep — exactly what provider-error localization needs.

Rejecting and stringifying are opposite answers to the same input. If a boundary needs validation, call the validator; if a diagnostic field needs to survive arbitrary provider data, call the sanitizer. Never let one grow the other's behavior.

docs.title: 📖 API Reference
docs.text: LibreFolio provides a comprehensive RESTful API built with FastAPI.

docs.title: 🔗 Quick Links
docs.text:
• API Overview - Architecture and design patterns
  • cURL Testing Guide - How to test APIs from terminal

docs.title: 🖥️ Interactive Documentation
docs.text:
When the server runs in debug mode (./dev.py server --debug), you can access the interactive documentation generated from the code. These pages allow you to explore the API endpoints, see the expected request/response schemas, and even execute requests directly from your browser.

  • 🚀 Swagger UI : Best for exploring and testing endpoints.
  • 💻 ReDoc: Best for reading the documentation in a structured format.

Off on every other instance

/api/v1/docs, /api/v1/redoc and /api/v1/openapi.json exist only where the documentation is switched on: with ./dev.py server --debug, which sets LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS=1, with that variable set by hand, or in test mode (the test lanes). Anywhere else, Docker and managed instances included, they answer 404 to a client ({"detail": "Not Found"}): an instance in use publishes no map of its API. A browser's page request to one of them, to any other unknown address under /api/ or to a missing /mkdocs/ page is redirected (302) to / instead, by address_not_found() in backend/app/services/platform/static_site.py: it looks at Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate, or at an Accept that wants HTML when the header is missing. In the web app, frontend/src/routes/+error.svelte sends an unknown page back to the page the user came from, or to /dashboard. The links above therefore work on a debug server only.

The schema does not need the pages: ./dev.py api schema (and ./dev.py api sync, which adds the TypeScript client) builds it in process from the application, so it works whatever the instance serves (API & Frontend Communication). The pages are LibreFolio's own (backend/app/api/api_docs.py), with their libraries pinned and checked: see The Content-Security-Policy and Frame Protection.

docs.title: 🔀 Dynamic Route Generation
docs.text:
FastAPI generates the API routes dynamically at startup based on the Python function definitions. This ensures that the documentation is always perfectly in sync with the code.

The API is structured into routers, each handling a specific domain (all mounted under /api/v1 by backend/app/api/v1/router.py):

  • /auth: Authentication and the account's own actions. Sign-in and sign-out (/auth/login, /auth/logout): the session is a cookie that lasts session_ttl_hours, with no refresh token (Token Expiration). The current account (/auth/me), registration (/auth/register, with an invitation where the registration mode asks for one), the profile and the password (/auth/profile, /auth/change-password), and the deletion of one's own account (DELETE /auth/users/me, with its preview). The account's user carries whats_new, the changelog chapters left to show after an update, and POST /auth/whats-new/seen records that the user closed them (What's new). The links an account receives: inspect a token (/auth/tokens/inspect), the password reset (/auth/password-reset) and the initial administrator's setup (/auth/setup). The Address Probe (/auth/address-probe).
  • /users: User management.
  • /email: The instance's email: its state, a test email and the links an administrator sends (GET /email/status, POST /email/test, POST /email/links, administrators only), and, without a session, the «forgot password» email and the verification link (POST /email/password-reset, POST /email/verification/confirm, POST /email/verification/resend); see The API of the Email Service.
  • /security: The security checks of the instance, evaluated on demand (GET /security/checks, administrators only); see The Checks on Demand.
  • /settings: User settings, admin-managed global settings, scheduler state/logs, the cache admin routes (/settings/cache/status, /settings/cache/clear/{name}, /settings/cache/clear-all — see Cache Registry & Admin), and the plugin settings (/settings/plugins — see Plugin Settings).
  • /system: Server info (/system/info: the app version only without a session, everything with one), health check (/system/health), readiness (/system/ready, no session: 200 when the database answers and its schema is at the head revision, 503 otherwise, with migrations behind or ahead, the database's database_revision and the running app_version: see System Information and Readiness), plugin diagnostics (/system/plugin-diagnostics), the connection and container-image checks, the public instance configuration (/system/instance, no session: see Public instance configuration), the block page (/system/block, signed-in users only: whether the hosting provider blocked the instance, its deletion date and, for an administrator, where the subscription is managed and whether a backup can still be downloaded; see Instance Block), the catch-up of the prices (GET /system/price-refresh, signed-in users only: whether the scheduler is catching up on prices now, for the web app's notice Updating prices…; see Catch-up Progress), and the scheduled wake-up (POST /system/wake-sync, with the LIBREFOLIO_WAKE_TOKEN token instead of a session: it runs the scheduler's due jobs and streams their report). System Information and Readiness details /system/info and /system/ready. One module per resource in the backend/app/api/v1/system/ package, whose __init__.py only composes the /system router.
  • /uploads: File uploads and media serving.
  • /assets: Asset management (CRUD, price history) — includes /prices, /provider (search, live quotes), /events.
  • /transactions: Transaction management.
  • /brokers: Broker management and sharing — includes /import (BRIM broker report import).
  • /backup: Backup & export.
  • /panel: The hosting panel's routes: GET /panel/metrics (get_panel_metrics, lot CL-M1), the read-only figures of the instance (PanelMetricsResponse: fifteen keys, always all present, each null when it cannot be measured, never a 500; sizes in MiB, counts, the checks of the Security tab that are not ok as PanelConfigWarning, the failures of the last 24 hours counted from the scheduler's job log, which keeps 500 entries), opened by a signed ticket of scope metrics only (no token, 404 while LIBREFOLIO_PANEL_PUBLIC_KEYS is not set), allowed on a blocked instance and on one awaiting a restore; and the status route, GET /panel/status (get_panel_status), with the LIBREFOLIO_PANEL_STATUS_TOKEN token instead of a session: where the setup of the initial administrator stands, as admin_setup_status() reads it. Its answer, PanelStatusResponse, holds exactly ten keys: admin_setup, one of none, pending, done and expired; setup_expires_at, when the setup link stops working, in UTC, only while pending (null otherwise); mode, normal or awaiting_restore; and restore, PanelRestoreSummary (state, reason, waiting, backup_created_at, stage_id), null when no restore was ever recorded (lot H-62); when the state of the restore cannot be read, state is unreadable with reason io, not_a_file or invalid, still in a 200 (decision D7); state is committed with reason owner_assignment when the restore is done but the owner of the restored data has no account yet (CL-6); users_used, the places the users take, as user_usage() counts them (lot H5-1); users_limit, LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS, null when it is not set or cannot be used (the route never answers 500 because of it): two counts, never a name, an email address or an id; owner_email_change, pending, blocked or null, where the change of the owner's address a hosting provider started stands, as instance_owner.owner_change_status() reads it (lot H5-4, workstream A's module): never the address; and instance_key, ok or mismatch, whether the instance key is the one its data was written with (The Key Check, lot H5-7): never the fingerprint; and users_over_limit, a boolean, true while the active accounts outnumber the limit of the plan, as user_limit_service.over_limit_state() reads it (Over the limit, lot H5-8): a yes or no, never who; and owner_language, en, it, fr, es or null, the language the owner chose in their account settings (null without an owner or without a chosen language, CL-9). Responses 200, 401, 404 (no token set: the route is off), 429 and 503; it answers on a blocked instance too. Its OpenAPI tag is «Hosting panel», the only tag of the fourteen routes a hosting panel calls: the two /panel routes, the four /backup/panel/jobs… routes, the seven /backup/panel/restore… routes (scope backup:restore, a signed ticket only: see Awaiting Restore) and POST /system/wake-sync. See The Hosting Panel's Access.
  • /portfolio: Portfolio analysis and metrics.
  • /fx: Foreign exchange operations — includes /fx/providers and /fx/currencies.
  • /signals: Domain-agnostic signal preview (POST /signals/preview).
  • /risk: Risk analysis — analytics catalog, queries, scenario catalog, and per-asset eligibility for a period (POST /risk/eligibility). The Asset Detail risk view and the What if…? simulation still carry a beta notice.
  • /ai-export: Versioned AI Export datasets and analyses.
  • /tools: Atomic Tool calculations — catalog, batch compute (POST /tools/compute), and per-process diagnostics; see Tool plugins.
  • /utilities: Reference data (ISO currencies, etc.).

On an instance blocked by its hosting provider (LIBREFOLIO_BLOCKED), every route but a short list answers 423 Locked with detail.code instance_blocked to a signed-in user, and 401 to a caller without a valid session, the public routes outside the list included: see Instance Block.

While the hosting panel restores an instance (LIBREFOLIO_AWAIT_RESTORE), every route but the probes, /system/instance, the scheduled wake-up and the panel's routes answers 423 Locked with detail.code instance_awaiting_restore, to anyone, signed in or not: see Awaiting Restore.

When the process found the state of the restore (.restore/restore.json) unreadable at its start, the same routes answer, but the panel's backup start, which answers 409 backup_restore_interrupted once the panel's credential is checked, and every other one answers 423 Locked with detail.code instance_restore_interrupted, to anyone, until the administrator runs ./dev.py backup pending --recover previous and restarts LibreFolio; GET /system/instance then says restore_interrupted: true and restore_interrupted_reason: "restore_state". The same answers hold, with the reason owner_assignment, while the owner of an instance restored from the app has no account yet (./dev.py backup pending --recover owner when it could not be given): see A Restore Stopped Half Way.

When the instance key is not the one the data was written with (instance_key: "mismatch" in GET /panel/status), the instance keeps serving, and only two things of the hosting panel stop: its backup start answers 409 backup_instance_key_mismatch, once the panel's credential is checked, and POST /system/wake-sync runs no job and answers the status instance_key_mismatch: see The Key Check.

docs.title: 📋 Pydantic Schemas
docs.text: The API uses Pydantic models for data validation and serialization. These schemas define the structure of the data exchanged between the frontend and backend. You can find the schema definitions in the backend/app/schemas/ directory.

docs.title: 🧪 API Testing with cURL
docs.text: This guide explains how to test LibreFolio's REST API using cURL from the terminal.

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication
docs.text: LibreFolio uses session-based authentication with HTTP-only cookies. To make authenticated API calls, you must first login and then pass the session cookie.

docs.title: 1️⃣ Step 1: Login and Get Session Cookie
docs.text:
# Login and save the session cookie
curl -v -X POST http://localhost:6040/api/v1/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"YOUR_USERNAME","password":"YOUR_PASSWORD"}' \
  -c /tmp/cookies.txt

This will:

  1. Send login credentials
  2. Receive a Set-Cookie header with the session token
  3. Save the cookie to /tmp/cookies.txt

Example response:

{
  "user": {
    "id": 1,
    "username": "alfy",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "is_active": true,
    "is_superuser": true
  },
  "message": "Login successful"
}

docs.title: 2️⃣ Step 2: Make Authenticated Requests
docs.text:
Use the -b flag to send the saved cookie:

# Get current user info
curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/auth/me

# List brokers
curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers

# List uploaded files
curl -s -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/uploads

docs.title: 🔑 Alternative: Direct Cookie Header
docs.text:
If -b doesn't work, you can extract the cookie from the login response and use it directly:

# From the login response, copy the session value from Set-Cookie header
# Example: session=PL4H9KVBq2...

# Use it directly
curl -s http://localhost:6040/api/v1/auth/me \
  -H "Cookie: session=YOUR_SESSION_TOKEN_HERE"

docs.title: 🏥 Health Check (No Auth Required)
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:6040/api/v1/system/health
# Returns: {"status":"ok"}

# Readiness: does the database answer, is its schema at the head revision? (-i shows the status code)
curl -i http://localhost:6040/api/v1/system/ready
# 200: {"status":"ready","checks":{"database":"ok","migrations":"ok"},"database_revision":"<revision>","mode":"normal","app_version":"<version>"}
# 503: {"status":"not_ready","checks":{"database":"ok","migrations":"behind"},"database_revision":"<revision>","mode":"normal","app_version":"<version>"}

# System info: the app version only without the cookie, everything with it
curl http://localhost:6040/api/v1/system/info
# Returns: {"app_version":"v1.2.0"}
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/system/info

The codes of /system/ready are listed in System Information and Readiness.

docs.title: 👤 User Management
docs.text:
# Get current user
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/auth/me

# Read your settings (language, base currency, theme, avatar)
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/settings/user

# Update them: every field is optional (language, base_currency, theme, avatar_url), an omitted one stays as it is
curl -X PUT -b /tmp/cookies.txt \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"language":"it","base_currency":"EUR"}' \
  http://localhost:6040/api/v1/settings/user

docs.title: 🏦 Brokers
docs.text:
# List all brokers
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers

# Get broker by ID (broker fields plus the caller's user_role and user_share_percentage)
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers/1

docs.title: 📥 BRIM (Broker Report Import)
docs.text:
# List BRIM files
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers/import/files

# Filter by status
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt "http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers/import/files?status=uploaded"

# Filter by broker IDs
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt "http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers/import/files?broker_ids=1&broker_ids=2"

# Upload a file (broker_id is a required form field)
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt \
  -F "file=@/path/to/report.csv" \
  -F "broker_id=1" \
  http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers/import/upload

# Get available plugins
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/brokers/import/plugins

docs.title: 📁 Static Files
docs.text:
# List uploaded files
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt http://localhost:6040/api/v1/uploads

# Upload a file
curl -b /tmp/cookies.txt \
  -F "file=@/path/to/image.png" \

docs.title: 🧰 Useful cURL Flags
docs.text: Flag Description -s Silent mode (no progress bar) -v Verbose (show headers) -i Include response headers -X METHOD HTTP method (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE) -H "Header: value" Add request header -d 'data' Send request body -F "file=@path" Send multipart form (file upload) -b file Send cookies from file -c file Save cookies to file -o file Save response to file -O Save with original filename -w "\n%{http_code}" Print HTTP status code

docs.title: 🧪 Test Mode
docs.text:
To test against the test database (port 6041):

# Start server in test mode
./dev.py server --test

# Use port 6041 for all requests
curl http://localhost:6041/api/v1/system/health

docs.title: 📖 API Documentation
docs.text:
For complete API documentation, start the server with ./dev.py server --debug and visit:

  • Swagger UI: http://localhost:6040/api/v1/docs
  • ReDoc: http://localhost:6040/api/v1/redoc
  • OpenAPI JSON: http://localhost:6040/api/v1/openapi.json

These three exist only in debug mode (LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS) and in test mode (port 6041); on any other instance they answer 404. ./dev.py api schema exports the schema without a running server.

docs.title: 🌐 API & Frontend Communication
docs.text: This section explains how the SvelteKit frontend communicates with the FastAPI backend, ensuring type safety and consistency across the stack.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
LibreFolio uses a strict OpenAPI-first approach (generated from code) to synchronize the backend and frontend.

graph LR
    Backend[FastAPI Backend] -- "Generates" --> OpenAPI[openapi.json]
    OpenAPI -- "openapi-zod-client" --> TSClient[generated.ts]
    TSClient -- "Imports" --> Frontend[SvelteKit Frontend]

    Frontend -- "Calls" --> TSClient
    TSClient -- "Validates (Zod)" --> TSClient
    TSClient -- "HTTP Request" --> Backend

docs.title: 🔄 The Synchronization Workflow
docs.text:
The synchronization process is automated via dev.py:

  1. Backend Definition: API endpoints and Pydantic models are defined in Python (backend/app/api/).
  2. Schema Export: ./dev.py api schema imports the application in a temporary process (scripts/list_api_endpoints.py) and writes app.openapi() to the openapi.json file. It starts no server and does not depend on LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS: the /api/v1/openapi.json route, like the Swagger UI and ReDoc pages, exists only on debug and test instances.
  3. Client Generation: ./dev.py api client uses openapi-zod-client to read the JSON schema and generate a TypeScript client (frontend/src/lib/api/generated.ts).

One-step sync

Use ./dev.py api sync to run both steps (schema export + client generation) in a single command. This is the recommended workflow after any backend API change.

docs.title: 💻 CLI Commands
docs.text:
# Export OpenAPI schema only
./dev.py api schema

# Generate TypeScript client from existing schema
./dev.py api client

# Both in one step (recommended)
./dev.py api sync

docs.title: ⚡ Generated Client Features
docs.text:
The generated client provides:

  • TypeScript Interfaces: Matching the Pydantic models (e.g., AssetRead, TransactionCreate).
  • Zod Schemas: Runtime validation schemas for API responses.
  • API Functions: Typed functions for each endpoint (e.g., api.getAssets()).

docs.title: 🖥️ Usage in Frontend
docs.text:
In the SvelteKit frontend, developers import the generated client to make API calls.

import { api } from '$lib/api';

async function loadPortfolio() {
    // 'data' is fully typed as PortfolioResponse
    const data = await api.getPortfolio();
    return data;
}

This ensures that if the backend API changes (e.g., a field is renamed), the frontend build will fail with a type error, preventing runtime crashes.

docs.title: 📜 Contract Rules
docs.text: Four rules the pipeline depends on. Breaking one of the first three fails the frontend build, not a backend test — which is why they are written down here. Rule 4 has a backend guard of its own: what it breaks can pass the build and fail only when the browser loads the client.

docs.title: 1. Every endpoint declares response_model
docs.text: Every API endpoint declares an explicit response_model Pydantic schema: the generated client is only as typed as the OpenAPI schema, and an endpoint without a model silently degrades to unknown. The audit (08) closed the last stragglers; the deliberate exceptions are endpoints that do not return JSON documents — the SSE stream (GET /assets/provider/search/stream), binary file downloads (FileResponse under /uploads/file/…, /brokers/import/files/…/download; inline only for the safe types of INLINE_SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES, an attachment otherwise: How a file is served), and a handful of legacy dict returns.

docs.title: 2. New discriminated-union members register in fix-openapi-discriminators.mjs
docs.text:
Pydantic discriminated unions (Annotated[A | B, Field(discriminator="kind")]) generate correct OpenAPI, but openapi-zod-client exports each member as const Member: z.ZodType<Member> = … — the exported z.ZodType<T> annotation hides the ZodObject methods that z.discriminatedUnion needs, and the generated client fails to compile. The post-processor frontend/scripts/fix-openapi-discriminators.mjs strips that annotation for a hardcoded list of schemas (56 today), letting TypeScript infer the concrete type while keeping the exported alias. It runs as part of npm run generate-api (which ./dev.py api sync / ./dev.py api client wrap) and throws if a registered schema is not found exactly once — a stale entry fails loud, never silently.

When you add a new member to a discriminated union, add its schema name to discriminatedSchemas in frontend/scripts/fix-openapi-discriminators.mjs, then re-run ./dev.py api sync.

docs.title: 3. Discriminator fields carry an explicit enum
docs.text:
The discriminator field of each union member must pin its value with Field(json_schema_extra={"enum": [...]}):

class SchedulerLogCurrentPriceEntry(BaseModel):
    job: Literal["current_price"] = Field(json_schema_extra={"enum": ["current_price"]})

Without the extra, the discriminator is emitted without an enum constraint and the generated TypeScript client fails to compile (real incident, 03/09 — the scheduler log union). This pattern is used across schemas/signals.py, schemas/ai_export_runtime.py, schemas/risk.py, schemas/risk_scenarios.py, schemas/settings.py, schemas/portfolio.py, and schemas/tools.py.

docs.title: 4. Descriptions must survive the client generator
docs.text:
./dev.py api sync pastes the descriptions of the OpenAPI document — model docstrings, Field(description=…), endpoint docstrings — into frontend/src/lib/api/generated.ts without escaping them for JavaScript: in a .describe(), a text with a line break becomes a raw template literal and a one-line text a raw double-quoted string. With openapi-zod-client 1.18.3 and the generate-api flags --export-types --with-docs --with-description:

Where the text lands in generated.ts Written as Must not contain .describe() of a property, of list items or dictionary values, of a parameter (trimmed) — text with a line break raw template literal a backtick, ${ (becomes a substitution), a backslash the same — one-line text raw double-quoted string a double quote, a backslash (a backtick is fine) endpoint description, non-2xx response descriptions, request-body description template literal written by Handlebars, which HTML-escapes backticks and quotes ${, a backslash JSDoc inside an exported type (inline fields, list items, union members) /** … */ comment */ in the description, pattern, enum, default or examples

In a multi-line .describe() a pair of backticks is a syntax error, and a doubled ``code`` parses as a tagged template that throws TypeError: "…" is not a function when the client loads: every page goes blank (real incident, 15/10 — the EmailInstanceConfig docstring). A backslash is either a syntax error (\x, \u, a trailing one) or a silently changed text. A property that is a $ref carries the docstring of the model or enum it references; a description set on the field itself is ignored. List items and dictionary values work the other way round: a description set beside the reference is written, the model's docstring is not. Many model and enum docstrings span lines with backticks today, harmless only because no schema uses one of them directly as a field (only in lists, unions, request bodies and responses): using one directly as a field is enough to break the client.

The pure pytest backend/test_scripts/test_schemas/test_openapi_client_text.py, run with ./dev.py test schemas openapi-client-text, reads app.openapi() — the same source as api sync — and fails naming the exact field, form and character. It is conservative: it may flag a text the current client would not carry, but never misses one. It also fails when the generator version in frontend/package-lock.json (1.18.3, pinned in the guard) or the generate-api flags change: re-verify these rules before moving the pinned version.

When the guard is red, keep a model docstring or field description on one line without " or \, or rephrase the text without backticks, ${ and \; move a long explanation into a code comment (the fix of the incident above). Never put */ in the description, pattern, enum, default or examples of any schema.

docs.title: 🗜️ Response Compression
docs.text:
Starlette's GZipMiddleware (minimum_size=1024, compresslevel=6) is the gzip entry of MIDDLEWARE_STACK (backend/app/services/platform/middleware.py), inside activity and security_headers and outside cors (the whole stack: Steps and Middleware: the Contract). install_middleware(app) puts the stack on the whole application, so GZip covers API JSON as well as the SvelteKit bundle and the documentation served by the same process.

  • A response is compressed only when the request's Accept-Encoding header contains gzip. Browsers send it and decompress transparently, so frontend code never handles compressed bytes.
  • A compressed response carries Content-Encoding: gzip. Its Content-Length is the compressed size; a streamed response drops the header.
  • Vary: Accept-Encoding is added to every response eligible for compression — 1 KiB or more, or streamed — whether or not the client asked for gzip, so a cache keeps the two variants apart.
  • Left untouched: bodies under 1 KiB sent in one piece, responses that already declare a Content-Encoding, 206 Partial Content range replies, Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream, such as GET /assets/provider/search/stream), AVIF, GIF, JPEG, PNG, and WebP images, WOFF and WOFF2 fonts, audio, video, and gzip or zip archives. SVG is text and is compressed.
  • A body chunk of 128 KiB or more is compressed in a worker thread, off the event loop.

curl sends no Accept-Encoding by default and therefore receives the uncompressed body. With --compressed it asks for gzip and decompresses transparently:

# Print the response headers of the compressed variant (Content-Encoding, Vary)
# (/api/v1/openapi.json exists on a debug server only: ./dev.py server --debug)
curl -s --compressed -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:6040/api/v1/openapi.json

docs.title: POST /api/v1/assets/prices/current — Bulk Current Price
docs.text:
Returns the current price of each asset in a list: the assigned provider's latest quote, or the last close stored in the database when no provider answers. The response is designed for the frontend's live-price polling.

Request body: List[int] — asset IDs.

Response (FACurrentPriceResponse, a BaseBulkResponse): one results item per requested ID, in request order; success_count, the number of items that carry a value; and errors, for operation-level errors, which this endpoint leaves empty — a per-asset problem goes in the item's error, and a failure of the whole call is an HTTP 500.

{
  "results": [
    {
      "asset_id": 1,
      "value": "123.45",
      "currency": "EUR",
      "as_of_date": "2026-04-10",
      "source": "provider:justetf",
      "error": null,
      "error_code": null,
      "retry_after": null
    },
    {
      "asset_id": 2,
      "value": "98.32",
      "currency": "USD",
      "as_of_date": "2026-04-09",
      "source": "db:last_known",
      "error": null,
      "error_code": "RATE_LIMITED",
      "retry_after": 1834.6
    },
    {
      "asset_id": 3,
      "value": null,
      "currency": null,
      "as_of_date": null,
      "source": null,
      "error": "No price data available",
      "error_code": null,
      "retry_after": null
    }
  ],
  "success_count": 2,
  "errors": []
}

value is a decimal string, and as_of_date is a date (YYYY-MM-DD), not a timestamp.

Resolution strategy (per asset, all assets in parallel — get_current_prices_bulk in backend/app/services/assets/price_query.py):

  1. If a provider is assigned, ask its get_current_value() — at most five calls at a time, ten seconds each — and answer with source: "provider:<code>", the value as the price columns keep it (storable_current_value(); X-R40, W-B62): in its own form when the history's truncation (12 decimal places, then 15 significant digits, rounded down) leaves it unchanged (101.5 stays 101.5), truncated otherwise (65432.1234567890999 → 65432.123456789). Only such a quote is cached, for two minutes, and a cached one is answered the same way. What "current" means is up to the provider: JustETF answers EUR with a real-time gettex quote, kept up to date by a WebSocket feed per ISIN, and otherwise (other currencies, or no quote) with the latest daily quote of its chart API; Yahoo Finance reads regularMarketPrice from ticker.info (then currentPrice or previousClose).
  2. Fallback: with no usable provider, when its call fails or times out, or when its quote is one no price column can keep (not finite, more than 12 digits before the decimal point, non-zero but 0 once truncated, such as 1E-13, or, since N92, not above 0: never answered, cached or written), return the latest close stored in PriceHistory that reads a number (one stored as ±inf is passed over), with source: "db:last_known". A provider paused after «too many requests» is not called at all, and one that refuses is paused (Provider Pauses): the item then also carries error_code: "RATE_LIMITED" and retry_after, the seconds until the provider may be called again, as asset 2 above.
  3. With no stored price either, value is null and error is No price data available — still with error_code and retry_after when the provider is paused — or Asset not found for an unknown ID.

Side effect: the call is not read-only. A provider quote dated today creates today's PriceHistory row (open, high, low and close all equal to the quote) or extends it (high and low widened, open set if missing, close replaced). A database fallback is never written back.

This endpoint is used by the Assets list (inline live prices on cards and table rows) and by the asset detail page (price summary and chart head) — see Live Prices.

docs.title: 🔎 GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search and /search/stream — Asset Search
docs.text:
Both search, in parallel, every provider with search support, or those named in providers, for the signed-in user: each provider receives that user's personal plugin settings, such as justETF's preferred currency (Plugin Settings). A provider that fails never fails the request; the answer says which one, and why:

  • /search answers FAProviderSearchResponse once every provider is done: results, providers_queried, providers_with_errors (every provider that failed) and providers_not_configured, those of them not called because a required setting has no value (NOT_CONFIGURED); an empty list otherwise.
  • /search/stream answers Server-Sent Events: one per provider as soon as it finishes, then done. The stream has no response_model (rule 1 of the Contract Rules above), so its events are not in the generated client:
data: {"event": "provider_results", "provider_code": "justetf", "results": [...]}

data: {"event": "provider_error", "provider_code": "my_provider", "error": "Provider my_provider is not configured: api_key missing", "error_code": "NOT_CONFIGURED"}

data: {"event": "provider_error", "provider_code": "yfinance", "error": "Provider yfinance is paused after too many requests: 1835 s left", "error_code": "RATE_LIMITED", "retry_after": 1834.6}

data: {"event": "done", "total_results": 12, "providers_queried": [...], "providers_with_errors": [...]}

provider_error carries error_code for every AssetSourceError: NOT_CONFIGURED, RATE_LIMITED with retry_after (the seconds before the provider may be called again), or the provider's own code, such as SEARCH_ERROR. An error of any other type has neither field. The search box, AssetSearchAutocomplete.svelte, reads the stream and falls back to /search only when the stream is unavailable; for each provider not configured it shows a row with Configure. Details: Interactive Search Stack.

docs.title: 🔐 Broker Access Control (RBAC)
docs.text: LibreFolio implements a granular Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system for Brokers. This allows users to share access to their brokerage accounts with other users (e.g., family members, accountants) while maintaining control over permissions.

docs.title: 📖 Overview
docs.text:
Access is managed via the BrokerUserAccess table, which links a User to a Broker with a specific UserRole.

erDiagram
    USER ||--o{ BROKER_USER_ACCESS : "has access"
    BROKER ||--o{ BROKER_USER_ACCESS : "granted to"

    BROKER_USER_ACCESS {
        int user_id FK
        int broker_id FK
        enum role "OWNER, EDITOR, VIEWER"
        decimal share_percentage "0..1, OWNER-only, scales aggregation"
    }

docs.title: 🛡️ Roles and Permissions
docs.text:
There are three roles with increasing levels of privilege:

Feature VIEWER EDITOR OWNER View Broker Details ✅ ✅ ✅ View Transactions ✅ ✅ ✅ View Reports/Charts ✅ ✅ ✅ View Report Files (BRIM) ✅ ✅ ✅ Add/Edit Transactions ❌ ✅ ✅ Upload/Parse/Delete Files (BRIM) ❌ ✅ ✅ Edit Broker Settings ❌ ✅ ✅ Manage Access (Add/Remove Users) ❌ ❌ ✅ Delete Broker ❌ ❌ ✅

For BRIM report files the administrator (is_superuser) needs no role, a file with no broker is its uploader's and the administrator's only, and a parse also needs EDITOR or OWNER on the broker it imports into: see Who reaches a report file.

docs.title: 📋 Role Definitions
docs.text:
1. 👁️ VIEWER: Read-only access. Ideal for sharing portfolio visibility without risk of data modification.
  2. ✏️ EDITOR: Operational access. Can manage the day-to-day data (transactions, imports) and broker settings (name, icon), but cannot perform destructive administrative actions (deleting the broker) or change who has access.
  3. 👑 OWNER: Administrative access. Full control over the broker.

docs.title: 📊 Ownership share (share_percentage)
docs.text:
Each access row carries a share_percentage (0.000000–1.000000) used only for portfolio aggregation, never for permissions:

  • OWNER: the broker's creator gets 1.00; through PUT /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access, every OWNER gets the share its item carries — 0 when the item has none, even for an OWNER already on the broker. The share may be reduced for co-ownership (e.g. joint accounts); EDITOR and VIEWER default to 0.00 (delegated operator, read-only accountant).
  • The sum of shares across a broker's users must not exceed 1.00 (validated on add/update); it can be less (a co-owner may simply not be in the system).
  • 0 % is a valid share: a 0 % OWNER keeps full admin rights but contributes nothing to the owner's aggregated numbers.
  • Aggregation scales by share only for OWNERs — EDITOR/VIEWER rows always carry share 0 by schema rule yet see full data, so the engine uses scale 1 for them (effective_share() in financial_math/native_cash.py, through broker_shares(), called by portfolio_service.py and financial_math/portfolio/engine.py). Role/share edits change every scaled number but not the underlying data, so they also join the cache fingerprint for instant invalidation.
  • apply_ownership_share=False on the report and the positions series (for the broker page) skips the scaling: every broker counts whole, as an EDITOR sees it, whatever the role and the share (native_cash.broker_shares(), the whole broker).

docs.title: 🔒 The "Last Owner" Rule
docs.text:
To prevent brokers from becoming "orphaned" (left without an OWNER to manage their access or delete them), the system enforces a strict rule:

A broker always keeps at least one OWNER. The last OWNER cannot be removed or downgraded — by anyone, themselves included — but can leave, and leaving deletes the broker.

If a broker has only one user with the OWNER role:

  • ❌ Nobody — neither that user nor the administrator — can remove them or change their role to EDITOR or VIEWER without making another user OWNER: PUT /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access (bulk_update_access()) refuses any configuration without an OWNER (400, "At least one OWNER is required").
  • ❌ That user cannot demote themselves with PATCH /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access/me (update_own_role()): 400, "The last OWNER cannot demote themselves — promote another user first".
  • ⚠️ That user can leave with DELETE /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access/me (leave_broker()), and leaving deletes the broker with its transactions: see Self-Management.
  • ✅ To leave without deleting the broker, they first make another user OWNER with the PUT; they can then leave, or drop their own row in that same PUT.

docs.title: 🔧 Self-Management
docs.text:
• 🚪 Leaving: any user can remove themselves from a broker at any time (leave_broker). EDITOR/VIEWER always succeed. An OWNER may leave when at least one other OWNER remains — otherwise leaving as the last OWNER deletes the broker entirely. Its transactions do not go by a database cascade: delete_by_broker() deletes them, and the other half of a pair held on another broker stays there without its link — as the standalone row a split of the pair leaves or, for the giving leg of a TRANSFER whose cost needs a missing conversion, still a TRANSFER (see Broker Deletion). BRIM report files are cleaned up by the API layer.
  • ⬇️ Self-demotion (update_own_role): EDITOR → VIEWER is always allowed; OWNER → EDITOR/VIEWER is allowed only when another OWNER remains, and demoting from OWNER zeroes the share (only OWNERs may hold share > 0). Promotions go through the PUT, OWNER or administrator only.
  • 🗑️ Deleting an account applies leave_broker() to every broker of the account, in one commit: see Deleting an Account.

docs.title: 🔧 Implementation Details
docs.text:
The logic is centralized in backend/app/services/brokers/access.py (BrokerAccessMixin, part of BrokerService).

  • 🔍 _check_user_access(broker_id, user_id, min_role): Core internal method to verify permissions.
  • 📋 list_accesses(): The users with access to a broker, with role and share.
  • 🔄 bulk_update_access(): Replaces a broker's whole access configuration in one step (OWNER or administrator): adds, role changes and removals; at least one OWNER must remain, and the shares add up to at most 100 %.
  • 🚪 leave_broker() / update_own_role(): The self-service paths described above.

docs.title: 🌐 API Endpoints
docs.text:
Access management is exposed via the following endpoints (backend/app/api/v1/brokers.py):

  • GET /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access: the users with access, with role and share (list_accesses()). Any authenticated user can read the list of any existing broker, email addresses included; 404 only when the broker does not exist.
  • PUT /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access: replaces the whole access configuration in one step (bulk_update_access()). The body is the complete desired list of {user_id, role, share_percentage}: users missing from it lose their access, new ones are added, roles and shares are updated, in one transaction. Granting, changing and revoking access all go through it. OWNER or administrator only (403 otherwise); 400 when a rule fails (no OWNER, shares adding up to more than 1.0, a duplicate or unknown user); 422 for an empty list or a share the schema refuses (outside 0–1, or above 0 for an EDITOR or VIEWER).
  • PATCH /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access/me: self-demotion only (update_own_role()), body {role}; 400 for any other change and for the last OWNER's demotion, 403 without access to the broker.
  • DELETE /api/v1/brokers/{broker_id}/access/me: leave the broker (leave_broker()); the response's broker_deleted is true when the last OWNER's leaving deleted it. 403 without access to the broker.

docs.title: 👑 Superusers and the User CLI
docs.text:
Besides the broker roles, every account carries one system-wide flag, users.is_superuser: the administrator of the admin manual. It belongs to the account, not to a broker.

  • Granted to the first account registered (POST /api/v1/auth/register while first_account_open() holds, that is while count_users() is 0, inactive accounts counted: accepted whatever the registration mode, and an administrator even when the invitation it spends grants a regular account), to an account registered with an invitation that grants it (grants_admin, see Invitations), to an account created with ./dev.py user create without --role user (--role admin is the default: scripts/user_cli.py maps it to its internal create-superuser command, which calls user_service.create_user() with is_superuser=True), by ./dev.py user promote, and by PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id} with is_superuser: true. ./dev.py user create … --role user maps to the internal create-user command instead (is_superuser=False): a regular account, even as the first account of an empty database. The administrator of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL is a superuser from its creation by the startup, inactive until its setup link is spent (The Initial Administrator).
  • Promote and demote go through user_service.set_user_admin() from the CLI, which refuses a no-op (already an admin, not an admin), the demotion of the last active administrator and, since lot A-43, the demotion of the initial administrator waiting for its setup, and through user_service.update_user_status() from the administrator API, whose route refuses that demotion first (409 PENDING_SETUP). A demotion also ends every session of the account (user_service.end_sessions() raises users.session_version, see Session Revocation); a promotion does not. Self-deletion has the same guard: DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/me answers 400 to an administrator when no other active administrator remains (count_active_superusers(), counted under the write lock since lot A-52: see Decided under the write lock), with detail {"error_code": "LAST_ADMIN", "message": "Cannot delete account: you are the last active administrator"} since lot A-16 (a bare sentence before); the deletion dialog words it with its own key (Account Errors). The administrator API deletes no administrator, active or not: DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id} answers 409 DEMOTE_FIRST until the account is demoted (Deleting an Account), except for the initial administrator waiting for its setup, which cannot be demoted and is deleted directly.
  • Stale reads (lot A-51): set_user_active() (user deactivate, user activate), set_user_admin() (user promote, user demote) and update_user_status() (the administrator API) read the account again under SQLite's write lock before they decide (refreshed_under_lock(), see Decided under the write lock): the last-administrator guard, then «waiting», which set_user_admin() reads to refuse a demotion, and set_user_active() and update_user_status() to tell a cancellation from a deactivation (A setup completed meanwhile). The account they first read may be stale: on a new instance whose only account is the initial administrator waiting for its setup, the setup can complete in the same millisecond as the command. Read stale, user demote used to remove the only administrator, and user deactivate to answer success and end the new owner's sessions without deactivating it, since the column it set was equal to the stale value. Both now refuse it as the last active administrator, nothing changed.
  • Applied at the next request: the user CLI writes the database directly, with the server running or not, and get_current_user() reloads the user on every request. A deactivated account (user deactivate, user_service.set_user_active(), or the administrator API) gets 401 User account is disabled; its login, with the right password, gets 403 ACCOUNT_DISABLED — or 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED while it waits for its email verification. Deactivation refuses the last active administrator, and ends every session of the account: user activate lets the user sign in again, but brings none of the old sessions back.
  • Password reset (user reset, user_service.reset_password()) sets the new hash, computed in a worker thread off the event loop, and ends every session of the account in the same commit: each device gets 401 at its next request, and signs in again with the new password. The same commit revokes the account's live password-reset links (A-27) and retires its setup links (A-32, The Initial Administrator). A password-reset link does the same when it is spent. To keep the account out altogether, deactivate it.
  • The account's own changes end its other sessions as well: a password change (POST /api/v1/auth/change-password) and an email change (PUT /api/v1/auth/profile, which asks for the current password: see Changing the Email). The device that made the change gets a new cookie and stays signed in; a username change ends no session. Every change that ends sessions is in Session Revocation.
  • A new address revokes the account's live email_change links together with its password-reset and setup links (user_service.update_profile, A5-4): a change of address asked for before cannot move it again. On a managed instance, ./dev.py user reassign-owner <username> (cmd_reassign_owner) takes an account back to the address of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL: it runs instance_owner.assign_owner_and_send_reset, the treatment of a restore (unusable password, sessions ended, links neutralised, one reset link), and refuses on a non-managed profile.
  • Password rules: create and reset call validate_password() in scripts/user_cli.py, a thin wrapper over password_policy.failed_rules(): the same rules as the API and the app (Password Rules), checked before anything is read from the database. Each rule missed prints a line that starts with its code, such as digit: the password must contain a digit, and the command exits with 1.
  • Usernames and addresses (lot A-21a): create refuses a username holding @ and, since lot A-46, one outside 3 to 50 characters, as registration and the Profile do; create and set-email refuse an address that is another account's username, in any A–Z case: through user_service.create_user() and user_service.update_profile(). The command prints the service's message after ❌ — A username cannot contain @: the sign-in reads it as an email address, A username must be 3 to 50 characters long, or Email already registered — and exits with 1, writing nothing. The service's refusal is an AccountError, a str that also carries a code (lot A-47), which the API reads instead of the message. See Which Account an Identifier Names.

The admin commands are in Command-Line Tools.

docs.title: 🚪 Registration, Invitations and the Admin API
docs.text: Who may create an account, how many accounts an instance may hold, and what an administrator can do to the other accounts. The rules are in backend/app/services/accounts/registration_service.py, the account changes in user_service.py, and the variables in backend/app/config/accounts.py (administrator side: Configuration, section «Accounts and Sign-ups»). The administrator an operator creates from the environment has its own section: The Initial Administrator.

docs.title: 🎚️ Registration Modes
docs.text:
effective_registration_mode(session) returns a RegistrationModeState(mode, locked): LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION when it is set (blank counts as unset; case and surrounding spaces are ignored), with locked=True; otherwise the global setting registration_mode (Settings System), with locked=False.

The default of that setting is invite (decision 36), and it has one source: GLOBAL_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS in backend/app/schemas/settings.py. The startup seeding writes it on a new install, and get_setting_value() answers it while the row is missing: the service passes no fallback of its own. The seeding creates only missing rows, so an existing install keeps its row, whatever its value. An install that holds accounts but no row has run with the earlier default, open: step 5 of migration 005_release_1_3_0_schema writes that open row before the seeding runs (GLOBAL_SETTING), so an upgrade never closes registration in silence.

Mode POST /api/v1/auth/register accepts open Anyone. An invite_token is optional, but must be a valid invitation when given, and then sets the role invite Only a valid invitation disabled Nobody, invitations included

Both sources fail closed. A LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION that is not a mode makes the mode disabled, and still locks the setting: registration_mode_pinned() only asks whether the variable is set. A stored value that is not a mode also reads as disabled. Either is logged by _report_invalid() as the error event Invalid account configuration, with two fields: problem, the variable or the row and its value, and consequence, registration stays closed until it is fixed. The function is a functools.cache, so each problem is logged once per process. The startup configuration checks do not cover these variables.

register_user() holds the rule of POST /api/v1/auth/register (AuthRegisterRequest, with an optional invite_token) and owns its transaction. The route checks the password before calling it, so PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK comes first:

Situation Outcome A password that misses a password rule 400 PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK, with rules, the codes missed. Checked by the route before anything else — the mode, the invitation, the limit, a taken username or email — the first account included. Nothing is written, and an invitation given with it stays unspent No account at all (first_account_open(): count_users() is 0, an inactive account counts) Created as an administrator, whatever the mode, the limit and the role of an invitation. Without an invite_token, nothing else is checked. With one, the invitation must be valid — otherwise 400 INVITE_INVALID, and the instance stays empty — and the registration spends it as any other does (row A valid invitation): its link then reads consumed Mode disabled 403 REGISTRATION_DISABLED Mode invite, no invite_token 403 INVITE_REQUIRED A token that is not a valid invitation: unknown, of another purpose, expired, used or revoked 400 INVITE_INVALID A valid invitation Created in the invitation's role (grants_admin; the first account is an administrator whatever it says). The account and the consumption of the invitation (consumed_by_user_id) are committed together. The limit is not checked: the invitation already holds its place Mode open, no invite_token Created as a regular account, within the user limit require_email_verification on, any account but the first Created inactive, with a verification token that holds its place; the answer says verification_required: true and verification_email: "sending", and the email goes after it — unless the client address already had the emails of LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS registrations in the hour (20 by default): the answer then says verification_email: "held", the account waits without its email, and its owner, told so by the sign-in, asks for the link again from there. "sending" means queued, not delivered; verification_email is null without verification. With no email with a link able to go out, 409 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE, and nothing is created: an invitation stays unspent. See Email Verification A username holding @ (lot A-21a: the sign-in reads it as an email address, see Which Account an Identifier Names) 400 USERNAME_INVALID, the first check of create_user(), after the mode and the invitation; the first account included. register_user() raises it from the code of the service's refusal, USERNAME_INVALID, never from its wording (lot A-47). Nothing is written, and an invitation given with it stays unspent. A username outside 3 to 50 characters never reaches it: AuthRegisterRequest answers 422 first Username or email already taken, or an email that is another account's username, in any A–Z case (lot A-21a) 400, with the plain-string detail it always had: Username already taken, Email already registered. Any refusal of create_user() but USERNAME_INVALID (USERNAME_TAKEN, EMAIL_TAKEN) becomes the RegistrationError ACCOUNT_EXISTS, which _REGISTRATION_REFUSALS does not list

The refusals with a code answer {"error_code": …, "message": …} in detail, plus rules for PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK. Two requests racing for one invitation cannot both spend it: consume_token() is one conditional UPDATE, and the loser rolls back with INVITE_INVALID.

With LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL the row No account at all never applies: the startup creates the waiting administrator before the first request, so the instance is never empty while it serves, and the mode decides (The Initial Administrator).

GET /api/v1/system/instance publishes the effective state as accounts: {registration_mode, registration_locked, first_account_open, password_rules} (AccountsInstanceConfig). About the users it says one thing only, whether there is one: first_account_open, from first_account_open(session), is true while the users table is empty (never with LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL, whose waiting administrator is a row), and the login page then offers Register here whatever the mode. No count, no limit (Public instance configuration; why the flag may be public: The First-Account Flag). password_rules is the list of the password rules, [{code, value}] (PasswordRuleRead), the same on every instance: the app checks a new password against it while the user types.

docs.title: ✉️ Invitations
docs.text:
An invitation is an invite account token: 7 days, single use, link /invite#token=…, and no user_id, as its account does not exist yet.

  • Created by create_invite(), from POST /api/v1/users/invites or ./dev.py user invite, with grants_admin, email and created_by_user_id (NULL from the command line). It refuses in mode disabled (REGISTRATION_DISABLED), and when the instance is full (USER_LIMIT_REACHED) unless called with enforce_limit=False, as only the command line does. It flushes and does not commit.
  • The email is a suggestion, not a constraint. It records whom the invitation is for, and POST /api/v1/auth/tokens/inspect returns it to whoever holds the token, but registration never compares it with the address of the new account: the developer rejected D-A16, the proposal to bind the two.
  • Listed by list_pending_invites(): the live ones (not consumed, not revoked, not expired), oldest first. Revoked by revoke_invite(invite_id), which returns False for anything that is not a live invitation; it flushes and does not commit.
  • Spent only by register_user(), as above.

POST /api/v1/auth/tokens/inspect {token, purpose}, with purpose invite, password_reset or admin_setup (The Initial Administrator), is public and writes nothing. It answers {status, purpose}, the status being valid, expired, consumed, revoked or unknown (also for a token of another purpose). Only a valid token adds expires_at, with grants_admin and email for an invitation, or username for a reset or setup link.

docs.title: 📏 The User Limit
docs.text: LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS (unset or blank: no limit) bounds the places counted by user_usage(): the active accounts (users.is_active), the live invitations, and the inactive accounts that wait: those holding a live email-verification token (Email Verification) and the administrator waiting for its setup (The Initial Administrator), each account counted once. A deactivated or deleted account frees its place; an invitation holds one from its creation until it is revoked or expires, and hands it to the account it opens; an account waiting for its email verification holds one while its link is live. A value that is not a whole number of at least 1 makes max_users() raise ValueError, and log_configuration_audit() calls it, so the start stops with an error that names the variable (CL-1). The registration check _max_users() still reads such a value as a limit of 0, logged like an invalid mode, for a process the audit does not guard; GET /panel/status answers users_limit: null for it, never a 500.

docs.title: Over the limit (A5-7)
docs.text:
The state «over the limit» is never stored: user_limit_service.over_limit_state() reads it from the accounts every time (active > max_users, one COUNT; no limit, or a limit max_users() cannot read, is never a state). A restore needs no code of its own: the restored accounts are counted like any other.

flowchart TD
    A[Request of a signed-in user] --> B{allowed for everyone?}
    B -- yes --> OK[answers as usual]
    B -- no --> C{active > limit?}
    C -- no --> OK
    C -- yes --> D{administrator and on the admin list?}
    D -- yes --> OK
    D -- no --> E[423 user_limit_exceeded]
  • api/v1/user_limit.py: the dependency refuse_when_over_limit, the fourth of the /api/v1 router, after the block, the awaiting-restore mode and the interrupted restore (the first that stands answers). ALLOWED_WHEN_OVER_LIMIT is ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED less the five routes of the administrator's backup; ALLOWED_WHEN_OVER_LIMIT_ADMIN holds those five and the two routes of the choice. The app's own restore is in neither list.
