The last one adds the job's warning instance_key_unusable (generated_key_unusable()): H's status names a problem, the file cannot be read, or the key is longer than that bound, which H's own check, a minimum length, lets through. The backup completes. Neither function creates the key file, and neither raises.
  • Announced by the manifest, outside manifest.files: instance_key: {included: true, sha256: <hex of the entry>} (ManifestInstanceKey, whose validator wants sha256 exactly when included). The entry holds the key's text, UTF-8.
  • Read in any archive whose manifest announces it: a decrypted envelope, or the plain zip that backup decrypt writes out of one. Refusing it in a zip would refuse LibreFolio's own output; the rule that matters is the writing. Present without the announcement: unexpected_entry; announced and missing: missing_entry; another SHA-256, more than 4096 bytes (INSTANCE_KEY_MAX_BYTES) or not UTF-8: checksum_mismatch; a folder or a link: not_a_file; encrypted: encrypted_entry; another compression: unsupported_entry (_check_key_entry(), _archive_instance_key() in staging.py). check_archive(), behind backup inspect, expects it the same way.
  • Never unpacked. The check reads it into memory (read_instance_key() in archive.py) before the unpacking, secrets/ is never part of the copy, and the swap never touches the live secrets/ (The Swap).

The check of an envelope (staging.py). _decrypt() comes first, in the phase decrypting (done_bytes of total_bytes, over the envelope): free space for the envelope's size plus 64 MiB (no_space), then decrypt_file() into .restore/stage/<id>/archive.zip (STAGE_DECRYPTED_ARCHIVE, 0600 in the stage's 0700 folder), through archive.zip.part. The checks of a zip follow on that archive, which is removed once unpacked; a check killed outright leaves it, or its .part, until the next start (What a Run Killed Outright Leaves). A chunk that fails ends the check failed with envelope_damaged, and nothing of the stage is left; stage_archive(…, key=None) on an envelope is password_required. RestoreErrorCode gains only these two codes: wrong_password and envelope_unsupported are synchronous answers of POST /backup/restore/stage, never the end of a check.

On the command line, inspect decrypts into a folder mkdtemp(prefix=".decrypt-") of backups/ (made private by ensure_private_dir()) and removes it at the end. A killed inspect leaves its folder: before it makes its own, inspect removes the .decrypt-* folders older than an hour (remove_stale_decrypt_folders() in leftovers.py; a younger one may be another inspect's, still running), and every start applies the same rule. restore decrypts through stage_archive(). decrypt FILE -o OUT writes OUT through _NewFile, and refuses, before it asks the password, an OUT that exists and a FILE that is not an envelope (not_an_envelope). Once OUT is written, it reads the manifest of the zip, and when the key is announced it adds 🔑 It also holds the instance key: with it, every saved provider key can be read. (_carries_instance_key(), B-24; a manifest it cannot read adds nothing, and the command still exits with 0).

The secrets of the copy (_plugin_secrets(), after the upgrade and the post-migration fixes, with X's functions on a sqlite3 connection to the copy's database):

  1. count_unreadable_secrets() with a random subkey counts every stored secret: with none, nothing more happens, and this instance's key is neither read nor generated.
  2. settings_subkey() gives this instance's subkey; on InstanceKeyError, every secret counts as unreadable, and the check goes on.
  3. With the archive's key, once derive_key_from() accepts it (_archive_subkey()): rekey_plugin_secrets(conn, old_subkey, new_subkey), committed. A row under the old key is decrypted with its own context and encrypted again with a fresh nonce, a row already under this instance's key is left alone, and any other stays as it is, counted unreadable. The rows rewritten decrypt with this instance's subkey, and their key_id is its own.
  4. Without it: count_unreadable_secrets(conn, settings_subkey()).

The report (StagingReport, RestoreStageReport) carries encrypted, secrets_rekeyed and secrets_unreadable {system, user} (RestoreSecretCounts) beside instance_key_included; a backup without the plugin settings tables gives zeros. The command line prints them, and the report window of the Backup tab shows restore-report-secrets-rekeyed and restore-report-secrets-unreadable, with data-count, when they are not zero.

Source What it holds backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/envelope.py The format: the header, the key, the chunks; is_envelope(), read_header(), unlock(), encrypt_file(), decrypt_file() backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/secure.py The password's rules (archive_password_rules(), archive_password_problems()) and the key a backup may carry (exportable_instance_key(), generated_key_unusable()) backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/jobs.py The creation: the key, the phase encrypting, the clear zip removed backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/archive.py, manifest.py, paths.py The key entry written, checked and read (read_instance_key(), check_archive()); ManifestInstanceKey; INSTANCE_KEY_ENTRY, STAGE_DECRYPTED_ARCHIVE backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/staging.py The check of an envelope (_decrypt()), the key entry, the secrets of the copy (_plugin_secrets()) backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/restore_jobs.py The password tried in the request, the upload kept, kind backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/leftovers.py What a run killed outright leaves in clear, removed at every start (below) backend/app/api/v1/backup/instance.py, backend/app/api/v1/backup/restore.py, backend/app/schemas/backup.py The routes and their models backend/app/api/no_echo.py NoInputEchoRoute scripts/backup_cli.py create --encrypt, --password-file, --password-stdin, decrypt frontend/src/lib/features/backup/ BackupDownloadCard.svelte (the choice, the password typed twice), RestoreCard.svelte and restoreFlow.svelte.ts (the state password), RestoreReportModal.svelte, backupApi.ts (isEnvelopeFile())

Tests: ./dev.py test services backup-envelope (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_backup_envelope.py: the header at its offsets, known answers built with cryptography, the bounds refused before any derivation, every tampering, NFC, no overwrite, 0600), ./dev.py test services backup-secure-rules (test_backup_secure_rules.py: the password's rules, the key a backup may carry), ./dev.py test services backup-secure (test_backup_secure.py: the creation, the check of an envelope, the key entry, the secrets re-encrypted or counted), ./dev.py test api backup-secure (test_api/test_backup_secure_api.py), ./dev.py test api no-echo-route (test_api/test_no_echo_route.py) and ./dev.py test utils backup-cli-secure (test_utilities/test_backup_cli_secure.py). The app's half: ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit (backupApi.test.ts, backupJob.test.ts, restoreFlow.test.ts, restoreI18n.test.ts) and ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit (BackupDownloadCard.test.ts, RestoreCard.test.ts, RestoreReportModal.test.ts, PasswordStrength.test.ts).

docs.title: What a Run Killed Outright Leaves
docs.text:
A run killed outright (a power cut, kill -9, a container stopped past its grace period) runs no clean-up, and three runs of the backup keep clear data on disk while they work (lot B4b, B-23, after E's review R13-SEC4):

  • the check of a secure backup decrypts it into its copy, .restore/stage/<id>/archive.zip (written through archive.zip.part), until it is unpacked: the backup's data, and the instance key when the backup carries it;
  • dev.py backup inspect decrypts one into a folder backups/.decrypt-<random>/;
  • a backup writes the database's copy and the zip into its job folder, backups/.jobs/<id>/: a secure one keeps the clear zip there until it is encrypted, then writes the envelope through .lfbk.part.

The startup step backup-leftovers, right after restore-commit (decision N66; see the startup steps), removes them at every start: sweep_backup_leftovers() in backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/leftovers.py, in a thread. Three parts, in this order:

  1. restore. restore_jobs.prune(), as at the start of a check: while no check runs, a check still recorded as running is ended failed, restore_interrupted, its copy and its upload removed, and prune() returns how many it ended; what is older than STAGE_LIFETIME (24 hours) goes as before. Then restore_jobs.remove_stray_decrypted_archives(): while .restore/ and .restore/stage/ are plain folders and the lock of the checks (.restore/stage/.stage.lock) is free, it removes archive.zip and archive.zip.part from every copy (a plain folder with a job-id name, the copy of a restore waiting for the next start included), each only when it is a regular file (lstat): a link or a folder of that name stays. A check removes the decrypted archive once unpacked, or the whole copy on any error, always under that lock: with the lock free, one still there is what a killed run left. The rest of the copy stays, its data/ and its report: prune() removes it at its age.
  2. decrypt_folders. remove_stale_decrypt_folders(), on backups/, removes with their content the entries named .decrypt-* (DECRYPT_FOLDER_PREFIX) that are folders themselves (lstat, never followed) and were last modified more than DECRYPT_FOLDER_LIFETIME (one hour) before: a younger one may be an inspect still running, and a link or a file of that name stays. inspect applies the same function before it makes its own folder: one rule, one home.
  3. jobs. jobs.end_interrupted_jobs(): while no run holds the run lock (backups/.jobs/.lock), every job folder (a plain folder with a job-id name) whose state reads running gets the end get_job() gives a run that died with its process (_end_interrupted()): failed, backup_interrupted, finished_at now, its state written, then everything in the folder but state.json removed. A state that cannot be read is left to the expiry. Then jobs.remove_expired_jobs(), as at the start of every backup, removes the jobs that ended more than JOB_RETENTION (one hour) ago, and a folder whose state cannot be read once it is that old: an interrupted job's state stays for that hour, like any finished job's. Both act only while backups/ and backups/.jobs/ are plain folders: with backups a link, .jobs in its target would look plain.

A read of a job, through get_job() (the Backup tab and the hosting panel following their jobs, the downloads), ends a dead run the same way, its work files included, without waiting for a restart.

A state that cannot be read is no job, to that read and to every cleanup (lot B-50): a content that is no job's state (a document that is not a JSON object, or a date without a time zone, included), a folder, a link or a special file in its place (lot B-53), or a file the server may not read. get_job() answers BackupJobNotFoundError, so the routes answer 404 backup_job_not_found, never a 500, and log one warning, A backup job's state cannot be read, with the job's id and the error's type name, never its content. A start goes on, and the folder expires by its date. The other errors of the disk, transient, stay as they come: a 500 the tab retries, which a «not found» would make it forget.

A restore check whose state cannot be read is likewise none, restore_stage_not_found, in silence: a content that is no check's state (a date without a time zone included), a folder, a link or a special file in its place, or no permission to read it; the other errors of the disk reach the caller the same way, so the check's read is a 500 the tab retries (lot B-55). prune removes such a state, and one a writer killed outright left half written (<id>.json.part), once older than a check's lifetime and while no check runs (lot B-54). The report of a finished check that cannot be read is no report: the check is answered without it, never a 500.

The state of a job or of a check, the report of a check and the outcome ticket of a restore are read through one reader, read_regular_file() (lot B-53): it never follows a link, never waits on a FIFO, and closes its descriptor whatever happens. Read the old way, a folder left a descriptor open at each read, and a FIFO held the read forever: the start of a backup, the reads of the tab and the startup sweep included.

  • Nothing a running process holds: the run lock of the backups (a dev.py backup create running while the server starts keeps its job), the lock of the checks (a check of the command line or of the app), an inspect younger than an hour. Nothing through a link: a folder is acted on only when lstat finds a folder itself (is_plain_dir()), and an entry that is a link is never followed.
  • Never raises. After restore-commit, a step that raises stops the start, and a cause that stays would stop every start (Steps and Middleware: the Contract). Each part runs in its own try: one that raises is logged as an error, A cleanup of backup leftovers failed, with part (restore, decrypt_folders or jobs) and error, the exception's type name only, no path and no message; the next parts still run.
  • The log. When something was ended or removed, one INFO line, Backup leftovers removed at startup, with checks_interrupted, decrypted_archives, decrypt_folders, jobs_interrupted and jobs_expired, in this order. A clean data directory, or one without .restore/ and backups/, logs nothing.

Tests: ./dev.py test services backup-leftovers (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_backup_leftovers.py: each part on its own, the locks held, the links, a part that raises, a clean data directory, the step), and the order restore-commit before backup-leftovers in ./dev.py test services backup-apply (test_backup_apply.py, section (j)).

docs.title: Configuration Checks of the Backup
docs.text:
backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/checks.py (lot B-9) gives four checks in the shape of H's ConfigCheck (Configuration Checks), under the same rules: they change nothing, never raise, and never put the token or a file's content in a result. With them, an unusable token, upload limit or restore limit shows in the start log, not only at the hosting panel's first call, at the first restore upload or at the first check (the third, backup.restore_limit, since lot B-35; the fourth, backup.recipients, since lot L3).

check_id State i18n_key detail Severity backup.panel_token (reads backup_download_token()) Neither LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN nor its _FILE is set, the default: the panel's routes answer 404 backup.checks.panelToken.off — ok: a default start logs nothing new, as email off is ok too backup.panel_token A usable token backup.checks.panelToken.ok — ok backup.panel_token BackupConfigError BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_NOT_VISIBLE_ASCII: a space, a tab or a character outside visible ASCII backup.checks.panelToken.notVisibleAscii — error backup.panel_token BackupConfigError BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_TOO_SHORT backup.checks.panelToken.tooShort {"minimum": 32} error backup.panel_token SecretFileError: the _FILE cannot give the token backup.checks.panelToken.unreadable {"reason": …}, the error's text: the variable and the path, never the content error backup.upload_limit (reads backup_max_upload_mb()) A limit, the managed profile's 500 included backup.checks.uploadLimit.limited {"limit_mb": n} ok backup.upload_limit No limit: 0, or unset in the self-hosted profile backup.checks.uploadLimit.unlimited — ok backup.upload_limit BackupConfigError BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB_INVALID: not a whole number backup.checks.uploadLimit.invalid — error backup.upload_limit ProfileDefaultError: the entry of ENVIRONMENT_PROFILE_DEFAULTS, asked only while the variable is unset, is missing or of the wrong type (H-27, H-37; Settings) backup.checks.uploadLimit.profileTable — error backup.restore_limit (reads backup_max_restore_mb(), The Restore Limit) A limit: the value set, or, while it is unset outside selfhosted, 8 times the upload limit, 4000 in managed backup.checks.restoreLimit.limited {"limit_mb": n} ok backup.restore_limit No limit: 0, unset in the self-hosted profile, or unset with an upload limit of 0 backup.checks.restoreLimit.unlimited — ok backup.restore_limit BackupConfigError: BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB_INVALID, not a whole number; or, while it is unset outside selfhosted, the upload limit's BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB_INVALID backup.checks.restoreLimit.invalid {"variable": …}, from exc.variable: LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB, or LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB in the second case error backup.restore_limit ProfileDefaultError: while it is unset outside selfhosted, the upload limit's entry of ENVIRONMENT_PROFILE_DEFAULTS is missing or of the wrong type backup.checks.restoreLimit.profileTable — error backup.recipients (reads backup_recipients(), Sealed Backups) One or two usable age1… recipients backup.checks.recipients.ok {"count": n} ok backup.recipients Unset, and backup_requires_recipients() false (any profile but managed): the panel's backups are clear zips backup.checks.recipients.off — ok backup.recipients BackupConfigError: BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_INVALID, BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_TOO_MANY or BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_DUPLICATE backup.checks.recipients.invalid {"reason": …}, the error's code, never the value error backup.recipients Unset in the managed profile (decision D1 of the L3 contract: never a clear zip to the panel) backup.checks.recipients.missingManaged — error
  • In CONFIG_CHECKS. BACKUP_CONFIG_CHECKS = (check_panel_token, check_upload_limit, check_restore_limit, check_recipients) is unpacked in CONFIG_CHECKS right after check_test_mode, the last of the platform's, before workstream A's ACCOUNTS_CONFIG_CHECKS and E's *EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS, which still close the tuple. The startup audit logs their error states as errors, each with its summary, a line naming its variable (quoted in «Startup Checks» of Configuration), and the start goes on. The routes are unchanged: 503, and their own error line at each call.
  • The import. config_audit imports this module to build its tuple, so checks.py imports ConfigCheck only when a check runs, as E's checks.py does (Email Service): either module can be imported first.
  • The messages. backup.checks.*, in the backup i18n subsystem, written whole in the module for the i18n usage scan; the «Security» tab of Settings › Administration shows them, from GET /security/checks.

Tests: ./dev.py test services backup-checks (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_backup_checks.py), and ./dev.py test services config-audit.

docs.title: 🔏 Sealed Backups (.tar)
docs.text:
A sealed backup (lot L3) is a secure backup whose password nobody types: LibreFolio draws it, encrypts it with age for one or two public keys, and forgets it. It serves the hosting panel's nightly backup, whose provider must be able to restore an instance without the instance being able to read its own backups, and the self-hoster's cron. The format was agreed with the cloud coordinator in BACKUP-contratto-L3.md, the L3 contract, kept in the project folder outside the repository (sealed.py's docstring names it); where the two differ, the code below is what ships. What the administrator sees is Sealed Backups.

No cryptography of our own. The .lfbk inside is the version-1 envelope of above, unchanged. The password is encrypted with age, a published format with a reference implementation in Go (age) and one in Rust (rage), through pyrage 1.4.0, the Python binding of rage, pinned in the Pipfile and on the coordinator's side alike. Only X25519 recipients and identities (pyrage.x25519): no SSH keys, no plugins. So a sealed backup opens with standard tools, tar and age -d, without LibreFolio, and the interoperability was checked once by hand with age 1.3.2 on the vectors (contract §9.2); test_sealed_011_* repeat it when an age binary is on the PATH, and skip visibly otherwise.

The file, librefolio-backup-<UTC>.tar (FILE_SUFFIX): a POSIX ustar archive, uncompressed, of exactly three members in this order (MEMBERS):

# Member Content 1 manifest.json build_manifest(): canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8, no final line break) with exactly format "lfbk-tar", version 1, recipients (the age1… strings, in the variable's order), lfbk_sha256, lfbk_size, created_at (UTC, …Z), librefolio_version, db_revision (string or null) and password_member "password.age". No personal data 2 password.age seal_password(): pyrage.encrypt() of the password, binary (not armored) 3 backup.lfbk The job's envelope, streamed into the tar
  • Small members first. With the two small members ahead, the first HEAD_BYTES (10 240 bytes, one tar record) hold the manifest, the password and the envelope's 52-byte header: the coordinator verifies a stored copy (manifest, password, scrypt check) with a ranged read, without downloading it.
  • Deterministic. write_sealed() writes through tarfile with USTAR_FORMAT, members 0600, uid/gid 0, empty names and mtime the job's creation time; the same three members give the same bytes (test_sealed_003_write_sealed_rebuilds_the_good_vector_byte_for_byte). The output goes through _NewFile (exclusive, 0600, <name>.part, fsynced, renamed), and _HashingFile computes its SHA-256 on the way.
  • The password. new_password(): secrets.token_bytes(32) in base64url without padding, 43 characters, ASCII, so NFC leaves it unchanged for the envelope's key derivation. One per backup. It lives in the job's thread only, as a secure backup's does: never in state.json, a log, an exception or a repr.

The job (jobs.py). start_backup() and run_backup() take a password or recipients, never both (_one_protection(), ValueError). With recipients, _run() draws the password, passes instance_key=None to build_archive() (decision 39: a sealed backup never carries the instance key, and never gets the instance_key_unusable warning), then _protect() runs _encrypt() as for a secure backup and _seal(): the free space for the envelope's size plus 64 MiB (backup_no_space), the phase sealing, the manifest built from the archive's own (app_version, alembic_revision), the .tar written. The job's file is the .tar: file_name, file_size and file_sha256 describe it, and the job records sealed: true and sealed_recipients (InstanceBackupJob; false and [] otherwise). The zip and the envelope are removed with the other work files, at the end of the run: until then, during sealing, the work folder holds the zip, the envelope and the .tar.

The recipients (config/backup.py). backup_recipients() reads LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_RECIPIENTS: unset or blank is None; otherwise comma-separated items, stripped, each one age1… and parsed by x25519.Recipient.from_str(), kept in its canonical form (lower case), at most MAX_RECIPIENTS (2), no duplicates. BackupConfigError carries BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_INVALID, BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_TOO_MANY or BACKUP_RECIPIENTS_DUPLICATE, and its message names the item's position, never its value: a private key pasted by mistake must not reach a log. Not a secret, so no _FILE. backup_requires_recipients() is true in the managed profile only. The panel's start (panel.py, _recipients()) reads both at each request: a value it cannot use, or none on a managed instance, answers 503 backup_panel_unavailable and logs the variable and the code, never a clear zip instead; unset on any other profile, the panel gets the clear zip of before. The check is backup.recipients, in the table above.

The strict reader. read_sealed() is LibreFolio's own, short ustar reader; tarfile is used only to write. tarfile reads PAX and GNU headers, links, folders and long or absolute names, which a backup has no use for; a reader written for exactly this file refuses them by construction, and the contract lets each side choose its reader under the same rules (the coordinator's is incremental, fed from a stream). It never extracts by name: it records each member's offset and size and reads there.

  • Each header (_header()): magic ustar\0 and version 00 (GNU's ustar \0 is refused), the checksum recomputed, type 0 or NUL only, no prefix, an ASCII name, octal numbers.
  • The archive (_members()): exactly three members, then a zero block; names and order equal to MEMBERS; manifest.json and password.age at most 4096 bytes each (SMALL_MEMBER_MAX); anything cut short refused.
  • The envelope: its first 52 bytes start with LFBK and pass EnvelopeHeader.from_bytes(), so its bounds are checked before any derivation.
  • The manifest (_manifest()): UTF-8 JSON, one object, duplicate keys refused, exactly the nine keys (an unknown key means a version 2), each of its type; read by content, not by bytes, so the canonical form is written, not required. lfbk_size and lfbk_sha256 must match the third member.
  • The opening. read_identities() reads a key file as age-keygen writes it (comments, blank lines, AGE-SECRET-KEY-1… lines); open_password() decrypts with them and wants exactly 43 base64url characters; check_password() is unlock_header() on the header already read, the scrypt check without decrypting a chunk; extract_envelope() copies the third member to a new file.

SealedError.code is sealed_tar_invalid, sealed_manifest_invalid, sealed_no_identity, sealed_password_invalid or sealed_identity_invalid; the messages hold no path and no secret. is_sealed() tells a sealed backup by the ustar magic at offset 257, whatever its name.

Where it is read. The command line (scripts/backup_cli.py): keygen writes an identity (identity_file_text(), O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0600) and prints its recipient; create --recipient/--sealed (_recipients_for()); inspect, restore and decrypt go through _sealed_first(), which refuses a sealed file without --identity-file (sealed_backup_needs_key) and --identity-file with any other, and _run_sealed(), which reads the key file before the switch of user (as --password-file), opens and checks the password, copies the envelope into a mkdtemp() folder removed at the end, and runs the same command on it with that password. The restore check of the app (staging.py, _open_archive()) recognises the magic and refuses the file with sealed_backup_needs_key: the server has no private key, by design.

Source What it holds backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/sealed.py The format: writing (new_password(), seal_password(), build_manifest(), write_sealed()), the strict reader (read_sealed()), the opening (read_identities(), open_password(), check_password(), extract_envelope()) backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/jobs.py _protect(), _seal(), the phase sealing, the job's sealed and sealed_recipients backend/app/config/backup.py backup_recipients(), backup_requires_recipients() backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/checks.py check_recipients() backend/app/api/v1/backup/panel.py, backend/app/api/v1/backup/job_views.py The panel's start and its 503; the download as application/x-tar backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/staging.py sealed_backup_needs_key in a check scripts/backup_cli.py cmd_keygen(), _recipients_for(), _sealed_first(), _run_sealed() backend/test_scripts/fixtures/backup_l3/ The vectors shared with the cloud coordinator: vectors.json, two TEST ONLY identities, the good archive, the rotation one and the negatives, made once by generate_vectors.py

Tests: ./dev.py test services backup-sealed (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_backup_sealed.py: every vector, the byte-for-byte rebuild, the reader's refusals, the identities, the cloud's key derivation, age interoperability when available), ./dev.py test utils backup-cli-sealed (test_utilities/test_backup_cli_sealed.py), ./dev.py test api backup-panel (test_api/test_backup_panel.py: the sealed panel job, the 503) and ./dev.py test services backup-checks (backup.recipients).

docs.title: 🩺 Configuration Checks
docs.text:
backend/app/services/platform/config_audit.py checks the settings that leave an instance weaker than it should be. Each check is a function that returns a ConfigCheck:

Field Content check_id Stable id, such as platform.jwt_secret severity ok, info, warning or error i18n_key Key of its message, written whole in the module of the check so the i18n usage scan (scripts/i18n_usage.py) sees it: instance.checks.* for the platform's (config_audit.py, plugin_secrets_check.py), whose 30 messages, the two of the plugin secrets check included, are in the instance i18n subsystem; auth.checks.* for workstream A's (services/accounts/checks.py), whose three messages are in the auth subsystem; backup.checks.* for workstream B's (services/platform/instance_backup/checks.py), whose thirteen messages are in the backup subsystem (Configuration Checks of the Backup); email.checks.* for workstream E's (Email Service). The «Security» tab of Settings › Administration shows these messages, all four subsystems', from GET /security/checks (SecurityTab); the log has the English summary instead detail The parameters of that message summary The English sentence written to the log

A check changes nothing, never raises and never puts a secret value in its result. Each judges the configuration, except platform.client_address, which reports what the running server has met since it started: it is ok at startup, so the startup audit never logs it. run_config_checks() evaluates the functions of CONFIG_CHECKS, in this order:

check_id Not ok when Severity platform.jwt_secret Neither JWT_SECRET nor JWT_SECRET_FILE is set, blank counting as not set: one key per start, the default info platform.jwt_secret The secret is shorter than 32 characters (JWT_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH); the summary names its origin (configured_jwt_secret_origin()): The session signing key from JWT_SECRET is … characters long: …, or from JWT_SECRET_FILE (<path>) warning; error with LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed, where log_configuration_audit() stops the startup first platform.jwt_secret JWT_SECRET_FILE cannot give its secret error platform.secrets_set_twice A secret is set both as NAME and as NAME_FILE, neither blank (secrets_set_twice()) warning platform.instance_key instance_key_status() reports a problem: the key cannot be used, including a generated key file out of reach (cannot be reached (Permission denied)) error platform.instance_key The folder or the file of the generated key gives group or others any access: the folder should be 0700, the file 0600 warning platform.session_cookie SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=never warning platform.client_address Since the start, forwarding headers came from an untrusted local peer (Behind a Proxy Nobody Trusts): instance.checks.clientAddress.untrustedProxy, detail {"headers": …} with the names met, such as "X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP", summary UNTRUSTED_PROXY_SUMMARY warning platform.client_address Since the start, they came from untrusted public peers only: instance.checks.clientAddress.publicForwarding, the names met in headers, summary PUBLIC_FORWARDING_SUMMARY info platform.frame_protection LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION is off with LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed, whose entry in PROFILE_DEFAULTS turns it on (The Content-Security-Policy and Frame Protection): a value set in the environment or in .env, or the entry lost from the table. instance.checks.frameProtection.offManaged, summary LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION is off in the managed profile: any site can show LibreFolio in a frame; the managed profile turns it on warning platform.csp_report_only LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY is off with LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed, the same way: instance.checks.cspReportOnly.offManaged, summary LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY is off in the managed profile: browsers list no Content-Security-Policy violation; the managed profile turns it on. Only an info: the wider policy it adds only reports, and never blocks; the enforced policy is on in every profile info platform.log_level LOG_LEVEL, after the LIBREFOLIO_LOG_LEVEL override, is DEBUG or TRACE info platform.hosting_panel LIBREFOLIO_WAKE_TOKEN or LIBREFOLIO_PANEL_STATUS_TOKEN, or its _FILE, is set but cannot be used (wake_token(), panel_status_token(); lot H-61): their routes answer 503 (The Hosting Panel's Access). instance.checks.hostingPanel.unusable, detail {"variables": …}, the unusable variables in that order, comma-separated, never a value; the summary adds each one's code, FILE_UNREADABLE for a SecretFileError: A hosting panel token cannot be used, and its route answers 503 to every call: LIBREFOLIO_WAKE_TOKEN (WAKE_TOKEN_TOO_SHORT). ok otherwise: instance.checks.hostingPanel.off while neither is set, instance.checks.hostingPanel.ok while each one set can be used. The backup token has workstream B's backup.panel_token, below error platform.test_mode LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE is on (is_test_mode(): 1, true or yes, in any case) outside a test lane, with LIBREFOLIO_TEST_LANE_ID unset, or not 16 to 128 characters once stripped (owning_test_lane_id(), H-49): instance.checks.testMode.outsideTestLane, detail {"data_dir": …}, the test data directory in use (str(get_data_dir())), summary TEST_MODE_OUTSIDE_LANE_SUMMARY, LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE is on outside a test lane: test-only providers are served, the data are kept in the test data directory <data_dir> and .env is not read; unset it on a production instance. The same in every profile (below) error; with LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed, log_configuration_audit() stops the startup first backup.panel_token LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN, or its _FILE, is set but cannot be used: backup.checks.panelToken.*, see Configuration Checks of the Backup error backup.upload_limit LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB, or the profile's entry for it, cannot be used: backup.checks.uploadLimit.*, see Configuration Checks of the Backup error backup.restore_limit LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB cannot be used, or, while it is unset outside selfhosted, the upload limit it follows: backup.checks.restoreLimit.*, see Configuration Checks of the Backup error accounts.login_limit LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT=off, in any case: the failed sign-in limit is off. auth.checks.loginLimit.off, and one fixed summary however off is written: LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT=off: failed sign-ins are not limited; turn it back on unless this is a test instance warning accounts.login_limit Any value other than on or off: auth.checks.loginLimit.invalid, detail {"value": <the value, stripped>}, as login_limit_value() reads it. log_configuration_audit() stops the start on such a value (below), so the error shows only for a value read after the start error accounts.owner_email_change The change of the owner's address a hosting provider started with LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL (workstream A, lot A5-1b; the check is lot H5-4's), read in memory from instance_owner.startup_change_state(), never an address: pending is info, auth.checks.ownerEmailChange.pending; blocked (another account holds the new address) is warning, auth.checks.ownerEmailChange.blocked; none waiting is ok. info or warning

The two checks of the managed profile's security switches (lot H-39), check_frame_protection() and check_csp_report_only(), read get_settings() and give no detail. Each is ok while its switch is on, in any profile (instance.checks.frameProtection.on, instance.checks.cspReportOnly.on), and while it is off outside managed, the self-hosted default (instance.checks.frameProtection.offSelfHosted, instance.checks.cspReportOnly.offSelfHosted). The managed expectation is written in the check, never read from PROFILE_DEFAULTS: read there, an entry lost from the table would change the expectation along with the value, and nothing would show. No value is refused at run time: a provider may turn a switch off on purpose, frame protection for a hosting panel that shows the app in a frame, and the checks only show it, in the startup log and in the checks on demand.

The check of test mode (lot H-46), check_test_mode(), the last of the platform's in CONFIG_CHECKS, gives the same result in every profile. It is ok while test mode is off (instance.checks.testMode.off), and while it is on in a test lane (instance.checks.testMode.testLane): a process that owns a LIBREFOLIO_TEST_LANE_ID the readiness probe accepts, 16 to 128 characters once stripped (owning_test_lane_id(), TEST_LANE_ID_MIN_LENGTH and TEST_LANE_ID_MAX_LENGTH in backend/app/config/platform.py, lot H-49; GET /system/test-lane-health declares its token with the same two constants). configure_test_runtime() in scripts/cli_base.py sets it, with ensure_test_lane_id(), 32 characters, for the test runner (dev.py test, its shared backend and its in-process pytest), for dev.py server --test and for the gallery's servers; configure_server_runtime() (dev.py server) sets LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE=0 and removes it. The lane id is no barrier against an attacker, since whoever writes the environment is the operator: it tells a configuration mistake from a test lane.

Where it matters: dev.py server always turns test mode off, but a server started without it, with uvicorn directly or from a service unit, takes LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE from its environment as it is. In test mode the test-only providers, mockprov and the two of mockfx (MOCKFX, MOCKFX_FAIL), are served, since provider_registry withholds a test_only plugin only while test mode is off (X-R44); get_data_dir() moves to the test data directory, LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR or backend/data/test/, where what is entered meanwhile is saved; and Settings reads no .env (settings_customise_sources). Test mode on the production data directory itself never starts: get_test_data_dir() runs validate_test_data_dir(), which rejects a test directory that overlaps or holds the production data. The image as shipped is not expected to reach the checks either. It starts uvicorn directly (the CMD of the Dockerfile), but backend/data/ is not in the image and entrypoint.sh hands only LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR to the user the server runs as, which therefore cannot create the default test data directory; and configure_logging() creates <data directory>/logs while backend.app.main is imported, so the import stops on a PermissionError before any check. That is read from the Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh and logging_config.py, and reproduced outside a container with a folder the server cannot write; it is not yet tried in a container. In the managed profile the start stops on the error (ManagedTestModeError, below); in the self-hosted profile it goes on, with the error in the log and in the checks on demand. The profile that counts is the one in the process environment, where a container's environment: or env_file: puts it: in test mode Settings reads no .env. Its tests are sections (h) and (i), lot H-49, of ./dev.py test services config-audit (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_config_audit.py): the three states, with the true and false spellings of the variable, a blank lane id and lane ids around the probe's two bounds; the same result in every profile; the startup log record; the managed stop with its exact message, the JWT stop staying first.

Workstream A's check, ok as auth.checks.loginLimit.ok while the limit is on, is check_login_limit() in backend/app/services/accounts/checks.py, in the tuple ACCOUNTS_CONFIG_CHECKS, which config_audit.py unpacks into CONFIG_CHECKS right before workstream E's EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS: E's three checks, email.smtp, email.smtp_encryption and email.links, stay last (Email Service). It reads the variable only through backend/app/config/accounts.py, login_limit_enabled() and login_limit_value(), never from os.environ: the rule of the configuration package (Settings System). Like E's module, checks.py imports ConfigCheck inside the check, when it runs, and under TYPE_CHECKING for its annotation: config_audit imports it to build its tuple, so either module can be imported first.

So CONFIG_CHECKS is the platform's checks, then workstream B's three (Configuration Checks of the Backup), then A's, then E's three, which close it.

At startup, the configuration-checks step of the lifespan (STARTUP_STEPS in backend/app/services/platform/app_lifespan.py) runs log_configuration_audit() in a thread (asyncio.to_thread), right after the Starting LibreFolio line:

  1. configured_jwt_secret(): an unreadable JWT_SECRET_FILE raises SecretFileError. In practice the import of auth_service.py has already failed on it. With LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed, a configured secret shorter than JWT_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH raises WeakSecretError; in the self-hosted profile it stays the warning of the table above.
  2. Test mode on outside a test lane, the error of platform.test_mode: with LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed, it raises ManagedTestModeError (a RuntimeError), whose message names the test data directory in use: In the managed profile LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE must not be on outside a test lane (no LIBREFOLIO_TEST_LANE_ID of 16 to 128 characters): test-only providers would be served and the data kept in the test data directory <path>; unset LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE. In the self-hosted profile it stays the error of the table above, and the start goes on.
  3. instance_blocked() and instance_deletion_date() (backend/app/config/platform.py): a value they cannot read raises ValueError. On a blocked instance, a warning Instance blocked by its hosting provider (LIBREFOLIO_BLOCKED): …, with deletion_date, goes to the log: see Instance Block.
  4. admin_bootstrap_config() (backend/app/config/accounts.py): an unusable LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_* value raises AdminBootstrapConfigError, which names the variable and never the token, and an unreadable LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE raises SecretFileError, on an instance with accounts too: see The Initial Administrator.
  5. login_limit_enabled() (the same module): a LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT other than on or off raises ValueError, which names the variable and the value: see Failed Sign-in Limit.
  6. instance_key_status(): a configured key (source == "configured") with a problem raises InstanceKeyError. The administrator chose that source, so the server does not start without it.
  7. Every check that is not ok is logged at its severity, with the summary as the event and check and detail as fields. A generated key file gone bad or out of reach is logged as an error, and the start goes on.

Tests: ./dev.py test services config-audit (the order of CONFIG_CHECKS included: the platform's checks, B's three, A's, then E's three; and the two checks of the managed profile's switches in every state, a PROFILE_DEFAULTS entry removed included); the stop on a LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_* value is in ./dev.py test services admin-bootstrap, the check accounts.login_limit and the stop on a LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT value in ./dev.py test services accounts-checks. What the administrator sees and does is in Configuration, section «Startup Checks», and in the app in «Security» of Global Settings.

docs.title: 🧩 Plugin Secrets Check
docs.text:
backend/app/services/platform/plugin_secrets_check.py finds the secrets of the plugin settings that the instance key can no longer read: a lost secrets/instance.key generated again, data restored without its secrets/, another LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY. It needs the database, and CONFIG_CHECKS run before the database step, so it cannot be one of them. check_plugin_secrets(session) -> ConfigCheck returns the ConfigCheck of config_audit.py all the same, so that the «Security» tab of Settings › Administration shows it with the others: GET /security/checks returns it after them, and the tab links its finding to the Plugins tab (SecurityTab). Unlike the functions of CONFIG_CHECKS, it can raise, on a database error for one: the startup step below catches it.

It asks plugin_secrets_key_status(session) (backend/app/services/plugin_settings/crypto.py), which counts by key_id, without decrypting, the stored secrets of each scope that the current key did not encrypt, or all of them when the key cannot be used. While no secret is stored it reads no key at all, so a fresh install never generates the key file at this step. With secrets stored, it derives the subkey with derive_key(), which generates a missing key file as any first use does: after a lost key file, every stored secret counts against the new key.

check_id Not ok when Severity platform.plugin_secrets At least one stored system secret cannot be read: i18n_key instance.checks.pluginSecrets.unreadable (an ICU plural on count), detail {"count": <system count>}, summary Stored plugin secrets that the instance key cannot read: <N>. Enter them again in the plugin settings, or restore the instance key they were saved with error

Otherwise the check is ok (instance.checks.pluginSecrets.ok, no detail). Only the system count reaches the result and the log, by the rule of the plugin settings: a user's secrets are that user's, who sees them unreadable in their own settings and enters them again. So when only user secrets are unreadable, the check is ok.

The startup step plugin-secrets-check (STARTUP_STEPS, after global-settings, admin-bootstrap and restore-commit) runs log_plugin_secrets_check(): it opens an AsyncSession on get_async_engine(), logs a result that is not ok at its severity, as log_configuration_audit() does (the summary as the event, check and detail as fields), and logs nothing when it is ok. It never raises: when the check fails, it logs the warning Plugin secrets check could not run, whose error field holds the class name of the exception, never its message, and the start goes on. A row keeps its key_id until its secret is saved again (a clear deletes the row), so the error comes back at every start until the secrets are entered again or the old key is restored.

Tests: ./dev.py test services plugin-secrets-check (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_plugin_secrets_check.py), and the step's place in ./dev.py test services app-lifecycle. What the administrator sees and does is in Configuration, section «Startup Checks».

docs.title: 📋 The Checks on Demand
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/security/checks (backend/app/api/v1/security.py, a router with prefix="/security" and the tag Security, included by one line of api/v1/router.py) evaluates the checks now, for administrators only (require_admin: 401 without a session, 403 Admin access required for a member). It runs run_config_checks() in a worker thread (asyncio.to_thread: some checks read files, such as the instance key), then check_plugin_secrets(session) on the request's session, and answers every result in that order, the ok ones included, so that a page can show what is not:

Model (backend/app/schemas/security.py) Fields SecurityChecksResponse items: a list of SecurityCheckRead SecurityCheckRead check_id; severity, ok, info, warning or error; i18n_key; detail, the parameters of the message

An item never carries the English summary, which may name a host or a path (nor does GET /email/status), and never a secret value. The web app reads it through one store, once per page load, for the «Security» tab of Settings › Administration (lot A8b, SecurityTab). Since lot N69b the sidebar's connection line asks first, on the first page an administrator opens, to show the tab's count as a dot on every page (The sidebar's dot); the Settings page, which asks before the tab is opened so that its badge counts, shares that read; the tab reads again on «check again». A member's app never asks. On a blocked instance the route is not on the allow-list: an administrator gets 423.

Each check has help, and who can solve it decides which (FB-27). The map is frontend/src/lib/features/instance/checkGuides.json: server, every check of GET /security/checks, in the order of its answer; browser, the findings the browser adds to the tab, today accounts.openRegistration (OPEN_REGISTRATION_NOTICE_ID, The Open-Registration Warning) and platform.blockedScript. Each value is one of two objects:

  • {"kind": "guide", "path": "admin/<page>/#<anchor>"}: the administrator solves it alone. The path is below /mkdocs/ without the language, which DocsLink adds, such as admin/configuration_security/#frame-protection for platform.frame_protection; it is the tab's «Guide» button (workstream A, N69d). A limit that applies to a self-hosted instance too (backup.upload_limit, backup.restore_limit) is a guide.
  • {"kind": "support"}: only whoever hosts the instance solves it, today platform.hosting_panel, backup.panel_token and accounts.owner_email_change. The tab shows «Contact support» instead of a guide.

checkGuides.ts reads the map: checkHelp(id) gives the object, checkGuidePath(id) the path of a guide and undefined for a support. CheckHelp.svelte (frontend/src/lib/features/instance/components/, rendered by SecurityTab.svelte on every row, passed for the folded ones) draws the choice: security-guide for a guide; for a support check that has not passed, check-support, a link built by supportChannel(supportUrl, {githubFallback: false}) and reportHref() (frontend/src/lib/features/support/supportChannel.ts) from the instance's LIBREFOLIO_SUPPORT_URL (support_url of GET /system/instance): a mailto: with subject and body, or the http(s) page, opened in a new tab, with title and body in its address. The report is buildCheckReport() (checkSupportReport.ts) and has no field for anything else than the check's code, its severity, the instance's address (location.origin), the app version and the date: no user, no email address, no secret, no parameter of the check. Without a usable address there is no link and no GitHub issue (it would be public): check-support-missing, a line that tells the user to contact whoever provides the service. A new check needs its entry, and the anchor of a guide must be an explicit {: #… } of the English page: ./dev.py test services config-audit fails when a check of the server has no entry, or an entry no check, and ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit (checkGuides.test.ts) when an anchor is missing, or when a translation gains or loses one: a ratchet, whose baseline in the test goes to zero after the release's translation.

Tests: ./dev.py test api login-throttle (in-process: 401 and 403, every check once, as run_config_checks() and check_plugin_secrets() evaluate them, accounts.login_limit ok with the limit on and a warning with off, no secret value in the body, nor the SMTP server and user that a summary names) and ./dev.py test api security-checks (on the lane's server: accounts.login_limit a warning, since the lane runs with the limit off; platform.jwt_secret and platform.plugin_secrets listed; a member 403, no session 401).

docs.title: 🛡️ Endpoint Protection
docs.text: All endpoints that access or modify user data require a valid session cookie (Depends(get_current_user) in FastAPI), except the hosting panel's routes (/backup/panel/jobs…, /system/wake-sync, /panel/status), which authenticate with a token per scope instead: see The Hosting Panel's Access.

docs.title: 🌐 Public Endpoints (no auth required)
docs.text:
Endpoint Method Purpose /auth/login POST User login, under the failed sign-in limit /auth/logout POST Clear session cookie /auth/register POST New user registration, under the password rules, the registration mode and the user limit /auth/tokens/inspect POST The status of an invitation, password-reset or setup link, for whoever holds its token: see Links in use /auth/password-reset POST Spend a password-reset link: a new password, under the password rules, and every session of the account ended /auth/setup POST Spend the setup link of the initial administrator: its password, under the password rules, the account activated and signed in /auth/address-probe GET Whether this instance issued a nonce: {match} and nothing else, readable from any origin; see Address Probe /auth/address-probe.png GET The same bit as the width of a PNG, 1×1 or 2×1 (H-55 v2); see Address Probe /system/health GET Health check: the server answers /system/info GET System information, the app version only without a valid session (SystemInfoPublicResponse) and everything with one (SystemInfoResponse): see System information and readiness /system/instance GET Public instance configuration, needed before sign-in: see Public instance configuration, and The First-Account Flag for the one fact about the users it tells /system/ready GET Readiness for health checks and orchestrators (200 when the database answers and its schema is at the head revision of the migrations, 503 otherwise): see System information and readiness /utilities/* GET Reference data (countries, currencies, sectors) /ai-export/catalog GET Static AI Export catalogue (no user data)

On an instance blocked by its hosting provider, the public endpoints outside its short list answer 401: see Instance Block.

docs.title: 🆕 The First-Account Flag
docs.text:
GET /system/instance tells anyone one fact about the users: accounts.first_account_open, true while the users table is empty, an inactive account counted (first_account_open(session) in backend/app/services/accounts/registration_service.py). The login page needs it: the first account of an empty instance can be created in any registration mode and becomes the administrator, so the page offers Register here while the flag is true, even on an instance that registers by invitation, the default of a new install. Publishing it is accepted (coordinator decision, 15/10/2026):

  • It tells nothing a registration attempt would not. An empty instance takes the first POST /auth/register it gets, whatever the mode: anyone can learn that it is empty by trying.
  • The window is short. The flag turns false with the first registration, normally minutes after the install; the administrator manual asks to register before exposing the instance (Global Settings, section «Who Can Sign Up»).
  • An instance with F02 never shows it. With LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL (The Initial Administrator), the admin-bootstrap startup step creates the administrator, inactive, before the server answers its first request: the instance is never empty while it serves, so the flag is false from the start, and nobody can register as the first account. Without the variable, a managed instance starts empty, like any other.

docs.title: 📢 The Open-Registration Warning
docs.text:
The web app warns an administrator who reaches an instance whose registration mode is open through a host that is not local (lot A7b): anyone who finds the instance can create an account. The warning is advice, and nothing more:

  • It blocks nothing. The registration rule stays the server's (register_user()). The warning is an instance notice, which the administrator can close until the next page load.
  • The browser decides, from the host of the page. isLocalHost(location.hostname) classifies the name or address the administrator used: localhost and *.localhost, the loopback, private and carrier-grade NAT IPv4 ranges, ::1, fc00::/7 and fe80::/10, single-label names, and the names under .local, .lan, .home.arpa and .internal are local; *.ts.net is not, since Tailscale Funnel can publish those names. Nothing is sent to the server for it, and nothing tests whether the instance can really be reached from the internet: a local name can still be published by a proxy or a tunnel, a public one can sit behind a firewall.
  • It tells nothing new. It reads the account's is_superuser, and the mode and whether LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION pins it, which GET /system/instance already publishes.

The «Security» tab of Settings › Administration lists the same warning among its findings, from the same openRegistrationNoticeFor(), whether or not the notice was closed (SecurityTab). The list of local hosts and the watcher: Open-Registration Warning; administrator side: «The Open-Registration Warning» in Global Settings.

docs.title: 🩺 System Information and Readiness
docs.text:
GET /system/info (backend/app/api/v1/system/info.py) runs the checks of get_current_user through its signed_in_user dependency, where a 401 means anonymous instead of an error. Without a valid session cookie (none, an expired or invalid token, an unknown or disabled account), the answer is the app version only, {"app_version": "..."} (SystemInfoPublicResponse). With one, it is the full SystemInfoResponse: app, Python and OS versions, platform, deployment mode, backend and frontend dependency versions. The OpenAPI 200 response is the anyOf of the two schemas, the full one first.

GET /system/ready (backend/app/api/v1/system/ready.py) tells whether the instance can serve requests, for Docker health checks, Uptime Kuma, orchestrators and hosting panels. check_readiness() (backend/app/services/platform/readiness.py) runs two checks, and the body (ReadinessResponse, backend/app/schemas/system.py) carries one code for each:

Check Codes database ok: the database answers a query; unreachable: it does not migrations ok: the database's revision, in alembic_version, is the head revision of the migration scripts; behind: it is a revision the scripts know but not the head, a migration was not applied or failed; ahead: it is a revision the scripts do not know, the database is newer than this version (or from another LibreFolio); unknown: a revision cannot be read (no alembic_version table or not exactly one row in it, several heads or no scripts), and whenever database is unreachable

status is ready, with 200, only when both checks are ok; otherwise it is not_ready, with 503 and the same shape:

{"status": "ready", "checks": {"database": "ok", "migrations": "ok"}, "database_revision": "<revision>", "mode": "normal", "app_version": "<version>"}
  • database_revision is the revision the database's migrations stand at, the one row of alembic_version, or null when it cannot be read (the database is unreachable, the table is missing or it does not hold exactly one row). It is there to tell a database behind or ahead of this version, a hosting panel after an update: a revision id says which migration the data reached, and nothing about its content (developer decision, 25/10/2026). The head the scripts expect is never in the answer, and neither is a count or a path.
  • mode is normal, or awaiting_restore while the hosting panel restores the instance (Awaiting Restore): ready then means ready to receive the backup.
  • app_version is the version that is running, get_git_version(): the very text GET /system/info gives without a session, so the answer shows nothing that was not already public. It is there so that a hosting panel checks the version after an update with this probe alone: a probe does not count as a user's presence, and /system/info and /system/instance do (lot H5-8). It is in the 503 body too, and on an instance awaiting its restore.
  • Codes and one revision. The body never carries an error message or a path. The details go to the server log, once per change of state: Instance not ready (warning, with both codes and the problem) or Instance ready (info). A monitor that asks every few seconds adds no log line while the state holds.
  • The head revision and the revisions the scripts know are read once per process, from the migration scripts of backend/alembic.ini: that read decides behind from ahead. A failed read is not cached: the next check tries again.
  • /system/health is a different question: it answers {"status": "ok"} as soon as the server answers, without touching the database. The image's HEALTHCHECK and both Compose files call it.

docs.title: 🔒 Private Endpoints (auth required)
docs.text:
All other endpoints — including Auth (profile, password), Settings (user settings, onboarding progress, and the global settings: any signed-in user reads them through GET /settings/global, only an administrator writes them; the login page needs none of them, it reads /system/instance), System diagnostics (/system/plugin-diagnostics), the block page (/system/block, see Instance Block), the catch-up of the prices (/system/price-refresh, see Catch-up Progress), Brokers, BRIM (files and plugins), Transactions, Uploads (CRUD + file serving + plugin assets), FX, Assets, Risk, Tools, Backup, and Users — require a valid session cookie. The routes of the hosting panel take a token of their own instead of a session cookie, one per scope, sent as Authorization: Bearer: the backup routes (/backup/panel/*, LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN), the scheduled wake-up (/system/wake-sync, LIBREFOLIO_WAKE_TOKEN) and the setup status (/panel/status, LIBREFOLIO_PANEL_STATUS_TOKEN); the panel's restore (/backup/panel/restore/*, scope backup:restore) takes a signed ticket only, never a token. One dependency checks them all, panel_access(scope): a missing or wrong token answers 401, too many refused ones from an address 429, and while a scope's token is not set its routes answer 404, as a path that does not exist: see The Hosting Panel's Access below. The account administration routes of /users (every route but /users/search) also require an administrator (require_admin): see Administrator API. So does GET /security/checks, the configuration checks on demand: see The Checks on Demand.

📁 Files are protected too

Uploaded files (/uploads/file/{id}) and plugin assets (/uploads/plugin/{type}/{path}) require authentication. Since auth uses HTTP-only cookies, the browser includes the session automatically for <img> tags — no special handling needed. A personal file needs more than a session: see Uploaded Files: Common and Personal.

📄 How a file is served: inline or attachment

GET /uploads/file/{id} (serve_file(), backend/app/api/v1/uploads.py) sends Content-Disposition: inline only when the file's stored type is in INLINE_SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES (backend/app/services/files/inline_media.py: application/pdf, application/json, text/plain, text/csv, and the images png, jpeg, gif, webp and bmp), so that the PDF fallback of the file preview, an <iframe>, shows the file instead of downloading it (H6-2). Any other type (HTML, SVG, XML…) and every request with ?download=true are an attachment: a type that can carry active content is never shown on the app's own address. Every response carries X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The broker report route (GET /brokers/import/files/{id}/download, backend/app/api/v1/brokers.py) imports the same list, so the two routes cannot disagree about what is safe to show.

For a complete endpoint reference, see the API Overview.

docs.title: 🔌 The Hosting Panel's Access
docs.text:
Lot H-61. A hosting panel calls the instance without a session, with one token per scope (decision Q2), and one dependency checks all its routes: panel_access(scope) in backend/app/services/platform/hosting_panel/access.py. PanelScope names the scopes:

Scope Routes Token reader, and its errors Bearer scheme 401 / 503 codes backup The four /backup/panel/jobs… routes, backend/app/api/v1/backup/panel.py (workstream B) backup_download_token(): SecretFileError, BackupConfigError BackupPanelToken backup_panel_unauthorized / backup_panel_unavailable wake POST /system/wake-sync, backend/app/api/v1/system/wake.py (workstream Z) wake_token(): SecretFileError, SleepWakeConfigError WakeToken wake_unauthorized / wake_unavailable status GET /panel/status, the setup status, read by admin_setup_status(), with the instance's mode and its restore (lot H-62), the two counts users_used and users_limit (lot H5-1), owner_email_change (lot H5-4), instance_key (lot H5-7, The Key Check) and users_over_limit (lot H5-8: a yes or no, Over the limit) panel_status_token() (backend/app/config/hosting_panel.py): SecretFileError, HostingPanelConfigError PanelStatusToken panel_status_unauthorized / panel_status_unavailable backup:restore (PanelScope.BACKUP_RESTORE) The seven /backup/panel/restore… routes, backend/app/api/v1/backup/panel_restore.py (lot H-62): see Awaiting Restore None: read_token always answers None, so no token opens it and, without the panel's public keys, it is off (404); a signed ticket of this scope only BackupRestorePanelTicket backup_restore_unauthorized / backup_restore_unavailable metrics (PanelScope.METRICS) GET /panel/metrics, get_panel_metrics in backend/app/api/v1/panel.py (lot CL-M1): the read-only figures of the instance, collected by collect_panel_metrics() in backend/app/services/platform/hosting_panel/metrics.py, answer PanelMetricsResponse None: read_token always answers None, so no token opens it and, without the panel's public keys, it is off (404); a signed ticket of this scope only PanelMetricsTicket panel_metrics_unauthorized / panel_metrics_unavailable

panel_access(scope) returns the same function for the same scope, so FastAPI runs it once per request. It takes the Request and the scope's HTTPBearer(auto_error=False), and returns PanelCaller(scope, credential="token"), a frozen dataclass. In this order:

  1. The token, read at each call. One of the scope's errors: the scope's error line (the backup's and the wake-up's worded as before H-61), one request line (below), then 503 with the scope's code. None, with no public keys either (L2, below): 404 {"detail": "Not Found"}, as a path that does not exist (decision Q3), with no line, nothing counted and the limiter not read.
  2. The limiter, on the key client_rate_key(rate_limit_address(request)) (The Client's Address), skipped when it is None, behind a proxy nobody trusts. A key over its limit (peek() not allowed) gets 429 with the code panel_too_many_attempts and Retry-After, the wait in whole seconds, rounded up, at least 1. The credential is not read.
  3. The credential, from Authorization: Bearer only, compared with the scope's token by hmac.compare_digest() on the UTF-8 bytes. Missing or different: hit() on the key, when there is one, then the scope's 401, with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.
  4. Accepted: the caller. A right credential is never counted, and clears nothing.

Every refusal but the 404 has the body {"detail": {"code": …, "message": …}}; those of the backup and wake-up routes are the ones they had before.

  • The limiter. PANEL_ATTEMPTS, built by new_panel_attempts(): one sliding-window limiter for the five scopes, PANEL_ATTEMPT_LIMIT (20) refused credentials per key in PANEL_ATTEMPT_WINDOW_SECONDS (600), in memory and per process. The dependency reads the module attribute at each call, so a test puts one of its own in place: monkeypatch.setattr(access, "PANEL_ATTEMPTS", SlidingWindowLimiter(20, 600, clock=fake)). In every test process the autouse fixture lift_panel_attempt_limit of backend/test_scripts/conftest.py gives each test one without a limit in practice, as the sign-in limit is off there.
  • The line. One per call, but for a scope that is off: Hosting panel request (REQUEST_LINE), INFO for the outcome accepted, WARNING for refused (reason: missing or mismatch), limited (retry_after) and unavailable (reason: unusable). Its other fields: scope, method, path (request.url.path, never the query) and credential ("token"), with the request_id from structlog's context variables (Request Logs). Never the token, the value sent, a header, the query or the client's address: uvicorn's access line has the address.
  • The OpenAPI tag. HOSTING_PANEL_TAG, «Hosting panel», is the only tag of the fourteen routes. FastAPI adds the tags of a router to those of what it includes, and never replaces them, so the tag sits on each include and the parent routers have none: backend/app/api/v1/backup/__init__.py includes panel.panel_router and panel_restore.panel_restore_router with it and its other routers with Backup & Export, backend/app/api/v1/system/__init__.py includes wake.wake_router with it and the others with System, and backend/app/api/v1/router.py includes the status route's router with the prefix /panel and the tag. Paths, methods and endpoint names did not move, so the operation ids and the aliases of the web app's client are those of before.
  • The bearer schemes. Each route asks for its scope's scheme alone, BackupPanelToken, WakeToken, PanelStatusToken, BackupRestorePanelTicket or PanelMetricsTicket, an HTTP bearer whose description names its variable: the OpenAPI document tells which token, or ticket, opens which route.
  • On a blocked instance the fourteen routes stay allowed: see Instance Block. The seven restore routes then answer 423 instance_blocked themselves, past the ticket (Awaiting Restore).

Level L2: signed tickets. Beside the tokens, panel_access() accepts a ticket signed by the panel's Ed25519 key (lot H-61, checkpoint 2), scope by scope. The panel's public keys are read at each call (panel_public_keys(), backend/app/config/hosting_panel.py), and a scope is off, with the 404, only when neither its token nor the keys are set.

Part Where What it does Verification verify_ticket(), backend/app/services/platform/hosting_panel/tickets.py PyJWT checks the signature and the algorithm, the rest is checked here, in the contract's order: unknown key, times (tolerance LIBREFOLIO_PANEL_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS), audience (the origin of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL), scope, jti and lifetime Registry record(), backend/app/services/platform/hosting_panel/ticket_registry.py Each accepted jti once, in <data dir>/panel_tickets.sqlite3 (mode 600, outside the backups), checked and recorded in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; rows pruned PRUNE_MARGIN_SECONDS (600 s, the widest tolerance plus the longest life) after their expiry, so a clock stepping back never revives a ticket; anything but a regular file (a symlink) or a file it cannot use raises TicketRegistryError, the scope's 503 Limiter _ticket_caller(), access.py Counts a ticket only when it proves nothing: unverifiable, or signed with an unknown key. A ticket with the panel's signature is never counted, so a panel whose clock is behind does not lock itself out Check check_hosting_panel(), backend/app/services/platform/config_audit.py Keys, tolerance and audience that cannot be used: error, and every route answers 503; in the managed profile a token beside usable keys is a warning

PanelCaller then carries credential="ticket", with the kid and the jti, and the request line adds both. The contract, the codes and the test vectors are in the panel's ticket verifier.

Tests: ./dev.py test services hosting-panel-access (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_hosting_panel_access.py: the status token's reader, the four steps for each scope, the limit across scopes and behind an untrusted proxy, the line), ./dev.py test api hosting-panel-routes (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_hosting_panel_routes.py: the tag, the endpoints and their operation ids, the schemes, the documented 429) and ./dev.py test api panel-status (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_panel_status_api.py: the status route).

docs.title: 🔢 Numbers in Requests
docs.text:
Every field typed float that a request fills, in the body or in a model nested in it, or as a query, path, header or cookie parameter, refuses infinity and NaN in its schema (lot H-32). It is Annotated[float, AllowInfNan(False)], which pydantic names FiniteFloat, or it carries bounds that exclude both: an upper bound (le, lt) excludes infinity and any bound excludes NaN, so ge=0 alone still lets infinity through. Money is Decimal, which refuses both by default; a finite value too large for its column is another matter: see Decimal Columns.

  • Why. Pydantic accepts inf, -inf and nan in a float by default (allow_inf_nan=True), and the request body is parsed with Python's json, which reads 1E+400 as infinity and accepts the NaN and Infinity tokens. A value the schema lets in can be saved and used, and reads back as null: FastAPI 0.141 serialises the answer of a route with a response_model through pydantic, which writes infinity and NaN as null. A route without a response_model that returns the value as it is fails with a 500 instead: Starlette's JSON renderer refuses them (allow_nan=False).
  • Field by field, not in the base model. allow_inf_nan=False on StrictModel (backend/app/schemas/common.py) would reach further than the requests: the same base backs the response models and the internal payloads (AI Export, risk), where a computed NaN would become an exception inside a service. The rule is for requests only.
  • The guard. ./dev.py test services request-float-inputs (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_request_float_inputs.py) walks every route of the app with fastapi.routing.iter_route_contexts, which also sees the routes of included routers, unlike a plain loop over app.routes. It judges each request float with a TypeAdapter: a float that accepts any of inf, -inf, NaN or 1E+400 fails it, named by route, model and field. Two barriers keep it from passing empty: a minimum number of routes walked, and at least one float found.
  • Today: six request floats. Five are signal parameters of the annotation requests that POST /assets/prices/query and POST /fx/currencies/convert accept (backend/app/schemas/signals.py): epsilon and relative_epsilon, declared in SignalAnnotationRequestBase, of both SignalLineCrossoverRequest and SignalThresholdCrossingRequest, and threshold of the second, all FiniteFloat already. The sixth is the plain value of a plugin setting (PluginSettingWriteItem.value, PATCH /settings/plugins/bulk): PluginSettingPlainValue (backend/app/schemas/plugin_settings.py) now has AllowInfNan(False) on its float branch, as validate_value() (backend/app/services/plugin_settings/fields.py) already refused a non-finite number before saving: see Types and Validation.
  • Free-form JSON (lot H-34). The H-32 rule is for float fields; a request can also carry free-form JSON, a position typed Any, object or pydantic's JsonValue, where any number may sit. The guard walks those positions too: it requires exactly the free-form positions it knows (KNOWN_FREE_FORM), and that each refuses a number that is not finite anywhere inside, at the top, in a list or in a nested mapping, without the number in the refusal's message. A new free-form position fails it until it is added there with its probe. Today there are five: FAProviderAssignmentItem.provider_params and FAProviderProbeRequest.provider_params (POST /assets/provider and /assets/provider/probe; their base is FAProviderConfigBase, in backend/app/schemas/provider.py), RiskAnalyticRequest.parameters (POST /risk/query, backend/app/schemas/risk.py), SignalRequest.params (POST /assets/prices/query, /fx/currencies/convert and /signals/preview; backend/app/schemas/signals.py) and ToolComputeItem.parameters (POST /tools/compute, backend/app/schemas/tools.py). The provider parameters hold Any, the other three JsonValue. The two provider requests and RiskAnalyticRequest now run ensure_json_safe (backend/app/utils/json_utils.py) in a field_validator(mode="before"), as SignalRequest.params already did: the answer is a 422 that names the path, such as provider_params.deep[1], never the value (Validation Errors Without the Input). Before H-34, a provider's parameter was saved as Infinity and read back as null. ToolComputeItem refuses through allow_inf_nan=False in the config of its base, ToolTransportModel, which JsonValue respects and Any does not; on top of that, the tools route's own JSON parser (parse_json() in backend/app/services/tools/wire.py) refuses the NaN and Infinity tokens, and a number too large for a double such as 1E+400.
  • Not covered: a bare dict or list. Without item types, the walk does not open it. TXMixedBatch (POST /transactions/validate and /commit, backend/app/schemas/transactions/batch.py) holds its rows so, as List[dict], and the service validates them one by one afterwards, each with its own model: a SafeDecimal there refuses infinity and NaN.

docs.title: 🧯 Error Answers
docs.text:
A 5xx tells the client what finds its failure in the log, never what the failure was (lot H-60, decision D2). The developer's rule (19/10/2026): when something fails, the useful information is printed, in the server log and in the browser console (The Browser Console). His question, whether what is printed exposes sensitive data, is answered by the rules below: no message or traceback in an answer, no query string, header or body in a line.

Failure Answer Log An HTTPException below 500 FastAPI's own, unchanged Nothing from the platform An HTTPException from 500 FastAPI's {"detail": …} plus request_id and error_type, with the exception's headers The failure once, unless the code that caught it logged it in this request; a short WARNING when another request's log has it An exception nobody handled 500, {"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": …, "error_type": …} One ERROR, Unhandled error, unless this request's log has it; a short WARNING when another request's log has it A response that breaks its model (H-33) 500, {"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": …, "error_type": "ResponseValidationError"} Its own ERROR, without the response (Request Logs)
  • Where. install_server_error_handler(app) (backend/app/api/server_errors.py), which main.py installs after the 422 handler and the H-33 one, answers every HTTPException: below 500 through FastAPI's own http_exception_handler(), the same body and headers; from 500 with FastAPI's body and the two keys. The body (error_body()) and the log lines (report_server_error(), report_unhandled_error()) live in backend/app/services/platform/failure_report.py, shared with the 500 of SecurityHeadersMiddleware and the H-33 handler, so every 5xx the platform builds has one shape.
  • request_id is the request's id, the one its X-Request-Id header carries (Request Logs): a user who reports an error quotes it, and the administrator finds every line of the request with it. The key is absent only for a request the request-id middleware did not see, which the app's stack rules out.
  • error_type is the class name of the root cause, the deepest exception a reader of the traceback reaches, following from each exception the cause attribute that the AI Export wrappers carry instead of __cause__, else __cause__, else a __context__ that is not suppressed (visible_causes() and root_cause(), backend/app/utils/runtime/errors.py). For an HTTPException the key is absent without a visible cause: raised outside an except, or from None. For an exception nobody handled it is always there, the exception's own class when it has no cause.
  • Never the message, never the traceback. A message can hold data (an SQL error quotes its statement), a traceback paths and values: both go to the log, and only there. detail stays what the route wrote.
  • The log gets the failure once. One exception object can reach several requests. The portfolio engine runs one build per key at a time, and when the build fails, every request waiting on it gets the same exception (one build per key, MF-J45b/d); the risk engines (backend/app/services/risk/quant/engine.py, optimization_engine.py) do the same. One mark on the object let the first request that logged the failure silence the others, which answered with ids no line carried. Since lot H-60r the mark is per request (Request Logs): the safety net writes the traceback once, and a short line with its own request_id for each other request the failure reaches. For a 5xx HTTPException, report_server_error() writes exactly one of:
    • for a visible cause nobody logged, one ERROR, Request failed, with request_id, status, method, path, error_type, error_chain (the class names from the HTTPException down to the root cause) and the traceback, in exception. When the chain goes through a cause attribute, the traceback is that of the last exception reached that way (shown_error()): Python never renders such a link, so that traceback says the most;
    • without a visible cause, and with nothing logged, one WARNING, Request answered a server error, with request_id, status, method and path, so that every id a client sees is in the log;
