docs.title: ⏱️ AI Export Technical Sampling
docs.text: AI Export reduces historical numeric density deterministically while preserving scope, indicators, outputs, summaries, latest values, and selected events.

docs.title: 📐 Rational Bucket Formula
docs.text:
Let:

  • \(x\): whole-calendar-day distance backward from snapshot_as_of;
  • \(P\): shape exponent;
  • \(M\): half-transition offset after the seven-day daily ramp;
  • \(K\): asymptotic maximum bucket width in calendar days;
  • \(T\): total requested inclusive calendar-day count.

The continuous width is:

\[ f(x;P,M,K) = 1+(K-1) \, \frac{\max(x-7,0)^P} {M^P+\max(x-7,0)^P} \]

The integer width is:

\[ D(x;P,M,K) = \max\left( 1, \operatorname{round}_{\text{half-up}}\left[f(x;P,M,K)\right] \right) \]

Boundaries are generated iteratively:

\[ x_0=0 \] \[ x_{n+1}=\min\left(T,\ x_n+D(x_n;P,M,K)\right) \]

Each offset interval becomes one bucket when translated back from snapshot_as_of. Runtime arithmetic uses Decimal with explicit ROUND_HALF_UP, not binary floating point or banker's rounding.

The result is deterministic, positive, monotonic in historical width, bounded by \(K\), gap-free, overlap-free, and clipped exactly to \(T\).

docs.title: 📅 Recent Daily Window
docs.text:
For every detail level and temporal class:

\[ 0 \le x \le 7 \Rightarrow D(x)=1 \]

The most recent seven calendar days therefore remain daily. This is calendar sampling, not market-session sampling. Empty intervals remain in bucket plans and diagnostics. Indicator payloads publish source/non-empty counts but omit empty rows; the public renderer also omits completely empty financial temporal rows and the empty buckets of price and rate series. Neither path invents observations or converts absence to zero. Empty price and rate buckets are not silent, though: each maximal run of them that holds a market-open day is reported, merged, as one gap carrying the last value stored before it, if any, never a value inside it. A weekend or a market holiday alone, whole empty daily buckets in this window, is never a gap, and neither is the snapshot day alone at the end of the series, whose price may not be synchronized yet (Price and Rate Gaps).

docs.title: 🧮 Full Policy Matrix
docs.text:
Reference counts use exact inclusive periods of 90, 180, and 365 calendar days.

Detail Temporal class P M K 90d 180d 365d Compact Very Fast 2 30 30 20 23 29 Compact Fast 2 25 35 18 21 26 Compact Medium Fast 2 20 42 16 18 23 Compact Medium 2 10 42 14 16 20 Compact Slow 2 5 49 12 14 17 Compact Very Slow 2 5 84 11 12 14 Standard Very Fast 2 30 14 26 33 46 Standard Fast 2 21 15 23 29 41 Standard Medium Fast 2 20 17 21 26 37 Standard Medium 2 15 20 18 23 32 Standard Slow 2 10 22 16 20 28 Standard Very Slow 2 5 28 13 16 23 Full Very Fast 2 30 7 35 49 75 Full Fast 2 28 8 32 44 67 Full Medium Fast 2 23 9 28 38 59 Full Medium 2 16 10 24 33 51 Full Slow 2 10 11 21 29 46 Full Very Slow 2 9 14 18 24 38

Within one detail level, density decreases from Very Fast to Very Slow. For one temporal class, Full is at least as dense as Standard, which is at least as dense as Compact. Very Fast is the original detail-only baseline.

docs.title: 💹 Price and Rate Policy
docs.text:
Asset prices, FX rates, and equivalent reference series use detail only:

Detail P M K Compact 2 30 30 Standard 2 30 14 Full 2 30 7

Signal temporal classes never change reference price/rate density.

docs.title: 📈 Indicator Policy
docs.text:
Indicator history uses:

detail_level + plugin-owned temporal_class → P, M, K

AI Export does not branch on signal codes. The plugin resolves one temporal class from normalized parameters; central policy resolves the matrix row.

docs.title: 🗂️ Initial Instance Mapping
docs.text:
The Asset bundle has 20 instances. Portfolio and Broker reuse it per eligible asset. FX uses the marked 12-instance subset.

Instance Signal Temporal class In FX ema_20 EMA(20) Medium ✓ ema_50 EMA(50) Slow ✓ ema_200 EMA(200) Very Slow ✓ sma_50 SMA(50) Slow ✓ sma_200 SMA(200) Very Slow ✓ kama_20 KAMA(20) Medium ✓ aroon_25 Aroon(25) Medium adx_14 ADX(14) Medium donchian_20 Donchian(20) Medium Fast rsi_14 RSI(14) Very Fast ✓ macd_12_26_9 MACD(12,26,9) Medium Fast ✓ ppo_12_26_9 PPO(12,26,9) Medium Fast ✓ roc_20 ROC(20) Fast ✓ stoch_rsi_14_3 StochRSI(14,3) Very Fast ✓ cci_20 CCI(20) Fast bollinger_20_2 Bollinger(20,2) Medium Fast ✓ atr_14 ATR(14) Fast natr_14 NATR(14) Fast mfi_14 MFI(14) Very Fast obv OBV Medium

EMA and SMA use exact parameter-match rules because one plugin produces multiple time horizons. Other listed plugins use one fixed class for their current curated instances. Unknown or ambiguous matches raise; official plugins do not silently fall back.

docs.title: 🧺 Multi-output Indicators
docs.text:
MACD, PPO, Bollinger, Donchian, Aroon, StochRSI, and ADX produce multiple outputs. Every output of one instance shares the same bucket boundaries. Scalar outputs and band components become columns in one row-oriented table.

For each populated cell:

  • one observation uses compact value + real date;
  • multiple observations preserve count, first, min, max, last, and their real observation dates.

period_summary is calculated across the entire exported period, independent of bucket density. Each output column also carries its latest observed value/date.

docs.title: 📦 Public Indicator History Limits
docs.text:
The backend applies one additional deterministic presentation limit to non-empty indicator buckets for each entity and Signal instance:

Detail Non-empty rows Compact 5 Standard 10 Full All

Compact and Standard select rows uniformly across the full exported period, including the first and last non-empty rows. This does not change the Signal set, Asset scope, output columns, latest values, or full-period summary. The public manifest exposes indicator_history_row_limit; each indicator payload retains source bucket and source non-empty row counts.

The compact text renderer uses row-relative date references inside history cells: s is the row start, e is the row end, and +N is a calendar-day offset from the row start. Event values are positional only when their definition declares the exact value_fields order. These are lossless text encodings, not additional financial calculations.

docs.title: 🔥 Calculation Range, Exported Range, and Warm-up
docs.text:
Indicators calculate on sessions — the quote days of a warm-up-inclusive input — with plugin-owned, parameter-aware warm-up. The loaded series keeps one point per calendar day. A day filled with an earlier price or rate carries backward_fill_info, and an Asset's stored weekend or market-holiday row that repeats the previous close exactly is marked as carried before the signals run (mark_market_closed_carries, the rule the Risk series use). For every plugin with computes_on_quote_days — the 17 technical indicators, so every curated instance — SignalService keeps only the quote days of the selected points (quote_day_points): points whose price was quoted on their own date, even when their exchange rate was carried. Periods, warm-up, minimum history, and visible points therefore count sessions, and indicator values are dated on sessions. States and annotations are also derived before numeric bucket aggregation.

Only the requested exported period is serialized:

warm-up-inclusive calendar input
→ keep its sessions (quote days)
→ full session-level indicator and event calculation
→ slice to exported period
→ aggregate numeric history

The load window is counted in calendar days: SignalExecutionPlan.max_history_days_before_visible is the largest warm-up of the requested instances, in sessions, times SESSION_WARMUP_DAY_MULTIPLIER (two calendar days per session). Asset loading delegates warm-up to SignalService through AssetSourceManager, which loads that window before the requested start. FX sizes its own load of earlier daily rates with the same plan value (_fx_warmup_days); a day without a published rate is backward-filled, carries backward_fill_info, and is not a session. The component response declares warmup_policy: component_owned; the current aggregate calculation_range and earliest_calculation_date metadata fields are not populated.

FX source history may begin after the requested start. Dates before the first stored rate are omitted from the warm-up input rather than failing the entire snapshot. SignalService then includes calculable ok/partial instances and reports unavailable instances through technical coverage. Coverage stays on the calendar although indicators count sessions: the snapshot metadata publishes requested/available ranges and calendar-day coverage, with the counts of observed and backward-filled days. No future rate is ever used.

docs.title: 🎯 Event Selection
docs.text:
Events are validated, observed-only filtered, epsilon checked, gap checked, and semantically deduplicated before selection. They are detected from original observations, never from buckets.

Policy is independent for every:

entity_id + annotation_key

For Portfolio and Broker, entity_id retains the originating Asset identity before events are merged. FX uses the canonical pair identity.

The complete recent window and minimum latest count are detail-owned:

Detail Complete recent window Minimum latest events Compact 7 calendar days 3 Standard 21 calendar days 10 Full 30 calendar days 20

For each group:

  1. sort newest to oldest;
  2. include every event satisfying the detail-owned inclusive recent boundary;
  3. if fewer than the detail-owned minimum are included, continue backward to that minimum;
  4. if fewer events exist, include all;
  5. restore deterministic public chronological order after selection.

This is not a hard cap. A volatile annotation may export more than the minimum when more events occur inside the complete recent window. There is no ranking, relevance score, family quota, or episode consolidation.

Each group exports a selection summary with detected/recent/exported counts, selection status, oldest/newest detected and exported dates, and optional upward/downward counts.

docs.title: 🧭 Focused Context Policies
docs.text:
The complete technical datasets and explicitly technical analyses continue to use the global policy above unchanged.

Semantic Composition V2 also exposes separate focused context components for financial analyses. Their backend-declared policies are intentionally narrower and do not alter global Compact/Standard/Full:

  • Portfolio/Broker general snapshots expose current/summary market fields, a 6/12/24-row observed-only uniform path per eligible Asset, and the latest selected structural event per category;
  • multi-Asset comparisons expose a bounded set of latest structural event types;
  • Portfolio Description uses an aggregate 30-day event digest, with the latest prior event when a type has no recent occurrence;
  • Asset Position Context exposes 8/16/30 uniform observed rows;
  • FX Market Context exposes 8/16/30 uniform genuine-observation rows;
  • Portfolio/Broker aggregate NAV paths expose 8/16/30 uniform rows. NAV values are explicitly flow-inclusive; normalized return uses historical TWRR;
  • focused rows carry bucket boundaries, the real representative observation, observation count, normalized index, and return from the first observation. Bucket extrema are omitted because the per-entity summary already carries full-period extrema;
  • Drawdown context sections carry no numeric history at all: they reuse the Risk drawdown_summary current/maximum episode dates and coverage verbatim;
  • PAC's per-Asset Drawdown snapshot is one observed-price row per Asset and also carries no Drawdown history;
  • technical coverage names current Assets excluded from technical eligibility and publishes a deterministic reason such as end_value_unavailable;
  • every detailed indicator block publishes its own result_status and partial_reason_code;
  • task-specific evidence datasets apply component-local monotonic detail (for example income Compact aggregates by (month, asset, income_type), Standard adds bounded recent dated rows, Full exposes every dated row).

These limits are semantic component contracts, not token-triggered truncation. They do not change the Signal or Asset scope; Full retains every non-empty indicator bucket and the complete 30-day/minimum-20 event policy.

docs.title: 🧹 Public Empty Temporal Rows
docs.text:
The generic public renderer applies the same no-empty-row principle to financial temporal tables that technical histories already use.

A row is omitted only when it contains nominal start/end/index metadata and no observation, flow, variation, P&L, extrema, reconciliation, meaningful observed date, or explicit non-absence status. Numeric zero remains meaningful and keeps the row.

This presentation rule does not modify:

  • backend bucket boundaries;
  • calculations or requested frequency;
  • sampling policy;
  • requested/effective/available periods;
  • coverage or insufficient-history warnings.

Probe diagnostics count empty rows detected/omitted and temporal rows remaining.

Price and rate series apply the same principle in their own renderer: BUCKETS lists only the buckets with an observation, and the omitted ones count in the same diagnostics. Their open-market absences are not dropped, though: the backend reports each maximal run of contiguous empty buckets that holds a market-open day as one merged gap (price_gaps, rate_gaps) carrying the last value stored before it, and the renderer prints the gaps right after BUCKETS, in a PRICE GAPS or RATE GAPS table followed by one meaning line (Snapshot Data Tables). A gap is missing data: not a zero, and not proof that the value stayed the same. Weekends and market holidays alone are never gaps.

docs.title: 🏷️ Latest-per-category Context Events
docs.text:
Focused market-context components select at most one latest event per (entity_id, signal_category). The category is plugin-owned (read from the Signal plugin's category, failing loudly for unknown plugins); candidates are the allowlist-filtered observation-level discrete events. Tie-breaks within a category are deterministic by (date, annotation key, signal code), and categories with no eligible event are omitted rather than emitted as null rows.

This is distinct from the technical event policy above, whose recent window and minimum count depend on detail. The permanent density probe therefore tracks these event families separately: detailed_event_rows (complete-policy events), context_event_rows, latest_event_rows with latest_event_category_count, and the Portfolio Description event_digest_group_count / event_digest_underlying_event_count.

docs.title: 💱 FX Observed Range Position
docs.text:
FX conversion-timing evidence frames the current rate against the observed period minimum/maximum as a plain range position (current - min) / (max - min), deliberately not a historical percentile or rank and not a forecast. A flat range (observed_maximum == observed_minimum) or an empty period reports range_position_ratio = None with an explicit reason (flat_observed_range / no_observed_rates_in_period). Partial source history is explicit through is_partial_history plus a partial_history_reason (source_history_starts_after_period_start / no_genuine_observations_in_period); only genuine, non-backfilled observations count and no future rate is ever consulted.

The same timing component (fx.timing_context) also publishes trailing 30- and 91-day returns, the period return, and daily-return volatility, all from genuine observations inside the AI period. A trailing return is null when the observed history does not reach back to its anchor date.

docs.title: 🧾 Manifest Examples
docs.text:
The public prompt manifest exposes only information that helps interpret the sampled data:

technical_sampling:
  detail_level: standard
  indicator_history_row_limit: 10
  price_policy:
    bucket_count: 46
  indicator_policies:
    - signal_instance_id: ema_200
      signal_code: EMA
      temporal_class: very_slow
      bucket_count: 23

detail_level appears once because every policy in one request shares it. temporal_class explains the indicator horizon, while bucket_count reports the backend aggregation density. indicator_history_row_limit reports the additional non-empty rows retained per entity/instance in the public payload.

P, M, and K remain normative internal policy parameters. They stay in the matrix, formula tests, mathematical probes, and engineering reports above, but are intentionally absent from the API response and copied prompt.

Top-level event policy audit:

event_selection:
  minimum_latest_events_per_annotation: 10
  complete_recent_window_days: 21
  grouped_by:
    - entity_id
    - annotation_key

Per-group payload summary:

entity_id: asset:42
annotation_key: ema_50_ema_200
detected_count: 37
recent_window_count: 6
exported_count: 6
selection_applied: true
oldest_detected_event_date: 2024-02-01
newest_detected_event_date: 2026-07-29
oldest_exported_event_date: 2026-07-18
newest_exported_event_date: 2026-07-29

docs.title: 🧪 Extension and Testing Checklist
docs.text:
When adding or changing an exportable indicator:

  1. declare plugin-owned ai_export_temporal_rules;
  2. use fixed rules only for one semantic horizon;
  3. use explicit parameter matching for multi-horizon plugins;
  4. verify exactly one rule resolves for every curated instance;
  5. keep warm-up, input validation, output validation, AI descriptions, states, and annotations plugin-owned;
  6. verify all outputs share one grid;
  7. test all relevant detail/class matrix rows and 90/180/365 counts;
  8. test daily first seven days, monotonic widths, \(K\) bound, exact final boundary, no gap, and no overlap;
  9. test unavailable/failed omission without sibling loss;
  10. test detail-owned event boundary inclusivity/minimums, unlimited events inside the complete recent window, grouping, deduplication, and order;
  11. inspect technical_sampling, event_selection, and selection summaries;
  12. run documentation validation.
./dev.py test services ai-export
./dev.py test services signal-plugin-matrix
./dev.py mkdocs build
./dev.py mkdocs check-links

docs.title: 🧠 AI Export Component Runtime
docs.text:
AI Export builds an authenticated, factual backend snapshot and lets the frontend compose a clipboard-ready prompt. LibreFolio does not call an LLM, upload the snapshot, or choose where the user pastes it.

First public contract: V1

Snapshot schema, public catalog, public Dataset/Analysis selections, instruction templates, and response contracts start at V1. Frontend and backend reject stale identities; there is no compatibility fallback.

docs.title: 🧱 Runtime Catalog
docs.text:
The component runtime contains:

Domain Components Registered datasets Registered analyses Public data Public analyses Page Portfolio 21 12 4 2 4 Dashboard Broker 20 12 3 2 3 Broker Asset 14 8 2 2 2 Asset FX 12 8 2 2 2 FX Total 67 40 11 8 11

Components are the smallest buildable facts. Datasets can be public or internal; visibility defaults to internal. The eleven registered Analyses are all public and may compose internal datasets. Direct requests accept only public selection IDs.

flowchart LR
    S["Authoritative sources and engines"] --> C["67 granular components"]
    C --> D["40 registered datasets"]
    D --> E["8 public Export Data"]
    D --> A["11 public Analyses<br/>+ frontend contracts"]
    A --> P["Request Analysis<br/>full prompt"]

See Composition & Prompt for dependency, ordering, and failure semantics.

docs.title: 🔄 Request Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as User
    participant F as AI Export frontend
    participant A as /api/v1/ai-export
    participant R as Component runtime
    participant S as Sources and engines
    participant C as Clipboard

    F->>A: GET /catalog
    A-->>F: 8 datasets + 11 analyses, V1 identities
    U->>F: Export Data or Request Analysis
    F->>A: POST /snapshot with selected V1 contract
    A->>R: Authenticated request + accessible broker scope
    R->>S: Load authoritative resources
    S-->>R: Financial and technical facts
    R-->>A: Ordered component envelopes + manifests
    A-->>F: Strict V1 snapshot response
    F->>F: Validate, serialize, add trusted local prompt text
    F->>C: Write final text
    C-->>U: Clipboard updated

The backend builds one request-scoped BuildContext. Shared DB reports, prices, rates, FIFO results, signal results, and component envelopes are memoized so overlapping datasets do not repeat work.

Before anything is built, prepare_request() bounds the requested period (R13-SEC7-1): it ends no later than latest_range_end() (tomorrow, utils/datetime_utils.py) and starts at most 100 calendar years before that end, never after it. Components walk the period day by day, and an unbounded one held the instance. The scope, every component, the bucket plan and the response meta (exported_period, snapshot_as_of, the FX history_coverage.requested_period) all read the bounded period; a request inside the bounds is unchanged, and no component contract changes.

The profile/assembler runtime that preceded the component runtime during development was removed before release. The first released snapshot schema is V1 (AI_EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1), so there is no older schema to accept or migrate. The API, diagnostic probes, and tests all use this component runtime; there is no legacy catalog or fallback execution path.

docs.title: 🧭 Ownership Boundary
docs.text:
Backend owns factual meaning Frontend owns presentation Authentication and broker authorization Localized labels and descriptions Component, dataset, and analysis registries Analysis instructions Portfolio Engine, FIFO, FX, provider, and Signal Plugin facts Response contracts Required/optional composition and applicability User notes and response language Sampling and event-selection policies Safe YAML/Markdown serialization Focused technical projection selection Localized Additional Data guidance FX requested/available history coverage A#/B#/F# public reference rendering Dataset, technical-sampling, and event-selection manifests Clipboard transport Typed failure semantics Prompt-size display

Frontend code must not recalculate portfolio metrics, FIFO, FX conversions, indicators, states, events, sampling, or event selection.

docs.title: 🏦 Broker Scope Semantics
docs.text:
Portfolio snapshots distinguish three Broker universes:

Public field Meaning scoped_broker_count Brokers selected for the calculation after access validation. position_broker_count Brokers with current open positions at snapshot_as_of. period_contributor_broker_count Brokers represented by period performance contributors. broker_scope The scoped universe rendered as B# references.

A scoped Broker may have no current position. A period contributor may be historical-only. The Entity Directory includes every scoped Broker, including all-accessible requests that did not send an explicit Broker filter.

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication and Failures
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/ai-export/catalog is static and user-data-free. POST /api/v1/ai-export/snapshot is authenticated and read-only.

HTTP Code Meaning 403 broker_access_denied Requested broker scope is not fully accessible. 404 entity_not_found Requested Asset, Broker, or other target does not exist. 409 version_mismatch Catalog, selection, instruction, or response-contract identity differs. 422 unsupported_selection Dataset or analysis is unknown or belongs to another domain. 422 selection_not_applicable Runtime facts do not satisfy an analysis applicability rule. 422 selection_not_applicable reason_code too_many_price_days: the prices a required component reads exceed one request's budget (J-50). 503 snapshot_source_failure A required component raised while building.

Required failures fail closed. Optional failures may be omitted and remain internally diagnosed. A successfully built empty payload is valid data, not a source failure.

docs.title: 📦 Completeness and Size
docs.text:
AI Export preserves the selected scope and detail level:

  • no token- or character-based truncation;
  • no segmented or paginated prompt;
  • no automatic detail downgrade;
  • no asset or indicator removal for size reasons;
  • no legacy builder fallback;
  • no LLM request.

Technical history uses deterministic density reduction rather than truncation. Events use deterministic per-annotation selection rather than ranking. See Technical Sampling.

Backend temporal buckets remain available for calculation and diagnostics. The public renderer omits only rows that contain nominal bucket boundaries and no observation, economic value, flow, P&L, extrema, reconciliation, meaningful date, or explicit non-absence state. Observed zero values remain public. Requested, effective, and available periods plus coverage/warnings remain visible.

General public snapshots combine the complete economic scope with focused market context. Portfolio/Broker paths use 8/16/30 uniform rows; per-Asset paths inside them use 6/12/24; single Asset and FX focused paths use 8/16/30. Detailed public market exports retain the complete technical sampling and event policies.

General snapshots also carry dated income, concentration bases, Broker cost/turnover, non-predictive FX conversion timing, peak-relative Drawdown, economic FIFO summaries, allocated-vs-unallocated cost semantics, and current Assets excluded from technical eligibility with reason codes.

Portfolio, Broker, and Asset FIFO payloads declare cost_allocation_semantics: lot fees and taxes contain only costs deterministically allocated to lots. Unallocated costs are excluded from lots (Portfolio payloads point to the fee/tax sections, Broker payloads to the flows and cost-efficiency evidence) and must never be read as a recorded zero. Conversely, asset.performance renders the zero realized P&L, income, and fees/taxes that the Portfolio Engine omits from contribution rows explicitly as recorded zero (zero_semantics).

FX snapshots may succeed with partial source history. The response keeps the requested period and separately reports the available period, calendar-day coverage, observed/backfilled counts, and insufficient_source_history warning. A snapshot still fails when no rate exists on or before the snapshot date. FX conversion-timing evidence frames the current rate against the observed period minimum/maximum as a plain range position, never a percentile and never a forecast.

docs.title: 🗃️ Database Migrations (Alembic)
docs.text: LibreFolio uses Alembic to manage database schema changes. Alembic is a lightweight database migration tool for SQLAlchemy that provides a versioning system for your database schema.

docs.title: 🔄 Workflow
docs.text:
The basic workflow for making a schema change is:

  1. Modify SQLAlchemy Models: Make changes to your db/models.py files (e.g., add a new column, create a new table).

  2. Generate a Migration Script: Run the dev.py command to automatically generate a new migration script. 

    ./dev.py db migrate "Your descriptive message"
    This command compares your SQLAlchemy models to the current state of the database and generates a Python script in backend/alembic/versions/ that contains the necessary upgrade() and downgrade() functions.

  3. Review the Migration Script: Always review the generated script. Alembic is not perfect, especially with SQLite, and may require manual adjustments.

  4. Apply the Migration: Run the upgrade command to apply the changes to your database. 

    ./dev.py db upgrade

docs.title: 📦 One Migration per Release
docs.text:
Each release ships one migration: 004_release_1_2_0_schema for 1.2, 005_release_1_3_0_schema for 1.3 (the developer's decision, 19/10/2026). During a cycle a migration is written whenever the work needs one; before the release, the cycle's unreleased migrations are folded into one 00N_release_<version>_schema, on the head of the previous release. The chain as it stands is in Migrations.

  1. Only what no released tag holds. A database stores the revision id in alembic_version, so an id that a released tag holds stays in the chain for good. Check each file before folding it:

    git cat-file -e <tag>:backend/alembic/versions/<file>   # succeeds when the tag holds the file

  2. Freeze the schema, then delete the chain. Once its files are gone the chain cannot run, so first freeze the schema it builds on a new database. For 1.3: every row of sqlite_master, its SQL with whitespace collapsed, in backend/test_scripts/fixtures/migrations/schema_1_3_retired_chain_v4.json, never regenerated.

  3. Test the new file against it. A new database taken to the new revision must be the frozen schema. For 1.3: ./dev.py test db migration-005 (backend/test_scripts/test_db/test_migration_005_release_1_3.py), which also carries the data scenarios of the retired tests.
  4. Keep the id within 32 characters, as for any revision: Alembic's alembic_version.version_num is VARCHAR(32). 005_release_1_3_0_schema has 24.

005_release_1_3_0_schema keeps the work of the retired revisions as steps, in their order, each checking before it acts, so that a run stopped half way can run again; its docstring maps each retired id to its step.

A database stamped with a retired id comes from an unreleased build. It is brought forward by hand, with the procedure the developer journal keeps, never by code in the app: the server does not start on it, and a backup at such an id is refused as from a newer LibreFolio (see «Retired revision ids» in Migrations).

docs.title: 🗂️ Indexes: Only the Ones a Query Uses
docs.text:
An index costs space, and time on every insert and update, and serves only the queries that read it. The rule (the developer's decision, 19/10/2026) came with an analysis that read every query of 67 endpoints with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: 005_release_1_3_0_schema dropped 13 indexes of 001_initial (001_initial.py stays as released), and no query plan got worse.

  • A UNIQUE constraint already creates its index (sqlite_autoindex_<table>_<n>). Never add an Index, index=True or CREATE INDEX on the same columns: in a model, Field(unique=True) or a UniqueConstraint alone. unique=True, index=True makes create_all build a unique index where a migration writes the constraint, and 001_initial, which wrote both, left six copies: idx_price_history_asset_date, idx_asset_provider_asset_id, uq_assets_display_name (the index; the UNIQUE on display_name stays), ix_brokers_name, ix_users_username and ix_users_email.
  • No index that is the left prefix of another. (broker_id, date, id) already serves every query on broker_id, and SQLite's foreign-key checks on it. Five of the 13 were such prefixes: ix_transactions_broker_id, ix_transactions_asset_id, ix_broker_user_access_user_id, idx_route_base_quote and ix_fx_conversion_routes_base.
  • Every new index has a query that uses it, proven with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. Name the query in the migration's docstring, with its plan line. The last two of the 13 had no reader: ix_transactions_date (every query on transactions is scoped by broker or asset) and ix_fx_conversion_routes_quote (a pair is always looked up with its base).

The plan line is what SQLite will do for the query, on any database at the revision:

sqlite3 app.db "EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE broker_id = 1 ORDER BY date, id"

QUERY PLAN
`--SEARCH transactions USING INDEX idx_transactions_broker_date (broker_id=?)

SEARCH <table> USING INDEX <name> (or USING COVERING INDEX <name>) is the proof that <name> serves the query; SCAN <table> means that no index does. Here idx_transactions_broker_date serves a filter on its first column, which is why ix_transactions_broker_id could go, and its date and id give the order with no USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY line. Filtered on date alone, the same query answers SCAN transactions: no index serves it, and none needs to, since every query of the app on transactions is scoped by broker or asset.

The guard. ./dev.py test db validate runs test_no_redundant_indexes (backend/test_scripts/test_db/db_schema_validate.py). It reads every index of every table from SQLite's catalogue, the automatic ones of the UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY constraints included, and fails on an index whose key columns equal another's, or are a left prefix of them, naming both. A UNIQUE index on a left prefix of a longer index (it enforces a constraint the longer one does not), a partial index and an index on an expression (such as ux_users_email_lower on lower(email)) are not redundancy. A redundancy kept on purpose goes in _REDUNDANT_INDEXES_ALLOWED, the pair with its reason on one line; an entry that no longer matches a pair fails too. An index nobody reads cannot be told from the catalogue: that is what the EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN rule is for.

docs.title: ⚠️ SQLite and Alembic Limitations
docs.text:
SQLite has limited support for ALTER TABLE statements, which can make schema migrations more complex than with other databases like PostgreSQL. Alembic works around this by using a "batch mode" that:

  1. Creates a new table with the desired schema.
  2. Copies the data from the old table to the new table.
  3. Drops the old table.
  4. Renames the new table to the original name.

docs.title: 🔍 The CHECK Constraint Problem
docs.text:
A significant limitation of this approach is that Alembic's autogenerate feature does not detect CHECK constraints in SQLite.

This means that if you add or modify a CHECK constraint in your SQLAlchemy model, you must manually add it to the generated migration script.

docs.title: 📝 Example: Manually Adding a CHECK Constraint
docs.text:
If you add a CHECK constraint to the Transaction model:

class Transaction(SQLModel, table=True):
    # ...
    __table_args__ = (
        CheckConstraint("quantity >= 0", name="check_quantity_positive"),
    )

Alembic will not include this in the autogenerated script. You must edit the upgrade() function in the migration file and add it yourself:

# In the generated migration file: backend/alembic/versions/xxxx_add_check.py

def upgrade() -> None:
    # ... other operations ...

    with op.batch_alter_table('transaction', schema=None) as batch_op:
        batch_op.create_check_constraint(
            'check_quantity_positive',  # Constraint name
            'quantity >= 0'             # SQL expression
        )

def downgrade() -> None:
    # ... other operations ...

    with op.batch_alter_table('transaction', schema=None) as batch_op:
        batch_op.drop_constraint('check_quantity_positive', type_='check')

The dev.py db upgrade command includes a post-flight check that will warn you if CHECK constraints are missing after a migration, guiding you to fix the issue.

docs.title: 📈 Asset Plugin Guide
docs.text:
How to create a new Asset Source Provider to fetch prices from a new data source.

Base class: AssetSourceProvider (defined in backend/app/services/assets/base.py) Plugin folder: backend/app/services/asset_source_providers/<name>/ — the code in plugin.py, beside an __init__.py holding only its docstring (see Plugin Folder and Translations) Registry: AssetProviderRegistry

Import from the defining module

Import AssetSourceProvider and AssetSourceError from backend.app.services.assets.base; the thread runner and shared caches live in backend.app.services.assets.core. No facade re-exports them: the backend/app/services/assets/ package __init__.py holds only a docstring.

docs.title: 🤖 Tip: Let an LLM scaffold the provider
docs.text:
Paste this entire page into an LLM with the data source's API documentation and use this prompt:

Suggested prompt

Here is the LibreFolio Asset Source Provider specification: [paste this page]

I want to add a provider for [DATA_SOURCE_NAME]. Their API works like this:
[brief description, or paste their API docs]

Write a complete Python AssetSourceProvider implementation. Follow all conventions:
@register_provider, FACurrentValue, FAHistoricalData, FAPricePoint, direct calls to
synchronous provider clients (never an internal asyncio.to_thread), test_cases, and
test_search_query if applicable. An API key or any other secret is a plugin setting
(settings_fields, read with self.settings in the operations, never in __init__), never a
provider_params field, and never in get_asset_url(), in cooldown_scope() or in a request
whose host comes from the identifier or the provider_params. LibreFolio's service layer
supplies thread isolation. On "too many requests" (HTTP 429), raise AssetRateLimitedError
(raise_if_rate_limited as the first line of the except) and never retry or sleep: the core
pauses the provider.

After scaffolding, implement get_current_value() and get_history_value(), add test cases, then save it as asset_source_providers/<name>/plugin.py, beside an __init__.py holding only a docstring, and restart.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
The system calls provider methods in three distinct phases:

graph TD
    subgraph P1["Phase 1 — Search"]
        S1["🔎 search(query)"]
        S2["list of<br/>{identifier, name,<br/>currency, type}"]
        S1 --> S2
    end

    subgraph P2["Phase 2 — Current Price"]
        C1["💰 get_current_value(<br/>identifier, type, params)"]
        C2["FACurrentValue<br/>(price, currency, date)"]
        C1 --> C2
    end

    subgraph P3["Phase 3 — Historical Data"]
        H1["📈 get_history_value(<br/>identifier, ..., start, end)"]
        H2["FAHistoricalData<br/>(prices[], currency)"]
        H3["🔧 Core fills gaps<br/>(weekends, holidays)"]
        H1 --> H2 --> H3
    end

    P1 ~~~ P2 ~~~ P3

    style S1 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style S2 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style C1 fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2e7d32
    style C2 fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2e7d32
    style H1 fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#e65100
    style H2 fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#e65100
    style H3 fill:#f3e5f5,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#7b1fa2

Phase 1 is optional but strongly recommended — enables users to discover and link assets without knowing the exact identifier. See Asset Search below.

Phase 2 fetches the latest price for the dashboard or manual refresh.

Phase 3 fetches historical OHLCV data. The plugin returns only actual trading days — core fills gaps (weekends, holidays) with last known value.

Plugin responsibility: Fetch raw price data from external source. Return only actual data points (trading days). Core responsibility: Gap filling (weekends/holidays → backward_filled=True), caching, database storage, currency conversion.

docs.title: 🧵 Provider Execution Boundary
docs.text:
Provider contracts are asynchronous, but the service layer treats provider implementations as an isolation boundary. Every provider I/O operation is invoked through the canonical assets.core._run_provider_in_thread() helper. The helper starts a dedicated worker thread, creates a new event loop in that thread, runs the provider coroutine to completion, and enforces the caller's timeout. Service code reaches it through assets.core.call_provider(), the one boundary of every provider call, on an instance from configured_provider(): the boundary first checks the provider's settings and whether it is paused after «too many requests» (Too Many Requests), then keeps its secrets masked while the call runs, and hides an error's texts whole when the call carries a personal secret (Secrets).

Consequently, a provider that wraps a synchronous SDK or HTTP client should call that client directly inside its async def method:

async def get_current_value(self, identifier, identifier_type, provider_params):
    raw = self._sync_client.fetch(identifier)  # Direct blocking call in provider thread
    return FACurrentValue(...)

Do not add asyncio.to_thread() or run_in_executor() inside the provider. Nesting another thread boundary obscures timeout/error behavior and is unnecessary: the manager operations, metadata refresh, current/history refresh, search, and URL resolution already route provider I/O through _run_provider_in_thread(). Async-native provider clients also work because their coroutines run on the dedicated thread's event loop.

This rule applies to provider I/O only. Ordinary endpoints and service functions still must not perform blocking I/O directly on the application's main event loop.

docs.title: ✅ Required (Abstract)
docs.text: Method Signature Description provider_code @property → str Unique identifier (e.g., "yfinance") provider_name @property → str Display name (e.g., "Yahoo Finance") test_cases @property → list[dict] Test cases for automated testing (identifier, identifier_type, provider_params) test_search_query @property → str \| None Search query for automated tests. None if search not supported. get_current_value(identifier, type, params) async → FACurrentValue Fetch latest price. Returns value, currency, as_of_date, source. When the quote carries a timestamp, as_of_date is its date in the exchange's timezone, not in UTC. get_history_value(identifier, type, params, start, end) async → FAHistoricalData Fetch historical OHLCV data for date range. Return raw data only — no gap filling. Date each point and event on its session's day in the exchange's timezone, not on the UTC date of a midnight timestamp: the refresh stores the dates as given (Dates on the Exchange's Own Day). Build each point as the source gives it: FAPricePoint checks no sign, and the refresh discards a day with a close of 0 or less, or a negative open, high, low or volume, and names it in its result (Discarded Days, N92). validate_params(params) → None Validate provider-specific provider_params. Raise AssetSourceError if invalid. Use pass if no params needed.

docs.title: 💪 Strongly Recommended (Override)
docs.text:
Implementing search() is strongly recommended

Without search, users must know the exact asset identifier (ticker, ISIN, URL) upfront. With search, they can type a name like "Apple" and pick from results.

Method Default Description search(query) Raises NOT_SUPPORTED Search for assets by name, ticker, or ISIN. Returns [{identifier, identifier_type, display_name, currency, type}]; a result may add quote_base_suggestion (Quote Base Suggestion).

docs.title: 🔧 Optional (Override)
docs.text: Method Default Description get_icon None Provider icon URL for the UI supports_history True Set False for providers that only support current prices (e.g., web scrapers) params_schema [] List of field definitions for provider_params. Used by frontend to generate dynamic forms. Each field has a key, a type (string, number, currency, select with options / option_labels, or ui_component for a custom editor), required (shown with a red *), and optionally default, placeholder, a short label (the caption) and a description (the tooltip). The caption is the translation assets.providerParams.<code>.label.<key>, else label, else the raw key — declare a label so users do not see internal names; the tooltip is assets.providerParams.<code>.description.<key>, else description. Both translations live in the provider's own fragment: see Plugin Folder and Translations. The parameters belong to one asset and are stored in clear with it: never a secret there, see Settings. get_asset_url(identifier, type, params) None Generate URL to the provider's page for this asset (e.g., Yahoo Finance quote page). Shown to the user: never a secret in it, see Secrets resolvable_url_domains [] Domains this provider can turn a page URL back into a search-item for (opt-in). See Asset Search & Link-Finder. resolve_url(url) None Inverse of get_asset_url: open a provider page URL → return one search-item dict, a list of dicts, or None. Enables the last-resort external search stack. accepted_identifier_types [TICKER, ISIN] Input types accepted by this provider (shown in frontend dropdown) fetch_asset_metadata(identifier, type, params) None Fetch asset metadata (type, sector, identifiers) from the provider suggest_quote_base(identifier, type, params) None How many units one price refers to (the asset's quote_base_quantity), as an FAQuoteBaseSuggestion, when the source's own data says it: Yahoo Finance suggests 100 for a line it quotes in pence. Asked by the probe's metadata operation only: see Quote Base Suggestion cooldown_scope(identifier, type, params) None The part of the provider a pause after «too many requests» covers, such as a site's host; None pauses the whole provider. Called before every call, so no I/O, and never a secret in the result: see Too Many Requests provider_help_url None URL to the provider's documentation page (served by the running instance) settings_fields () The values the provider needs from the instance or from each user: an API key, a region, a preference. Read with self.settings in the operations, never in __init__: see Settings test_only False True for a provider that exists for the tests: hidden from the provider list and from the settings catalogue and, outside test mode, not served at all (Test-Only Plugins) tier FAProviderTier.COMMUNITY Where the provider stands in the asset search: PREMIUM for a source the instance vouches for, such as licensed data; when at least one premium provider is available, its results come first. A class attribute; a valid string ("premium") is accepted. See Search Order search_priority 100 The provider's place in the search inside its tier, lower first: a whole number of at least 0. A class attribute; a wrong value stops the import shutdown() no-op Called at app teardown to clean up resources (close sessions, stop threads). Override if your provider holds persistent connections. generate_static_url(path) — Helper to build /api/v1/uploads/plugin/asset/{path}

docs.title: 🔎 Asset Search
docs.text: The search(query) method allows users to discover assets by name, ticker, or ISIN across several providers simultaneously.

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
1. User types a query in the UI (e.g., "Apple", "MSCI World", "IE00B4L5Y983")
  2. Frontend calls the streaming endpoint GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search/stream?q=Apple&providers=… with the providers selected in the dialog; the batch GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search only as a fallback when the stream is unavailable
  3. Backend queries the requested providers in parallel via AssetSearchService.search_stream() (batch: AssetSearchService.search(), asyncio.gather); without providers (a direct API call), every registered provider but the test-only ones (_default_search_codes())
  4. Providers that don't implement search (default raises NOT_SUPPORTED) are silently skipped
  5. Results are aggregated and returned to the user, provider by provider, in the search order

docs.title: 🥇 Search Order
docs.text:
services/assets/provider_policy.py decides the order, from what each provider declares and what the instance overrides:

  • The tier (tier): premium providers come first, but only when at least one is available. No shipped provider is premium today, so without one the order stays what it was.
  • The priority (search_priority): inside a tier, lower first; ties keep the registry's order.
  • The instance's overrides, read at every call (config/plugins.py): LIBREFOLIO_ASSET_PROVIDERS_PREMIUM makes exactly the listed providers premium; LIBREFOLIO_ASSET_PROVIDERS_ORDER puts the listed providers first, in its order. A code that no provider has is ignored and logged once.

GET /assets/provider shows each provider's effective tier and priority. The non-streaming search (GET /assets/provider/search) returns the results in this order; the streaming one sends them as they arrive, and the frontend orders them the same way as they land (frontend/src/lib/components/assets/assetSearchSections.ts, from the tier and priority of that list): premium first, then lower priority, with a stable sort, so with every provider at its defaults the list keeps the order of arrival. Only when a premium provider took part in the search does the dropdown split it into a Premium section and a closed community section; otherwise it is one list.

docs.title: 🔌 Provider Support
docs.text:
Provider search() test_search_query get_asset_url Notes Yahoo Finance ✅ "Apple" ✅ Full ticker search with the core query cache (15 min TTL) JustETF ✅ "iShares Core S&P 500" ✅ ISIN-based search across cached ETF list; a row per currency, or only the user's preferred_currency (Shipped Plugins) CSS Scraper ❌ None ✅ No search — URL must be provided manually Scheduled Investment ❌ None — Synthetic provider, no external search Borsa Italiana ✅ "ENEL" ✅ Full search on borsaitaliana.it; funds price by provider_params.codice_fondo; search and resolve_url emit IT + EN rows, or only the user's preferred_language

supports_search detection

The list_providers endpoint checks instance.test_search_query is not None (a local property) to determine search support. This avoids cold-start HTTP calls.

docs.title: 🧵 Last-resort external fallback (optional)
docs.text:
A provider can go beyond its own on-site search. When search() returns 0 results, the orchestration can fall back to an external engine (web_link_finder, ddgs by default) to find candidate provider-domain URLs and then resolve them back into search-items. To opt in, a provider sets resolvable_url_domains and implements resolve_url(url) (see the Optional overrides list). The caller may also pass hints (extra identifiers/names, e.g. from a broker report) to narrow the external query and post-filter the results by known identifier.

resolve_url is an alternate entry point into interactive search, not into pricing. It may return:

  • one search-item dict;
  • a list of search-item dicts when one page maps to several canonical choices;
  • None when the URL is not recognised.

The search layer flattens lists and de-duplicates by (identifier, language). Borsa Italiana uses this to return the IT + EN canonical set for a fund or scheda page, or only the row of the user's preferred language.

This whole stack — the web_link_finder module, the two-stage "stringone", and the identifier post-filter — is documented on its own page:

  • 🔎 Asset Search & Link-Finder — the generic three-layer resolution (on-site → link-finder → resolve_url), config, and invariants.

Never on price fetches

The external stack is interactive-only. Once an asset exists it must be priced by its stored identifier / provider_params, never by re-searching. For Borsa Italiana funds, the stored provider_params.codice_fondo is the price key; the ISIN is descriptive/identity data, not the NAV lookup key.

docs.title: 🧾 Alternative identifiers
docs.text: Asset.identifier_other is a JSON list (list[str]) of soft or technical identifiers. Use it for alternate broker labels and provider-specific codes that do not deserve a first-class identifier column. Provider metadata patches should return a list, not a scalar; for example, Borsa Italiana fund metadata stores the internal fund code as identifier_other=["2FADB…"] while pricing uses provider_params.codice_fondo.

docs.title: 🌐 API Endpoints
docs.text:
Standard search (returns all results at once):

GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search?q=Apple&providers=yfinance,justetf

Streaming search (Server-Sent Events — results arrive as providers respond):

GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search/stream?q=Apple&providers=yfinance,justetf

Query parameters (both endpoints):

  • q (required): Search query, min 1 character
  • providers (optional): Comma-separated provider codes. Default: all providers with search support.

Response (standard):

{
  "query": "Apple",
  "total_results": 5,
  "results": [
    {
      "identifier": "AAPL",
      "display_name": "Apple Inc.",
      "provider_code": "yfinance",
      "currency": "USD",
      "asset_type": "stock",
      "provider_url": "https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL"
    }
  ],
  "providers_queried": ["yfinance", "justetf"],
  "providers_with_errors": [],
  "providers_not_configured": []
}
  • Searches are executed in parallel — one slow provider won't block others
  • Provider-specific errors are logged but don't fail the entire request
  • Errors are reported in providers_with_errors for debugging
  • A provider that is not configured, a required setting without a value, is not called: the standard search lists it in providers_with_errors and in providers_not_configured, and the stream's provider_error event carries error_code: "NOT_CONFIGURED"; the search box then offers Configure for it (NOT_CONFIGURED)
  • A provider paused after «too many requests» is not called: the standard search lists it in providers_with_errors, and the stream's provider_error event adds error_code: "RATE_LIMITED" and retry_after (see Too Many Requests)
  • The stream's provider_error carries an error_code for every AssetSourceError, the provider's own codes included (SEARCH_ERROR, for example); an error of any other type has none
  • provider_url is generated by the provider's get_asset_url() method (if implemented)
  • quote_base_suggestion is the plugin's quote base suggestion for the line, null when it gives none; each result of the stream's provider_results event carries it too

docs.title: 🧪 Probe Endpoint
docs.text:
After a provider is configured, use the probe endpoint to dry-run test it:

POST /api/v1/assets/provider/probe

This runs selectable operations (current_price, history, metadata) without persisting anything. See Asset Architecture for details.

docs.title: 🔢 Quote Base Suggestion
docs.text:
An asset's quote_base_quantity (Units per single price in the asset form) says how many units one market price refers to: the holding value is quantity / quote_base_quantity × price (compute_holding_value() in backend/app/services/financial_math/valuation.py). It is 1 for most lines. A line quoted in a minor unit needs more: Yahoo Finance reports a London line quoted in pence with the currency GBp, and LibreFolio stores the code as GBP with the numbers unchanged, so the asset needs a quote base of 100, or every price counts 100 times.

A plugin whose source says so can suggest the quote base, as an FAQuoteBaseSuggestion (backend/app/schemas/provider.py), a StrictModel, so an unknown key is refused:

Field Type Meaning quantity int, required, at least 1 The units one price refers to: 100 for a line quoted in pence. 1, «per unit», is a valid suggestion too quote_currency str \| None The quote currency as the source reports it, not normalized (GBp stays GBp): why the quantity is suggested

It can give one in two places, both optional:

  • In a search result: add the key quote_base_suggestion to the search-item dict, as a dict ({"quantity": 100, "quote_currency": "GBp"}) or as an FAQuoteBaseSuggestion. AssetSearchService validates it into FAProviderSearchResultItem.quote_base_suggestion, in the standard search and in the stream. One that does not validate is dropped with a warning in the log, Search result: quote_base_suggestion dropped, naming the provider and the identifier; the result itself stays. Without the key, the field is null.
  • suggest_quote_base(identifier, identifier_type, provider_params=None): an async method beside fetch_asset_metadata(), returning an FAQuoteBaseSuggestion or None. The base class returns None without any I/O.

Suggest only what your own data says. Return a suggestion when the source itself tells the unit, as Yahoo Finance's GBp does, and None otherwise. MINOR_UNIT_FACTORS (backend/app/utils/currency_units.py) lists the minor units a provider may report, exactly as reported, with their factor: only GBp, 100, today. minor_unit_factor(currency) gives the factor of a reported code, or None; Yahoo Finance builds its suggestion from it.

When the core asks suggest_quote_base():

  • Only in the probe's metadata operation (POST /api/v1/assets/provider/probe), with the arguments of fetch_asset_metadata(), once that call has answered, with a patch or None. The answer is ProbeMetadataResult.quote_base_suggestion, beside patch_data and never inside it; its time counts in the operation's execution_time_ms.
  • After the metadata, never in parallel: through call_provider(), in your provider's thread and under the metadata's cooldown scope, with a timeout of its own, 5 s. When a pause after «too many requests» ends, call_provider() lets one trial call through (Provider Pauses), and that call goes to the metadata.
  • Not at all when the metadata call failed (an error, a refusal, a timeout), or when your class keeps the base class's method.
  • Best-effort: an error, a refusal, a timeout or an answer that does not validate gives null, logged at info level (Probe: no quote base suggestion); the metadata result stays as it was.
  • Nowhere else: not in the metadata request (POST /api/v1/assets/provider/probe, the "Ask the provider" flow), nor in the price refresh. The core only returns a suggestion: it never writes one on an asset. Keep it that way, and never set quote_base_quantity in the FAAssetPatchItem your fetch_asset_metadata() returns: the metadata refresh writes that patch on stored assets without asking.

The web app's asset form reads both: a picked search result writes its suggestion into Units per single price, as it writes the name, and the metadata probe's becomes a ticked row of the Provider Data Comparison dialog when it differs from the field; without a suggestion the form proposes the type's default (100 for a BOND, 1 otherwise), and a probe of the same line whose suggestion came back null reuses the last one the form received for that line (R1). The suggestion reaches the form only by the user's hand (a pick, Apply Selected), and the asset only when it is saved: see Asset Identity.

Testing. The test-only mockprov answers the search query lf-minor-unit (MINOR_UNIT_QUERY) with one GBp STOCK, MOCK_MINOR_UNIT (MINOR_UNIT_IDENTIFIER), carrying {"quantity": 100, "quote_currency": "GBp"}; its suggest_quote_base() gives the same for that identifier and None for any other. ./dev.py test services quote-base-suggestion pins the contract without a server, and ./dev.py test api assets-provider its HTTP side.

docs.title: 💻 Implementation Example
docs.text:
# backend/app/services/asset_source_providers/my_provider/plugin.py

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal
from backend.app.db import IdentifierType
from backend.app.db.models import ProviderInputType
from backend.app.services.assets.base import AssetSourceError, AssetSourceProvider
from backend.app.services.assets.registry import AssetProviderRegistry
from backend.app.services.provider_registry import register_provider
from backend.app.schemas.prices import FACurrentValue, FAHistoricalData, FAPricePoint

@register_provider(AssetProviderRegistry)
class MyProvider(AssetSourceProvider):

    @property
    def provider_code(self) -> str:
        return "my_provider"

    @property
    def provider_name(self) -> str:
        return "My Data Provider"

    @property
    def test_cases(self) -> list[dict]:
        return [
            {"identifier": "AAPL", "identifier_type": IdentifierType.TICKER, "provider_params": None}
        ]

    @property
    def test_search_query(self) -> str | None:
        return "Apple"  # Return None if search not supported

    @property
    def params_schema(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Optional: define fields for frontend dynamic form."""
        # Per-asset parameters, stored in clear with the asset: never a secret here.
        # An API key is a plugin setting (settings_fields): see Settings below.
        return [
            {"key": "exchange", "type": "string", "required": False, "label": "Exchange", "description": "Exchange to price the asset on"},
        ]

    def get_asset_url(self, identifier, identifier_type, provider_params=None) -> str | None:
        """Optional: URL to the provider's page for this asset."""
        return f"https://myprovider.com/asset/{identifier}"

    async def get_current_value(
        self, identifier: str, identifier_type: IdentifierType, provider_params: dict
    ) -> FACurrentValue:
        # A synchronous client call stays direct; the service runs this coroutine
        # in the dedicated provider thread.
        price = self._sync_client.fetch_price(identifier)
        return FACurrentValue(
            value=Decimal(str(price)),
            currency="USD",
            as_of_date=date.today(),
            source=self.provider_name,
        )

    async def get_history_value(
        self, identifier: str, identifier_type: IdentifierType,
        provider_params: dict | None, start_date: date, end_date: date
    ) -> FAHistoricalData:
        # Return ONLY actual trading days; do not add an internal to_thread call.
        raw_data = self._sync_client.fetch_history(identifier, start_date, end_date)
        prices = [
            FAPricePoint(date=d, close=Decimal(str(p)), open=None, high=None, low=None, volume=None, currency="USD")
            for d, p in raw_data
        ]
        return FAHistoricalData(prices=prices, currency="USD", source=self.provider_name)

    def validate_params(self, params: dict | None) -> None:
        # No params required — accept anything
        pass

docs.title: 🗂️ Plugin Folder and Translations
docs.text:
A provider is a folder of asset_source_providers/:

backend/app/services/asset_source_providers/
├── static/            ← the family's icons, served under /api/v1/uploads/plugin/asset/… (generate_static_url)
└── my_provider/
    ├── __init__.py    ← its docstring and nothing else
    ├── plugin.py      ← the code above
    └── i18n/          ← optional: en.json, it.json, fr.json, es.json

Restart the app: AssetProviderRegistry loads plugin.py as backend.app.services.asset_source_providers.my_provider.plugin. Import and patch the provider's names from that module: the package re-exports nothing. A helper only this provider uses sits beside plugin.py as _*.py. Discovery, the layout and the gate that keeps it (./dev.py test utils gate-plugin-layout) are in Plugin Folder Layout.

Translations. A provider has two spaces, both keyed by the code provider_code returns, which need not be the folder's name — the yahoo_finance/ folder registers yfinance:

  • assets.providerParams.<provider_code>: the captions and tooltips of its params_schema fields, label.<key> and description.<key>;
  • pluginSettings.asset.<provider_code>: the texts of its settings, label.<field>, description.<field> and option.<field>.<value>, the keys its settings_fields declare (Labels and Translations).

Borsa Italiana's fragment (borsa_italiana/i18n/) holds both; justETF's (justetf/i18n/) holds its setting's texts only. Add the keys in the four languages, naming the folder with --into:

./dev.py i18n add "assets.providerParams.my_provider.label.exchange" --en "Exchange" --it "Borsa" --fr "Place de cotation" --es "Bolsa" --into asset_source_providers/my_provider
./dev.py i18n add "assets.providerParams.my_provider.description.exchange" --en "Exchange to price the asset on" --it "…" --fr "…" --es "…" --into asset_source_providers/my_provider
./dev.py i18n where "assets.providerParams.my_provider.label.exchange"   # the file that holds the key

Without --into, add refuses a new provider's first key, because the keys under assets.providerParams and pluginSettings.asset belong to plugins only; it also refuses every new key of a provider whose keys lie under both branches, as Borsa Italiana's do. ./dev.py test utils gate-plugin-i18n-ownership then keeps every key under the provider's spaces in its fragment (A Plugin's Translations).

docs.title: 🎛️ Settings
docs.text:
A provider that needs an API key, a region or a user's preference declares it in settings_fields. The core resolves the values (environment variable, saved value, default), decrypts the secret ones and binds them to a new instance before each use; the provider reads them in its operations with self.settings.get("key") and self.settings.secret("key"):

from backend.app.services.plugin_settings.fields import PluginSettingField, SettingScope, SettingType


class MyProvider(AssetSourceProvider):
    settings_fields = (
        PluginSettingField(key="api_key", type=SettingType.STRING, scope=SettingScope.SYSTEM, secret=True, required=True, label="API key"),
    )

    async def get_current_value(self, identifier, identifier_type, provider_params=None) -> FACurrentValue:
        api_key = self.settings.secret("api_key")  # never in __init__
        ...
  • Never read settings in __init__. The core binds them after the instance is created, so __init__ sees only the declared defaults and no secret. The same holds for the members the core may call on an instance it did not configure: properties, params_schema, get_asset_url(), validate_params().
  • Scopes. A system field holds one value for the instance, saved by an administrator or set by LIBREFOLIO_PLUGIN_ASSET_<CODE>_<FIELD>; a secret one may also keep, in env, the variable the provider read its key from before it declared settings. A user field holds each user's own value, which reaches only search(), resolve_url() and the probe: prices, history and metadata get the instance's values only. Either kind can be secret.
  • A secret is a setting, never a provider parameter: provider_params are stored in clear with the asset, shared by its users and returned by the asset API.
  • A required field without a value makes call_provider() answer NOT_CONFIGURED before any I/O. Never return a secret, log it, or put it in a URL you log or in an exception message: masking is only a safety net.
  • Texts. Declare label_key and description_key on each field, and label_key on the options that need a translation, under pluginSettings.asset.<provider_code>; the texts go in your fragment (Translations). The English label stays the fallback.
  • Where users set them. Settings › Plugins lists every provider that declares a field the user may see, and the asset dialog shows Configure next to the provider; while the provider is not configured, the asset dialog shows To configure and a search offers Configure on a row of its own (The Interface).

docs.title: 🔐 Secrets Stay Out of the Caller's Reach
docs.text:
Any signed-in user can probe a provider with an identifier and parameters of their choosing (POST /api/v1/assets/provider/probe, Test Configuration), on an instance that carries the instance's secrets. So:

  • Never put a secret in get_asset_url(): the URL is shown to the user, as the Provider URL of the asset dialog. As a last line of defence, the probe withholds a URL that shows one of the provider's secrets (core.public_asset_url()): it answers provider_url: null, and the log has a warning naming the provider, Provider asset URL withheld: it shows a secret.
  • Never put a secret in cooldown_scope(): the core asks it before the call, outside the masking, and the scope keys the pause registry and appears in its log lines.
  • Never send a secret in a request whose host comes from the identifier or the provider_params: the caller would choose the host, and receive the secret. No masking reaches a request that has left. Send it only to the hosts your provider knows.

A caller's own secret hides the call's errors whole. When a call carries a user secret, a value its caller chose (self.settings.carries_user_secrets), call_provider() turns every text of the error that shows a secret, the caller's or the instance's, into *** entirely, instead of masking each occurrence in place: masked in place, the text would tell whether a chosen value occurs next to an instance secret, and so read it a guess at a time. The error's type and error_code stay, and so does every details item that shows no secret: put what explains a failure there. The log lines keep the precise masking, and so does a call that carries only instance secrets. In both cases, every occurrence of a secret is found at once, and occurrences that overlap or touch become a single *** (Secrets).

The full contract (types, environment variables, secrets, caching, the API and the security model) is in Plugin Settings.

docs.title: 🚦 Too Many Requests
docs.text:
When a source refuses for too many requests (an HTTP 429, or a library's own error for it), the core pauses the provider: call_provider() stops calling it for a while and answers every caller at once with AssetRateLimitedError (error_code="RATE_LIMITED", retry_after in seconds), without a thread or any I/O. By default the pause starts at 60 s and doubles at each refusal in a row, up to 1 h, plus up to 10 % of jitter; a Retry-After the source sent is honoured, up to 24 h. A cached value is still served meanwhile. What each caller returns during a pause is in Asset Architecture → Provider Pauses.

The plugin's part is only to report the refusal:

  • Raise AssetRateLimitedError (backend/app/services/assets/base.py), with the source's Retry-After in seconds as retry_after when it sent one. It is an AssetSourceError, so an except AssetSourceError: raise clause lets it through.
  • Never retry or sleep in your thread after a refusal. A retry is one more request to a source that has just refused, and a sleep holds the provider's thread: the core decides how long to wait. Other transient errors (a timeout, a reset connection) may still be retried.
  • Never swallow a refusal in a handler that otherwise returns [] or None, such as a best-effort search() or fetch_asset_metadata(): the refusal would read as "no result", and the provider would never be paused. Yahoo Finance's search (with the currency lookup it makes for each result, Z-39) and metadata, justETF's metadata, and Borsa Italiana's metadata and resolve_url had to be fixed for this; the two Borsa Italiana enrichments that still swallow one, on purpose, are listed on its page.

docs.title: 🧰 Helpers
docs.text:
Helper (assets/base.py) Use rate_limited_from_response(response, provider_name, scope=None) An httpx or requests response: an AssetRateLimitedError when it is an HTTP 429, with its Retry-After; else None rate_limited_from_exception(error, provider_name, scope=None) A caught exception: an AssetRateLimitedError when it is one already, when its response is an HTTP 429 (requests.HTTPError, httpx.HTTPStatusError, with the Retry-After), or when its message says, in any case, «status 429», «status code 429», «HTTP 429», «HTTP Error 429» (urllib) or the reason phrase «Too Many Requests» (requests' «429 Client Error: Too Many Requests», httpx's «Client error '429 Too Many Requests'»), as libraries without an error class of their own do; else None. In a message, 429 counts only as a whole number, and a colon may precede it («status: 429») raise_if_rate_limited(error, provider_name, scope=None) The first line of an except: raises the refusal (from error) and lets every other error go on to the plugin's own handling

A library with an error class of its own is translated in the plugin, as Yahoo Finance does with yfinance's YFRateLimitError and Borsa Italiana with the library's RateLimitRaggiunto: raise AssetRateLimitedError("…") from error. Mind what the library does before it raises: Borsa Italiana's library retries a 429 by itself and sleeps in the provider's thread, a known gap (Borsa Italiana Provider).

docs.title: 🎯 Narrowing a pause: cooldown_scope()
docs.text:
A refusal pauses the whole provider. A provider that reaches many independent sites overrides cooldown_scope(identifier, identifier_type, provider_params) and returns the part of itself a pause should cover. The CSS Scraper returns the host of the page URL (lowercase, without the port), so a site that refuses pauses itself and not the other sites.

  • The callers that have an identifier (live price, refresh, metadata refresh, probe) ask the hook before every call: it must do no I/O. A hook that raises is logged, and the pause then covers the whole provider.
  • The scope never holds a secret: it is computed outside the masking, keys the pause registry and appears in its log lines (Secrets).
  • Search and resolve_url have no identifier, so no scope: they check and record the provider-wide pause. That is a key of its own: a site's pause does not hold up a search, nor does a refused search pause the sites.
  • An error raised with scope= should carry the hook's value: the core checks a pause under the hook's scope, and records a refusal under the error's scope (the hook's when the error has none).

docs.title: 💡 Example
docs.text:
from backend.app.services.assets.base import AssetSourceError, raise_if_rate_limited


class MyProvider(AssetSourceProvider):
    async def get_current_value(self, identifier, identifier_type, provider_params):
        try:
            raw = self._sync_client.fetch(identifier)  # raises requests.HTTPError on a 4xx/5xx
        except Exception as error:
            raise_if_rate_limited(error, self.provider_name)  # a 429 leaves as RATE_LIMITED: no retry, no sleep
            raise AssetSourceError(f"Quote failed for {identifier}: {error}", "FETCH_ERROR") from error
        ...

    async def fetch_asset_metadata(self, identifier, identifier_type, provider_params=None):
        try:
            info = self._sync_client.fetch_info(identifier)
        except Exception as error:
            raise_if_rate_limited(error, self.provider_name)  # a refusal is not "no metadata"
            return None
        ...

docs.title: 🧪 Testing a refusal
docs.text:
The test-only mockprov refuses for too many requests on demand:

  • an asset whose provider_params hold mock_rate_limited — a number of seconds, sent as the Retry-After, or true for none — is refused by get_current_value(), get_history_value() and fetch_asset_metadata();
  • the search query lf-rate-limited is refused, with a Retry-After of 30 s.

The pause that follows is real and holds for the whole process. Use these modes in in-process tests only, where the test replaces PROVIDER_COOLDOWNS (backend/app/services/platform/provider_cooldown.py) with a fresh Cooldowns, so no pause outlives it; never on a lane's shared test backend, where the pause would outlive the test.
