It runs after the answer, as a background task with a session of its own, and never raises. update_profile (PUT /api/v1/auth/profile, backend/app/api/v1/auth.py) queues it on the request's engine (session.bind) after a change of address — an email that differs from the stored one, compared exactly, saved with the current password — with the address read before the change. A username-only change, or a refused one, queues nothing. In this order:

  1. The old and the new address the same, as workstream A's user_service.same_email() compares them (A–Z in any case, nothing else folded, decision P18): nothing, not even a log line. A's route already queues the notice only for a real change, so this is a second guard.
  2. Email off — no host set, the default of a self-hosted instance — gives the info event Email change notice: email is off, nothing sent, never a warning. The configuration is read in a worker thread.
  3. An account that no longer exists: the info event Email change notice: the account no longer exists, nothing sent.
  4. Email usable now (require_email()): set but unusable, or the instance blocked, ends with the warning event Email change notice: not sent.
  5. The limits, peeked: EMAIL_CHANGE_NOTICES_BY_ACCOUNT (3 an hour, by user_id) and EMAIL_CHANGE_NOTICES_BY_MAILBOX (3 an hour, by the old address through mailbox_budget_key()). Past either, the info event Email change notice: past its limits, nothing sent: nothing is composed, nothing is spent.
  6. build_email_changed() in the account's language, with the instance's name alone — no username and nothing of the new address (No Stranger's Text) —, then send_email() to the old address and the Email change notice sent to the previous address event. Only then are both limits hit, so an email that did not go counts for neither. The email spends a unit of the hourly budget like any other; past it, or when the server does not take the message, the warning event says why.

The email carries no link, so it does not need LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL: the variable, when usable, only names the instance (LinksState.instance), and INSTANCE_FALLBACK, «LibreFolio», does otherwise. Its own events hold neither address; Email sent gives the domain of the old one, as for any email (What Is Logged).

Three decisions of the night of 15/10, to be reviewed, the first since replaced:

  • (a) The new address: first shown masked, ***@domain; since night decision N62 (17/10), not shown at all, nor the username (No Stranger's Text).
  • (b) The instance's name: the host of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, else «LibreFolio», never the host of a request, which whoever sends the request writes.
  • (c) The old address only: the new address gets no email.

And one from the security review of lot E4b (16/10), to be reviewed:

  • (d) The limits. Without them an account could point its email at any address, change it again, and so have the instance write to that address as often as the hourly budget allows. Per account they bound what one account sends; per mailbox they bound what one address receives, its aliases included. The cost: whoever sends 3 notices to a mailbox in the hour silences the fourth, but to do so they write to that mailbox three times, and taking an account over still needs its password.

docs.title: ✅ Email Verification (verification.py)
docs.text:
With the global setting require_email_verification on, an account created by signing up cannot sign in until its owner confirms the address from the link of a verification email (developer decision 44). backend/app/services/email/verification.py holds the email side of the feature — the wait, the emailed link, its confirmation, «send the link again» — and its module docstring is the contract. Every link comes from email_link(), so from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL alone (developer decision 45).

The hooks in workstream A's files, written by workstream E:

  • Registration: register_user() calls hold_for_verification() once the account, and the invitation it spends, are written (imported inside the function: email imports the accounts services). Its RegistrationError rolls the whole registration back, the invitation included, and POST /auth/register answers it with 409 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE (_REGISTRATION_REFUSALS). Otherwise the answer carries verification_required (AuthRegisterResponse, false by default) and, since lot E-26, verification_email (Literal["sending", "held"] | None, null by default): the state of the sending of the email, never an address. It is null while verification_required is false (the option off, or the instance's first account). When verification_required is true, the User registered event has waits_for_email, and before it queues the email the route asks registration_email_verdict() with rate_limit_address(http_request) (workstream H's, Which client address: None for a request through a reverse proxy LibreFolio does not trust, on a local address, which is counted under no address and so never held). Allowed: the route queues registration_email_work() on the request's engine (session.bind), and the answer says "sending", which means queued, not delivered: the work runs after the answer, and what then stops the email (the recipient mailbox's limit, VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX; the hourly budget; an SMTP failure; links no longer available) is only logged, as Verification email: not sent, so the answer cannot tell it. The mailbox limit is deliberately not read before answering: an answer that varied with it would tell anyone who registers with another person's address whether that mailbox just received emails. Past LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS emails an hour (20 by default) from the same client address (the one count of registrations, «send the link again» and «forgot password»), or with the hourly budget of the instance spent, the account is created and waits all the same (201, verification_required: true), but no email is queued: the answer says "held" with verification_retry_after_seconds (int | None: the longest wait of the counters that held it, rounded up, at least 1; null unless "held"), the route logs Verification email held: address limit or instance budget reached, and the owner asks for the link again from the sign-in, under the limits of «send the link again» (a night decision of 16/10, to be reviewed; the owner learns of it from the sign-in's message since lot E-26). The English message changes only in its middle piece: «Registration successful», «Registration successful: check your email to activate the account» ("sending") or «Registration successful: the activation email is held (too many registrations from this address); sign in to ask for a new link» ("held"), each followed by (Admin) for a superuser (EVH-018: an invited administrator held keeps it). The frontend reads the two fields, never the message.
  • The user limit: user_usage() also counts, once each, the inactive accounts holding a live verification token (_live_verifications(): not consumed, not revoked, not expired). Such an account already holds its place (holds_place()): PATCH /users/{id} reactivates it on a full instance without 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED, and user activate without the limit warning. Once its link has expired, it needs a free place like any deactivated account. GET /users gives each account its holds_place (place_holders(), one query for the list), and so does the answer of PATCH /users/{id}; UserRow keeps Reactivate usable on a full instance for an account that holds its place.
  • The Users list (lot E-7): GET /users gives each account its pending_verification (AdminUserRead.pending_verification, false by default): email_verification.waiting_ids(), one query for the list, the ids of the inactive accounts with a verification token neither consumed nor revoked, live or expired; the answer of PATCH /users/{id} gives it from awaiting_verification(), the criterion of the sign-in's 403. It tells a waiting account from a deactivated one, and is not holds_place: once the link expires the account still waits, but holds no place. An account deactivated while it waits has its links revoked, and stops waiting.
  • The login: with the right password, a waiting account gets 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED and the event Login refused: email not verified (user_id); an account an administrator deactivated still gets ACCOUNT_DISABLED.
  • Status changes: update_user_status() (the administrator API) revokes the account's verification tokens when it changes is_active; set_user_active() (user activate, user deactivate) whenever it runs. A PATCH with is_active: false on a waiting account, inactive already, ends the wait as user deactivate does: its links are revoked, its place is free, and the answer says holds_place: false; on an inactive account that does not wait, it still changes nothing. The Users tab offers no Deactivate for an inactive account: there, an administrator turns a waiting account away with Delete.
  • The option: update_global_settings() checks an off-to-on change of require_email_verification with ensure_verification_can_be_enabled() (_refuse_what_cannot_turn_on()). A refusal is GlobalSettingUnavailableError, which PATCH /api/v1/settings/global/bulk answers with 409 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE and the key, saving none of the items. A save that sends the value already stored is not checked, so a bulk save keeps working while email is down.
  • The frontend: In the Frontend.

The coordinator's decisions:

  • Every account but the first verifies its address, the ones opened by an invitation included: hold_for_verification() skips only the instance's first account.
  • The safe side: with the option on and no email with a link possible (email off or not working, no usable LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, a blocked instance), registration is refused with 409, rather than creating an account that would wait for a link nobody can send.
  • A waiting account takes a place under LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS while its link is live (The User Limit). Once the link has expired the place is free again, and «send the link again» needs one.
  • «Send the link again» asks for the username (or the email address) and the password, checked as the sign-in checks them.
  • Turning the option off leaves the waiting accounts waiting: only hold_for_verification() reads the option, at registration, so their links and «send the link again» keep working.

docs.title: ⏳ The Wait and Its Tokens
docs.text:
An account waits when it is inactive and holds an email-verification token that is neither consumed nor revoked, live or expired (awaiting_verification()): the wait has no column of its own. Every change of status an administrator makes revokes those tokens (update_user_status(), set_user_active()), so a deactivated account never waits, and an old link never wakes it up. users.email_verified_at (migration 005, NULL for every account that existed before) records when a link was confirmed.

Token Created by email Role The hold hold_for_verification(), inside the registration's transaction NULL Marks the wait and, while live, holds the account's place. Its text never leaves the server: the function keeps nothing of it, and confirm_email() refuses a token without email, without revoking it An emailed link _issue_and_send(), after the registration's answer or for «send the link again» The account's address Replaces the account's other verification tokens, the hold included, and goes by email. It keeps the wait and, while live, the place. The per-account limits count these tokens alone. When its email does not go, it loses its address and stays as a hold (Emailing a Link)

Both last 24 hours, the default lifetime of the email_verification purpose, and the link is /verify-email#token=… (Single-use Account Tokens).

docs.title: 🧩 The Functions
docs.text:
Function What it does async verification_required(session) Whether the global setting require_email_verification is on (REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION of the settings registry, off by default) async links_can_go() Whether an email with a link can go out now: the instance not blocked (sending_blocked()), email usable (email_config_state(), read in a worker thread) and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL ready (links_state()) async ensure_verification_can_be_enabled() EmailVerificationUnavailableError (code EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE) unless links_can_go(): the guard of the option async awaiting_verification(session, user) Whether the account waits: inactive, with an unspent verification token async holds_place(session, user, *, now=None) Whether an inactive account already holds a place under LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS: it waits with a live link, which user_usage() counts. PATCH /users/{id} and user activate reactivate such an account without counting a new place, and the PATCH answer carries the flag async place_holders(session, *, now=None) The ids of every account holds_place() would say yes to, in one query: the holds_place of each account in GET /users async waiting_ids(session) The ids of every account awaiting_verification() would say yes to, in one query: inactive, with an unspent verification token, live or expired. The pending_verification of each account in GET /users (lot E-7); the PATCH answer asks awaiting_verification() for its one account async registration_email_verdict(address) Whether a registration from the client address may send its verification email now, as a RegistrationEmailVerdict (allowed, retry_after, by_address, by_instance). Two counters: the client address's, delivery.ADDRESS_BUDGET (LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS an hour, 20 by default, through workstream H's client_rate_key(), an IPv6 client by its /64; none for a request without an address), and the instance's hourly budget (LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR, peeked with budget_status(), only while email is usable). Both are peeked first; the address's hit is recorded only when both admit, so a refused registration spends nothing; when either refuses, retry_after is the longest wait of the counters that refuse. The limit is read from the environment at every call (address_budget_limit()) and passed to hit(key, limit=…), as send_email() does with INSTANCE_BUDGET: one thread-safe limiter per process, nothing read at import, and a test sets the variable instead of reloading a module. A value that cannot be used does not raise: the default applies, since email_config_state() has turned email off and reported it. POST /auth/register asks it before it queues registration_email_work(), and answers verification_retry_after_seconds with ceil(retry_after), at least 1 async hold_for_verification(session, user, *, first, now=None) Inside register_user()'s transaction, once the account is written. False for the instance's first account or with the option off. Otherwise, unless links_can_go(), it raises RegistrationError("EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE"), imported inside the function since registration_service is its caller; else the account becomes inactive and gets the hold (flushed, not committed), and it returns True async registration_email_work(user_id, *, engine=None, now=None) The verification email of a registration, after the answer, with a session of its own. Nothing goes when the account no longer waits (an administrator changed its status meanwhile). It never raises: a refusal or a failure is logged, the account keeps waiting, and «send the link again» works, at once after a failed email async confirm_email(session, token, *, now=None) Spends a link and returns the account: Confirming a Link async resend_verification(session, *, identifier, password, address, now=None) «Send the link again», returning the email's language: Sending the Link Again

Its refusals are EmailErrors, each with its code: EmailVerificationUnavailableError (EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE), EmailVerificationLinkInvalidError (the token's status), EmailVerificationNotNeededError (EMAIL_VERIFICATION_NOT_NEEDED), VerificationCredentialsError (INVALID_CREDENTIALS), VerificationAccountDisabledError (ACCOUNT_DISABLED) and VerificationUserLimitError (USER_LIMIT_REACHED).

docs.title: 📨 Emailing a Link
docs.text:
_issue_and_send() emails the account a new link, for registration_email_work() and resend_verification(), in this order:

  1. Email usable (require_email()), links ready (require_links()), the hourly budget peeked, then the recipient's mailbox (VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX, peeked on the address through mailbox_budget_key()): past either, EmailRateLimitedError with the wait. Nothing is created when the email cannot go.
  2. The account's verification tokens revoked, the hold included. That first write takes SQLite's write lock, so what follows sees every request that wrote before it. When it revokes nothing, the account no longer waits — its link was confirmed, or an administrator activated or deactivated it meanwhile — and a new link would make it wait again: the transaction rolls back, with EmailVerificationNotNeededError for an active account and VerificationAccountDisabledError for an inactive one, and nothing is sent. Otherwise a new token is issued that carries the account's address.
  3. The per-account limits counted again inside the write transaction, the new link included (_emailed_in_last_hour()): with more than 3 in the last hour, or more than one in the last 5 minutes, the transaction rolls back, the revocations with it, and it raises EmailRateLimitedError with a wait of 300 seconds. Of two requests that passed the first count together, the second stops here (SQLite writes one at a time).
  4. With needs_place — «send the link again» for an account whose link has expired, which holds no place — the user limit counted again in the same transaction, the new link included, as register_user() counts it: over the limit, the transaction rolls back with VerificationUserLimitError. Of two requests that saw the same last free place, the second sees the first one's link here.
  5. Only for «send the link again» (count_address, with the client address; registration_email_work() was counted at the registration): a unit of the address's counter (delivery.ADDRESS_BUDGET, address_budget_hit()). Refused — another request took the last unit since the first look — the transaction rolls back with EmailRateLimitedError. The unit stays spent if the email then fails. Then the commit, before the email.
  6. build_verification() in the account's language, with the link from email_link(), what is left of its lifetime (link_ttl()) and the instance's name (LinksState.instance), and no username (No Stranger's Text); then send_email() to the account's address, as stored. Once the email went out, a hit on VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX, and the Verification link emailed event.
  7. When anything after the commit raises (the language, the link, the message or send_email(), whatever the exception), the email did not go as far as LibreFolio knows: the token just committed loses its address (email set to NULL, committed) and the exception goes on to the caller.

The token stays as a hold, rather than being revoked as a forgotten password's link is: the account needs an unspent token to keep waiting, and keeps it, with its place while the token is live. The link cannot be confirmed, since confirm_email() refuses a token without email (without revoking it: Confirming a Link), and it counts neither against the per-account limits, which count only tokens with an address, nor against the mailbox, which counts only emails that went out: «send the link again» works at once. The same holds after a failed background email, which registration_email_work() logs. A registration's email refused by the mailbox's limit leaves the hold in place: the account waits, and its owner asks for the link again later (the answer has said sending by then: it could not know).

docs.title: 🔓 Confirming a Link
docs.text:
confirm_email() spends a link for POST /email/verification/confirm, in this order:

  1. The token inspected for the purpose email_verification (token_service.inspect_token()): any status but valid raises EmailVerificationLinkInvalidError, its code the status, expired, consumed, revoked or unknown. A token whose account no longer exists is unknown.
  2. A token without email — a hold, or a link whose email did not go out as far as LibreFolio knows — is refused with revoked but not revoked, and nothing is written: it may be the account's only unspent token, and revoking it would end the wait. The account keeps waiting and «send the link again» works. The Email verification refused: the link's email did not go out event is logged.
  3. A token emailed to an address the account no longer has (compared with user_service.same_email(), decision P18) is revoked and committed, the Email verification refused: the link was sent to another address event is logged, and the refusal is revoked.
  4. consume_token(): a link that another request spent meanwhile rolls back as consumed.
  5. The account active, email_verified_at set, its other verification tokens revoked; the commit, then the Email verified event.

Why a link whose email «did not go out» can be confirmed at all: when the connection is lost, or the 20 s timeout runs out, after the message was sent (DATA) but before the server's answer, deliver() reports a failure while the server may have queued the message. The email then arrives with a link that LibreFolio counts as never sent.

docs.title: 🔁 Sending the Link Again
docs.text:
resend_verification() is the sign-in's «send the link again», for POST /email/verification/resend, in this order:

  1. The per-address counter, only looked at (address_budget_peek()), before the password: a full one refuses at once with the longest wait of this counter and the instance's budget. A try costs it nothing, so wrong passwords (which have the sign-in's own limit) cannot use up the registrations or the forgotten passwords of a network. A request without a client address skips it.
  2. The account, looked up as the sign-in does (get_user_by_username_or_email()), and the password checked with workstream A's verify_password_or_dummy() in a worker thread: an unknown account costs a dummy hash, and both log Verification resend refused: wrong credentials, then raise VerificationCredentialsError.
  3. An active account raises EmailVerificationNotNeededError; an inactive one that does not wait, VerificationAccountDisabledError.
  4. Email usable (require_email()) and links ready (require_links()).
  5. The per-account limits, on the links already emailed: EmailRateLimitedError with the wait.
  6. Without a live link, the account's place went with its link: if the instance is full now (user_usage()), it raises VerificationUserLimitError, and emailing the link counts again inside its write (needs_place).
  7. Emailing a link; its step 5 spends the unit of the address's counter.

Since lot A8a, workstream A's limit on failed sign-ins sits between steps 1 and 2: when login_throttle.refusal(identifier, address) refuses, on the sign-in's own two counts, the request gets EmailRateLimitedError with that wait, before the password is checked. In step 2, a wrong password or an unknown account counts there (record_failure()), and the right password forgets the identifier's failures (record_success()) before step 3, whatever follows.

Limit Counted on Past it delivery.ADDRESS_BUDGET: LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS emails an hour, 20 by default, one count for the registrations, «send the link again» and «forgot password» The client address, workstream H's rate_limit_address(request), through its client_rate_key() (Which client address): an IPv6 client by its /64; no count behind a reverse proxy LibreFolio does not trust, on a local address. A resend only peeks it at the start (the sign-in's own limit brakes wrong passwords) and hits it in _issue_and_send() once every check has admitted the email (count_address, set by resend_verification() only: registration_email_work() was counted at the registration), just before the commit and the email — a refusal there rolls everything back, and an email the SMTP server then refuses stays counted; a registration hits it only when its email may go (registration_email_verdict(): the instance's budget peeked too). The refusal of a resend says the longest wait of this count and the instance's budget when that one is spent too 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED; for a registration, no email queued (Verification email held: …), the answer says held with verification_retry_after_seconds, and the account still waits Workstream A's limit on failed sign-ins: 10 failures every 15 minutes per identifier, 50 per client address (login_throttle) The sign-in's own counts, shared both ways: the identifier as typed, A–Z folded, and the client address through client_rate_key(). Only a wrong password or an unknown account counts 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED, before the password One email every 5 minutes, 3 an hour (VERIFICATION_EMAIL_MIN_INTERVAL, VERIFICATION_EMAILS_PER_HOUR) The account's verification tokens that carry an address, created in the last hour: the links emailed, never a hold, so never a link whose email did not go out, which lost its address. «Send the link again» counts them first; every email counts them again inside the write transaction 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED, with the wait VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX: 3 emails an hour The recipient's address through mailbox_budget_key(), the aliases of one mailbox together, whatever account gives it: the registration's email and «send the link again» alike. Peeked before anything is created, hit only once the email went out 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED for «send the link again», with the wait; for a registration, no email (Verification email: not sent) after an answer that said sending, and the account still waits The hourly budget of the instance budget_status(), peeked before anything is created; the email spends its unit 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED A place under LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS Only when the account's link has expired: a live link keeps the place. Counted before, then again inside the write transaction 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED

delivery.ADDRESS_BUDGET and VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX are SlidingWindowLimiters in the memory of the process, like the «forgot password» limiters (VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX is the counterpart of FORGOT_BY_MAILBOX), with the same consequences; the two per-address limiters follow the same proxy rules (A Forgotten Password). The per-account limits and the place read the database.

docs.title: 📝 What Is Logged
docs.text:
Event Level Fields Registration waits for email verification info user_id: hold_for_verification() Verification email held: address limit or instance budget reached info user_id, by_address, by_instance: POST /auth/register (api/v1/auth.py), past delivery.ADDRESS_BUDGET or with the instance's hourly budget spent; the account waits without its email, and the answer says verification_email: "held" Verification link emailed info user_id, token_id, language: after Email sent Verification email: the account no longer waits, nothing sent info user_id: registration_email_work(), for an account whose status changed meanwhile, or that no longer exists, whether its first check or the first write of _issue_and_send() finds it Verification email: not sent warning user_id, reason (the exception's class), code: a refusal or a failed delivery in registration_email_work(), such as email off, the hourly budget or the mailbox's limit spent, or a message the SMTP server did not take (its link lost its address); a waiting account keeps waiting, and the only sign of it is this line: the answer had said "sending" Verification email: the request failed error user_id, error (the exception's class), and no traceback: a database error would print its SQL parameters Email verified info user_id, token_id Email verification refused: the link's email did not go out info user_id, token_id: a token without email, refused but not revoked; the account keeps waiting Email verification refused: the link was sent to another address info user_id, token_id: the link is revoked Login refused: email not verified info user_id: the login route (api/v1/auth.py), for a waiting account that gave the right password Verification resend refused: wrong credentials warning None: resend_verification(), for a wrong password or an unknown account. Logged as the login logs its failures, without the identifier, so that what watches those sees these too

No event holds a token, an address or an identifier. The User registered event of workstream A has waits_for_email, true when the new account waits for its link. Of the refusals of «send the link again», only the wrong credentials leave an event; the answer says the others. The email itself leaves Email sent or Email not sent (What Is Logged), and workstream A's token_service logs each token it issues, consumes or revokes.

docs.title: 🖥️ In the Frontend
docs.text:
File Role features/email/verificationApi.ts The seam over the generated client, shared by the page and the notice. confirmEmailVerification(token) calls confirm_email_verification_api_v1_email_verification_confirm_post and gives {username}; readLinkRefusal(error) gives the status of a 400 TOKEN_INVALID (expired, consumed, revoked, and unknown for any other), blocked while the hosting provider blocks the instance (lot E-10: the 423 instance_blocked of a signed-in browser, recognised by workstream H's isInstanceBlockedError(), or the 401 of an anonymous one, the only 401 of this public route, which stays outside ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED), and null for any other failure (no answer, a server error), which may be tried again. resendEmailVerification(username, password) calls resend_email_verification_api_v1_email_verification_resend_post and gives the email's language; readResendFailure(error) gives a ResendFailure, {errorCode, retryAfter}: INVALID_CREDENTIALS for the route's own 401, whose detail carries that code; INSTANCE_BLOCKED while the hosting provider blocks the instance (lot E-11: any other 401, the anonymous browser's, since this public route stays outside ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED too, or the 423 instance_blocked that isInstanceBlockedError() recognises); else the error_code of the detail, UNKNOWN without one features/email/emailApi.ts Exports the readers of a refusal that verificationApi.ts shares with readTestFailure(): refusalBody(), refusalStatus() (the HTTP status, undefined without an answer), refusalDetail() (the detail object, null for a plain-text detail or none) and retryAfterOf() (a finite retry_after) features/email/emailText.ts VerifyPageStatus (ready, checking, a refusal of the link, blocked, missing, error: nine statuses, ready since lot E-25) and VERIFY_PAGE_KEYS, each status to its whole email.verification.page.* key. resendFailureMessage(): a key of email.verification.resendErrors.* of its own for INVALID_CREDENTIALS, EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED (with the minutes, minutesUntil(); one neutral text for every 429, whether the per-address limit, the limit on failed sign-ins, a per-account limit or the hourly budget), EMAIL_VERIFICATION_NOT_NEEDED, USER_LIMIT_REACHED and ACCOUNT_DISABLED; INSTANCE_BLOCKED with workstream A's auth.instanceBlocked, the text of lot A7b: E has no key of its own for it, so the sentence has one home; unavailable for EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE, EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE, EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED and EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID; generic for anything else features/email/VerifyEmailCard.svelte What the page of a link shows: the button that confirms the address, the wait, why the link cannot be used, a blocked instance, or a check that failed, and the way back to the sign-in (never in ready) features/email/VerificationNotice.svelte The sign-in's notice for an account that waits: «verify your email», and «Send the link again» routes/verify-email/+page.svelte The page of the link, /verify-email#token=…
  • The page takes the token out of the address bar on mount, with workstream A's takeLinkToken() and replaceAddress() (Account Link Pages), keeps it in memory and shows ready: email.verification.page.ready, the button Confirm my email address (email.verification.page.confirm, the words of the email's button) and, under it, email.verification.page.notSignedUp, for whoever did not sign up. In ready it asks the server nothing about the link, and the card has no way back to the sign-in: whoever did not sign up closes the page. Only the click spends the link (lot E-25): confirm() shows checking, with nothing left to click (a double click cannot spend twice), and calls POST /email/verification/confirm. Once the address is verified, the page hands email.verification.verified, with the username, to the sign-in (setAuthFlash()) and goes to /. Without a token it shows missing, with no button; a refused link shows its status, after the click; a blocked instance shows blocked, without Retry: the block stopped the request before the route, so the link is untouched and works again once the instance is unblocked (an anonymous 401 reaches the page once workstream A's lot A7b keeps the link pages out of the interceptor's redirect to the sign-in); any other failure shows error, with Retry, which is confirm() again, on the token the page kept. A link pasted into a tab already on the page changes only the fragment, so a hashchange listener reads it and brings the page back to ready: it waits for a click too, and a fragment without a token changes nothing. A generation counter, raised by every link read and every click, lets only the latest one write: the answer about an older link, arriving late, is dropped, and the page stays in ready for the new link. Like the other link pages, it sets <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">.
  • Why a click (lot E-25): the mail filters that scan the links of a message (Microsoft Defender Safe Links, Proofpoint, Mimecast) open each one in a sandboxed browser that runs scripts. A page that spent its token on load would verify the address in place of its owner, and the owner's own click would then find the link used. Opening the page now spends nothing; the route and its answers are unchanged (POST /email/verification/confirm).
  • VerifyEmailCard sits on workstream A's AuthCard, not on its LinkStatusCard: that card sends the reader of a dead link to an administrator (auth.link.askAdmin), while a dead verification link is fixed by signing in, which offers a new one. No text of the page names an administrator.
  • VerificationNotice takes the username and the password typed in the sign-in form and sends the link again with them. LoginCard shows it instead of its error line when the login answers 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED: the auth store's loginErrorKey() maps that answer to email.verification.loginRequired (a member of AuthErrorKey), and LoginCard passes the form's username and password. Its button is disabled while the request runs, and without a username or a password. The outcome is rendered from the stored outcome, so it follows a change of language, and each one is an app event through notify(), without a toast: email.verification.resent with the language, or email.verification.resendFailed with the failure fields. On a blocked instance the sign-in still answers (auth.login is in ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED), so the notice shows; «send the link again» then gets the block's 401, which reaches the notice: the sign-in is /, where the interceptor does not redirect a 401. The notice says it as INSTANCE_BLOCKED, never as wrong credentials (lot E-11, the reasoning of the page's blocked in lot E-10). The block refuses the request before the route, so nothing is counted or sent; the button stays enabled, and a click after the unblock works.
  • In workstream A's components: RegisterCard returns to the sign-in with email.verification.registeredHeld when the answer says verification_required and verification_email is 'held' (lot E-26), with email.verification.registered for any other answer that says verification_required, a server that sends no verification_email at all included (an older one: it can only mean «sending»), and with auth.accountCreated without verification; the message shows in the sign-in's usual box (login-success). describeRegistrationError() turns 409 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE into email.verification.signUpUnavailable. The Global Settings tab (GlobalSettingsTab.svelte) disables the switch while its saved value is off and email.links of GET /system/instance is false, with the hint email.verification.settingNeedsEmail (once saved on, it can go off and on again until the next save), and shows a 409 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE as email.verification.settingUnavailable; PLACEHOLDER_KEYS is empty. UserRow turns Reactivate off on a full instance only for an account without holds_place (AdminAccount.holds_place). Since lot E-7, UserRow shows the badge users-badge-pending-verification, Waiting for verification (settings.usersTab.badges.pendingVerification), in place of Deactivated (now users-badge-inactive) when AdminAccount.pending_verification is true, the account inactive and not pending_setup, the setup's wait winning: the badge stays once the link has expired. The badge has a hover hint, and the opened panel the hint users-pending-verification-hint, both settings.usersTab.pendingVerificationHint (the settings i18n source); the row publishes data-pending-verification with that derived state. The actions are those of any inactive account. The command line's user list marks nothing.
  • Test hooks: verify-email-page (the page's AuthPageFrame), verify-email-status (the card, with data-status), verify-email-message (aria-live="polite"), verify-email-confirm and verify-email-hint (on ready only, and the button only with an onconfirm), verify-email-retry (on error only), verify-email-goto-login (in every status but ready and checking); email-verification-notice (with data-busy and aria-busy), email-verification-resend, email-verification-outcome (aria-live="polite", data-outcome sent or failed).
  • The texts are in the email i18n source, under email.verification.*: the page's (page.*, verified), the notice's (loginRequired, resend, resending, resent, resendErrors.*), and those of workstream A's components (registered, registeredHeld, signUpUnavailable, settingNeedsEmail, settingUnavailable). For a blocked instance, the notice borrows auth.instanceBlocked from the auth source.

docs.title: 🌐 The API (api/v1/email.py)
docs.text: backend/app/api/v1/email.py is a router with prefix="/email" and the tag Email, which api/v1/router.py mounts under /api/v1; its models, all StrictModel, are in backend/app/schemas/email.py. Three routes are for administrators, /status, /test and /links: they depend on require_admin (backend/app/api/v1/settings.py), 401 without a session, 403 for an account that is not an administrator; then the email configuration is not read, and nothing is sent or spent. /password-reset, /verification/confirm and /verification/resend need no session. One more route, outside this router, publishes whether email is usable: email in GET /api/v1/system/instance.

docs.title: 📊 GET /api/v1/email/status
docs.text:
A plain def: reading the configuration may read the password file, so FastAPI runs the route in its thread pool, not on the event loop. Every call evaluates EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS and email_config_state() afresh; it opens no connection and resolves no name. It answers an EmailStatusResponse:

Field Value state off (no host), ready (usable) or invalid (a value cannot be used: email stays off) problem, variable invalid only: the code and the variable at fault, as in Email Off, Usable or Unusable; null otherwise checks The three checks of EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS, in that order, each an EmailCheckRead: check_id, severity, i18n_key, detail budget ready only: an EmailBudgetRead from budget_status(), which spends nothing — max_per_hour, remaining, and retry_after_seconds, the limiter's retry_after rounded up, 0 while an email fits links Every state: an EmailLinksRead from links_state() — ready, base (LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, the base of every emailed link, which the Email tab checks from the browser) and problem (PUBLIC_URL_MISSING or PUBLIC_URL_INVALID)

EmailCheckRead is a ConfigCheck without its summary, because the English log line of the plain-text warning names the SMTP host. No state returns the host, the port, the user, the sender, the Reply-To, the password or the path of a password file.

docs.title: 📮 POST /api/v1/email/test
docs.text:
An async def without a body. It calls flows.send_test_email(session, admin, instance=request.url.netloc): the test email goes to the administrator's own address, in their language, and names the instance by the host the request was sent to, port included (behind a reverse proxy, the Host header it forwards): a label in the text, never a link. Like any send_email(), it spends one unit of the budget once the configuration and the address pass.

Status Body When Budget 200 EmailTestResponse: language (en, it, fr or es) and message, Test email sent The server accepted the message Spent 409 detail: error_code EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE, problem, message EmailUnavailableError: problem is EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED without a host, else the code of the configuration problem Not spent; no connection 422 detail: error_code EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID, message The administrator's stored address is not exactly one address: the EmailRecipientError of compose_message(), caught by name (another ValueError is a 500) Not spent; no connection 429 detail: error_code EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED, retry_after, message; the Retry-After header EmailRateLimitedError: retry_after and Retry-After are the same whole number of seconds, at least 1 Not spent; no connection 502 detail: error_code EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED, smtp_code, message EmailDeliveryError: smtp_code is the SmtpErrorCode Spent

The rows follow the order of the checks in send_email(): an unusable configuration answers 409 even for an address that is not one address. message is a fixed English sentence; the interface translates the codes. No answer carries the server's own words, which reach only the log, masked (What Is Logged). After a 200 the route logs Test email sent by an administrator, with admin_id and language.

docs.title: ✉️ POST /api/v1/email/links
docs.text:
An async def. The body is an EmailLinkRequest: purpose (invite or password_reset), token (as the creating route answered it, 1 to 512 characters, never logged), and for an invitation only to (an EmailStr) and language (en, it, fr or es). It calls send_link_email() and answers an EmailLinkResponse: purpose, to (where the email went) and language.

Status detail When 409 error_code EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE, problem Email is off or unusable 409 error_code EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE, problem LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is missing, or cannot start a link (Links) 409 error_code EMAIL_LINK_INVALID, status The token is not a live link of that purpose: expired, consumed, revoked or unknown 409 error_code EMAIL_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE A password-reset link of an account that is not active 422 error_code EMAIL_RECIPIENT_REQUIRED An invitation without to and without an address written in it 422 error_code EMAIL_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED A to for a password-reset link 422 error_code EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID The address the email would go to, written in the invitation or the account's, is not exactly one address 429 error_code EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED, retry_after; the Retry-After header The hourly budget is spent 502 error_code EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED, smtp_code The SMTP server did not take the message

Each detail also has a fixed English message. A to that is not an email address fails the validation of the body first, with FastAPI's own 422.

docs.title: 🔑 POST /api/v1/email/password-reset
docs.text:
An async def, without a session. The body is a PasswordResetEmailRequest: identifier, a username or an email address, 1 to 254 characters. It runs the admission with rate_limit_address(request), queues forgotten_password_work() as a background task on the request's engine (session.bind), and answers 202 PasswordResetEmailAccepted, whose message is the same for everyone: If an active account matches, its owner gets an email with a link to choose a new password.

Status detail When 202 — Admitted: the work runs after the answer 409 error_code EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE Email is off or unusable; no problem, unlike the administrators' routes 409 error_code EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is missing, or cannot start a link; no problem either 429 error_code EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED, retry_after; the Retry-After header Past the limit per address or per identifier, or the hourly budget spent

None of them depends on the accounts. EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE and EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE say nothing that GET /system/instance does not publish already (email.available and email.links).

docs.title: 🔓 POST /api/v1/email/verification/confirm
docs.text:
An async def, without a session: the link proves that its reader received the email. The page of the link calls it only on the owner's click, never when it opens (In the Frontend). The body is an EmailVerificationConfirmRequest: token, 1 to 256 characters, read from the fragment of the link. The route calls confirm_email() and answers 200 EmailVerificationConfirmResponse: the username of the account, for the sign-in, which names it in its confirmation (In the Frontend).

Status detail When 200 — The account is active, its address verified, its other verification links revoked 400 error_code TOKEN_INVALID, status Not a live verification link: expired, consumed, revoked or unknown. revoked also for a link emailed to an address the account no longer has, which is revoked then, and for a link whose email did not go out, which is left as it is: the account keeps waiting

The 400 also has a fixed English message. An expired link is not the end: signing in offers to send a new one (/verification/resend).

docs.title: 🔁 POST /api/v1/email/verification/resend
docs.text:
An async def, without a session: the credentials of the sign-in stand in for one. The body is an EmailVerificationResendRequest: username, the username or the email address as at sign-in, 1 to 254 characters, and password, 1 to 1024. The route calls resend_verification() with rate_limit_address(request) for the per-address limits, its own and the sign-in's, and answers 200 EmailVerificationResendResponse: the language of the email.

Status detail When 200 — A new link went to the account's address; the older ones no longer work 401 error_code INVALID_CREDENTIALS A wrong password or an unknown account: one answer for both, at the same cost, with the sign-in's status, counted as a failed sign-in (Failed Sign-in Limit) 403 error_code ACCOUNT_DISABLED An inactive account that does not wait: an administrator deactivated it 409 error_code EMAIL_VERIFICATION_NOT_NEEDED The account is active: there is nothing to verify 409 error_code EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE Email is off or unusable, or the instance is blocked 409 error_code EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is missing, or cannot start a link 409 error_code USER_LIMIT_REACHED The account's link expired, and its place with it: the instance is full now 429 error_code EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED, retry_after; the Retry-After header Past the per-address limit or the limit on failed sign-ins (both before the password), a per-account limit, or the hourly budget 502 error_code EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED The SMTP server did not take the message: the new link lost its address, the account still waits, and a new request may follow at once 422 error_code EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID The account's address is not exactly one address

Each detail object also has a fixed English message; a body that fails validation gets FastAPI's own 422. Only the 401 and the two 429s before the password, the per-address limit and the limit on failed sign-ins, can answer someone without the account's password. Like /password-reset's, the two …_UNAVAILABLE answers carry no problem, and the 502 carries no smtp_code: whoever asks is not an administrator.

The 401 carries its code since lot E-11; before, it was the sign-in's plain string Invalid credentials. Any other 401 of this route is the instance block's: like /verification/confirm, the route is public and stays outside ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED, so on a blocked instance the block answers first. A caller without a session gets the 401 of get_current_user, a plain string; a signed-in one gets the 423 instance_blocked. The web app reads both as the block (In the Frontend).

docs.title: 🌍 email in GET /api/v1/system/instance
docs.text:
The public configuration of the instance, which answers without a session (Public instance configuration), has an email field: an EmailInstanceConfig (backend/app/schemas/email.py) with two booleans. get_instance_config() (backend/app/api/v1/system/instance.py) fills it with email_instance_config(), through asyncio.to_thread: the read may open the password file.

  • available: a server is set, every variable can be used, and the hosting provider does not block the instance (sending_blocked()); with the instance not blocked, that is the state ready of GET /api/v1/email/status. Usable, not delivered: nothing is sent and no server is contacted to tell, so a server that refuses the login still counts as available.
  • links: available, and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL a usable base (Links): emails with a link can go out. The server never checks that this address reaches the instance; only the Email tab does, from the administrator's browser.
  • Nothing more: the answer is the same for whoever asks and never holds the configuration, the address or the budget. An unusable value read here is logged like any other read, at most once per process for the same reason.
  • Off by default: both booleans default to False, and InstanceConfigResponse declares the field with default_factory=EmailInstanceConfig, so it is optional in the schema: an answer built without it, or read from an older server, says that nothing can be sent.

In the frontend, email.links decides three things: whether the share dialogs offer «Send by email» (sendByEmailVisible()), whether the sign-in's Forgot Password? card shows the «forgot password» form (Links by Email in the Interface), and whether the Global Settings tab lets the switch of email verification turn on (In the Frontend).

docs.title: 🖥️ The Email Tab
docs.text:
The tab is in frontend/src/lib/features/email/, its texts in frontend/src/lib/i18n/email/. The same folder holds the frontend of email verification (In the Frontend), «Send by email» and the «forgot password» form (Links by Email in the Interface).

File Role emailApi.ts The seam over the client that ./dev.py api sync generates: fetchEmailStatus() and sendTestEmail() call get_email_status_api_v1_email_status_get and send_test_api_v1_email_test_post. fetchEmailStatus() narrows the answer into EmailStatus, its six keys present: the generated type of an optional field is wider than its runtime schema (string \| null also admits an array), so problem and variable become a string or null, checks a list, budget an object or null, and links an EmailLinks (linksOf()): ready only with a base, never a base when not ready, not ready when absent. issueProbeNonce() asks for a nonce of the address check (issue_address_probe_api_v1_users_address_probe_post, POST /users/address-probe, administrators only). readTestFailure() reads the detail of a refused test — from the AxiosError the generated client rejects with, or from an ApiError — into {errorCode, problem, smtpCode, retryAfter}; errorCode is UNKNOWN without a detail object, after a network error for one. It reads them with refusalBody(), refusalStatus(), refusalDetail() and retryAfterOf(), exported for verificationApi.ts emailLinks.ts The check of the links' base from the browser (developer decision 45). probeEmailLinks(base, {pageProtocol, issueNonce, fetchImpl?, timeoutMs?}) never throws and gives a LinksOutcome: invalid when workstream A's normalizeBase() refuses the base, and insecure when the page is https: and the base http: (a browser blocks that mixed content), both before any request; otherwise A's checkAddress(), its verdict mapped: match to match, mismatch to otherInstance, unverifiable to unreachable. A's helper (settings/users/addressProbe.ts) is imported as it is, never copied; its nonce, its CORS simple request and its 8-second timeout are in LinkShare and Address Probe emailText.ts Every code to a whole i18n key and every state to whole classes of the theme roles (*-lf-*), as string literals that the i18n audit and the colour gates can see: STATE_LABEL_KEYS, STATE_BADGE_CLASSES, NOTICE_CLASSES, OUTCOME_CLASSES. problemKey() falls back to email.problems.unknown (only the maps' own entries count: a code such as constructor finds nothing); minutesUntil() gives whole minutes, at least 1; testFailureMessage() falls back to email.smtpErrors.SEND_FAILED for an unknown smtp_code and to email.test.errors.generic for any other failure. For the check of the links: LINKS_PROBE_KEYS (each LinksProbeState to its email.links.probe.* key), LINKS_PROBE_CLASSES (a running check and a match as a line of text, any other outcome as a warning notice) and linksProbeWarns(), true for an outcome that is neither running nor a match. For email verification: VERIFY_PAGE_KEYS and resendFailureMessage() (In the Frontend). For the links by email: linkSendFailureMessage() and forgotFailureMessage() (Links by Email in the Interface) EmailSettingsTab.svelte The tab body, in Svelte 5 runes

What the tab does:

  • On mount it reads GET /email/status; a failure shows email.loadError, above the last state read if there is one. Only the latest read writes: an older answer never replaces a newer one. data-busy (and aria-busy) is true while a request runs, the status or the test email.
  • The state: a badge (email.state.*), then the explanation for off; for invalid, the message of the problem with its {variable} and the reminder to restart; for ready, the budget — email.budget.remaining, or email.budget.spent with the minutes to wait when none is left.
  • The checks: one line for each check that is not ok, except email.smtp, whose problem the state already explains. Today that leaves the plain-text warning and the email.links notice, info or warning.
  • The links' base, when the state is ready and links.ready: the block email-links (data-base) shows email.links.base with the base (email-links-base), then the line of the check (email-links-probe, aria-live="polite", data-outcome set to checking or the outcome). A warning outcome adds Check again (email-links-recheck), which runs the check once more. Without a base — email off or invalid, or links not ready — nothing is shown or checked. The check runs once per base: the status read again after a test email keeps the same base, and nothing is checked again. A generation counter lets only the latest check write: «Check again», a new base or leaving the tab drops an older one. Each finished check is notified as email.links.checked with {outcome}, without a toast. The block has its own data-busy and aria-busy while the check runs; the tab's data-busy covers the status and the test email only.
  • The test email, in ready only. The button is disabled while any request runs, the status read again included, so one click sends one email. The outcome shows below it, role="status" or role="alert", rendered from the stored outcome so that it follows a change of language; then the tab reads the status again, so the budget follows. Each outcome is also an app event, through notify() without a toast since the outcome is already on screen: email.test.sent with the language, or email.test.failed with the failure fields.
  • The guide: the header's DocsLink opens admin/email/, the administrator's guide.
  • Test hooks: a data-testid on each part (email-tab, email-state, email-problem, email-budget, email-check, email-links, email-links-base, email-links-probe, email-links-recheck, email-test-button, email-test-outcome…) and the values a test checks as data-* attributes: data-state, data-problem, data-variable, data-remaining, data-max, data-check-id, data-severity, data-base, data-outcome.

The texts are a subsystem source of the frontend catalogue (The Sources): its prefixes.txt owns email, and the four languages hold the same keys. They cover the tab, the states, the nine problem codes and unknown, the messages of the three checks (email.checks.*, the i18n_key values of checks.py), the base of the links and the outcomes of its check (email.links.*), the budget, the test email and its errors, the seven SmtpErrorCode values (email.smtpErrors.*), the page and the notice of email verification (email.verification.*), «Send by email» (email.sendLink.*) and the «forgot password» form (email.forgot.*). The emails' own texts stay in the backend catalogue (The Catalogue).

SETTINGS_TABS, the tab registry of the Settings page, registers the tab:

{id: 'email', labelKey: 'email.tab.label', icon: Mail, order: 130, component: EmailSettingsTab, visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser, group: 'administration'},

group puts it in the «Administration» group, on the right of the bar on a wide screen: the tab is in the group's second bar, where order 130 puts it after Global Settings (100), Users (110) and Backup (120), and ?tab=email opens it inside the group. visible keeps it for administrators: a regular user never sees it, and a ?tab=email they open is ignored.

docs.title: 📮 Links by Email in the Interface
docs.text:
Two components of frontend/src/lib/features/email/ put the emailed links in front of people: «Send by email» in the share dialogs of the Users tab, for an administrator (POST /email/links), and the «forgot password» form of the sign-in, for anyone (POST /email/password-reset).

Where they are hosted, in workstream A's files:

  • «Send by email»: {id: 'send-by-email', component: SendLinkByEmail, visible: () => sendByEmailVisible()} in LINK_SHARE_ACTIONS (Link-Share Actions Registry): both share dialogs draw it under the link while email.links is true. SendLinkByEmail imports only a type from the registry, so the two modules form no cycle.
  • The «forgot password» form: ForgotPasswordCard calls instanceConfig.load() on mount and, while email.links of GET /system/instance is true, shows ForgotPasswordEmailForm in place of its warning (forgot-email-unavailable); on a self-hosted instance the box of server commands stays below it, in a panel closed by default (the developer's decision P1, 16/10), and on a managed one forgot-ask-admin takes its place (F05; ForgotPasswordCard). When the request fails before any answer (instanceConfig.failed, never loaded), email.links is unknown: the card shows only forgot-ask-admin, the advice that holds in both profiles (FPM-08, workstream A).
  • The email change notice: update_profile (PUT /api/v1/auth/profile) queues email_changed_work() after a change of address.

docs.title: 📧 Send by Email
docs.text:
File Role sendLinkApi.ts tokenFromLink(link): the token parameter of the link's #token= fragment, null without one. sendByEmailVisible(): whether email.links of the instance configuration (GET /system/instance, read through instanceConfig) is true, the condition of the action. sendLinkByEmail({purpose, token, to, language}) calls send_link_api_v1_email_links_post, with to and language only when they are given, and gives {to, language}. readLinkSendFailure(error) gives a LinkSendFailure, {errorCode, smtpCode, retryAfter}. A 422 without a detail object is the request's own validation, and the only field an administrator types is the address: it reads as EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID, so the specific text shows. Any other failure without one (no answer) is UNKNOWN SendLinkByEmail.svelte The action, with the props of workstream A's registry: {link, purpose, context} (LinkShareActionProps)
  • Only the token travels. The component takes the token out of the link the dialog shows and sends it alone: the email's link is built by the backend from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (Links), whatever address the dialog shows, and a line above the button says so (email.sendLink.publicUrlHint). Without a token in the link, the button stays disabled.
  • The recipient. An invitation goes to the address in the field, filled with the one the dialog knows (context.email, the address written in the invitation) and editable; left empty, the backend uses the address written in the invitation. A reset link has no field: a line says that it goes to the account's address, and no to is sent.
  • The language (lot E-8, decision N69): an invitation has a selector under the address, the app's SimpleSelect labelled email.sendLink.languageLabel (also its ariaLabel). Its first option, chosen by default, is the instance's language (email.sendLink.languageInstance, value ''), then the four languages of LANGUAGE_OPTIONS, each by its native name with its flag. On the default no language key is sent at all, so the backend writes in the instance's default language as before; a language chosen is sent as its code. Only the email's language: it does not become the language of the account the invitation creates, which would need the token to carry it (decision N69). A reset link has no selector and never sends a language: its email goes in the account's language (A Link an Administrator Emails).
  • The outcome is rendered from the stored outcome, so it follows a change of language: email.sendLink.sent with the address the email went to and the language it was written in, from the answer (not from the choice), by its native name (LOCALE_NAMES; a code the interface does not know, as it is), or linkSendFailureMessage() — a text for each error_code of POST /email/links, the email.smtpErrors.* text of the smtp_code for EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED (SEND_FAILED for an unknown one) except RECIPIENT_REFUSED, which has its own email.sendLink.errors.RECIPIENT_REFUSED (the refused address is the invitee's or the account's, not the administrator's own as for the test email), and email.sendLink.errors.generic for anything else. Each outcome is an app event through notify(), without a toast: email.link.sent with purpose and language, or email.link.sendFailed with purpose and the failure fields.
  • Test hooks: send-link-email (data-purpose, data-busy, aria-busy), send-link-email-to (an invitation's field), send-link-email-language (an invitation's language selector: its trigger send-link-email-language-button, its options send-link-email-language-option-<code>, the default one send-link-email-language-option-instance), send-link-email-target (a reset link's line), send-link-email-button, send-link-email-outcome (aria-live="polite", data-outcome sent or failed, and on sent data-language, the code the email was written in).

docs.title: 🔑 The «Forgot Password» Form
docs.text:
File Role forgotPasswordApi.ts requestPasswordResetEmail(identifier) calls request_password_reset_email_api_v1_email_password_reset_post; readForgotFailure(error) gives a ForgotFailure, {errorCode, retryAfter}: INVALID for a 422, else the error_code of the detail, UNKNOWN without one ForgotPasswordEmailForm.svelte The form: a username or an email address, then a reset link by email if an active account matches
  • The same answer for everyone. The 202 never says whether an account matches, and the form shows it as information (email.forgot.accepted, in the colours of an info notice), never as «sent»: check the inbox and the spam folder, the link works for 30 minutes.
  • A refusal: forgotFailureMessage() gives unavailable for EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE and EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE, EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED with the minutes, and generic for anything else.
  • The identifier is trimmed and at most 254 characters long; the button is disabled while it is empty or while the request runs. Each outcome is an app event through notify(), without a toast: email.forgot.accepted, or email.forgot.refused with the failure fields.
  • Test hooks: forgot-email-form (data-busy, aria-busy), forgot-email-identifier, forgot-email-submit, forgot-email-outcome (aria-live="polite", data-outcome accepted or failed).

docs.title: 🪟 The Sliding-Window Limiter
docs.text:
backend/app/utils/runtime/rate_window.py is the one primitive for every limit that counts events in a moving window: the hourly email budget, the «forgot password» limits of flows.py and the per-address limit of «send the link again» (verification.py) use it, and so does workstream A's limit on failed sign-ins (lot A8a), which «send the link again» consults too. A new limit of this kind uses it too, instead of a counter of its own.

Member Contract SlidingWindowLimiter(limit, window_seconds, *, max_keys=10_000, clock=time.monotonic) ValueError when limit < 1, window_seconds <= 0 or max_keys < 1; limit and window_seconds are properties peek(key=None, *, limit=None) The RateDecision a hit would get now; counts nothing and never creates a key hit(key=None, *, limit=None) The same decision; records the hit only when it is allowed count(key=None) How many hits of key are in the window now reset(key=None), clear() Forget one key, or every key len(limiter) The number of keys holding a hit still in the window RateDecision(allowed, remaining, retry_after) Frozen
  • The window: a hit at t counts while clock() - t < window_seconds; exactly window_seconds later it no longer does.
  • Allowed while the count is below the limit: remaining is limit - count for a peek and limit - (count + 1) after an allowed hit; retry_after is 0.
  • Refused: remaining is 0 and retry_after = ts[count - limit] + window_seconds - now, where ts are the live hits, oldest first: the wait until enough of them leave. With a limit of 3 and a 60 s window, hits at 1000, 1001 and 1002 make a fourth at 1003 wait 57 s.
  • A refused hit is not recorded: a caller that keeps knocking does not push its own unlock further away.
  • Per-call limit: limit= replaces the default for that call only (below 1, a ValueError); lowered below the count, the wait is for enough hits to expire.
  • Keys are any hashable value, and None, the default, is a key like any other.
  • Bounded memory: at most max_keys keys, always, and a new key is never refused for want of room. A new key beyond them evicts the key with the fewest hits still in the window at that moment, and among those the one used or regrouped longest ago: a key goes to the end of its group when it is peeked, hit or counted, and when one of its hits leaves the window. No limit, the limiter's own or a call's, enters the choice. The new key is never the one evicted, and an evicted key's hits are forgotten with it. Only an allowed hit creates a key, and a key whose hits have all left the window is dropped at the next call, read or not.
  • Why the fewest hits go (lot E-14, from workstream E's review of decision N70): a key sprayed to make room holds one hit, so a spray of fresh keys never frees a key that holds more, locked or not. To free a key with n hits, every other key must hold n hits too: for workstream A's limit on failed sign-ins per identifier (10 in 15 minutes, 10,000 keys), about 90,000 failures within the window buy 9 more guesses. Measured on the limiter, the cheapest attack costs about 10,000 requests per extra guess. N70's eviction (the first key not full among the 32 least recently used, as eviction_scan) cost about 1,100, no better than plain least-recently-used eviction: an identifier stopped one failure short of the lock is never full, so a spray of 10,000 fresh ones freed it.
  • Exact expiry: a heap holds, for each key, when its oldest hit leaves the window, and every call first takes the hits that have left out of their keys. A key whose hits have left keeps no protection, read or not: with expiry only on reading, a crowd of keys kept at a count they no longer hold would let a key with fewer hits go for one request each.
  • No search: the keys are grouped by count, each group oldest first, so a new key costs the same however many keys there are: about 30 µs for a new key and its 10 hits beside 10,000 full keys, where a walk of every key costs about 7 ms. The «forgot password» limits are hit at every request, before anything else is read (admit_forgotten_password()), so a walk would make a cheap request a CPU amplifier. The heap keeps at most two entries per key plus 64, and is rebuilt from the keys past that: memory stays bounded whatever the rate of requests.
  • Injectable clock: tests move a fake clock instead of waiting.
  • Thread-safe: one lock; threads hitting a key with a limit of N get exactly N hits allowed.
  • Per process, in memory: with N worker processes a limit is N times the configured one, and a restart forgets every count.

The backend files are under backend/test_scripts/. All thirteen backend entries are pure in the runner catalogue: no lane database, no server. The two E2 files build their database as a private SQLite file under tmp_path, and api email mounts the real auth and email routers under the API prefix in an app of its own: its accounts sign in through POST /auth/login, over httpx.ASGITransport. api email-verification-hooks does the same with the auth, users, settings and email routers, on a private SQLite file. The Settings tab registry's own test (settingsTabs.test.ts) pins the Email tab: administrators only, no props, in the «Administration» group after Backup. The gallery has a settings/email shot, with the state answered ready by the test.

  • No inherited configuration. Every module, the rate window's included, starts with an autouse fixture that removes every LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* variable; each test then sets only what it needs with monkeypatch, and password files live in tmp_path. A test lane already drops them: configure_test_runtime() (scripts/cli_base.py) removes every variable .env.example documents and every LIBREFOLIO_* name, so the lane's server runs without email. The fixture keeps a run outside a lane honest too: a new email test follows the same rule and never reads the lane's environment.
  • Never a real network. FakeSmtpServer (backend/test_scripts/fixtures/email/fake_smtp.py) is written with the standard library and listens on 127.0.0.1, on a port the OS picks. It speaks the part of SMTP that smtplib uses (EHLO with AUTH PLAIN LOGIN, then 8BITMIME and SMTPUTF8 unless smtputf8=False, STARTTLS only when given a tls_context, MAIL, RCPT, DATA, QUIT), can refuse at each step (credentials, refuse_sender, refuse_recipients, refuse_data, quit_code, greet=False), and records messages, auth_attempts and connections; each message keeps its mail_options, the parameters after MAIL FROM:<…>. SMTPUTF8 lets an address with letters outside ASCII through, as real servers do: without it, smtplib refuses such an address on the client side, SEND_FAILED (EMD-047). Read such an address from rcpt_tos or data, never from the parsed message, whose parser turns those bytes into escapes. A refused recipient is named in the 550 reply, as Postfix does, so the masking of the log meets a real server's habit. As a context manager it closes every socket, joins every thread and fails the test on a defect of its own. closed_port(), also a context manager, yields a port of 127.0.0.1 that refuses connections and holds it for the whole block, so no listener started meanwhile can take it. In api email, socket.getaddrinfo resolves the loopback only and records any other name, which proves that the status never looks up the configured host.
  • No waiting. The delivery, flows and API tests replace delivery.INSTANCE_BUDGET with a limiter on a fake clock, clear the cache of _report_invalid() around each test, and lower smtp.SMTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to 5 s as a bound for a hang; both are module attributes read at call time for that purpose. The only real wait is the timeout test, 0.2 s.
  • «Forgot password» as shipped. Since lot E4 nothing holds it: test_email_flows.py and test_email_api.py run the admission, the route and the work as the modules ship them, without a fixture to lift anything, and check that no hold is left (EMF-053, EMA-049).
  • TLS tests. EMD-017 (STARTTLS against a certificate the client trusts) and EMD-018 (an untrusted certificate refused: the verification is real) build their certificates with cryptography, a dependency of the Pipfile since release 1.3; pytest.importorskip still skips them in an environment without it.
