docs.title: 📅 Asset Events
docs.text: Asset events represent significant occurrences that affect an asset's price or generate distributions. They live in the asset domain, not the portfolio/transaction domain.

docs.title: 📋 Event Types
docs.text:
Event Type Effect on Price Who Generates Description 💰 DIVIDEND Price drops by event value (ex-date) Provider (yfinance, justetf) or manual Cash distribution from equity/ETF 📈 INTEREST Price drops by event value Scheduled Investment (generate_interest) or manual Interest payment from debt/loan. Resets accrued interest 📊 PRICE_ADJUSTMENT Algebraic change (+/−) Manual, or listed in a Scheduled Investment schedule Non-cash value change (write-down, haircut) ✂️ SPLIT Changes quantity, not total value Provider (yfinance) or manual Stock/unit split 🏁 MATURITY_SETTLEMENT Final capital return Scheduled Investment (generate_interest) or manual Asset reaches maturity — no further calculations

The type is always one of these five values (AssetEventType). FAAssetEventPoint (schemas/assets/events.py), the event point of the API, of the provider output and of the Scheduled Investment asset_events, trims and upper-cases it (normalize_type(): dividend becomes DIVIDEND) and refuses anything else: POST /api/v1/assets/events answers 422. Until 1.3 a type was stored as it came (a hand-written CSV could store dividend), and one the enum does not know broke every later read of the asset's events (LookupError, a 500). The post-migration fix event_types repairs the rows stored that way, once, at the first start after the upgrade (decision 23 of release 1.3; see Post-migration fixes).

docs.title: 🗃️ Database Model
docs.text:
erDiagram
    ASSET ||--o{ ASSET_EVENT : "has events"
    ASSET_PROVIDER_ASSIGNMENT ||--o{ ASSET_EVENT : "generates"

    ASSET_EVENT {
        int id PK
        int asset_id FK "→ assets.id"
        date date "Event date"
        enum type "DIVIDEND, INTEREST, PRICE_ADJUSTMENT, SPLIT, MATURITY_SETTLEMENT"
        decimal value "Monetary value"
        string currency "ISO 4217"
        int provider_assignment_id FK "nullable — NULL = manual"
        text notes "nullable"
    }

No UniqueConstraint on (asset_id, date, type) — auto-generated and manual events can coexist on the same date and type. Nothing forbids two rows of the same source on one key either: the upsert below collapses such legacy duplicates when a batch brings fewer events for that key.

Indexes: (asset_id, date), (asset_id, type, date), (provider_assignment_id).

docs.title: 🔄 Dedup Strategy
docs.text:
_write_asset_events() (assets/event_store.py) writes both kinds of events in place, one source per call: a sync passes the assignment's id through _upsert_asset_events(), which returns their count; the manual upsert passes None and gets back the id of the row each event wrote. It groups the incoming events by (date, type) and matches each key against the stored rows of the same source only (same asset_id and provider_assignment_id, IS NULL for manual events):

# Simplified logic of _write_asset_events() and _write_event_group(), for each (date, type) key
stored = rows on the key with this asset_id and provider_assignment_id, ORDER BY id
for row, evt in zip(stored, incoming):  # paired lowest id first: updated, id kept
    row.value, row.currency = evt.value.amount, evt.value.code or default_currency
    row.notes, row.updated_at = evt.notes, now
session.add_all(incoming[len(stored):])  # extra incoming events are inserted
surplus = stored[len(incoming):]  # legacy same-key duplicates of this source
# UPDATE transactions SET asset_event_id = stored[0].id WHERE asset_event_id IN surplus
# DELETE FROM asset_events WHERE id IN surplus

A key thus ends with as many rows as the batch brings, the lowest ids kept, and the transactions of a collapsed duplicate move to the row that stays. Rows of another source on that key are never touched, and a stored key the batch does not mention is kept. Keys are written in slices of PRICE_UPSERT_CHUNK_SIZE (1,000), each one flushed: a sync commits every slice (commit=True, the default of _upsert_asset_events()), while the manual upsert (commit=False) leaves the commit to bulk_upsert_events(), which commits once for the whole request.

The upsert used to DELETE the stored rows of each key and INSERT the new ones. But transactions.asset_event_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so that failed as soon as a transaction realised the event: a provider refresh of such an event reported Event upsert failed, and editing a linked manual event answered HTTP 500. A row updated in place keeps its id, so the transactions linked to it stay linked.

docs.title: 🤖 Auto-Generated Events (provider_assignment_id IS NOT NULL)
docs.text:
A sync passes the assignment's id. This ensures:

  • An event the provider returns again updates the stored one of the same date and type, which keeps its id: a transaction linked to it stays linked
  • Events from different providers for the same asset are independent, and manual events are never touched
  • A stored event the provider no longer returns is kept: the upsert only touches the date and type pairs of its batch

A parametric provider (Scheduled Investment) derives its whole series from its parameters. When they change, or when the asset leaves it for another provider, provider_management.py deletes the asset's prices and that assignment's events, first unlinking the transactions that pointed to them (asset_event_id = NULL); manual events stay. While a SPLIT among those events has linked incoming adjustments without a cost, the change is refused with a 409 and nothing is deleted (Parametric Provider Change).

Removing the asset's provider (No Provider) deletes the assignment and, with it, every event it generated, whatever the provider; manual events stay. It unlinks nothing: while a transaction is linked to one of those events, the removal is refused with a 409 and nothing is deleted (Provider Removal).

The data editor shows these events read-only: the events of POST /assets/prices/query carry is_auto (provider_assignment_id IS NOT NULL). An edit would be overwritten by the next sync. The editor can still delete one, through delete_ids like a manual event (below), but the deletion lasts only until the provider returns the event again.

docs.title: ✋ Manual Events (provider_assignment_id IS NULL)
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/assets/events (bulk_upsert_events()) takes a list of FAEventUpsert items, {asset_id, mode, events, delete_ids}, whose points are FAEventUpsertPoint: an FAAssetEventPoint with an optional id (schemas/assets/events.py).

The request is all or nothing (decision 22 of release 1.3). Its items run in order in one transaction: _write_manual_item() checks an item, then writes and flushes it, so a later item sees what the earlier ones wrote, and a single commit closes the request. Any refusal rolls the whole request back, the items before it included: nothing of it is stored.

An item's mode (decision 20) is "upsert" by default; the data editor and its CSV import send none:

  • An event with id edits that manual row in place, every field included (date, type, value and currency, notes), and the row keeps its id. The data editor sends the id of every saved row, so changing the Type of a saved event no longer adds a second event.
  • Events without id go through _write_asset_events(provider_assignment_id=None): matched on (date, type) among the manual rows and updated in place, so a manual event still replaces the manual event of the same date and type, keeping its id.

With mode: "create", an item only adds events, and none of them may carry an id. An event on a (date, type) the asset already has, manual or from a provider, is refused with EVENT_EXISTS (_reject_existing_events()): a new event never overwrites another one. The transaction form's + New event (EventCreateMiniModal) sends this mode. On EVENT_EXISTS it shows params.existing (EventExistsPanel): Use this links the stored event and writes nothing; Edit this, for a manual event only, loads it into the form, which then saves it by id in an upsert item.

delete_ids (upsert items only) lists events of the item's asset to delete, manual or from a provider: a provider's event comes back at the provider's next sync. _delete_item_events() runs first in _write_manual_item(), right after the asset lookup and before every other check, and flushes: an edit of the item may then take the (date, type) of an event the item deletes. Every id must be an event of the item's asset (EVENT_NOT_DELETABLE), and none may be linked to a transaction (EVENT_IN_USE). An item may only delete, with no events. The data editor saves its Events tab this way, in one request: the rows marked deleted in delete_ids, the edited and new rows in events.

In both modes, an event in a currency other than the asset's is refused (EVENT_CURRENCY_MISMATCH), and so is a value with more than 12 digits before the decimal point, 6 decimal places or 15 significant digits, or one that is not finite, which is never rounded (EVENT_TOO_MANY_DIGITS, C-97; the digits before the point since W-B58). So is a SPLIT whose ratio, its value, is not a number above 0 (EVENT_INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO, X-R47), however it is written: added, matched on its date and type, or edited by id, including an edit that turns another type into a SPLIT. Until X-R47 such a split was stored, and as soon as a transaction linked it the portfolio engine raised (financial_math/portfolio/engine.py): the Dashboard report answered 500. Since lot MF-D4 a split stored that way counts as missing. Only its ratio is dropped: the linked ADJUSTMENT rows stay the split's rescale, with their cost kept. No trade price before the split is restated by that ratio, the FIFO lots skip it, and the Dashboard names the asset in an INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO warning (see DataQualityBanner). The user fixes the ratio here.

Each result carries event_ids: the id of the event each point of the item wrote, in request order. An edit keeps its id, an event matched on its date and type gets the id of the row it updated, and an added event the id of its new row. deleted_ids lists the ids of delete_ids, all deleted, in request order; success_count also counts an item that only deletes.

A provider's event never meets these refusals: _upsert_asset_events(), which a sync calls, first drops every event whose value asset_events.value cannot hold — not finite, or past 12 digits before the decimal point (_storable_events(), storable_value()) — and writes each of the others as the column keeps it: truncated (ROUND_DOWN) to 6 decimals, then to 15 significant digits, like a provider's price, and only when that changes it, so a value that fits keeps its form (W-B68: written whole, a value read back rounded, 784.0774475 as 784.077448, so what was read differed from what was written). Among those, it drops every SPLIT whose ratio, as truncated, is not above 0 (is_valid_split_ratio(), X-R47; a ratio of 1E-7 truncates to 0), then writes the rest (W-B58: a value past a double's range, stored as a REAL inf, broke every response of the asset's events, for every user). A raw event the event schema itself refuses — a value that is no number, or whose exponent is past ±100 (check_decimal_exponent(), R13-SEC7-3) — is dropped the same way, one event at a time: parsed in one go, it made the sync lose every event it fetched. A dropped event is only logged, as a warning: the sync result does not report it, and its events_fetched still counts it. A call logs at most one warning per reason, Events skipped: no event value can keep them for the values and Splits skipped: a split's ratio must be a number above 0 for the splits, each with asset_id, count and the first five dropped (events); an event the schema refused is listed by its date and type only, as (refused by the schema), never with its value, which can be of any length.

Every refusal below stops the whole request:

Refused Answer A type that, trimmed and upper-cased, is not one of the five event types HTTP 422, from FAAssetEventPoint.normalize_type() The same id twice in one item HTTP 422 Duplicate event id in one upsert item, from the FAEventUpsert validator An id in a create item HTTP 422 A create item cannot name an event id, from the FAEventUpsert validator delete_ids in a create item HTTP 422 A create item cannot delete events, from the FAEventUpsert validator The same id twice in delete_ids HTTP 422 Duplicate id in delete_ids, from the FAEventUpsert validator An id both in delete_ids and on an event of the same item HTTP 422 An event cannot be deleted and edited in one item, from the FAEventUpsert validator An item with neither events nor delete_ids HTTP 422 An upsert item needs at least one event or one id to delete, from the FAEventUpsert validator An item whose asset does not exist HTTP 400 EVENT_ASSET_NOT_FOUND (until 1.3, a 200 whose result had count 0) An id of delete_ids that is not an event of the item's asset: unknown, already gone, or another asset's HTTP 400 EVENT_NOT_DELETABLE; params.ids: those ids An id of delete_ids whose event a transaction is linked to HTTP 409 EVENT_IN_USE; params.events: one {id, date, type, linked_transactions} per such event, ordered by date, type and id. Counts only, no transaction id: the transactions may belong to other users An event in a currency other than the asset's HTTP 400 EVENT_CURRENCY_MISMATCH; params: expected (the asset's currency) and events, one {event_index, date, type, currency} per such event of the item An event whose value has more than 12 digits before the decimal point, more than 6 decimal places or more than 15 significant digits, trailing zeros not counted, or is not finite (_reject_too_many_digits(), the limits of asset_events.value) HTTP 400 EVENT_TOO_MANY_DIGITS; params: max_integer_digits (12), max_decimal_places (6), max_significant_digits (15) and events, one {event_index, date, type} per such event of the item A SPLIT whose ratio, its value, is not a number above 0: new, matched on its date and type, or edited by id, another type the edit turns into a SPLIT included (_reject_invalid_split_ratios(); the rule is is_valid_split_ratio() of financial_math/splits.py, the portfolio engine's own) HTTP 400 EVENT_INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO; params.events: one {event_index, date, type, ratio} per such split of the item, in request order, type always SPLIT and ratio the value sent, as a string. A value that is not finite or has too many digits is refused first, with EVENT_TOO_MANY_DIGITS An id that is unknown, belongs to another asset, or names a provider event HTTP 400 EVENT_NOT_EDITABLE; params.ids: those ids An edit that changes its date or type (a mover) landing on a key another edit of the item ends on, or on a key held by a manual row the item does not edit HTTP 400 EVENT_KEY_CONFLICT; params: the date and type of the key An event without id on a key an edit of the item ends on HTTP 400 EVENT_KEY_CONFLICT; params: date and type An edit that changes the type of a SPLIT while a linked incoming ADJUSTMENT (quantity above 0) has no cost_basis_override (_reject_split_retype_without_costs(); costless_incoming_split_adjustments() of financial_math/splits.py finds those rows). Without the split, such a row would be an acquisition of unknown cost: the rule of P-10 (decision 27). An edit that keeps the type, or an outgoing row, is never refused HTTP 409 EVENT_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST; params: the first such edit in request order, event_id, date (the stored event's), transaction_ids (sorted, only the transactions the caller can see: a BrokerUserAccess row for their broker) and hidden_transactions_count (the others). The message names no transaction, only their count In a create item, an event on a (date, type) the asset already has, manual or from a provider HTTP 409 EVENT_EXISTS; params.existing: the stored events on every such key of the item, ordered by date, type and id, each {id, date, type, value: {code, amount}, notes, is_auto, linked_transactions}, the last one the number of transactions linked to the event

A 400 or a 409 answers detail = {error_code, message, params} (_REFUSAL_STATUS in api/v1/assets/events.py): message is the English text, which starts with the code, and params always holds item_index (the item's position in the request, from 0) and asset_id, plus the fields above. Any other AssetSourceError stays a 500 with a string detail. A 422 is FastAPI's validation error: nothing has run, and its loc points at the item, or at the event for a type. _split_manual_events() also raises EVENT_KEY_CONFLICT, with params.ids, for an id repeated in one item: over HTTP the 422 comes first, so only a caller that skips the schema meets it.

Allowed: two edits swapping their keys, edits that keep a shared key (legacy duplicates stay editable), an event without id on a key a mover vacates, and an edit landing on the key of an event the item deletes: that deletion is flushed before the checks run. These checks only cover keys an edit ends on: in an upsert item, an event without id on the key of a manual row the item does not edit updates that row, and two events without id on one key are both stored.

A type change is allowed even when a transaction is linked to the event: the link stays, and the transaction is then read according to the new type. compute_wac_iterative() (portfolio_service.py) counts an ADJUSTMENT as split-linked only while its event is a SPLIT: the type is joined live, and the split-linked set is part of the WAC cache fingerprint. Once the event is retyped to PRICE_ADJUSTMENT, a +qty adjustment becomes an acquisition at its cost basis and a −qty one a plain reduction that takes its share of the cost away (in the test, the total cost halves from 1,500 to 750). A +qty adjustment without a cost basis (the Auto mode stores none on a split-linked row) would become an acquisition of unknown cost (MISSING_COST_BASIS): that retype is refused, EVENT_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST above (P-10). The forward case, refused and then accepted once the adjustment has a cost (40 a share: WAC 70), is pinned by test_forward_split_whose_adjustment_has_no_cost_is_retyped_only_once_the_adjustment_has_one, the reverse one by test_reverse_split_relabelled_as_price_adjustment_becomes_a_reduction, both in test_scripts/test_api/test_lots_wac_history.py.

Manual events are never deleted by the sync process. They survive provider re-syncs, provider changes, and bulk refreshes. Only an explicit user deletion removes them, or the market-data wipe of a currency change, which deletes every event of the asset except the SPLITs, manual ones included (Market-Data Wipe). A user deletes events through delete_ids of POST /api/v1/assets/events, the data editor's save: all or nothing, so an event a transaction uses stops the whole request (EVENT_IN_USE). The request is scoped to one asset (decision 21 of release 1.3): an id of another asset in delete_ids is EVENT_NOT_DELETABLE. The separate DELETE /api/v1/assets/events route, which deleted per id and committed the deletable ones even when others were blocked, was removed.

docs.title: 🧹 Market-Data Wipe
docs.text:
Changing an asset's currency deletes its market data, because prices and events are stored in the old currency: mixing them with new-currency rows would be worse than starting again. Since N68 (lot X5-3, decided by the developer on 19/10/2026) the change is never refused; policy D is now «the splits stay». The rule lives in assets/currency_change.py:

Function Role events_that_go() The condition of the events a currency change deletes: every event of the assets except SPLIT. A dividend or an interest carries a currency; a split is a ratio, it means the same in any currency, and the ADJUSTMENTs linked to it keep their meaning delete_market_data_of_assets() Three statements whatever the number of assets, no commit: UPDATE transactions SET asset_event_id = NULL for the transactions linked to an event that goes, DELETE of those events, DELETE of the assets' prices provider_cache_keys() / drop_provider_caches() The cache keys of the assets' provider assignments, read before the commit (it expires the rows' attributes), and the drop of their history and current-price entries after it. A cache that fails to drop is logged and skipped: the data is already committed CurrencyChangeOperations.wipe_market_data_for_currency_change() The counters and the same deletion for one asset, behind the currency PATCH and the summary dry run

What goes and what stays:

Row After a currency change Every price of the asset Deleted Every manual event that is not a SPLIT Deleted Every event generated by the provider that is not a SPLIT Deleted The transactions linked to a deleted event Kept, with asset_event_id set to NULL (the FK is RESTRICT, so the UPDATE comes first) Every SPLIT event, manual or from a provider Kept The transactions linked to a SPLIT Kept, still linked: the adjustments of the split keep their link and their cost basis

Where it happens:

  • PATCH /api/v1/assets (AssetCRUDService.patch_assets_bulk()). It remembers the currency of every patched asset before the loop; after the loop, for the assets whose currency now differs, it reads the cache keys, calls delete_market_data_of_assets(), and commits once, so the change and the deletion are one transaction. Then it drops the caches. There is no blocker token any more: CURRENCY_CHANGE_BLOCKED_BY_MARKET_DATA is gone from the per-item message and from the route, which no longer answers 409 when every item failed. The deletion follows the result (the stored currency changed), so it runs for any caller of the API, not only the interface.
  • GET /api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/market-data/summary, the dry run, counts without writing. It answers {prices, events_manual, events_provider, splits_kept, linked_tx, oldest, newest, dry_run}: events_manual and events_provider count the events that go, SPLITs not included; splits_kept counts the SPLIT events that stay; linked_tx counts the transactions linked to the events that go; oldest and newest are the price range (ISO dates, null without prices).

The currency PATCH is the only caller that wipes: there is no stand-alone wipe route (the former POST /api/v1/assets/{asset_id}/market-data/wipe was removed). It never answers 409: the refusal for costless split adjustments (X-R48, MARKET_DATA_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST) was removed together with the reason for it, because the splits are no longer deleted. The summary's 404 ASSET_NOT_FOUND (string detail) for an unknown asset is the only answer other than 200 and the generic 500.

The refusal that remains is the provider's

The rule of P-10 (a SPLIT deleted under linked incoming ADJUSTMENTs without a cost would turn them into acquisitions of unknown cost) is still enforced where a split can be deleted: the retype of a split (EVENT_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST, above) and the changes of provider below (PROVIDER_WIPE_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST, X-R49). assets/split_guard.py serves those, not the currency change.

The transactions that lost their link can be linked again: GET /api/v1/transactions/event-reconciliation proposes the event of the same day for each, and the user confirms (see Event Reconciliation). Nothing relinks by itself.

In the asset form (AssetModal.svelte, in frontend/src/lib/components/assets/) the flow is:

sequenceDiagram
    actor U as User
    participant M as AssetModal (saveEdit)
    participant C as AssetCurrencyChangeModal
    participant API as Backend

    U->>M: Save Changes with a new currency
    M->>API: GET /assets/{id}/market-data/summary (dry run)
    alt the dry run fails
        API-->>M: error
        M-->>U: error banner, nothing is sent
    else nothing would be lost
        M->>API: PATCH /assets
        API-->>M: 200, currency changed
    else prices, events or links would be lost
        M->>C: open with the counts
        U->>C: optional backup (CSV / JSON)
        U->>C: Delete & change currency
        C->>API: PATCH /assets (one call)
        API-->>C: 200, currency changed and data deleted
        opt a provider is assigned and there were prices
            C->>API: POST /assets/prices/sync (oldest price date to today)
        end
        C-->>U: toasts, the modal closes
    end

saveEdit() asks the dry run first through loadCurrencyChangeImpact() (currencyImpact.ts) whenever the form's currency differs from the stored one. The dry run is a gate: when it fails the save fails and nothing is sent, because the PATCH deletes without any other check. hasSomethingToLose() decides whether to ask: prices, events or linked transactions above zero; the kept splits alone are information, not a loss, and the PATCH then goes on its own. The confirmation (AssetCurrencyChangeModal.svelte, props impact, patchPayload, providerAssigned) lists the price points with their date range, the manual events, the events generated by the provider, the transactions that lose their link to a deleted event and the split events that stay, and offers the backups (prices and events, CSV or JSON). The wording is shared with the provider-change dialog: «price points», «events generated by the provider», «lose their link to a deleted event». The sync after the PATCH runs only if the asset has a provider assignment and the dry run found prices (its start is the oldest deleted price); a failed sync is only an error toast: the change is already made. currencyBlocker.ts and the 409 handling of the old flow are deleted.

Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_market_data_wipe_keeps_splits.py (./dev.py test services market-data-wipe-keeps-splits), test_asset_currency_change.py; in the frontend currencyImpact.test.ts, AssetModal.currencyChange.test.ts and AssetCurrencyChangeModal.test.ts, in the same folder, and e2e/assets/asset-currency-change.spec.ts.

docs.title: 🔁 Parametric Provider Change
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/assets/provider (assign_providers_bulk() in api/v1/assets/providers.py, bulk_assign_providers() in assets/provider_management.py) saves its items in order and commits once, after the last. For an asset that already has an assignment, an item that gives a parametric provider (FAProviderKind.PARAMETRIC_GENERATION: today only Scheduled Investment) new provider_params, or moves the asset away from one, wipes the asset's market data (#R3-4, #R6-4): every price of the asset, manual ones included, and every event of the assignment (provider_assignment_id its id), after unlinking their transactions (asset_event_id = NULL), then the cache entries of the old parameters. Manual events (provider_assignment_id IS NULL) survive, and new parameters of an online provider wipe nothing. _wipe_reason() decides, one answer for the write loop and for the check below: "params changed", "provider changed", or "" for no wipe. The dry run POST /assets/provider/impact counts what such an item would delete before it is sent.

Among those events can be a SPLIT. The plan editor (ScheduledInvestmentEditor.svelte) offers only Interest, Price Adjustment and Maturity Settlement events, but the schema (FAScheduledInvestmentSchedule.asset_events) accepts a SPLIT, so a plan's split comes through the API; the sync stores it under the assignment, as the plan's other events. Its linked incoming ADJUSTMENTs (quantity above 0) without a cost_basis_override (a cost of 0 is a cost) would be acquisitions of unknown cost once the wipe deletes it: the rule of P-10, enforced here and in the retype of a split, but no longer in the currency change, which keeps the splits. Before the request's first write, _reject_wipes_of_costless_split_adjustments() follows the items in order, as the write loop does (an asset named twice is compared with its previous item), and for each item that would wipe reads the events of that assignment and passes them to split_guard.splits_with_costless_adjustments(). Manual events are not read: they survive the wipe. When a SPLIT among them has such adjustments, the whole request is refused and nothing of it is written, the items before the refused one included. The route answers HTTP 409 with detail = {error_code, message, params}:

  • error_code: PROVIDER_WIPE_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST;
  • params.asset_id and params.item_index: the refused item's asset and its position in the request, from 0;
  • params.splits: one {event_id, date, transaction_ids, hidden_transactions_count} per such split, ordered by date, then id; transaction_ids lists, sorted, only the adjustments the caller can see (a BrokerUserAccess row for the transaction's broker), and hidden_transactions_count counts the others. The route passes current_user_id=_current_user.id; the service called without current_user_id names none and counts them all;
  • message: the English text, which starts with the code and gives only the totals, how many splits and how many adjustments.

Any other error of the endpoint keeps its answer, a 500 with a string detail.

In the asset form (AssetModal.svelte, in frontend/src/lib/components/assets/), saveEdit() first PATCHes the asset's fields (step 1), then assigns the provider (step 2). A step-2 refusal with this code is shown inline, in the form's error banner (formError, data-form-error): one sentence in the interface language built by wipeRefusalMessage() (currencyChangeErrors.ts, which maps each code to its key: PROVIDER_WIPE_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST to assets.modal.planSplitAdjustmentsWithoutCost, PROVIDER_REMOVAL_CONFLICT to assets.modal.providerRemovalConflict; the currency change's own code is unknown to it since N68): the first split's date, its adjustments without a cost, the hidden ones among them, and how many more splits have some. Then it stops: no toast, no automatic sync, the form stays open, and the next save asks its confirmation again. What step 1 saved stays saved: only the provider and its parameters are unchanged, as the sentence says. The catch sits in saveEdit() itself, so the sentence is the same on every way in: after the impact confirmation (new parameters or another provider) and on the plain save, where doSave() would read the 409 as a duplicate name. Any other error keeps its handling.

Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_provider_wipe_split_guard.py (./dev.py test services provider-wipe-split-guard); in the frontend, currencyChangeErrors.test.ts and AssetModal.providerLifecycle.test.ts, in the same folder.

docs.title: 🗑️ Provider Removal
docs.text:
DELETE /api/v1/assets/provider?asset_ids=… (remove_providers_bulk() in api/v1/assets/providers.py, bulk_remove_providers() in assets/provider_management.py), which the asset form's No Provider calls, deletes the assignments of the listed assets in one DELETE, then commits. asset_events.provider_assignment_id is ON DELETE CASCADE (db/models.py), so the events each assignment generated go with it, whatever their type: a market provider's dividends and splits, a Scheduled Investment plan's coupons (INTEREST events). Manual events (provider_assignment_id IS NULL) stay, with their links, and so do the prices: the removal never touches prices, unlike a parametric change.

transactions.asset_event_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT. Until X-R62 the DELETE therefore failed with an IntegrityError as soon as a transaction was linked to a generated event (HTTP 500 with the SQL text), X-R62 replaced that with a 409 that asked the user to unlink the transactions first, and X5-1 replaced the 409: the removal now does what a change of provider has always done (Policy D). In the same transaction as the DELETE, bulk_remove_providers() sets transactions.asset_event_id to NULL for every transaction linked to an event of the removed assignments (_unlink_transactions_of(), one UPDATE), whoever owns the broker, and only then deletes the assignments. The transactions are kept; only the link is lost. Every asset of the request is answered a success (deleted_count 1), one without an assignment included.

The one refusal left is the rule of X-R49, here for the removal too. Before the request's only write, _reject_removals_of_costless_splits() follows asset_ids in order (an asset named twice is read once, at its first position; an asset without an assignment is skipped), reads the events of the asset's assignment (_assignment_event_rows()) and passes them to split_guard.splits_with_costless_adjustments(), as the parametric change does. With the generated SPLIT gone, its linked incoming adjustments without a purchase cost would be acquisitions of unknown cost, so when such a split exists the whole request is refused and nothing of it is removed, the assets before the refused one included. The route answers HTTP 409 with detail = {error_code, message, params}:

  • error_code: PROVIDER_WIPE_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST, the code of the change, not a code of its own;
  • params.asset_id and params.item_index: the refused asset and its first position in asset_ids, from 0;
  • params.splits: one {event_id, date, transaction_ids, hidden_transactions_count} per such split, as in the parametric change: transaction_ids lists, sorted, only the adjustments the caller can see (a BrokerUserAccess row for the transaction's broker), and hidden_transactions_count counts the others. The route passes current_user_id=_current_user.id; the service called without it names none and counts them all;
  • message: the English text, which starts with the code and gives only the totals, how many splits and how many adjustments.

The check, the unlinking and the DELETE are separate statements, so a transaction linked to one of those events after the service read their ids can still make the DELETE fail. bulk_remove_providers() then rolls the session back, logs a server-side warning and raises PROVIDER_REMOVAL_CONFLICT, which the route also answers HTTP 409, with empty params and a message without SQL: nothing was removed. Any other error of the service keeps its answer, a 500 with a string detail.

History: X-R62 is gone

PROVIDER_REMOVAL_LINKED_TRANSACTIONS (X-R62: a removal refused while any transaction was linked to a generated event) is no longer raised and has no sentence in the frontend catalogue; a client that still handles it can drop the branch.

In the asset form (AssetModal.svelte, in frontend/src/lib/components/assets/), saveEdit() removes the provider in step 2, the providerNoProvider branch, once step 1 has PATCHed the asset's fields. Before step 1 it asks the dry run what the removal deletes and, when something goes, shows one confirmation (below). Its catch mirrors the assign branch's, just below it (X-R49): a refusal with either code is shown inline, in the form's error banner (formError, data-form-error), one sentence in the interface language built by wipeRefusalMessage() (currencyChangeErrors.ts):

  • PROVIDER_WIPE_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST maps to assets.modal.planSplitAdjustmentsWithoutCost (read from params.splits, as for a change; its sentence says the provider was not changed or removed);
  • PROVIDER_REMOVAL_CONFLICT maps to assets.modal.providerRemovalConflict, which takes no values and names nothing: the provider was not removed, some data still refers to the events it generated; reload the page and try again.

Then the save stops there: pendingSaveAssetId is reset and the banner scrolled into view; no toast is shown, and the form stays open on the draft, still set to No Provider, so the save can be tried again. What step 1 saved stays saved: only the provider is unchanged. Without the catch, doSave() would read the 409 as a duplicate name. Any other error is thrown on and keeps its handling (trySave()).

Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_provider_removal_link_guard.py (./dev.py test services provider-removal-link-guard); in the frontend, currencyChangeErrors.test.ts and AssetModal.providerLifecycle.test.ts, in the same folder.

docs.title: 🔎 Provider Change Impact (Dry Run)
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/assets/provider/impact (provider_change_impact() in api/v1/assets/providers.py, AssetSourceManager.provider_change_impact() in assets/provider_management.py) tells, before anything is done, what the change or the removal would delete. It writes nothing and needs a signed-in user (the caller's view decides which transactions are named, as in the refusals). The body is FAProviderImpactRequest (schemas/provider.py): assignments, the items POST /assets/provider takes (FAProviderAssignmentItem), and removals, the asset ids DELETE /assets/provider takes; both default to an empty list, and unknown keys are a 422. The answer holds one FAProviderImpactResult per assignment, then one per removal, in the order of the request:

Field Meaning asset_id, action The asset, and assign or remove reason none: nothing is lost (a change between market providers, the same provider and parameters, an asset without an assignment). params_changed: a parametric provider with new parameters. provider_changed: the asset leaves a parametric provider. provider_removed: a removal of an existing assignment prices_deleted Every price of the asset for params_changed and provider_changed (manual ones included); always 0 for a removal, which keeps the prices events_deleted The events the stored assignment generated; manual events are not counted transactions_unlinked The transactions linked to those events, in total: the ones on brokers the caller cannot see are counted too, and none is ever named blocking_splits The SPLITs among those events with linked incoming adjustments without a purchase cost, as the refusals name them (event_id, date, transaction_ids, hidden_transactions_count). Not empty: the real operation is refused

The rule is the same as the operations': _wipe_reason() decides reason for an assignment, as it decides the write loop's wipe, and a removal measures the events of the assignment it would delete. reason follows the items in order, as the write does (an asset named twice is compared with its previous item), while the counts are always read from what is stored now. A removal of an asset without an assignment answers none with zeros.

Parity rule. The dry run's numbers are what the operation then does: the prices, events and transactions it counts are the ones the real change or removal deletes and unlinks, and a non-empty blocking_splits is the 409 the real call answers. A new way for either operation to delete or unlink something must change both together; test_parity_the_dry_runs_numbers_are_what_the_operation_then_does and test_parity_a_blocking_split_is_the_refusal_the_operation_answers in backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_provider_change_impact.py pin it (./dev.py test services provider-change-impact).

The asset form (AssetModal.svelte) is the only client. saveEdit() asks it through loadProviderImpact() of providerImpact.ts, for an existing asset that had a provider when the modal opened, in two cases: the user chose No Provider (one removal), or kept a provider whose code or parameters changed (one assignment). loadProviderImpact() is advice, never a gate. It returns nothing, and the save goes on without a dialog, when the request fails (a warning in the console), when reason is none, when every count is 0, or when blocking_splits is not empty: the real call is then made and refused, and the refusal is shown inline as above. Otherwise saveEdit() opens one ConfirmModal that states the server's counts: the prices and the provider events that go (impactValues()), and how many transactions lose their link (they are kept). The reason picks the dialog (IMPACT_DIALOG): params_changed the regenerate dialog, provider_changed the switch one, provider_removed the removal one, each with its own data-testid (asset-scheduled-regen-confirm, asset-parametric-switch-confirm, asset-provider-remove-confirm). Confirming re-enters saveEdit() with pendingSaveAssetId set, which skips the question; cancelling resets it and saves nothing. This one dialog replaced the two older ones (regenerate on new parameters, and discard-the-series on leaving a parametric provider), whose counts came from the market-data summary; the keys live under assets.modal.providerImpact.*.

Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_provider_change_impact.py; in the frontend, providerImpact.test.ts and AssetModal.providerLifecycle.test.ts, in the same folder.

docs.title: 📈 Yahoo Finance: Dividends & Splits
docs.text:
During sync, the Yahoo Finance provider generates:

  • DIVIDEND events from ticker.dividends — ex-dividend dates with the per-share payout value and currency.
  • SPLIT events from ticker.splits — split dates with the split ratio as the event value (e.g., 4.0 for a 4:1 split).

Both are written by the standard _upsert_asset_events() pipeline, scoped by provider_assignment_id.

Their dates are the exchange's own day, as the prices' (_normalize_yahoo_date()). An event an older version stored a day early stays, so a sync that fetches it again stores a second one on its day (Dates on the Exchange's Own Day).

docs.title: 🔍 JustETF: Dividends from Chart Data
docs.text: During sync, the JustETF provider parses dividend data from load_chart() response. Distribution dates and amounts are extracted and stored as DIVIDEND events.

docs.title: 📊 Scheduled Investment: generate_interest
docs.text:
When a schedule period has generate_interest = True, the Scheduled Investment provider auto-generates:

  1. INTEREST events at each maturation date within the period
  2. After each INTEREST event, accrued interest resets: total_interest = 0, event_adjustment = 0 → value returns to initial_value

The maturation frequency is controlled by maturation_frequency on each interest rate period (DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, SEMIANNUAL, ANNUAL).

The events entered in the schedule itself (asset_events in the provider parameters, Add Event in the asset form) travel the same way: get_history_value() returns them with the generated ones, so the sync stores them under the assignment and the data editor shows them read-only.

docs.title: 🏁 MATURITY_SETTLEMENT
docs.text:
Auto-generated when:

  • The schedule ends and generate_interest = True on the last period
  • Or late interest is configured with generate_interest = True

After settlement, the engine is "off" — get_current_value() returns the settlement value for all future dates.

docs.title: 📐 Event Impact on Pricing
docs.text:
The Scheduled Investment engine's pricing formula incorporates events:

price(d) = initial_value + accrued_interest - Σ(INTEREST events) + Σ(PRICE_ADJUSTMENT events)
  • Interest is always calculated on initial_value (not running value)
  • INTEREST events subtract from the running price (coupon paid out)
  • PRICE_ADJUSTMENT events are algebraic (can add or subtract)
  • After MATURITY_SETTLEMENT, no further calculations occur

docs.title: 🇮🇹 Borsa Italiana Provider (borsa_italiana)
docs.text: The Borsa Italiana provider fetches financial data from borsaitaliana.it using the borsa-italiana-scraping library. It supports stocks, bonds (including BTP), ETFs listed on Borsa Italiana markets (MTA, MOT, ETFPlus), and funds/SICAVs exposed on Borsa fund-detail pages.

docs.title: ⚙️ How it Works
docs.text:
1. Identifier: An ISIN code (e.g., IT0003128367 for ENEL S.p.A.) for listed instruments.
  2. Identifier Types: ISIN for listed instruments. Mutual funds are priced by a Borsa internal code carried in provider_params.codice_fondo (see Mutual funds below); the asset identifier is still the real ISIN when the fund page exposes one, otherwise an OTHER identifier is used.
  3. provider_params:
    • language — optional ("en" or "it", default "en"). Controls the language of asset names, metadata descriptions, and the provider URL.
    • codice_fondo — optional Borsa internal fund code (e.g. 2FADB602822). When present, current/historical value use the fund NAV path instead of the market API.
    • mic — optional market MIC (e.g. ETLX for EuroTLX, MOTX for MOT). Auto-filled from the search result's own link; routes the instrument page (get_asset_url) and metadata to the right market.
    • platform — optional trading platform (e.g. TLX for EuroTLX). Required by some markets so the universal search/scheda.html URL redirects to the real market page.
    • url — not a form field (absent from params_schema): set automatically to the instrument's own page address — the site's search link, or the page resolve_url actually loaded (scheda.url_pagina). get_asset_url and metadata prefer it, so a EuroTLX link keeps working even when platform is missing (e.g. an asset created while the site search had the ISIN de-indexed).

docs.title: 🧭 Market routing (mic / platform)
docs.text:
Borsa Italiana lists the same instrument families across several markets (MTA, MOT, ExtraMOT, ETFplus, SeDeX, MIV, EuroTLX, GEM). Most resolve through the universal search/scheda.html?code={ISIN} URL, but EuroTLX does not — it requires mic=ETLX&platform=TLX or the URL stays on a dead generic page. The provider takes mic/platform from the site's own search link (never a hardcoded map), stores them in provider_params, and reuses them everywhere:

  • Search results carry provider_params: {language, mic, platform?, url} (url = the site's own link) — so the URL and pricing are correct by construction for any market, present or future.
  • Dead-result filter: a non-fund result with no parseable mic in its link is skipped (never emit a result whose URL would be the unresolved /search/ page). Indices (Indice/Index) are excluded — they are benchmarks, not purchasable instruments.
  • History auto-discovery (library ≥ 0.3.0): the chart API only knows XMIL/ETLX; if an ISIN is unknown to XMIL and no exchange is passed, the library discovers the MIC via the site search and retries. This self-heals legacy assets saved before mic was propagated.
  • UNSUPPORTED_PAGE: when even mic/platform can't resolve a parseable market page (a family we don't handle yet), the provider raises UNSUPPORTED_PAGE with a message inviting the user to open a GitHub issue — instead of a cryptic parse error.

docs.title: 💱 Currency
docs.text:
A listed instrument is priced in its trading currency on Borsa Italiana: EUR for most listings, but e.g. USD for FX-denominated EuroTLX bonds such as the US Treasury US912810TU25. One source serves both sides: the metadata currency is the currency the prices carry.

  • Prices (get_current_value, get_history_value): the currency of the grafici.borsaitaliana.it chart-API reply (ottieni_prezzo_corrente / ottieni_storico), EUR when the reply carries none. History goes through _storico_con_mic_retry: default route first, then, on StrumentoNonTrovato, the stored mic as the chart-API exchange.
  • Metadata and resolve_url (listed instruments): the currency is not read from the scheda page. ETF/ETC scheda pages often show only the fund's denomination currency («Valuta di Denominazione USD»), while the instrument trades — and is priced — in EUR; read off the scheda, it gave USD metadata over EUR prices (e.g. Invesco Physical Gold ETC IE00B579F325, iShares Core MSCI World IE00B4L5Y983, iShares Core S&P 500 IE00B5BMR087). The module helper _price_api_currency(identifier, mic) asks the chart API instead: the same _storico_con_mic_retry call, the same EUR default.
  • Currency unknown: when that chart-API call fails (any exception), fetch_asset_metadata leaves currency unset in the returned FAAssetPatchItem (patch contract: present, even if None → update/blank; absent → keep), so a metadata refresh keeps the stored asset currency instead of blanking it. resolve_url rows carry currency: None.
  • Search: rows for listed instruments carry currency: None — the cerca payload has no currency; the metadata fetch fills it.
  • Funds (codice_fondo): unchanged — the currency comes from the fund page (DatiFondo.valuta, default EUR).

Note (library ≥ 0.3.2): the scheda parser no longer takes the denomination row for the trading currency — «Valuta» / «Currency» match only as an exact label — and exposes the denomination separately as SchedaStrumento.valuta_denominazione, which the plugin does not use. The fix still matters for current prices: ottieni_prezzo_corrente falls back to scraping the scheda when its chart-API read fails.

docs.title: 💰 Current Value (get_current_value)
docs.text:
• Funds (when provider_params.codice_fondo is set): returns the fund NAV only if the published NAV is dated today. A fund NAV is published once per day with a lag, so exposing a stale NAV as the "current" value would misstate the portfolio. When the NAV date ≠ today, the provider raises NO_DATA: no price is stored for today, and valuation carries the latest observation forward through the unified price resolver (backend/app/services/financial_math/price_marks.py) — the last NAV point, or a more recent trade-derived mark (LAST_TRADE_PRICE). There is no separate last-buy fallback.
  • Listed instruments: uses ottieni_prezzo_corrente(isin, mic=…, platform=…) from the scraping library. If it raises StrumentoNonRisolto / StrumentoNonTrovato and a mic is stored, it retries once with exchange=mic (EuroTLX answers under its own exchange code, equal to the MIC).
  • Returns FACurrentValue with price, date, currency, and source ("Borsa Italiana").

docs.title: 📈 Historical Data (get_history_value)
docs.text:
• Funds (when provider_params.codice_fondo is set): the fund page exposes only the latest NAV (no series), dated to the day it actually refers to (never today). The provider returns a single price point at that real NAV date; the core backward-fills the gaps up to the requested range. Out-of-range NAV dates yield no points.
  • Listed instruments: uses ottieni_storico(isin, periodo) from the grafici.borsaitaliana.it JSON API.
    • Returns full OHLCV data (open, high, low, close, volume) for each trading day.
    • Period selection: The API uses fixed windows (1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, MAX). The provider automatically selects the smallest period that covers the requested start_date..end_date range.
    • Results are filtered in-memory to the exact requested date range.
    • The core handles gap filling (weekends, holidays) — the plugin returns only actual trading days.

docs.title: 🧾 Mutual funds (NAV by internal code)
docs.text:
Mutual funds / SICAVs are not on the XMIL market API, so ottieni_storico / ottieni_prezzo_corrente cannot price them. Their only public NAV source is the fund detail page /borsa/fondi/dettaglio/{code}.html, addressed by a Borsa internal code (2FADB…) that is not the ISIN. The scraping library exposes:

  • ottieni_dati_fondo(codice, sessione) — fetch NAV, currency, NAV date (dd/mm/yy), name, and the real ISIN extracted from the page (DatiFondo). DatiFondo also carries the descriptive sections scraped from the page — caratteristiche, societa_gestione, costi (each a label → value dict, N.D. placeholders dropped) — consumed by fetch_asset_metadata to enrich the fund description.
  • ottieni_dati_fondo_da_url(url, sessione) / estrai_codice_da_url(url) — the URL variant used by resolve_url.

The provider captures the internal code into provider_params.codice_fondo at asset creation (from search or resolve_url); pricing afterwards uses that stored code with no external search. Price fetches never hit any web search — that invariant is what keeps automated syncs deterministic.

docs.title: 🔎 Search (search)
docs.text:
• Uses cerca(query) — the internal JSON search engine of borsaitaliana.it.
  • Searches across all instrument types: stocks, bonds, ETFs, ETC/ETN, and funds.
  • Fund names are indexed with Borsa abbreviations (for example Obbligaz. instead of Obbligazionaria), so the provider retries common full-word variants with abbreviated terms.
  • Funds: cerca returns the Borsa internal code in the isin field (not a real ISIN). The provider fetches each fund page once per code (in-search cache) via ottieni_dati_fondo to recover the real ISIN, sets it as the identifier (ISIN), and carries the internal code in provider_params.codice_fondo. If the page can't be fetched or no ISIN is present, it falls back to the code as an OTHER identifier — still priceable by NAV.
  • Dual-language results: emits two entries per instrument (🇮🇹 Italiano + 🇬🇧 English) with flag emojis in display_name, or only the one of the user's preferred_language (it or en; all, the default, keeps both). Each result carries provider_params: {language: "en"|"it"} so the user's selection is propagated on assignment. The preference is the user's own setting (scope=user), read in _emitted_languages(), which search and resolve_url share: it chooses the rows emitted, never the language cerca is called in, the first of _languages_in_order(), Italian (Plugin Settings).
  • Result ordering: results are grouped by the cerca-level identifier (the internal code for funds, the real ISIN otherwise), preserving first-seen order, and within each group Italian is emitted before English. This keeps sibling funds — whose internal codes may differ by a single letter — from interleaving across languages. Grouping also de-duplicates per (identifier, language).
  • Last-resort external fallback: when cerca returns nothing, the search orchestration calls the LibreFolio web_link_finder stack to turn the query into a candidate Borsa page URL, then resolve_urls it. The caller can pass hints (report-extracted ISIN + names) which drive a two-stage "stringone" query and an identifier post-filter that narrows the resolved siblings to the exact ISIN when it is known — all handled centrally, see Asset Search & Link-Finder. Best-effort, interactive-only, never on price fetches.

docs.title: 📋 Metadata (fetch_asset_metadata)
docs.text:
• Listed instruments (ISIN path): uses ottieni_scheda(isin, lingua) — scrapes the instrument detail page in the configured language, routed by the stored mic/platform. If that raises StrumentoNonRisolto and provider_params.url is stored, the scheda is read straight from that page (url_diretto).
  • Extracts:
    • Name: from <h1> tag on the page, appended with language flag emoji (e.g., "ENEL S.p.A. 🇬🇧").
    • Type: mapped from instrument type field (e.g., obbligazione → BOND, azione → STOCK, etf → ETF). etc/etn also maps to ETF, so ETFs, ETCs and ETNs all arrive as plain ETF — the frontend provider-data comparison treats a stored ETF subtype (e.g. ETF_STOCK) as agreeing with it (isFamilyOnlyProposal in frontend/src/lib/utils/assetTypes.ts). Fund labels (fondi comuni, fondo chiuso, closed-end fund, …) → FUND; other obbligazione… / bond… labels fall back to BOND by prefix; unknown labels → no type.
    • Currency: from the chart API that prices the asset, not from the scheda; left unset when unknown — see Currency.
    • Description: assembled from page description, market, issuer, maturity date, coupon rate, structure, tipology, coupon frequency.
    • Ticker: if available on the page (mainly for stocks).
    • Geographic Area: inferred from issuer name via _ISSUER_TO_COUNTRY (exact match, then substring), e.g. "Republic of Italy" → ITA, "United States of America" → USA.
    • Sector: inferred from settore (stocks) or tipologia (bonds) fields. Bond tipologia goes through _TIPOLOGIA_TO_SECTOR (EN + IT labels): government paper → Government Bonds, corporate → Corporate Bonds, supranational → Financials; an unmapped tipologia yields no sector. The mapping only shapes the metadata offered: values already stored on an asset change only through the provider-data comparison.
  • Bond-specific fields available in the raw data: cedola_annua, scadenza, emittente, rendimento_lordo, struttura_bond, frequenza_cedola.
  • Funds (when provider_params.codice_fondo is set): funds are not on the XMIL scheda, so metadata is built from the fund detail page by internal code instead. The short_description is assembled from the fund name, the real ISIN, and the non-N.D. entries scraped from the page's Caratteristiche, Società di Gestione and Costi sections (e.g. … | ISIN: LU2178929613 | Classe: P | Grado di Rischio: 3 | Categoria Assogestioni: Bilanciati | Costi — Gestione: 1.3 …). The internal code is persisted in identifier_other as a JSON-list entry (["2FADB…"]). The section fields are read defensively, so metadata degrades to just name + ISIN if the installed scraping library predates the enriched DatiFondo.

docs.title: 🔗 get_asset_url
docs.text:
Precedence, first match wins:

  1. Funds with provider_params.codice_fondo → https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/fondi/dettaglio/{codice_fondo}.html?lang={language}, the NAV page keyed by the internal fund code (the generic scheda page does not resolve a fund by ISIN).
  2. A stored provider_params.url → that page, with lang={language} appended when it is missing. It is a working page by construction.
  3. Otherwise → https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/search/scheda.html?code={ISIN}&lang={language}, plus &mic={mic} and &platform={platform} when stored. Without them the bare URL still resolves for MTA, MOT, ETFplus, SeDeX and MIV, but not for EuroTLX.

The lang parameter follows the user's provider_params.language selection (default en).

docs.title: 🔁 resolve_url (inverse of get_asset_url)
docs.text:
The provider opts into the generic URL → search-item capability:

  • resolvable_url_domains = ["borsaitaliana.it"] → supports_url_resolution is True.
  • resolve_url(url) recognises two public page families:
    • Fund detail pages (/borsa/fondi/dettaglio/{code}.html) — fetches the page and returns the full canonical set a normal search would emit for that fund: the IT + EN pair (Italian first, with flag in display_name), or the row of the user's preferred language alone, each {identifier: <ISIN from page> or code, identifier_type, display_name, currency, type: "FUND", provider_params: {codice_fondo, language}}.
    • Stock / bond / ETF scheda pages (…/scheda/{ISIN}[-{MIC}].html) — returns the same canonical set, priced by ISIN. The rows' currency comes from one chart-API call shared by every row (None if it fails), not from the scheda.

It is only a different entry point — the orchestration flattens the list and de-dupes by (identifier, language). Anything that is not a recognisable Borsa page (off-domain, no extractable fund code or ISIN path) returns None. Best-effort: fetch/parse errors return None, never raise — except a refusal for too many requests, on the fund page, in the market-parameter search (cerca) or on the scheda page, which leaves as RATE_LIMITED so that the core pauses the provider. The search's link-finder, which calls resolve_url, then skips that URL without reporting an error. Only the rows' currency lookup still swallows a refusal (see Error Handling).

This lets an externally discovered page URL (e.g. found via web_link_finder, or pasted by the user in a future UI) be turned into a ready-to-create asset with the correct pricing params.

docs.title: 🌐 web_link_finder (last-resort external search)
docs.text:
Central reference

The link-finder is generic. This section keeps only the Borsa-Italiana-relevant summary — the full contract (three layers, hints, identifier filter, config, invariants) lives on Asset Search & Link-Finder, which is the source of truth.

backend/app/services/assets/web_link_finder.py is a LibreFolio-level module (deliberately not inside the scraping library, so the choice of external engine stays a LibreFolio concern). It turns a free-text query/ISIN into candidate provider-domain URLs, used only at search time as a last resort when a provider's on-site search yields nothing.

  • Best-effort: any failure (rate-limit, anomaly page, network/parse error) yields [] and is never fatal — the search always completes and emits done.
  • Async-safe: sync I/O runs in asyncio.to_thread; short timeout, small TTL cache, domain-filtered hits, structured logs.
  • Pluggable engine: default DdgsEngine wraps the ddgs metasearch library (bing/brave/google/DuckDuckGo/… aggregated via backend="auto") with an ApiKeyEngine seam for a paid API (Brave/Bing/SerpAPI) later; searxng reserved for a deferred Fase B.
  • Config: optional environment variables, read in backend/app/config/plugins.py; the full list (including LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_API_KEY_FILE for Docker secrets) is in Asset Search & Link-Finder.

Invariant

External search is only ever hit during interactive asset search. Price fetches (frequent, automated) must never call web_link_finder — once an asset exists it is priced by its stored provider_params (a fund's codice_fondo), not by search.

docs.title: HTTP Session
docs.text:
The provider maintains a shared Sessione instance across all calls:

  • WAF handling: The library manages Imperva WAF cookies automatically.
  • JWT token: Extracted from the interactive chart page (required for the grafici.borsaitaliana.it API).
  • Rate limiting: Built-in minimum pause between requests (0.5s default).
  • Shutdown: The session is closed via shutdown() at app teardown.

docs.title: params_schema (Dynamic UI Form)
docs.text:
The provider exposes optional parameters via params_schema:

Key Type Options Default Description language select en (🇬🇧 English), it (🇮🇹 Italiano) en Language for names and metadata codice_fondo string — — Borsa internal fund code (e.g. 2FADB602822); when set, current/history use the fund NAV path mic string — — Market MIC (auto-filled from search, e.g. ETLX for EuroTLX); routes the instrument page and metadata platform string — — Trading platform (auto-filled from search, e.g. TLX for EuroTLX); needed by some markets to resolve the page

Uses option_labels for human-readable display in the frontend dropdown. Each field also carries a short label — the form caption (Language, Fund internal code, Market MIC, Platform) — and a longer description shown as its tooltip; the frontend translates both under assets.providerParams.borsa_italiana.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Library Exception Mapped Error Code Meaning StrumentoNonRisolto UNSUPPORTED_PAGE Instrument found but its market page can't be resolved/read (unhandled market family) — user is invited to open a GitHub issue StrumentoNonTrovato NOT_FOUND ISIN not recognized DatiNonDisponibili NO_DATA No data available (market closed, delisted, or empty window for an illiquid instrument) RateLimitRaggiunto RATE_LIMITED HTTP 429 after the library's own retries, or HTTP 403 (the Imperva WAF blocked the session): _raise_if_rate_limited() raises AssetRateLimitedError, with no Retry-After, and the core pauses the provider (Provider Pauses) RicercaNonDisponibile FETCH_ERROR Search endpoint down BorsaItalianaErrore FETCH_ERROR Generic library error

RateLimitRaggiunto is recognised in current value, history, fund NAV, search, metadata (listed instruments and funds), where it used to read as "no metadata" (None), and the three lookups of resolve_url: the fund page, the market-parameter search and the scheda page. During a search, the link-finder skips a URL whose resolve_url was refused without reporting an error; the provider is paused all the same.

Two best-effort enrichments still swallow a refusal, on purpose: it pauses nothing, and the operation goes on as after any other failure there.

  • The fund-page lookup inside search() (ottieni_dati_fondo): the fund's rows fall back to its internal code, as an OTHER identifier.
  • The chart-API currency lookup (_price_api_currency()), in a listed instrument's metadata and in resolve_url's scheda rows: the currency stays unknown.

Known gap: the library sleeps in the provider's thread

On an HTTP 429 the library's Sessione retries by itself before raising RateLimitRaggiunto: three attempts, each followed by a time.sleep of 2, 4 and 8 s, 14 s in all in the provider's thread — against the rule of the Asset Plugin Guide. The library is a separate package (borsa-italiana-scraping, 0.3.2): the gap stays until it raises at the first 429. A 403 raises at once.

Note (library ≥ 0.3.0): an empty history window (e.g. an illiquid ExtraMOT bond over 1M) now maps to NO_DATA, never NOT_FOUND — the library distinguishes "unknown instrument" from "known but no trades in the window" via a MAX-period probe.

docs.title: 🌐 CSS Scraper Provider (css_scraper)
docs.text:
The CSS Scraper is a versatile provider that can extract a price from any public webpage using a CSS selector. It is one of the Asset Providers — it does not rely on a specific financial data API.

📖 User Guide: CSS Scraper — User Manual

docs.title: ⚙️ How it Works
docs.text:
1. Configuration: When assigning this provider to an asset, you must provide:

    • identifier: The URL of the webpage to scrape.
    • identifier_type: URL — the form's input type; it is stored as IdentifierType.OTHER (map_input_type_to_identifier_type), which is why test_cases use OTHER.
    • provider_params:
      • current_css_selector (required): The CSS selector to locate the price element on the page (e.g., #sp-last, .price-value).
      • currency (required): The currency of the price (ISO 4217).
      • decimal_format (optional): us (e.g., 1,234.56) or eu (e.g., 1.234,56). Default: us.
      • timeout (optional): HTTP request timeout in seconds. Default: 30.
      • user_agent (optional): Custom User-Agent header. Default: LibreFolio/1.0.
      • headers (optional, not in params_schema, so not in the form): a dict of extra HTTP headers merged over the defaults (User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.5) with mergedeep.

  2. Execution:

    • Fetches the HTML of the specified URL via httpx — a fresh httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=…) per call, follow_redirects=True, then raise_for_status().
    • Uses BeautifulSoup (html.parser) and select_one() — the first element matching the selector. No JavaScript runs, so a price rendered client-side is invisible to the scraper.
    • Extracts the text content and parses it into a Decimal value, handling different number formats based on decimal_format.
    • as_of_date is always today. During a refresh the core stores that value as the day's price point, so a history builds up one sync at a time.

  3. get_asset_url(): Returns the identifier URL itself (the page being scraped).

  4. params_schema: Exposes all 5 configuration fields for dynamic form generation in the frontend. The fields declare no label, so the form shows the raw keys as captions, with each description as tooltip.

Error codes raised by get_current_value() (history always raises NOT_IMPLEMENTED):

Code When Message starts with MISSING_PARAMS No params, or current_css_selector / currency missing CSS scraper requires provider_params / Missing required params INVALID_PARAMS decimal_format other than us / eu decimal_format must be 'us' or 'eu' NOT_FOUND The selector matches nothing Price element not found with selector PARSE_ERROR Empty or non-numeric text Empty price text / Failed to parse price RATE_LIMITED HTTP 429: AssetRateLimitedError with the response's Retry-After, scoped to the page's host CSS Web Scraper: too many requests (HTTP 429) HTTP_ERROR Any other non-2xx response HTTP error {status}: {reason} REQUEST_ERROR Network error or timeout (httpx.RequestError) Request failed SCRAPE_ERROR Anything else Scraping failed NOT_AVAILABLE httpx / beautifulsoup4 not installed httpx and beautifulsoup4 not available

docs.title: 🔢 Decimal Format Remapping
docs.text:
The decimal_format parameter controls how the scraped text is parsed into a number:

Format Input Example Parsed Value us (default) 1,234.56 1234.56 eu 1.234,56 1234.56

The parser first removes whitespace and the symbols € $ £ ¥ %. It then drops the group separator (, for US; . for EU, where , also becomes .) and converts to Decimal. Any other character — e.g. a currency code such as EUR next to the number — makes the conversion fail with PARSE_ERROR.

docs.title: ⚡ Caching & Performance
docs.text:
• No response caching: Each get_current_value() call performs a fresh HTTP request. This is intentional — scraped data may change frequently and the provider cannot predict staleness.
  • No connection pooling across calls: each get_current_value() opens and closes its own httpx.AsyncClient.
  • Timeout handling: Configurable per-asset via timeout parameter. Default 30s prevents blocking on slow sites.

docs.title: 📋 Use Cases
docs.text:
• Tracking the price of an asset from a financial news website.
  • Scraping data from a niche market data provider that doesn't have an API.
  • Tracking the value of a collectible from an auction site.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• No Historical Data: supports_history = False. It can only fetch the current value.
  • Fragile: If the website's layout changes, the CSS selector may break. Use the probe endpoint to test before saving.
  • Requires Public Access: It cannot access pages that require a login, nor read prices that JavaScript adds after the page loads.
  • Rate limits: No built-in rate limiting. High-frequency sync may trigger the target site's anti-bot protection. An HTTP 429 pauses that site only: cooldown_scope() returns the host of the identifier URL (lowercase, without the port), so the other scraped sites keep working (Provider Pauses).

docs.title: 🔍 JustETF Provider (justetf)
docs.text:
The JustETF provider fetches ETF prices and metadata from justetf.com using the justetf-scraping library. It provides comprehensive ETF data including sector and geographic distributions.

📖 User Guide: JustETF — User Manual

docs.title: ⚙️ How it Works
docs.text:
1. Identifier: An ISIN code (e.g., IE00B4L5Y983 for iShares Core MSCI World).
  2. Identifier Types: Only ISIN is accepted.
  3. provider_params: {"currency": "EUR"|"USD"|"CHF"|"GBP"} (default: EUR).

docs.title: 💱 Currency Architecture
docs.text:
The provider supports 4 currencies via JustETF's chart API (load_chart(isin, currency)). JustETF performs server-side FX conversion.

Currency Current Value History Notes EUR ✅ ✅ gettex live quote, falling back to the daily latestQuote; chart USD ✅ ✅ Daily latestQuote only + chart (converted by JustETF) CHF ✅ ✅ Daily latestQuote only + chart (converted by JustETF) GBP ✅ ✅ Daily latestQuote only + chart (converted by JustETF)

Key distinction: fundCurrency (from overview API) = NAV denomination ≠ trading currency. A USD-denominated fund (e.g., MSCI World) trades in EUR on European exchanges.

docs.title: 💰 Current Value (get_current_value)
docs.text:
1. EUR — live gettex quote. _ensure_live_feed(isin) starts (or reuses) the persistent feed, then the quote is read from _live_quote_store, else fetched once with load_live_quote(isin). The market-maker mid is preferred over last, which stays stuck at the opening-auction level all day on thinly traded ETFs. The date comes from the quote timestamp.
  2. Any currency — daily fallback. When no live price is found (and always for USD/CHF/GBP), load_raw_chart(isin, currency)["latestQuote"]["raw"], dated latestQuoteDate. This is how USD, CHF and GBP get a current value.
  3. Neither available → NOT_FOUND; any other exception → FETCH_ERROR.

docs.title: 📈 Historical Data (get_history_value)
docs.text:
• Uses load_chart(isin, currency, add_current) from justetf-scraping.
  • currency read from provider_params (default EUR).
  • add_current=True only if end_date >= today AND currency == "EUR" — gettex quotes are EUR-only.
  • Returns close prices. Only today's EUR point (with add_current) is enriched with intraday open/high/low from load_intraday_ohlc(isin), when the installed library provides it.
  • Date range filtering is done in-memory after fetching the full chart.
  • Cache key includes currency: chart_{isin}_{currency}_{add_current}.

docs.title: 🔎 Search (search)
docs.text:
• Searches against a cached ETF list (load_overview() DataFrame).
  • Search is performed in-memory across: name, ticker, wkn, and ISIN (index).
  • Case-insensitive string matching using pandas vectorized operations.
  • Multi-currency: emits one result per ETF match in each of the 4 currencies (EUR/USD/CHF/GBP), with flag emojis; only in the user's preferred_currency when it is one of them. The setting is the user's own (scope=user, default all), read with self.settings.get("preferred_currency") in search() only, after the cached ETF list: prices and history never depend on it (Plugin Settings).
  • Fund's native currency marked with 👑 (e.g., "🇺🇸👑 iShares Core MSCI World" for a USD-denominated fund); with a preferred currency, 👑 appears only on the funds denominated in it.
  • All results have identifier_type: ISIN and type: "ETF".

docs.title: 📋 Metadata (fetch_asset_metadata)
docs.text:
• Uses get_etf_overview(isin, include_gettex=False) for detailed profile data.
  • Extracts:
    • Description: description + TER + distribution_policy
    • Geographic Area: countries[] → normalized to ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes via normalize_country_to_iso3(), renormalized to sum to 1.0
    • Sector Area: sectors[] → validated against FinancialSector enum, unknown sectors logged and mapped to "Other"
    • Currency: from provider_params["currency"] (user's chosen price currency)
    • Identifiers: identifier_isin (input ISIN), identifier_ticker (if available)
  • asset_type is always ETF.

docs.title: 🔗 get_asset_url
docs.text: Returns https://www.justetf.com/en/etf-profile.html?isin={identifier}.

docs.title: 📡 Live Quote Streaming
docs.text:
The JustETF provider maintains persistent WebSocket connections to the Gettex exchange for real-time price feeds:

  • iterate_live_quote(isin) opens a WebSocket stream and yields price updates as they arrive.
  • A background daemon thread per ISIN keeps the connection alive, reconnecting with exponential backoff (1 s, doubling, capped at 60 s).
  • Prices are stored in a module-level _live_quote_store dictionary.
  • get_current_value() (EUR only): ensures the persistent feed first (_ensure_live_feed), then reads _live_quote_store, falling back to a one-shot load_live_quote().
  • shutdown_live_feeds() stops all daemon threads (called from the provider's shutdown() method at app teardown).

docs.title: 📅 Asset Events
docs.text: During sync, the provider parses dividend data from load_chart() and generates DIVIDEND events via the standard event pipeline.

docs.title: ⚡ Caching Strategy
docs.text:
Cache Key TTL Max Size Purpose ETF list "etf_list" 1 hour 100 Avoid reloading the full overview DataFrame for each search Chart data chart_{isin}_{currency}_{add_current} 1 hour 500 Cache historical chart per ISIN and currency Overview overview_{isin} 1 hour 500 Cache ETF profile/metadata per ISIN

All caches are global (module-level) TTL caches via get_ttl_cache(). They are populated lazily and cleared on server restart. Live gettex quotes are not TTL-cached: they sit in _live_quote_store, refreshed by the feed threads.

No pre-warm of the ETF list

The provider-prewarm startup step (_prewarm_provider_caches() in backend/app/services/platform/app_lifespan.py) only instantiates each registered asset provider, and JustETFProvider does no work when constructed. The ETF list is loaded by the first search() (etf_list() → load_overview()), which waits for the download; later searches read it from the cache until its 1-hour TTL expires.

docs.title: 🧪 Test Configuration
docs.text: Property Value test_cases [{identifier: "IE00B4L5Y983", identifier_type: ISIN}] test_search_query "iShares Core S&P 500"

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• ISIN only: Does not accept tickers — use Yahoo Finance for ticker-based search.
  • Live price in EUR only: the gettex feed is EUR; USD/CHF/GBP current values are the daily latestQuote, converted by justETF.
  • Scraping fragility: The library scrapes justetf.com HTML. Site layout changes may break it.
  • Too many requests: justetf-scraping has no error class of its own and reports an HTTP 429 only in its message («Got status 429…»). raise_if_rate_limited(), first in the handlers of current value, history, search and metadata, turns it into AssetRateLimitedError; metadata no longer answers None for it. No Retry-After reaches the plugin, so the pause is the core's own (Provider Pauses).
  • Blocking I/O: All justetf-scraping calls are synchronous — wrapped in asyncio.to_thread() to avoid blocking the event loop.

docs.title: 📦 Dependency
docs.text:
• Library: justetf-scraping — installed from the local subrepo or PyPI.
  • Optional import: If not installed, the provider raises AssetSourceError("NOT_AVAILABLE") on every call.
  • Transitive: pandas, requests, beautifulsoup4.
