docs.title: 📅 Scheduled Investment Provider (scheduled_investment)
docs.text:
A synthetic, deterministic provider that calculates the value of an asset based on a predefined interest schedule. It makes no external calls and requires no DB access for calculation. It is one of the Asset Providers.

📖 User Guide: Scheduled Investment — User Manual

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration Schema
docs.text:
The asset's value is determined entirely by provider_params, which follow the FAScheduledInvestmentSchedule schema:

Field Type Required Description initial_value Currency ✅ Principal / face value (e.g., {"code": "EUR", "amount": 10000}) interest_type SIMPLE \| COMPOUND — Global interest method (default: SIMPLE) day_count ACT/365 \| ACT/360 \| ACT/ACT \| 30/360 — Day count convention (default: ACT/365) schedule FAInterestRatePeriod[] ✅ List of interest rate periods (non-overlapping, contiguous) late_interest FALateInterestConfig — Optional penalty rate after maturity asset_events FAAssetEventPoint[] — Manually defined asset events

The ScheduledInvestmentEditor shows these as Initial Value / Currency, Interest Type and Day Count; each period row as Period, Rate % (= annual_rate × 100), Frequency (maturation_frequency) and Generate Coupon (generate_interest). The ⚡ Late Interest switch adds the late row — grace days are set from its Period cell — with a Simple/Compound select next to the switch. Asset events are added with Add Event (types Interest, Price Adjustment, Maturity Settlement).

docs.title: 📊 Interest Rate Period (FAInterestRatePeriod)
docs.text: Field Type Default Description start_date date — Period start (inclusive) end_date date — Period end (inclusive) annual_rate Decimal — Annual rate as decimal (e.g., 0.05 for 5%) maturation_frequency MaturationFrequency DAILY Emission granularity: DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, SEMIANNUAL, ANNUAL generate_interest bool false Auto-generate INTEREST events at each maturation date

docs.title: 🚧 Bounds
docs.text:
The schedule is walked day by day (see the accrual walk), so its span is the work and the memory of a computation. The schema (backend/app/schemas/assets/scheduled_investment.py) refuses a schedule outside these limits (night decision N73):

Limit Value Checked in Every period's start_date and end_date 1900-01-01 … 2200-12-31 (SCHEDULE_MIN_DATE, SCHEDULE_MAX_DATE) FAInterestRatePeriod.validate_date_bounds Span, from the first period's start to the last period's end at most 36 525 days, 100 years (SCHEDULE_MAX_SPAN_DAYS) FAScheduledInvestmentSchedule.validate_schedule_continuity Number of periods at most 1 200 (SCHEDULE_MAX_PERIODS) FAScheduledInvestmentSchedule.validate_schedule_continuity Manual events (asset_events) at most 10 000 (SCHEDULE_MAX_EVENTS, MF-SI2) the field's max_length Late interest grace_period_days 0 … 36 525 (LATE_INTEREST_MAX_GRACE_DAYS) FALateInterestConfig.validate_grace_period

The ValueError reaches validate_params(), which raises AssetSourceError with error_code="INVALID_PARAMS". The provider probe (Test Configuration, a dry run) reports it on its current-price and history operations; a sync fails the asset before any computation (refresh.py validates the parameters first) with Invalid provider params. The plugin adds two limits of its own: late interest is valued up to SCHEDULE_MAX_DATE at most (see Late Interest), and a large result is never cached (see Caching & Invalidation).

100 years cover any dated security and the model of a perpetual; dates outside 1900–2200 are not a live security's.

Tests: ./dev.py test schemas scheduled-investment-bounds (each limit and its boundary value, validate_params() → INVALID_PARAMS) and ./dev.py test services scheduled-investment-cost-bounds (the COMPOUND late closed form against the former day-by-day walk, each late history point equal to the value on its date and independent of the read window, a late-history cost linear in its days, the cache cap, the late horizon, the late settlement).

Why: R13-SEC7-2

Before the bounds, the period dates were only checked for order and contiguity. A dry-run probe of a DAILY schedule from year 1 to year 9999 walked millions of days, in provider threads that the probe's 15 s timeout stops waiting for but does not stop, and cached about 0.7 GB for that one schedule. Any signed-in user can run a probe, and the same schedule saved on a shared asset blocked its sync too.

docs.title: 📐 Calculation Engine
docs.text:
Price formula:

price(d) = initial_value + accrued_interest - Σ(INTEREST events) + Σ(PRICE_ADJUSTMENT events)

The three terms run from the first period's start, or from the last auto-coupon, which resets them; the events in the formula are the manual ones.

  • SIMPLE: I = P₀ × r × Δt — interest always on initial principal
  • COMPOUND: I_day = (P₀ + accrued_interest) × r × Δt — interest on the principal plus the interest accrued so far; the manual events do not enter the base

Emission: Price points are emitted only at maturation dates (not every day), matching the maturation_frequency. Start and end dates of each period always produce a point regardless. A maturation date's point is the day's value before its coupon.

History range: get_history_value(start_date, end_date) returns the points and events dated in the range; a start before the schedule's first value adds an initial_value anchor point on that start. start_date="min" (AssetHistoryStartDate, «from the earliest available point») is the earliest of the schedule's first value date and its first manual event's date, or end_date with neither. The history is then the one an explicit start on that date returns: a manual event before the schedule's start brings the anchor on its date. The refresh asks for "min" when it resumes an asset with no stored price yet, that is on its first sync. Before lot MF-SI1, "min" raised CALCULATION_ERROR (the literal was still compared with dates), so the first sync of every new Scheduled Investment asset failed. Test: ./dev.py test services scheduled-investment-min-start.

docs.title: 👣 The Accrual Walk
docs.text:
One generator, _accrual_days(schedule, until), walks the schedule day by day from the first period's start to until; every value of the scheduled range comes from it. Each day, in this order:

  1. Interest: the day's interest at the rate of the period that covers the day, on the base of the interest type above — calculate_simple_interest(base, annual_rate, Δt) with Δt = calculate_day_count_fraction(day − 1, day, day_count), both from financial_math/interest.py. None on the first day, nor on a day no period covers.
  2. Manual events of the day: an INTEREST lowers the value, a PRICE_ADJUSTMENT moves it by its signed amount.
  3. Value: initial_value + accrued interest + manual adjustments, yielded as an _AccrualDay with the day's coupon, if any.
  4. Auto-coupon: on a maturation date of a generate_interest period, when the value is above initial_value, the coupon pays everything above it, and the accrual restarts from initial_value the next day.

The value of a maturation date is therefore the one before its coupon: the peak the chart shows on the day the coupon is paid. Emitted after the reset instead, a generate_interest + DAILY schedule would draw a flat initial_value line.

Two readers share the walk, so they cannot disagree:

  • _generate_schedule_values() walks to the last period's end, keeps the value of every maturation date and turns each coupon into an INTEREST event; its result is cached (see Caching & Invalidation below).
  • _compute_value_at(schedule, target_date) walks to target_date and returns that day's value — on a maturation date, the same pre-coupon value. get_current_value() calls it for a day between two maturation dates, where the last cached point would miss the days since, and after a coupon would be the pre-coupon peak.

A golden test pins, digit for digit, what _generate_schedule_values(), _compute_value_at() and _compute_late_interest_value() return on 33 schedules — four shapes under the four day counts and both interest types, plus the empty schedule: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_synthetic_yield.py against backend/test_scripts/fixtures/scheduled_investment/accrual_golden.json, run with ./dev.py test services synthetic-yield accrual_golden. Regenerate the file only for a reviewed, intended change of these numbers, with LIBREFOLIO_TEST_REGEN_SI_ACCRUAL_GOLDEN=1 in front of the same command.

docs.title: 🔄 Auto-Generated Events (generate_interest)
docs.text:
When generate_interest = True on a period (step 4 of the accrual walk):

  1. At each maturation date, after the day's interest and manual events, the engine checks whether the value is above initial_value
  2. If it is, it generates an 💵 INTEREST event dated that day: value = current_value - initial_value, the accrued interest plus the manual adjustments since the last coupon. If it is not, no coupon is paid and nothing resets
  3. After the event: total_interest = 0, event_adjustment = 0 → value resets to initial_value; the maturation date's own price point keeps the value before the coupon
  4. Interest accrual restarts from zero on the next day

Coupon Reset Behavior

The INTEREST event represents a "coupon payout" — the accumulated interest is crystallized and paid out, resetting the running value back to the original principal.

docs.title: 🏁 MATURITY_SETTLEMENT Event
docs.text:
Auto-generated when:

  • The last schedule period has generate_interest = True and no late_interest is configured
  • Or late_interest has generate_interest = True (settlement at the last late maturation date)

Without late interest, the settlement is worth what the last day leaves after its coupon: the principal when the final coupon is paid that day, as the INTEREST event of the same date, or the day's value when no coupon is paid (no gain above the principal). values[last_end], the chart's last point, stays the pre-coupon peak. Before CP-14b (J-39) the settlement read that peak, so the final coupon was counted twice.

After settlement, the engine is "off" — get_current_value() returns the settlement value for all future dates.

See Asset Events for the full event type reference.

docs.title: ⏰ Late Interest (FALateInterestConfig)
docs.text:
Applied after the asset's maturity date (last period end_date):

Field Type Default Description annual_rate Decimal — Annual late interest rate grace_period_days int 0 Days after maturity before late interest starts interest_type SIMPLE \| COMPOUND COMPOUND Late interest compounds by default (penalties grow) maturation_frequency MaturationFrequency DAILY Emission frequency for late period generate_interest bool false Auto-generate INTEREST + MATURITY_SETTLEMENT events

During the grace period (from the day after maturity through maturity + grace_period_days) interest keeps accruing at the last schedule period's annual_rate; after it, the late annual_rate applies. Both segments start from the value at maturity and use the late interest_type and the global day_count (_compute_late_interest_value).

Both interest types are closed-form, one segment per rate. With m the maturity date, V_m the value on it, g = m + grace_period_days and Δt from calculate_day_count_fraction():

  • SIMPLE: V(t) = V_m + P₀ × r_last × Δt(m, min(t, g)) + P₀ × r_late × Δt(g, t), the last term only once t > g.
  • COMPOUND: V(t) = V_m × compound_growth(m, min(t, g), r_last) × compound_growth(g, t, r_late) (_late_compound_growth). compound_growth(a, b, r) from financial_math/interest.py is Π (1 + r × Δt(d − 1, d)) over the days d in (a, b], 1 for an empty or reversed span: the daily step V += V × r × Δt in closed form, at a cost that does not grow with the span (see Technical Notes below). The grace-period factor is the same for every date after the grace period, and the memo of compound_growth computes it once.

Every reader values a late date the same way, with _compute_late_interest_value():

  • get_history_value() builds the late maturation grid, from the day after maturity to the end of the late range (below), and values only the dates of the requested range plus the last date of the grid (_late_interest_values), SIMPLE and COMPOUND alike;
  • get_current_value() values today's date;
  • with generate_interest, the late MATURITY_SETTLEMENT is dated on the last date of the grid and carries that date's late price, the value the chart draws on it.

A day therefore has the same digits in the history, in the current value and in the settlement, and a date's value never depends on the window it is read in.

Late interest is valued up to SCHEDULE_MAX_DATE (2200-12-31) at most: get_history_value() ends the late range, and its grid, at min(end_date, SCHEDULE_MAX_DATE) and emits no point after it; a schedule with late interest that matures on that very day emits nothing after maturity (the flat line drawn after the maturity of a schedule without late interest does not apply).

Closed form per date (R13-SEC7-2, MF-SI1)

Before R13-SEC7-2, COMPOUND late interest walked day by day from maturity for every date it was asked on, so a long DAILY late history cost a number of steps quadratic in its days. Now a date costs the same however far it is from maturity, so a history costs in proportion to the dates it values, and the horizon caps how many there can be. Under ACT/ACT, SIMPLE late interest reads the memoized year prefix of the day count (see Technical Notes below). The closed form is also more exact than rounding at every step: the COMPOUND late values differ from the former day-by-day walk only in the last digits of the 28-digit Decimal, far below the 12 decimals a stored price keeps.

docs.title: ⚡ Caching & Invalidation
docs.text:
The engine caches the full schedule computation as a tuple[dict, list[FAAssetEventPoint]]:

  • Key: MD5 of the canonical JSON of the validated schedule (_cache_key).
  • Invalidation: Cache is invalidated when provider_params changes (i.e., the user reconfigures the schedule via the frontend ScheduledInvestmentEditor).
  • Stored data: saving new provider_params, or another provider, deletes the asset's prices and the events the plan generated (bulk_assign_providers() in provider_management.py); with new parameters, the next sync regenerates them, and the asset form starts one after the save. The change is refused, nothing written, while a SPLIT the plan generated (listed in asset_events: the editor offers no split, so it comes through the API) has linked incoming adjustments without a purchase cost: see Parametric Provider Change.
  • Hit behavior: On cache hit, get_history_value() slices the pre-computed dict to the requested date range — O(1) per point.
  • Miss behavior: Full schedule recomputation from initial_value through all periods. This is deterministic (no I/O); see the measured times below.
  • Size cap: a result with more than 3 660 points (_CACHE_MAX_POINTS, ten years of DAILY points, about 1 MB) is never stored: it is computed again on every call. The 256 entries stay bounded by about 256 MB (R13-SEC7-2; see Bounds).

The cache is a module-level TTL cache (get_ttl_cache("scheduled_investment"), 256 entries, 48 h TTL), in memory and per process. It survives across multiple sync calls but is cleared on server restart.

Measured times, rounded (one process at nice 10; indicative, not a benchmark). The first, second and last rows were measured at a machine load around 35, the late-interest rows (after MF-SI1) around 25:

Schedule Time Typical: 5 years, MONTHLY ~13 ms the first time, then ~0 ms from the cache The bounds' worst case: 100 years, DAILY, SIMPLE or COMPOUND (over the cap, never cached) ~130 ms for the current value, ~250 ms for the full history Matured in 1900, DAILY COMPOUND late interest: a 7-day history ~40–130 ms (120–270 ms before MF-SI1) The same, full history to 2200-12-31 (≈ 110 000 points) ~1.9 s under ACT/365, ~2.9 s under ACT/ACT, ~3.9 s under 30/360, within the 55 s timeout of the sync's history call The same, current value ~1–2 ms The report's DAILY schedule from year 1 to year 9999 refused in < 1 ms (INVALID_PARAMS)

docs.title: 🔧 Internal State Variables
docs.text:
During computation, the walk (_accrual_days) tracks these internal variables per day:

Variable Description Reset behavior total_interest Cumulative accrued interest since last coupon/start Reset to 0 after an auto-coupon event_adjustment Net sum of the manual events since last coupon/start: − INTEREST, + PRICE_ADJUSTMENT Reset to 0 after an auto-coupon value initial_value + total_interest + event_adjustment Computed per day; yielded in an _AccrualDay (day, value, is_maturation, coupon)

These variables are NOT persisted — they exist only during computation.

docs.title: 📋 Use Cases
docs.text:
• P2P/Crowdfunding Loans: Model a loan with fixed interest rate and periodic coupon payouts.
  • Fixed-Rate Bonds: Calculate bond value including accrued interest and coupon payments.
  • Any asset with predictable, deterministic cash flows.

docs.title: 📐 Example
docs.text:
A P2P loan of €10,000 with 5% simple annual interest (ACT/365), one period from 1 January, monthly coupons (generate_interest: true). Maturation dates fall on the start date and then every month after it:

  • 1 January → 1 February: value grows from €10,000 to ≈ €10,042.47 (31 days × 10,000 × 5% / 365)
  • 1 February (first coupon): the day's price point is ≈ €10,042.47, and a 💵 INTEREST event of ≈ €42.47 pays out everything above the principal → the value restarts from €10,000 on 2 February
  • February: value grows again from €10,000
  • Maturity: 🏁 MATURITY_SETTLEMENT event → engine stops

docs.title: 🔧 Technical Notes
docs.text:
• Interest math in the financial math layer: the day count conventions and simple interest — calculate_day_count_fraction(), which implements ACT/365, ACT/360, ACT/ACT (ISDA: a span is cut at each 1 January it crosses, each piece over its own year's length, the pieces summed in calendar order) and 30/360 through three helpers, and calculate_simple_interest() — live in backend/app/services/financial_math/interest.py (lot CP-14a, U10, developer decision D-8), and the plugin imports them from there. _compute_maturation_dates() stays in scheduled_investment/plugin.py: it reads the domain's MaturationFrequency. Before U10 the primitives lived in the plugin itself, which had absorbed the former backend/app/utils/financial_math.py; the layer guard now fails if one of them is defined anywhere else in backend/app.

  • Daily compounding and the memos (R13-SEC7-2, MF-SI1): interest.py also holds compound_growth(), the closed form of daily compounding that COMPOUND late interest uses (see Late Interest). Its cost does not grow with the span:

    • ACT/365 and ACT/360: one power;
    • ACT/ACT: the first year's days, one power for the whole common years and one for the whole leap years in between, then the last year's days;
    • 30/360: one power per step size (0, 1, 2 or 3 days over 360). The step counts of the span are differences of closed-form counts up to each date: a whole year has 7 steps of 0 (onto the 31sts), one of 3 (common year) or 2 (leap year) onto 1 March, the rest of 1, then month by month in the last year. Integers, so exact.

    It is memoized (_compound_growth, an LRU cache of 4 096 entries), keyed on the span, the rate as written (0.05 and 0.050 are equal Decimals with other digits), the convention and the caller's Decimal precision and rounding. The ACT/ACT day count across years memoizes its full-year prefix with the same precision-and-rounding key: _act_act_years_before(start, end_year, …), the pieces from the start to 1 January of the end year, in an LRU cache of 4 096 entries. A long run of dates from one start, such as a SIMPLE late-interest history, sums the years once per end year instead of once per date, with the same digits as the plain per-year sum. - identifier_type: Always AUTO_GENERATED — the engine generates its own UUID identifier. - params_schema: Exposes a single ui_component field (key: "_ui_component", default: "scheduled_investment") telling the frontend to render the dedicated ScheduledInvestmentEditor instead of generic fields. - Events: there is no supports_events flag. get_history_value() returns price points and events together in FAHistoricalData.events (auto-generated + manual, filtered to the requested range).

docs.title: 📈 Yahoo Finance Provider (yfinance)
docs.text:
The Yahoo Finance provider fetches stock, ETF, crypto, and index prices using the yfinance library. It is the primary market data provider for LibreFolio.

Implementation: backend/app/services/asset_source_providers/yahoo_finance/plugin.py

📖 User Guide: Yahoo Finance — User Manual

docs.title: ⚙️ How it Works
docs.text:
1. Identifier: A Yahoo Finance ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, BTC-USD, IE00B4L5Y983).
  2. Identifier Types: TICKER and ISIN are both accepted. ISIN is resolved by yfinance internally.
  3. No provider_params: Yahoo Finance does not require any additional configuration.

docs.title: 💰 Current Value (get_current_value)
docs.text:
1. The asset-source service checks its core current-value cache (120s TTL) before invoking the provider.
  2. Calls ticker.info — the Yahoo quoteSummary endpoint. Returns regularMarketPrice, currency, and regularMarketTime in a single lightweight call.
  3. Fallback price: currentPrice → previousClose (if regularMarketPrice is null).
  4. as_of_date is the date of regularMarketTime in the exchange's timezone, info["exchangeTimezoneName"], which the plugin's private _exchange_zone() turns into a ZoneInfo: UTC when Yahoo gives none or one the server's timezone database does not know (see Limitations), and the server's today without regularMarketTime. Up to 1.2.1 the date was always UTC's, the day before for the part of a session that falls before UTC midnight, such as Sydney's or Auckland's (Z-33).
  5. No history() call at all — current value polling never touches the chart API.

Avoid history() and fast_info for current price

  • ticker.history() calls the chart API and logs noisy Entering history() lines.
  • ticker.fast_info internally triggers 2 heavy HTTP calls (range=1y + range=5d).
  • ticker.info uses the quoteSummary endpoint — lighter, returns price + currency together.

Cache TTL vs Polling Interval

Frontend polls every 30s for responsive UI, while the core cache has a 120s TTL. Repeated polls for the same provider key can therefore return without another Yahoo call.

docs.title: 📈 Historical Data (get_history_value)
docs.text:
The public method now delegates its local work to focused helpers without changing its contract:

  1. Acquire — _acquire_history_data()
  2. start_date == "min" calls ticker.history(period="max", auto_adjust=False).
  3. A finite range calls ticker.history(start=start_date, end=end_date + 1 day, auto_adjust=False), preserving LibreFolio's inclusive end date over yfinance's exclusive end.
  4. The closes are the exchange's own (auto_adjust=False, Z-35): Close is not rewritten for the dividends paid since. yfinance's default would rewrite it as of the day it is read, so rows saved on different days carried different adjustments, and a return counted a dividend twice (in the price and in its event). Yahoo's Close stays adjusted for splits in either mode (checked on AAPL's 4:1 of 31 Aug 2020: the raw close of 28 Aug is 124.81, not about 499); the splits come as events too. The extra Adj Close column of the raw frame is ignored.
  5. Currency metadata falls back to USD.
  6. Otherwise the currency is Yahoo's own code (ticker.info["currency"]), passed on unchanged as FAHistoricalData.currency: GBp for a London line quoted in pence, whose price points and dividends carry GBP (their schemas upper-case the code) with the numbers in pence. Two guards in test_yahoo_finance_errors.py pin it: no validator may fold that field, and the plugin converts nothing. Such an asset needs a quote base of 100, which the plugin suggests (Quote Base Suggestion).
  7. Dividend and split series are acquired independently and best-effort; one failing does not suppress the other or the prices.
  8. Map — _map_history_prices()
  9. Each row takes the calendar date of its own index value (_normalize_yahoo_date()): yfinance 1.7.0 stamps a daily bar, a dividend and a split at midnight in the exchange's timezone (scrapers/history.py, tz_localize(tz_exchange)), so that date is the session's. Up to 1.2.1 the plugin converted the index to UTC first, which gave the day before the session for every exchange east of UTC: Milan all year, London in summer time, Tokyo (Z-33). The rows stored that way stay as they are (Dates on the Exchange's Own Day).
  10. Rows are filtered to the requested inclusive range.
  11. A row with Close = NaN is skipped. Optional Open, High, Low, or Volume NaNs become None.
  12. The provider returns only actual trading days; the query layer performs backward fill.
  13. Events — _parse_dividend_events() and _parse_split_events()
  14. Positive in-range dividends and non-trivial in-range split ratios become typed asset events, dated by _normalize_yahoo_date() as the prices.
  15. A dividend of a minor-unit line is divided by the unit's factor (Z-32 a/b): Yahoo gives a London line's dividends in pence like its closes, so 1.9542 on a GBp line becomes 0.019542 GBP (minor_unit_factor(), utils/currency_units.py). The prices keep their pence (the asset's quote base divides them) and a split ratio is a number of shares, never scaled.
  16. The two parsers are also isolated best-effort, so either event family can survive a failure in the other.

Validation and data failures remain typed AssetSourceErrors: unsupported identifier types use INVALID_IDENTIFIER_TYPE, a missing optional dependency uses NOT_AVAILABLE, empty/unusable history uses NO_DATA, and malformed or unexpected Yahoo responses use FETCH_ERROR.

No provider-internal thread hop

Yahoo's yfinance calls remain synchronous and direct. The provider does not call asyncio.to_thread(); the asset-source service invokes the whole provider coroutine through assets.core._run_provider_in_thread() in a dedicated thread with a new event loop.

docs.title: 🔎 Search (search)
docs.text:
• Uses yfinance.Search(query) for real-time ticker search.
  • Minimum query length: 2 characters.
  • Results limited to top 20 quotes.
  • quoteType is normalized to LibreFolio asset types: equity → STOCK, etf → ETF, mutualfund → FUND, cryptocurrency → CRYPTO, etc.
  • Currency is fetched per-symbol via _fetch_currency() (fast_info), cached separately for 24 hours. Only an answer is cached: a currency, or Yahoo answering without one (Z-39).
    • A refusal for too many requests (_is_rate_limited()) raises AssetRateLimitedError at once, with no retry and nothing cached: the whole search leaves as rate limited at that result, the remaining results' currencies are not asked, and the core pauses Yahoo.
    • Any other error gives that result no currency and is not cached: the next search asks again.
  • A result whose currency is a minor unit carries a quote_base_suggestion: GBp gives {"quantity": 100, "quote_currency": "GBp"}; any other currency, or none, adds no key (Quote Base Suggestion).

docs.title: 📋 Metadata (fetch_asset_metadata)
docs.text:
• Fetches full ticker.info from Yahoo Finance.
  • Extracts: asset_type, currency, short_description (from longBusinessSummary), sector (single-sector distribution), identifier_ticker, identifier_isin.
  • ISIN is obtained via ticker.isin (not available for all markets).
  • Unknown sectors are logged as warnings and mapped to "Other".

docs.title: Fund data (quoteType etf / mutualfund)
docs.text:
For a fund the plugin also reads Ticker.funds_data (_read_fund_extras), one more Yahoo request in the same cached metadata call. An equity never touches it.

Piece Source Goes to Sector breakdown sector_weightings classification_params.sector_area, replacing the single info["sector"] Description description short_description, only when longBusinessSummary is empty Expense ratio fund_operations («Annual Report Expense Ratio») \| TER: x% after the description Issuer fund_overview["family"] \| Issuer: <family> after the TER
  • Sector keys are Yahoo's own spellings (consumer_cyclical, realestate, financial_services…), which FinancialSector.from_string does not know: _YAHOO_FUND_SECTORS maps the eleven explicitly. A key outside the table goes to «Other» with the unknown-sector warning. The weights are renormalised to 1, as justETF's are.
  • The expense ratio is a fraction (0.0003 = 0.03 %): it is shown as a percentage rounded to two decimals. A missing, NaN or non-positive value is left out (VWCE.DE has none).
  • The 500-character cap cuts the head of the description, never the tail, so the TER and the issuer always survive.
  • Error policy: every piece is read apart (_read_fund_piece), so one that Yahoo lacks or that cannot be read costs only itself and is logged as a warning; the metadata still comes back. A «too many requests» refusal is the exception and leaves as AssetRateLimitedError, like every other Yahoo call.
  • The country breakdown, the holdings and the asset classes are not read: Yahoo gives no countries, and the rest has no field to land in yet (TODO_FUTURI.md, «Profilo dei dati dell'asset»).

docs.title: 🔢 Quote Base Suggestion (suggest_quote_base)
docs.text:
The prices of a London line quoted in pence (GBp) are stored in pence as GBP (see Historical Data above), so its asset needs a quote base (quote_base_quantity, Units per single price) of 100. The plugin suggests it in two places, both through _quote_base_suggestion(currency):

  • Search: from the currency each result already reads, as listed above.
  • suggest_quote_base(): from the currency of fast_info, read through _fetch_currency(identifier) and its 24-hour cache, shared with the search. A GBp line gives FAQuoteBaseSuggestion(quantity=100, quote_currency="GBp"); any other currency, none, an empty identifier or a missing yfinance gives None. The core asks it in the probe's metadata operation only, after fetch_asset_metadata() has answered, with 5 s of its own (Asset Plugin Guide).

_quote_base_suggestion() reads the factor from minor_unit_factor(), whose list is MINOR_UNIT_FACTORS (backend/app/utils/currency_units.py): the codes are matched as reported, whitespace stripped, so GBP or gbp get no suggestion. Only GBp, 100, is listed: ZAC and ILA, the cents of Johannesburg and the agorot of Tel Aviv, are not ISO 4217 codes, and the schemas refuse them (Currency.validate_code() and iso_currency_code() in backend/app/schemas/common.py). The portfolio data-quality report reads the same list (Data Quality Banner).

docs.title: 🔗 get_asset_url
docs.text: Returns https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/{identifier}.

docs.title: 📅 Asset Events
docs.text:
During sync, the provider generates:

  • DIVIDEND events from ticker.dividends — ex-dividend date + per-share amount.
  • SPLIT events from ticker.splits — split date + ratio value (e.g., 4.0 for a 4:1 split).

Event acquisition and parsing are best-effort and independent. Events that are returned are persisted by assets/event_store.py::_upsert_asset_events(), keyed by provider_assignment_id. They are dated on the exchange's day, as the prices; one an older version stored a day early stays, beside the one a sync fetches again (Dates on the Exchange's Own Day).

docs.title: ⚡ Caching Strategy
docs.text:
Owner / Cache Key TTL Max Size Purpose Core current value Provider code + identifier + identifier type (refresh also includes the provider-parameter hash) 120 sec 300 Avoid repeated ticker.info calls during current-price polling and refresh. Core history Provider code + identifier + identifier type + provider-parameter hash 15 min 500 Reuse fetched date ranges during provider-driven refresh. Core search query Provider code + normalized query 15 min 500 Avoid repeating the same provider search. Yahoo currency lookup symbol 24 hours 2000 Cache the provider's fast_info currency sub-operation used by search() and suggest_quote_base(). Only answers are cached, never a refusal or an error.

All are in-memory, per-process TTL caches created with get_ttl_cache(). The shared result caches are owned by assets/core.py; Yahoo owns only its currency sub-operation cache.

No provider-level history cache

Yahoo has no provider-level history cache. The outer refresh layer may reuse its core history cache and persists fetched prices to the database. get_prices_bulk() is DB-only; it never calls Yahoo while serving a historical query (see Architecture — Price Query).

docs.title: 🧪 Test Configuration
docs.text: Property Value test_cases [{identifier: "AAPL", identifier_type: TICKER}] test_search_query "Apple"

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• Rate limits: Yahoo Finance may refuse for too many requests. _is_rate_limited() recognises yfinance's YFRateLimitError and, in any error message, «429» as a whole word, «too many requests» or «rate limit»; _yf_with_retry() then raises AssetRateLimitedError at once, without retrying in the thread, and search and metadata let it through instead of answering [] or None. The core pauses the provider (Provider Pauses); yfinance gives no Retry-After, so the pause is the core's own. A false positive costs a pause of about a minute. Other transient errors (timeouts, reset connections, 503…) are still retried: at most three attempts, 1.5 s and then 3 s apart.
  • ISIN resolution: Not all ISINs are resolvable by yfinance (depends on market coverage).
  • Data gaps: Some tickers may have missing days or delayed data.
  • Rows dated a day early by 1.2.1 or earlier stay as they are: a sync rewrites only the session days it fetches, and an event it fetches again is stored beside the old one (Dates on the Exchange's Own Day).
  • No timezone database (Windows outside Docker without the PyPI tzdata package, a minimal container): _exchange_zone() gives None, so the current value is dated in UTC, and an Area/Location name (Europe/Rome) is logged as a warning once per name and process, Exchange timezone unknown to this server's timezone database: the current value is dated in UTC. A fixed offset or a name without an area is not logged. Adding tzdata is Z-36, a developer decision.
  • Splits rewrite the past (known limitation, MF-SPL1, option C for 1.3). Yahoo's Close and ticker.dividends are both expressed in the share count after every later split: AAPL's close of 28 Aug 2020 is 124.81 (the real one was about 499) and its dividend of 7 Aug 2020 is 0.205 (the real one was 0.82), the 4:1 of 31 Aug 2020; NVDA's 2023 dividends are 0.004 (paid 0.04) after the 10:1 of June 2024. auto_adjust=False does not undo it: the raw frame is split-adjusted too. The engine changes a quantity only with the adjustment linked to the SPLIT event, on the day of the split, and reads the quotation as it is, so a position held before a split is valued at its pre-split quantity times a post-split price (10 × 124.81 = 1,248 instead of 4,990; the TWRR jumps and a false loss appears), and a dividend event times the pre-split quantity comes out short. Nothing in the plugin can fix it (Yahoo offers no unadjusted close); the correction belongs to the engine, from the SPLIT events, after 1.3 (TODO_FUTURI.md).
  • Rows saved before Z-35 stay adjusted (developer decision of 23 Oct 2026: no clean-up of saved data). The history is stored as it was read: a row written before the change keeps the dividend adjustment of the day it was fetched, and the scheduler re-reads only the last 14 days. The user who notices re-reads the whole history with the full Sync (the dialog of C-66 warns before it overwrites). The same holds for the dividends of a pence line saved before Z-32, still in pence until that Sync.

docs.title: 📦 Dependency
docs.text:
• Library: yfinance — installed via pipenv install yfinance.
  • Optional import: If yfinance is not installed, current/history/search calls raise an AssetSourceError with error code NOT_AVAILABLE; metadata refresh degrades to None.
  • Transitive: pandas (required by yfinance).

docs.title: 🔎 Asset Search & Link-Finder
docs.text:
LibreFolio resolves an interactive asset search through a three-layer stack. The goal is to turn whatever the user types — a name, a ticker, an ISIN, or a whole line copied from a broker report — into a concrete, priceable asset candidate, while keeping automated price fetches completely free of any web search.

This page documents the generic machinery (the orchestration in AssetSearchService, the web_link_finder module, the resolve_url capability, the hints mechanism, and the identifier post-filter). Provider-specific behaviour lives on each provider page — see Borsa Italiana, which is currently the only provider that opts into layers 2 and 3.

docs.title: 📂 Where it lives
docs.text:
The system is not one function — it is a small standalone module (the engine) plus service-layer orchestration plus a thin per-provider hook:

Piece File Role web_link_finder module backend/app/services/assets/web_link_finder.py Self-contained subsystem: the external-engine client (ddgs metasearch by default), config, TTL cache, domain filter. Knows nothing about providers or assets. Search orchestration backend/app/services/assets/search.py → AssetSearchService Ties it together: _augment_with_link_finder, _build_link_finder_queries, _filter_items_by_known_identifiers, _provider_url_for_item. Decides when to fall back and how to narrow. Provider hook each provider's resolve_url / resolvable_url_domains Turns a resolved URL back into search-item(s). Only Borsa Italiana implements it today. Endpoints backend/app/api/v1/assets/providers.py /assets/provider/search[/stream] accept the optional hints query param.

So the answer to "is it its own subsystem or just a service function?" is both: a dedicated module for the engine, orchestrated by the service layer, with a thin per-provider hook.

graph LR
    EP["API /assets/provider/search[/stream]"] --> SVC

    subgraph SVC["assets/search.py — AssetSearchService (orchestration)"]
        A["_augment_with_link_finder"]
        B["_build_link_finder_queries"]
        C["_filter_items_by_known_identifiers"]
    end

    SVC -->|"query + domains"| WLF["web_link_finder.py<br/>(standalone engine module)"]
    WLF -->|"candidate URLs"| SVC
    SVC -->|"resolve_url(url)"| PROV["provider.resolve_url<br/>(e.g. Borsa Italiana)"]
    PROV -->|"search-item(s)"| SVC

    style WLF fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#e65100
    style PROV fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2e7d32

docs.title: 🧱 The three layers
docs.text:
graph TD
    Q["User query<br/>(name / ticker / ISIN / report line)"] --> L1

    subgraph L1["Layer 1 — On-site search"]
        S1["provider.search(query)"]
    end

    L1 -->|"results"| OUT["Aggregated results"]
    L1 -->|"0 results"| L2

    subgraph L2["Layer 2 — web_link_finder (last resort)"]
        F1["find_candidate_urls(query, allowed_domains)"]
        F2["candidate provider-domain URLs"]
        F1 --> F2
    end

    L2 --> L3

    subgraph L3["Layer 3 — resolve_url"]
        R1["provider.resolve_url(url)"]
        R2["search-item dict or list<br/>{identifier, type,<br/>currency, provider_params}"]
        R1 --> R2
    end

    L3 -->|"non-None items"| OUT

    style S1 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style F1 fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#e65100
    style R1 fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2e7d32
    style R2 fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2e7d32
Layer Where When it runs Purpose L1 — on-site search provider.search(query) Always The provider's own search (e.g. borsaitaliana.it cerca, Yahoo, justETF). L2 — web link-finder web_link_finder.find_candidate_urls() Only when L1 returns 0 items and the provider opts in and the finder is enabled Uses an external metasearch engine (ddgs by default — bing / brave / google / DuckDuckGo / … aggregated) to find candidate provider-domain URLs for the query. L3 — URL resolver provider.resolve_url(url) For each L2 candidate URL Opens the page, extracts data, and returns one search-item dict, a list of search-item dicts, or None — the inverse of get_asset_url.

Invariant — external search is interactive-only

Layers 2 and 3 are hit only during interactive asset search. Price fetches (frequent, automated) must never touch web_link_finder. Once an asset exists it is priced by its stored identifier and provider_params (for Borsa Italiana funds, provider_params.codice_fondo), never by re-searching. This keeps scheduled syncs deterministic and independent from external metasearch availability.

docs.title: 🎼 Orchestration (AssetSearchService)
docs.text:
Both search() (batch) and search_stream() (SSE) query every eligible provider in parallel, each a core.configured_provider(code, user_id=…) that carries the searching user's personal settings. Each provider.search() call goes through assets.core.call_provider(), the boundary of every provider call, which runs it in _run_provider_in_thread(). After a provider yields its L1 results, the shared augment helper decides whether to fall back to the external stack:

# backend/app/services/assets/search.py
async def search(query: str, provider_codes=None, hints: Optional[list[str]] = None, *, user_id: int | None = None) -> FAProviderSearchResponse
async def search_stream(query: str, provider_codes=None, hints: Optional[list[str]] = None, *, user_id: int | None = None) -> AsyncGenerator[str]
  • _augment_with_link_finder(code, provider, query, hints=None) — invoked when a provider returns 0 items and provider.supports_url_resolution and web_link_finder.is_enabled(). It builds the candidate queries (see Hints), calls find_candidate_urls, then resolves each hit through assets.core.call_provider() (resolve_url may do sync I/O). The helper flattens one-item/list results, de-duplicates by (identifier, language), and returns the non-None items. Any failure is caught and yields [] — the search always completes and emits done.
  • _provider_url_for_item(code, item) — DRY helper used during serialization so the provider_url display link is (re)computed from the item's provider_params on every request.
  • Results are flagged as "found via web" for the UI.

The stream sends one event per provider, then a last one:

Event Fields provider_results provider_code, results provider_error provider_code, error (the message), error_code for every AssetSourceError (NOT_CONFIGURED, RATE_LIMITED, or the provider's own code), retry_after with RATE_LIMITED done total_results, providers_queried, providers_with_errors

The batch search lists every provider that failed in providers_with_errors, and those not called because a required setting has no value also in providers_not_configured: see the reasons in Interactive Search Stack.

Why the fallback fixes the old \"searching… hangs\" bug

Because the augment path is fully time-boxed and best-effort, an SSE search always reaches a terminal done event even when the external engine is slow or blocked. A provider returning 0 results no longer leaves the stream open with no No-Match state.

docs.title: 🌐 web_link_finder module
docs.text:
backend/app/services/assets/web_link_finder.py is a LibreFolio-level module, deliberately kept out of any scraping library — the choice of external engine is a LibreFolio concern, not a provider's.

async def find_candidate_urls(query: str, allowed_domains: list[str], *, max_results: int | None = None, path_hint: str | None = None) -> list[str]
def is_enabled() -> bool
  • Best-effort: any failure (rate-limit, network error, missing optional dependency) yields [] and is never fatal.
  • max_results: None, the default, takes LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_MAX (5 when unset).
  • Async-safe: the engine's synchronous search() runs inside asyncio.to_thread; short timeout, small TTL cache, domain-filtered hits, structured logs.
  • Pluggable engine: the default DdgsEngine wraps the ddgs metasearch library (the maintained successor of duckduckgo_search), which aggregates ~10 upstream engines (bing / brave / google / duckduckgo / startpage / …) behind one text(query, backend="auto") call. An ApiKeyEngine seam is in place for a paid API (Brave / Bing / SerpAPI) later; the searxng engine name is reserved for the deferred SearXNG adapter (see Transport history below).
  • Defensive import: ddgs is imported behind a _DDGS_OK guard, so a missing dependency simply disables the module instead of breaking search.

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration (env vars, all optional)
docs.text:
The variables are read in backend/app/config/plugins.py, from the process environment only: web_link_finder.py calls its web_link_finder_*() accessors and reads no variable itself.

Variable Default Meaning LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_ENABLED 1 1/0 master switch. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_ENGINE ddgs ddgs | apikey (searxng reserved for Fase B). LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_API_KEY "" Key for the apikey engine (engine self-disables if absent). LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_API_KEY_FILE "" Path of a file holding the API key instead: the key is a secret, read by env_secret() (Secrets from Files), so a blank value counts as unset. Read only when the apikey engine is built: a file that cannot give the key makes _build_engine() log web_link_finder: <error>; disabling and return no engine, so the search returns [] and the server keeps running. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_DDGS_REGION wt-wt ddgs region (e.g. wt-wt worldwide, it-it). The worldwide default avoids US bias so IT pages aren't down-ranked. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_DDGS_BACKEND auto ddgs backend(s): auto rotates/aggregates, or a comma list (e.g. google,bing). LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_TIMEOUT 6 Per-request timeout, seconds, read as a float: at least 1. Unset, blank, not a number, not finite or below 1: the default. ddgs takes whole seconds, so a fraction is rounded up (math.ceil): 1.5 gives 2. LIBREFOLIO_WEB_LINK_FINDER_MAX 5 Max candidate URLs returned, read as an int: at least 1. Unset, blank, not a whole number or below 1: the default.

docs.title: 🕰️ Transport history (why ddgs)
docs.text:
The original transport was a hand-rolled DuckDuckGoEngine that scraped the html.duckduckgo.com HTML endpoint. It proved fragile: under back-to-back backend queries DDG's bot-detection returns an HTTP 202 "anomaly" page with zero results (the same query works in a browser — a trusted human session). Because 202 is a 2xx, raise_for_status() never fired, so the empty page was parsed as "no hits" and — worse — cached for 15 minutes. Net effect: a query that Google/DDG resolve fine in a browser returned nothing from the backend.

The scraper was retired in favour of the ddgs metasearch library (2026-07-28). By rotating and aggregating multiple upstream engines it sidesteps any single engine's rate-limiting, needs no extra infrastructure (a pure pip dependency), and drops straight into the existing synchronous _SearchEngine seam. DuckDuckGo remains one of its backends, so no coverage is lost.

Deferred: SearXNG (Fase B)

A self-hosted, anonymized SearXNG metasearch container is planned as an optional power-user upgrade, sitting in front of ddgs as the runtime chain [searxng → ddgs]. It is deferred until search usage outgrows ddgs; the searxng engine name is already reserved in _build_engine. See the plan under Release_2/Phase_0/04_webSearchEngine/ and the backlog note in Release_2/todo_futuri.md.

docs.title: 🔁 resolve_url — the generic URL → search-item capability
docs.text:
Any provider can opt into turning a page URL back into search-item(s) (the inverse of get_asset_url). It is defined on the AssetSourceProvider base class:

Member Default Description resolvable_url_domains: list[str] [] Domains this provider can resolve. supports_url_resolution derived bool(resolvable_url_domains). async resolve_url(url) -> dict \| list[dict] \| None None Open → extract → return search-item(s), or None when the URL is not a recognisable asset page for this provider.

resolve_url is only an alternative entry point into search: it returns the same shape search would for that instrument. When a single page maps to several canonical rows — e.g. one item per language (Italian + English, with flags), exactly like an on-site cerca hit — return them all as a list. The orchestration flattens the result and de-duplicates by (identifier, language), so sibling language-URLs of the same instrument don't pile up.

Each item must match the search-item shape (identifier, identifier_type, display_name, currency, type, provider_params) so the create-asset flow can consume it directly. resolve_url must be best-effort — parse/fetch errors return None, never raise. The one exception is a refusal for too many requests: raise it as AssetRateLimitedError, so that the core pauses the provider (Too Many Requests); the link-finder then skips that URL without reporting an error.

Scope

The capability is generic in the base class, but Borsa Italiana is the only provider that implements it in the current pass: a fund detail page resolves to the IT + EN pair (Italian first, with flags), each carrying the fund's codice_fondo, or to the row of the searching user's preferred language alone.

docs.title: 🧵 Hints — the two-stage "stringone"
docs.text: When the caller holds extra technical identifiers and names (typically extracted from a broker report during import), it passes them as hints. Hints do two things:

docs.title: 1️⃣ Two-stage candidate query
docs.text:
_build_link_finder_queries(query, hints) produces an ordered, de-duplicated candidate list:

  1. Rich string — every hint plus the base query concatenated (whitespace-collapsed, not truncated or reordered). Example: "LU2178929613 EURIZON NEXT 2.0 DIVERSIFICATO 40 P".
  2. Base query — the bare query as a fallback.

_augment_with_link_finder tries them in order and returns items from the first candidate that resolves anything. The rich query narrows the external engine when the bare query is too ambiguous (a bare ISIN on a site-restricted external search often surfaces every sibling share class); if it is over-constrained and finds nothing, the base query still runs. With no hints, the list is just [base] (legacy behaviour).

Hints never touch the on-site cerca

The stringone lives only in the link-finder stage. It must not be fed to the provider's L1 on-site search, which is stricter and would return 0 for a concatenated blob — losing the on-site path when the name alone would have matched.

docs.title: 2️⃣ Identifier post-filter
docs.text:
Even with the rich query, the external engine can still return sibling instruments. So resolved items are narrowed by _filter_items_by_known_identifiers(items, [*hints, query]):

  • If any resolved item's identifier matches a known term (case-insensitive), only the matching items are kept.
  • If nothing matches, all items are returned (the user chooses).

Free-text name hints are inert here — a name never equals an ISIN/ticker identifier — so only real identifiers (ISIN, ticker) actually filter. This is what turns a bare-ISIN search that surfaced 5 sibling funds into the single exact match.

docs.title: 📥 Where hints come from
docs.text: Source Hints passed Import wizard (create-asset) Extracted ISIN + symbol + all candidate report names (_createNames). Manual asset search The query itself doubles as an identifier hint via the [*hints, query] merge in the filter.

docs.title: 🌐 API
docs.text:
Both search endpoints accept an optional, repeatable hints query parameter:

GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search?q=LU2178929613&providers=borsa_italiana&hints=LU2178929613&hints=EURIZON+NEXT+2.0+DIVERSIFICATO+40+P
GET /api/v1/assets/provider/search/stream?q=...&hints=...&hints=...

hints is an optional nullable array in the generated client (./dev.py api sync). Omitting it preserves the legacy single-query behaviour.

docs.title: 🖥️ Frontend wiring
docs.text:
Component Prop Role AssetSearchAutocomplete.svelte hints?: string[] Appended as repeated &hints= on the SSE fetch URL (deduped client-side). It also reads why a provider did not answer: error_code: "NOT_CONFIGURED" on the stream, providers_not_configured on the REST fallback, each giving the provider a row with Configure. AssetSearchAutocomplete.svelte reportContext?: SearchReportContext What the caller's form already holds (currency, asset type, identifiers), added to the «Let us know» report below; null by default. AssetModal.svelte searchHints?: string[] Forwarded to the autocomplete, with searchReportContext as its reportContext: the form's currency, type and the identifier rows that have a value. ImportWizardModal.svelte searchHints Built from the extracted ISIN + symbol + all candidate report names.

No UI change is required for the feature to work end-to-end — an asset created from a resolved result already carries its provider_params, so it is priceable immediately.

«Can't find it? Let us know» (P20). Once a search has finished, whatever its outcome, the dropdown shows a report row: at its bottom, or between the Premium and the community sections when they show (reportPlacement). assetSearchReport.ts holds its logic. supportChannel(value, {githubFallback}) turns the instance's support_url (GET /api/v1/system/instance, through instanceConfig) into a channel, checking it again although the backend validated it, so that nothing but http(s) and mailto: with one address becomes a link: mailto (subject and CRLF body in the link), or page for an address that new URL() parses as http(s) with a host name and no user name or password (the page opens in a new tab, with the report in its query as title and body, encoded as for a GitHub issue, and the body still goes to the clipboard, with a toast either way). A page carries the parsed url.href, normalized and absolute, never the raw value: a spelling such as https:host would otherwise resolve, as an href, to a path on the instance itself. Anything else, user info included, counts as missing, like an unset value: github (a prefilled new issue) with githubFallback, null without it.

N61: AssetSearchAutocomplete.svelte passes githubFallback = selfHostedConfirmed() (the helper of lib/features/instance/profile.ts: loaded, and profile is selfhosted; see Instance configuration), since a public issue would publish the profile, the provider codes and the identifiers. On a managed instance, or while GET /api/v1/system/instance has not answered on this page load (until then instanceConfig holds DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CONFIG, which says selfhosted: hence the loaded guard), a missing address gives a null channel: reportPlacement is then null, and the dropdown has no report row. A valid address works in both profiles.

buildSearchReport() writes the English subject and body, reportHref() the link. Each queried provider's outcome comes from the stream, provider_results (a count) or provider_error (its error_code, never the error message), or on the REST fallback from providers_queried, providers_with_errors and providers_not_configured; a provider still silent when the search ends is no answer. The report leaves from the browser, never from the server.

docs.title: 🐞 Fragility & limits
docs.text:
• External metasearch is keyless by default and best-effort — treat L2 as a convenience, not a guarantee. The current transport uses the ddgs library, not LibreFolio HTML scraping; upstream engine failures, missing dependencies, or timeouts degrade to [].
  • L2/L3 only trigger on a 0-result L1 — a provider that returns any on-site result never reaches the external stack (by design).
  • Site-restricted ranking is fuzzy — the identifier post-filter, not the engine, is what guarantees precision when a known identifier is available.
  • For a paid, reliable engine, implement the ApiKeyEngine and set …_ENGINE=apikey + …_API_KEY.

docs.title: 🔑 Feature Key
docs.text:
• 📈 History: Can fetch historical OHLC data.
  • 🔎 Search: Supports searching for assets by name/ticker. Detected via test_search_query is not None.
  • 📋 Metadata: Can fetch asset details (sector, description, identifiers) via fetch_asset_metadata().
  • 💰 Current Value: Can fetch the latest real-time price.
  • 📊 Events: Can produce asset events, returned with the history in FAHistoricalData.events — dividends and splits (Yahoo Finance), dividends (JustETF), interest and settlements (Scheduled Investment). There is no supports_events flag.
  • 🔗 get_asset_url: Generates a link to the provider's page for this asset (e.g., Yahoo Finance quote page).
  • 🧩 params_schema: Exposes a form schema for the frontend to render dynamic configuration fields.
  • 🧪 Probe: All providers support POST /assets/provider/probe for dry-run testing (current_price, history, metadata operations).

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• CSS Scraper get_asset_url returns the identifier itself (which is the URL to scrape).
  • Scheduled Investment uses AUTO_GENERATED identifier type — no external identifier needed.
  • Mock Provider (mockprov) is test-only: always registered, but served only when LIBREFOLIO_TEST_MODE is on; outside test mode its registry withholds it, and naming it reaches nothing (Test-Only Plugins).

docs.title: 📈 Yahoo Finance (yfinance)
docs.text:
The primary market data provider — fetches stock, ETF, crypto, and index prices using the yfinance library.

  • Features: History, Search, Metadata, Current Value
  • Identifier types: TICKER, ISIN
  • Key details: ticker.info for current price (no history() or fast_info), core search-query cache (15 min TTL), currency caching (24h), single-sector metadata (no geographic split)
  • 📖 Technical Details →
  • 📖 User Guide →

docs.title: 🔍 JustETF (justetf)
docs.text:
Specialized ETF provider — fetches data from justetf.com including sector and geographic distributions.

  • Features: History, Search, Metadata, Current Value (gettex live in EUR, daily latestQuote otherwise)
  • Identifier types: ISIN
  • Key details: Cached ETF list for instant search, Gettex WebSocket for real-time quotes, geographic/sector distributions, pre-warm at startup
  • 📖 Technical Details →

docs.title: 🇮🇹 Borsa Italiana (borsa_italiana)
docs.text:
Italian market data provider — fetches stocks, bonds (BTP), and ETFs listed on Borsa Italiana using the borsa-italiana-scraping library.

  • Features: History, Search, Metadata, Current Value
  • Identifier types: ISIN
  • Provider params: Optional language ("en" / "it"), codice_fondo for mutual funds, mic / platform for market routing; the page url is stored automatically
  • URL resolution: resolvable_url_domains = ["borsaitaliana.it"]; resolve_url(url) returns the canonical IT + EN result set for fund/detail pages, then search flattens and de-dupes by (identifier, language)
  • Key details: Full OHLCV history for listed instruments, dual-language search with flag emojis, fund NAV pricing by internal codice_fondo (not ISIN), current fund NAV only when NAV date is today, fund history as one NAV point at its real date, identifier_other stored as a JSON list for alternative technical identifiers
  • 📖 Technical Details →

docs.text:
A versatile provider that can extract a current price from any public webpage using a CSS selector. Useful for tracking assets from niche sources without an API.

  • Identifier type: URL
  • Key config: current_css_selector, currency, decimal_format

A synthetic, deterministic provider that calculates asset value based on a predefined interest schedule. No external calls, no DB access — pure math.
