docs.title: 🔒 Balance Validation
docs.text:
Transaction batches perform a final end-of-day balance replay before the response is finalized. The stage wrapper is transaction_batch_stages.validate_balances(); the broker replay itself remains TransactionService._validate_broker_balances().

This is validation inside the caller's current database transaction. It is not a commit and it does not own rollback.

docs.title: 🧭 Pipeline Boundary
docs.text:
Balance replay runs after delete, split, update, updated-pair validation, create, promote, create-link resolution, inline WAC/FX handling, and required-cost-basis validation.

TransactionBatchContext.earliest_date_by_broker is updated by successful mutation stages. For each broker, the context retains the minimum date reported by those operations; a moved update uses the earlier of its old and new dates. Immediately before replay, validate_balances():

  1. calls session.flush() so queries see the staged mutations;
  2. maps successful result IDs back to their operation and batch index for issue attribution; and
  3. calls _validate_broker_balances(broker_id, from_date, batch_tx_ids=...) for each affected broker.

docs.title: ⚖️ What Is Validated
docs.text:
Two independent dimensions are tracked per broker:

Dimension Unit Violation Cash Amount per currency code End-of-day cash balance below zero Asset holdings Quantity per asset ID End-of-day asset quantity below zero

Broker settings control each check:

Broker flag Effect when True allow_cash_overdraft Negative cash is permitted allow_asset_shorting Negative asset quantity is permitted

When both flags are true, _validate_broker_balances() returns without querying or replaying transactions.

docs.title: 📅 End-of-day Replay
docs.text:
For an incremental replay beginning at from_date, the service first obtains cash and asset balances from all rows with date < from_date (_get_balances_before_date(), summed in Python, never in SQL: see Balance Queries). It then queries the broker's rows from from_date onward, groups them by date, and applies every row for a date before checking either balance dimension:

balances = SUM(all rows before from_date)

for from_date, then each later date that holds a transaction, in order:
    apply every cash and quantity delta dated that day
    validate all cash balances unless overdraft is allowed
    validate all asset balances unless shorting is allowed

The invariant is therefore end-of-day, not per-row or intraday. Opposing movements on the same date are netted before validation. A later date cannot repair an earlier negative close because each visited date is checked before replay advances.

The replay visits only those dates (R13-SEC7-3): the days that hold a transaction, and from_date, because the balances carried into it may already be negative. No balance changes on a day without transactions, so the first negative close always falls on one of them, and the result is the one a walk over every calendar day gives. Without a from_date — the full replay BrokerService runs when an update turns allow_cash_overdraft or allow_asset_shorting off — the visited dates are the transaction days alone, from the broker's first row. The cost grows with the number of days that hold a transaction, not with the calendar span between them. Before, the replay stepped through every calendar day from its start to the broker's last row, on the event loop: about 740 000 days for a replay starting at a row dated 0001-01-01, while a row dated 9999-12-31 made every later replay of its broker walk up to it, then fail on the date's overflow (a Balance validation error without a code). Such dates can no longer be written (see Transaction dates).

Starting at the earliest affected date preserves correctness for backdated creates, deletes, splits, promotions, and updates without replaying the broker's complete history on every batch.

docs.title: 🚨 Issue Shape and Stop Condition
docs.text:
BalanceValidationError is defined in backend/app/services/transactions/transaction_batch_context.py and carries:

broker_id: int
date: date
currency_or_asset: str
balance: Decimal
code: str
params: dict
batch_index: int
batch_operation: str

The two stable validation codes are:

Code Condition balanceCashNegative A currency closes a day below zero balanceAssetNegative An asset quantity closes a day below zero

Before either, the replay counts the broker's transactions whose quantity or amount cannot be read — a stored value that is no number reads None since W-B58 — with count_unreadable_rows() (unreadable_rows.py), every date included: the starting balances skipped such a row (a wrong balance, the batch checked against it) and the walk failed on it (a codeless error). Any such row stops the replay with a third code, at index −1 since it is the broker's and not a row's (W-B74):

Code Condition ledgerUnreadable params {brokerId, count}: that many transactions of the broker hold a value that is not a number, so its balances cannot be checked

The broker's list cannot show such rows either; the way out is a data repair (W-B63). A broker that allows both overdraft and shorting is not replayed, so it is not refused either.

The frontend turns each code into transactions.errors.<code> (resolveIssueMessage() in lib/features/transactions/resolveValidationMessage.ts): Saving would cause … to go negative … on {date} at {brokerName}. The bulk workspace groups these issues under This configuration causes data inconsistencies (transactions.validate.balanceIssuesHeader), each with the workspace rows that contribute to it.

When possible, the replay attributes the issue to the last staged batch transaction that reduced that currency or asset on the failing date. Otherwise it uses operation create and index -1 as a broker-level fallback.

validate_balances() wraps the broker loop in one try block. It catches the first BalanceValidationError, appends one TXValidationIssue, and exits the stage; it does not continue collecting later balance exceptions from other currencies, dates, or brokers. Unexpected replay exceptions likewise become one broker-level balance-validation issue.

docs.title: 🔁 Transaction Ownership
docs.text:
The replay only flushes the session. Neither the stage nor execute_batch() calls commit() or rollback():

  • /transactions/validate always rolls back after receiving the response;
  • /transactions/commit commits only when response.committed is true;
  • any balance issue makes committed false, so the commit route rolls back all staged mutations.

This caller-owned boundary is what makes a multi-broker batch atomic while still allowing the same service pipeline to power a dry run.

docs.title: ❓ Why End-of-day Instead of a DB Constraint?
docs.text: Running balances depend on the aggregate of all prior rows and cannot be expressed as a simple row constraint. Checking once after all rows for a date also avoids rejecting a valid same-day set merely because of insertion order, while still rejecting a negative close before a later day's deposit or acquisition can mask it.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• 🏗️ Transaction Service — Ordered stages and response semantics
  • ✂️ Split & Promote — Mutations that feed the replay boundary
  • 📖 Access Control (RBAC) — Broker ownership model

docs.title: 🧬 FIFO Lot Engine
docs.text:
The package backend/app/services/financial_math/fifo/ contains LibreFolio's pure, event-sourced FIFO engine for one asset across many brokers. Unlike wac.md, which computes an aggregated per-position weighted average cost, FifoLotEngine keeps individual lots alive through buys, sells, splits, transfers, and adjustments so the "FIFO Lots Analysis" panel can explain which lot moved where, when, and why.

The package belongs to the financial math layer and re-exports nothing: import each name from the module that defines it — the data types (input transactions, events, lots, fragments, closures, economic allocations, FifoEngineResult) from models.py, eligible_income_quantity() from eligibility.py, FifoLotEngine and run_fifo_lot_engine() from engine.py.

Use this vs WAC

FifoLotEngine answers lot-level lifecycle questions: FIFO matching, realized P&L per lot, custody fragments, transfer transit, split-adjusted quantities, and lot history for charts/modals.

portfolio_service.compute_wac_iterative() plus services/financial_math/average_cost.py answer position-level cost basis questions: one running WAC per (broker, asset) scope, suitable for transaction validation and broker summaries.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
The engine is intentionally isolated from I/O:

  • No DB queries
  • No FX conversion
  • No quote_base_quantity scaling
  • No current-price fetches
  • No asset price-feed dependency

It consumes already-loaded transactions plus a few deterministic helpers, then returns a FifoEngineResult. FIFO cost matching and realized P&L always come from real transaction prices (amount / quantity, cost-basis overrides, and split/transfer replay), never from the asset price feed. Open-position valuation is added later by LotsAnalysisService through the unified build_asset_price_series() resolver.

def run_fifo_lot_engine(
    transactions: Sequence[TransactionLike | FifoInputTransaction],
    broker_shorting: dict[int, bool],
    *,
    split_ratios_by_tx_id: dict[int, Decimal] | None = None,
    split_event_ids_by_tx_id: dict[int, int] | None = None,
    reference_price_lookup: ReferencePriceLookup | None = None,
    economic_events: Sequence[EconomicEvent] = (),
    target_currency: str = "",
    replay_until: date | None = None,
) -> FifoEngineResult:

docs.title: ⚙️ Inputs
docs.text: Input Meaning transactions Chronological asset transactions for one asset only. broker_shorting Per-broker flag controlling whether a SELL remainder may open a SHORT lot. split_ratios_by_tx_id Split transaction ID → ratio used to synthesize SPLIT events. split_event_ids_by_tx_id Split transaction ID → its SPLIT AssetEvent id, carried by the synthesized event as asset_event_id. Yield on Cost passes it; the lots analysis does not. reference_price_lookup Optional pure lookup used by current implementation when ADJUSTMENT_IN opens a new LONG lot. The lots analysis passes one that reads the asset's daily marks (see Reference Price); without a lookup, or when it returns None, the lot gets reference_price_source = "unavailable". economic_events Asset-linked DIVIDEND / INTEREST / FEE / TAX as EconomicEvents, each with its native amount and the target-currency amount its caller resolved; consumed by the economic allocation stage. target_currency The caller's report currency; each EconomicEvent also carries its own target_currency. _close_position_piece() also reads it: a lot or a closing price without a currency counts in it when a closure's currency is compared with its lot's (see Closure currency). replay_until The last day the replay reaches; None reaches every event. An event dated after it is neither applied nor returned in classified_events: a lots analysis passes its date_to, so a transfer whose arriving leg is dated later departs and stays IN_TRANSIT (see Transfers In Transit at the End). The pairing still reads both legs.

docs.title: 📤 Output
docs.text:
FifoEngineResult contains:

  • normalized classified_events
  • final lots
  • custody fragment_intervals
  • FIFO closures
  • issues
  • derived analysis_status (COMPLETE, DEGRADED, or FAILED)

The engine does not compute market valuation

FifoEngineResult intentionally exposes no market-valuation helper. Market value (open_quantity / quote_base_quantity * market_price), target-currency FX, and estimated-at-cost fallback are presentation concerns owned by the lots analysis — LotsAnalysisService and its functions in financial_math/lots/ — not this engine. Keeping them out of the engine avoids a latent ×quote_base_quantity valuation bug.

docs.title: 📦 FifoLot
docs.text:
One FIFO lot. Usually opened by a BUY, by the remainder of an ADJUSTMENT_IN, or by a short-opening SELL.

Field Meaning lot_id Stable lot identifier. In practice equals opening transaction ID. asset_id Asset handled by this engine instance. direction "LONG" or "SHORT". opening_transaction_id Source transaction that opened lot. opening_broker_id Broker where lot started. opening_date Opening date. original_quantity Original lot quantity, adjusted later by splits. opening_unit_price Per-unit opening cost currently attached to lot. original_cost Original economic cost basis kept invariant across splits/transfers. currency Currency of the opening price, captured at open time: the opening row's currency for a BUY or a short-opening SELL; for an ADJUSTMENT_IN priced by its cost_basis_override, the cost basis's (cost_basis_currency, or the row's currency when that is empty — an adjustment moves no cash, so its own currency is often empty); for one without, the row's currency. open_quantity Remaining open quantity after FIFO closures. realized_quantity Quantity already closed. realized_pnl Cumulative native realized P&L from closures, in the lot's currency; None from the first closure in another currency on (see Closure currency). cumulative_proceeds Native, in the lot's currency. LONG lots: cumulative closure proceeds — a SELL's cash, plus the value a transfer leg read at the scope's edge hands over (an ADJUSTMENT_OUT read from the database adds 0) — None from the first closure in another currency on. SHORT lots: the opening proceeds, which closures never change. reference_unit_price Optional reference price the engine resolves for a lot (e.g. when an ADJUSTMENT_IN opens a new LONG lot), consumed downstream by LotsAnalysisService. reference_price_source "exact", "fallback", "unavailable", or None.

reference_unit_price is stored on the market/quote_base_quantity axis when the lookup supplies one — resolver marks already live on that axis. When the lot has none — opened by a BUY or a short-opening SELL, or by an ADJUSTMENT_IN with no observation on or before its opening date — opening_reference_price() (financial_math/lots/prices.py) falls back to lot.opening_unit_price * quote_base_quantity before the lots analysis computes relative_return; the engine itself does not know quote_base_quantity.

docs.title: 🧩 FragmentInterval
docs.text:
Custody fragment for one lot. This is what powers Gantt lanes and custody history.

Field Meaning fragment_id Stable fragment key such as origin or transfer-derived IDs. lot_id Owning lot. direction Same lot direction ("LONG" / "SHORT"). custody_type "BROKER" or "IN_TRANSIT". quantity Quantity living in this fragment interval. unit_price Cost per unit carried by this fragment. start_date Inclusive start date. broker_id Broker for broker-custodied fragments. end_date None while fragment is active. source_broker_id Transfer source broker for transit fragments. destination_broker_id Transfer destination broker for transit fragments.

docs.title: 🔚 LotClosure
docs.text:
Single FIFO close operation against one fragment, in native amounts: the lots analysis converts it, each leg at its own date (see Closure currency).

Field Meaning lot_id Closed lot. transaction_id Transaction causing closure. quantity Quantity matched in this closure step. close_date Closure date. close_reason "SELL", "BUY", or "ADJUSTMENT_OUT". fragment_id Exact fragment consumed. open_unit_price Cost carried by the consumed fragment, in the lot's currency. close_unit_price Price the piece closed at, in close_currency: the SELL / BUY unit price; for an ADJUSTMENT_IN closing a SHORT, its cost_basis_override (0 without one); for an ADJUSTMENT_OUT, 0 — a row read from the database never carries a cost basis (N78-1) — or, for a transfer leg read at the scope's edge, the cost_basis_override of its copy, the same for every fragment, or each fragment's own unit cost (hands_over_at_own_cost). realized_pnl Native realized P&L of the piece, in the lot's currency; None when close_currency is not the lot's. proceeds quantity × close_unit_price, in close_currency, on LONG closures — a SELL's cash, or the value a transfer leg read at the scope's edge hands over (0 for an ADJUSTMENT_OUT read from the database); 0 on every SHORT closure. close_currency Currency of close_unit_price and proceeds, None counting as the report currency: a SELL's or BUY's currency; for an ADJUSTMENT_IN closing a SHORT, its cost basis's (cost_basis_currency, or the row's currency when empty) when it carries a cost_basis_override, else the row's currency; for an ADJUSTMENT_OUT, _handover_currency(): the lot's currency without a cost basis (every row read from the database); for a scope-edge copy that carries one, its cost_basis_currency, the lot's when empty.

docs.title: 📊 FifoEngineResult
docs.text:
Returned snapshot of complete run.

Field Meaning asset_id Asset processed by engine. classified_events Normalized event stream after transfer/split classification. lots Final lots sorted by (opening_date, lot_id). fragment_intervals All custody intervals sorted by start date. closures All FIFO closures sorted by close date. issues Data-quality / unsupported-scenario issues. economic_allocation_groups 3-level economic audit (income + FEE/TAX) with source tx, rule, weights, native+target amounts. economic_accumulators_by_lot Per-lot gross_income (signed: a negative income correction lowers it), allocated_fees, allocated_taxes (positive magnitudes), all in the target currency. asset_orphan_income / asset_orphan_fees / asset_orphan_taxes Amounts with no eligible lot, kept at asset level.

Useful helpers on result:

  • analysis_status: "FAILED" if any issue is a non-isolable quantitative-replay error (fails_the_replay(code): a code of _QUANTITATIVE_FAILURE_CODES in models.py), else "DEGRADED" if issues is non-empty, else "COMPLETE"
  • get_lot_states(lot_id): derives LONG/SHORT, OPEN/PARTIALLY_CLOSED/CLOSED, plus IN_TRANSIT, DISTRIBUTED, DEGRADED
  • active_fragments(...): filter live custody fragments

docs.title: 🧠 FifoLotEngine
docs.text:
Mutable runner around pure input/output contract.

Member Purpose __init__(...) Validates non-empty single-asset input and stores runtime config. classify_events() Normalizes raw transactions into FifoEvent objects. run() Applies each event and emits FifoEngineResult. signed_quantity_for_broker() Current signed broker exposure from active broker fragments.

run() dispatches strictly by normalized event kind:

for event in events:
    if event.kind == "BUY":
        self._apply_buy(event)
    elif event.kind == "SELL":
        self._apply_sell(event)
    elif event.kind == "ADJUSTMENT_IN":
        self._apply_adjustment_in(event)
    # ... TRANSFER_DEPART / TRANSFER_ARRIVE / SPLIT

docs.title: 🔁 Event Handling
docs.text:
EventKind is defined exactly as:

EventKind = Literal[
    "BUY",
    "SELL",
    "ADJUSTMENT_IN",
    "ADJUSTMENT_OUT",
    "SPLIT",
    "TRANSFER_DEPART",
    "TRANSFER_ARRIVE",
]

docs.title: 🗂️ Classification rules
docs.text:
• BUY transaction → BUY
  • SELL transaction → SELL
  • positive ADJUSTMENT → ADJUSTMENT_IN, its unit_price the row's cost_basis_override (0 without one)
  • negative ADJUSTMENT → ADJUSTMENT_OUT, its unit_price the row's cost_basis_override (0 without one), which FifoInputTransaction.from_transaction() drops for a row read from the database: such a row has no value, so every fragment closes at 0 (see An ADJUSTMENT_OUT has no value)
  • transaction ID found in split_ratios_by_tx_id → SPLIT, when its ratio passes is_valid_split_ratio(); otherwise the row is skipped: never an ADJUSTMENT_IN / ADJUSTMENT_OUT, no rescale, no exception (lot MF-D4)
  • paired TRANSFER legs → synthesized TRANSFER_DEPART + TRANSFER_ARRIVE

docs.title: 📋 Inventory effects
docs.text:
Event kind Effect on inventory BUY First closes existing SHORT fragments on same broker (close_reason="BUY"). Any remainder opens new LONG lot. SELL Closes LONG fragments FIFO on same broker. Any remainder opens new SHORT lot only if broker_shorting[broker_id] is true; otherwise emits FIFO_SOURCE_QUANTITY_MISSING. ADJUSTMENT_IN First closes existing SHORT fragments on same broker (close_reason="BUY") at the event's unit_price — the row's cost_basis_override, 0 without one — in the cost basis's currency when the row carries one (cost_basis_currency, else the row's currency), else in the row's currency. Any remainder opens a new LONG lot at that price, in that currency, and resolves its reference price. ADJUSTMENT_OUT Closes LONG fragments FIFO on same broker (close_reason="ADJUSTMENT_OUT"): a row read from the database at close_unit_price = 0 in the lot's currency — it has no value, so it realizes minus the fragments' cost; a transfer leg read at the scope's edge on a day with a price, at its copy's cost_basis_override, the market value of one unit that day, in cost_basis_currency (the lot's currency when empty); flagged hands_over_at_own_cost (a transfer leg leaving the lots' scope on a day without a price, see Transfers Across the Scope's Edge), every fragment at its own FIFO unit cost in the lot's currency — realized 0. If quantity still missing, engine emits issue; it never opens/consumes unsupported SHORT adjustment legs. TRANSFER_DEPART Extracts LONG broker fragments FIFO from source broker, optionally opens IN_TRANSIT fragments, records pending transfer pieces, realizes no P&L. TRANSFER_ARRIVE Closes matching transit fragments and reopens broker custody at destination with same quantity and unit price. SPLIT Multiplies active fragment quantities by ratio, divides unit prices by ratio, then recomputes lot-level quantities/reference price while preserving cost.

Event ordering on same date

classify_events() sorts same-day events as TRANSFER_DEPART → TRANSFER_ARRIVE → SPLIT → ordinary transactions. This preserves half-open transfer intervals and lets same-day splits see post-transfer custody state.

docs.title: ⛏️ FIFO Matching Algorithm
docs.text:
FIFO is enforced by _broker_fragments(), which sorts active broker fragments by lot age:

return sorted(
    [fragment for fragment in self._active_fragments.values() if ...],
    key=lambda fragment: (
        self._lots[fragment.lot_id].opening_date,
        fragment.lot_id,
        fragment.start_date,
        fragment.fragment_id,
    ),
)

Then _consume_broker_fragments() walks oldest fragments first:

  1. Select matching broker fragments for one direction
  2. Take matched = min(remaining, fragment.quantity)
  3. Call _close_position_piece(...)
  4. Reduce fragment or close it entirely
  5. Continue until requested quantity is satisfied or inventory runs out

Every fragment closes at the one close_unit_price the caller passes, in the close_currency it passes or in the one the optional per-fragment hook close_currency_of(fragment) gives it. _apply_sell() and _apply_buy() pass the row's currency, _apply_adjustment_in() the currency of its price; only _apply_adjustment_out() passes the hook, _handover_currency(), since a fragment it closes without a cost basis, or with one that has no currency, closes in its own lot's currency (see An ADJUSTMENT_OUT has no value).

docs.title: 🧮 Realized P&L math
docs.text:
• LONG close: matched_quantity * (close_unit_price - fragment.unit_price)
  • SHORT close: matched_quantity * (fragment.unit_price - close_unit_price)

Both are native, in the lot's currency, and computed only when the closure is in that currency (see Closure currency). SELL and ADJUSTMENT_OUT — the two closures of LONG inventory — create proceeds = matched_quantity * close_unit_price: a sale's cash, or the value a scope-edge transfer leg hands over. An ADJUSTMENT_OUT read from the database closes at 0, in the lot's currency: no proceeds, and it realizes -matched_quantity * fragment.unit_price. BUY and ADJUSTMENT_IN close SHORT inventory but do not add proceeds.

docs.title: 💱 Closure currency
docs.text:
A closure's two prices can be in two currencies: open_unit_price in the lot's (FifoLot.currency), close_unit_price and proceeds in close_currency (see the LotClosure table). A lot moved to a broker of another currency and sold there closes in the sale's currency; a scope-edge transfer leg whose price is in another currency than the lot's closes in that price's.

The engine has no rates, so _close_position_piece() computes the native realized P&L only when the two currencies are the same — None counts as target_currency on both sides, as the lots analysis reads an amount without a currency. Otherwise:

  • the closure's realized_pnl is None;
  • the lot's realized_pnl is None from that closure on, and so is a LONG lot's cumulative_proceeds.

The figures in the report currency are the lots analysis's: convert_closure() converts each leg at its own date — the lot's side at the lot's opening date, the closing side at the closure date — and never reads the native realized_pnl (developer decision 26; see Closures: each leg at its own date).

docs.title: 📤 An ADJUSTMENT_OUT has no value
docs.text:
A negative ADJUSTMENT has no value, whatever cost_basis_override the row holds (developer decision N78-1, 21/10/2026): its units only leave the quantity. FifoInputTransaction.from_transaction() drops the override and its currency of every such row read from the database, so the event's unit_price is 0 and every fragment closes at 0 in its lot's currency: proceeds = 0, realized_pnl = -matched_quantity * fragment.unit_price. The Dashboard agrees: no capital leaves, and the average cost the pool gives up is realized as a loss (DailyStateBuilder, see WAC & Cost Basis — Portfolio engine). Example, in one currency: 10 units bought at 50; an ADJUSTMENT_OUT of 2 closes 2 units of that lot at 0 — realized_pnl = -100, proceeds = 0 — and the 8 left keep their unit cost of 50.

Until N78-1 a cost basis on the row handed the units over at that cost (decision 47, J-24): every fragment closed at it, and the Dashboard took that value out of the capital. The API now refuses one on such a row (costBasisNotAllowed, rule 12b); one an older version stored stays in the database, ignored.

The engine keeps the mechanics of a priced ADJUSTMENT_OUT for the copies the lots analysis builds itself (J-10, financial_math/lots/scope_boundary.py): a transfer leg leaving the analysed brokers is read as an ADJUSTMENT_OUT at the market value of one unit on its day, in the mark's currency, or, on a day without a price, flagged hands_over_at_own_cost (see Transfers Across the Scope's Edge). _handover_currency(tx, fragment) gives each closure its close_currency: the copy's cost_basis_currency, or the lot's currency when it is empty or the row carries no cost basis. A price in another currency than the lot's leaves the closure's native realized_pnl None (see Closure currency); the lots analysis converts each leg at its own date.

docs.title: ✂️ Split Handling
docs.text: _apply_split() transforms active fragments in split scope, not historical intervals.

docs.title: 🎯 Split scope
docs.text:
Current judgement call in code:

  • broker fragments match when fragment.broker_id == split broker
  • in-transit fragments match when source_broker_id == split broker or destination_broker_id == split broker

docs.title: 🔄 Ratio transformation
docs.text:
For each impacted fragment:

  • new_quantity = fragment.quantity * ratio
  • new_unit_price = fragment.unit_price / ratio
  • fragment cost must remain invariant

After fragment transitions, engine updates each impacted lot:

  • recompute open_quantity
  • adjust original_quantity
  • recompute opening_unit_price = original_cost / original_quantity
  • scale reference_unit_price by old_open_qty / new_open_qty when available

Split invariant uses tolerance, not exact equality

_COST_INVARIANT_TOLERANCE = Decimal("0.01") exists because ratios like 3:1 produce non-terminating decimals under default Decimal precision. Sub-cent drift from truncation is tolerated; larger drift raises AssertionError.

docs.title: 🚚 Transfer Handling
docs.text: Transfers are modeled as custody moves, not disposals.

docs.title: 🔗 Pair normalization
docs.text:
classify_events() accepts only bidirectional TRANSFER pairs where:

  • both rows are TRANSFER
  • each row points to other via related_transaction_id
  • one leg quantity is negative, other positive
  • absolute quantities match
  • both legs belong to same asset

Otherwise engine records TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING and skips pair. The engine sees only the rows it is given: a lots analysis reads a leg whose partner pairs back from a broker outside its scope before the replay, as an adjustment (see Transfers Across the Scope's Edge), so that leg never reaches this rule.

docs.title: 🛫 Depart
docs.text:
TRANSFER_DEPART:

  1. refuses current SHORT exposure on source broker (SHORT_TRANSFER_NOT_SUPPORTED)
  2. extracts source LONG fragments FIFO
  3. shrinks/closes source broker fragments
  4. opens IN_TRANSIT fragment when transit_start < transit_end
  5. stores _PendingTransferPiece until arrival

Both issues a departure can record (SHORT_TRANSFER_NOT_SUPPORTED, and FIFO_SOURCE_QUANTITY_MISSING when the source broker holds less than the leg moves) name the giving leg, the row to fix: raw_transaction_ids[0], the out leg of the pair (J-12). The event's own transaction_id is the pair's, which may be the receiving leg.

docs.title: 🛬 Arrive
docs.text:
TRANSFER_ARRIVE:

  1. pops pending pieces for pair_id
  2. closes transit fragment on arrival date if one exists
  3. opens destination BROKER fragment with same quantity and unit_price

Lot identity stays same across brokers, so frontend can render one lot life with changing custody lanes.

docs.title: 💸 Economic Allocation Stage
docs.text: After the replay loop, run() calls _allocate_economics(). This stage is read-only with respect to inventory: quantities, fragments and closures are never mutated. It consumes economic_events (DIVIDEND / INTEREST / FEE / TAX, each carrying a native_amount and a target_amount) and produces per-lot accumulators, an audit trail, and asset-level orphans.

docs.title: 💵 Income (DIVIDEND / INTEREST)
docs.text:
_allocate_income_pools() groups income by pool key (broker, date, economic_type, native_currency, target_currency) and allocates it to eligible lots:

  • Eligibility = D-1: a lot is eligible if it has open LONG quantity as of date - 1 (eligible_income_quantity(...), eligibility.py), scoped to the paying broker (including quantity that left that broker as IN_TRANSIT). A BUY made on the income date is therefore not eligible; a lot already closed by end of date - 1 is not either. It is the shared D-1 eligibility seam: transaction-ledger Yield on Cost (backend/app/services/financial_math/yield_on_cost.py) counts eligible quantity with the same public function.
  • weight w_i = EligibleQty_i / Σ EligibleQty_j, distributed with a running remainder so the pool total is conserved exactly;
  • signed amounts: a pool sums its native_amount / target_amount values with their sign, as the Dashboard does (NativeCash.flows() keeps income signed; developer decision D-MF3): a negative correction lowers the income of the lots, and an orphan pool can be negative;
  • no eligible lot → the whole pool becomes asset_orphan_income, with an ASSET_INCOME_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS issue and an audit group tagged ASSET_INCOME_HOLDINGS.

docs.title: 💸 FEE / TAX
docs.text:
_allocate_cost_pools() pools asset-linked cost and matches it to operations with a deterministic ladder (_match_cost_operations), weighting by target_amount. Unlike income, a cost pool sums its amounts in absolute value, as the Dashboard counts fees and taxes:

Cost Matching order (first non-empty wins) FEE same-day trades → previous-day trades → holdings fallback → orphan TAX same-day income → same-day trades → previous-day income → previous-day trades → holdings fallback → orphan

The chosen rule is recorded per group (SAME_DAY_MIXED_TRADES, SAME_DAY_TRADES, PREVIOUS_DAY_TRADES, OPEN_LOTS_FALLBACK, income-linked variants). Allocation to a matched trade crosses to the lots that trade touched (BUY → the opened lot; SELL → the FIFO-consumed lots), so a cost follows the same lots the FIFO algorithm already selected. A cost with no eligible target becomes asset_orphan_fees / asset_orphan_taxes.

Per-pool conservation (locked by tests)

For every pool: Σ allocated_to_lots + orphan == converted pool total. TestEconomicConservation asserts this invariant, so allocated FEE/TAX/income can never be silently lost or double-counted.

docs.title: 🔎 Three-level audit
docs.text:
Each pool emits an EconomicAllocationGroup (level 1) → operation_allocations (level 2, one per matched BUY/SELL/income) → lot_allocations (level 3, one per lot), all carrying source_transaction_ids, rule, weight, and both native_* and target_* amounts. The service maps these to economic_allocation_groups for the response; the frontend does not yet render the provenance (only the numeric net breakdown).

Costs without an asset are out of scope here

FEE / TAX with asset_id = null are excluded from economic_events entirely — the Portfolio Engine accounts for them. Only asset-linked cost reaches this stage.

docs.title: 📈 Net annualization handoff
docs.text: The engine returns realized P&L plus economic accumulators; lot_summary_figures() (financial_math/lots/summary.py), called by LotsAnalysisService._build_lot_summaries(), derives total_pnl, subtracts allocated FEE/TAX into net_total_pnl, computes net_total_return, and annualizes that net figure over opening_date → closing_date (closed lots) or opening_date → analysis_end (open lots). The shipped LotSummarySchema.annualized_return therefore annualizes net_total_return, not gross total_return.

docs.title: ⚠️ Known Constraints and Gotchas
docs.text:
SHORT support is intentionally partial

SELL may open SHORT lots when broker shorting is enabled, and BUY / positive adjustment may close them. TRANSFER_DEPART on SHORT inventory and ADJUSTMENT_OUT against SHORT inventory are currently rejected with SHORT_TRANSFER_NOT_SUPPORTED and SHORT_ADJUSTMENT_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Reference price behavior is narrower in code than broad system docs may suggest

Current implementation calls _resolve_reference_price() only in _apply_adjustment_in() before opening a remainder LONG lot. Ordinary BUY openings pass reference_resolution=None, so many lots will have reference_unit_price is None unless populated by adjustment flow.

Estimated valuation lives outside FIFO

The engine has no ESTIMATED_AT_COST branch and does not emit CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST. On a day with no observation on or before it — no quote, no BUY or SELL, no transfer cost estimate — the lots analysis values the open slice of a LONG lot at cost, with no market P&L (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback); a trade-origin mark is a price, flagged estimated=True on the price series (price_history, market_price_history).

Issues degrade result instead of aborting run

Missing source quantity, broken transfer pairs, and reference-price gaps are recorded in issues; the replay loop never raises, so the engine still returns best-effort lots/fragments/closures for the rest of the input stream. analysis_status then becomes DEGRADED for isolable (economic) issues, or FAILED for quantity-topology breakages (oversell, broken transfer, short-not-supported) that cannot be isolated because they change which lots later events consume via FIFO order.
