docs.title: 📊 Lots Analysis Service
docs.text:
backend/app/services/lots_analysis_service.py is the orchestration layer behind POST /portfolio/lots/analysis.

It runs FifoLotEngine once, then converts engine output into LotsAnalysisResponse: FX-normalized values, qbq-aware valuations from the unified price resolver, lot/event histories, WAC series, income allocation, and valuation at cost on the days the asset has no price yet. Frontend consumer: LotsAnalysisPanel.svelte.

docs.title: 🗂️ Where the Code Lives
docs.text:
The service keeps the orchestration (get_lots_analysis()), the database loaders, the response builders — lot summaries (_build_lot_summaries()), Gantt segments (_build_gantt_segments()), event rows (_build_lot_event_rows()) — and the analysis' data-quality report (_build_data_quality_report(), _report_gaps()). The pure math it calls lives in the financial math layer, as functions of backend/app/services/financial_math/lots/ that take every input as an argument:

Module What it holds prices.py What the lots read from the asset's AssetPriceSeries: opening_reference_price(), a lot's reference price at its opening (see Reference Price), and last_day_without_observation(), the last day valued at cost, found by bisection (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback) conversions.py FxRateResolver; convert_closure() → ConvertedClosure, a closure's two legs each in its own currency at its own date, and need_closure_rates(), the two rates it reads (see Closures: each leg at its own date); the conversions each view needs: collect_fx_needs(), collect_performance_fx_needs(), needs_market_series(), unconvertible_ids() economic_events.py The engine's income and FEE/TAX inputs (build_income_economic_events(), build_cost_economic_events(), build_engine_transactions()), their outputs (extract_income_outputs(), extract_cost_outputs()), WithheldEconomics / withheld_economics() and map_economic_groups() histories.py The value, return, price, market price and performance histories (build_value_history(), build_return_history(), build_price_history(), build_market_price_history(), build_performance_history()) with their per-day snapshot helpers, lot_history_end_date(), known_realized_pnl(), known_cumulative_proceeds() change_days.py The days the daily series can change on: lot_change_days(), over the dates analysis_event_dates() gathers, and expand_to_days(), which fills every day of the window from them (see Change Days) summary.py A lot's figures, read by the lot summary and the histories: residual_cost(), the original cost of the quantity still open (also the AI Export's lot_residual_cost_basis()); lot_value(), a lot's total value and P&L by direction; lot_summary_figures() → LotSummaryFigures, the lot summary's computed figures from its converted inputs — _build_lot_summaries() gathers those inputs and maps the result average_cost_lines.py ALL_BROKERS, and the broker and cumulative WAC history points (build_broker_wac_history(), build_cumulative_wac_history(), average_cost_points())

FxRateResolver.load() is the package's only async step and its only I/O: one unit_rate_steps() call for the rates asked since the previous load, read as steps (L1b, see FX Conversion). The FIFO replay is in financial_math/fifo/ (FIFO Lot Engine), the daily marks in financial_math/price_marks.py (Price Resolver). The functions of lots/ and the service's sync builders are tested by ./dev.py test services lots-analysis-pure.

docs.title: 🛣️ Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /portfolio/lots/analysis

Router entrypoint:

@portfolio_router.post("/lots/analysis", response_model=LotsAnalysisResponse)
async def get_lots_analysis(body: LotsAnalysisQuery, ...):
    ...
    return await service.get_lots_analysis(
        user_id=current_user.id,
        asset_id=body.asset_id,
        broker_ids=body.broker_ids,
        date_from=date_from,
        date_to=date_to,
        target_currency=body.target_currency,
        selected_lot_ids=body.selected_lot_ids,
        requested_analyses=body.requested_analyses,
    )

If date_range contains min/max sentinels, router resolves them before calling service.

docs.title: 🧾 Request Body — LotsAnalysisQuery
docs.text: Field Type Required Notes asset_id int Yes Asset to analyze broker_ids list[int] \| None No None = all accessible brokers date_range OpenDateRangeModel \| None No Limits emitted histories/visible intervals, not engine starting state target_currency str \| None No Defaults to global base currency selected_lot_ids list[int] \| None No Lot subset for lot-scoped analyses requested_analyses list[LotAnalysisType] Yes Non-empty, duplicates rejected

docs.title: 🧩 LotAnalysisType
docs.text: Enum member Response field Meaning LOT_SUMMARY lots One row per lot with scalar metrics, states, custody, current valuation GANTT_TOPOLOGY gantt_segments Custody fragments for Gantt lanes CUSTODY_HISTORY custody_history Custody-only event subset EVENT_HISTORY lot_events Full lot chronology: openings, splits, transfers, closures VALUE_HISTORY value_history Per-lot open_value, proceeds, total_value, pnl, income RETURN_HISTORY return_history Per-lot total_return, relative_return, income PRICE_HISTORY price_history Per-lot market-price series, over each selected lot's life; the app no longer requests it MARKET_PRICE_HISTORY market_price_history The asset's market-price series, one point a day whatever lots are open (MarketPriceHistoryPoint: a LotPriceHistoryPoint without lot_id); ignores lot selection, kept with FAILED BROKER_WAC_HISTORY broker_wac_history Broker-scoped WAC time series CUMULATIVE_WAC_HISTORY cumulative_wac_history Combined WAC time series PERFORMANCE_HISTORY performance_history Asset-wide ROI/TWRR, ignores lot selection INCOME_EVENTS income_events Dividend/interest markers allocated to open LONG lots

docs.title: 📦 Response Shape — LotsAnalysisResponse
docs.text:
Top-level fields always present:

Field Meaning asset_id Requested asset target_currency Final response currency quote_base_quantity Asset qbq, needed by frontend price/WAC axis calculation_status COMPLETE, DEGRADED, or FAILED (public global status; an empty-but-valid analysis is COMPLETE). A COMPLETE engine run becomes DEGRADED when a conversion is missing — in a WAC line or in any other figure of the analysis — or a WAC line misses a cost basis (see FX Conversion and WAC Lines). With FAILED the lot figures are withheld (see A Failed Reconstruction) calculation_metadata Broker scope, selection, requested/computed date bounds, generation date data_quality FIFO/data-quality issues mapped to UI-friendly DTOs economic_allocation_groups 3-level economic audit (income + FEE/TAX) mapped from the engine, None unless LOT_SUMMARY requested asset_orphan_income / asset_orphan_fees / asset_orphan_taxes Amounts that belonged to no eligible lot, kept at asset level (never dropped, never double-counted)

All analysis payload sections are None unless explicitly requested — and, with FAILED, every section but the WAC lines and the market price series (see A Failed Reconstruction).

docs.title: ⚙️ Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
Service entrypoint:

async def get_lots_analysis(
    self,
    user_id: int,
    asset_id: int,
    broker_ids: list[int] | None,
    date_from: date_type | None,
    date_to: date_type | None,
    target_currency: str | None,
    selected_lot_ids: list[int] | None,
    requested_analyses: list[str | LotAnalysisType],
) -> LotsAnalysisResponse:

High-level flow:

  1. Load accessible brokers, asset transactions, split ratios, broker shorting flags, price_history, asset income and FEE / TAX transactions. A split whose stored ratio fails is_valid_split_ratio() stays in the ratio map, so its row is still split-linked and the WAC lines still treat it as a split, but the FIFO engine skips it: no lot is rescaled, lot_events has no SPLIT row for it, and the analysis reports no issue (lot MF-D4).
  2. Build one qbq-aware resolver series with build_asset_price_series(), from the price_history rows and the loaded transactions — before the engine, which reads it for reference prices (see Unified Price Resolver). Then read the transfer legs that cross the scope's edge with read_transfers_at_scope_boundary(): every later step reads the list it returns (see Transfers Across the Scope's Edge).
  3. When a requested analysis reads income, fees or taxes, build the engine's economic inputs first — income and FEE / TAX events and the BUY / SELL amounts that weight the FEE / TAX split, each converted at its own date (build_income_economic_events(), build_cost_economic_events(), build_engine_transactions()). Then build reference_price_lookup() over the series (see Reference Price) and run run_fifo_lot_engine(...).
  4. Resolve selected lots, and the days valued at cost: at_cost_until = last_day_without_observation(price_series, history_dates) (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback).
  5. Collect needed FX pairs with collect_fx_needs() / collect_performance_fx_needs(), then batch-load rates through FxRateResolver.
  6. Extract the engine's economic stage outputs — income, FEE/TAX and net metrics — with extract_income_outputs() and extract_cost_outputs() (allocation itself happens inside the engine, not here).
  7. Convert the marks of the days the requested analyses read into the two valuation maps, market_prices and estimated_market_prices, both from the same series.
  8. When BROKER_WAC_HISTORY or CUMULATIVE_WAC_HISTORY is requested, compute the average-cost lines with one compute_average_costs() call (see WAC Lines); their gaps — missing rates, unknown costs — are reported in step 11.
  9. Compute the change days once, with lot_change_days(): the days of history_dates on which a daily series can change. The seven daily builders run on those days only, and expand_to_days() fills every day of the window, [display_from, actual_to], from the last change day on or before it (see Change Days).
  10. Emit only requested DTO sections.
  11. Once every builder has run, report the gaps once, for the whole analysis: _report_gaps() adds to data_quality the WAC lines' gaps and every conversion FxRateResolver could not make (see FX Conversion).

Step 1's broker scope comes from _get_scope_broker_ids(): every broker the user can access, in any role, intersected with broker_ids when given. No owner share is applied anywhere in the analysis — quantities, values and P&L are each broker's full figures, unlike the portfolio summary, which scales an OWNER's brokers by their share_percentage. The lot modal says so next to its quantities (brokers.lots.modal.absoluteQuantityTooltip).

docs.title: ↔️ Transfers Across the Scope's Edge
docs.text:
A scope can hold one leg of a transfer and not the other: broker_ids names the receiver alone, or a co-owner sees one of the two brokers. The engine replays the scope's rows only, so on its own it could not pair that leg and would fail the whole asset (TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING). Instead, read_transfers_at_scope_boundary() (financial_math/lots/scope_boundary.py, J-10, decision N76) reads the leg the way the scope sees it, as the broker-scope Dashboard does:

Leg Read as Effect In (quantity > 0) An ADJUSTMENT in, at the leg's own cost_basis_override / cost_basis_currency (the Auto cost a receiving leg carries) A new lot opens on the arrival day at that cost. Without a cost basis (old data) it is a costless adjustment: MISSING_COST_BASIS, DEGRADED Out (quantity < 0) An ADJUSTMENT out, at the market value of its own day: the resolver's mark brought to one unit (compute_holding_value), in the mark's currency The lots close on the departure day; the scope realizes market − FIFO cost, the gain the units made while in it Out, no observation on or before its day An ADJUSTMENT out flagged hands_over_at_own_cost Each fragment leaves at its own FIFO cost: realized 0. The day is one the analysis already values at cost (CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST)
  • When. Only when the partner (related_transaction_id) exists, sits at a broker outside the scope and pairs back: a TRANSFER, linked to the leg, of the same asset, of the opposite sign and the same absolute quantity — the checks of the engine's own pairing. A pair really missing or broken is left as it is, and the engine still fails it.
  • What is read of the partner. Its pairing columns only (_read_at_scope_boundary() selects id, broker, asset, type, quantity and link): never an amount or a cost, so nothing of a broker outside the scope reaches the figures — for an owner filtering one broker as for a co-owner who sees only one.
  • Detached copies. Each read leg is a FifoInputTransaction (type ADJUSTMENT, no link, amount 0) in the leg's place; the ORM rows are never changed. The split ratios and the price series come from the rows as loaded, before the reading: a TRANSFER or an ADJUSTMENT is never a split link nor an observation.
  • Every reader. The engine, the histories, the conversions and the average-cost lines all read the returned list. FifoInputTransaction.from_transaction() hands a copy back as it is, so the flag survives build_engine_transactions().
  • Labels. The rows of a read leg keep the adjustment kind, which every figure reads, and carry LotTimelineEventSchema.scope_boundary for their label (J-48): IN on the arriving leg's opening row (ADJUSTMENT_IN), OUT on every closure row of the departing leg (ADJUSTMENT_OUT), None on every other row. _build_lot_event_rows() passes boundary.legs to _build_opening_and_split_rows() and _build_closure_rows(), and _boundary_direction() looks each row's transaction_id up there. A label only: the partner broker is never named. The lot views show such a row as a transfer (see Lots Analysis).
  • Performance. build_performance_history() moves a read leg's market value of the day across the scope — money in for a leg that arrives, out for one that leaves — through PerformanceSourceContext.boundary_legs, exactly as it counts a transfer whose two legs the re-run over the accessible brokers holds. The two paths give the same series. The re-run reads the edge of the accessible brokers in turn, for a partner at a broker the user cannot see. On a day valued at cost a leg moves the cost of its units instead (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback).
  • Yield on cost. financial_math/yield_on_cost.py reads the arrivals alone, with read_arrivals_at_scope_boundary() (J-51): an arrival whose partner pairs back from a broker the user cannot see becomes an ADJUSTMENT in, and its partner leaves the replay, which would otherwise join a broker with no history and fail. A departure keeps its partner, because the yield on cost counts units in transit for the broker they left. It needs no price: the yield's cost is the Dashboard's average cost of the position, never the replay's.
  • The same rule as the Dashboard. In a broker's own view the Dashboard counts an incoming leg's cost basis in the average cost and its market value as capital, and an outgoing leg's market value as the capital that left (lot 41, D2 and D5): lots and Dashboard agree broker by broker.

The timeline shows a read leg as an ADJUSTMENT_IN / ADJUSTMENT_OUT row, with scope_boundary set.

docs.title: ⏳ Transfers In Transit at the End
docs.text:
The analysis reads the rows up to date_to, so a transfer still on its way that day (departure ≤ date_to < arrival, in either order of the two legs' dates) would lose its arriving leg, and the engine would fail the asset (TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING) even over every broker (J-47). The Dashboard keeps such units in transit from the departure to the arrival; the lots do the same:

  • _load_late_transfer_legs() loads the partners, dated after date_to, of the scope's TRANSFER legs that sit in the scope (same asset, a TRANSFER), as detached FifoInputTransaction copies. They go to the engine only: no history, WAC line or rate reaches past date_to.
  • The engine replays up to date_to (replay_until): the arrival is not applied, so the fragment stays IN_TRANSIT, valued at market like any open fragment. The lot carries the IN_TRANSIT state, the Gantt draws the transit to the end, and the timeline has the TRANSFER_DEPART row and no TRANSFER_ARRIVE (_build_transfer_rows() writes no arrival for a fragment still in transit).
  • The re-run over the accessible brokers of PERFORMANCE_HISTORY does the same. Its performance counts the transit value only when both brokers are in the requested scope (_fragment_in_scope), as the Dashboard's combined view.
  • A partner outside the scope is read at the scope's edge instead (see Transfers Across the Scope's Edge), whatever its date.

docs.title: 📅 A Transfer That Leaves and Arrives the Same Day
docs.text:
A move that takes days leaves an IN_TRANSIT fragment, which names its source and destination broker: _build_transfer_rows() reads a TRANSFER_DEPART row and a TRANSFER_ARRIVE row off it. A move that leaves and arrives on one day opens no transit (transfer_date < arrival_date is false in the engine), so its only piece is the destination fragment lot:{lot}/transfer:{pair}/to:{broker}, which names neither (J-68). The pair's brokers are in the engine's classified TRANSFER_DEPART events: _transfer_brokers() maps each pair id to its (source, destination), and the service gives the move the same two rows on that day:

  • the TRANSFER_DEPART row names no broker of its own and carries both ids, as a move of days does;
  • the TRANSFER_ARRIVE row keeps the destination as its broker_id and carries both ids too;
  • both read the destination fragment (fragment_id, quantity and price), and the departure sorts first, though both share the pair id as transaction_id.

A piece whose pair the replay did not classify (a leg read at the scope's edge, whose partner sits outside it) keeps its one arrival row and names no origin. No figure changes: the histories read the fragments, not these rows.

docs.title: 🛑 A Failed Reconstruction
docs.text:
A replay that hits a quantitative failure is FAILED: a code of _QUANTITATIVE_FAILURE_CODES — a sale or a transfer beyond the quantity held (FIFO_SOURCE_QUANTITY_MISSING), a transfer or an adjustment out of SHORT inventory (SHORT_TRANSFER_NOT_SUPPORTED, SHORT_ADJUSTMENT_NOT_SUPPORTED), a transfer leg without its partner (TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING). The lots it leaves do not match what the account holds, and every later event consumes the wrong ones, so every lot figure would be wrong. Missing data is declared, never shown wrong (J-12, decision N81): right after the engine, the service keeps only the analyses that do not read the lots, _REPLAY_FREE_ANALYSES: the two average-cost lines and, since Y-30, the market price series.

  • Withheld. Every section that reads the lots is None, requested or not: lots, gantt_segments, custody_history, lot_events, value_history, return_history, price_history (one series per lot), performance_history, income_events and economic_allocation_groups, and the three orphan totals. After the replay no rate is registered for them and no lot is valued.
  • Kept. The WAC lines (broker_wac_history, cumulative_wac_history) come from the transactions, and the market price series (market_price_history) from the asset's price series — its quotes and its BUY / SELL marks — not from the replay: they are built as usual, with their gaps. So are quote_base_quantity, calculation_metadata — whose requested_analyses are still those asked for — and data_quality.
  • The issues. data_quality holds the issues that fail the replay and the gaps of what is kept (_report_gaps()): the missing rates of the WAC lines and of the market price series — each pair in missing_fx_pairs, with its MISSING_FX_MARKET / MISSING_FX_RATES issue — and the WAC lines' MISSING_COST_BASIS. The issues about what is withheld are left out: REFERENCE_PRICE_FALLBACK / REFERENCE_PRICE_UNAVAILABLE, ASSET_INCOME_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS / ASSET_COST_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS, CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST — the market price series values nothing at cost — and the rates of the lot figures. One exception: when a requested analysis reads income, fees or taxes, the income and FEE / TAX events, and the BUY / SELL amounts that weight the FEE / TAX split, are converted before the replay (step 3 above), and a rate missing there is still reported.
  • The row to fix. _build_data_quality_report() gives each issue that fails the replay (fails_the_replay(), financial_math/fifo/models.py) two more message_params: transaction_date, the ISO date of its transaction_id, and fails_analysis: true, so a reader needs no list of codes. transaction_id is always a row of the scope — for a transfer, the giving leg (see Depart); a copy read at the scope's edge or still in transit keeps the id of its row. related_transaction_id is the partner, never the row to fix.

analysis_failure_codes(response) reads them back: the sorted unique codes of the issues that carry fails_analysis. The AI Export declares a FAILED asset with them instead of exporting its lots (see Snapshot Data Tables). A DEGRADED analysis is not concerned: its gaps are isolable, and its figures stay.

docs.title: 💱 FX Conversion
docs.text:
FxRateResolver (financial_math/lots/conversions.py) is a thin prefetch + conversion helper. It reads its rates as steps (L1b): a rate only changes on the days a row is stored, so it asks for the windows of days it needs, never for one conversion a day.

  • need(currency, as_of_date) asks the rate of one day; a day inside a window need_days() already asked adds nothing
  • need_days(currency, first, last) asks every day of [first, last] for one currency: nothing for a blank code, for the target currency, or for a window that ends before it starts
  • load(session) makes one unit_rate_steps() call (FX Architecture) for every currency asked since the previous load — a single-day need() is a one-day window, and a load with nothing new asks nothing. It keeps the rates as steps, answered on the asked days only (AskedDayRates, financial_math/fx_rates.py): one map per load, and a day nobody asked has no rate. Each currency is still read as Currency(code=…) writes it, so usd reads the USD rates and a code Currency refuses raises at load; a currency that is the target under another spelling (eur for EUR) converts at exactly 1. The values are, digit for digit, those of one convert_bulk() unit per day, the contract of unit_rate_steps()
  • convert(amount, currency, as_of_date) applies date-specific conversion into target_currency — an amount without a currency is taken as already in it; a conversion it cannot make — a non-None amount in a currency other than the target, with no loaded rate for that (currency, date) — returns None and is recorded
  • missing_pairs() returns the recorded misses as WACMissingPairInfo(pair, dates), one entry per FROM/TO pair with its dates sorted

Service converts:

  • lot opening cost and opening unit price
  • each selected lot's reference price, from its currency at the lot's opening date (see Reference Price)
  • event-history opening rows (BUY / ADJUSTMENT_IN, _build_opening_and_split_rows()): the opening unit price, from the lot's currency at the opening date — a BUY's own currency, the cost basis's for an ADJUSTMENT_IN priced by its cost_basis_override (see FifoLot.currency in FIFO Lot Engine); and opening_value, the lot's original cost at the opening date — the summary's original_cost, in the currency of unit_price; for these rows collect_fx_needs() registers the lot's currency on every opening event
  • closures, through convert_closure() alone: each leg in its own currency at its own date — the lot's side at the lot's opening date, the closing side at the closure date — the value a scope-edge transfer leg hands over included (see Closures: each leg at its own date)
  • Gantt fragment unit prices
  • native resolver marks from build_asset_price_series(), each at the date it values: when an analysis reads the market series (needs_market_series()) or MARKET_PRICE_HISTORY is requested, even alone, collect_fx_needs() asks one window per currency of the marks — the price rows' and the BUY / SELL trades' — need_days(currency, computed_from, actual_to), every history day of it
  • dividend / interest and FEE / TAX amounts, and the BUY / SELL amounts that weight the FEE / TAX split (economic-stage inputs)
  • performance-history external flows

One window, not one need a day. Before L1b the market series asked each currency one need() a day and load() handed convert_bulk() one conversion per need: a lot bought on 2 January 1900 meant about 44 000 needs and a 44 000-conversion call, to answer a window of a month. Now it is one window per currency, read in one unit_rate_steps() call per load — the cost follows the rows stored, not the days asked. What stays daily, by design: the conversion of each day's mark (the service's per-day loop over history_dates, FxRateResolver.convert() on each), the record of each day without a rate in missing_pairs(), and the scan of lot_change_days() over those marks (see Change Days).

No native fallback. A figure that needs a missing rate is never computed from the unconverted amount — it is None, or it has no point:

  • Daily valuation: a mark whose rate is missing leaves that day unvalued — market_prices[date] is None, the day has no point in either price series (price_history, market_price_history), and a still-open lot has no value or return point that day. Never at cost: only a MISSING day, with no observation on or before it (up to at_cost_until), values a lot at cost; see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback.
  • Value and return histories (_lot_value_basis() and _lot_snapshot_on_date(), shared by both builders): a lot whose original cost — or, for a SHORT, its proceeds — has no rate gets no point; a lot's series stops the day before the first closure whose proceeds — for a SHORT, its buy-back cost — have no rate (_closure_prefix(lot, closures, fx_resolver, leg), in financial_math/lots/histories.py, returns the running sum of that converted leg by close date and that date). Same rule as the WAC Lines: a point that cannot be computed is omitted. Within an emitted point, the income, fee and tax fields that a degraded economic pool withholds — and the figures read from them — are None instead (see Economic events and degraded pools).
  • Performance history: a BUY amount, an ADJUSTMENT-in's money (_adjustment_native_cost() / adjustment_cash_flow_cost()) or a SELL closure's proceeds without a rate — the sale's currency at its date — set invalid_external_flow_from: ROI and TWRR are None from that date. So do a short sale's proceeds without a rate at its opening date, and the cost of a purchase closing a short without a rate at its date (MF-E2). collect_performance_fx_needs() registers each of those rates (none for an ADJUSTMENT-out, which has no value, N78-1); for a SHORT lot, its currency at its opening date.
  • Lot summary: original_cost and opening_unit_price are None when the rate at the opening date is missing; cumulative_proceeds (known_cumulative_proceeds()) when one closure's closing rate is missing — for a SHORT lot's proceeds, the opening-date rate — and realized_pnl (known_realized_pnl()) when one closure misses either of the two rates it reads (see Closures: each leg at its own date); reference_unit_price when the rate of its currency at the opening date is missing, and reference_price_source whenever reference_unit_price is None — a reference that could not be converted has no source, as in the return history. total_value (when the proceeds have no rate), pnl, market_pnl, total_pnl, cash_yield, total_return, net_total_pnl, net_total_return and annualized_return are None when one of their inputs is unknown — an amount above, or the income, fees or taxes a degraded economic pool withholds — and the estimated-at-cost branch values no lot without a converted cost.
  • Gantt topology: GanttSegmentSchema.unit_price is None when the rate at the fragment's start_date is missing.
  • Economic events (income, FEE, TAX): a missing rate on an event degrades its pool, and one on a trade can degrade a FEE / TAX pool that the trade weights; the figures a degraded pool feeds are withheld — see Economic events and degraded pools.

The misses are reported once, after every builder: _report_gaps() merges missing_pairs() with the WAC lines' gaps into data_quality (see WAC Lines), and any of them turns a COMPLETE run DEGRADED. Only what is returned is converted, so the report holds no gap of a figure nobody reads: event rows (_build_lot_event_rows()) are built only when CUSTODY_HISTORY or EVENT_HISTORY is requested, and the daily valuation covers every history day only for the value, return, price, market price and performance histories (daily_series) — a LOT_SUMMARY alone values just the last day, the only one it reads.

The WAC lines do not go through FxRateResolver: compute_average_costs() converts each acquisition itself, at its own date.

docs.title: 💱 Closures: each leg at its own date
docs.text:
A closure has two legs, and each converts in its own currency at its own date (developer decision 26): the lot's side from the lot's currency at the lot's opening_date — the opening rate, a LONG lot's purchase rate — and the closing side from the closure's close_currency at its close_date — the closing rate, a LONG lot's sale rate. close_currency is the currency of the closing price, which need not be the lot's: a lot moved to a broker of another currency is sold in that currency, a transfer leg leaving the scope hands its units over in the currency of its day's mark (see Closure currency).

The rule has one home, convert_closure(closure, lot, fx_resolver) (financial_math/lots/conversions.py), which returns a ConvertedClosure in the target currency:

Field Converted from open_unit_price closure.open_unit_price, at the opening rate close_unit_price closure.close_unit_price, at the closing rate proceeds closure.proceeds, at the closing rate: a sale's cash, or the value a scope-edge transfer leg hands over; 0 for an ADJUSTMENT_OUT read from the database and on a SHORT closure cost The leg the closure gives up: for a LONG lot, the purchase cost of the units, quantity × open_unit_price at the opening rate; for a SHORT lot, the purchase that closes it, quantity × close_unit_price at the closing rate realized_pnl realized_gain(proceeds, cost) (financial_math/returns.py), the proceeds minus cost: for a LONG lot its closing leg, the proceeds above; for a SHORT lot its opening leg, the proceeds of its opening sale, quantity × open_unit_price at the opening rate

realized_gain() is the function the Dashboard applies to its realized sales too (portfolio_service.py: proceeds at the sale date, cost at the purchase dates), and each caller keeps its own rule for summing: the Dashboard sums the sales it can value and reports the others in the data quality, while a lot with one unknown closure has an unknown realized P&L.

The engine's native LotClosure.realized_pnl is never read: it is None whenever close_currency is not the lot's. A missing rate leaves None the figures that need it, never one computed from native amounts — close_unit_price and proceeds need the closing rate, open_unit_price the opening rate, cost the rate of its leg, realized_pnl both. need_closure_rates() registers the two, (close_currency, close_date) and (lot.currency, opening_date): collect_fx_needs() calls it for the closures of the lot summary, the return history and the event rows, collect_performance_fx_needs() for a LONG lot's SELL closures.

Every reader converts closures through convert_closure():

  • Lot summary: realized_pnl (known_realized_pnl()) sums the closures' and is None as soon as one of them is; cumulative_proceeds (known_cumulative_proceeds()) sums a LONG lot's closure proceeds — a SHORT lot's are those of its opening sale, converted at the opening date;
  • Value and return histories: the running sums of _closure_prefix(lot, closures, fx_resolver, leg) (financial_math/lots/histories.py) — a LONG lot's closure proceeds, a SHORT lot's cost;
  • Performance history: the SELL closures' proceeds, its inflows;
  • Event history: the closure rows (_build_closure_rows()) — unit_price and close_unit_price at the closing rate, open_unit_price at the opening rate, proceeds and realized_pnl as above. Their broker_id is the broker the units leave (§29): the closed fragment's, FragmentInterval.broker_id of the closure's fragment_id (fragment_brokers, from _build_lot_event_rows()), and the lot's opening_broker_id only for a fragment without a broker (in transit) or unknown — a lot opened at A, moved to B and sold at B reads B on its SELL row, not A.

The lot summary keeps market_pnl = pnl − realized_pnl. Every closure's cost converts at the opening date, like original_cost, so a LONG lot's market_pnl is its open value minus the cost of its open units at the purchase rate: a fully closed LONG lot has a market_pnl of 0 and a realized_pnl equal to its pnl, and the exchange-rate move between purchase and sale is realized with the units, as on the Dashboard. The theory page FIFO Lot Analysis works an example through.

An ADJUSTMENT_OUT read from the database has no value (N78-1, see An ADJUSTMENT_OUT has no value): every fragment closes at 0 in its lot's currency, so the closure realizes minus the lot's cost at the opening date, and the performance history counts no flow for it. Only a transfer leg leaving the scope carries a value, the market value of its day in the mark's currency: its proceeds convert from that currency at the leg's date and realize against the lot's cost at the opening date, whatever the lot's currency.

docs.title: 🧾 Economic events and degraded pools
docs.text:
An income / FEE / TAX event without a rate still enters the engine with its native amount, only as a placeholder: the engine then places it — pools it, matches it, lets a TAX follow the income it taxes — exactly as it would place a converted one. _engine_target_amount() hands that amount over, for the events and for the BUY / SELL amounts that weight the FEE / TAX split, and the resolver records the miss. unconvertible_ids() collects the events (unconvertible_event_ids) and the trades (unconvertible_trade_ids) without a rate on their date, and withheld_economics() finds the engine pools (EconomicAllocationGroup) they degrade:

Pool Degraded when Unknown Amount-degraded One of its source events is in unconvertible_event_ids Its target-currency amount, hence every target share of it Split-degraded A trade-weighted FEE / TAX rule (SAME_DAY_TRADES, SAME_DAY_MIXED_TRADES, PREVIOUS_DAY_TRADES), with a weighting trade in unconvertible_trade_ids and weighting trades in more than one currency Its split: every operation weight and every per-lot share

When every weighting trade is in one currency, the pool is not split-degraded: the trades share one date, hence one rate, and their native placeholders keep the exact ratios.

WithheldEconomics records, per lot, the date from which its income (income_from), fees (fees_from) and taxes (taxes_from) are unknown — the date of the earliest degraded pool of that kind that allocates to the lot — with the degraded pool indexes (amount_degraded, split_degraded), unconvertible_event_ids and the kinds whose orphan pool is degraded (orphan_unknown). The response withholds:

  • Lot summary (_build_lot_summaries()): on a lot a degraded pool reaches, that kind's asset_income, allocated_fees or allocated_taxes is None, and so is every figure that reads it — total_pnl, cash_yield and total_return read the income; net_total_pnl, net_total_return and annualized_return read all three. The lot's net_metrics_status is "UNAVAILABLE" (withheld.reaches(lot_id)).
  • Value and return histories (_economics_on_date(), _known_prefix_on_date(), _lot_returns()): each kind is None from its date on — the value history's income, allocated_fees and allocated_taxes, and its net_pnl with the fees or the taxes; the return history's income, its total_return with the income, and its net_total_return with any of the three. An earlier date sums only earlier pools, all of them known.
  • Income events: LotIncomeEventSchema.amount is None for an event in unconvertible_event_ids.
  • Orphans: asset_orphan_income, asset_orphan_fees or asset_orphan_taxes is None when an orphan pool of that kind is degraded.
  • Audit (map_economic_groups()): an amount-degraded pool has target_pool_total, target_orphan and each lot allocation's target_amount set to None; a split-degraded pool has each operation weight and each lot allocation's native_amount and target_amount set to None. The native pool total, the native orphan and each lot's weight inside an operation — a quantity ratio — stay.

Orphan issues. The engine builds an orphan pool's ASSET_INCOME_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS / ASSET_COST_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS issue with the pool's target_amount and target_currency in its params. _build_data_quality_report() passes them through _orphan_issue_params(): for an amount-degraded orphan pool — matched by the issue's transaction_id, the pool's first source — the issue states the pool in its own currency, target_amount = native_pool_total and target_currency = native_currency, so the banner shows an orphan 70 VND dividend without a rate as "70 VND", never "70 EUR". The message keys keep their target_ names: such an issue holds a native amount and currency under them, and summing message_params.target_amount across issues would mix currencies. A convertible orphan pool keeps its converted amount in the target currency.

The native placeholder therefore never reaches the response.

docs.title: ⚠️ qbq Scaling Gotcha
docs.text:
Two price scales coexist

price_history.close is quoted per quote_base_quantity.

opening_unit_price, closure unit prices, and WAC values are per single unit.

For bonds this mismatch is dangerous: comparing raw opening_unit_price with raw market price mixes two scales and historically caused huge fake returns/P&L. Example: a bond can trade near 100, while opening_unit_price is near 1 because cost was divided by nominal quantity.

The analysis fixes this in two places:

  • Valuation path: lot_summary_figures() (financial_math/lots/summary.py, the lot summary) and the financial_math/lots/histories.py functions build_value_history(), build_return_history() and build_performance_history() call compute_holding_value(..., quote_base_quantity) so open_value = (qty / qbq) * price.
  • Reference-price fallback path: opening_reference_price() (financial_math/lots/prices.py) multiplies lot.opening_unit_price * quote_base_quantity when the lot has no market reference: opened by a BUY or a short-opening SELL, or by an ADJUSTMENT_IN with no observation on or before its opening date (see Reference Price).

Exact fallback scaling code:

scale = quote_base_quantity if quote_base_quantity > 0 else 1
return lot.opening_unit_price * scale, lot.currency, lot.opening_date, "exact"

That multiplication is only for the lot's own price. Resolver marks — market quotes, and trade prices already lifted by build_asset_price_series() — arrive in per-qbq scale and must not be multiplied again.

docs.title: 🧭 Unified Price Resolver
docs.text:
LotsAnalysisService uses backend/app/services/financial_math/price_marks.py as the single daily mark path — the resolver's full contract (tiers, staleness semantics, qbq scale, the "only valuation path" invariant) lives in its own page: Price Resolver.

price_series = build_asset_price_series(
    price_rows=[(row.date, row.close, row.currency) for row in prices],
    transactions=transactions,
    split_linked_tx_ids=set(split_ratios_by_tx_id),
    asset_currency=asset.currency,
    quote_base_quantity=quote_base_quantity,
)
mark = price_series.resolve(current_date)

The series is built once, before the FIFO engine runs, from the price_history rows _load_prices() reads — the window and the last quote before it — and from the loaded transactions, those of the brokers in scope: each of their BUY and SELL rows with an amount is a trade observation, and so is the cost of an incoming TRANSFER while the asset has nothing else on or before its day (Transfer cost as an estimate). The series reads these rows as loaded, before the scope's edge is read: a leg from a broker outside the scope is still a TRANSFER there. It decides three things:

  1. The reference price of a lot opened by an ADJUSTMENT_IN, which the engine reads while it replays (see Reference Price).
  2. The days valued at cost: those with no observation on or before them, up to at_cost_until (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback).
  3. The daily valuation: the two maps below.

Resolution tiers are owned by AssetPriceSeries.resolve():

Tier MarkSource Meaning 1 MARKET Same-day asset-system price_history.close. 2 TRADE_AVG Same-day BUY/SELL average, or an incoming TRANSFER's cost as an estimate for an asset with nothing else yet. An ADJUSTMENT is never an observation, with or without a cost basis. 3 CARRIED Last observation carried forward (LOCF), market- or trade-origin. 4 MISSING No observation on/before the day.

Marks stay in native currency and on the market × quote_base_quantity axis. The service converts mark.unit_price with FxRateResolver.convert(..., current_date), so carried foreign marks use FX for the valuation date, not the original observation date.

Both internal maps are built from this same resolver:

  • market_prices[date] = target-currency mark or None feeds lot summaries, value/return history, performance NAV, and transfer valuation.
  • estimated_market_prices[date] = (target-currency mark, mark.estimated), only on a day whose mark converts, feeds the two price series: PRICE_HISTORY, per lot, and MARKET_PRICE_HISTORY, once a day whatever lots are open.

The old duplicate map pattern (_build_market_price_map plus _build_estimated_market_price_map) is gone in shipped code. There is no separate market-only valuation path to document.

ResolvedMark.estimated means TRADE-origin, including a trade mark carried forward. A real market quote carried forward is stale (price_backward_fill) but not estimated.

docs.title: 🎯 Reference Price
docs.text:
A lot's reference price is the denominator of its Open Return, relative_return = market price / reference − 1. The engine resolves one only when an ADJUSTMENT_IN opens a LONG lot (_apply_adjustment_in()): a lot opened by a BUY or a short-opening SELL has none and is compared with its own price — a trade is a price. The service hands the engine reference_price_lookup(asset_id, opened_at), which reads price_series.resolve(opened_at):

Mark on the opening day What the engine stores Engine issue MARKET: a quote of that day mark.unit_price, reference_price_source="exact" — TRADE_AVG: no quote, that day's BUY / SELL average mark.unit_price, "fallback" REFERENCE_PRICE_FALLBACK CARRIED: a quote or a trade mark of an earlier day mark.unit_price, "fallback" REFERENCE_PRICE_FALLBACK MISSING: no observation on or before that day reference_unit_price=None, "unavailable" (the lookup returns None) REFERENCE_PRICE_UNAVAILABLE

The lots banner groups the issues of one code that name a lot into a single message, with a chip for each lot, so the two messages (dataQuality.referencePriceFallback, dataQuality.referencePriceUnavailable) say how the reference is chosen and never a price: one price could not stand for every lot of the group (J-36). The reference_price param of REFERENCE_PRICE_FALLBACK stays in message_params, unread by the texts.

An ADJUSTMENT is never an observation (developer decision P2): a lot opened by an opening position, a succession or a transfer from an untracked broker is compared with the market — the last quote, or a BUY / SELL more recent than it — and with its own cost basis only when the asset has no observation on or before its opening day. A leg from a broker outside the scope, read here as an ADJUSTMENT_IN, on an asset with no quote and no other operation on or before its day, is itself that day's observation (its cost, estimated): its reference is that cost, "fallback", with REFERENCE_PRICE_FALLBACK where it used to be "unavailable".

opening_reference_price(lot, price_series, quote_base_quantity) (financial_math/lots/prices.py) gives the lot summary, the return history and collect_fx_needs() the reference as (price, currency, date, source):

  • a lot with a reference_unit_price keeps it, in the currency of the mark it came from (price_series.resolve(lot.opening_date).currency), dated lot.opening_date: the reference converts at the rate of the day it stands for, never at the date of an older observation it was carried from (developer decision P21: every amount at the rate of its day);
  • any other lot falls back to its own price, lot.opening_unit_price × quote_base_quantity, in the lot's currency at the opening date, with source "exact" (see qbq Scaling Gotcha). An ADJUSTMENT_IN without a cost basis opens its lot at a unit price of 0, so that lot has no relative_return.

collect_fx_needs() registers that (currency, opening date) for each selected lot when LOT_SUMMARY or RETURN_HISTORY is requested. A reference whose rate is missing is None, and so is its reference_price_source, in the summary and in the return history, whose point then has no relative_return.

docs.title: 💸 Economic Stage — Income, FEE/TAX & Net Metrics
docs.text:
Since FIFO v5 the allocation of asset-linked income (DIVIDEND / INTEREST) and asset-linked cost (FEE / TAX) happens inside the engine's economic stage (see FIFO Lot Engine), not in the service. The service only extracts the already-computed per-lot accumulators and audit groups, withholding what a missing rate leaves unknown, through the functions of financial_math/lots/economic_events.py:

  • extract_income_outputs(engine_result, ...) reads engine_result.economic_accumulators_by_lot[*].gross_income
  • extract_cost_outputs(engine_result, ...) reads .allocated_fees / .allocated_taxes
  • map_economic_groups(...) maps the 3-level audit into economic_allocation_groups
  • withheld_economics(...) finds the pools a missing rate degrades, whose figures the response withholds (see Economic events and degraded pools)

Allocation rule moved and changed

The pre-v5 same-day rule w_i(t) = OpenQty_i(t) / Σ OpenQty_j(t) no longer applies. Income eligibility is now D-1 (OpenQty_i(D-1)) and broker-scoped to the paying broker, and FEE/TAX use a deterministic operation-matching ladder. The math lives in the engine; see the theory page FIFO Lot Analysis.

docs.title: 📤 Extracted outputs
docs.text:
• income_by_lot → scalar cumulative income for LotSummarySchema.asset_income
  • income_prefix_by_lot → per-date cumulative prefixes for value/return histories
  • income_events → chart markers with source tx and affected lot ids
  • fees_by_lot / taxes_by_lot → scalar allocated_fees / allocated_taxes, plus per-date prefixes for history

docs.title: 🧮 Net metrics (LotSummarySchema)
docs.text:
FEE/TAX are stored as positive magnitudes already converted to target_currency, and net metrics are derived only when they can be meaningful:

net_total_pnl    = total_pnl - allocated_fees - allocated_taxes          # total_pnl INCLUDES income
net_total_return = net_total_pnl / original_cost       (original_cost > 0)

History builders expose their own net lines: build_value_history() emits net_pnl = pnl - allocated_fees - allocated_taxes (pnl excludes income), while build_return_history() emits an income-inclusive net_total_return. The asymmetry is intentional — each net line mirrors its gross counterpart minus costs.

net_metrics_status

A lot that a degraded economic pool reaches is emitted with net_metrics_status = "UNAVAILABLE" (withheld.reaches(lot_id)): its income, fees or taxes are unknown, and so are its net figures (see Economic events and degraded pools). Every other lot is "AVAILABLE". The status speaks only for the economic pools: a net figure can also be None because its total P&L or its opening value needs a missing rate, with the status still "AVAILABLE"; every missing pair goes to data_quality (see FX Conversion).

docs.title: 🧺 Orphans & conservation
docs.text:
When income or FEE/TAX has no eligible lot (e.g. a cost after the position is fully closed), the amount is not dropped: it is returned at asset level as asset_orphan_income / asset_orphan_fees / asset_orphan_taxes and surfaced as a ASSET_INCOME_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS / ASSET_COST_NO_ELIGIBLE_LOTS data-quality issue. The engine guarantees, per pool, Σ allocated + orphan == converted pool total. For a pool whose amount has no rate, it conserves the native placeholder instead: the response withholds that pool's target figures and, for an orphan pool, the asset-level orphan total of its kind, and the orphan issue states the pool in its own currency (see Economic events and degraded pools).

Costs without an asset

FEE / TAX with asset_id = null never enter the FIFO/lots analysis at all — they are handled by the Portfolio Engine. Only asset-linked costs can produce allocated net figures here.

docs.title: 🧮 Estimated-at-Cost Fallback
docs.text:
A day with no observation on or before it — no price_history close (_load_prices() reads the window and the last quote before it) and no BUY or SELL with an amount among the loaded transactions — values an open LONG lot at its cost: the per-day rule of the Dashboard's DailyStateBuilder._value_held_position() (see Price Resolver — No observation: valued at cost). The resolver carries every observation forward, so such days only come before the asset's first one. The service finds them once, after the engine run:

history_dates = list(_date_range(computed_from, actual_to))
at_cost_until = last_day_without_observation(price_series, history_dates)

actual_to is the requested date_to (today when it is not given), never later than latest_range_end() (tomorrow, utils/datetime_utils.py): the histories walk every day of that range, and an end far in the future held the instance (R13-SEC7-1). The response's requested_date_to and computed_date_to carry that bounded end.

computed_from is the first transaction's date, whatever its year (D-P4, L2: the 1 January 1900 floor of R13-SEC8 is gone, because the histories are steps and the prices and rates are read on the days that change something: a transaction of 1850 or of year 1 costs its changes, not its days; the year-1 test holds the price series to 2 000 reads and the peak under 150 MB). The response's computed_date_from carries it. From it start history_dates, the window _load_prices() reads and the rates of the market series (collect_fx_needs()). display_from, the first day the histories are cut from (see Change Days), is the requested date_from (or computed_from); requested_date_from stays as requested, and the response's range starts on the later of display_from and computed_from. A transfer leg needs the value of its own day: when that day has no observation on or before it, the leg moves the cost of its units, as on any day valued at cost (J-33); only when the first history day already has an observation, a quote stored before it, has the leg neither a price nor a cost, and the ROI/TWRR series stops from its date on — here, the whole series.

last_day_without_observation() (financial_math/lots/prices.py) returns the last of the ascending days whose price_series.resolve() is MISSING: the day before the first observation, actual_to when the asset has none, None when the first transaction's day already has one — a quote before it included. resolve(day).is_missing is true up to the first observation and false after it, so the days with an observation are a tail of the days: the function finds the first of them by bisection (bisect.bisect_left()), a few resolve() calls whatever the length of the history, where it used to resolve every day up to that observation. The days valued at cost are [computed_from, at_cost_until], whether or not the asset is priced later:

Reader What it does with at_cost_until build_value_history(), build_return_history() Pass at_cost = current_date <= at_cost_until to _lot_snapshot_on_date() (see below) build_performance_history() On such a day without a mark, the NAV of the open fragments in the scope at cost, and a transfer that day moves the cost of its units (see below, J-33) _build_lot_summaries() estimated_mode = at_cost_until == actual_to: the summary reads the end date only, so it is at cost only when that day has no observation — when the asset has none at all Data quality For a lot analysis that reads prices (needs_market_series(): LOT_SUMMARY and the value, return, price and performance histories), one CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST warning (dataQuality.currentPriceAssumedAtCostRange) with date_from = computed_from and date_to = at_cost_until: exactly the days valued at cost. No warning when at_cost_until is None, nor for MARKET_PRICE_HISTORY, even requested alone: it values nothing at cost, and a day at cost has no point in it FX needs When an analysis reads income (needs_income_alloc), every lot's currency at its opening date, the rate of the cost those days read; for PERFORMANCE_HISTORY, collect_performance_fx_needs(at_cost_until=…) registers the same for every LONG lot of the replay it reads

In the value and return histories, _lot_snapshot_on_date() (financial_math/lots/histories.py) values a day without a market_price this way:

  • a lot with no open quantity left is valued from its closures alone, on any day;
  • on an at_cost day, a still-open LONG lot is worth open_quantity × original_cost / original_quantity, its cost converted at the opening date — a lot whose cost has no rate has no point at all (see FX Conversion);
  • after at_cost_until, a market_price of None can only be a mark whose rate is missing: a still-open lot has no point that day, never one at cost.

The return history has no relative_return on an at_cost day. An asset first priced after a lot opened by an adjustment therefore shows that lot at cost — a flat value line, no market P&L — from its opening to the day before the first quote, BUY or SELL, then at the mark.

In the summary (lot_summary_figures()), estimated_mode values the remaining quantity of a LONG lot at residual cost, provided the cost itself converts (original_cost, converted at the opening date, is not None; otherwise the lot is not valued):

open_value = residual_cost(original_cost, lot.open_quantity, lot.original_quantity)
value_source = "ESTIMATED_AT_COST"
market_pnl = Decimal("0")

Outside estimated_mode the end date always has a mark — every observation is on or before it — so a lot's latest mark is None only when its rate is missing: the lot then has no value and no value_source, as the LotSummarySchema.value_source description says.

Implications:

  • LotSummarySchema.value_source = "ESTIMATED_AT_COST" only for an asset with no observation up to the end date — one held only through adjustments, or through transfers that gave no estimate, with no quote
  • total_value, total_pnl, cash_yield, total_return remain usable, as long as the proceeds and realized P&L they read convert (see FX Conversion)
  • relative_return stays None: there is no market price to compare with the reference
  • data quality report adds CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST, from the first transaction to the end date

A TRADE-origin mark is a price: valuation uses it, the lot summary's value_source is then MARKET_PRICE — the label of any mark — and its point in either price series carries estimated=True. A BUY or a SELL gives one, and so does an incoming TRANSFER's cost while the asset has nothing else (Transfer cost as an estimate): an asset that arrived only by such transfers has no day at cost and a point, estimated=True, from its first transfer. An ADJUSTMENT never does, with or without a cost basis (see Price Resolver).

build_performance_history() reads the same days at cost (J-33). On a day <= at_cost_until without a mark, _nav_at_cost() values the open fragments in the scope at their lot's cost converted at the opening date (_cost_at_opening(), the value history's own rule); a day where one of them belongs to a SHORT lot, or its cost has no rate, has no NAV point. A transfer that day moves the cost of its units, never an unknown market value: a leg read at the scope's edge brings its own cost basis when it arrives and, when it leaves — handed over at its own cost — the cost of the pieces it closes (_boundary_leg_cost()); a transfer the re-run holds moves the cost of the pieces of its pair (_moved_cost(), from the pair's fragments). So the series starts on the first day held, ROI and TWRR are 0 while the position sits at cost, and the TWRR chain holds the move from cost to the first price, as the ROI does: before, the first NAV was the first mark, the base of the TWRR, and that move fell outside its chain. An asset with no observation has ROI and TWRR 0 every day. Neither price series has a point on the days at cost.

docs.title: 🎯 Selection Model
docs.text:
Backend method:

def _resolve_selected_lot_ids(self, selected_lot_ids: list[int] | None, lots_by_id: dict[int, FifoLot]) -> list[int]:
    if selected_lot_ids is None:
        return list(lots_by_id)
    ...
    return list(dict.fromkeys(selected_lot_ids))

Meaning at raw API level:

  • selected_lot_ids = None → all lots in backend scope
  • explicit non-empty list → exactly those lots
  • explicit unknown ids → ValueError

Frontend empty-selection convention

UI state uses different semantics: empty selection means all visible lots, not "none".

LotsAnalysisPanel.svelte implements that by expanding empty UI selection into effectiveSelectionIds = visibleLots.map((lot) => lot.lot_id) before lot-scoped requests.

So if you call API directly, send null/omit field for "all lots", or send explicit visible IDs for "all visible lots after frontend filtering". Do not assume raw [] automatically means all.

Also note: PERFORMANCE_HISTORY and MARKET_PRICE_HISTORY ignore lot selection entirely by schema/implementation.

docs.title: 📈 WAC Lines
docs.text:
BROKER_WAC_HISTORY and CUMULATIVE_WAC_HISTORY come from LibreFolio's single average-cost implementation, compute_average_costs() (see WAC & Cost Basis). The lines are computed only when one of the two analyses is requested.

_compute_average_cost_lines() maps the loaded asset transactions (ordered by date, then id) with cost_movement_from_transaction() — split-linked adjustments become splits — and makes one call for all the lines:

Line key Movements Feeds Broker id That broker's movements broker_wac_history (BrokerWACHistoryPoint) "__all__" (ALL_BROKERS) Every broker in scope, pooled: a transfer between two brokers in scope leaves at the pool's average and comes back in at its cost basis cumulative_wac_history (CumulativeWACHistoryPoint)

The report currency is the analysis target_currency, with asset_leg=False. Each acquisition is converted at its own date; quantities are the brokers' own, with no owner share applied.

average_cost_points(line, history_dates) (financial_math/lots/average_cost_lines.py) emits (date, wac, pool_qty) for each date it is given — the change days (see Change Days) — from the line's first movement on, reading line.state_at(date): wac is unit_cost_report (per single unit, in the target currency), pool_qty the pool's quantity. A date on which the pool lacks part of its cost has no point — a missing conversion or an acquisition without cost basis — so the chart shows a gap rather than a wrong average. expand_to_days() then fills the displayed range: each day takes the point of the last change day on or before it, and has none when that change day has none. A line moves only on the date of one of its steps (state_at() reads the last step on or before the day), and every such date in history_dates is a change day.

_report_gaps(data_quality, lines, conversion_gaps, target_currency, asset) puts in the response what the lines could not compute, merged with every other conversion the analysis could not make (conversion_gaps = fx_resolver.missing_pairs(), see FX Conversion). It runs once, after every builder, through the same build_data_quality_report() (financial_math/portfolio/data_quality.py) as the Dashboard banner:

  • Missing conversions (the lines' report leg plus conversion_gaps): data_quality.missing_fx_pairs receives one WACMissingPairInfo(pair, dates) per pair, its dates merged across sources, and data_quality.issues the MISSING_FX_MARKET / MISSING_FX_RATES issues derived from them, given the configured and real-provider pair sets of load_configured_fx_pair_sets();
  • Acquisitions of unknown cost (unknown_cost_movement_ids on any line): one MISSING_COST_BASIS issue for the analysed asset, built with missing_cost_basis_assets=[(asset.id, asset.display_name)] — the same issue as the portfolio banner;
  • calculation_status turns from COMPLETE to DEGRADED when a line misses a rate or a cost basis, or any other conversion of the analysis is missing: the gap is isolable.

In the panel, the issues appear in LotDataQualityBanner: one block per code, without call-to-action buttons. The issues of a code that name a lot (a finite message_params.lot_id) share one line, the first one's message, and the visible lots are its chips. Each issue without a lot gets a line of its own, with its own params (J-53): each orphan income or cost pool, which the engine reports with one issue per pool (financial_math/fifo/engine.py:899-913, :1015-1029), with its own amount, currency and day; and each notice of _report_gaps(), so both MISSING_FX_RATES messages show: dataQuality.missingFxRates (the pairs with a provider, with their date range) and dataQuality.missingFxRatesManual (the manual pairs). The banner adds no total: an amount-degraded orphan pool is stated in its own currency (see Economic events and degraded pools), and each pool has its own day. The banner itself is described in Lots Analysis.

docs.title: 🕰️ History Builders
docs.text:
Key builders — in the service:

  • _build_lot_summaries() — scalar lot rows for table/modal
  • _build_gantt_segments() — custody fragments
  • _build_lot_event_rows() — full lot chronology

and in financial_math/lots/:

  • build_value_history() — continues closed lots to date_to via lot_history_end_date(..., extend_closed=True), unless a rate is missing (see FX Conversion); values a still-open LONG lot at cost up to at_cost_until (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback)
  • build_return_history() — same continuity and at-cost rules, plus relative_return against opening_reference_price() (see Reference Price)
  • build_price_history() — truncates at closure date, no post-close points
  • build_market_price_history() — the asset's market price: one point per history day with an entry in estimated_market_prices — the resolver's mark of that day, converted at that day's rate, estimated when it comes from a trade (see Unified Price Resolver) — whatever lots are open. No truncation at closure: after every lot is closed the series runs on to actual_to, and selected_lot_ids does not change it. A day with no observation on or before it, or without a rate, has no point; the missing rate is reported (see FX Conversion). Kept with FAILED (see A Failed Reconstruction)
  • build_broker_wac_history() / build_cumulative_wac_history() — WAC points read from the average-cost lines via average_cost_points() (see WAC Lines)
  • build_performance_history() — asset-wide ROI/TWRR from NAV + external cash flows. The NAV is read on a day with a mark, and on a day with no observation on or before it at cost, up to at_cost_until (J-33; see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback). Money in: a BUY's amount and an ADJUSTMENT-in's money. Money out: a LONG SELL closure's proceeds. Transfer legs crossing the broker scope count at market value: a pair the re-run over the accessible brokers holds whole, and a leg read at the scope's edge (see Transfers Across the Scope's Edge). An ADJUSTMENT-out has no value (N78-1): a quantity correction, never a flow, whatever cost basis the row holds. A flow dated on a day without a NAV stays on its day, and counts on the first day after it with one (returns.flows_by_snapshot_date(), MF-E2b): the units it bought or sold are in that day's value, so the money joins them there. The units of an ADJUSTMENT-out leave the NAV with no flow to offset them, so ROI and TWRR read their whole value as a loss. Short positions (MF-E2): an open short is a debt, −quantity × price, and on a day at cost − its share of the opening sale's proceeds at the opening date's rate (_signed_nav_on_date(), _proceeds_at_opening()). The sale that opens it is money out, its proceeds at the opening date's rate (collect_performance_fx_needs() asks that rate); the purchase that closes it — a BUY, or an ADJUSTMENT-in at its cost basis — is money in, as any BUY. With a short in the scope the returns are read on the gross exposure: the TWRR divides each day's gain by |long values| + |short values| of the day before (calculate_twrr_series(..., exposure_by_date=)), the ROI the gain (NAV plus the net flows) by the capital committed, the long side's net deposit plus the proceeds of every short sale so far (calculate_simple_roi_series(..., capital_by_date=), _committed_capital_by_date()). Selling 10 short at 100 and buying them back at 80 gains 200: ROI +20 % on the 1 000 committed, TWRR +22.2 % (+10 % on 1 000, then +11.1 % on the 900 still owed), higher because the exposure shrinks as the price falls — the return of a short rebalanced daily. Without a short in the scope the series are those of the long-only rule, unchanged.

Important nuance: date_from only selects the emitted rows, through the expansion — expand_to_days() fills [display_from, actual_to] (see Change Days). The engine still starts from the earliest in-scope asset transaction so FIFO state stays correct, and the change days still start from computed_from.

docs.title: 📆 Change Days
docs.text:
The seven daily builders — build_value_history(), build_return_history(), build_price_history(), build_market_price_history(), build_broker_wac_history(), build_cumulative_wac_history() and build_performance_history() — run only on the change days: the days of history_dates on which one of their series can change (lot L1a, financial_math/lots/change_days.py). get_lots_analysis() computes them once, after the two valuation maps and the average-cost lines, and hands them to every builder as its history_dates:

change_days = lot_change_days(
    days=history_dates,
    market_prices=market_prices,
    estimated_market_prices=estimated_market_prices,
    at_cost_until=at_cost_until,
    event_dates=analysis_event_dates(
        transactions=[*transactions, *late_legs, *performance_context.transactions, *income_transactions, *cost_transactions],
        engine_results=(engine_result, performance_context.engine_result),
        prefixes=(income_prefix_by_lot, fees_prefix_by_lot, taxes_prefix_by_lot),
        withheld=withheld,
        average_cost_lines=average_cost_lines.values(),
    ),
)

Why. Before L1a every builder valued every selected lot on every day of history_dates — every day since the first transaction, floored at 1 January 1900 — and trim_dates(), since removed, then cut the rows to the window: the cost grew with the age of the book, not with the window. On the parity tests' 1900 book — a lot bought on 2 January 1900, read from 16 January to 15 February 2021 — that made 221 200 calls of the per-day snapshot helpers _lot_snapshot_on_date() and _open_value_on_date() (44 240 days, five calls a day) to answer 31 days; on its change days the same reading stays under the test's budget of 400 calls.

Which days. lot_change_days(*, days, market_prices, estimated_market_prices, at_cost_until, event_dates) returns, ascending, the days of days that are:

Change day What can change there The first and the last day Every day then has a change day on or before it; the last is history_dates[-1], the day _lot_value_basis() and lot_history_end_date() read A day whose market_prices or estimated_market_prices entry is not the previous day's in its exact representation (Decimal.as_tuple()) The converted mark: a new observation, a mark that appears or disappears, a new estimated flag, or a new exchange rate — each mark is converted at its own day's rate, so a rate that moves the mark is caught here. Decimal("1.10") is not Decimal("1.1"): it would print otherwise at_cost_until + 1 The valuation at cost ends (see Estimated-at-Cost Fallback), even when no mark changes that day — a first observation without a rate Every date of event_dates An input other than the mark (below) The day after each of the above A series that changes the day after its input (below)

Only days of days count: an event dated after actual_to (a late transfer leg) or before computed_from adds nothing.

analysis_event_dates(*, transactions, engine_results, prefixes, withheld, average_cost_lines) gathers the dates on which an input other than the mark changes:

  • the dates of the rows: the scope's (as read at its edge), the late transfer legs, the performance re-run's, the income and the FEE / TAX rows;
  • from the engine result — and from the re-run's too, when PERFORMANCE_HISTORY re-runs the engine over every broker the user can see: the lot openings, the starts and ends of the fragments, the closures and the classified events;
  • the dates of the cumulative income, fee and tax prefixes (income_prefix_by_lot, fees_prefix_by_lot, taxes_prefix_by_lot);
  • the dates a pool becomes unknown from (WithheldEconomics.income_from, fees_from, taxes_from; see Economic events and degraded pools);
  • the steps of the average-cost lines.

The rows and the engine give overlapping dates today; both are kept, so that a date one of them derives on its own is never missed.

Some series change on the day after an input, with no input of their own changing that day: the TWRR's first value is on the day after the first NAV snapshot (calculate_twrr_series() has no point on the first snapshot), and a closed lot's price line stops on the day after its last closure (build_price_history() emits up to the closure date). Without that day, the expansion would carry the row before it: no TWRR, or a price past the closure. A day that is a change day only as the day after another brings no day after of its own.

Expansion. expand_to_days(rows, *, key, change_days, window_from, window_to) turns a builder's rows on the change days into the rows of every day of [display_from, actual_to]. Key by key, in the order the builder emitted them, each day takes the row of the last change day on or before it, re-dated with model_copy(update={"date": day}) (a change day keeps its own row). A day before the first change day, or whose change day has no row for that key, gets none — as when every day was computed.

key Builders row.lot_id Value, return and price histories row.broker_id Broker WAC history None (one line) Market price history, cumulative WAC history, performance history

Why the figures are the same, byte for byte. Between two change days every input a builder reads for a day is the same Decimal, in the same representation, as on the last change day — the converted mark (its price and its rate together), the open fragments, the closures' running sums, the income, fee and tax prefixes, the withheld pools, the average-cost step, the at-cost flag — so a day computed there would repeat that change day's figures. The two series that accumulate from day to day do not move either: on such a day the TWRR multiplies by exactly Decimal("1") — (x − x) / x has exponent 0 — and the ROI adds a zero cash flow. The readers of history_dates[-1] (_lot_value_basis(), lot_history_end_date()) still see the last day, which is always a change day. The output contract is unchanged: one point per day of the window, the same JSON.

Still read on every day of history_dates: the two valuation maps, for the histories that read the marks (daily_series, see FX Conversion) — a resolve() and a conversion a day — and the scan of lot_change_days() over them. No lot is valued there. The rates behind those conversions are no longer a request a day (L1b, FX Conversion): they are read as steps in one unit_rate_steps() call per load, so what stays daily is the in-memory conversion, the scan and the record of the days without a rate.

One rule with the engine. The change days are the lots' application of the portfolio engine's rule, developer decision 28 «recompute whenever a term of the formula changes» (see The Days the Engine Recomputes). Not the same function: the engine and the native cash share native_cash.change_days(), the one home of «the day a rate changes», which compares rates; the lots compare the converted marks themselves, in their exact representation, because their output must stay byte-identical.

Tests. The first two cover the change days (L1a), the last two the rates read as steps (L1b, see FX Conversion).

  • test_services/test_financial_math/test_lot_change_days.py (./dev.py test services financial-math, pure): the contract of lot_change_days() and expand_to_days(), and last_day_without_observation() against a day-by-day walk, in at most 34 resolve() calls over 20 000 days.
  • test_services/test_financial/test_lots_change_days_parity.py (./dev.py test services roi-fifo-utils): the service against itself with every day a change day (lot_change_days replaced by «every day»): the same JSON, generated_at aside, on 13 books × their windows × their scopes, 178 cases; and the two reds on the 1900 book — at most 400 calls of the two snapshot helpers, and one call of lot_change_days().
  • test_services/test_financial/test_lots_fx_steps_parity.py (./dev.py test services roi-fifo-utils): the rates read as steps against a verbatim copy of the old resolver (one convert_bulk() unit per need) — the same JSON, generated_at aside, over the books of the change-days parity test and their windows and scopes, read in EUR, plus fx-daily read in HUF and the 1900 book read in USD; the resolver alone, asked the same needs as the old one over seeded rates, answers alike on every asked day and on the days around, digits and exponent included (Decimal.as_tuple()), and reports the same missing_pairs(); and the two reds on the 1900 book read in USD — at most 400 conversions handed to convert_bulk() and one or two unit_rate_steps() calls.
  • test_services/test_lots_analysis_pure.py (./dev.py test services lots-analysis-pure, pure): TestFxRateResolverLoad and TestFxRateResolverNeedDays stub unit_rate_steps where conversions reads it — the pending windows of each load, the days a window answers and the days around it that it does not, nothing asked for a blank code, the target or a reversed window — and collect_fx_needs() asks the market currencies as windows, not a need() a day.
