docs.title: 📈 Price Resolver — the single valuation-mark source
docs.text:
backend/app/services/financial_math/price_marks.py answers the one question every engine needs — what is the per-unit mark of asset X on day D? — with a single coherent daily model, so charts, valuation (NAV) and metrics (MWRR/TWRR/ROI) all read from the same numbers. The module belongs to the financial math layer.

Since the legacy valuation engine was removed (1.1 dev cycle), the resolver is the only valuation path: there is no market-only fallback cascade and no transition flag. If a price reaches a report, it came through here; a holding the resolver cannot mark at all is counted at its book cost, never at a price (see No observation: valued at cost).

docs.title: 🪜 The daily model
docs.text:
Per asset, per day D, AssetPriceSeries.resolve(D) returns a ResolvedMark whose source is decided by a four-tier ladder:

Tier MarkSource Meaning 1 MARKET An asset-system price (price_history.close) exists on D — the exact real quote 2 TRADE_AVG No quote, but same-day TRADE observations exist — average of their unit prices (BUY/SELL rows, or transfer cost estimates) 3 CARRIED Otherwise, the last observation ≤ D carried forward (LOCF; market- or trade-origin) 4 MISSING Nothing on or before D — unit_price = 0, currency = None

Construction collapses the observation stream to one value per day first: a MARKET quote wins the day; otherwise same-day TRADE observations are averaged. Queries are O(log n) via bisect.

MISSING is the resolver's last word, not the holding's: the portfolio engine counts a held position of known cost at that cost instead — see No observation: valued at cost.

docs.title: 📏 Staleness and the estimated flag
docs.text:
Two orthogonal flags ride on every mark — do not conflate them:

  • price_backward_fill — None for an exact same-day observation; a BackwardFillInfo (actual_rate_date + days_back) when the value was carried forward. This is the project-wide staleness contract FX and asset pricing already expose, so the frontend renders the "value fades with age" line for free.
  • estimated — True whenever the value did not come from a real asset-system quote (i.e. it is TRADE-derived), independently of freshness. A real quote carried forward is stale but not estimated; a fresh trade mark is estimated but not stale.

docs.title: 🕯️ Intraday range: open / high / low
docs.text:
PriceObservation and ResolvedMark carry three optional fields, open, high and low, on the same market ×quote_base_quantity scale as the close. They are filled only on an exact MARKET day whose price_history row has all three; everywhere else they are None:

Mark open / high / low MARKET, full triple in price_history The row's values MARKET, one or two of the three missing None — a partial triple counts as no range; an extremum is never guessed TRADE_AVG None — a trade has one unit price, no intraday range CARRIED None — nothing traded that day, and the range of an earlier day is never carried forward MISSING None

latest() never carries a range either.

The range enters through build_asset_price_series(ohlc_by_date=…): an optional map date → (open, high, low) for MARKET days already present in price_rows. It is a separate argument, not a wider price_rows tuple, so the other caller (lots_analysis_service.py) keeps the (date, close, currency) shape; a day left out of the map has no range.

Only the portfolio engine (financial_math/portfolio/engine.py) passes it, and only for a calculation run with include_candles=True, which POST /api/v1/portfolio/report requests through include_pnl_candles. The Growth chart asks for it lazily — when the user switches to the P&L Candles submode and no candles are loaded yet — on the Dashboard and on a broker page (see the Portfolio Growth Chart); a failed request is asked again at most three times, 2, 4 and 8 s later (Lazy sections after a failure). The engine builds the map from the price_history rows it already loads, with no extra query, and composes one synthetic P&L candle per day:

  • each held asset with a range contributes its value at open, high and low; an asset without one contributes a flat value (open = high = low = close);
  • offset = total_pnl − Σ close, and the candle is offset + Σ open, offset + Σ high, offset + Σ low, closing at total_pnl, the day's total P&L — the offset absorbs cash, the capital baseline and in-transit value;
  • a day on which any held asset is MISSING gets no candle at all.

docs.title: 🧊 Design contract
docs.text:
• Two layers. AssetPriceSeries is a pure, synchronous, immutable calculator built from pre-normalized observations — no I/O, no DB, no async, no FX — so engines (themselves pure) can query it and trust it blindly. Data acquisition happens once per calculation in the async caller, which then feeds normalized observations via build_asset_price_series(). This mirrors the load-once / query-sync shape of FxRateResolver (financial_math/lots/conversions.py).
  • Native currency, market ×quote_base_quantity scale — conversion belongs to the engine. Every observation stays in its own native currency; each ResolvedMark carries that currency so the consuming engine converts to the reporting currency at the valuation date (a carried mark must translate at the day it is read — otherwise a foreign holding freezes a stale FX). Trade unit prices are lifted to the qbq axis (× quote_base_quantity) so a qbq=100 bond lands on its ~100 par axis alongside market quotes. The portfolio engine takes those rates from fx_rate_map, preloaded once per calculation by _preload_fx_rates() (financial_math/portfolio/engine.py) with a single unit_rate_steps() call, the rates of convert_bulk() kept as steps (P3) — see FX Architecture.
  • Never for realized / cost basis. The mark is for open-position valuation and the price line only. Realized P&L and cost basis always come from the actual transaction prices, never from this estimate.
  • What feeds it (build_asset_price_series): MARKET observations from price_rows ((date, close, currency); close is already per-qbq and is not re-scaled), with their optional intraday range from ohlc_by_date, and TRADE observations from BUY/SELL rows with an amount (|amount| / |quantity| in the transaction currency), plus the transfer cost estimates. Split-linked rows are skipped.
  • An ADJUSTMENT is never a price, incoming or outgoing, with or without a cost basis (developer decision P2): its cost_basis_override is a cost — often the position's average cost — not what the asset was worth that day. One that takes units out has no value at all (N78-1). Market quotes and BUY/SELL trades mark an asset; an incoming TRANSFER does only as an estimate (see Transfer cost as an estimate).
  • A market quote is read in the units of its own day; a split moves the quantity. The portfolio engine values a holding as quantity × mark. The quantity changes at a split only through the ADJUSTMENT rows linked to the SPLIT event, on the split's date. The split ratio restates only a trade-derived mark (LAST_TRADE_PRICE, _cumulative_split_ratio() in financial_math/portfolio/daily_state.py), never a market quote. So a provider that stores closes already adjusted for later splits undervalues every day before a split, by its ratio, and the day of the split shows a jump that is not a flow. Yahoo Finance does this: its Close is split-adjusted even with auto_adjust=False. Example: 10 AAPL on 28 August 2020 count 10 × 124.8 = 1 248 instead of 4 990, and on 31 August, 40 × 129 = 5 160. From the split on, the numbers are right. This is a known limit of release 1.3 (developer decision of 23/10/2026, MF-SPL1 C). The target is to store as-traded closes, with the readers that need a continuous line (charts, signals, risk) applying the SPLIT events themselves.

docs.title: 🔁 Transfer cost as an estimate
docs.text:
W-B94 (developer decision of 30/10/2026, road b), _transfer_cost_estimates() in price_marks.py: the cost of an incoming TRANSFER is a price observation for an asset that has nothing else to be priced by yet. A TRANSFER row with quantity > 0, a positive cost_basis_override and a cost_basis_currency, not split-linked, becomes a TRADE observation — so estimated=True, TRADE_AVG on its day and CARRIED after — at cost_basis_override × quote_base_quantity, in cost_basis_currency (a TRANSFER row has no amount and no currency of its own).

It counts only on a day strictly before the asset's first real event: the earliest of its market quotes and of every other counted row (non-zero quantity, not split-linked) among the transactions passed in — BUY, SELL, ADJUSTMENT and outgoing TRANSFER. An ADJUSTMENT is never a price, yet it still stops the estimate. Other incoming legs do not: each one before that day is an observation, and those of one day are averaged like trades. A quote or a trade is never overridden. Example: an ETF quoted 200 up to Friday, bought years ago at 50 and moved between two brokers on Saturday resolves to the carried 200 on Saturday and Sunday, never 50 — the old BUY and the quote both precede the transfer.

"First" is computed over the rows the caller passes, which for both consumers are the scope's: the portfolio engine's rows of the asset at the brokers in scope, the lots analysis's loaded transactions. An internal transfer between two brokers of the scope gives no estimate (its outgoing leg is on or before its incoming one); a leg from a broker outside the scope does, when nothing of the scope precedes it.

What it changes downstream, for an asset that arrived only by transfer with a cost basis and has no price source:

Reader Before With the estimate Portfolio valuation (DailyStateBuilder) ESTIMATED_AT_COST: book cost, converted at the acquisition day's rate and frozen LAST_TRADE_PRICE: the transfer's unit cost, converted at each day's rate; in transaction_implied_asset_ids In-kind capital of the leg (_transfer_leg_capital()) The cost the leg moves in its pool Its market value on its own day — that same cost, so the transfer stays neutral on its day Dashboard data quality, asset with a provider VALUED_AT_COST, after the 14-day grace from the first acquisition TRANSACTION_IMPLIED, after the same 14-day grace, counted from the transfer's arrival (its first lot movement, as it has no BUY/SELL; see Data Quality Banner) Lots analysis Days at cost, CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST, value_source = ESTIMATED_AT_COST, no price line A mark from the transfer day: value_source = MARKET_PRICE, price series points with estimated=True; a boundary leg's reference resolves "fallback" (REFERENCE_PRICE_FALLBACK)

Example (test_transfer_cost_estimate.py): 10 units at 50 USD, report in EUR, USD→EUR 0.9 / 0.8 / 0.7 on three days → value 450 / 400 / 350 and P&L 0 / −50 / −100, capital 450; before, 450 every day. Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_financial_math/test_price_marks_transfer_estimate.py (pure) and backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_financial/test_portfolio_engine/test_transfer_cost_estimate.py (the engine).

docs.title: 🧾 No observation: valued at cost
docs.text:
When the series has nothing on or before the day, the portfolio engine does not leave a held position unvalued if its cost is known. DailyStateBuilder._value_held_position() (financial_math/portfolio/daily_state.py) asks _market_value_for() first; on a MISSING answer, a position whose average-cost pool is complete in the report currency (CostStep.report_complete) counts at its book cost, cost_report_for(qty) — each acquisition converted at its own date, never at the valuation date. That is a declared estimate, not a price (developer decision, option A):

ValuationResult field Value at cost source ValuationSource.ESTIMATED_AT_COST market_value The book cost of the held quantity, in the report currency effective_unit_price / effective_currency None — no price is reported reference_date / reference_unit_price / reference_currency None stale, missing_fx_pair False, None — no price ages and no rate is read

The position is not missing, so the day's NAV stays complete and its synthetic P&L candle is not dropped (the cost counts as a flat value). Its unrealized result is zero: _add_unrealized_part(..., at_cost=True) adds nothing to the unrealized split, neither an asset nor an exchange-rate part (see WAC & Cost Basis). With its cost unknown or incomplete, the position stays MISSING and is left out of the NAV. A missing exchange rate on a mark that exists is not this case: the mark is there, only its conversion fails.

The choice is made day by day, with no look-ahead: the cost stands in only on the days before the asset's first observation. From the first quote, BUY, SELL or transfer cost estimate on, the resolver always has a mark — carried forward when it is old, and flagged stale past STALE_PRICE_THRESHOLD_DAYS — and the price wins.

A cost stands in wherever the engine needs the value of a security with no observation — the book cost, except for units in transit, which keep the cost recorded on the transfer:

Where Value Held position, daily and end-date snapshot (_value_held_position()) The book cost of the held quantity Orphan TRANSFER leg (_transfer_leg_capital()) The cost the leg moves in its pool (step.cost_report_change): the cost it adds, or the average cost it removes — the capital follows the pool's book cost both ways, as for an incoming in-kind ADJUSTMENT (an outgoing one, which has no value, moves no capital). An unknown cost counts as zero, the pool's own convention. While the pool's cost is complete the leg is neutral, the holding being valued at that same cost; with the pool's cost incomplete the holding is MISSING, yet the leg still moves its known cost, so nothing is left in capital once the units are gone. An incoming leg with a cost basis reaches this case only when something of the scope precedes it (an ADJUSTMENT, an outgoing leg): otherwise its cost is the asset's estimated mark on its day, and the leg counts at that market value Internal TRANSFER pair between two brokers (_internal_pair_value()) The book cost the arrival adds to the receiver's pool (_movement_cost_step() of the receiving leg: the cost recorded on that leg, converted at its date), rescaled from the receiver's share to the sender's, whether or not the receiver's pool is complete; an arrival of unknown cost adds 0, so there is no flow. With the receiver's pool complete, that is what its NAV takes the units at. With it incomplete, the receiver's holding is MISSING: the receiver's line takes the gap — its own unknown cost, with the NAV incomplete — and the sender's line is the same as with a complete pool Units in transit (_compute_in_transit()) The cost recorded on the transfer, converted at the arrival date

The holding's valuation hierarchy is therefore MARKET_PRICE (a quote, exact or carried) > LAST_TRADE_PRICE (the last BUY/SELL, carried) > ESTIMATED_AT_COST > MISSING. The Dashboard warns about the at-cost positions of assets with a provider with VALUED_AT_COST, more than 14 days after the asset's first acquisition (see Data Quality Banner). The lots analysis follows the same day-by-day rule: it values an open LONG lot at its cost on every day with no observation on or before it, and its own warning, CURRENT_PRICE_ASSUMED_AT_COST, names those days — see Lots Analysis Service.

docs.title: 🔌 Who consumes it
docs.text:
Two consumers use the resolver today:

Consumer What it uses it for Portfolio engine (financial_math/portfolio/) The daily valuation brain: engine.py builds one AssetPriceSeries per held asset, and DailyStateBuilder (daily_state.py) reads it to build the daily portfolio states → NAV snapshots → ROI/TWRR/MWRR (financial_math/returns.py) and the value/P&L history lines; on request, also the synthetic P&L candles (with ohlc_by_date) lots_analysis_service.py One series per analysis, built before the FIFO engine runs: the reference price of a lot opened by an ADJUSTMENT (its mark on the opening day), the days valued at cost (last_day_without_observation()), then the qbq-aware lot valuations, the market_prices / estimated_market_prices maps and the performance NAV — see Lots Analysis Service

Everything downstream (dashboard KPIs, portfolio/broker reports, AI Export valuation sections) reads numbers these two produced, which is what makes the resolver the single source: a change here moves every chart and every metric together.

docs.title: 🧾 Transaction Service Architecture
docs.text:
Transaction batch execution is split across these source modules, in backend/app/services/transactions/:

File Responsibility backend/app/services/transactions/transaction_service.py TransactionService: the execute_batch() orchestrator and delete_by_broker(), composed of the mixins below backend/app/services/transactions/access.py TransactionAccessMixin: broker access checks, once per broker a batch touches backend/app/services/transactions/validation.py TransactionValidationMixin: asset event links, the rows that require a cost basis, linked-pair rules backend/app/services/transactions/queries.py TransactionQueryMixin: the transaction query, partner brokers, rows by id backend/app/services/transactions/balances.py TransactionBalancesMixin: the balance replay and the balances at a date backend/app/services/transactions/event_suggestions.py TransactionEventSuggestionsMixin: asset events a transaction can link to (suggest_events_bulk()) and the list of transactions that have none (event_reconciliation()) backend/app/services/transactions/promotion.py TransactionPromotionMixin: transfer promotion, the split and promote type maps, promote suggestions backend/app/services/transactions/auto_cost.py TransactionAutoCostMixin: WAC dispatch for the Auto cost basis backend/app/services/transactions/unreadable_rows.py count_unreadable_rows() and UnreadableLedgerError: the transactions whose stored value cannot be read, counted before the Auto cost's pool (W-B69) and a broker's balances (W-B74) backend/app/services/transactions/transaction_batch_context.py TransactionBatchContext and the balance-replay exception shared across stages backend/app/services/transactions/transaction_batch_stages.py The stages that open and close a batch: parse, the decimal-limit, date and cost-basis-sign checks, preload/access, balance replay, response backend/app/services/transactions/batch_edits.py Deletes, splits, updates, and the check of updated linked pairs backend/app/services/transactions/batch_creates.py Creates, promotes, and the links between the legs of new pairs backend/app/services/transactions/batch_costs.py WAC and FX issues, and the required cost basis

The former 637-line execute_batch() C901 hotspot has been decomposed. The public orchestrator is now approximately 50 source lines and makes the execution order explicit.

docs.title: 🧰 Responsibilities
docs.text: Area Current owner CRUD and pair helpers TransactionService Batch inputs and cross-stage state TransactionBatchContext Access scope and ordered mutations transaction_batch_stages.py (access), batch_edits.py and batch_creates.py (mutations) Linked-pair persistence Stage code writes reciprocal related_transaction_id values WAC _compute_wac_for_auto_items() delegates to compute_wac_iterative() Balance validation The final mutation stage flushes, then replays each affected broker from its earliest affected date. The cash is read by financial_math.native_cash.first_negative_cash (never summed by hand), and a broker without allow_cash_overdraft is refused on a negative cash even when it is the opening one and no transaction follows the first affected date (W6-12); the quantities walk the same days; the lowest day wins, the cash on a tie Transaction completion The API caller commits or rolls back; the service does neither

docs.title: 🚪 Entry Point — execute_batch()
docs.text:
The /transactions/validate and /transactions/commit routes call the same method:

async def execute_batch(
    self,
    creates_raw: List[dict],
    updates_raw: List[dict],
    deletes: List[int],
    splits_raw: List[dict] | None = None,
    promotes_raw: List[dict] | None = None,
    user_id: Optional[int] = None,
    commit: bool = False,
) -> TXBatchResponse:

Its order is contractual:

# Stage call Purpose 1 parse_inputs(), then check_decimal_limits(), check_dates() and check_cost_basis_sign() Parse create, update, split, and promote rows independently; then refuse a quantity, cash amount, manual cost basis or the cost basis a promote resolves over its column's limit (C-97, see Decimal limits), a date after tomorrow by the server's calendar (N74, see Transaction dates), and either cost basis below 0 (J-60, see Cost basis sign) 2 preload_and_authorize() Load referenced rows, collect touched brokers, and require EDITOR access 3 apply_deletes() Stage valid deletions 4 apply_splits() Split linked pairs before any dependent update 5 apply_updates() Apply and validate merged update state. An explicit cost_basis_override: null removes the row's cost basis where its type and side take one, unless the update is in Auto; step 11 then refuses the update where one is required (decision P5, see Persisted Cost Basis) 6 validate_updated_pairs() Re-check shared description/tags on updated linked pairs 7 apply_creates() Add and flush valid creates so generated IDs are available 8 apply_promotes() Resolve saved or same-batch rows and promote them in place 9 resolve_create_links() Resolve unconsumed create correlation groups into reciprocal database links 10 compute_wac_and_fx_issues() Run create/update auto-WAC; convert missing FX data into issues, and refuse an Auto row whose average of 0 comes from a pool with nothing to average (autoCostEmptyPool, autoCostUnknownPool, N88: Nothing to average) 11 validate_cost_basis() Flush and enforce required cost basis after WAC and promote handling 12 validate_balances() Flush and replay end-of-day balances from each broker's earliest affected date 13 finalize_response() Derive committed, result statuses, counts, and WAC output

docs.title: 🧳 Shared batch context
docs.text:
TransactionBatchContext.from_inputs() normalizes optional split/promote lists and stores all state that must survive across stages. This includes:

  • parsed rows with their original per-operation indices;
  • issues (blocking), warnings (non-blocking) and per-operation results;
  • preloaded transactions and the touched-broker set;
  • the earliest affected date per broker;
  • every row apply_creates() flushed, by its create index (created_by_index): the row a create's Auto cost is written on (W-B67);
  • transient create-correlation groups and the groups consumed by promote;
  • optional inline wac_results; and
  • commit_requested, which affects only final response semantics.

Keeping this state explicit lets each stage remain independently readable without changing the single-session behavior of the old implementation.

docs.title: 🧯 Error collection boundaries
docs.text:
Raw create, update, split, and promote rows are parsed leniently, and the mutation loops append row-level failures while continuing with other rows. This is not a promise that every possible error is collected:

  • any accessDenied issue, a checked value past its column's digits before the decimal point (see Decimal limits), or a date out of range (see Transaction dates), causes an early response right after the access check, before the mutation stages run: committed=False, the issues collected so far, empty results;
  • inline WAC is skipped when a non-balance issue already exists; and
  • balance replay catches the first balance exception and does not continue through the remaining broker/date replays.

docs.title: 📏 Per-type rules
docs.text:
validate_transaction_business_rules() (backend/app/schemas/transactions/transactions.py) checks the final state of each created, updated and promoted row. Its callers are TXCreateItem.validate_transaction_rules (after the create-only rules 1–4), _validate_updated_final_state() (batch_edits.py) and _promoted_state_issues() (batch_creates.py). Rules 5–12 read the type's row of TX_TYPE_METADATA (get_tx_type_metadata()), the table GET /transactions/types serves to the frontend, each time they run, so they follow any change to it:

Rule Reads Refuses 5 asset_mode: required A missing asset (assetRequired); optional (rule 6) checks nothing, and forbidden is left to a create's rules 3, 3b and 4 (an update or a promote cannot set an asset) 7, 8 cash_mode: required, forbidden Missing cash (cashRequired); a cash movement (cashForbidden) 9 event_compatible() An asset event link on another type (eventTypeIncompatible, its allowed param from event_compatible_types()) or without an asset (eventRequiresAsset) 10, 11 quantity_sign, cash_sign A quantity, or a non-zero cash amount, of the wrong sign (qtyPositive, qtyNegative, qtyZero, qtyNonzero; cashSignPositive, cashSignNegative); a zero cash amount where cash_sign is nonzero (cashNonzero; see below for when) 12 cost_basis_allowed() A cost_basis_mode where the type and side take no cost basis (costBasisModeIncompatible; see Persisted Cost Basis) 12b cost_basis_allowed(), cost_basis_set A non-null cost_basis_override the request sets without a cost_basis_mode where the type and side take no cost basis, an ADJUSTMENT taking units out included (costBasisNotAllowed; see below)

Decision P6 (the developer's, 2026-10-16) sets when four of these refusals hold: a TRANSFER's cash (cashForbidden), FX_CONVERSION's non-zero quantity (qtyZero), TRANSFER's zero quantity (qtyNonzero), and the zero cash of FX_CONVERSION and CASH_TRANSFER (cashNonzero). In an update, each holds only when its field changes: the cash for the first and the last, the quantity for the middle two. changed_rule_fields() compares the row by value with stored_rule_values, the row as stored before the batch, so a row stored outside the table stays editable: its notes, tags or date, or the field re-sent as stored. A promote changes the type, which counts as a changed cash and quantity, so it checks all four. A create (changed_fields=None) keeps them in its own rules 2, 3 and 3b. This mirrors N2's cost check, which judges only an update that touches the cost (see Persisted Cost Basis).

Rule 12b (W-B72; night decision N78, and N78-1, the developer's decision of 21/10/2026) reads cost_basis_set: whether the request sets a non-null cost_basis_override. The create passes it from TXCreateItem.validate_transaction_rules, the update from _validate_updated_final_state(); _promoted_state_issues() leaves it false, as a promote's resolved cost basis has its own check (_resolved_cost_issues(), see Request shape). Where cost_basis_allowed() is false, the cost basis is refused with costBasisNotAllowed, params {type, qty}. That includes an ADJUSTMENT taking units out: it has no value (N78-1), and every engine ignores a cost basis an older row of that kind still stores (FifoInputTransaction.from_transaction()). Rule 12b is rule 12's elif: a request that names a mode gets costBasisModeIncompatible alone. It judges only a cost basis the request sets: never one the row already stores — a notes-only edit of an older row carrying a stray one commits and keeps it — and never an explicit null. Before W-B72, a cost basis sent without a mode was stored on any type. Tests: ./dev.py test services transaction-cost-basis-rule (TestN78*).

A create meets its business rules at the lenient parse (_parse_lenient(), transaction_batch_stages.py): TXCreateItem raises a lone business-rule error as it is, and packs several into multipleBusinessRuleErrors, which the parse unpacks into one issue each. The parse takes each issue's params from error_params() and an error's field from loc_to_field() (a packed sub-error has none), both in backend/app/utils/pydantic_errors.py: the one home of the rule (W-B77), which the broker import's BRIMProvider._create_transaction() shares, so a row the import's parse refuses and the same row the batch refuses carry the same field and params. params is a copy of the error's context when every value is plain data (PLAIN_PARAM_TYPES: str, int, float, bool or None), null otherwise, whatever the error: a lone business rule ({type}, {type, qty}; since W-B72, before which its message lost the {type} it names), each sub-error of a packed one, filtered one by one (W-B70; before, each context was copied as it came), and a field's error (W-B70), so the app's message can name the limit (transactions.pydantic.stringTooLong for string_too_long, in resolveValidationMessage.ts): string_too_long keeps {max_length: 500} on a description, greater_than {gt: 0} on an id, greater_than_equal {ge: 0} on an update's asset_event_id, a date's parsing error pydantic's {error: <text>}, model_type {class_name}. A value_error, whose context holds the exception itself, a bound held as a Decimal, and an error without context (missing, extra_forbidden, string_type) keep params null. An update's and a promote's rule errors, raised after the parse, already carried their context.

The frontend reads the two codes as transactions.errors.costBasisNotAllowed and transactions.errors.costBasisModeIncompatible, messages that name the type and leave qty out. The second had no message before W-B72, so the app showed the backend's English. TestN78TheMessages (test_transaction_cost_basis_rule.py) holds every business-rule code of backend/app/schemas/transactions/transactions.py — the literal first argument of each PydanticCustomError, the multipleBusinessRuleErrors wrapper aside — to a message in English, Italian, French and Spanish.

docs.title: 🔢 Decimal limits
docs.text:
check_decimal_limits() (transaction_batch_stages.py; C-97, issue #43) reads every parsed create and update, and the cost basis each promote resolves (resolved_fields.cost_basis_override, a merged value only an API client sends: see Request shape), on the same cost_basis_override column: until W-B58 a promote's cost skipped the check, and the REAL rounded it in silence. A quantity keeps 10 decimal places, a cash.amount 6 and a manual cost_basis_override — a per-unit price — 12, the scales of their transactions columns; any of them at most 15 significant digits; and at most 15 digits before the decimal point for a quantity or a cash amount (decision N63), 12 for a cost basis: decimal_limit_issue() (backend/app/db/precision.py) takes the scale and the digits before the point (max_integer_digits()) from the model, and does not count trailing zeros. An Auto cost basis (cost_basis_mode auto or auto-detail) is not checked: the batch recomputes its amount and reads only its currency (auto_cost.py), so the preview's average the Form sends back, 100 / 3 in full, is no value of the user's. A value over a limit is refused, never rounded: one issue per field, with code decimalPlacesExceeded, significantDigitsExceeded or integerDigitsExceeded (all three in TXValidationCode, listed by GET /transactions/types → validation_codes), the first in that order when a value is over several, integerDigitsExceeded also for a value that is not finite; params {"max": N} and field (quantity, cash.amount or cost_basis_override). A promote's issue has operation promote and the promote's index. The English error names the field and the limit, such as Quantity: at most 15 digits before the decimal point. The frontend puts the field label in front of the three codes, listed with dateOutOfRange in FIELD_PREFIXED_CODES (resolveValidationMessage.ts; the third is transactions.errors.integerDigitsExceeded, At most {max} digits before the decimal point): Quantity: At most 10 decimal places.

The issue keeps the batch from being committed, but the row stays in it: the later stages still apply it, so a linked pair is not broken by it, and the batch's other issues are reported with it (the inline WAC is skipped, as for any non-balance issue). Not so when a checked value has more digits before the decimal point than its column takes, or is not finite, whatever code its issue got (a quantity of 400 digits keeps significantDigitsExceeded, the first in order): check_decimal_limits() then returns True, and execute_batch() stops right after preload_and_authorize(), step 2 above, with the early response of a denied access: committed=False, the issues collected so far, no results. The stages after it compute with the values (products, averages, the double a REAL stores), and a value that large broke them with a 500 where the user is owed the issue (W-B58). The check runs when a batch is confirmed (/transactions/validate, /transactions/commit), not when a broker import builds its rows (decision D2): the import hands its rows to the bulk workspace, which shows the refusal with the batch's other issues. A figure a plugin computes instead of reading it, such as a per-unit cost from a total, is rounded by the plugin (decision D6, see Decimal places): on a RealDecimal column, a quantity, a cash amount (since W-B60) or a per-unit cost, it then meets neither of the first two refusals; no rounding takes away digits before the decimal point, which are checked as for any other value. The column types are in Decimal Columns.

Above these limits sits the exponent bound of the currency schema (R13-SEC7-3, see Decimal Columns): a Currency amount — a cash amount, a cost basis, the cost basis a promote resolves (typed since H-41) — whose exponent (Decimal.adjusted()) is outside ±100, 0E-999999999 included, never reaches check_decimal_limits(). The lenient parse refuses its row, or its promote: a value_error issue on the field (cash.amount, cost_basis_override.amount), no params. As with any parse refusal, the batch's other operations are still checked, and nothing is committed. A quantity is no Currency: 1E+1000000 units still get integerDigitsExceeded. Before R13-SEC7-3, a promote's resolved cost basis that the currency schema refused, such as an amount that is no number, reached the promotion, whose Currency.model_validate() raised out of the batch: a 500.

docs.title: ➖ Cost basis sign
docs.text:
check_cost_basis_sign() (transaction_batch_stages.py; J-60) runs after check_decimal_limits() and check_dates(), and refuses a manual cost basis below 0; 0 stays allowed, -0 included (a gift, the new shares of a split). It reads the cost where check_decimal_limits() reads it (_decimal_limit_values(), _promote_cost_amount()): the manual cost_basis_override of a create, or of an update that sends one, and the cost basis a promote resolves (resolved_fields.cost_basis_override). An Auto cost basis (cost_basis_mode auto or auto-detail) is not checked: it is the batch's own average, not a value of the user's. Below 0, the row gets one issue: code costBasisNegative (TXValidationCode.COST_BASIS_NEGATIVE, listed by GET /transactions/types → validation_codes), field cost_basis_override, the row's operation and index, an update's id as ref_id, no params, and the English error Cost basis override: cannot be negative, 0 or more. The frontend reads the code as transactions.errors.costBasisNegative, The cost basis can't be negative: enter 0 or more., without the field label in front (it is not in FIELD_PREFIXED_CODES).

The issue keeps the batch from being committed (finalize_response(): any issue means committed=False), but, unlike the integer digits and the dates, the check does not stop the batch: a negative cost overflows nothing the later stages compute. The row stays in the batch, so a linked pair is not broken by it, and the row's other refusals come in the same answer: its decimal places, or a balance it takes below zero, which only the replay of step 12 finds; the inline WAC is skipped, as for any non-balance issue. An update that does not send the cost is not checked: a row an older version stored at a negative cost stays editable (notes, tags) until its cost is touched. An update that sends that cost back, even unchanged, is refused; the app sends only the fields that change (buildUpdateDiff()). A broker import confirms through this batch, so a negative cost read from a file is refused when the bulk workspace validates or saves its rows (decision D2). Tests: ./dev.py test services transaction-cost-basis-rule J60 (TestJ60*).

docs.title: 📅 Transaction dates
docs.text:
check_dates() (transaction_batch_stages.py; decision N74 of R13-SEC7-3) runs right after check_decimal_limits(). A transaction's date may be no later than tomorrow by the server's calendar (latest_range_end(), utils/datetime_utils.py: server_today(), the server's local date, plus one day); latest_transaction_date() returns it. There is no first date since decision D-P4 (26/10/2026): a transaction of 1850, or of the year 1, is written like any other, and the engine and the lots replay it from its own day (before, the floor was 1900-01-01). The protection against a typo in the year is in the interface: the form, the bulk editor and the import review ask for one confirmation before a date earlier than 1900 (preFloorDate.ts). The last day is also the last one a price or a rate written by hand may carry (N83). The stage reads:

  • the date of every parsed create;
  • the date of an update that sets one: an update that leaves an older row's date alone is not refused for it;
  • the date a promote resolves (resolved_fields.date): typed since H-41, so one that is no date, or an explicit null, is already refused at the parse (see Request shape).

Past the ceiling, the row gets one issue: code dateOutOfRange (TXValidationCode.DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE, listed by GET /transactions/types → validation_codes), field date, params {"max"} as an ISO date, and the English error Date: not after 2026-10-20 on a server whose today is 19 October 2026. The code kept its name when the floor went; it had {"min", "max"} before D-P4. A promote's issue has operation promote and the promote's index; an update's has the row's id as ref_id. check_dates() then returns True, and execute_batch() stops right after preload_and_authorize(), as for the integer digits: the batch's usual 200, with committed=False, the issues collected so far and no results. It stops because the stages after it replay a broker's days and look rates up at a row's date. A broker import (BRIM) confirms through this batch, so its rows are checked here too, when the bulk workspace validates or saves them (as for the decimal limits, decision D2).

The bound is tomorrow, not today, as slack for a user east of the server, whose today can already be the server's tomorrow. No legitimate date goes further: the interface never offers a future date (SingleDatePicker, whose allowFuture is false by default), and a broker import keeps only settled rows (the rule The operation date, and only settled rows of the plugin guide), so a later date is a typing error. Lot N74 set the bound there; before, it was a year after today, for the settlement dates a broker's report puts ahead: under that rule, a plugin now leaves such a row out until it has settled. The frontend reads the code as transactions.errors.dateOutOfRange, Not after {max}, behind the field label (FIELD_PREFIXED_CODES): Date: Not after 2026-10-20.

docs.title: 🔁 Session and Response Semantics
docs.text:
execute_batch() mutates and flushes the AsyncSession supplied to TransactionService. It never calls commit(), rollback(), begin(), creates a savepoint, or opens a replacement session. The commit argument only selects the response that finalize_response() builds.

Caller Service response Caller action /transactions/validate (commit=False) committed=False, whether clean or not Always session.rollback() /transactions/commit (commit=True), no issues committed=True session.commit() /transactions/commit (commit=True), any issue committed=False; successfully staged results become simulated session.rollback()

TXBatchResponse has no rolled_back field. Its transaction-specific contract is:

Field Meaning committed Whether the commit route is allowed to commit this batch issues Structured TXValidationIssue entries: each one blocks the commit warnings Structured TXValidationIssue entries that never block a commit and correct nothing (B2); [] when nothing warns. Present in every response, committed or not results Per-operation operation, original index, affected ids, optional create link_uuid, and status success_count Number of operations staged successfully; this is not proof that their rows persisted wac_results Optional WAC output for create/update rows using auto or auto-detail

The response also inherits errors from BaseBulkResponse; transaction validation failures are reported through issues. On a dry run, a successfully staged result keeps status success even though the route rolls back. On a failed commit request, those same staged results are marked simulated.

Multi-broker atomicity at the route boundary means a batch may span brokers, but the commit route persists none of it when committed=False.

docs.title: 🔐 Access Control
docs.text:
preload_and_authorize() derives the access scope from parsed creates and from database rows referenced by updates, deletes, splits, and saved promote references. _denied_brokers() calls _check_broker_access(..., min_role=UserRole.EDITOR) once per distinct touched broker. _append_access_issues() then refuses each row that touches a denied broker, on that row's own coordinates: one accessDenied issue, with params {"brokerId": id}, per row and denied broker.

Row Issue operation, index ref_id Create on a denied broker create, the row's index None Update or delete update / delete, the row's index The saved transaction it names Split or promote split / promote, the row's index The saved leg on the denied broker: two issues when the two legs sit on two denied brokers Promote leg named by link_uuid — None added: the create it names already carries the refusal No row (fallback) create, -1 None

A row that touches the same denied broker twice, such as a split of an intra-broker FX_CONVERSION, gets one issue. The fallback covers a denied broker that no row explains, so a denial is never silent. The bulk editor maps operation:index back to its rows, so the refusal lands on the row that caused it — for example the receiving leg (1b) of a new TRANSFER whose destination is a broker the user can only view — and labels an issue with a negative index by the broker in params.brokerId.

When a broker is denied, preload_and_authorize() returns True and execute_batch() responds before any delete, split, update, create, or promote is applied.

Role hierarchy is OWNER > EDITOR > VIEWER; mutation requires at least EDITOR.

docs.title: 🔗 Linked Pairs
docs.text:
TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION, and CASH_TRANSFER are two-row composite transactions. A create request uses link_uuid only as transient correlation:

  1. apply_creates() records each flushed row by its create index in context.created_by_index (where the Auto cost finds it, see Inline Batch Auto Modes), and one carrying a link_uuid in context.link_uuid_map too;
  2. resolve_create_links() validates each unconsumed two-row group; and
  3. the stage writes reciprocal related_transaction_id values.

Transaction has no persisted link_uuid column. The durable relationship is A.related_transaction_id = B.id and B.related_transaction_id = A.id.

_validate_linked_pair() requires equal pair types (pairTypeMismatch), distinct brokers for TRANSFER and CASH_TRANSFER (pairSameBroker), and one broker for both legs of an FX_CONVERSION (pairBrokerMismatch, params brokerA/brokerB). A TRANSFER pair must also move one asset (pairAssetMismatch, params assetA/assetB) by exactly opposite quantities, compared as Decimal (pairQuantityMismatch, params qtyA/qtyB): what leaves one broker arrives at the other, and no unit is created or lost. A CASH_TRANSFER pair must move one currency (pairCurrencyMismatch, params currencyA/currencyB) by exactly opposite amounts, again compared as Decimal (pairAmountMismatch, params amountA/amountB), and an FX_CONVERSION pair must change currency (pairCurrencySame, param currency) (W6-7). These are the pair_field_constraints of TX_TYPE_METADATA; test_linked_cash_pair.py fails when the table declares a constraint the function does not know. Only a pair being created is judged: a pair a database already holds is never read by these rules. The first rule that fails is the group's only issue, on operation create at the first leg's index, and the two rows stay unlinked. Pair description and tags are checked separately by _validate_pair_description_tags().

A pair in the wrong order is a warning, never an error (B2). When the arrival leg of a linked TRANSFER or CASH_TRANSFER is dated before its departure leg, the pair is saved as sent and warnings carries pairArrivalBeforeDeparture (params departureDate and arrivalDate, ISO dates; the message is transactions.errors.pairArrivalBeforeDeparture). The departure is the leg with the negative quantity (the negative amount, for cash); equal dates are in order. It is judged at the two places a pair gets its dates: a create group (resolve_create_links(), on the first create of the group, ref_id null) and an update that really changes the date of a leg of a stored pair (warn_inverted_updated_pairs(), on the first update that changed one, ref_id its id), on the final dates of both legs: one warning per pair, none when both legs move to a normal order. A pair already stored in the wrong order is never judged again, and an update carrying the stored date changes nothing.

docs.title: 🔁 Event Reconciliation
docs.text:
A transaction of type DIVIDEND, INTEREST or ADJUSTMENT can point at an asset event (asset_event_id). It loses the pointer when a currency change deletes the events that are not SPLITs (N68), and it never had one when the dividend was booked before the event was synced. GET /api/v1/transactions/event-reconciliation lists those transactions with the event each could take, so the user can link them again. It is the read half of the flow: it writes nothing and never links by itself.

sequenceDiagram
    actor U as User
    participant P as Transactions page (EventReconciliationModal)
    participant API as Backend

    U->>P: Relink events
    P->>API: GET /transactions/event-reconciliation
    API-->>P: rows: unique / none / several
    U->>P: Link (one row) or Link every row with one event
    P->>API: POST /transactions/commit  updates: [{id, asset_event_id}]
    API-->>P: committed, or issues and nothing linked
    P-->>U: linked rows leave the list; the page reloads

Rows (TransactionEventSuggestionsMixin.event_reconciliation(), services/transactions/event_suggestions.py): the caller's transactions with an asset_id, no asset_event_id and an event-compatible type (event_compatible_types() of schemas/transactions/type_metadata.py), on the brokers where the caller holds a BrokerUserAccess row of role EDITOR or OWNER: the ones they could link on, so a viewer's brokers never appear. Optional query parameters broker_id and asset_id (both above 0) narrow the list. Order: date descending, then id descending.

Candidates reuse suggest_events_bulk() with tolerance_days=0: the same asset, the same date, and the event type that corresponds to the transaction type, with no window of dates:

Transaction type Event types it can take DIVIDEND DIVIDEND INTEREST INTEREST ADJUSTMENT PRICE_ADJUSTMENT, SPLIT

The mixin asks once per distinct (asset, date, type), so a day with several dividends of one asset costs one query. The answer is a list of TXEventReconciliationItem (schemas/transactions/event_suggest.py): transaction_id, broker_id, asset_id, date, type, status and candidates (the same TXEventSuggestCandidate the suggest endpoint returns: id, date, type, value, currency, is_auto, distance_days).

status Candidates What the interface does unique exactly one Proposes it: Link on the row, and the row counts for Link every row with one event none zero Says no event exists that day several two or more, all listed Proposes nothing, never guesses: the user picks the event in the transaction form

The tolerance_days=0 is deliberate: a dividend credited a few days after the event is not matched, and the user links it by hand. Automatic linking is not done; it is on the list of future work.

Frontend. The Relink events button (data-testid="tx-reconcile-events-button") of the Transactions page opens EventReconciliationModal.svelte (frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/). The module eventReconciliation.ts reads the list (loadEventReconciliation()), selects the rows that are safe to link (uniqueRows(): status unique and exactly one candidate, a double check of the server) and links them with linkReconciliation(), which sends one POST /transactions/commit with updates: [{id, asset_event_id}] (commitTransactions() of txCommitApi.ts). The commit is atomic like every batch: any issue and nothing is linked, and the rows are not retried with fewer. With nothing to link there is no request. On success the page reloads its transactions softly (onlinked).

Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_event_reconciliation_api.py (./dev.py test api event-reconciliation); in the frontend eventReconciliation.test.ts and EventReconciliationModal.test.ts (frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/) and e2e/transactions/tx-event-reconciliation.spec.ts.

docs.title: ✂️ Split Type Map
docs.text:
The split stage re-types the negative/source and positive/destination legs deterministically:

Paired type From leg To leg CASH_TRANSFER WITHDRAWAL DEPOSIT TRANSFER ADJUSTMENT ADJUSTMENT FX_CONVERSION WITHDRAWAL DEPOSIT

See Split & Promote for the in-place mutation rules and the separate legacy promote endpoint.

docs.title: 🗑️ Broker Deletion
docs.text:
delete_by_broker(broker_id) deletes every transaction of a broker and returns how many it deleted. Its callers are in BrokerService:

Caller When delete_bulk() DELETE /brokers?ids=…&force=true on a broker that still has transactions; it requires OWNER on the broker. An administrator may pass as_user_id (403 for anyone else): all skips the role check, <id> checks that user's role instead leave_broker() The last OWNER leaves (DELETE /brokers/{broker_id}/access/me): it calls delete_bulk() with force. Account deletion (delete_user(), accounts/user_service.py) calls leave_broker() on every broker of the account

The method checks neither access nor balances. The broker's own pairs, both halves on it (an intra-broker FX_CONVERSION), go whole: their links are cleared, then every row of the broker is deleted. A pair with another broker loses one half. The other half — on that broker, whatever the caller's role there — becomes the standalone row a split of the pair leaves (backlog V-3; D-J4, decisions of 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-15), instead of a linked type without its partner, which the FIFO lots refuse for a TRANSFER (TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING). One case only loses the link: a link no split knows.

Surviving half Becomes Received TRANSFER (quantity > 0) ADJUSTMENT with the same quantity, asset, cost basis and its currency, cash currency, date, description and tags; first given its sender's Auto cost when it has no cost basis (below) CASH_TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION WITHDRAWAL when its amount is negative, DEPOSIT otherwise, without asset Giving TRANSFER (quantity < 0) ADJUSTMENT with the same quantity, asset, cash currency, date, description and tags, without a cost basis: an ADJUSTMENT taking units out has no value (below) Any other type carrying a link (an ADJUSTMENT can, in data stored before: a new batch refuses to link two, pairAdjustmentNotAllowed) The same type, without its link

Each of these rows loses its related_transaction_id and gets a new updated_at, so the caches fingerprinted on it — the portfolio engine's (_compute_tx_fingerprint()) and the WAC facade's (compute_wac_iterative()) — compute again. No quantity or amount changes: the other broker's balances stay as they were.

The side rule and the per-half conversion are the split's own helpers in batch_edits.py, shared with apply_splits(): pair_sides() returns the giving and the receiving half (by quantity for a TRANSFER, by amount otherwise), and make_standalone() re-types one half in place, clears its link — and its asset, unless it becomes an ADJUSTMENT — and sets updated_at.

A received TRANSFER without a cost basis. One is required today — a batch that creates such a leg without it is refused with costBasisRequired (see Persisted Cost Basis) — but older data can lack it. Such a leg first gets its sender's Auto cost, computed while the sender's rows still exist: _auto_cost_source() names the pool — the sender's broker up to the date the units left, without the outgoing leg — _auto_cost() runs compute_wac_iterative() on it, and _write_auto_cost() writes cost_basis_override and cost_basis_currency together; all three helpers come from _compute_wac_for_auto_items() (auto_cost.py), which uses them too. Every cost is computed before any row changes, so a computation that fails leaves every row as it was (delete_bulk() reports that broker as failed). An empty pool gives what Auto gives, a zero cost (backlog P-1); a missing conversion writes nothing, and the ADJUSTMENT stays without a cost basis (see WAC & Cost Basis — Diagnostics).

The giving leg of a TRANSFER (decision 47 of release 1.3, as the developer changed it on 21/10/2026, N78-1). The outgoing side of a TRANSFER takes no cost basis (cost_basis_pair in TX_TYPE_METADATA marks it forbidden), and an ADJUSTMENT taking units out has no value: its units only leave the quantity, at 0 in the FIFO lots, and their cost is realized as a loss (see An ADJUSTMENT_OUT has no value). So make_standalone() turns the leg into an ADJUSTMENT and delete_by_broker() clears cost_basis_override and cost_basis_currency. No cost is computed for it, so it needs no rate and is always converted. Until N78-1 the leg left at the Auto cost of its own broker, and stayed a TRANSFER without its link when that cost needed a missing conversion.

An unreadable pool (W-B69). The Auto cost of a receiving leg raises UnreadablePoolError when its pool — the deleted broker's — holds a row whose quantity, amount or cost basis cannot be read (see Unreadable pool). The deletion of that broker then fails whole: delete_bulk() rolls back its savepoint and reports it failed with the error's message, which gives the number of such rows and never an id; nothing of that broker changes, and the other brokers of the request go on.

A giving leg leaves its pair the same way wherever else it does: on a split of the pair (see Split & Promote), and, on the legs that a deletion before 1.3 left as a TRANSFER without its partner, by the lone-transfer-legs step that runs right after the post-migration fixes (see Lone giving legs). Tests: ./dev.py test services broker (TestDeleteBulkCrossBrokerPair) and ./dev.py test services orphan-transfer-numbers (TestOrphanOutgoingTransfer: the sending broker's lots and Dashboard once the receiver is deleted).

What the conversion changes in the figures:

  • Received asset. The receiving broker's lots open a new lot on the transfer date, at the cost basis (ADJUSTMENT_IN in financial_math/fifo/engine.py): the holding period restarts, since the sender's lots can no longer move there with their own dates. On the Dashboard, the receiving broker's capital takes the units at their cost, as for any priced in-kind ADJUSTMENT (_is_capital_adjustment()), instead of their market value at arrival (DailyStateBuilder._transfer_leg_capital()): its gain also counts what the units gained before the transfer.
  • Given asset. The sending broker's lots no longer fail on TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING: the ADJUSTMENT_OUT closes its FIFO lots at 0, realizing their cost as a loss, and the asset's performance history counts no money out (see Lots Analysis Service). On the Dashboard the sending broker's capital does not move, instead of losing the units' market value on the transfer date (_transfer_leg_capital()): the units leave its NAV, and the average cost they give up is realized as a loss (DailyStateBuilder, see WAC & Cost Basis — Portfolio engine).
  • Cash halves. Capital and P&L do not change: an unlinked CASH_TRANSFER or FX_CONVERSION already counted as an external cash flow (ScopeAwareTransactionClassifier), as the DEPOSIT or WITHDRAWAL it becomes does, and the cash pools that fund purchases from new capital or from reinvested returns (K_b, R_b, W of the Three-Pool Cash Model) move for the unlinked leg exactly as for that DEPOSIT or WITHDRAWAL (B3, MF-J3). What reads the type now counts the converted row: the portfolio summary's total_deposited, total_withdrawn and net_deposited_capital; and the deposits series of get_deposit_history() (DEPOSIT only).

One savepoint per broker. delete_bulk() deletes each broker of a request in a savepoint of its own (self.session.begin_nested()) through _delete_one(), which flushes its writes, the broker's own delete included, while the savepoint is open: a write error surfaces before the savepoint is released. A broker whose deletion fails at any point — even after delete_by_broker() wrote an Auto cost on a surviving half or unlinked the broker's own pairs — leaves every row as it was, its own and the other halves on other brokers. Its result has success=False and the error as message; the brokers before and after it in the request are still deleted. delete_bulk() never commits; its caller does:

  • DELETE /brokers commits when response.errors is empty, which delete_bulk() never fills: a broker that fails is reported in results;
  • DELETE /brokers/{broker_id}/access/me commits when leave_broker() succeeds;
  • account deletion (delete_user()) is all or nothing: it rolls everything back when a broker cannot be released, and the savepoints nest inside its transaction.

Nesting needs an open transaction, and pysqlite defers BEGIN until the first write: a savepoint opened after reads alone is SQLite's outermost transaction, and its RELEASE commits — the caller's later rollback can no longer bring that broker back. So delete_bulk() first calls begin_writes(self.session, Broker) (backend/app/db/session.py), which runs an UPDATE of that table matching no row (where(false())): pysqlite emits BEGIN before it, and inside an open transaction it changes nothing. A write path that opens per-item savepoints after reads must call begin_writes() first; AssetCRUDService.delete_assets_bulk() (assets/crud.py) runs its own no-op UPDATE for the same reason. A global SQLAlchemy begin listener emitting BEGIN up front is ruled out: a session that reads, sees another writer commit, then writes, fails at once with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT.

Tests: ./dev.py test services broker (TestDeleteBulkOneSavepointPerBroker, BR-U-081…085) and ./dev.py test services user-profile (TestDeleteUser, the two test_delete_user_is_all_or_nothing_* cases); BR-U-082 and those two fail without begin_writes().

docs.title: ⚖️ Balance Queries
docs.text:
The service exposes two public query methods (TransactionBalancesMixin, balances.py):

await svc.get_cash_balances(broker_id, as_of=None)   # Dict[currency, Decimal]
await svc.get_asset_holdings(broker_id, as_of=None)  # Dict[asset_id, Decimal]

Both count the broker's rows dated up to as_of, inclusive, and every row when as_of is None.

  • Cash comes from the layer, the one home of cash per broker and currency: cash_movement_from_transaction(tx) turns each row with an amount and a currency into a movement at share 1 — the broker's own cash, not a user's share — and financial_math.native_cash.native_balances(), the function behind NativeCash.balances(), sums them by currency without any rate (see The Native-Cash Function). A currency whose movements cancel out keeps its line, at zero.
  • Holdings come from the layer too: financial_math.ledger_totals.position_quantities() sums the quantity of the broker's rows per asset, with the same date cut (see Ledger Control Totals). It skips a row of quantity 0, so an asset whose rows all have quantity 0 has no line: read a missing line as zero.

Both sums run in Python, exactly, over the rows the query returns; the query keeps only the filters. get_balances_at_end_of() sums the same way, through _get_balances_before_date(..., through=True) — the rows dated up to as_of included, never the eve of as_of + 1 day, which the calendar's last day does not have (W-B71); first it counts those whose quantity or amount cannot be read and raises UnreadableLedgerError for any (W-B74) — the starting balances of the end-of-day replay, and LibreFolio's side of the BRIM gap-fix, without its excluded ids — and so does the asset list's set of held assets (AssetCRUDService.list_assets(), then > QUANTITY_DUST_THRESHOLD). Never an SQL SUM (C-97): SQLite stores these columns as doubles, and SUM adds the doubles, not the decimals — 0.1 + 0.2 − 0.3 gives 2.8e-17, not 0 — an error the read at 6 decimals used to hide. Summed in Python, a zero balance is exactly zero.

The broker page does not call these two methods: its cash and its positions come from the portfolio report (see WAC & Cost Basis).

docs.title: 🧭 Valuation Boundary
docs.text:
TransactionService does not build market marks, portfolio NAV, or lot valuation. Its transaction prices are persisted facts; valuation consumers later feed those facts into build_asset_price_series() together with price_history.

Current flow:

flowchart LR
    TX[transaction_service.py<br/>CRUD + stored trade prices] --> FIFO["financial_math/fifo/<br/>realized matching from trades"]
    TX --> Resolver["financial_math/price_marks.py<br/>MARKET / TRADE_AVG / CARRIED / MISSING"]
    Prices[price_history] --> Resolver
    Resolver --> Lots[lots_analysis_service.py<br/>open-lot valuation + price history]
    Resolver --> Portfolio["portfolio_service / financial_math/portfolio/<br/>portfolio marks"]

So the transaction layer can affect marks only by storing transaction facts: the amounts and quantities of BUY and SELL rows. An ADJUSTMENT's cost basis is a cost, never a mark — it reaches valuation only as the book cost of a holding the resolver cannot mark at all (see Price Resolver — No observation: valued at cost). The layer never reads current prices and never performs estimated-at-cost valuation.

docs.title: ✂️ Split & Promote
docs.text:
Split and batch promote both change the shape of composite transactions, but they are not implemented as delete-and-recreate inverses:

Operation Direction Batch behavior Split Composite pair → two standalone rows Mutates both persisted rows in place and removes their reciprocal links Promote Two standalone rows → composite pair Mutates the resolved rows in place and creates reciprocal links

The durable pair is always stored with reciprocal related_transaction_id values. link_uuid is only a request-scoped correlation value for creates; it is not a column on Transaction.

docs.title: 🔢 Pipeline Position
docs.text:
The relevant execute_batch() stages run in this order:

delete → split → update → updated-pair validation → create → promote → create-link resolution
       → WAC and FX issues

Split deliberately precedes update. A batch can therefore split a pair and then apply updates whose type swaps are legal only for the resulting standalone types. Promote follows create so its references can resolve either persisted rows or rows that were flushed earlier in the same batch.

docs.title: ⚙️ In-place behavior
docs.text:
For each TXSplitBatchItem, apply_splits():

  1. resolves both required database IDs;
  2. verifies that each row's related_transaction_id points to the other;
  3. determines source/destination by negative/positive quantity for TRANSFER, or by negative/positive amount for cash pairs;
  4. changes both row types using SPLIT_TYPE_MAP;
  5. clears both related_transaction_id values;
  6. clears asset_id for the cash split outcomes;
  7. for a TRANSFER pair, clears cost_basis_override and cost_basis_currency on the giving leg, an ADJUSTMENT without a value (see The giving leg of a TRANSFER); and
  8. records both brokers' affected dates and a two-ID split result.

The rows keep their IDs. No create or delete is involved.

Source composite type Negative/source leg Positive/destination leg CASH_TRANSFER WITHDRAWAL DEPOSIT TRANSFER ADJUSTMENT ADJUSTMENT FX_CONVERSION WITHDRAWAL DEPOSIT

Deleting a broker with its transactions converts the surviving half of each pair with another broker by the same rules, through the same helpers of batch_edits.py: pair_sides() (step 3) and make_standalone() (steps 4–6), and leaves a giving TRANSFER leg without a cost basis, as a split does (below). One difference: a received TRANSFER without a cost basis first gets its sender's Auto cost, which a split does not write. See Transaction Service — Broker Deletion.

docs.title: 📤 The giving leg of a TRANSFER
docs.text:
A split TRANSFER pair leaves two ADJUSTMENTs. The receiving one keeps its cost basis. The giving one takes units out, and an ADJUSTMENT taking units out has no value (decision 47 of release 1.3, as the developer changed it on 21/10/2026, N78-1; see An ADJUSTMENT_OUT has no value): its units only leave the quantity, at 0 in the FIFO lots, and their cost is realized as a loss.

  • apply_splits() clears the leg's cost_basis_override and cost_basis_currency (step 7). No cost is computed, so the split needs no rate and is never refused for that leg: until N78-1 it left at the Auto cost of its own broker, and a missing conversion (wacFxUnavailable) or an unreadable pool (autoCostUnreadable) refused the split.
  • An update of the same batch cannot give the leg a cost: rule 12 refuses a cost_basis_mode on an ADJUSTMENT taking units out (costBasisModeIncompatible), and rule 12b a cost_basis_override set without one (costBasisNotAllowed, W-B72; see Per-type rules).

Tests: ./dev.py test services transaction-cost-basis-rule (TestDecision47TheGivingLegOfATransfer).

docs.title: 📦 Request shape
docs.text:
Split is a first-class item in the unified batch:

POST /transactions/commit
{
  "splits": [
    {"id_a": 101, "id_b": 102}
  ]
}

id_a and id_b must be different positive IDs and must identify the two reciprocally linked rows. Their input order does not determine source and destination; the signed quantity or amount does.

The Transactions page sends this item on its own, outside the bulk workspace: Split pair in a row's actions asks for confirmation, then calls commitTransactions({splits: [{id_a, id_b}]}). Inside the workspace a saved pair is queued in pendingSplits and travels with Save All instead (see Transaction Staging State).

docs.title: ⚙️ In-place behavior
docs.text:
apply_promotes() accepts:

  • two saved rows (id_a + id_b);
  • two creates from this batch (link_uuid_a + link_uuid_b); or
  • one saved and one same-batch row.

Each side must provide exactly one reference form: id_* or link_uuid_*, never both. After resolving the references, the stage:

  1. rejects a row that already has related_transaction_id;
  2. calls _find_promote_rule_match() to infer the target type from TX_TYPE_METADATA.promote_from and its field constraints;
  3. validates both rows as they would be once promoted: _promoted_state_issues() runs validate_transaction_business_rules() on each row with the target type, the per-type rules that creates and updates go through too. Each error becomes an issue on operation promote, at the promote's index, with ref_id set only for a saved row. _resolved_cost_issues() checks the merged cost basis beside them: a non-null resolved_fields.cost_basis_override where neither row takes a cost basis under the target type — a cash pair, CASH_TRANSFER or FX_CONVERSION — gets one costBasisNotAllowed, field cost_basis_override, params {type, qty}, no ref_id (W-B72, night decision N78). On any issue the promote is then skipped and neither row changes;
  4. assigns the inferred type to both existing ORM rows;
  5. writes reciprocal related_transaction_id values;
  6. clears cost_basis_override and cost_basis_currency on a side whose new type takes no cost basis (cost_basis_allowed() is false: the giving side of a TRANSFER), such as an ADJUSTMENT taking units out that an older version left with a cost; the receiving side keeps its own (decision 47);
  7. applies the merged values of resolved_fields, the keys the request names (see Request shape);
  8. marks same-batch correlation keys as consumed so the later create-link stage does not process them again; and
  9. emits a promote result containing the same two row IDs.

No original row is deleted and no replacement row is created.

Step 3 exists for a row linked to an asset event, such as an ADJUSTMENT linked to a SPLIT. A promote never clears asset_event_id, and the business rules accept that link only on the types TX_TYPE_METADATA marks event_compatible (DIVIDEND, INTEREST, ADJUSTMENT; see Per-type rules): every promote target has event_compatible: false, so such a row is refused with eventTypeIncompatible. Without the check it would become a TRANSFER still linked to the split, and the average cost, which treats every row linked to a SPLIT event as a split whatever its type, would read it as one.

docs.title: 🧭 Inferred target rules
docs.text:
The batch payload does not contain new_type. The current metadata permits:

Standalone input types Inferred target Required constraints ADJUSTMENT + ADJUSTMENT TRANSFER Same asset_id, different brokers, opposite quantities WITHDRAWAL + DEPOSIT FX_CONVERSION Same broker, different cash currencies WITHDRAWAL + DEPOSIT CASH_TRANSFER Different brokers, same cash currency, opposite cash amounts

The match is symmetric: either row may be supplied as side A.

docs.title: 📦 Request shape
docs.text:
A saved-row promote can carry merged values, resolved_fields:

POST /transactions/commit
{
  "promotes": [
    {
      "id_a": 201,
      "id_b": 202,
      "resolved_fields": {
        "description": "Broker transfer",
        "tags": ["internal"],
        "date": "2026-09-11",
        "cost_basis_override": {"code": "EUR", "amount": "42.50"}
      }
    }
  ]
}

resolved_fields is a TXPromoteResolvedFields (backend/app/schemas/transactions/batch.py; H-41, within R13-SEC7-3): a StrictModel typed like a create's fields, so an unknown key is refused.

Key Type Applied to description Optional[str], at most 500 characters Both rows tags Optional[List[str]], through the create's tag validator (validate_tags_list(): a list, or a comma-separated string) Both rows date Optional[date]; an explicit null is refused Both rows cost_basis_override Optional[Currency] For an asset transfer, the positive-quantity receiver only; the sender's is cleared (decision 47). A cash pair takes none: a value is refused (costBasisNotAllowed, step 3), where before W-B72 it was written on both rows; a null clears both

_apply_promote_resolved_fields() (batch_creates.py) applies the keys the request names (model_fields_set): a key left out leaves both rows alone, and an explicit null clears the description, the tags or the cost basis. Once parsed, the resolved cost basis is checked against its column (check_decimal_limits(), see Decimal limits) and the resolved date against the range (check_dates(), see Transaction dates), before any stage applies them.

A value the model refuses becomes an issue of the promote at the batch's parse (_parse_lenient()): operation promote, pydantic's error type as code, as params pydantic's context when it is plain data — {max_length: 500} for a description past 500 characters, {error: <pydantic's text>} for a malformed date, {class_name} for a cost basis that is no object — and null otherwise, for a value_error or an error without context (W-B70, the rule of Per-type rules; before, params was always null here), and a field named by the merged field itself, without the resolved_fields. prefix (loc_to_field() of backend/app/utils/pydantic_errors.py): description, tags, date, cost_basis_override, cost_basis_override.amount, or the unknown key. The issue thus carries that field's label. As with any parse refusal of this lenient batch, the other operations are still checked, then nothing is saved (committed=False). Before H-41 the dict was applied as sent: a malformed date, tags or cost basis raised out of the batch, a 500; a description that was no string reached the Text column; an unknown key was ignored.

The Transactions page sends a saved-row promote on its own, outside the workspace, when exactly two selected rows are unpaired, sit on brokers the user can edit, and match a rule (findPromoteMatch() on the promote_from metadata of GET /transactions/types, which finds none when a row is linked to an asset event and the target type refuses the link). 🔗 Promote pair then opens a plain confirmation, or PromoteMergeModal when the two rows differ in description, tags, date or cost basis; only the merge dialog adds resolved_fields, with description and tags alone, as Merge all does in the bulk workspace (PromoteAllModal): date and cost_basis_override come from API clients only. The merged description joins the two with a line break (mergeStrings() in frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/bulk/promoteHelpers.ts), so two long descriptions can pass 500 characters, which the backend refuses with string_too_long, as it refuses a create's (TXCreateItem.description takes 500 too). The frontend stops before it (W-B70; the backend limit is unchanged): PromoteMergeModal counts the merged description in code points, as Python's len() does (textLength() against TX_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH), and keeps Confirm promotion disabled past 500; Merge all with Combine leaves such a pair unpromoted, for the merge dialog, and a warning counts the pairs left (see Promote suggestions).

A mixed saved/new request uses a create correlation value:

POST /transactions/commit
{
  "creates": [
    {
      "broker_id": 8,
      "type": "DEPOSIT",
      "date": "2026-09-11",
      "cash": {"code": "EUR", "amount": "300"},
      "link_uuid": "draft-deposit-8"
    }
  ],
  "promotes": [
    {"id_a": 201, "link_uuid_b": "draft-deposit-8"}
  ]
}

Here link_uuid_b resolves the just-flushed create. Once consumed by promote, that correlation group is skipped by resolve_create_links(). The persisted rows contain only reciprocal related_transaction_id values.

docs.title: 🧮 Cost basis boundary
docs.text:
A promote item has no cost_basis_mode, and apply_promotes() does not calculate WAC. The later _compute_wac_for_auto_items() worklist is built only from parsed create and update items. Promote-specific cost-basis resolution therefore comes from resolved_fields.cost_basis_override, which only an API client sends (the merge dialogs send description and tags); without that key, the receiver keeps the cost basis it already has, and the sender is left without one (step 6).

Because apply_promotes() writes related_transaction_id before the WAC step, a create or update in Auto that the promote makes the receiving side averages its partner's broker, as of the partner's date and without the partner's outgoing leg.

validate_cost_basis() then checks the receiving side like any other row: a new row as a create and a saved row also in updates[] as that update (the promote changes its type, so even an update of its notes alone is checked), both unless in Auto; any other saved row without a cost basis gets costBasisRequired on operation promote, with the promote's index and ref_id set to that row. See WAC & Cost Basis.

docs.title: 🧯 Errors and Rollback
docs.text:
Split/promote row failures are accumulated as TXValidationIssue entries while their stage loops continue. Common stable codes are:

Code Cause txNotFound A split ID does not resolve splitIdsMismatch Split IDs are not reciprocal partners typeCannotSplit The current pair type has no split mapping promoteRefNotFound A saved or same-batch promote reference cannot be resolved alreadyPaired A promote candidate already has a persistent partner noPromoteRule No metadata rule and constraint set matches the two rows eventTypeIncompatible A promoted row is linked to an asset event, which the target type refuses (step 3) costBasisNotAllowed On operation promote: a cash pair's resolved cost_basis_override, which neither leg takes (step 3, W-B72)

The service does not roll the session back itself. /transactions/validate always rolls back; /transactions/commit commits only when TXBatchResponse.committed is true and rolls back otherwise. Access denial, a value past its column's digits before the decimal point or a date out of range may return before either mutation stage, and balance replay stops after its first balance exception, so the overall pipeline is not an unconditional collect-every-error pass.
