docs.title: 🏷️ Release Tag Convention (F14 update prompt)
docs.text:
The in-app "new version available" prompt reads GET /repos/Librefolio/LibreFolio/releases/latest (GitHub Releases API) and compares tag_name numerically against the running version. It runs automatically for administrators after login, and on demand from the changelog modal. Rules for any new release:

  • Tag the release vX.Y.Z — the leading v is optional (1.2.0 works too), but the tag must be exactly three numbers. Anything else, a pre-release suffix such as -rc.1 included, is rejected as an invalid release: the automatic check stays silent, and a manual check reports an error.
  • Not a draft, not a prerelease — releases/latest never returns those, so a prerelease never triggers the prompt (by design: it prompts only for stable updates).
  • Numerically greater than the version users run — the comparison is per segment (major, minor, patch). A suffix on the running version is ignored: a build made five commits after v1.2.0 reports v1.2.0-5-g<sha> and counts as 1.2.0.
  • The release name is free-form — the prompt never reads it: the comparison uses tag_name, and the modal shows the tag.
  • The image must be on GHCR — images carry the version without the v: release v1.2.0 publishes 1.2.0 (full), plus 1.2.0-light and latest (light), see Docker Images and Tags. Before prompting, the frontend asks the backend, through the authenticated endpoint GET /api/v1/system/container-image-status?tag=1.2.0, whether the release's X.Y.Z image is published. The backend performs GHCR's anonymous token handshake, which a browser cannot complete through CORS, then sends a manifest HEAD request for ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:X.Y.Z. A 404 means pending: no prompt yet, and a manual check reports the image as pending. Any other failure is an error, and the check fails closed. The full X.Y.Z image is the pipeline's last push, after X.Y.Z-light and latest: no administrator is prompted while the release run is still building, or when it fails before that push (a failed light build included), and when the prompt does appear, every tag of the release already exists.

See also .github/copilot-instructions.md → "Changelog Rules" for the CHANGELOG.md conventions the in-app changelog modal renders.

docs.title: 🧰 1. Runner, Caches and Setup
docs.text:
The job runs on ubuntu-latest, deliberately left unpinned. It checks out the full history (fetch-depth: 0: mkdocs gh-deploy needs the branches, and the version stamp needs the tags), then sets up Python 3.13, Pipenv and Node.js 24.

Three caches are restored before anything is installed:

Cache Path Key, after the <runner.os>-<RUNNER_IMAGE_OS>- prefix Pipenv virtualenv ~/.local/share/virtualenvs pipenv- and the hash of Pipfile.lock; the restore key falls back to the newest pipenv- entry npm ~/.npm node- and the hash of the package-lock.json files; the restore key falls back to the newest node- entry Playwright browsers ~/.cache/ms-playwright playwright- and the @playwright/test version of frontend/package.json; exact match only

The Pipenv key, for example:

key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.RUNNER_IMAGE_OS }}-pipenv-${{ hashFiles('**/Pipfile.lock') }}

Every key includes RUNNER_IMAGE_OS because ubuntu-latest changes Ubuntu release over time (24.04 → 26.04, see actions/runner-images#14748), while runner.os is Linux on both: keyed on it alone, a virtualenv or a browser build made on one image would be restored on the other. The step «Expose the runner image for cache keys» exports the runner's ImageOS variable (for example ubuntu24) as RUNNER_IMAGE_OS through $GITHUB_ENV, with unknown as fallback: ImageOS is an environment variable of the runner, not part of the expression env context.

The installation then runs:

pipenv install --dev
# «Generate VERSION file for Docker», «Freeze the app version for the frontend builds»
pipenv run ./dev.py install        # pipenv install --dev again, npm ci at the root and in frontend/, Playwright Chromium
# «[CHECK] Checkout after dev.py install» (warning only)
pipenv run ./dev.py front build
# «[CHECK] Checkout after the frontend build» (warning only)

The two steps after pipenv install --dev freeze the version before any step that could write tracked files: the backend's in VERSION, the app's in LF_APP_VERSION. The [CHECK] steps never fail; they name a step that changed the checkout. Version Stamps and a Clean Checkout describes both.

dev.py install installs the root project's tools with npm ci, like the frontend's dependencies: npm ci installs package-lock.json exactly as committed, never rewrites it, and fails when it no longer matches package.json. Commit a change to the root package.json with its updated package-lock.json, as in frontend/.

docs.title: 🧪 2. Documentation Checks, Gallery and Rebuilds
docs.text:
The documentation steps run in this order:

pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs translate-diff --issues-only
pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate --hide-localized
pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs check-links
pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs build                # mkdocs build --strict
# «[CHECK] Checkout after the docs build» (warning only)
pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs gallery --workers 4
# «[CHECK] Checkout after the gallery» (warning only)
pipenv run ./dev.py front build                 # production rebuild, for the images
pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs build                # rebuild, with the screenshots
  • The site is built before the gallery. The gallery's test server serves /mkdocs, and the gallery's build step (next bullet) builds the site only when mkdocs_src/site/ is missing or older than its pages: here it finds the site up to date. The order dates from when that build ran inside the startup window of Playwright's webServer, where building the site once made the gallery time out; the build step now runs before Playwright starts, outside that window.
  • The gallery always runs. There is no screenshot cache, and no input to skip or force the step: every run regenerates the screenshots. dev.py mkdocs gallery populates the test database, prepares the test server with its build step, dev.py server --test --build-only (in the foreground, with the environment it then gives Playwright; a failed build stops the gallery there), runs frontend/e2e/gallery.spec.ts for the desktop and mobile Playwright projects, and writes the PNGs under mkdocs_src/docs/gallery/, where they are gitignored. When the run ends, failed or not, it converts the PNGs to WebP at quality 85, beside them (scripts/gallery_webp.py, Pillow, in parallel on the CPUs): only a PNG with no WebP or newer than it, so a partial run (-f) converts its own shots and a second run does nothing. A PNG that cannot be converted is listed and fails the command, after the others were converted. The WebP is a third of the PNG's weight; Playwright cannot write it, and scripts/visual_review/ reads the PNGs, so the gallery keeps writing PNG. The webServer's dev.py server --test then finds its builds up to date and starts in seconds. --workers 4 matches the 4 vCPUs of the ubuntu-latest runners for public repositories: 8 workers oversubscribed them, and the CPU contention made a different test time out on each run. The step's timeout is 120 minutes.
  • The frontend is rebuilt for production. The gallery's build step rebuilds frontend/build/ in debug mode (no minification, sourcemaps), the kind dev.py server --test serves. The images copy frontend/build/, so dev.py front build runs again. The Dockerfile's frontend stage refuses anything else: scripts/docker/check_frontend_build.sh fails the image build on a debug build, a coverage-instrumented build or any sourcemap. Like the first build, both rebuilds take the app's version from LF_APP_VERSION (see Version Stamps and a Clean Checkout).
  • The site is rebuilt with the screenshots. The first build had none. The site keeps both files of every screenshot, because the images already released and the README read the PNGs from GitHub Pages. The pages ask for the WebP (javascripts/gallery-img-loader.js, which falls back to the PNG, then to GitHub Pages). The full image's docs stage deletes the gallery's PNGs and keeps the WebP; the light image's docs stage deletes every screenshot.
  • Each build checks its own output. Once mkdocs build --strict succeeds, dev.py resolves every relative file URL of the built site (images, video and audio, links to files) from its page's folder, as a browser does, and exits 1 on a broken one, which fails the step. It catches, for example, a raw-HTML image path that a translation copied unchanged from the English: the translated page is built one folder deeper (site/<lang>/...), so the path is one ../ short; translate-validate reports such a copy earlier, as html-asset-depth (see Validation Checks).

The ordering is pinned by ./dev.py test utils release-image-contract (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_release_image_contract.py): a production frontend build and a docs build between the gallery and both image builds, a nightly report that reads every soft-gated step, and a Dockerfile that takes frontend/build/ only through the checked stage. The same test also pins the RUNNER_IMAGE_OS cache keys, the gallery's release gate and its failure-report upload, the release, nightly and manual-from-main tags of Docker Images and Tags, the prerelease rule (no latest, no deploy, no :latest line), the release tag guard (-rc.N for prereleases, plain vX.Y.Z for stable releases), the image-build guards, the light-before-full build order, and the tags the release notes pull, which it checks by running the step's script in bash with a stand-in gh. It also pins the version stamps and the clean checkout: the LF_APP_VERSION export right after VERSION and before every frontend build, vite.config.ts preferring it to git describe (run in node with a stand-in git), the four checkout checks and the outputs of their script, npm ci at the root of dev.py install, and the icon record — the generators redraw a set only when its source's hash or recipe changes, never because of the PNG bytes, and the committed record matches the committed logos.

docs.title: Release gate and nightly tolerance
docs.text:
Six steps carry continue-on-error: ${{ github.ref_name == 'dev' }}:

Step Command (pipenv run ./dev.py …) Check MkDocs translation structure consistency mkdocs translate-diff --issues-only Validate broken MkDocs translation links mkdocs translate-validate --hide-localized Validate cross-boundary links mkdocs check-links Build MkDocs Documentation mkdocs build Generate Screenshots with Playwright mkdocs gallery --workers 4 Rebuild MkDocs Documentation (with the gallery screenshots) mkdocs build
  • On dev, the nightly continues past a failure. The step «Report soft-failed steps (nightly)», which runs on dev only and with always(), lists the failed steps in a "⚠️ Soft-failed steps" section of the job summary and raises a warning annotation. After a failed gallery, the nightly ships the screenshots that succeeded; the documentation loads the missing ones from the public site (mkdocs_src/docs/javascripts/gallery-img-loader.js).
  • On any other run, a published release included, a failure stops the pipeline: no image is pushed, the site is not deployed, and the release notes are not updated; only the artifact steps still run. On a release, github.ref_name is the tag (for example v1.2.0), so the expression is false. The reason: the full image bundles the gallery and a release deploys the documentation site, so a release must not ship missing or broken screenshots. The GitHub release itself is already published at that point, but the in-app update prompt stays silent, because the image tag never reaches GHCR (see Release Tag Convention).

docs.title: 🔢 3. Version Stamps and a Clean Checkout
docs.text:
The backend and the app each compute their version with git describe --tags --always --dirty, which appends -dirty as soon as a tracked file differs from the commit. The job freezes both right after pipenv install --dev, before any step that could write tracked files, and every later step reads the frozen value:

Version Shown in Frozen by Read by Backend GET /api/v1/system/info (app_version, the one field it also answers without a session), Settings → About «Generate VERSION file for Docker», which writes VERSION with get_git_version() (backend/app/utils/runtime/version.py); the next step exports it as LF_APP_VERSION get_git_version(), once per process, takes the first source that gives a version: LF_APP_VERSION when it is set and not blank (frozen_app_version(), backend/app/config/platform.py); git describe where the project root has .git (a folder, or a file in a worktree or a submodule); a VERSION file that is not blank; otherwise unknown. The job's servers read LF_APP_VERSION. The image has no .git/ and does not set the variable, so the Dockerfile copies VERSION App The sidebar, and the changelog modal it opens (APP_VERSION, frontend/src/lib/version.ts) «Freeze the app version for the frontend builds», which runs echo "LF_APP_VERSION=$(cat VERSION)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV" getAppVersion() in frontend/vite.config.ts, at every frontend build: LF_APP_VERSION when it is set and not blank, git describe otherwise

Both read LF_APP_VERSION first, so in the job the backend reports the same frozen version as the frontend builds. Without the variable, as in every local checkout and every install, git describe decides wherever there is .git: a VERSION file left over by an earlier ./dev.py docker build cannot hide newer commits. .env.example lists LF_APP_VERSION commented out, under «App Version»: leave it unset. The version of pyproject.toml and of frontend/package.json (with the two root entries of package-lock.json), 0.0.0 in all of them, is not the app's version: nothing reads it, so no release has to update it.

VERSION alone freezes only the backend's version in the images. Vite compiles the app's version into the bundle, and the job builds the frontend three times, each after steps that may write tracked files: the first dev.py front build, the debug rebuild of the gallery's build step, and the production rebuild for the images. The gallery's server starts its backend after such steps too. Before LF_APP_VERSION, the published 1.1 gallery showed v1.1.0-dirty in the sidebar, and the nightly of 2026-10-12 v1.1.0-1390-g85170bc1f-dirty. Written to $GITHUB_ENV, LF_APP_VERSION reaches every later step of the job, the same job for nightlies, manual runs and releases:

  • The gallery. dev.py mkdocs gallery passes its environment to its build step, dev.py server --test --build-only, and to Playwright, which passes its own to its webServer, dev.py server --test: the build step's debug rebuild (the sidebar of every screenshot) and the webServer's backend (Settings → About) both carry the frozen version.
  • The images. The Dockerfile builds no frontend: both variants copy the production frontend/build/ that the job built with LF_APP_VERSION set, and VERSION for the backend.

Locally LF_APP_VERSION is unset, and every build and server reads git describe. Set on a command, it gives the frontend builds and the servers of that command a chosen version, for example to rehearse a release gallery the way the job builds it:

LF_APP_VERSION=v1.2.0 ./dev.py front build       # production build, as in the job
LF_APP_VERSION=v1.2.0 ./dev.py mkdocs gallery    # its build step rebuilds in debug mode, with the same version
  • It reaches only the builds and servers the command starts. The gallery's build step rebuilds frontend/build/ only when it is missing, older than its sources, or not a debug build, hence the production build first: a debug build already up to date would be reused, with the version it carries.
  • It changes the backend's version too. get_git_version() reads it first, so the server the gallery starts shows it in Settings → About, like the sidebar.
  • It leaves no file behind, only the version compiled into frontend/build/ until its next build. A VERSION file would change neither version: in a checkout get_git_version() reads it only when git describe fails, and the app's version never reads it. ./dev.py docker build is different: it writes get_git_version(), and so the variable, into VERSION, frontend/build/.build-version and the image tags (see Local image builds).

docs.title: Local image builds
docs.text:
./dev.py docker build and ./dev.py docker rebuild freeze the version of a local image too, without the job (all the steps: What ./dev.py docker build Does). _docker_ensure_assets_built() asks get_git_version() once, before any step that could write a tracked file, and gives the answer to both versions of the image:

  • The app. _docker_ensure_frontend_built() rebuilds frontend/build/ in production mode, with LF_APP_VERSION set to the frozen version for that build only, unless _docker_frontend_stale_reason() finds that the bundle already fits: sources not newer than the build, .build-debug saying it is a production build, and frontend/build/.build-version holding the frozen version. It writes .build-version after its build. Every frontend build empties frontend/build/, so the file exists only when the last build was made for an image: any other build is rebuilt once, and so is the bundle of an earlier image after a new commit, even one that touched no frontend file.
  • The backend. VERSION receives the same version at the end, and the Dockerfile copies it.

The sidebar and GET /api/v1/system/info therefore report the same version in a locally built image. The image tags are computed apart: _get_docker_tag() clears get_git_version()'s cache and asks again after the asset steps, so a step that changed a tracked file adds -dirty to the tags, not to the versions inside the image.

docs.title: Checkout checks
docs.text:
Four warning-only steps, «[CHECK] Checkout after dev.py install», «[CHECK] Checkout after the frontend build» (the first front build), «[CHECK] Checkout after the docs build» (the first mkdocs build) and «[CHECK] Checkout after the gallery», each run sh scripts/ci/warn_if_tree_changed.sh "<step>" right after the step they name. The script compares the checkout with its commit through git status --porcelain, and its log reads:

  • Checkout unchanged after <step>.: nothing changed, and no annotation.
  • The git status --porcelain list, then a warning «Checkout changed after », also shown as an annotation on the run's summary page. The warning counts tracked and untracked (??) paths apart. Tracked changes are the ones that make git describe --dirty read -dirty; untracked paths are files a step wrote that Git does not ignore, and do not change the version.
  • A warning «Checkout check failed after »: git status itself failed, and the message carries its error.

    The script always exits 0: the checks diagnose, they do not gate, on nightlies and releases alike. Each compares the checkout with the commit, not with the previous check, so a change stays in every later warning: the first check that warns names the step that made it, and the lists of two consecutive checks show what the steps between them added. Before these checks, the logs of the v1.1.0 release run and of the nightly of 2026-10-12 already showed dev.py install leaving the checkout clean (the git status --short it prints after its npm installs is empty): the checkout changed later, and the known cause is the icons below.

docs.title: Generated icons
docs.text:
dev.py draws two icon sets with Pillow: generate_favicon() writes frontend/static/favicon.png from logo.png, and generate_pwa_icons() the five PWA icons of frontend/static/icons/ from logo_square.png (see PWA → Icon Generation). dev.py front build runs the first, and every docs build runs both through copy_docs_assets(), which then copies them into mkdocs_src/docs/static/. All these PNGs are tracked, and Pillow does not guarantee the same bytes for the same image on every platform: regenerated on the runner, unchanged icons became modified files.

A set is therefore regenerated only when one of its outputs is missing, or when frontend/generated-icons.json does not record its current source and recipe. That file, committed with the icons, holds one entry per set, favicon and pwa-icons, with the source's path and sha256 and the recipe number, FAVICON_RECIPE or PWA_ICONS_RECIPE in dev.py. A regeneration rewrites the set's entry; otherwise the set is left untouched, and the log says so (favicon.png is up to date (logo.png unchanged)). The decision reads the source's hash, never the outputs' bytes, which can differ from one platform to another.

To Do Change a logo Replace frontend/static/logo.png or logo_square.png and run ./dev.py mkdocs build, which regenerates the set, rewrites its entry and copies the icons into mkdocs_src/docs/static/. Commit the changed files under both static/ folders together with frontend/generated-icons.json: without the new entry, every other checkout, the runner's included, would regenerate the set again Change what a function draws Bump its recipe number, FAVICON_RECIPE or PWA_ICONS_RECIPE: without the bump the record still matches, and the change never reaches the icons Force a regeneration Delete the set's entry from frontend/generated-icons.json (or the whole file), or one of its outputs, then build again

docs.title: 🐳 4. Docker Images and Tags
docs.text:
pipenv requirements > requirements.txt generates the requirements the Dockerfile installs. The job then sets up QEMU and Buildx, and logs in to GHCR with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN. Two docker/metadata-action steps compute the tags, and two docker/build-push-action steps build ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio from the repository root and push it, sharing the GitHub Actions layer cache (type=gha, mode=max). The light variant is built and pushed first:

  1. Light variant — the build with DOCS_VARIANT=light: the Dockerfile's docs-light stage deletes the documentation images before they reach the final image.
  2. Full variant — the default Dockerfile build, with the documentation screenshots as WebP (the docs-full stage deletes the PNGs).

The order serves the in-app update prompt, which checks the plain X.Y.Z tag, the full variant's (see Release Tag Convention). Pushed last, that tag appears only once X.Y.Z-light and latest exist. If the light build fails, the full build does not run (an if: without a status function implies success()), so X.Y.Z is never pushed and no one is prompted.

Each build runs only when its own metadata step yields a tag: if: steps.meta-light.outputs.tags != '' for the light build, if: steps.meta.outputs.tags != '' for the full one. A push without a tag can only fail (buildx: tag is needed when pushing to registry), so a variant with nothing to publish is skipped instead.

Neither build sets platforms, so each image is built for the runner's platform (linux/amd64).

What the two variants contain, and which tag users should pick, is specified for users in Installation → Image Variants. The tags the two metadata steps compute:

Run Light variant (pushed first) Full variant (pushed last) Stable release vX.Y.Z published X.Y.Z-light, latest X.Y.Z Prerelease vX.Y.Z-rc.N published, e.g. v1.2.0-rc.1 X.Y.Z-rc.N-light X.Y.Z-rc.N Push to dev, or manual run from dev nightly-light nightly Manual run from main latest none: build skipped Manual run from any other branch none: build skipped none: build skipped
  • No v in image tags. The version tags are docker/metadata-action's {{version}}: release v1.2.0 publishes 1.2.0, not v1.2.0. Only the GitHub release tag has the v, and the in-app update prompt accepts both forms.

  • latest is the light variant, moved only by a stable release or a manual run from main. docker/metadata-action adds latest on its own whenever a type=semver tag matches a stable version, if the flavor is latest=auto. The full-variant step sets flavor: latest=false. The light step uses auto only for a release that is not a GitHub prerelease, and false for every other run; its raw latest tag is enabled only on main. Hence:

    • a GitHub prerelease publishes only its own version tags, X.Y.Z-rc.N and X.Y.Z-rc.N-light: the release tag guard lets no other tag through, and the false flavor would keep latest in place on any tag;
    • a stable release reaches these steps only on a plain vX.Y.Z tag, which the same guard enforces: on a tag such as v1.3.0-rc.1, latest would stay in place, since under auto metadata-action skips semver pre-releases;
    • the flavor is never latest=true, which would add latest to every raw tag as well, nightly-light included.

    latest-light is no longer published: latest itself is the light variant.

# Extract Docker Metadata (Version): full variant
flavor: |
  latest=false
tags: |
  type=semver,pattern={{version}}
  type=raw,value=nightly,enable=${{ github.ref_name == 'dev' }}

# Extract Docker Metadata (Light Variant)
flavor: |
  latest=${{ (github.event_name == 'release' && !github.event.release.prerelease) && 'auto' || 'false' }}
tags: |
  type=semver,pattern={{version}},suffix=-light
  type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref_name == 'main' }}
  type=raw,value=nightly-light,enable=${{ github.ref_name == 'dev' }}

Why the full variant turns latest off

Before this setting, both variants pushed latest, and the light one won only because it was pushed second. With latest=false on the full variant, latest no longer depends on the push order, which now puts the light variant first.

docs.title: 🌍 5. Documentation Deployment
docs.text:
if: github.ref_name == 'main' || (github.event_name == 'release' && !github.event.release.prerelease)
run: pipenv run ./dev.py mkdocs deploy

dev.py mkdocs deploy copies the documentation assets and runs mkdocs gh-deploy --force -f mkdocs_src/mkdocs.yml, which builds the site again and force-pushes it to the gh-pages branch as github-actions[bot] (configured by the «Setup Git User» step). The step comes after the image builds. Its condition keeps both dev changes and GitHub prereleases off the public site: only a stable release or a manual run from main deploys it. A manual run from main reaches the step after pushing only the light latest image, the full build being skipped.

docs.title: 🗂️ 6. Artifacts
docs.text:
Two steps archive the gallery's output:

Artifact Content Kept Uploaded playwright-screenshots The gallery PNGs, mkdocs_src/docs/gallery/**/*.png (not the WebP copies, nor the gallery's Markdown pages) 1 day On every run that is not cancelled, a failed one included playwright-gallery-report frontend/playwright-report/ (the HTML report) and frontend/test-results/ 3 days Only when the gallery step failed, on dev too, where that failure is soft

Both steps run under !cancelled(), so a failed step earlier in the job does not skip them: the gallery fails a release, and a failed run is when the screenshots and the report are most useful. Both also set if-no-files-found: ignore. The report step adds steps.gallery.outcome == 'failure', which also holds on dev, where continue-on-error keeps the job going. On CI, Playwright retries a failed test twice and records a trace and a video on the first retry, plus a screenshot on failure: the report carries them. No later run restores either artifact: they are for inspection.

docs.title: 📝 7. Release Notes
docs.text:
On a release (github.event.release.tag_name is set), the last step appends a "📦 Docker Installation" section to the release notes. gh release edit has no option to append, so the step reads the current notes and writes them back with the section added:

TAG_NAME="${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}"
IMAGE_TAG="${TAG_NAME#v}"   # image tags have no leading "v"
# DOCKER_CMD: the "📦 Docker Installation" section, built with printf from IMAGE_TAG;
# the :latest line only when PRERELEASE (github.event.release.prerelease) is not "true"
CURRENT_NOTES=$(gh release view "$TAG_NAME" --json body -q .body)
gh release edit "$TAG_NAME" --notes "${CURRENT_NOTES}${DOCKER_CMD}"

For the stable release v1.2.0, the appended commands are:

# Latest release, light variant (documentation screenshots load from the online docs site)
docker pull ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:latest

# This release, full variant (documentation fully offline)
docker pull ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:1.2.0

# This release, light variant
docker pull ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:1.2.0-light

A prerelease's section has only the last two commands, with its own version: a prerelease does not move latest, so its notes have no :latest line.

docs.title: 🌐 Translation Pipeline
docs.text: Automated translation of LibreFolio MkDocs documentation into multiple languages using Aphra — an LLM-based agentic translation workflow. Supports both cloud (OpenRouter) and local (Ollama) LLM backends.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The pipeline translates *.en.md source files into it, fr, es. The translated files (*.it.md, *.fr.md, *.es.md) are picked up by mkdocs-static-i18n (suffix strategy) to build a multilingual documentation site.

Scope Files Translated? User Manual 94 files ✅ Admin Manual 8 files ✅ Financial Theory 99 files (LaTeX) ✅ Gallery 3 files ✅ Root and Community (Home, FAQ, Contribute, Credits) 4 files ✅ Developer Manual 114 files ❌ EN-only

Total: 208 source files → 624 translated files (3 languages)

Besides the documentation, the pipeline translates the repository's CHANGELOG.md, which the app's changelog modal shows, into CHANGELOG.it.md, CHANGELOG.fr.md and CHANGELOG.es.md beside it: see The CHANGELOG.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
mkdocs_src/aphra-pipeline/
├── .env                    # API key + model config (gitignored)
├── .env.example            # Template for contributors
├── .gitignore              # Ignores .env, config.toml, Python caches
├── .translate-hashes.json  # Translation cache, tracked in git (see Caching)
├── README.md               # Quick-start guide
├── changelog.py            # CHANGELOG.md units, pieces and release policy (see The CHANGELOG)
├── code_blocks.py          # Fenced-block pairing + code indentation restore (shared helper)
├── glossaries/             # glossary.json: term mappings per language (Critique + Refine)
├── page_anchors.py         # Anchor ids of a page's MkDocs render (anchor-missing, check-links)
├── prompts/short_article/  # Aphra prompt overrides (see 7. Prompt overrides)
├── translate_docs.py       # Orchestration script (integrated with dev.py)
└── validate_translations.py # translate-validate checks (integrated with dev.py)

The two scripts integrate with dev.py via their register_subparser() (translate_docs.py for the first five, validate_translations.py for translate-validate), adding:

  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate — translate docs via Aphra (LLM agent)
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-check — check translation pipeline setup
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-diff — structural diff: compare EN vs translated files
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-stamp — mark file(s) as already translated in the cache (no LLM call)
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-inspect — inspect saved translation artifacts (analysis, critique, diff)
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate — validate translated docs (structural cross-check)

docs.title: Workflow: Shared Analysis
docs.text:
The key optimization over vanilla Aphra: Step 1 (Analyze) runs once per source file and its result is shared across all target languages. This saves ~25% of LLM calls when translating to 3 languages.

flowchart TB
    subgraph per_file["📄 Per Source File"]
        source["source.en.md"]
        analyze["🧠 Step 1: Analyze<br/><i>Analyzer model (27B)</i><br/>Identify key terms, structure"]
        source --> analyze
    end

    subgraph per_lang["🌐 Per Target Language"]
        direction TB
        translate["✍️ Step 3: Translate<br/><i>Writer model (9B)</i><br/>Initial full translation"]
        critique["🔎 Step 4: Critique<br/><i>Analyzer model (27B)</i><br/>Compare original vs translation"]
        refine["✨ Step 5: Refine<br/><i>Writer model (9B)</i><br/>Final translation with fixes"]
        translate --> critique --> refine
    end

    analyze -->|"shared analysis"| per_lang

    refine --> clean["🧹 Post-process<br/>Strip [N] glossary, tags<br/>Restore code indentation"]
    clean --> output["source.it.md"]

    style per_file fill:#e8f4fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2196f3
    style per_lang fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#ff9800
    style analyze fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style critique fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style translate fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17
    style refine fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17

Step 2 (Search) skipped by default

Aphra's optional web search step adds cost ($4/1000 queries via OpenRouter :online plugin) and latency. It's disabled by default for technical documentation where terms are well-known.

docs.title: Multi-language flow
docs.text:
When translating to 3 languages, the full flow for one file is:

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Source File
    participant A as 🧠 Analyzer (27B)
    participant W as ✍️ Writer (9B)

    S->>A: Analyze (ONCE)
    Note over A: Key terms, structure

    rect rgb(255, 243, 224)
        Note over W: → Italian
        A->>W: Translate (it)
        W->>A: Critique (it)
        A->>W: Refine (it)
        W-->>S: ✅ source.it.md
    end

    rect rgb(232, 245, 233)
        Note over W: → French
        A->>W: Translate (fr)
        W->>A: Critique (fr)
        A->>W: Refine (fr)
        W-->>S: ✅ source.fr.md
    end

    rect rgb(243, 229, 245)
        Note over W: → Spanish
        A->>W: Translate (es)
        W->>A: Critique (es)
        A->>W: Refine (es)
        W-->>S: ✅ source.es.md
    end

Savings: 1 Analyze call instead of 3 = −67% analyze calls across 3 languages.

docs.title: Model Roles
docs.text:
The pipeline splits LLM work into two categories, allowing different models for different tasks:

Category Steps Env Variable Recommended Reasoning Analyze + Critique APHRA_ANALYZER Larger model (27B) Generation Translate + Refine APHRA_MODEL / APHRA_WRITER Faster model (9B) 
graph LR
    subgraph reasoning["🧠 Reasoning (27B)"]
        A["Step 1: Analyze"]
        C["Step 4: Critique"]
    end
    subgraph generation["✍️ Generation (9B)"]
        T["Step 3: Translate"]
        R["Step 5: Refine"]
    end

    A -->|"key terms"| T
    T -->|"draft"| C
    C -->|"feedback"| R

    style reasoning fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style generation fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17

docs.title: Priority hierarchy
docs.text:
APHRA_ANALYZER  → defaults to APHRA_WRITER → APHRA_MODEL → hardcoded default
APHRA_WRITER    → defaults to APHRA_MODEL → hardcoded default
APHRA_CRITIQUER → defaults to APHRA_ANALYZER (reasoning task)
APHRA_SEARCHER  → defaults to APHRA_MODEL → hardcoded default

docs.title: How We Customized Aphra
docs.text: Aphra is used as a library, not via its CLI. We bypass aphra.translate() to gain control over several aspects:

docs.title: 1. Config path injection
docs.text:
Aphra's translate() passes config.toml to LLMModelClient (API key) but not to workflow.load_config(). Without our fix, the workflow loads its internal default.toml with expensive defaults (Claude Sonnet 4 + Perplexity Sonar).

Fix: Call workflow.load_config(global_config_path=config_path) directly.

docs.title: 2. Base URL override (Ollama support)
docs.text: LLMModelClient.__init__ hardcodes base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1". We patch model_client.client.base_url after construction to point to Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

docs.title: 3. Shared analysis across languages
docs.text: Vanilla Aphra analyzes the source text once per translation call. We extract the Analyze step and reuse its result across all target languages for the same file.

docs.title: 4. Per-step model swapping
docs.text:
We modify workflow_config['writer'] at runtime between steps:

  • Before Analyze: set to models['analyzer'] (27B reasoning)
  • Before Translate/Refine: set to models['writer'] (9B generation)
  • Critique uses models['critiquer'] (defaults to analyzer)

docs.title: 5. Web search bypass
docs.text: Step 2 (Search) uses OpenRouter's :online plugin which costs $4/1000 results. We skip it entirely for technical docs via APHRA_WEB_SEARCH=false.

docs.title: 6. Post-processing cleanup
docs.text:
Aphra's output contains artifacts we strip automatically:

  • <translation> / </translation> wrapper tags
  • Inline glossary markers [N] (preserving markdown links)
  • Glossary definition blocks at the end of the file
  • Translator notes the LLM adds on its own (a trailing "Translator's Notes" section, [^N] footnotes)

Removing an inline marker leaves a double space behind. The cleanup collapses runs of two or more spaces to one only between non-space characters and only outside fenced code blocks: leading indentation (nested lists, admonition and content-tab bodies), Markdown hard breaks (two trailing spaces) and every line of a code block stay as they are. An earlier version collapsed every run of spaces in the whole document, which flattened code indentation to 0–1 space (a docker-compose example in the IT/FR/ES admin manual was no longer a valid compose file), pushed nested fences out of their list items and content tabs (numbered lists split, tabs rendered empty) and removed hard breaks. The step that re-pads !!! admonition bodies from 1 to 4 spaces stays as a safety net.

The file written by _translate_one_lang() is the output of _finalize_translation(): _clean_translation() followed by restore_code_indent(), which gives every translated code block the indentation of its English block back (see below). When something was restored, the run log shows 🧹 Restored the source indentation on N code line(s).

docs.title: Code block indentation
docs.text:
Translation never has a reason to move code, so the English indentation of every fenced block is the reference. The helpers live in mkdocs_src/aphra-pipeline/code_blocks.py (standard library only) and are shared by the pipeline and the validator. They see backtick and tilde fences at any indentation (list items, content tabs, admonitions):

  • pair_blocks() pairs each translated block with its English block by content: the same code pairs even when its #/// comments or <placeholders> are translated, so a block added or missing on one side does not shift the others. Blocks left over in a stretch that differs (e.g. Mermaid with translated labels) pair in order when language and line count match.
  • restore_code_indent() gives each paired block the English leading whitespace back, line by line, fences included. A line whose tokens equal the English line becomes the English line; any other line keeps its translated text (comments, labels) behind the English indentation, and gets the English gap before an inline comment back when its code part is identical. Blank lines, prose, unpaired blocks, blocks with a different line count and unclosed fences are left alone.
  • code_indent_issues() lists the translated lines whose indentation still differs from the English block.

./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate re-checks every translation with the code-block-indent check (❌ ERROR, non-zero exit). It pairs blocks the same way and reports each drifted block once: first drifted line, line range of the translated block, how many of its lines are off, and the relative indentation levels of the English block versus the translation. The positional code-block-modified notice (🌐 LOCALIZED) attributes a changed code line to translated comments only: indentation drift is never treated as an intentional localization.

In the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml, step Validate broken MkDocs translation links) the command runs with --hide-localized. The step is continue-on-error only on dev, where the nightly run lists it as a soft failure in the job summary; on any other run, a published release included, an ERROR fails the pipeline.

Tests: ./dev.py test utils translation-code-blocks (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_translation_code_blocks.py). Besides the unit cases, a corpus guard checks that every up-to-date translation (English MD5 equal to the cached one and language in langs_done, the rule translate uses to skip a page) keeps the English code indentation.

docs.title: 💬 7. Prompt overrides
docs.text:
The generated config.toml points Aphra's prompts_dir at mkdocs_src/aphra-pipeline/prompts/short_article/. A file there named like an Aphra prompt replaces it (step1_system.txt and the system and user prompts of steps 3, 4 and 5), and step1_user_append.txt is added after Aphra's own Step 1 user prompt.

For HTML, the three prompts that write or judge the translation share one rule:

  • tags, attribute names and technical attribute values (src, href, class, id, style, and data-* other than data-title, such as data-category or data-name) are copied character for character;
  • the human-readable values of alt, title, aria-label and data-title (the carousel caption) are prose: Translate (step3_user.txt) and Refine (step5_user.txt) translate them, keeping any HTML inside a data-title unchanged, and Critique (step4_user.txt) checks that they were not left in English.

The earlier wording asked to copy every HTML attribute, which left image descriptions in English. The text-untranslated check (Validation Checks) reports the values of three words or more still in English.

docs.title: Local mode (Ollama)
docs.text:
APHRA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
APHRA_ANALYZER=kwangsuklee/Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled-GGUF
APHRA_MODEL=kwangsuklee/Qwen3.5-9B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled-GGUF
APHRA_WEB_SEARCH=false

Install Ollama and pull models:

brew install ollama   # macOS
ollama pull kwangsuklee/Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled-GGUF
ollama pull kwangsuklee/Qwen3.5-9B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled-GGUF

docs.title: Cloud mode (OpenRouter)
docs.text:
# APHRA_BASE_URL=        ← commented out = cloud mode
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-your-key-here
APHRA_MODEL=google/gemini-2.5-flash

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Check setup
./dev.py mkdocs translate-check

# Dry run (shows plan + estimated tokens)
./dev.py mkdocs translate --dry-run

# Translate specific files
./dev.py mkdocs translate --file faq.en.md --lang it

# Translate entire folder (glob)
./dev.py mkdocs translate --file 'user/**/*.en.md' --lang it fr es

# Translate only the repository CHANGELOG (see The CHANGELOG)
./dev.py mkdocs translate --file CHANGELOG.md

# Translate all (skips cached)
./dev.py mkdocs translate

docs.title: 🦋 Cloud mode — Doubleword.ai (Autobatcher / Flex Queue)
docs.text:
Doubleword.ai provides an OpenAI-compatible API with a flex queue pricing model: requests are batched and processed at reduced rates during off-peak periods, making it significantly cheaper than synchronous cloud inference.

Configure .env:

APHRA_BASE_URL=https://api.doubleword.ai/v1
DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY=dw-your-key-here
APHRA_MODEL=google/gemma-4-31B-it

# Optional: lower from 4h default if you prefer faster failure + retry
# DOUBLEWORD_QUEUE_TIMEOUT=14400

Run with parallel language branches for maximum throughput:

./dev.py mkdocs translate --workers 3

Model recommendation

google/gemma-4-31B-it is the recommended model for Doubleword — it balances translation quality and cost. Because Doubleword uses flex pricing, you can use a single model for all 4 roles without worrying about per-step cost differences.

docs.title: How queue scheduling works with the 4-step pipeline
docs.text:
Aphra's workflow makes one LLM call per step. Each call to DoublewordClient.call_model() becomes one independent request submitted to Doubleword's flex queue via autobatcher.

For a single file translated into 3 languages, the pipeline submits 10 requests total:

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph LR
    A1["🧠 Step 1\nAnalyze\n× 1"] --> T1["✍️ Step 3\nTranslate IT\n× 1"]
    A1 --> T2["✍️ Step 3\nTranslate FR\n× 1"]
    A1 --> T3["✍️ Step 3\nTranslate ES\n× 1"]

    T1 --> C1["🔎 Step 4\nCritique IT\n× 1"]
    T2 --> C2["🔎 Step 4\nCritique FR\n× 1"]
    T3 --> C3["🔎 Step 4\nCritique ES\n× 1"]

    C1 --> R1["✨ Step 5\nRefine IT\n× 1"]
    C2 --> R2["✨ Step 5\nRefine FR\n× 1"]
    C3 --> R3["✨ Step 5\nRefine ES\n× 1"]

    style A1 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style T1 fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17
    style T2 fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17
    style T3 fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17
    style C1 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style C2 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style C3 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style R1 fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17
    style R2 fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17
    style R3 fill:#fff8e1,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#f57f17

Greedy parallel execution with --workers

Use --workers 3 to translate IT, FR, ES in parallel via independent threads. Each language branch advances to its next step as soon as it finishes the current one — without waiting for the other languages:

Thread IT: [Translate]──→[Critique]──→[Refine]     ← finishes first
Thread FR:    [Translate]────→[Critique]──→[Refine]
Thread ES:       [Translate]──────→[Critique]──→[Refine]

Each step is a new, independent conversation — Doubleword has no context window continuity between steps. This is by design: Aphra's prompts are self-contained and include all necessary context (source text, analysis, prior translation) in each individual request.

docs.title: Technical: sync shim over async autobatcher (thread-safe)
docs.text:
Aphra's call_model() interface is fully synchronous. autobatcher.AsyncOpenAI is async. DoublewordClient bridges both while remaining thread-safe for --workers:

# In translate_docs.py — DoublewordClient.call_model()
# A new AsyncOpenAI client is created per call so each thread
# gets its own event loop + client (httpx.AsyncClient is not
# safe to share across asyncio.run() boundaries).
async def _call() -> str:
    client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url)  # per-call
    response = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model=writer_model,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content or ""

# asyncio.wait_for enforces DOUBLEWORD_QUEUE_TIMEOUT (default 4h)
result = asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(_call(), timeout=timeout_s))

asyncio.run() creates a fresh event loop per call, which is safe in Python 3.10+. The autobatcher library handles queue submission and polling transparently.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: mkdocs_src/aphra-pipeline/.translate-hashes.json (tracked in git) records which languages of each English page are up to date, and for which version of the English. Only the English side is hashed: translated files never enter the decision, so a manual repair of a translation (a whitespace-only fix, for example) neither triggers a re-translation nor needs a stamp.

docs.title: 🗃️ Entries and the skip rule
docs.text:
One entry per English page, keyed by its path under mkdocs_src/docs/ (for example user/assets/create-edit.en.md):

Field Content md5 MD5 of the English version the languages in langs_done were translated or stamped from langs_done The languages up to date for that version langs.<lang> The language's record: translated_at with the run's models, critique, structural_diff, structural_issues and elapsed_s after a translation (plus final_structural_diff and final_structural_issues when the written file has structural issues); stamped_at and stamped_by after a stamp; failed, failed_at, failure_reason and failed_models after a failure last_translated Time of the last successful translation; a stamp that creates the entry sets it to the stamp time analysis, analysis_model The Step 1 (Analyze) output shared by the languages, and the model that wrote it

translate plans each page and language for which _needs_translation() holds: a language is skipped only when the English MD5 equals the entry's md5 and the language is in langs_done. The records under langs are history: the skip rule reads only those two fields. Use --force to ignore the cache and re-translate every page and language in scope (--file, --lang).

docs.title: 🔄 Transitions
docs.text:
Every write to an entry goes through one of four functions of translate_docs.py, so a language counts as done only for the English text it was translated or stamped from. Before them, an analysis moved md5 to the new English and kept langs_done, so a language that then failed, or was never reached, stayed done and its stale translation was never offered again.

Event Function Effect on the entry The analysis of the page succeeds (a failed one writes nothing) _cache_mark_analyzed() Sets md5 to the analyzed version, with analysis and analysis_model. A changed md5 empties langs_done, the same md5 keeps it. The langs records stay: they still describe the files on disk A language succeeds _cache_mark_translated() Adds the language to langs_done, sets last_translated and replaces the language's record with a fresh one (translated_at, models, …), which drops any failure or stamp fields A language fails _cache_mark_failed() Never marks the language done. Adds failed, failed_at, failure_reason and failed_models to its record and keeps its last translated_at: a translation file is written only on success, so the old file is left as it was ./dev.py mkdocs translate-stamp _cache_stamp() Moves md5 to the current English and adds the stamped languages to langs_done. The other languages stay done only if md5 did not change; otherwise the command lists them as pending again. Records stamped_at and stamped_by and clears the failure fields of the stamped languages

A failed --force retry of an up-to-date page leaves the language done, since its file still translates that version. translate-stamp skips an entry already current for the stamped languages (Already stamped, skipping), so it does not clear that failure record; the next successful translation does.

The MD5 recorded is the one of the text translated: _read_source() reads the English page once and returns its text with the MD5 of the same bytes, and the analysis records that MD5. An English edit saved after that read, while the analysis or the translation steps run (on the Doubleword flex queue a step can wait hours), is therefore translated by the next run instead of being recorded as done.

So after a failure, an interruption or a --lang subset, the next run, and translate --dry-run, which prints the same plan, offer exactly the page and language pairs not yet done for the current English.

Tests: ./dev.py test utils translation-cache (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_translation_cache.py), next to translation-code-blocks (Code block indentation). It drives the real run_translate and run_stamp, on the parallel (--workers 3) and the sequential path, over a docs tree and a cache in a temporary directory with the LLM calls faked, and checks _needs_translation() and the four transitions directly.

docs.title: 📜 The CHANGELOG
docs.text:
The pipeline also translates the repository's CHANGELOG.md, the file the app's changelog modal renders. The English file, at the repository root, is written by the release coordinator only; the pipeline writes CHANGELOG.it.md, CHANGELOG.fr.md and CHANGELOG.es.md beside it. The rules are pure functions (no LLM, no cache writes) in mkdocs_src/aphra-pipeline/changelog.py, shared by translate_docs.py and validate_translations.py; both read the file's path from DOCS_DIR at call time (_changelog_source()), so a test that points DOCS_DIR at a temporary tree never sees the repository's CHANGELOG.

  • Chapter lines are copied. A translation holds the translated preamble, then the chapters in the English order, each opened by its English ## [x.y.z] - date line, byte for byte (assemble()). The app splits a changelog at these lines and reads each chapter by the version between the brackets (parseChangelog() in frontend/src/lib/features/changelog/changelog.ts, whose foldable sections are the ### and #### headings). The French chapters are shown with French spacing, applied when the app loads CHANGELOG.fr.md (French Typography).
  • A chapter not translated yet is absent, never an English copy: for that version, the app shows the English chapter.
  • Structure never reaches the model. The chapter line and the --- rule that closes a unit are copied from the English.

docs.title: ✂️ Units, pieces and keys
docs.text:
The preamble (the text before the first chapter line) and each chapter are units. A unit of up to PIECE_THRESHOLD (30,000) characters is one piece, keyed CHANGELOG.md#<version> (CHANGELOG.md#preamble for the preamble). A longer unit is cut at its ### and #### lines, outside fenced code (cut_parts()):

  • the intro, before the first heading, is a piece of its own;
  • a part that is only its heading joins the part that follows: ### 🐛 Fixed, directly followed by #### 🔒 Security, opens the fixed/security piece;
  • each piece is keyed by its headings' words (part_ids()), the ### in force and then its ####, as in CHANGELOG.md#1.2.0/fixed/documentation; the intro is intro, and a repeated key gets -2, -3.

An added #### therefore shifts no other key, and a line added under a heading changes only the piece that holds it. On 12 October 2026, [1.2.0] (74,510 characters) is cut into 21 pieces: intro, added, thirteen fixed/…, changed, four changed/… and breaking-changes; the preamble, [1.1.0] (26,120 characters), [1.0.1] and [1.0.0] are one piece each. A chapter whose length crosses the threshold, either way, gets new keys and is translated again as a whole, once.

docs.title: 🔑 Cache entries
docs.text:
• Each piece has its own entry in .translate-hashes.json, keyed by the piece key, with the fields and the four transitions of a page (Caching); its md5 is the MD5 of the piece's English text.
  • One field is added, langs.<lang>.index: the piece's position (from 0) in the translated chapter when that chapter was last written or stamped. A run cuts the translated chapter by the same rule and pairs its parts with the keys through these indexes (locate()), or by position before any index exists, so it finds each piece's translated part even after pieces were added, removed or moved in the English. When the number of parts does not match, the whole chapter is translated again.
  • The entry of a piece gone from the English is dropped by a translate run (_changelog_prune()) once no language records an index for it any more.

docs.title: ⌨️ Commands
docs.text:
• ./dev.py mkdocs translate with no --file translates the nav pages, then the CHANGELOG (run_translate()); --file CHANGELOG.md alone translates only the CHANGELOG. A piece goes to the model when it is not done for its current text (_needs_translation(): new, changed, or not done in that language) or when its translated part cannot be found in the file; --force, --lang and --dry-run work as for a page. Each piece goes through the page steps (one Analyze, then Translate, Critique and Refine per language) from a temporary piece-NNN.en.md, and --workers N translates N pieces at a time.
  • The files are written at the end of the run, once every piece has been tried: an interrupted run writes none, and the next one translates the same pieces again. A chapter is rewritten only when every piece of it has a translation, new or found in the file; otherwise it stays as it was (absent, if it was), and its pieces translated in that run are not recorded as done: the next run offers them again.
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-stamp --file CHANGELOG.md stamps the CHANGELOG; never by default, since without --file the command stamps the pages only. In each language, every chapter present whose translated parts, cut by the same rule, match the English pieces in number has each piece stamped at its current MD5, with its index; a chapter whose parts differ in number is named (N translated parts for M pieces, not stamped) and left as it is, and the command exits 1.
  • ./dev.py mkdocs translate-diff and ./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate check the CHANGELOG with no --file, as the release workflow runs them, or when --file names CHANGELOG.md (see The open chapter). ./dev.py mkdocs translate-inspect --file CHANGELOG.md shows the pieces' analyses and critiques.

docs.title: 🚦 The open chapter
docs.text:
released() names the units whose translation must be complete: the preamble, every chapter but the newest (the first in the file), and the newest once its tag, v<version> or <version> (the two forms the release workflow's tag guard accepts), exists in the repository or is the ref of the CI run (GITHUB_REF is refs/tags/v1.2.0 on the release run of 1.2.0). Until then the newest chapter is the open one, still being written; a release candidate's tag (v1.2.0-rc.1) leaves it open. An empty newest chapter still counts as the newest: a fresh ## [1.3.0] line with nothing under it yet (its closing --- aside) makes the chapter below it, [1.2.0], released, for translate-validate and translate-diff alike; the empty chapter has no piece to translate or check.

Finding Released chapter Open chapter changelog-missing: the file, or the chapter, is not translated yet ❌ ERROR ℹ️ INFO changelog-stale: pieces changed since their translation (from the cache), named ❌ ERROR ℹ️ INFO changelog-chapter: the chapter line differs from the English one ❌ ERROR ℹ️ INFO The page checks (Validation Checks) on each chapter present, through validate_text() As for a page ERROR and WARN become ℹ️ INFO translate-diff: a chapter's structural anomalies, a missing chapter Counted (exit 1) Printed as ℹ️, not counted changelog-chapter: a line that is no English chapter, a chapter written twice, chapters out of the English order ❌ ERROR ❌ ERROR

The open chapter's findings carry (open chapter) (_open()). Both commands run in the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml), continue-on-error only on dev (Release gate and nightly tolerance): a translation of the open chapter that is incomplete or behind the English fails no check before the release, while the release run, on its tag, fails on a missing, stale or wrong chapter, the newest included.

docs.title: ➕ Adding a line to a chapter
docs.text:
When the release coordinator adds a line to CHANGELOG.md, only the piece that holds it changes: ./dev.py mkdocs translate --dry-run --file CHANGELOG.md lists it, once per language. Then either:

  1. Translate it: ./dev.py mkdocs translate --file CHANGELOG.md sends only that piece to the model and rewrites the three files, the other pieces as they were; or
  2. Port it by hand into CHANGELOG.it.md, CHANGELOG.fr.md and CHANGELOG.es.md, at the same place and with the same ### and #### lines as the English, then run ./dev.py mkdocs translate-stamp --file CHANGELOG.md.

./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate --file CHANGELOG.md then reports no changelog-stale. A fix inside a translated chapter that keeps its ### and #### lines needs no stamp: as for a page, only the English is hashed.

The stamp covers every chapter present

translate-stamp --file CHANGELOG.md stamps each piece not yet done of every chapter present in each CHANGELOG.<lang>.md, in every language unless --lang narrows it, not only the piece you ported. Port the line into the three files, or stamp only the languages ported, and preview with --dry-run: it must name only the pieces you ported. A wrong stamp records a stale translation as done, and changelog-stale no longer reports it until its English piece changes again.

docs.title: 🔎 Validation Checks
docs.text:
./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate (validate_translations.py) compares each translation with its English page, for every target language, and exits non-zero on any ❌ ERROR, which fails the release workflow outside dev (see Code block indentation). Among its checks (code-block-indent is described above, admonition-empty-line under Prettier Compatibility), four catch what a translation can break while the structure stays intact:

  • text-untranslated (⚠️ WARN): an alt, title, aria-label or data-title value (in double quotes), or the alt text of a Markdown image, of at least three words (two letters or more each) that is identical to one of the English page's values, so left in English. Code is ignored, and the name "Buy Me a Coffee" is allowed. The html-attrs check skips these attributes, whose translation is expected; this one checks that it happened.
  • anchor-missing (❌ ERROR): a Markdown link to page.md#anchor or #anchor in a translation (code ignored) must land on an anchor of the page it opens: the translated target page.<lang>.md, or the English page when no translation exists. A page's anchors are the ids of its own MkDocs render with the site configuration (page_anchors.py), exactly the ids mkdocs build --strict checks a link against: heading ids (an explicit {: #id } replaces the text slug), raw-HTML ids and <a name>; the front matter is not rendered. The strict build stops at the first language with a warning, so it surfaces these links one language at a time; this check reports every language in one pass.
  • inline-code-missing (⚠️ WARN): every inline code span of the English must appear verbatim in the translation, as many times; digit grouping is ignored, so 1,000.50 matches 1.000,50, but the message names a missing span as the English writes it. Identifiers, enum values and parameters are never translated.
  • html-asset-depth (❌ ERROR): a relative file path in raw HTML (src, srcset, poster, an href to a file rather than a page) that the translation copied unchanged from the English page; code is ignored. A translated page is built one folder deeper, under site/<lang>/, which holds only HTML pages and no other file; MkDocs rewrites the paths of Markdown images and links, not those of raw HTML, so the English path is one ../ short. The message gives the translation's line and the path to write, ../ followed by the English path. Whether a corrected path resolves is left to ./dev.py mkdocs build, which afterwards resolves every relative file URL of the built site (images, video and audio, links to files) and exits 1 on a broken one.

docs.title: 🧬 Equivalence checks
docs.text:
A page can keep its headings, links and fences and still say something else in another language. These checks (page_equivalence.py, standard library only, wired into ALL_CHECKS and into the structural diff) compare what a reader needs to find. All are ❌ ERRORs; each language is compared with the English page, so when a page is translated by hand from another language (the Italian admin guide became the source of the English one in E9E) the same tools prove the four languages equivalent: English equal to Italian, and French and Spanish equal to English.

Check What must be the same mermaid-count, mermaid-structure Number of diagrams; per diagram the skeleton: front matter, node ids and shapes, arrows, subgraph ids, style / classDef / class lines, sequence participants and message directions. Labels, messages, notes and titles are blanked before comparing, so they may be translated tab-count, tab-marker, tab-nesting, tab-title, tab-indent Content tabs (=== "…"): count, marker (===+), nesting depth; a product name of the English title (Caddy, Fly.io, Nginx… the PROPER_NAMES set, or any word like macOS / Node.js) stays in the translated title; a body indented by less than 4 spaces table-count, table-shape Tables outside code: count, rows, and cells per row (a pipe inside a code span or escaped does not split a cell) variable-*, command-*, path-* The set of UPPER_SNAKE variables, dev.py <subcommand…> commands and paths cited in inline code and code blocks (comments and Mermaid labels aside; bare prose is not read: a theory page localizes lifecycle states on purpose) code-block-content A fenced block is the same code once comments, <placeholders> and spacing are put aside. code-block-modified files every difference as «comments translated» (🌐 LOCALIZED, hidden by -L); this one is the error for a changed command, setting or log line admonition-nested-count, admonition-sequence Admonitions at any depth (inside list items and tabs too): same order, marker (!!!, ???, ???+), type and depth. admonition-count reads column 0 only anchor-id, anchor-order Every explicit {: #id } of the English stays, in order; the translation adds none except the id MkDocs builds from an English heading (a translated heading keeps the English id that way)

Tests: utils translation-equivalence (test_translation_equivalence.py), including a corpus guard that runs every check on every page of every language of mkdocs_src/docs.

The HTML checks (html-tag-mismatch, html-attr-missing, html-attr-mismatch) read only rendered HTML: fenced code (any fence, found by code_line_mask() in code_blocks.py) and inline code are removed first, so inline code such as EUR<USD is no longer taken for a tag.

The structural diff, _structural_diff() in translate_docs.py, runs on each draft before the Critique step (its report goes to Critique and Refine), on every file a run writes, and in ./dev.py mkdocs translate-diff, which exits non-zero on any issue or missing translation. Its LINE_COUNT check compares blank-line-separated blocks, not lines, and flags a difference of more than max(3, 15% of the English blocks): the English wraps at about 80 columns while a translation often keeps a paragraph on one line, but a dropped or truncated section still removes blocks.

Tests: ./dev.py test utils translation-validator (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_translation_validator.py). It covers the four checks above, page_anchors.py included, the code stripping of the HTML checks and the block-based LINE_COUNT, on pages in memory and on a docs tree in a temporary directory. ./dev.py test utils gate-docs-links (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_docs_links_gate.py) covers the build's check of the relative file URLs.

docs.title: 🇫🇷 French Typography
docs.text:
French keeps a sign or a unit with the word before it: a non-breaking space stands before : ; ? ! % and a currency symbol, inside « », and between the groups of a number. The French translations, as the pipeline writes them, use plain spaces, so a line could break before a colon or inside an amount like 28 398 €; fixing the *.fr.md sources would not last, since the next run writes plain spaces again. The hook mkdocs_src/hooks/fr_typography.py, listed under hooks: in mkdocs_src/mkdocs.yml, therefore applies the French spacing at build time, to the rendered HTML of the French pages: the sources are never changed.

typeset() only replaces whitespace that is already there and never inserts a space, so 16:9, https://, Next: Select Files (an English UI label) and «sans» stay as written:

Plain whitespace Becomes Before : U+00A0 (no-break space) Before ; ? ! U+202F (narrow no-break space) Before %, and before € $ £ ¥ after a digit U+202F After « and before » U+00A0 Between the groups of a number (28 398) U+202F

: ; ? ! count only when they close a phrase, that is when followed by a space, the end of the text, closing punctuation or an entity.

typeset_html() reads text only: tags and their attributes (URLs, alt, title and data-title texts) pass through byte for byte, and so do comments and the content of code, pre, kbd, samp, var, svg, math, of the raw-text elements (script, style, textarea, iframe, noembed, noframes, xmp, skipped up to their end tag, so a <!-- inside them opens no comment) and of any element of class arithmatex (formulas).

on_page_content typesets a page only when page.file.locale is fr: mkdocs-static-i18n sets it to the language of the source file, so an English page shown in the French build (the Developer Manual, English only) keeps its English text. The page's table-of-contents titles (page.toc) get the same treatment. on_nav runs at event_priority(-110), after the on_nav of mkdocs-static-i18n (-100) has applied nav_translations; in the French build only, it typesets the navigation titles that are French labels (values of the French nav_translations). The sidebar, the tabs, the header and the browser tab title show these titles; a front-matter title:, which the hook leaves as written, replaces them in the header and the browser tab.

Measured on two builds, with and without the hook: every English, Italian and Spanish file is byte-identical (only the search indexes differ, as they hold the French text); the 322 French pages differ only in whitespace, with identical start tags and identical code and formula content; plain whitespace before : ; ? ! % in their French text (sidebar included) drops from 6,580 to 0, while the 28 in the English text of the English fallback pages stay, by design.

The hook does not reach the app's changelog modal, which renders CHANGELOG.fr.md with marked, outside MkDocs. frontend/src/lib/features/changelog/changelog.ts therefore exports typesetFrench(), the hook's typeset() ported with the same rules and the same characters (the table above), and typesetFrenchMarkdown(), which applies it to the prose of a Markdown text. In createLocalizedChangelog(), load() typesets the French file before parseChangelog() cuts it into chapters, through TYPESETTERS, a per-language table in which only fr has an entry. The English chapters the French UI shows for versions not translated yet, and the Italian, Spanish and English changelogs, stay as written; CHANGELOG.fr.md itself keeps the plain spaces the pipeline writes.

  • What stays byte for byte: fenced code, backtick or tilde, at any indentation (a fence inside a list item included); inline code spans, which never cross into another block; link destinations with their titles; inline images whole (![alt](src "title")), since in HTML the alt is an attribute; reference definitions and autolinks; HTML comments, tags with their attributes, and the content of code, pre, kbd, samp, var, svg, math, script, style and textarea; bare URLs.
  • A marker ends a run of text, as a tag does in the hook's HTML: : ; ? ! also count before an emphasis, code, link or tag marker (* _ ~ ` [ <), so *Mot de passe oublié ?* gets the narrow no-break space the hook gives <em>Mot de passe oublié ?</em>.
  • Measured on 12 October 2026 with a Node probe against the hook, on the real CHANGELOG.fr.md (4 chapters, 7 italic questions like the one above): typesetFrench() equals typeset() on all 617 prose runs, and for each chapter the HTML marked renders from the typeset Markdown is byte-identical to typeset_html() applied to the HTML of the plain chapter (197 no-break and 178 narrow no-break spaces); the same holds on a synthetic document covering every construct above.

Tests: ./dev.py test utils docs-fr-typography (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_docs_fr_typography.py) for the hook, and ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit for the changelog (frontend/src/lib/features/changelog/changelog.test.ts, with the hook's typeset() cases ported as tables).

docs.title: 🔎 Search by Language
docs.text:
MkDocs builds one search index, search/search_index.json, for every language of the site, so a visitor reading Italian downloaded the English, French and Spanish pages too (10.58 MB on the current build) and found the four versions of a page together in the results. Two pieces make the search follow the language of the page being read:

  • The hook mkdocs_src/hooks/search_language_split.py, listed under hooks: in mkdocs_src/mkdocs.yml. Its on_post_build (event_priority(-100), after the search plugin and the merge of mkdocs-static-i18n) reads the full index and writes one file per language next to it: search/search_index.en.json, .it.json, .fr.json and .es.json. Each has the same config as the full index and only the entries written in that language. The full search_index.json is left as it is.
  • The script mkdocs_src/docs/javascripts/search-language.js, loaded from <head> by mkdocs_src/overrides/main.html (block extrahead), not through extra_javascript: it must run before Material's bundle, which starts loading the index as soon as it loads. Material 9.7.7 loads it with XMLHttpRequest (the browser lists the request as xmlhttprequest, not fetch), so the script wraps XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open, and fetch too in case a later Material changes. The wrapped call sends the request for search/search_index.json to search/search_index.<lang>.json, where <lang> is the primary subtag of <html lang> (English when the site has no such language). Any other request is untouched.

A page belongs to the language its address starts with (it/, fr/, es/); every other address, the default language having no prefix, is English. A page that exists only in English, such as the whole Developer Manual, has therefore no copy in the other languages' index: a reader of Italian finds it only with the checkbox below. The hook skips the intermediate builds that mkdocs-static-i18n runs for each non-default language (their index is merged into the main one afterwards, and the main one is what is split); if the full index is missing or unreadable it logs a warning and writes nothing.

The checkbox. The script adds a checkbox as the first child of the result area of the search dialog (data-testid="docs-search-all-languages"), labelled «Search the other languages too» in the language of the page (LABELS, English, Italian, French and Spanish). Checking or unchecking it stores the choice in localStorage (key lf-docs-search-all-languages, value 1, removed when off), keeps the typed query in sessionStorage (key lf-docs-search-query) and reloads the page, because Material prepares its search once per page. After the reload the search opens again with the query in the field. With the choice on, the script leaves the request for the full index alone, so the results come from all four languages, on every page. Every access to a storage is in a try: where there is none (a private window, a blocked storage) the page searches its own language only. The style is the .lf-search-language rule at the end of mkdocs_src/docs/static/extra.css.

Index Entries Size English (search_index.en.json) 3911 5.98 MB Italian 1843 1.36 MB French 1840 1.44 MB Spanish 1844 1.38 MB Full (search_index.json) all 10.58 MB

Measured on the build of 23 October 2026. By default a reader of Italian, French or Spanish downloads about 1.4 MB, a reader of English about 6 MB, instead of 10.5 MB.

Adding a language. Add it to the LANGUAGES tuple of the hook and to the LANGUAGES array and the LABELS table of the script (the label in the new language), keeping the default language first in the tuple. The site's own language list in mkdocs.yml is the other place that must already know it.

Tests:

  • ./dev.py test utils docs-search-split (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_docs_search_split.py): the language of an entry, the split (every entry in exactly one file, the input untouched), the files on_post_build writes, the real built index, the hook and the script in the configuration and in main.html, and the built site (four files, the script in the head before Material's bundle).
  • ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit: the Vitest files searchLanguage.test.ts and searchLanguage.dom.test.ts in frontend/src/lib/utils/docs/ (the rewriting of the request, the storage failures, the checkbox and the reopening of the search).
  • ./dev.py test front-utility docs-search-language: the Playwright spec frontend/e2e/docs/search-language.spec.ts, which searches the built documentation in the four languages and with the checkbox on and off. It needs ./dev.py mkdocs build first: a site built before this feature answers 404 for search_index.<lang>.json.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Prettier uses the remark parser (CommonMark). In CommonMark, !!! info "title" is an unknown construct — admonitions don't exist. Prettier treats the 4-space indented body as "continuation text" and strips the indentation, breaking the admonition box:

<!-- BEFORE Prettier -->
!!! note "Title"
    Content inside the box.     ← 4 spaces (INSIDE the box)

<!-- AFTER Prettier — BROKEN -->
!!! note "Title"
Content inside the box.         ← 0 spaces (OUTSIDE the box)

tabWidth: 4 does NOT fix this — it only controls tab→space conversion, not paragraph indentation preservation.

docs.title: The Solution
docs.text:
Add an empty line between the directive and the indented body. With the empty line, Prettier leaves the block completely untouched, and MkDocs renders identically:

<!-- ✅ CORRECT — survives Prettier unchanged -->
!!! note "Title"

    Content inside the box.
    Second line.

<!-- ❌ WRONG — Prettier will strip indentation -->
!!! note "Title"
    Content inside the box.
    Second line.

This applies to both !!! (admonitions) and ??? (collapsible details).

docs.title: Automated Checks
docs.text:
The empty-line rule is enforced at three levels:

Check Where Severity Description Pre-build warning dev.py → _check_admonition_empty_lines() ⚠️ Warning Runs before every ./dev.py mkdocs build. Scans all .md files and warns if any admonition is missing the empty line. Translation validation validate_translations.py → admonition-empty-line ⚠️ WARN Checks translated files during ./dev.py mkdocs translate-validate. Structural diff (critic) translate_docs.py → _structural_diff() → ADMONITION_EMPTY_LINE Info to LLM Injected into the Step 4 (Critique) context so the critic LLM can flag and fix the issue during refinement.

docs.title: 🎨 Frontend Development
docs.text: This section covers the SvelteKit frontend architecture, components, and development patterns.

docs.title: 📖 Overview
docs.text:
LibreFolio's frontend is built with:

  • SvelteKit 2.x - Full-stack web framework
  • Svelte 5 - Reactive UI framework using Runes ($state, $derived, $effect)
  • Tailwind CSS 4.x - Utility-first CSS (configured via @theme in CSS)
  • TypeScript - Type safety
  • lucide-svelte - Icon library

docs.title: ⚡ Svelte 5 Runes
docs.text: New components use Svelte 5's Runes for reactivity, but a minority of older components use no rune at all, so Svelte compiles them in legacy mode (export let props, $: statements). The one consequence to know: in a legacy component, a function call inside a template expression compiles into $.untrack(…), so runes state read inside that function is not tracked — that is why the Brokers page stopped following the privacy toggle (R20). Render such a value through a runes child (e.g. lib/components/ui/display/CurrencyAmount.svelte) or migrate the component; see Legacy components freeze masked output.

docs.title: 🔑 Key Runes Used
docs.text:
• $state: Declares reactive state. 
    let count = $state(0);
  • $derived: Declares derived state (automatically updates when dependencies change). 
    let double = $derived(count * 2);
  • $effect: Side effects (runs when dependencies change). 
    $effect(() => {
    console.log(count);
});
  • $props: Declares component props. 
    let { title, active = false } = $props();
