Pruning

Branches are pruned early: if a neighbor is in visitedNodes or the provider is at max usage, tryEdge returns immediately without recursing.

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text:
With \(N\) = number of currencies, \(E\) = number of edges, \(D\) = maxDepth:

Metric Value Notes Time (worst case) \(O(E^D)\) Exponential in depth, but \(D=4\) is small Time (practical) < 1ms ~4 providers × ~25 currencies, ~200 edges Space \(O(D)\) Path stack depth (recursive DFS) Output Sorted by length Shortest paths first

The graph is small enough that Web Worker parallelization is not needed. Profiling shows sub-millisecond execution even with all providers enabled.

docs.title: Session-Level Caching
docs.text:
The graph is built once per browser session and cached in currencyGraphStore.ts:

// Module-level singleton
let cachedGraph: MultiDirectedGraph | null = null;

export async function getOrBuildGraph(): MultiDirectedGraph {
    if (cachedGraph) return cachedGraph;

    const [providers, currencies] = await Promise.all([
        fetchProviders(),
        fetchCurrencies(),
    ]);
    cachedGraph = buildCurrencyGraph(providers, currencies);
    return cachedGraph;
}

Why this works: the currency list (GET /utilities/currencies, built from pycountry) and the FX providers with their base currencies do not change while the server runs. Each provider's target_currencies in GET /fx/providers come from a 24 h backend cache (backend/app/services/fx/catalog.py): when the provider's fetch fails or takes longer than 5 s, the backend answers with the last list that provider returned in this process (empty before its first success) and retries after 5 minutes. currencyGraphStore.ts has no invalidation API: it keeps the graph in module state until the page is reloaded — client-side navigation reuses it, a full reload fetches both endpoints again, and a failed request is not kept (the next use retries). Until that reload the graph keeps the lists it was built with, including an empty one served before a provider's first successful fetch.

docs.title: Route Sorting in the UI
docs.text:
When multiple paths are found, FxProviderSelect.svelte sorts them:

  1. Direct routes (1-step) appear first in their own section
  2. Chain routes are grouped by step count (2-step, 3-step, 4-step)
  3. Within each group, chains are sorted by:
    1. Configured intermediate legs (descending) — chains that reuse already-registered pairs appear first
    2. Unique provider count (ascending) — fewer providers = simpler
    3. Key (alphabetical tiebreaker)

The picker opens from Add conversion route and also lists, under Not usable, every provider other than MANUAL that appears in no path for the pair. When there is no direct route, the first chain group opens by itself. The search splits the query on spaces and keeps a route only when every token matches its search text: provider codes and names, plus the code, name, flag and country names of each currency on the path. A provider's warning_i18n shows as ⚠️ on a selected route.

docs.title: Output Format
docs.text:
Each path is a ChainStep[] array, directly usable as chain_steps in POST /fx/providers/routes:

interface ChainStep {
    from: string;    // Source currency (logical direction)
    to: string;      // Target currency (logical direction)
    provider: string; // Provider code (e.g., "ECB")
}

// Direct route
[{ from: "EUR", to: "USD", provider: "ECB" }]

// 2-step chain
[
    { from: "RON", to: "EUR", provider: "ECB" },
    { from: "EUR", to: "USD", provider: "ECB" }
]

No transformation is needed between the DFS output and the API request body.

docs.title: 💾 How the Modal Saves the Routes
docs.text:
FxPairAddModal.svelte builds the POST /fx/providers/routes body from the selection:

  • The selected routes sit in an OrderableList (drag and drop); they are posted in list order with priority 1…n, so the first one is the primary route.
  • With no route selected, the pair gets one MANUAL step ({from: base, to: quote, provider: "MANUAL"}) at priority 999, the backend's MANUAL_PRIORITY (backend/app/services/fx_providers/manual/plugin.py).
  • Also create intermediate pairs (shown when a chain is selected) adds, for every chain step whose pair is neither configured yet nor the main pair, a 1-step route at priority 1, deduplicated across chains.
  • A pair that is already configured cannot be created again: the save button is disabled, and before posting the modal checks the configured pairs it holds and drops the save if the pair is among them. It does not reload them: ensureFxRoutesLoaded() (fxRoutesStore.ts) answers from the store until invalidateFxRoutes() empties it (after a save of this tab), so a pair another tab configured since the last load is not seen.
  • In edit mode (Providers on the pair page) the modal posts the new list in one request with ?replace=true (X-R75): the backend keeps exactly those routes for the pair, in one transaction, so a save that fails or never arrives leaves the pair as it was. With an empty list it posts the MANUAL item, and the pair becomes manual. Before X-R75 the modal deleted all the pair's routes first, so a failed post left the pair with no route, and an empty list deleted the pair: a whole-pair delete never reinstates the MANUAL sentinel.
  • In edit mode, the intermediate pairs go first, in a plain request, then the pair alone with ?replace=true (X-R79): replace applies to every pair a request names, so a leg another tab configured meanwhile would lose its other routes. The plain request keeps them, though it still rewrites the leg's priority 1, as a creation does. Legs refused: nothing is written. Legs written and the pair refused: the pair is as it was, and the legs stay configured. A creation posts the pair and its intermediate pairs in one plain request.

docs.title: 🌍 Internationalization (i18n)
docs.text: LibreFolio supports multiple languages to ensure accessibility for a global audience. The frontend uses svelte-i18n for managing translations and locale switching.

docs.title: 🗣️ Supported Languages
docs.text:
Currently, the following languages are supported:

  • 🇬🇧 English (en) - Default
  • 🇮🇹 Italian (it)
  • 🇫🇷 French (fr)
  • 🇪🇸 Spanish (es)

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
The app loads one catalogue per language, frontend/src/lib/i18n/{en,it,fr,es}.json: index.ts registers each with svelte-i18n (register('en', () => import('./en.json'))). These four files are generated, so never edit them. Their sources are the generic vocabulary in base/, one folder per subsystem, and each plugin's own fragment:

frontend/src/lib/i18n/
├── base/{en,it,fr,es}.json        # Source: the generic vocabulary
├── <subsystem>/                   # Source: one folder per subsystem (22)
│   ├── prefixes.txt               #   the key prefixes it owns
│   └── {en,it,fr,es}.json
├── {en,it,fr,es}.json             # Generated: the catalogue the app loads (ignored by git, read-only)
├── .generated                     # Generated: the sha256 stamp of the four files
├── index.ts                       # Configuration and initialization
└── catalogIcuLocale.test.ts       # Unit test: no locale-sensitive ICU message shared by two catalogues

backend/app/services/<family>/<plugin>/i18n/{en,it,fr,es}.json   # Source: a plugin's own keys

docs.title: 🏭 The Generated Catalogue
docs.text:
scripts/i18n_catalog.py merges the sources into the four files. It uses the standard library only and runs on Python 3.9 or later, because the npm hooks call it with the system python3 (the PYTHON environment variable picks another interpreter).

  • Not tracked. frontend/.gitignore ignores the four files and the stamp. The files are read-only (0444), and .generated records the sha256 of each language; it is not a .json, so nothing takes it for a language.
  • Written only when its content changes, so a run that changes nothing leaves the files, and the bundle built from them, untouched.
  • Never edited by hand. A generated file whose content matches neither this build nor the stamp of the last one stops the next build, which names the file and asks to move the change to its source (./dev.py i18n where <key>); ./dev.py i18n build --force overwrites it.
  • Who writes it:
    • the npm pre-hooks of dev, build, build:debug, check and check:watch, through frontend/scripts/i18n-catalog-build.mjs (by hand: npm run i18n:build), so also ./dev.py front dev and ./dev.py front check;
    • Vitest's globalSetup (frontend/vitest.config.ts), before every run;
    • ./dev.py front build, before svelte-check;
    • ./dev.py lint --dead-code, before knip;
    • the AI Export real-prompt probe (backend/test_scripts/diagnostics/ai_export_real_prompt_probe.py), before it starts its frontend bridge;
    • every ./dev.py i18n command that writes.
  • Staleness. check_frontend_needs_build() (scripts/cli_base.py) asks for a frontend build when a generated file is missing, even when the bundle is fresh. Besides the sources under src/ and the files under static/, it watches the plugin fragments and scripts/i18n_catalog.py.
  • Prettier skips the generated files (frontend/.prettierignore). The sources under src/ stay under Prettier, which writes them in the generator's own form, json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus a trailing newline: the *.json override of .prettierrc sets the two-space indent.

docs.title: 📚 The Sources
docs.text:
Every source is nested JSON with absolute keys, one file per language, and there are three kinds.

base/<lang>.json, the generic vocabulary, owns every key nobody else claims: common, datePicker, csvImport, dataEditor, sectors, table, import, prices, assetPicker, error, header, filter, sharedResource, nav, date.

<subsystem>/<lang>.json: one folder per product area, whose prefixes.txt declares the key prefixes it owns, one per line (# starts a comment). The 22 subsystems today (the prefixes.txt files are the truth):

Subsystem Prefixes aiExport aiExport app changelog, support, updateCheck, donationPopup, help, connectionSecurity, legal assets assets, assetDetail, providerErrors, events auth auth backup backup brokers brokers charts chartSettings, chart, measure, signals dashboard dashboard dataQuality dataQuality email email files uploads, fileStatus, files fx fx, fxDetail importWizard importWizard instance instance liveUpdates liveUpdates onboarding onboarding pacAllocator tools.pacAllocator pluginSettings pluginSettings risk risk settings settings tools tools transactions transactions

backend/app/services/<family>/<plugin>/i18n/<lang>.json: a plugin's own keys, beside its code (72 fragments today). Which keys a plugin may hold, how to add them and the gate that keeps them there: A Plugin's Translations, Adding a Plugin's Keys and The Ownership Gate.

A subsystem and the plugins can share a namespace. pluginSettings holds the texts of the Plugins tab of Settings and of Configure (pluginSettings.tab.*, pluginSettings.secret.*, pluginSettings.refusals.*…), while the labels, descriptions and options of each plugin's own settings live in that plugin's fragment, under pluginSettings.asset.<provider_code> (justETF and Borsa Italiana today) or pluginSettings.fx.<code>: the keys the plugin declares in its settings_fields (Labels and Translations). The fragment wins over the subsystem's prefix, as below.

docs.title: 🔑 Who Owns a Key
docs.text:
A key belongs to the plugin whose fragment holds it; otherwise to the subsystem with the longest declared prefix (tools.pacAllocator.* to pacAllocator, the rest of tools.* to tools); otherwise to base. A fragment wins over the prefixes: risk.analytics.stress.name lives in the stress plugin, the rest of risk.* in the risk subsystem. Keys several plugins share stay in their subsystem (signals.reference.* and signals.tooltips.riskWindow, in charts), and so does the risk.warnings.* vocabulary, in risk.

The sources must agree. These are errors, and the build, ./dev.py i18n check and the gate report them all at once:

  • a key in two sources;
  • a string in one source and a branch in another;
  • a key outside the folder its prefix names;
  • a prefix declared twice;
  • a subsystem without prefixes;
  • a source without English;
  • a key English lacks;
  • a value that is not a string;
  • unreadable JSON;
  • a language base does not have.

The generated file lists base first, then the subsystems by name, then the plugins by path; each source keeps its own key order in each language.

docs.title: 🌐 Languages and Fallback
docs.text: English is mandatory: base/en.json must exist, the languages are those of base/, and a source with any file must have its en.json. When a source lacks a translation, the build fills it from English and prints a warning, so the app always ships every key; the strict check — ./dev.py i18n check, the audit and utils gate-i18n-catalog — fails on it instead. Backend tests read the catalogue with load_catalog(lang, fallback=False) from scripts/i18n_catalog.py: the sources merged in memory, without the English fallback and without a frontend build, so a test asserting "translated in every language" can still fail.

docs.title: 💻 Usage in Components
docs.text:
To use translations in Svelte components, import the t store:

<script>
  import { t } from '$lib/i18n';
</script>

<h1>{$t('dashboard.welcome')}</h1>
<p>{$t('common.save')}</p>

$lib/i18n also re-exports _, svelte-i18n's other name for the same store: $_('common.save') and $t('common.save') are interchangeable, and both appear in the codebase.

docs.title: 🔀 Dynamic Values
docs.text:
Messages use the ICU MessageFormat syntax (svelte-i18n formats them with intl-messageformat):

{
  "greeting": "Hello, {name}!",
  "positions": "{n, plural, one {# position} other {# positions}}"
}

Pass the variables under the values option:

<p>{$t('greeting', {values: {name: 'Alice'}})}</p>
<p>{$t('positions', {values: {n: 3}})}</p>

Without values the message comes back as written, placeholders included: $t('greeting', {name: 'Alice'}) renders Hello, {name}!.

docs.title: ⚠️ Locale-Sensitive ICU Messages
docs.text:
svelte-i18n 4.0.1 (the locked version) caches compiled message formatters by message text only: getMessageFormatter is wrapped in monadicMemoize, which keys the cache on its first argument and never sees the locale (frontend/node_modules/svelte-i18n/dist/runtime.js, lines 383–392 and 496). The app switches language in place, so a message that is byte-identical in two catalogues keeps the rules of whichever locale compiled it first.

This changes what the user reads only for locale-sensitive elements: plural, selectordinal, number, date and time. Plain text, {name} substitutions and select render the same in every locale. For example, 0 selects one in French but other in English: if the French catalogue reused the English positions text above verbatim, a page rendered in English first would keep showing 0 positions after a switch to French, instead of 0 position.

Rule: a locale-sensitive message must never be byte-identical across catalogues. When a translation would coincide with another locale's text, make it differ. For a French plural, add the CLDR many branch:

{
  "positions": "{n, plural, one {# position} many {# positions} other {# positions}}"
}

The unit test frontend/src/lib/i18n/catalogIcuLocale.test.ts enforces the rule on the four catalogues. It also pins the library behaviour: if a svelte-i18n upgrade adds the locale to the cache key, its characterization test turns red, which is the signal to revisit the rule.

docs.title: 🔢 Numbers, amounts and dates
docs.text: The rule (M-18, developer decision of 2026-10-12): every figure — number, amount, percentage, exact decimal, file size, duration, date, chart axis and tooltip — is written in the interface language, through one source: uiLocale() from $lib/stores/app/uiLocale. Never in the browser's own locale, so a percentage never sits beside an amount written another way. Paths below are relative to frontend/src/.

docs.title: 🗺️ Which locale
docs.text:
resolveUiLocale(uiLanguage, browserTag) builds the locale from the interface language. The browser counts only for its region: when its primary tag (navigator.language) is in the interface language and names a region, that tag is the locale. The navigator.languages list is never read: browsers list en-US among the secondary languages of most users, so reading it would give an Italian who chose English American dates. The rule lives in its own module, lib/stores/app/uiLocaleRule.ts, which uiLocale.ts re-exports and which imports nothing (uiLocale.test.ts checks it): an E2E spec imports it by path to write a day as the app does (dayAsThePanelWritesIt, in brokers-detail.spec.ts), and Playwright resolves neither $app nor $lib.

Browser primary tag Locale Examples In the interface language, with a region The browser's tag, canonical en-GB, en-US, it-CH, fr-CA, es-MX, es-419 Without a region, in another language, absent (server side) or invalid The language's default: en-GB for English (12/10/2026, 12 Oct 2026, 14:05), the bare language for it, fr, es English UI on en or it-IT → en-GB; Italian UI on en-US → it

So an Italian interface on an it-CH browser writes a decimal point (12.50%), a French one on fr-CA writes numeric dates the ISO way (2026-10-12), and a bare en browser gets en-GB: kept as it is, Intl would write it American (10/12/2026, 2:05 PM).

docs.title: 🧰 Formatters
docs.text:
Every formatter below defaults to uiLocale(), so runes code passes no locale; a legacy component passes $uiLocaleStore (see Reactivity), and a unit test may pass a fixed locale to stay deterministic.

Formatter File Writes formatPercent(value, {digits, signed, scale, suffix, empty, locale}) lib/utils/core/formatPercent.ts A percentage through Intl (style: 'percent'), rounded first with toFixed so the digits are the ones toFixed gave. digits defaults to 2 and signed to true: a + before a positive value, no sign on zero. scale: 100 for a fraction, suffix: 'pp' for percentage points, '' for a bare number. formatFixed(value, digits, {signed, trim, locale}) lib/utils/core/formatFixed.ts The localized toFixed: the same digits and rounding, with the locale's decimal mark and grouping. trim turns digits into a maximum; signed defaults to false. formatExactDecimal(value, {minFrac, maxFrac, locale}) lib/utils/core/formatFixed.ts An exact decimal — a backend decimal string, a quantity, a rate, a split ratio — with no float in between. The digits are those of formatDecimalForDisplay: cut after maxFrac (default 8), never rounded, trailing zeros dropped, padded to minFrac (default 0), -0 read as 0. Intl.NumberFormat is handed them as a string and only writes them. Empty input gives ''; a value that is not a plain decimal is returned unformatted. formatPrice(value, {minDecimals, floorDecimals, signed, locale}), priceFractionDigits(value, {minDecimals, floorDecimals}) lib/utils/core/formatFixed.ts A price (C-97c, decision D-C97c-1): as many decimals as 4 significant digits need, never fewer than floorDecimals, never more than 12, and at least minDecimals shown (2 by default; an exchange rate passes 4). floorDecimals (default minDecimals) lets a site keep the range it showed: the data editor {minDecimals: 0, floorDecimals: 4}, the running average {minDecimals: 2, floorDecimals: 4}. 0.0000034573 → 0,000003457, 1.23456 → 1,235, 65000.123 → 65.000,12, 0.5 → 0,50. A string is written exactly, a number as it is; '' for an empty, non-numeric or non-finite value, never its input. priceFractionDigits gives the same {min, max} to a formatter that writes the amount itself (formatCurrencyAmountPlain's minFraction/maxFraction). formatCurrencyAmountPlain, formatCurrencyAmountHtml lib/utils/currency/currencyFormat.ts Money, masked under privacy; option locale. formatDateTime(value, locale?) lib/utils/core/formatDateTime.ts A date and time, to the minute. formatAxisDate(locale, value, withYear?) lib/utils/core/formatAxisDate.ts A short date for a chart axis or tooltip. An empty locale means uiLocale(); a bare YYYY-MM-DD is read as a local calendar day.

The domain helpers built on them take a locale parameter that defaults to uiLocale() as well:

  • lots, in lib/features/brokers/lots/: formatLotQuantity, formatLotQuantityMasked, formatLotQuantityCell, formatQuantity (Gantt), formatAxisPercent, formatAxisCurrency, formatAxisAmount, formatAxisNumber;
  • risk, in lib/features/risk/: formatCurrencyAmount, formatScopedCurrencyAmount, dayFormatter;
  • the PAC planner, in lib/features/tools/pac-allocator/planner/format.ts: formatPlannerDate, formatPlannerTimestamp, formatCopyStamp;
  • file sizes: formatBytes, in lib/utils/files/upload.ts.

docs.title: 🚫 Never, for display
docs.text:
• toFixed or toPrecision: they write no locale at all, so an Italian screen read 9.2 beside 4788,01;
  • formatDecimalForDisplay for a figure that is only read: it writes a dot in every language, where formatExactDecimal writes the same digits in the interface locale;
  • toLocaleString(undefined, …), a toLocaleString(), toLocaleDateString() or toLocaleTimeString() with no locale, Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, …) or any other Intl.*Format(undefined, …): the browser's locale;
  • a hard-coded 'en' or 'en-US';
  • $currentLanguage or $locale as the locale of a figure: a bare language drops the browser's region, and a bare en writes American dates.

$currentLanguage and $locale stay right for text, which this rule does not cover: translations, country, currency and sector names, Intl.ListFormat, the AI Export response language. Name collation (nameComparator) is text as well; its callers pass no locale today, so it sorts by the browser's rules.

docs.title: ⚡ Reactivity
docs.text:
uiLocale() reads the store through Svelte's fromStore, so the read is tracked wherever Svelte tracks:

  • Runes components: a read in a template, a $derived or an $effect is tracked, even inside a helper's default parameter, so {formatPercent(value)} follows an in-place language switch.
  • Legacy components (no runes: export let, $:): a function call in a template expression is compiled into $.untrack(…), so a read inside the helper is untracked and the figure keeps the language of the mount. The template reads $uiLocaleStore itself and passes it down: formatSharePercentage(broker.user_share_percentage, $uiLocaleStore) in routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte, formatDate($currentUser?.created_at, $uiLocaleStore) in lib/features/settings/tabs/ProfileTab.svelte. It is the trap behind the privacy freeze (devWiki: problems/legacy-component-language-untracked).
  • ECharts: formatter and renderItem callbacks run outside any tracking. The $effect that calls setOption reads the locale itself, void uiLocale(); beside its other void dependencies, so a switch rebuilds the option and redraws the chart (lib/components/charts/ScatterChart.svelte), as it does for the privacy flag.

docs.title: 🧩 Known exceptions
docs.text:
• Decimal fields: formatDecimalForDisplay (lib/utils/core/formatDecimal.ts) stays locale-neutral, with a dot, wherever its output must read back through normalizeDecimalInput (lib/utils/core/parseDecimalInput.ts): the value of ExactDecimalInput and ExactQuantityInput, the edit buffer of CompactCashCell. Localizing a field means localizing its reading too. It also serves logic that displays nothing: pluralCount in the PAC planner's format.ts, and the "did the amount change" comparison of WacPreviewSection.
  • Native date fields: an <input type="date"> is drawn by the browser, in the browser's language (backlog T-DI).
  • Figures inside catalogue messages (backlog T-ICU): svelte-i18n writes an ICU number argument and the # of a plural in its own locale, the bare language, without uiLocale()'s region. The only number argument is {covered, number, percent} in risk.warnings.historical_replay_mostly_excluded, and the catalogues hold no ICU dates. It shows only where the region changes the notation: on an es-MX browser a plural's # reads 1234 where the rest of the page writes 1,234.
  • The AI Export prompt writes its figures locale-neutral by design, so uiLocale() never changes a byte of it; the interface language reaches it only as text (the response language, the translated additional-data section, the legal notice, and Export Data's reply sentence, aiExport.replyInstructions.dataReceived). The panel's token count and byte size, and the copied message, are figures like any other.
  • Currency minor digits: new Intl.NumberFormat('en', {style: 'currency', currency}) only reads maximumFractionDigits (lib/features/ai-export/templates/snapshotDataRenderer.ts, lib/features/tools/pac-allocator/planner/format.ts); it writes nothing.
  • The time zone: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone (lib/features/settings/tabs/GlobalSettingsTab.svelte) reads the browser's zone, not a notation.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text:
• Drive the language with currentLanguage.set(…) ($lib/stores/app/language), as the language selector does, and set it back to English after the test.
  • Pin navigator.language when the region matters: the test runtime's tag can follow the host (LANG=it_CH.UTF-8 gives it-CH). Stub it before the first import, as lib/utils/core/__tests__/formatPercent.test.ts does with vi.hoisted(() => { vi.stubGlobal('navigator', {language: 'en-US', languages: ['en-US']}); }), or per test with vi.stubGlobal, vi.resetModules() and a fresh import(), as lib/stores/app/uiLocale.test.ts does.
  • Compute a localized expectation with Intl in the same runtime, never as a typed literal: French, Italian and Spanish output carries no-break spaces (U+202F, U+00A0), and ICU has changed which one goes where between releases. Check that the expectation differs from the English text, or the case proves nothing.
  • Switch the language in place, after mount and in both directions: only that catches a legacy freeze.
  • Two source gates read figure sites. The HTML escaping gate (htmlInterpolation.gate.test.ts) trusts a computed-key read passed as the first argument of formatFixed, formatPercent or formatPrice, as it trusts x[k].toFixed(n): only those three names and only that argument, so formatExactDecimal(x[k]) in an HTML template is still reported. The money gate (lib/utils/privacy/moneyRenderSites.test.ts) keys its registry by file and snippet: rewriting a registered expression, a toFixed into a formatFixed, means updating its snippet.

docs.title: 🛠️ Managing Translations
docs.text: LibreFolio provides a full CLI toolkit for the translation sources via ./dev.py i18n (./dev.py i18n --help gives the exact text of every command). Every command that writes rebuilds the catalogue.

docs.title: 🧭 Where a Key Goes
docs.text:
./dev.py i18n where KEY names the file that holds a key, or the one add would write it to:

$ ./dev.py i18n where common.save
frontend/src/lib/i18n/base/en.json (exists)
$ ./dev.py i18n where brokers.newFeatureTitle
frontend/src/lib/i18n/brokers/en.json (new key)
$ ./dev.py i18n where signals.rsi.newLevel
backend/app/services/signal_plugins/rsi/i18n/en.json (new key)
$ ./dev.py i18n where myFeature.title
frontend/src/lib/i18n/base/en.json (new key; 'myFeature' is a new namespace in base, the generic vocabulary: if it belongs to a subsystem or a plugin, use --into, or move it (dev.py i18n move myFeature --into <subsystem|family/plugin>))

A new key goes to the owner its path names (Who Owns a Key): under the branch a plugin's keys share (signals.rsi above), to that plugin; under a branch that only plugins share (brimPlugins.<new>, risk.analytics.<new>, assets.providerParams.<new>, pluginSettings.asset.<new>), nowhere — add refuses and asks for --into <family>/<plugin>, as it does for every new key of a plugin whose keys share no branch (Borsa Italiana); otherwise to the subsystem with the longest declared prefix, else to base. A key that opens a new top-level namespace in base, which holds only the generic vocabulary, comes with the notice above: if it belongs to a subsystem or a plugin, name the target with --into, or move it.

docs.title: ➕ Add, Update, Remove Keys
docs.text:
# Add a key in the four languages, to the source that owns it
./dev.py i18n add "dashboard.new_feature" --en "New Feature" --it "Nuova Funzionalità" --fr "Nouvelle Fonctionnalité" --es "Nueva Característica"

# Name the source: base, a subsystem, or a plugin as <family>/<plugin> (its folder must hold plugin.py)
./dev.py i18n add "signals.typicalPrice.name" --en "Typical Price" --it "…" --fr "…" --es "…" --into signal_plugins/typical_price

# Update an existing key in specific languages, in the source that holds it
./dev.py i18n update "dashboard.title" --en "My Dashboard" --it "La mia Dashboard"

# Remove a key from every source and language
./dev.py i18n remove "obsolete.key"

# Remove without confirmation prompt
./dev.py i18n remove "obsolete.key" -f

add prints the file it wrote (📁 Source: …/<lang>.json). Without --into, a key that opens a new namespace in base also prints the notice; an explicit --into is the author's choice and prints none. Always pass --into for a plugin's keys (Known Limits). Removing the last key of a plugin's fragment deletes the fragment.

docs.title: 🔎 Search & Explore
docs.text:
# Search for keys or values containing a query (keys + values in every language)
./dev.py i18n search "broker"

# Search only in keys
./dev.py i18n search "broker" -k

# Search only in values
./dev.py i18n search "broker" -v

# Restrict the value search to one or more languages (comma-separated)
./dev.py i18n search "courtier" -l fr

# Show key tree structure
./dev.py i18n tree

# Show tree for a prefix with key counts
./dev.py i18n tree "fx" --counts

search shows every key it finds in the four languages, followed by the source that owns it (the Source column).

docs.title: ⚙️ Build and Check
docs.text:
# Regenerate src/lib/i18n/<lang>.json from the sources
./dev.py i18n build

# A missing translation is an error instead of an English fallback
./dev.py i18n build --strict

# Overwrite a generated file edited by hand
./dev.py i18n build --force

# Validate the sources, strictly: every rule above, every language complete
./dev.py i18n check

# Accept a missing translation, as the build does
./dev.py i18n check --lenient

# Also prove the catalogue equal to the one at a git revision
./dev.py i18n check --against <rev>

--against compares key by key and language by language, without the English fallback. It reads the revision in either layout: the four tracked single files of the old layout, or the sources tracked at that revision. It is the proof that a reorganisation lost nothing.

docs.title: 🚚 Move, Split, Absorb
docs.text:
# Move every key under a prefix, in every language, to another source
./dev.py i18n move "signals.typicalPrice" --into signal_plugins/typical_price

# Put every key of base and of the subsystems in the folder its declared prefix names
./dev.py i18n split

# Replay what a branch changed in the catalogue since its merge-base
./dev.py i18n absorb --base <merge-base> --theirs <branch>
  • move PREFIX --into SOURCE moves a key, or every key under a prefix, in every language. SOURCE is base, a subsystem, or <family>/<plugin>. A move that would break a rule of Who Owns a Key — a key outside the folder its prefix names — is refused and writes nothing: to hand a branch to another subsystem, declare its prefix there and run split.
  • split puts every key of base and of the subsystems where its declared prefix says, and leaves the plugins' keys alone. It is re-runnable: with nothing to move it answers «Every key is already in place».
  • absorb --base REV --theirs REV [--prefer ours|theirs] replays on the sources what a branch on an older layout changed in the catalogue. It is a three-way merge of base, ours (the sources here) and theirs, per key and language: what only theirs changed is applied, a new key going where add would put it, and a key one side removed while the other changed one of its translations is one conflict on the whole key. Without --prefer every conflict is listed and nothing is written; --prefer settles them all one way. All or nothing: any problem writes nothing. A new key under a branch only plugins share has no owner to guess: add it first with add --into, then absorb again.

docs.title: 🔍 Audit
docs.text:
Report translation coverage, key usage and, optionally, duplicate values across the four languages. The audit reads the sources, merged per language without the English fallback, so a translation a source lacks is reported missing; it starts with the strict check of the sources (Checking the sources (strict)):

# Default: warnings only, on the terminal (no full translation table)
./dev.py i18n audit

# Include the duplicate-value analysis
./dev.py i18n audit --duplicates

# Full Markdown report (adds the complete translation table), on the terminal
./dev.py i18n audit --format md

# Excel workbook: i18n-audit.xlsx in the current directory
./dev.py i18n audit --format xlsx

# Markdown and Excel files in a chosen directory
./dev.py i18n audit --format both --output ./reports/

# Markdown report to a chosen file
./dev.py i18n audit --format md --output i18n-report.md
Flag Description --format, -f none (default): warnings only, on the terminal. md: the full Markdown report, on the terminal or, with --output, in a file. xlsx: an Excel workbook. both: the md and xlsx files. --output, -o Directory or file path for file output (default: the current directory). A directory receives i18n-audit.md / i18n-audit.xlsx; a path ending in .md or .xlsx is used as given. --duplicates, -d Also report keys sharing the same value (case-insensitive), grouped by how many of the four languages share it: 🔴 all four, 🟠 three, 🟡 two, 🟢 one.

The key-usage verdicts below are part of the Markdown output only (terminal or .md file). The workbook holds the translation table, the missing translations, a coverage summary and, with --duplicates, one sheet per tier. The command exits with status 1 when a key the backend assigns in a metadata field (message_i18n_key="…", label_key="…", an x-i18n-key schema entry) is missing from the catalogue, or when the sources break a rule of the strict check (Source problems in the summary); unused keys never fail it.

docs.title: 🧾 What the Audit Reports
docs.text:
Besides coverage (keys missing in some languages) and the optional duplicates, the audit gives every catalogue key one of three verdicts. The classifier is classify() in scripts/i18n_usage.py, called by generate_unused_keys_report() in frontend/scripts/i18n-audit.py.

Verdict Meaning Report section used Proven by the evidence below. not listed not verified Under a real dynamic family, or only under a legacy truncated prefix (listed as Dynamic prefixes detected): the final segment is built at runtime and named nowhere. Not evidence of death. 🔵 Not Verified dead No evidence anywhere. The only actionable list. ❌ Likely Unused

How the evidence is gathered:

  • Product sources only: *.svelte, *.ts and *.js under frontend/src/, plus the Python sources of backend/app/. Tests prove nothing: *.test.ts, *.spec.ts (and their .js twins), anything under __tests__/ or __mocks__/. Generated clients are skipped too, even where a source imports them: ./dev.py api sync writes generated.ts, generated-tools.ts and *.generated.ts into frontend/src/lib/api/ and git ignores them, so a verdict resting on them would change on a fresh clone. The backend they are generated from is read directly anyway.
  • Any whole-key literal counts, whatever receives it: wrappers such as translateOr($_, 'k', …), label('k', …) or tr('k', …), props such as afterCopyKey: 'k'. Backend literals count too: dictionaries, ..._i18n_key= fields.
  • Templates are expanded: string constants (`${NS}.leaf`), literal conditionals (cond ? 'a.b' : 'a.c'), typed unions and single-literal parameter types (prefix: 'errors'), nested templates, camelCase continuations (`…scheduler.historyDays${day}`) and 'ns.' + code concatenations. A final segment built at runtime leaves a family; backend f-strings such as f"aiExport.additionalData.reason.{reason}" are families too.
  • Family members are proven by the producer's vocabulary or by what the file building the family names (titleKey: values, the values of an indexed map). The vocabulary is the backend's string literals, and a member also matches a code spelling it in capitals or in lower case (IN_TRANSIT proves brokers.lots.modal.state.in_transit); a code may begin with a digit ("3m" proves aiExport.additionalData.period.3m), but a number or a sentence is no code. A narrow family, at least two segments deep (risk.assetSet.band.) or a camelCase continuation, also accepts the words its file quotes and those of the modules that file imports directly, in any form (static, type-only, re-export, dynamic import()) with a relative or $lib specifier: CorrelationHeatmap.svelte builds `risk.assetSet.band.${band}` and the band names live in the correlationHelpers.ts it imports. One hop only: a word two imports away, or in a neighbouring module the file does not import, proves nothing, and a wide family (`ns.${x}`) reads no import.
  • Shapes: a template with several runtime segments, or with one before a literal tail (`assets.providerParams.${code}.${kind}.${field.key}`, `assets.panels.${panel.id}Hint`), keeps its shape. Each runtime segment becomes a slot of exactly one segment, and a segment that resolves (a constant, a union such as kind: 'label' | 'description') takes only its values. A key with that shape is used when every slot is a word of the building file or of a module it imports directly, or a backend code. One slot named nowhere leaves the key not verified, a key with an extra segment does not match, and a template without a dotted literal head (`${a}.${b}`) has no shape: any two quoted words would make a key.
  • 👻 Backend Families Without Catalogue Keys lists the prefixes the backend builds inside an existing namespace but with no catalogue key under them. It is informational and never counts as unused.
  • 📦 Kept Alive Only by Unreferenced Sources lists the keys whose verdict would weaken without the sources no SvelteKit entry reaches, each followed by the verdict it would then get (→ dead or → not verified), then every unreferenced source: a file nothing reaches renders nothing, yet still proves the keys it reads. The entries are the route files under frontend/src/routes/ (+page, +layout, +error.svelte, +server, .server variants and layout resets such as +page@.svelte included), the hooks at the root of frontend/src/ (hooks.ts, hooks.server.ts, hooks.client.ts) and the service worker; reachability follows every import form listed above, dynamic import() included. A .d.ts file is never reported, and a test is no source, so a component imported only by tests is unreferenced. The section appears only when some key depends on such a source. It is informational, never counts as unused and changes no verdict: decide whether the source is dead, then remove it with its keys.

docs.title: 🛡️ Gates
docs.text: Unit What it holds ./dev.py test utils gate-i18n-catalog The library's rules, each proven both ways on synthetic trees, and the repository's sources: a strict merge, the four languages, the generator's format, the ignore rules, and no generated file tracked beside base/ (backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_i18n_catalog_gate.py). ./dev.py test utils gate-plugin-i18n-ownership Each plugin's keys in its own fragment, judged by the metadata its registry publishes: see The Ownership Gate. ./dev.py test utils gate-i18n-usage The audit's three-verdict classifier, scripts/i18n_usage.py (see What the Audit Reports).

docs.title: 🚧 Known Limits
docs.text:
• A plugin mounted at runtime has no translations (U-B1). The fragments are merged when the frontend is built, so a plugin added with a docker-compose volume has its code but not its keys, and the UI shows its untranslated fallback.
  • The development server does not watch the sources (U-B6). npm run dev generates the catalogue when it starts; a source you edit by hand reaches it only after ./dev.py i18n build. The dev.py i18n commands rebuild by themselves.
  • add does not know the plugins' spaces (U-B7). Without --into, the first key of a new signal or Tool lands in a subsystem (charts, tools), and so does the first settings key of an FX provider (pluginSettings); only utils gate-plugin-i18n-ownership catches it: always pass --into <family>/<plugin> for a plugin's keys.

docs.title: 🧭 Onboarding Guides
docs.text:
LibreFolio 1.2 adds a guided onboarding: a Welcome setup for new accounts, a short intro tour of the navigation, and contextual guides that start the first time a user reaches a page, an Add modal, a detail view, the Import Wizard or the bulk workspace. A guide is a sequence of coachmarks pointing at real controls. The server keeps one versioned status per user and flow; the browser remembers where an unfinished guide stopped.

This page explains how the system is built, for developers who add or change a guide. What users see is described in Getting Started and User Preferences.

docs.title: 🧱 Ground rules
docs.text:
1. The guide observes; it never acts. It may scroll its target into view, and the intro tour moves to /dashboard and opens the sidebar for its stops, but nothing in the system clicks, fills or saves for the user. When a step advances on a click of its target, the click still reaches the control: the coachmark only listens to it. The guideAnchor action registers nodes and does nothing else (guideAnchors.test.ts checks it).
  2. Anchor only what is rendered. A registered anchor that is hidden counts as absent and stalls the step (Anchors and stalls).
  3. A step describes its own section or control. It never announces that another guide will start. guideCopy.test.ts scans every step text of the overlay host, in all four languages, for the words that name a guide or a tour; a mention that describes rather than announces is added to its REGISTRY, with a reason.
  4. Pages talk to the engine, not to the stored state. Starting, finishing, skipping and replaying go through onboardingGuide; persistence, resume, stall handling and the cross-tab close all live behind it.

docs.title: 🗺️ The sixteen flows
docs.text:
The flows are the OnboardingFlow enum in backend/app/db/models.py, mirrored by ONBOARDING_FLOWS in frontend/src/lib/types/onboarding.ts. welcome is a page of its own; the other fifteen are guided flows, declared in ONBOARDING_GUIDE_CATALOG (frontend/src/lib/features/onboarding/onboardingGuideCatalog.ts).

Flow Kind Starts when Steps welcome Setup page the layout gate redirects to /welcome — intro_tour Tour Welcome hands off, or the layout settles on a page 9 transactions_page_guide Page /transactions has loaded 4 transaction_create_guide Modal the transaction form opens in create mode 4 transaction_bulk_guide Step-managed the bulk workspace reaches each milestone 4 import_guide Step-managed the Import Wizard shows each step; the last one in the bulk editor 9 broker_page_guide Page /brokers has loaded 4 broker_guide Modal the Add Broker modal opens 3 broker_detail_guide Detail /brokers/[id] has loaded its broker 5 fx_page_guide Page /fx has loaded 4 fx_guide Modal the add-pair modal opens 2 fx_detail_guide Detail /fx/[pair] has initialized 4 asset_page_guide Page /assets has loaded 4 asset_guide Modal the add-asset modal opens 3 asset_detail_guide Detail /assets/[id] has loaded its asset 5 tools_page_guide Page /tools has answered its catalog 2

Kind is descriptive. The catalogue itself knows three fields: trigger (automatic for the tour, contextual for every other guide), completionMode: 'steps' for the two step-managed flows, and navigationMode: 'checkpoint' for the bulk workspace. Every flow is at version 1 in ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS (backend/app/services/accounts/onboarding_service.py).

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    Login["🔐 Login"] --> Load["🚪 (app)/+layout.svelte<br>appBootstrap.load()"]
    Load -.->|"GET progress"| API[("🗄️ /api/v1/settings/onboarding")]
    Load -->|"blocked"| Block["⛔ OnboardingBootstrapBlock<br>Retry / Log out"]
    Load -->|"ready / degraded"| Resolve{"resolveDestination()"}
    Resolve -->|"Welcome due<br>or replay armed"| Welcome["👋 /welcome?returnTo=…"]
    Resolve -->|"otherwise"| Page["📄 Requested page"]
    Welcome -->|"complete / skip"| API
    Welcome -->|"Continue / Skip"| Intro["🎬 maybeStartIntro()"]
    Page -->|"route settled"| Intro
    Page -->|"page, modal or detail ready"| Contextual["📍 maybeStartContextual(flow)"]
    Intro --> Host["🖼️ OnboardingOverlayHost<br>intro scene or coachmark"]
    Contextual --> Host
    Host -->|"position at every step"| Storage[("💾 localStorage")]
    Host -->|"automatic Finish / X"| API

Frontend paths below are relative to frontend/src/.

Module Role lib/types/onboarding.ts Flow list, wire types, the "due" predicates lib/features/onboarding/onboardingApi.ts Client for the endpoints, with strict Zod schemas lib/stores/app/onboarding.svelte.ts Controller: server progress, plus the positions stored in localStorage lib/features/onboarding/onboardingGuideCatalog.ts Step ids and flow definitions lib/features/onboarding/onboardingGuide.svelte.ts The engine, singleton onboardingGuide: start, step, finish, skip, replay, queue lib/features/onboarding/guideAnchors.svelte.ts Anchor registry and the guideAnchor action lib/features/onboarding/appBootstrap.svelte.ts Bootstrap loads and the Welcome redirect rule; starts the open-registration warning lib/features/onboarding/onboardingRouteSettlement.ts Applies the redirect, or starts the tour, once per settled route lib/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingOverlayHost.svelte Presentation table of every step; renders the intro scene or the single coachmark lib/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingCoachmark.svelte Measures the anchor; spotlight, pointer, panel placement, waiting and stalled states lib/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingReplaySection.svelte The replay list in Settings lib/features/onboarding/components/DeferredAppPopups.svelte Holds automatic popups while a guide runs routes/(app)/welcome/+page.svelte The Welcome route, rendering WelcomePage.svelte and WelcomeForm.svelte

Each of these singletons resets its in-memory state when the signed-in account changes, through registerClientSessionReset (lib/stores/app/clientSession.ts).

Tour surfaces are not wired

lib/features/onboarding/onboardingTourSurfaces.svelte.ts keeps preview handlers for the create modals (brokers.create, fx.create, assets.create). Only its unit test exercises it: no component registers a handler, and no guide step requests one.

docs.title: 🚪 From login to the first guide
docs.text:
The (app) route group renders on the client only (routes/(app)/+layout.ts sets ssr = false). Once the auth check succeeds, routes/(app)/+layout.svelte runs appBootstrap.load(): user settings, onboarding progress and global settings load in parallel, and the bootstrap settles on one state.

State When The layout renders blocked user settings failed, or progress failed and no completed or skipped Welcome was loaded before OnboardingBootstrapBlock, with a retry and a logout button degraded progress failed, but a completed or skipped Welcome was already loaded the app, with OnboardingBootstrapBanner and its retry button ready everything loaded the app

Before the loaders, as soon as load() knows the user — right after its guard on the user id, and before it returns early for a user already loaded — it calls startOpenRegistrationNotice(), a dependency of createAppBootstrap() like the loaders. The default calls the open-registration warning's startOpenRegistrationNotice() without arguments and ignores the stop function it returns. So the warning starts even when a loader fails or hangs, and never without a user. Every load() may call it: only the first start watches.

appBootstrap.resolveDestination() turns the requested path into a destination. While Welcome is due — or a Welcome replay is armed — every app route resolves to /welcome?returnTo=<requested path>; once it is not, /welcome resolves back to its returnTo, or to /dashboard. Only same-origin absolute paths are accepted as returnTo.

lib/features/onboarding/onboardingRouteSettlement.ts acts on that destination once per route snapshot (state, path, destination): it navigates with replaceState when the destination differs, and otherwise starts the intro tour (onboardingGuide.maybeStartIntro()). The initial load owns the settlement; the layout's reactive gate claims only snapshots that were not handled yet, and never while the load owns it. The layout is a legacy (non-runes) component, so it reads appBootstrap.ready through toStore(): that is what makes its $: gate re-run when the bootstrap settles. routes/(app)/layout.gate.test.ts pins it — while a redirect is pending, the layout shows onboarding-redirecting, never the requested page.

docs.title: 👋 Welcome
docs.text:
routes/(app)/welcome/+page.svelte renders the form: language, base currency and avatar, pre-filled from the user's settings. A new account's settings row is created by its first GET /api/v1/settings/user (get_or_create_user_settings in backend/app/services/accounts/settings_service.py) from the instance defaults default_language, default_currency and default_theme, so Welcome starts from the administrator's choices, as its hint says (onboarding.welcome.defaultsHint). Changing the language previews it immediately; skipping restores the saved one.

  • Continue completes the flow with the choices attached (welcome_settings); complete_welcome_onboarding() saves the settings and the completion in one transaction.
  • Skip setup permanently skips the flow and saves no setting.
  • In a replay, Continue saves through PUT /api/v1/settings/user and leaves the onboarding status alone; Exit tour saves nothing.

Every path ends in onboardingGuide.maybeStartIntro(returnTo): the page then moves to /dashboard if the tour starts, and to returnTo otherwise.

Under its card, WelcomePage.svelte shows the instance's legal notice, LegalNotice (F09). It frames the page and is not part of the flow, with no anchor and no step: adding it changed no version in ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS, so the Welcome did not come back for anyone.

docs.title: 🎬 Intro tour
docs.text:
intro_tour opens with intro.scene, a full-screen scene (OnboardingIntroScene.svelte) that plays three phrases and starts the tour on Start tour, or by itself after 8 seconds. Eight coachmark stops follow, all on navigation controls: intro.navigation (the sidebar toggle), then intro.dashboard, intro.transactions_nav, intro.brokers_nav, intro.fx_nav, intro.assets_nav, intro.tools_nav and intro.settings_nav, anchored on the sidebar links (nav.dashboard, nav.transactions, …, derived from each link's href in lib/components/layout/Sidebar.svelte).

During the tour the overlay host keeps the user on /dashboard and opens the sidebar (the mobile drawer) for the stops that point into it, while the layout makes the app shell inert (data-guide-inert="true"), so the page behind the tour cannot be operated. Finish and X both lead to the returnTo that Welcome received, or to /dashboard.

docs.title: 📍 Contextual guides
docs.text:
A page, modal or detail view starts its guide with onboardingGuide.maybeStartContextual(flow) once its content is ready: routes/(app)/brokers/+page.svelte calls it at the end of onMount, after loadBrokers(), and the detail pages wait until their broker, pair or asset has loaded. The engine starts the guide only if the flow is due (resuming at a stored position when there is one) or if a replay is armed for it (Progress and positions).

Around the host, a few calls keep the state consistent:

  • Opening an Add modal from a page guide — the page dismisses its own guide first (dismissHost()), which keeps its position, then starts the modal's guide.
  • Closing a modal — dismissHost({restartAtFirst: true}) rewinds a linear guide to its first step, so the next opening starts over. Step-managed flows ignore the rewind.
  • Leaving the host route — each step declares a hostRoute: an exact path, or a prefix when it ends with /, as '/brokers/' for broker details. On any other route the overlay host suspends the guide on its current step; coming back resumes it there.
  • Another guide is running — the request is queued, and maybeStartQueued() starts it later; the overlay host calls it right after suspending a guide whose route was left.
  • A nested dialog — every modal built on lib/components/ui/modals/ModalBase.svelte bumps document.body.dataset.modalScrollLockCount. While that depth exceeds the step's allowedModalDepth (0 for page steps, 1 or 2 inside modals), the coachmark is hidden but the guide stays active.

On contextual steps whose pointer is 'cursor', clicking the real target also advances the guide: to the next step, to the end on the last step, or completing the current step of a step-managed flow. The coachmark's X reads Skip this tour in an automatic guide and Exit tour in a replay; both call onboardingGuide.exit(), an alias of skip().

The presentation table of OnboardingOverlayHost.svelte follows one convention: a step that explains an area spreads areaPresentation (highlight: 'pulse', a pulsing green frame), a step on a control the user can try sets pointer: 'cursor' (a bouncing cursor over its centre), and no contextual step uses both. The intro stops spread corePresentation (cursor, pulse and backdrop), the Import steps spread importPresentation (cursor, panel on top, scrollPolicy: 'none').

docs.title: 🧩 Step-managed flows
docs.text:
import_guide and transaction_bulk_guide declare completionMode: 'steps'. The server tracks each of their steps, an automatic guide completes or skips one step at a time, and the owning component decides which step is current: ImportWizardModal.svelte calls startImportAt() as the wizard moves, and TransactionBulkModal.svelte queues each Bulk step when the workspace reaches the matching milestone. The engine's next() and previous() do nothing for these flows. Bulk is also a checkpoint flow (navigationMode: 'checkpoint'): no progress counter, no Back, and a Got it button.

Finishing or skipping touches the current step only (completeStep() or skipStep() on the controller), never the steps the component did not reach. A step a clean import never shows — import.assets, import.fix, import.duplicates, import.gapFix — therefore stays pending, and its flow with it, until an import reaches it: that is why the Settings list can show the Import guide as Pending after a first import.

The Import guide's wiring, including its hand-off to the bulk editor for import.bulk, is documented with the wizard in Onboarding: the contextual import guide.

docs.title: 🎯 Anchors and stalls
docs.text:
A step targets an anchor id, never a CSS selector. Components register the element with the guideAnchor action, next to the test id that tests use (trimmed from routes/(app)/brokers/+page.svelte):

<button data-testid="add-broker-button" use:guideAnchor={'broker.page.add'} on:click={openCreateModal}>

The registry (lib/features/onboarding/guideAnchors.svelte.ts) maps each id to one element, the last one registered. It forgets elements that left the DOM, accepts several ids on one node (use:guideAnchor={['a', 'b']}) and is cleared when the account changes. The steps table of OnboardingOverlayHost.svelte maps every step id to its anchor id.

OnboardingCoachmark.svelte then decides whether the anchor is usable:

  • Absent — not registered, disconnected, 0×0 (display:none, a box-less wrapper), or failing checkVisibility({visibilityProperty: true}) (visibility:hidden). Opacity does not count: hover-revealed controls start transparent.
  • Settled — the anchor's box is identical on two consecutive frames. From then on the coachmark follows resizes, scrolling and CSS transitions.
  • Waiting, then stalled — while the anchor is absent, the panel is centred and reads Waiting for this area to become available…. After GUIDE_STALL_MS (3 s) the step stalls: the panel says the area did not load in time, and the primary button becomes Continue anyway. In a step-managed flow that button skips the step, which was never really shown; elsewhere it behaves as Next or Finish. The countdown does not run while a nested dialog suspends the step.

Two more rules keep the page readable behind the panel:

  • Moving targets — while a settled target scrolls, resizes or runs a CSS transition, the geometry is revalidating: the step keeps its text and spotlight instead of falling back to the waiting message. Only a target that loses its box returns to waiting.
  • Panel fade — PANEL_FADE_MS (3 s) after a step appears, the panel turns translucent (bg-white/80 with backdrop-blur-sm). It is opaque again while the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, the timer restarts at every step, and a stalled or suspended step does not fade.

With the default scrollPolicy: 'nearest-if-hidden', the coachmark scrolls only when the target is outside its scroll container or under the app header; an element marked data-guide-scroll-root (the Import Wizard body, the transaction form) is used as that container. For tests, the coachmark root (data-testid="onboarding-coachmark") exposes data-step-id and data-guide-state (waiting, anchored, stalled, error). It also carries data-geometry-state (waiting, revalidating, stable), and the panel (onboarding-coachmark-panel) carries data-subdued. The complete rules, and the page-author rule for tabs and collapsed panels, are in Anchor presence and stalls.

docs.title: 📱 Desktop and mobile
docs.text:
OnboardingOverlayHost.svelte switches to its mobile variant below 1024 px (matchMedia('(max-width: 1023px)')):

  • intro.navigation targets nav.toggle.mobile, the header's menu button, instead of nav.toggle.desktop, the sidebar's collapse button. Both stay registered (guideAnchors.test.ts checks that they coexist), and the host picks one by viewport.
  • A step may set mobilePanelPlacement beside panelPlacement. The panel tries the preferred side first, then the side with the most room, avoiding the target, and is centred as a last resort.

The guide walks in frontend/e2e/onboarding-guides.spec.ts run on both a desktop and a mobile viewport.

docs.title: 💾 Progress and positions
docs.text: Two stores cooperate. The server keeps, per user and flow, whether the guide is still due. The browser keeps where an unfinished guide currently is.

docs.title: 📏 When a guide is due
docs.text:
Each progress row has a status (pending, completed, skipped) and the version the user went through; the API adds current_version (from ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS) and update_available (version < current_version). The frontend rule, isOnboardingProgressDue() in lib/types/onboarding.ts, is:

progress.status === 'pending' || progress.version < progress.current_version

A guide therefore starts by itself while it is pending, and again after its version is bumped, even if the user completed or skipped the older version. A completed or skipped guide at the current version never starts by itself: the user can replay it from Settings. Step-managed flows apply the same rule to each step (isOnboardingStepProgressDue()).

Every complete or skip request carries the expected_version the client rendered. The server answers 409 (onboarding_version_mismatch) when it differs from the current version, so a client that rendered other content cannot record it as seen.

A version bump reaches every account

A bumped flow becomes due for every account whose row is at an older version, including the accounts older than 1.2.0, which were seeded skipped at version 1 (Accounts older than 1.2.0). Bump only when users should really see the guide again.

docs.title: 🗂️ Positions in this browser
docs.text:
The controller (lib/stores/app/onboarding.svelte.ts) saves the active guide's position in localStorage when the guide starts and at every step change, under one key per account, flow and content version:

lf_{userId}_onboarding_replay_{flow}_v{version}

The value records the step id, the mode (automatic or replay), the steps left in a step-managed replay, and the returnTo. From that key:

  • A guide resumes at the step it left. A reload or a closed tab loses only the in-memory guide; its next trigger reads the key and resumes there. A step id that no longer exists falls back to the first step, and an unreadable value is deleted.
  • Logging out keeps it. An account change resets the in-memory state only (createOnboardingSessionResetter); the keys stay, and the same account resumes after logging in again on this browser. Keys are never shared across accounts, browsers or devices.
  • A version bump drops it. Reading or writing a flow's key removes that flow's keys for every other version.
  • A guide that ends in one tab closes in the others. All tabs share the keys. Ending a guide — finishing it, skipping it, or cancelling an armed replay — deletes its key, and the storage listener registered at the bottom of onboardingGuide.svelte.ts (createReplayStorageListener) makes every other tab drop its copy and close the step, so a stale tab cannot write the key back. The browser's storage event is the whole mechanism; there is no BroadcastChannel.

docs.title: 🔁 Replays from Settings
docs.text:
OnboardingReplaySection.svelte, the Onboarding category of the Preferences tab, lists the flows in groups written by hand (setup, core, transactions, broker, fx, asset):

  • Welcome — arms a Welcome replay and opens /welcome; the gate redirects there while it is armed.
  • Quick tour — starts at once, in replay mode, on /dashboard.
  • Any other guide — Replay at next trigger only arms the key in replay mode; the guide starts the next time its page or modal calls the engine. An armed replay can be cancelled.
  • Replay all — arms every flow, then opens /welcome.

A replay never calls the onboarding complete or skip endpoints: its Finish and X only update or delete the stored key, so the server status does not change. The Settings components are documented in Settings.

docs.title: 🔕 Deferred popups
docs.text:
The layout mounts DeferredAppPopups.svelte, which owns the popups nobody asked for, one at a time and in this order: What's new (lot C-54), the donation prompt and the update-available modal. It holds them while a guide is active or any modal is open, and shows the next one when both are gone; the host says which one shows in data-active-popup (whats-new, donation, update or none). A prompt the user did ask for — a manual update check, shown with updateAvailable.show(release, {requested: true}) — appears at once, above a guide or a modal.

The backend decides the donation prompt at sign-in: record_login_and_maybe_show_popup() (backend/app/services/accounts/donation_popup_service.py) counts the login and sets show_donation_popup in the login response (login() and setup_admin() in backend/app/api/v1/auth.py). Counting from the last prompt, or from the account's creation if there was none, it fires after MAX_DAYS_WITHOUT_PROMPT (60) days, or after MIN_LOGINS_BETWEEN_PROMPTS (10) sign-ins once MIN_DAYS_BETWEEN_PROMPTS (7) days have passed. On a managed instance it never fires: is_donation_popup_disabled() is always true with LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed (F05), and the login counters still advance (./dev.py test services donation-managed). Nor does the update-available modal come there by itself: the check at an administrator's sign-in probes only a self-hosted instance (Container Image Check). DonationPopupModal.svelte has no close button and ignores backdrop clicks and Esc (closeOnBackdropClick={false}, closeOnEscape={false}): only Buy Me a Coffee and Maybe later dismiss it, and a share button opens the share dialog above it.

docs.title: ✨ What's new since your last version
docs.text:
After an update, each signed-in user sees once the chapters of the changelog released since the version whose changelog they saw last (lot C-54). It is the same in both profiles; on a managed instance, where no update check runs, it is how users hear of an update. The user's side: «What's new after an update» in Changelog Modal.

  • The backend says whether, and from which release. users.last_seen_version holds a base release X.Y.Z (USER). whats_new_service.pending_for(user) (backend/app/services/accounts/whats_new_service.py) compares it with current_release(), the base release of config.get_version(): release_of() reads v1.3.0-7-gabc1234 and 1.3.0-rc1 as 1.3.0, 1.3 as 1.3.0, and finds no release in unknown, dev, a bare hash or a base of 0.0.0, which is how get_git_version() reports a checkout with no tag (v0.0.0-g<hash>). A pre-release thus counts as its release: an account that closed the window on 1.3.0-rc1 does not see the 1.3.0 chapter again at the final release, even if that chapter grew in between — acceptable for the instances that run release candidates (E's review of C-54). Every answer that carries the user — POST /auth/login, GET /auth/me, POST /auth/register, PUT /auth/profile and POST /auth/setup — puts the result in user.whats_new (WhatsNewRead, {since, release}), through _auth_user() in backend/app/api/v1/auth.py; since is null for a NULL column, an account from before the feature, which sees the release chapter alone. user.whats_new is null when nothing is newer than what the user saw, a downgrade included; when the running version names no release, a checkout with no tag included, where create_user() therefore writes nothing; and when whats_new_disabled() says so, a hidden switch like the donation prompt's (decision D-A7), which the test lanes turn on (Automated Setup).
  • A new account has nothing to catch up on. user_service.create_user() writes the running release into last_seen_version.
  • Closing the window records it. POST /api/v1/auth/whats-new/seen (204, a session required, idempotent) calls mark_seen(), which writes the server's own running release, never a value from the client, and logs What's new seen (user_id, release) when it changes the column. With the running release unknown it writes nothing. It never goes backwards: it reads the account again under SQLite's write lock, and a stored release as new as the running one or newer — a downgrade, an older worker of a rolling update — stays as it is (E's note on C-54, WN-MONO and WNAPI-MONO).
  • The app picks the chapters. whatsNewChapters(chapters, whatsNew) (lib/features/changelog/whatsNew.ts) keeps the released chapters of the bundled changelog with since < version ≤ release, or the release chapter alone when since is null, never [Unreleased], in the changelog's order, newest first. Versions compare as numbers, with the update check's compareVersions().
  • The store. whatsNew (lib/features/changelog/whatsNewStore.svelte.ts) reads user.whats_new from the auth store. shouldShow holds while a user is signed in, the window was not closed on this page load, and at least one chapter matches: a whats_new that names no bundled chapter shows nothing, and records nothing. dismiss() hides the window at once and posts; a failed POST is only logged, and the window comes back at the next page load, since the server still says it. The closed flag is reset when the client session ends (registerClientSessionReset).
  • The window. WhatsNewModal.svelte (whats-new-modal): the title changelog.whatsNew.title; the intro changelog.whatsNew.intro, or changelog.whatsNew.introRelease with the version when since is null; one whats-new-chapter per chapter, its version in data-version, in the interface language when the bundle translates it (localizedChangelog, loaded as ChangelogModal loads it), in English otherwise, with the pill changelog.notTranslated (whats-new-not-translated); the Markdown rendered by marked and passed through sanitizeHtml() at the {@html} sink itself, as the htmlSink gate requires; whats-new-full-changelog (changelog.whatsNew.fullChangelog), the changelog on GitHub in a new tab, rel="noopener noreferrer"; whats-new-close (changelog.whatsNew.close, Got it). Every close — the button, Esc, the backdrop — calls dismiss(). The window uses colour roles only, and ChangelogModal is unchanged.
  • Tests. ./dev.py test services whats-new (test_services/test_whats_new_service.py, WN-001 to WN-010: the base release, the switch, pending_for(), create_user(), mark_seen()) and ./dev.py test api whats-new (test_api/test_whats_new_api.py, WN-API-01 to WN-API-07, in-process: user.whats_new in the answers, the POST). ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs whatsNew.test.ts (WN-01 to WN-11) and whatsNewStore.test.ts (WNS-00 to WNS-12), component-unit runs WhatsNewModal.test.ts (WNM-01 to WNM-10), and onboarding-component-unit runs DeferredAppPopups.test.ts (DAP-WN-01 to DAP-WN-05: first of the three, then the next one once closed; held by a guide or a modal; under a requested update, interrupted and not dismissed). ./dev.py test front-utility whats-new (frontend/e2e/layout/whats-new.spec.ts, WNE-01 to WNE-06, both profiles) answers GET /auth/me with the real response and its user.whats_new replaced, and POST /auth/whats-new/seen itself, so it never writes a shared test user.

docs.title: 🗄️ Backend
docs.text:
backend/app/services/accounts/onboarding_service.py holds the registry and the transitions:

Name Role ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS Current content version of each flow ONBOARDING_FLOW_STEPS Step ids of the step-managed flows (transaction_bulk_guide, import_guide) get_onboarding_progress() Inserts any missing flow or step row as pending (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, never rewriting stored progress), then returns every flow in registry order transition_onboarding_progress() Completes or skips a flow; on a step-managed flow, applies the status to every registered step transition_onboarding_step_progress() Completes or skips one step, then recomputes its flow complete_welcome_onboarding() Saves the Welcome settings and completes welcome in one transaction reset_onboarding_progress() Puts every flow of a user, or one, back to pending, steps included, clearing completed_at and skipped_at; for administrators: POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/onboarding/reset (Administrator API) and ./dev.py user reset-onboarding

A step-managed flow stays pending until every registered step is terminal at the current version; it then becomes skipped if all its steps were skipped, and completed otherwise.

Rows live in user_onboarding_progress (one per user and flow) and user_onboarding_step_progress (one per user, flow and step), both deleted with their user; see Users & Access. The flow column is a plain string without a CHECK on its values, so a new flow needs no schema change.

docs.title: 🔌 Endpoints
docs.text:
Declared in backend/app/api/v1/settings.py, for the signed-in user:

Method Path Body GET /api/v1/settings/onboarding — POST /api/v1/settings/onboarding/{flow}/complete expected_version; welcome_settings for welcome only POST /api/v1/settings/onboarding/{flow}/skip expected_version POST /api/v1/settings/onboarding/{flow}/steps/{step_id}/complete expected_version POST /api/v1/settings/onboarding/{flow}/steps/{step_id}/skip expected_version

A version mismatch answers 409 with code, flow, expected_version and current_version. welcome_settings anywhere but the Welcome completion, or a step the flow does not register, answers 422. The frontend client, lib/features/onboarding/onboardingApi.ts, validates responses with strict Zod schemas that list the flows explicitly: a flow the client does not know makes the progress load fail, so the backend and frontend lists change together.

docs.title: 👴 Accounts older than 1.2.0
docs.text:
Migration backend/alembic/versions/004_release_1_2_0_schema.py creates both tables and seeds every user that exists when it runs: welcome as completed, because their settings are already configured, and the other fourteen flows as skipped, with skipped rows for the steps it lists (four Bulk steps, eight Import steps). skipped silences the triggers like completed while recording that the guide was never shown, so the guides can still be offered later — by a version bump, for instance.

Accounts created afterwards get nothing from the migration. Their rows appear as pending on the first progress read, so a new user lands on Welcome, pre-filled with the administrator's defaults (Welcome).

The seed lists are frozen

The migration lists flows and steps in literal SQL; it does not read the service registry. Anything registered later — a new flow, or a new step of a step-managed flow — reaches older accounts as pending through the lazy insert, like everybody else. import.gapFix is such a step: the migration seeds the other eight Import steps. Keeping a later addition from older accounts takes a migration of its own.

Test accounts. On a fresh test database the migration runs before the E2E users exist, so _grandfather_onboarding_for_test_users (backend/test_scripts/test_db/populate_mock_data.py) marks the canonical users — among them e2e_test_admin and e2e_test_empty, which the gallery logs in with — completed on every flow and step, at its current version. Guide specs never walk them: frontend/e2e/fixtures/onboarding-accounts.ts registers a disposable account, takes it through the real Welcome, closes the intro scene, skips over the API every due flow except the ones under test, and provides deleteDisposableUser() to remove it at the end.

docs.title: 🆕 A new guide
docs.text:
1. Backend registry — add the flow to OnboardingFlow (backend/app/db/models.py) and to ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS at version 1; a step-managed flow also lists its steps in ONBOARDING_FLOW_STEPS.
  2. Frontend flow lists — ONBOARDING_FLOWS (lib/types/onboarding.ts) and the flow enum in onboardingApi.ts.
  3. Catalogue — a …_STEP_IDS constant and an ONBOARDING_GUIDE_CATALOG entry in onboardingGuideCatalog.ts: trigger: 'contextual', plus completionMode or navigationMode when needed.
  4. Presentation — one entry per step in the steps table of OnboardingOverlayHost.svelte: anchorId, titleKey and descriptionKey as string literals (the copy gate reads them from the source), hostRoute, allowedModalDepth, and optionally pointer, highlight, panelPlacement, mobilePanelPlacement and scrollPolicy.
  5. Anchors — use:guideAnchor on elements that are actually rendered for their step.
  6. Trigger — call onboardingGuide.maybeStartContextual(flow) when the page or modal is ready. For a modal, dismiss the page guide before opening it, and call dismissHost({restartAtFirst: true}) when it closes.
  7. Settings — add the flow to its group in OnboardingReplaySection.svelte; a step-managed flow also adds its steps to stepTitleKeys there.
  8. Copy, in four languages — the flow name under onboarding.flows.<flow>, and each step's title and description under onboarding.<guide>.steps.<step>, for example onboarding.brokerPageGuide.steps.add.title. The dev.py i18n commands are in Internationalization.
  9. Older accounts — by default the new flow is pending for everybody, including accounts older than 1.2.0 (above); hiding it from them needs a migration.
  10. User docs — the guide groups in User Preferences.

docs.title: ✏️ Changing a guide
docs.text:
• Content users should see again — increment the flow in ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS. The frontend reads current_version from the server, so the bump is a backend change, plus the pinned registry test below. Positions stored for the old version are dropped on their next read.
  • A wording fix that should not re-show the guide — leave the version alone.
  • A new step — add it to the catalogue and to the presentation table. In a linear guide, only users for whom the guide is still due see it automatically, unless you bump the version. In a step-managed flow, also add it to ONBOARDING_FLOW_STEPS: every account then receives it as a pending step on its next progress read.

docs.title: 🧪 Tests
docs.text:
File What it pins backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_settings_service.py The registry: exactly sixteen flows, the two step lists, every flow at version 1. Update it when you add a flow or bump a version backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_settings_api.py The endpoints, including the exact flow and step arrays of the progress read backend/test_scripts/test_db/db_schema_validate.py Migration 004 and its grandfathered rows backend/test_scripts/test_db/test_db_referential_integrity.py The canonical E2E users, completed on every flow and step frontend/src/lib/stores/app/onboarding.test.ts Controller, API contract (ONBOARDING_FLOWS pinned by hand), storage keys, cross-tab drop, bootstrap, including the start of the open-registration warning (before the loaders, also when they fail, never without a user) frontend/src/lib/features/onboarding/guideAnchors.test.ts Anchor registry and action frontend/src/lib/features/onboarding/guideCopy.test.ts No step text announces another guide frontend/src/lib/features/onboarding/onboardingRouteSettlement.test.ts Welcome redirect or tour start, exactly once frontend/src/routes/(app)/layout.gate.test.ts The layout gate follows the bootstrap frontend/src/lib/features/onboarding/components/*.test.ts Coachmark geometry and stalls, intro scene, replay section, deferred popups, Welcome and its legal notice (WelcomePage.legal.test.ts) frontend/e2e/onboarding-guides.spec.ts Broker, FX and Asset guides walked to completion on desktop and mobile; pause and resume across routes; positions across tabs and logout frontend/e2e/onboarding-tour.spec.ts Intro-tour order and Transactions overview geometry, scroll clearance, the Import and Bulk step interplay

Some E2E specs list the flows by hand, frontend/e2e/settings.spec.ts and frontend/e2e/transactions/tx-import-flow.spec.ts among them: when you add a flow, search frontend/e2e/ for an existing flow id.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: LibreFolio is installable as a Progressive Web App (PWA). This page documents the technical implementation for developers.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ app.html                                         │
│  ├── viewport meta (no-zoom, viewport-fit)       │
│  ├── manifest link                               │
│  ├── Apple meta tags + apple-touch-icon link     │
│  ├── theme-color                                 │
│  ├── early beforeinstallprompt capture           │
│  └── Service Worker registration                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ static/manifest.json                             │
│  └── display: standalone, icons, colors          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ static/sw.js                                     │
│  ├── offline fallback (navigate fail → cache)    │
│  └── // build: <md5(offline.html)[:8]> stamp     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ static/offline.html                              │
│  └── branded fallback page (i18n, dark mode)     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ static/icons/ (generated by dev.py)              │
│  ├── icon-192.png           (any, white)         │
│  ├── icon-512.png           (any, white)         │
│  ├── icon-maskable-192.png  (maskable, beige)    │
│  ├── icon-maskable-512.png  (maskable, beige)    │
│  └── apple-touch-icon.png   (iOS, 180×180)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ HelpMenu.svelte                                  │
│  └── Install App button + platform detection     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ app.css                                          │
│  └── Mobile CSS (overscroll, touch-action, etc)  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
