docs.title: Key Files
docs.text: File Purpose frontend/src/app.html Viewport, manifest link, Apple meta tags, apple-touch-icon link, early prompt capture, SW registration frontend/src/app.css Mobile CSS optimizations frontend/static/manifest.json PWA manifest (display, icons, colors) frontend/static/sw.js Service Worker (offline fallback only) frontend/static/offline.html Offline fallback page (static, i18n, dark mode) frontend/static/icons/icon-{192,512}.png App icons, manifest purpose any (generated) frontend/static/icons/icon-maskable-{192,512}.png App icons, manifest purpose maskable (generated) frontend/static/icons/apple-touch-icon.png iOS home-screen icon, 180×180 (generated) frontend/src/lib/components/layout/HelpMenu.svelte Install button logic dev.py → generate_pwa_icons() Icon generation from logo_square.png frontend/generated-icons.json Committed record of the source sha256 and recipe each generated icon set was drawn from: an icon set is redrawn only when it no longer matches dev.py → stamp_service_worker() Writes the // build: stamp of sw.js from offline.html, and only when the stamp changes; run by every docs build and by ./dev.py front build backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_pwa_assets.py Gate: icons, manifest icon entries, apple-touch-icon link, sw.js stamp, and how stamp_service_worker() and ./dev.py front build stamp it

docs.title: Mobile CSS
docs.text:
Applied globally via app.css (excerpt):

html {
    overscroll-behavior-x: none;          /* Disable swipe-back on Android */
    scrollbar-gutter: stable;             /* A modal's scroll lock never shifts the layout */
}

body {
    overscroll-behavior: contain;          /* No pull-to-refresh */
    -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; /* No blue flash on tap */
}

/* Prevent iOS auto-zoom on input focus; dense toolbar inputs opt out with .zoom-guard-exempt */
@media (max-width: 768px) {
    input:not(.zoom-guard-exempt),
    select:not(.zoom-guard-exempt),
    textarea:not(.zoom-guard-exempt) {
        font-size: 16px !important;
    }
}

/* Disable double-tap zoom on interactive elements */
a, button, input, select, textarea, [role='button'] {
    touch-action: manipulation;
}

/* iOS standalone mode: content below the status bar / notch */
.safe-top {
    padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);
}

The other global classes are listed in Styling → Utility Classes.

The viewport meta in app.html: 

<meta content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no, viewport-fit=cover" name="viewport" />

docs.title: PWA Manifest
docs.text:
Excerpt of frontend/static/manifest.json (description, start_url, scope and orientation left out):

{
    "name": "LibreFolio",
    "short_name": "LibreFolio",
    "display": "standalone",
    "theme_color": "#1a4031",
    "background_color": "#f5f4ef",
    "icons": [
        { "src": "/icons/icon-192.png", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png", "purpose": "any" },
        { "src": "/icons/icon-512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png", "purpose": "any" },
        { "src": "/icons/icon-maskable-192.png", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png", "purpose": "maskable" },
        { "src": "/icons/icon-maskable-512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png", "purpose": "maskable" }
    ]
}

One entry per purpose and size, each naming its own file: no file serves both any and maskable.

docs.title: Splash and Theme Colours
docs.text:
Surface Colour Set by Android splash screen Beige #f5f4ef, with the app icon Manifest background_color Title bar of the installed app #1a4031; #156534 in dark mode Manifest theme_color, and the <meta name="theme-color"> of app.html, which the anti-FOUC script rewrites in dark mode (offline.html does the same) iOS status bar Translucent, over the page apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: black-translucent; .safe-top pads content below it In-app loading splash (#app-splash) Beige #f5f4ef; #0f172a in dark mode Inline in app.html: the logo on a white tile and a spinner, faded out and removed by routes/+layout.svelte once the translations are loaded

The iOS home-screen icon is apple-touch-icon.png (180×180), linked from app.html.

docs.title: Icon Generation
docs.text:
dev.py → generate_pwa_icons() draws five icons with PIL from frontend/static/logo_square.png (944×944 RGBA) into frontend/static/icons/:

File Manifest purpose Background Logo icon-192.png, icon-512.png any White Side = size / 1.24, a margin of ~12 % of the logo per side icon-maskable-192.png, icon-maskable-512.png maskable Splash beige #f5f4ef (the manifest background_color) Scaled so its farthest pixel sits at 0.37 × size from the centre apple-touch-icon.png (180×180) — (linked from app.html) White As the any icons

Every icon is saved as opaque RGB, with no alpha channel. The logo is resized premultiplied (RGBa), so its transparent black pixels do not bleed a dark fringe into its edge, then laid on the background with Image.alpha_composite.

The generator runs inside copy_docs_assets(), right before stamp_service_worker(): on ./dev.py mkdocs build, serve and deploy, and when ./dev.py server or ./dev.py docker build rebuilds a stale docs site. ./dev.py front build does not run it, though it does stamp sw.js before building (see the note below). The PNGs are committed, and mirrored into mkdocs_src/docs/static/icons/: after changing logo_square.png, run ./dev.py mkdocs build and commit the regenerated icons together with frontend/generated-icons.json, which records the sha256 of the logo they were drawn from. The generator redraws only when an icon is missing or when that hash, or PWA_ICONS_RECIPE in dev.py, no longer matches the record: Pillow does not write the same PNG bytes on every platform, so the decision never looks at the PNGs themselves. A change to the code that draws the icons must therefore bump PWA_ICONS_RECIPE, or nothing is regenerated.

Icons and the splash screen

  • Maskable safe zone: a launcher crops a maskable icon to its own shape (circle, squircle…), and only a centred circle of radius 0.40 × size is sure to survive. The logo reaches 0.37 × size, about 0.38 with its antialiased edge, so the crop never bites into it. An any icon is shown whole instead, which is why each purpose has its own files.
  • Beige: the maskable icons are beige to the edges because #f5f4ef is the colour of the Android splash screen (background_color), so the cropped icon meets it without a seam. Change both or neither.
  • Opacity: Android's splash screen and iOS paint transparent pixels black, so every icon is opaque RGB — no alpha channel and no tRNS colour key. That is what keeps black corners off the Android splash and off the iPhone home-screen icon.
  • Service-worker stamp: stamp_service_worker() writes // build: <md5(offline.html)[:8]> as line 2 of sw.js. Any byte change in sw.js makes browsers update the worker, so every offline.html edit must be restamped (see Updating the Offline Page). It writes sw.js only when the stamp changes: with offline.html unchanged, sw.js keeps its bytes and its modification time. check_frontend_needs_build() watches frontend/static/, so a rewrite at every docs build would cost a frontend rebuild for nothing. It runs with every docs build (copy_docs_assets()) and with ./dev.py front build, before the npm build, so a build always ships the stamp of the offline.html it copies.

The gate is backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_pwa_assets.py, a pure pytest module. It reads the committed files and checks the icons are opaque RGB at their exact sizes, the maskable logo stays inside 0.40 × size on the beige, the manifest has the four icon entries, app.html links the 180×180 apple-touch-icon.png, and the stamp equals md5(offline.html)[:8]. On copies of sw.js and offline.html under tmp_path, it also runs the stamping: stamping twice leaves sw.js untouched, an edited page is restamped on line 2 with the rest of sw.js kept, a missing sw.js or offline.html writes nothing, and ./dev.py front build stamps before its build command, debug or production. Run it with ./dev.py test utils pwa-assets.

docs.title: Install Button Logic
docs.text: The HelpMenu.svelte component handles three platform scenarios:

docs.title: 1. Chrome/Edge/Android (beforeinstallprompt)
docs.text:
app.html (early) → captures event on window.__pwaInstallPrompt
     ↓
HelpMenu onMount → reads window.__pwaInstallPrompt as fallback
     ↓
User clicks "Install App" → calls deferredPrompt.prompt()
     ↓
Chrome shows its native install dialog

Race Condition

beforeinstallprompt can fire BEFORE Svelte components mount. That's why we capture it early in app.html on window.__pwaInstallPrompt, then read it in onMount.

Both listeners — the early one in app.html and the one HelpMenu.svelte adds in onMount — call e.preventDefault(), so the browser keeps the event instead of showing its automatic install prompt (the mini-infobar of Chrome on Android); the app calls prompt() only from Install App. A captured prompt is used once (deferredPrompt = null afterwards), and an accepted one hides the button (isStandalone = true).

docs.title: 2. iOS (Safari only)
docs.text:
• Detected via user agent: /iPad|iPhone|iPod/ or MacIntel + maxTouchPoints > 1
  • Shows localized instructions: "Tap Share → Add to Home Screen"
  • No programmatic install possible on iOS

docs.title: 3. Desktop Fallback
docs.text:
• If deferredPrompt not captured (e.g. Firefox, or event missed)
  • Shows hint: "Look for ⊕ in address bar"
  • On Android (/Android/ in the user agent) the same fallback shows help.installAppAndroid instead: HTTPS required for install. Use Chrome menu ⋮ → "Add to Home Screen" as shortcut — typically on a plain-HTTP LAN address

docs.title: Standalone Detection
docs.text:
isStandalone = window.matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches
    || (window.navigator as any).standalone === true; // iOS property

When isStandalone === true, the Install button is hidden entirely.

docs.title: Service Worker (Offline Fallback)
docs.text: LibreFolio uses a minimal Service Worker for offline fallback only — it does NOT cache app assets.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
User opens PWA → browser checks sw.js for updates (byte-diff)
     ↓
SW install event → pre-caches /offline.html (~22 KB)
     ↓
User navigates → SW intercepts (mode === 'navigate')
     ↓
fetch(request) succeeds → normal response (no caching)
fetch(request) fails → serve cached /offline.html

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text: Decision Rationale No app caching Updates are instant — no stale cache issues Only navigate intercept API calls, CSS, JS pass through untouched skipWaiting() + clients.claim() New SW activates immediately // build: stamp in sw.js (fixed cache name offline-fallback) Editing offline.html changes sw.js, so clients install the new SW, which re-fetches the page Auto-retry (10s interval) Page reloads automatically when server returns

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File Purpose frontend/static/sw.js Service Worker (~30 lines); line 2 is the // build: stamp frontend/static/offline.html Fallback page (static, inline styles, i18n) backend/test_scripts/test_utilities/test_pwa_assets.py Gate: fails when the stamp is not md5(offline.html)[:8]

docs.title: Offline Page Features
docs.text:
• Inline CSS and script; the only external resource it loads is /lf-flags.css (the flag font face, see Fonts), which the service worker does not pre-cache
  • Dark mode from the app's stored theme (librefolio-theme), falling back to prefers-color-scheme, with its own theme toggle
  • i18n: detects navigator.language → EN/IT/FR/ES, with a language menu
  • Auto-retry: pings server every 10s, reloads on success
  • Same animated background as the login page, and a toolbar with Buy Me a Coffee, theme, language and a link to the online documentation

docs.title: Updating the Offline Page
docs.text:
1. Edit frontend/static/offline.html. Keep its event handlers in its script (addEventListener), never an inline onclick: the managed profile's report-only policy allows the page's script by its hash, and no hash covers an inline handler (see Frame Protection and the Report-Only Policy)
  2. Restamp sw.js with ./dev.py mkdocs build or ./dev.py front build, which both run stamp_service_worker()
  3. Commit sw.js together with the page: the gate test_pwa_assets.py fails while the stamp and the page disagree
  4. Deploy — browser auto-updates SW on next PWA open

docs.title: iOS Notes
docs.text:
• Service Workers supported since iOS 11.3 (2018)
  • Cache eviction possible after 7 days of non-use — irrelevant here (1 file, re-cached on next visit)
  • All iOS browsers use WebKit → same SW behavior everywhere

docs.title: HTTP vs HTTPS Behavior
docs.text:
Feature HTTPS HTTP localhost HTTP LAN Manifest loaded ✅ ✅ ✅ Service Worker (offline page) ✅ ✅ ❌ beforeinstallprompt ✅ ✅ ❌ Browser's own automatic install banner ❌ suppressed by preventDefault() ❌ suppressed by preventDefault() ❌ no event Native install dialog from Install App (prompt()) ✅ ✅ ❌ a hint instead Manual "Add to Home" ✅ ✅ ✅ (Android) iOS Add to Home ✅ ✅ ✅

Service workers and the install prompt need a secure context: HTTPS, or localhost. On a plain-HTTP LAN address the browser exposes no navigator.serviceWorker, so app.html skips the registration and there is no offline page.

docs.title: Future: Share Target (File Receiving)
docs.text:
Not Implemented

This section documents a potential future feature.

The Web Share Target API would allow LibreFolio to appear in the OS "Share" menu when sharing files (e.g., broker CSV exports).

Requirements: - Service Worker (to handle the POST request) - HTTPS mandatory - Works on: Android Chrome ✅, iOS ❌ (Apple doesn't support share_target)

iOS Alternative: iOS Shortcuts automation — a Shortcut that accepts files from the Share Sheet and posts them to the broker-report upload endpoint, POST /api/v1/brokers/import/upload (multipart: file, broker_id), with an authenticated session.

docs.title: Updating the PWA
docs.text:
Updates flow automatically:

  1. Admin updates Docker container (new sw.js and/or app code)
  2. User reopens the installed PWA
  3. Browser detects sw.js changed (byte-diff) → installs new SW
  4. New SW activates → pre-caches updated offline.html
  5. App loads fresh assets from server (no caching layer)

No manual "update app" action needed. If offline.html content changes, restamp sw.js (see Updating the Offline Page) to force a refresh.

docs.title: 🎨 Styling & Design System
docs.text: LibreFolio uses Tailwind CSS v4 for styling, providing a utility-first approach with a custom design system.

docs.title: 🧰 Technology Stack
docs.text:
• Tailwind CSS v4 (tailwindcss, through @tailwindcss/postcss): the utility-first CSS framework.
  • CSS-first configuration: src/app.css imports Tailwind and declares the design tokens with the @theme directive. tailwind.config.js only holds an empty extend and is not loaded: Tailwind v4 reads a JavaScript config only through @config, which app.css does not use.
  • CSS Variables: Used for theming (Dark/Light mode) and brand colors.
  • Fonts: system and locally installed fonts, plus one self-hosted face for flags — see Fonts.

docs.title: 🎯 Design System
docs.text: The design system is defined in src/app.css using the @theme directive.

docs.title: 🎨 Brand Colors
docs.text:
Color Name Hex Usage libre-green #1a4031 Primary brand color, buttons, active states. libre-beige #f5f4ef Backgrounds, cards, warmth. libre-sage #9caf9c Secondary accents, borders. libre-dark #111111 Text, dark mode backgrounds.

In dark mode html.dark redefines --color-libre-green (#00d681) and --color-libre-banner (#00834f). @theme also defines libre-banner (#1a4031, not used by components today), a primary-50…900 (green) and a surface-50…500 (beige) palette, and the shadow-card / shadow-card-hover shadows.

docs.title: 💻 Usage
docs.text:
You can use these colors directly in Tailwind classes:

<div class="bg-libre-green text-white p-4 rounded-xl">
  Primary Button
</div>

<div class="bg-libre-beige text-libre-dark">
  Card Content
</div>

docs.title: 🔤 Fonts
docs.text:
Every font stack the app sets starts with the 'LF Flags' face:

/* src/app.css — @theme */
--font-sans: 'LF Flags', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif;
--font-mono: 'LF Flags', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', 'Courier New', monospace;

The html element uses the same sans stack. Inter is not self-hosted: it is used where it is installed, and system-ui takes over elsewhere.

'LF Flags' is declared in static/lf-flags.css, linked by src/app.html and by static/offline.html. Its unicode-range: U+1F1E6-1F1FF covers only the regional indicator symbols that make up a flag, so it draws flags and nothing else: digits, #, * and every other emoji keep the fonts after it.

  • Apple devices draw their own flags: the face resolves to the system Apple Color Emoji through its local() sources, and nothing is downloaded.
  • Everywhere else — Windows included, whose Segoe UI Emoji has no flags and prints the two letters instead — it uses a locally installed Noto Color Emoji when there is one, and otherwise the self-hosted Noto Color Emoji flags subset, /fonts/noto-color-emoji/noto-color-emoji.0.woff2, fetched only when a flag is on screen.

The subset is not committed (frontend/static/fonts/ is gitignored): scripts/update_js_cache.py downloads Noto Color Emoji from Google Fonts and keeps only the flags range (keep_unicode_ranges). ./dev.py front build and ./dev.py docker build run it first and stop when the font is missing and cannot be fetched; ./dev.py server runs it too.

Chart text is out of the stacks' reach: ECharts draws legends, labels and axes on a canvas and writes its tooltip with an inline font, so no CSS applies to it. The charts get the face through the theme they are created with, CHART_INIT_THEME (src/lib/components/charts/chartFont.ts), whose font puts 'LF Flags' before ECharts' default family; the same module requests the face before the first chart paints, since canvas text does not make the browser fetch it. See Flags in chart text.

Never name an emoji font in a font-family

No stack may name Apple Color Emoji, Noto Color Emoji, Segoe UI Emoji or Segoe UI Symbol: an emoji font placed before the text font draws digits, # and * with emoji glyphs. Those names appear only as local() sources in static/lf-flags.css. A component that sets its own stack (a monospace cell, an inline style) starts it with 'LF Flags', or wraps the flag in .emoji-flag, which applies the app's sans stack.

The gate src/flagFont.gate.test.ts checks the face, the stacks of app.css and offline.html, and that no source names an emoji font; e2e/fx/fx-flag-font.spec.ts reads from the browser (Chrome DevTools Protocol) which font actually draws a flag.

docs.title: 🌙 Dark Mode
docs.text:
Dark mode is the dark class on the <html> element. An inline script in src/app.html sets dark or light before the first paint, from the stored preference (librefolio-theme in localStorage) or, when there is none, from prefers-color-scheme. app.css binds Tailwind's dark: variant to that class:

@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

Components write explicit dark: variants next to the light classes (bg-white dark:bg-slate-800): this is the main mechanism.

docs.title: 🔧 Theme Variables
docs.text:
app.css also defines semantic variables for both themes (:root, html.light and html.dark): --theme-bg-*, --theme-text-*, --theme-border-*, --theme-accent* and --theme-shadow*.

:root,
html.light {
    --theme-bg-primary: #ffffff;
    --theme-text-primary: #111827;
}

html.dark {
    --theme-bg-primary: #0f172a;
    --theme-text-primary: #f8fafc;
}

Components do not read them directly. They feed a set of global html.dark overrides in app.css that remap common light utilities — .bg-white, .bg-gray-50, .text-gray-800, .border-gray-200, inputs, .bg-libre-beige, … — to the dark palette, a safety net for markup written without a dark: variant.

docs.title: 🛠️ Utility Classes
docs.text:
Global classes defined in src/app.css:

Class Purpose .emoji-flag Applies the app's sans stack, so a flag inside an element with its own font (a monospace cell) is still drawn by 'LF Flags'. .lf-compact-number-input Shared typography of compact numeric inputs: inherited font, 0.75rem/1rem, tabular numerals. Below 768 px the anti-zoom rule still sets inputs to 16 px, and the class only raises the line height. Used by the custom axis bounds of ChartAestheticsSection.svelte. .zoom-guard-exempt Opts an input out of the mobile 16 px font size that prevents iOS auto-zoom, for dense toolbars (date fields). .safe-top, .safe-top-offset Padding / offset for the iOS safe area (notch, status bar) in standalone mode. .scrollbar-hidden Scrollable without a visible scrollbar. .lf-price-flash-up, .lf-price-flash-down One-shot colour flash of a live price — see Live Prices.

docs.title: 🧱 Component Styling
docs.text:
The recurring patterns in the code base:

  • Cards: bg-white dark:bg-slate-800 rounded-xl shadow-sm, often with border border-gray-100 dark:border-slate-700
  • Inputs: rounded-lg borders with focus:ring-libre-green / focus:border-libre-green
  • Primary buttons: bg-libre-green text-white rounded-lg (dark mode darkens bg-libre-green to #166534 for contrast)

docs.title: 🧩 Frontend Components
docs.text: This section documents the reusable UI components in LibreFolio, organized by functional area.

docs.title: 📚 Component Categories
docs.text: The library is split into two architectural layers: Core UI (generic atoms and molecules) and Features (domain-specific components).

docs.title: Core UI
docs.text: Component Details Core UI overview Modals (ModalBase, ConfirmModal, sync modals), feedback (ToastContainer, Tooltip, InfoBanner), pickers (DateRangePicker), PageToolbar, DataEditor, atoms and inputs (PrivacyToggle, ExactDecimalInput, ExactQuantityInput, CompactDurationBadge), display blocks (KpiMetricBar, KpiDivergingFlowBar, RiskMetricCard, RiskCardGrid). Generic building blocks. DataTable Advanced data grid with sorting, filtering, pagination, sticky columns and column management. File Upload & Media FileUploader, ImageCropper, ImageEditModal, AssetPickerModal, LazyImage. Select & Dropdowns SimpleSelect, SearchSelect and TreeSelect with keyboard navigation, specialized wrappers (AssetTypeSelect, CurrencySearchSelect, …) and AssetPickerPanel on SelectPopover + CheckMenu. A typed search ranks matches in the option's name or value above matches found only in its description — see Ranking the matches.

docs.title: Features (Domain)
docs.text: Component Details Transaction Form Complex modal for creating/editing transactions with reactive auto-calculation and live WAC preview. Import Wizard Multi-file staged broker import: duplicate detection (vs DB and in-batch), the file-priority batch resolver, and the N-way compare modal. Brokers BrokerCard, BrokerForm, BrokerModal, DeleteBrokerDialog, and Broker Sharing. Settings The tab registry and its «Administration» group, SettingsLayout, PreferencesTab, GlobalSettingsTab, UsersTab with LinkShare (shared links and their address check), SecurityTab (the configuration checks, and their dot on the sidebar's connection line), AccountDeletionDialog (shared by the Profile and Users tabs). Authentication LoginCard, RegisterCard, ForgotPasswordCard, the account link pages (LinkStatusCard, ResetPasswordCard), the password-manager contract. Live Prices How the Assets list (every 60 s) and the asset detail page (every 30 s, one request for the price summary and the chart head) poll POST /assets/prices/current, how the polls pause while nobody uses the page, and how a price change is shown. Lots Analysis LotsAnalysisPanel and its chart/table/modal group: per-lot WAC vs market price, custody Gantt, unified lots table, value/return comparison, custody drill-down modal. Risk UI The Correlation tab of the Assets page and the Dashboard's Risk tab: the selection, the requests over one shared window, the section frames and notices, and each block's rules.

docs.title: 🧭 App Header
docs.text:
lib/components/layout/Header.svelte is the bar above every authenticated page (mobile menu, the Buy Me a Coffee link on a self-hosted instance only, privacy and theme toggles, language and help menus). It is sticky on every viewport and gives the page its height back while the user reads:

  • Scrolling down at least 8 px in a row hides it (it slides up by its own height); scrolling up at least 4 px brings it back. Within the first header-height of the page it is always shown.
  • It stays pinned — never hides — while keyboard focus is inside it, while the Help or Language menu is open, while the mobile sidebar is open, while any modal is open (it watches the ModalBase scroll-lock counter on document.body), while an onboarding guide runs, or when the keepVisible prop is set.
  • A route change, a window resize or a change of its own height shows it again.

The scroll position is sampled once per animation frame; the slide is a 200 ms transform, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. The state is published as data-scroll-state (visible, hidden, pinned) next to data-menu-open, data-modal-open, data-sidebar-open and data-guide-active: Header.test.ts tests the state machine, e2e/layout/header-scroll.spec.ts the real geometry.

On a phone the sidebar, with its connection line, hides behind the menu button (mobile-menu-toggle), so the button carries a dot, mobile-menu-security-dot, for an insecure connection (plan 36) and, since lot N69b, for an administrator's security warnings, with data-severity error or warning; its accessible name appends the insecure level and the count. The header only reads the stores and never asks for the checks: see The sidebar's dot, with its tests.

docs.title: 📏 Component Guidelines
docs.text:
• ModalBase: ALL modals are built on ModalBase.svelte (directly, or through ConfirmModal / SyncModalBase) with configurable z-index
  • Svelte 5 Runes: Use $state, $derived, $effect, $props
  • Event handling: Use onclick instead of on:click (Svelte 5 syntax)
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS utilities + dark mode with dark: prefix — see Styling
  • HTML strings: escape user- and provider-supplied text with escapeHtml before it reaches {@html}; toasts and tooltips also sanitise what they render
  • Amounts: format money through the shared currency formatters, so the privacy toggle masks it — see Privacy masking
  • Accessibility: Keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, focus management
  • i18n: All user-facing text via $t('key') translation function

docs.title: Chart Animations
docs.text: How we implement smooth transitions in LibreFolio's ECharts-based charts.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
echartsAnimationConfig.ts          ← Centralized config + helpers
├── CHART_ANIMATION_CONFIG         ← Timing/easing settings
├── CHART_SET_OPTION_OPTS          ← setOption flags (notMerge/replaceMerge)
└── namedPoint(date, value)        ← Named data point for shift animation

docs.title: 1. Dashboard charts (GrowthChart, AllocationHistoryChart)
docs.text:
These use shift animation — when the time period changes, shared dates translate to new positions and new dates appear/disappear smoothly.

Requirements:

  • xAxis: { type: 'time' } — ECharts understands temporal coordinates
  • Data as namedPoint(date, value) → {name: date, value: [date, val]}
  • Partial setOption on data-only updates: each series is sent as {name, data} only (no full option rebuild)
  • Full setOption only when something the partial update cannot express has changed (see below)

Key insight (from ECharts developers):

ECharts performs shift animation if it recognizes part of the old data in the new data. This matching is done via the name property on each data point.

// echartsAnimationConfig.ts
export function namedPoint(date: string, value: number | null) {
    return {name: date, value: [date, value]};
}

Partial vs Full update pattern (lib/features/dashboard/GrowthChart.svelte, used by the Dashboard and Broker detail):

// GrowthChart.svelte — renderChart(forceFullXAxisRebuild = false)
const renderedModeKey = viewMode === 'pnl' ? `pnl:${pnlSubmode}` : viewMode;
const masked = shouldMaskAmount();
const seriesData = buildChartUpdateSeries(isDark, activeData, logicalRange.startDate);
const seriesKey = seriesData.map((series) => series.name).join('\u0000');
const needsFullInit =
    forceFullXAxisRebuild ||
    lastRenderedMode !== renderedModeKey ||
    lastRenderedDark !== isDark ||
    lastRenderedMasked !== masked ||
    lastRenderedSeriesKey !== seriesKey;

if (needsFullInit) {
    // Axes, tooltip, legend, series: setOption(option, CHART_FULL_UPDATE_OPTS)
    applyFullOption(isDark, buildFullSeries(isDark, seriesData), zoomWindow);
} else {
    // Data only, {name, data} per series: setOption({...}, CHART_SERIES_UPDATE_OPTS)
    updateChartData(activeData, isDark, zoomWindow, false, logicalRange.startDate);
}
Full rebuild trigger Why the partial update is not enough renderedModeKey The mode (eur, pct, pnl) and, in pnl, the submode: the series type changes (line, candlestick, bar), which {name, data} cannot express. isDark Colours are set once, in the full option. masked The privacy toggle: ECharts caches the axis labels, so the tick formatter has to run again. The tooltip formatter reads the flag on every hover. seriesKey The names of the series last drawn, in order: a broker that joins, leaves or is swapped under the P&L line changes the list, and from {name, data} alone ECharts would keep the old series and their legend entries. forceFullXAxisRebuild The x-axis leaves its compact layout (a narrow container widening on resize).

The two flag sets differ on purpose:

  • CHART_SERIES_UPDATE_OPTS = {notMerge: false, replaceMerge: ['dataZoom']} — series must not be in replaceMerge here: the partial update sends only {name, data}, and replacing the matched series would drop the type and styles set by the full option, leaving a blank chart.
  • CHART_FULL_UPDATE_OPTS = {...CHART_SET_OPTION_OPTS, replaceMerge: ['series', 'xAxis']}.

A resolution switch (daily ↔ weekly/monthly, chosen from the zoom) goes through the partial path without animation, after hiding the tooltip.

Where GrowthChart's code lives. The component keeps everything reactive; what it computes lives in three modules in the same folder, which hold no state and see the component only through their arguments:

File Holds GrowthChart.svelte Props, state, the $derived inputs and the memo of each aggregation, zoom handling, the ECharts lifecycle (renderChart, updateChartData, applyFullOption) and the template. buildChartUpdateSeries and buildFullSeries are thin wrappers that pass the view on screen to the series module. growthChartData.ts The inputs mapped to one value per day (mapEurStackedData, mapPctValues, mapBrokerPnlSeries, mapCandlesByDate, alignFlowToDates), the buckets (buildBucketInfos for the cascade of Abs, % and the P&L line, buildLadderBuckets for the ladder of Candles and Income), their reductions (aggregateMetric, aggregateFlowMetric, aggregateCandleMetric and their ladder* counterparts), one entry per resolution or rung (buildResolutionData, buildLadderData) and the zoom-window geometry (buildZoomWindow, cascadeIndicesAt, ladderIndicesAt). growthChartSeries.ts What each view draws: buildGrowthUpdateSeries (the {name, data} of the partial update) and buildGrowthFullSeries (every series with its type and style, for the full option), with splitBySign, toCandlestickPoint (the '-' gap), findReferenceTotalPnl and PNL_REFERENCE_SERIES_NAME. growthChartTooltip.ts buildGrowthTooltip, the HTML ECharts shows on hover, built from a GrowthTooltipView the formatter assembles on every hover (entry on screen, mode, labels, translator, currency); amounts are masked under privacy.

The one rule: an aggregation reads its data only through AggregationInputs. Each memo (resolutionCache, ladderCache) is keyed on the identity of the aggregationInputs $derived object, which Svelte rebuilds whenever one of its members changes, so a new input is added to that object and to the AggregationInputs type, never passed as one more argument (the other arguments are the memo's keys: the resolution or rung, and today for the ladder). An input that bypasses the object does not invalidate the memo, which keeps returning entries computed before it changed.

Weekly and monthly points. In the time-axis views (Abs, % and the P&L line submode, whose daily, weekly and monthly resolutions the code calls the cascade), buildBucketInfos stands each weekly or monthly point on the last day of its bucket that the history holds, the day its aggregated value comes from (aggregateLineSeries keeps a bucket's last point): the calendar end of a whole period, the last day with data of the period still running. The line reaches the latest data and the axis ends on that day, never on a Sunday or a month end still to come. On a time axis ECharts maps a dataZoom percent linearly to time over the drawn extent, not to a point index; the two agree only while the points are evenly spaced, which the running period's point, or a gap in the history, breaks. So the cascade reads and writes its window in time: getLogicalRangeFromChart turns the percents into days from the first point (cascadeDayOffsetsOf) and widens the window to the points at or outside its edges (cascadeIndicesAt), so a partly visible period is never lost; an edge within 0.1 day of a point (ZOOM_EDGE_SNAP_DAYS) stands on it, which absorbs float and DST error. buildZoomWindow writes the percents the same way, in days over the drawn span. The ladder (below) keeps index percents on its category axis, each edge rounded to the nearest bucket as ECharts snaps it (ladderIndicesAt).

Tooltip dates. The tooltip headers of GrowthChart, AllocationHistoryChart and the broker lots' LotComparisonChart write every day in the interface locale, never as a raw ISO date: through formatDay (lib/utils/core/formatAxisDate.ts: 1 Oct 2026 in en-GB, Oct 1, 2026 in en-US) in the first two, through the chart's own formatLongDate, same format, in the third. On their time axes, chart.tooltip.valueAt under a weekly or monthly point prints the point's own day, and a weekly header (chart.tooltip.weekRange) runs from the bucket's first day up to it (bucketSpanUpTo, priceChartHelpers.ts, as in PriceChartFull and CandlestickChart): a whole week or month ends on its bucket end, the one still running, or the one the series stops inside, on its last day with data, never on a day still to come. LotComparisonChart reads that day from the hovered point (tooltipBucketInfo, lotComparisonChartHelpers.ts). The ladder header names the whole calendar period instead (below).

Privacy redraw. The render runs inside tick().then(…), where reading a store registers no dependency, so the render $effect reads shouldMaskAmount() itself: toggling privacy re-runs it, and the changed masked value forces the full rebuild. The y-axis ticks mask the digits and keep the sign outside the mask and the k/M suffix inside it. Tooltip amounts go through the chart's own fmtCurrency (the currency code, then maskFormattedNumber), so the code and the sign stay readable; the Abs composition rows (assets at cost, returns, capital) print — at zero, masked or not. The general rule is in ECharts formatters.

docs.title: P&L submodes
docs.text:
The pnl mode has three submodes (pnlSubmode). The mode and the submode persist per user (dashboard-growth-mode, dashboard-growth-pnl-submode), shared by Dashboard and Broker detail; the defaults are eur and line. After every completed load, a pct view, restored or picked, over a history without % data (hasPctData) shows eur, and the % button is disabled. The fallback is display-only: the stored value is kept and pctFallback marks the fallback, so the next loaded history with % data brings the view back to pct, and the next mount still restores pct; selectMode() clears pctFallback, so a mode picked meanwhile, eur included, wins. The submode buttons float over the plot's top-left corner and fold to their icon below a 640 px container (CONTROLS_COMPACT_BELOW_PX), keeping the label as title and aria-label.

Submode Series x-axis line Total P&L split by sign into two series (zero crossings interpolated), a dashed reference line flat at the first visible day's P&L (__pnlReference__, left out of the legend), and one line per broker when brokerPnlHistory holds two or more (Broker detail passes none) Time axis, shift animation candles One candlestick series of the total P&L, without broker overlay. A gap is ECharts' empty value '-': a null item crashes the candlestick series on a category axis Category axis (the ladder) income Six bar series in three columns per bucket: the income stack (dividends and interest above zero, costs below), deposits, and acquisitions split between new capital and reinvested returns Category axis (the ladder)

The ladder (Candles and Income) draws on a category axis, one slot per bucket, so every candle body and bar gets the same width at any zoom; its labels and separators come from a ladder plan (growthLadderAxis.ts) instead of the responsive time-axis policy. Each submode keeps a fixed number of series in a fixed order, which the partial update relies on across zoom and pan.

  • Rungs are calendar periods (growthLadderBuckets.ts): 1D; 1W from Monday to Sunday; 1M from the 1st; 3M, 6M and 1Y as quarters, halves and years. 3D and 2W have no calendar unit: they are fixed blocks counted from 1970-01-01 and from Monday 1969-12-29, so their edges never move. The caption's unit letter comes from datePicker.granularity.*Short.
  • Axis labels (planLadderAxis): a label names the start of its bucket's calendar period on the entry's rung (entry.rung), even when the series covers only part of it: data from Thursday 1 January 2026 gets Dec 29 as its first 1W label. On the day rungs (1D, 3D, 1W, 2W) a label is the day number, with the month on the first visible label and wherever the month changes, and the two-digit year as well wherever the year changes — Oct 6 · 13 · 20 · 27 · Nov 3 · 10 … Dec 29 · Jan 5 '26 · 12 … — but never the year on the first visible label. 1M prints the month, 3M the quarter (dashboard.pnlAxisQuarter, Q{quarter}) and 6M the months it spans joined by an en dash, each with the two-digit year (dashboard.pnlAxisWithYear, {label} ''{year}) on the first visible label and wherever the year changes: Oct '25 · Nov · Dec · Jan '26, Q4 '25 · Q1 '26 · Q2 · Q3, Jul–Dec '25 · Jan–Jun '26. 1Y prints the year, 2026. "Changes" compares a bucket with the previous labelled one, so two neighbouring labels never read the same. Dates go through Intl.DateTimeFormat in the interface locale and both keys are translated, so a quarter reads Q4 '25 in English and T4 25 in Italian.
  • Label layout: horizontal labels need 8 px between them (LADDER_LABEL_GAP_PX, widths estimated at 0.6 × font size × characters), and the outermost ones move inward to stay 2 px inside the canvas (LADDER_EDGE_SAFETY_PX). If even one visible label does not fit, all of them turn 45°, never just some. Turned labels are thinned only when they would still overlap, that is when slot × √½ is less than one label row (LADDER_LABEL_ROW_EM): then every second, third… bucket keeps a label, counted back from the most recent one, which keeps its own. In practice only dense Candles get there; an Income slot is always wide enough. A turned label that the canvas edge would cut off is left out (on the left, the next candidate becomes the first label). For the band under the axis, ladderLabelMeasure measures the turned labels at 14 px in the chart's font (echarts.format.getTextRect) and gives every label the widest one's box (labelBox), so containLabel reserves room for it.
  • Offer (availableCandleWidths, against the measured plot width): a rung is removed, not disabled, when a candle body would be narrower than 2.5 px (LADDER_MIN_BODY_PX) or, in Income, when each of the three bars would be narrower than 4.5 px (INCOME_MIN_BAR_PX; the bars keep 30 % of the slot between buckets and 10 % of a bar between columns). A rung also needs three buckets, except 1D. Income starts at 1W, and the offer is never empty: the floor rung stays.
  • Selection (reconcileCandleWidth): the first ladder render takes the finest rung offered, and every entry into Income takes 1M, or the nearest rung offered (incomeOpeningPending). Otherwise Candles and Income share candleWidth. A rung that leaves the offer climbs to the next wider one offered, or to the widest. The width is not persisted, and a zoom never changes it: it only re-plans the axis labels.
  • Edges of the series: a bucket the series starts inside, or a past bucket it stops inside, is partial and drawn at half opacity (PARTIAL_BUCKET_OPACITY) in both submodes; otherwise the bucket that has not ended yet is current and drawn whole. The tooltip header prints the rung and the whole calendar period, by design (1M - 1 Oct 2026 → 31 Oct 2026 in en-GB), then chart.tooltip.partialBucket or chart.tooltip.currentBucket (none on a one-day bucket), then chart.tooltip.valueAt the last day with data, except in Income, whose bars are sums. Every day goes through formatDay; a 1D bucket prints only its date.
  • Candles: the daily OHLC comes from the backend (see Price Resolver), requested through onRequestPnlCandles on entry while none is loaded. The effect calls it tracked, on purpose: what the page's loader reads before its first await becomes a dependency, so a saved Candles view asks again once the Dashboard knows its brokers (canAsk), and a failed request is asked again when a retry falls due, at most three times, 2, 4 and 8 s later (Lazy sections after a failure); an untrack around the call would silence both. A bucket takes the first open, the highest high, the lowest low and the last close of its days that have a candle (ladderCandleMetric); a bucket with none is a gap, whose tooltip prints common.noData. The disclosure caption (dashboard.pnlCandlesHypotheticalShort) stays on one line under the plot, scrolled by scrollOnOverflow when it does not fit, unless the user prefers reduced motion.
  • Income: a bucket sums its days (ladderFlowMetric). Both acquisition series are named dashboard.bookValue, so the legend, deduplicated by name, lists five entries and one click toggles both zones; since ECharts keeps legend state by name, it also toggles the Abs area with the same text. The tooltip lists dividend, interest and their total, then costs, deposit and the purchase value with its two ↳ halves, each only when non-zero. The four flow series come from POST /api/v1/portfolio/report (include_income_history, include_cost_history, include_deposit_history, include_acquisition_funding): the first three scan the transactions of each broker in scope, asset-linked or not, keep their sign, and leave out an amount whose FX conversion fails, listing its pair in missing_fx_pairs; the funding split comes from the engine's per-broker cash pools, where a BUY spends the returns pool before capital.

docs.title: 2. Detail page charts (LineChart, CandlestickChart, PriceChartFull)
docs.text:
These use instant rendering (animation: false) because:

  • Complex segmented series (baseline coloring, stale gradient) create N sub-series with variable count between renders
  • ECharts cannot reliably match segments across period changes
  • The visual priority is precision, not animation

For these charts, the UX pattern is: keep old data visible until new data arrives (stale-while-revalidate at the store level), then swap instantly.

docs.title: Asset detail: Prices and Rolling Return
docs.text:
routes/(app)/assets/[id]/+page.svelte keeps the primary series in primaryMode, 'price' or 'calendar-return' (the Prices and Rolling Return buttons). It opens in the asset's saved view: detailModesForPrimaryView(settings.primaryView) gives the mode (and Abs or %) on every load of the asset, and persistPrimaryView() saves the change into the asset's chart settings (primaryView), where the asset's list card reads it too. setPrimaryMode() stops the measure mode of the panel it leaves.

'price' 'calendar-return' Main series the resolved closes (chartData) the ASSET_CALENDAR_ROLLING_RETURN points (calendarReturnView) Signals panel every definition allowedSignalTypes = ['asset-comparison']: the other configs stay saved, only hidden; no backend indicator is requested PriceChartFull line or candlestick, Abs/% toggle, event markers, editMode valueUnit="percentage", disableCandlestick, hideViewModeToggle, no event markers Measures MeasurePanel a second MeasurePanel, measurementUnit="percentage-points": Δ pp and Days replace Δ % and Δ%/yr Data editor its button and panel button hidden, panel hidden and inert

The rolling return is a backend signal. loadChartData() sends one POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query: the main asset's item carries {signal_code: 'ASSET_CALENDAR_ROLLING_RETURN', params: {window_days}}, with target_currency when the chart is converted, and each Asset comparison gets an item of its own — include_price: false, include_events: true, target_currency set to the chart currency — with the same signal request, so every line uses one window and one currency. The page's queryAssetPricesBulkWithSignalIsolation() sends it, and parseAssetPriceQueryWithSignalIsolation() (lib/components/assets/detail/assetDetailPriceQuery.ts) validates each signal result on its own, so one malformed result does not discard the response. The page then reads the signal results inside a try of their own (X-R16): a malformed one fails the signals only, with the panel's notice «Technical signals could not be updated», while the prices still reach the chart, the price cache and the All start. The FX detail page reads POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert the same way, through parseFxConvertWithSignalIsolation() (lib/components/fx/fxDetailConvertQuery.ts), so its rates survive a malformed signal result too.

The same plugin is also in the signal catalog (see Plugin Contract): in 'price' mode the Signals panel offers it in its Risk group as Rolling Return, a config of signalType asset-calendar-rolling-return whose card edits window_days (30 by default, at least 1). buildBackendSignalRequestPlan() requests it like any other backend indicator, and its calendar_return line is drawn over the prices on a secondary axis of its own, independent:calendar_return. Overlay and mode compute the same metric, the price return against the resolved close window_days calendar days earlier, but never in the same request: loadChartData() requests the overlay only in 'price' mode, with its card's window, and the mode's series only in 'calendar-return' mode, with the Window control's days. In 'calendar-return' mode the overlay config stays saved and hidden, like every config but the Asset comparisons.

calendarReturnWindow.ts turns the Window control into days: presets 1w, 1m, 3m, 1y are 7, 30, 90 and 365 days, and a custom amount is multiplied by 7, 30 or 365 (weeks, months, years); the default is 1m. The selection is saved in the asset's chart settings (calendarReturnWindow, below).

Each point of the answer carries a provenance: its status, reference_target_date, and the price and FX dates actually used, each with its days_back. PriceChartFull reads it through mainPointContext and adds up to three tooltip rows to the main line: ↩ the reference target date (followed by chart.tooltip.valueAt when the reference price is older), 📅 the current price date when it is older than the point, and 💱 the current and reference FX dates. The plugin leaves a point empty (missing_reference, invalid_current_price, invalid_reference_price) rather than estimating it and trims the leading empty points, so each line starts on its own first computable date. With some empty points the result is partial (undefined_metric_window warning); with no computable point it is unavailable (undefined_metric).

docs.title: FX detail: Prices and Rolling Return
docs.text:
routes/(app)/fx/[pair]/+page.svelte has the same two modes (lot X5-F1), with the same AssetChartPrimaryMode type. Differences from the asset page:

  • State and persistence. primaryMode opens from openingMode(), which reads primaryView of the pair's chart settings (getSettingsForPair(canonicalSlug, 'fx')): 'calendar-return' opens the rolling return, any other view opens prices and is remembered as priceViewBeforeCalendar. persistPrimaryView() writes calendar-return, or that remembered price view, back with setPairSettings(). The key is the canonical slug and the value is the one the pair's card in the list reads, so a card in the rolling return opens the detail in it. The window is the shared calendarReturnWindow / calendarReturnWindowAuto of the same settings (effectiveCalendarReturnWindow()).
  • Request builder. lib/charts/fxDetailCalendar.ts (pure) builds the body of POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert: buildFxDetailCalendarQuery() returns a conversion of 1 unit of the page's base into its quote, in the direction the page shows (data.urlBase / data.urlQuote), daily over dateStart..dateEnd, with one signal, the calendar rolling return (fxCalendarRequest(windowDays)); then one more conversion per saved fx-pair signal, in that signal's own direction (_inverted). A compared pair equal to the page's own is skipped. Unlike the list cards (utils/reducedFxQuery.ts) it sets no key, max_points or sample_like. fxDetailCalendarViews() reads signal_results by request_index into the page's CalendarReturnView and a Map by fx-pair config id.
  • When it is asked. loadCalendarReturn() runs only in the rolling return, under a generation counter that drops a stale answer, and never throws (a failure is the view's error state). It runs on the first load, on a session change, with the chart load that follows a period change, on a window change (setCalendarPreset() / setCalendarCustom()), on a change of the compared pairs (handleSignalsChange()) and on Refresh. Going back to prices asks nothing: the rates are in the FX store, and the mode switch only bumps the generation. The comparison lines come from renderCalendarPairComparisons().
  • Shared components. The page reuses AssetChartModeToggle and AssetCalendarWindowControls with the new optional idPrefix prop (default asset, fx here), which prefixes their test ids: fx-chart-primary-price, fx-chart-primary-calendar-return, fx-calendar-window-*, fx-calendar-return-docs. The states use fx-calendar-return-loading, -unavailable and -error. The chart card fx-detail-chart publishes data-primary-mode and, in the rolling return, data-window-days, data-series-state and data-calendar-comparison-ready / -partial / -unavailable / -error (the fx-pair config ids by state).
  • Signals and buttons. The Signals panel gets allowedSignalTypes = ['fx-pair'] (the other configs stay saved, hidden). PriceChartFull gets valueUnit="percentage" and hideViewModeToggle; the measure and edit buttons are not rendered (measureMode, editMode are forced off, setPrimaryMode() stops a running measure); the Measures panel itself stays on the page (its data are the rates).

Tests: frontend/e2e/fx/fx-detail-rolling-return.spec.ts, charts/__tests__/fxDetailCalendar.test.ts and fxDetailRollingReturn.wiring.test.ts.

docs.title: Asset detail: where the chart state lives
docs.text:
Layer Holds Backend database Asset prices and events, FX rates: the only persisted sources Chart settings in localStorage (Where settings live) The asset's override asset-<id>, including its calendarReturnWindow and its signals (indicator and comparison configs with their params, order and styles) The period in sessionStorage The start and end shared by the pages of the tab Page runtime Signal results, the rolling-return series and their provenance, comparison series, synthetic benchmarks, measures: a reload discards them

Measure rows and their endpoint results are runtime-only. Each measure's summary DataTable keeps only its own layout (page size, column widths, order and visibility) under its storageKey (measure-summary-<id>, asset-calendar-measure-summary-<id>).

docs.title: Asset detail: page sync and comparison sync
docs.text:
requiredFxPairs (built by buildRequiredFxPairs(), lib/components/assets/detail/assetDetailFxRequirements.ts) lists the FX pairs the page needs to convert into the chart currency: the asset's, each Asset comparison's, and those of their events' currencies. Each pair has a status (ok, missing, no-data, partial-gap) that drives the data-quality banners. The toolbar Sync (handleSync()) opens the page sync modal with the main asset (when it has a provider), the comparison assets, and every listed pair except the missing ones: a pair is never registered implicitly. The button is disabled for an asset without a provider and for an archived one.

A comparison card's Sync (handleSyncAsset() → runSyncAsset()) sends, in parallel, POST /api/v1/assets/prices/sync for the peer and POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync for collectConfiguredComparisonFxSlugs() — the configured pairs between the chart currency and the peer's currency or its events' currencies. Both use buildComparisonSyncRange() (charts/loadComparisonData.ts): the chart range, extended back by the window in 'calendar-return' mode, then widened by padSyncRange() (7 days either side, the end capped at today). In 'price' mode, comparison points the backend could not convert stay in their native currency (see Price Query); loadComparisonAssetsData() (same file) drops them and flags the card with _conversionFailed, so a comparison line never mixes currencies.

docs.title: Measure mode
docs.text:
The asset detail and FX pair pages measure on their chart through MeasurePanel (lib/components/charts/MeasurePanel.svelte). The asset page mounts one panel per primary mode and talks to the one on screen (activeMeasurePanel()). 📏 calls the panel's startMeasureMode() or stopMeasureMode(); the panel reports its mode through onmeasuremodechange, and the page hands it to the chart as measureMode, with the chart's two measure callbacks wired to the panel:

  • onMeasureClick(date, value) calls addPoint(date, value). The first click leaves the start pending. A second click on the start's day is ignored: no measure, measure mode stays on, the start stays pending. A click on another day adds the measure, its dates sorted, and stops measure mode.
  • onMeasureHover(date, value) returns updatePendingEnd(date, value) straight through: (date, value) => activeMeasurePanel()?.updatePendingEnd(date, value) in routes/(app)/assets/[id]/+page.svelte, (date, value) => measurePanel?.updatePendingEnd(date, value) in routes/(app)/fx/[pair]/+page.svelte. updatePendingEnd draws the dashed live preview (__pending__) from the start to date and returns a boolean: true on the pending start's day, where it also removes the preview if one is drawn; false elsewhere, with measure mode off, or with no start pending.

No measure spans a single day (lot Y-N65, as in the date pickers). The expanded card's DateRangePicker cannot publish a range of one day, so updateMeasureDates no longer refuses one on its own: that silent refusal was bug N65, where the card's picker showed the same day in «From» and «To» while the measure kept its old dates. The panel's + (addMeasureFromChartData()) measures from the first measurable point to the last, and does nothing when both fall on the same day.

The cursor. zrender writes its own cursor inline on its element at every pointer move, before its listeners run (Handler.mousemove, zrender 6), so the cursor-crosshair class that the chart container carries in measure mode was hardly ever seen. PriceChartFull (line view) and CandlestickChart (candles) therefore set their cursor through zrender:

  • On every zr mousemove while measureMode is on (and an onMeasureHover is given), synchronously and before the requestAnimationFrame throttle, the chart calls zr.setCursorStyle('crosshair'), or 'not-allowed' while the last resolved hover was refused.
  • In the frame it resolves the point under the pointer, calls onMeasureHover, and applies the cursor of the new answer. onMeasureHover is typed (date, value) => boolean | void; true means refused. The container publishes the answer as data-measure-hover: "blocked" over a refused day (the measure's start), "free" anywhere else, including off every point. Out of measure mode the attribute is absent, and a hover still queued when measure mode ends publishes nothing.
  • Outside measure mode the chart never calls setCursorStyle: zrender keeps its own cursor.

These rules are pinned in the Y-N65 describes of MeasurePanel.test.ts and PriceChartFull.test.ts. The latter runs each case on the line view and on the candle view, with an ECharts stand-in whose zr records every setCursorStyle call.

docs.title: Chart Settings and Axis Scales
docs.text: The FX and Asset charts (list cards, detail pages, and the Chart Settings modal's preview) share one settings store and one set of axis controls.

docs.title: Where settings live
docs.text:
lib/stores/chartSettingsStore.svelte.ts keeps the settings in localStorage, per user (lf_<userId>_chartSettingsStore, written 250 ms after the last change). Each chart reads, in order:

  1. its own override, keyed by the pair slug for FX and asset-<id> for an asset: a card's ⚙️ and the detail page's aesthetics and Signals panels all write this one;
  2. its scope's default, __global_fx__ or __global_assets__, written by Settings in the list toolbar;
  3. the base defaults (DEFAULT_CHART_SETTINGS): area fill, baseline colours, grid lines and stale gradient on, the price axis on Auto and the percentage axis on Include 0, no signals.

Saving a scope default (setGlobalSettings(settings, scope)) deletes every override of that scope, detail pages included, and leaves the other scope alone. The period is not a chart setting: dateRangeStore.svelte.ts keeps it in sessionStorage (librefolio_dateRange), shared by the Dashboard, broker, asset and FX pages of the tab.

The stored document carries a version, STORAGE_VERSION (3). When the store reads it, migratePersistedChartSettings() brings a version 1 or 2 document to version 3, in the global settings and in every override; a document of any other version is ignored, and the defaults apply. Version 3 follows the developer's decision 29, one Rolling Return measured in calendar days: the observation-count RISK_ROLLING_RETURN plugin is gone, so every saved risk-rolling-return config becomes an asset-calendar-rolling-return one. Its window param becomes window_days, with the same number; the style of its rolling_return output moves to calendar_return in componentStyles; and the secondary-axis scale saved under independent:risk_return moves to independent:calendar_return, unless that key already holds one. Every other field and every other signal stay as they were. A window of N observations thus becomes N calendar days: 30 observations of an exchange-traded asset, about 42 calendar days, become 30 days, while a crypto-asset, quoted every day, sees no change. The store writes the migrated document back to localStorage at once; chartSettingsStore.migration.test.ts covers both the function and that rewrite.

docs.title: Axis rows and ranges
docs.text:
axisScales holds one setting per axis: absolute and percentage for the primary axis, secondary[key] for the others. The detail pages and the modal build their axis rows from the primary row of the active view plus collectConfigurableSecondaryAxes() (chartCoreHelpers.ts), which lists one row per secondary axis that the overlays on screen use, keyed independent:<axisKey>, volume:<axisKey> or legacy:<index>.

Each row has three modes, resolved by buildPriceYAxis() for the primary axis and resolveSecondaryAxisScale() for the others:

  • Auto: the range of the data shown;
  • Include 0: the same range, stretched to zero;
  • Custom: the Min and Max typed in, swapped if inverted; an empty field leaves that end to the data.

No plugin bound is applied. The minimum and maximum a backend signal declares on its axis (RSI's 0–100, for example) reach the row descriptor as defaultMin / defaultMax, but no range reads them: Auto fits the data.

Min and Max are type="number" inputs with use:numericArrows (lib/actions/numericArrows.ts: ↑/↓ step by 1, a held key speeds up by powers of ten at round values, within the field's min/max when set) and the .lf-compact-number-input class (app.css: 0.75rem tabular figures). Below 768 px the iOS zoom guard (Mobile CSS) sets every input without .zoom-guard-exempt to 16 px; the class then only resets the line height.

docs.title: Signal rendering shared by cards, preview and detail pages
docs.text:
lib/charts/chartSignalRendering.ts is the one place that turns a chart's saved signals into RenderedSignal[]. It is pure (no Svelte state, no store read): the caller says where the series come from.

Function Role renderLocalSignal(config, baseData, viewMode, sources) one saved local signal, rebuilt with signalFromConfig(), given its data, rendered on baseData; nothing if the type is unknown or the series it reads is missing renderLocalSignals(configs, definitionsByType, baseData, viewMode, sources) a chart's local signals in order; backend-owned and unknown definitions are skipped renderBackendResults(configs, results, definitionsByType, baseData, viewMode, translate?) a chart's backend results in order, each drawn with the current config of its id SignalDataSources fxPairData(slug), comparisonTarget(assetId) and selfAssetId: where an FX-pair or comparison signal gets its series; NO_SIGNAL_SOURCES is the empty set

The Assets list (routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte), the FX list (routes/(app)/fx/+page.svelte) and ChartSettingsModal call these functions with their own SignalDataSources, so a signal looks the same on a card and in its preview: a comparison is named after its target, a comparison with the chart's own asset (selfAssetId) is never drawn, and an FX pair follows the direction of the card.

The two detail pages (routes/(app)/assets/[id]/+page.svelte and routes/(app)/fx/[pair]/+page.svelte) use the same functions: renderLocalSignals for their saved local signals, renderBackendResults for their backend results and, on the FX page, the module's fxPointToLineDataPoint to turn store points into chart points. They build their SignalDataSources with the pure helper detailPageSignalSources({configs, assets, fxPairPoints, selfAssetId?}) (lib/charts/chartPageSignals.ts):

  • an FX pair reads the points of the FX store, straight (the signal's own _inverted turns them), asked lazily, one pair at a time;
  • a comparison reads the series that the comparison load wrote into its config (params._resolvedData), named with icon and type by the assets the page knows (an unknown asset gets the catalogue fallback name);
  • there is no base point, because the detail pages draw daily data;
  • the asset detail page passes its own asset as selfAssetId.

So a signal looks the same on a card, in the preview and on a detail page. signalRendering.gate.test.ts keeps it that way: no file outside the module calls signalFromConfig(), and the list of known copies (KNOWN_COPIES) is empty and can only shrink.

docs.title: Series for comparisons
docs.text:
A saved comparison names its target; it never carries the series. The settings store keeps only the config (params.assetId for an asset-comparison, params.pairSlug for an fx-pair), and the renderers read the series through SignalDataSources (comparisonTarget(assetId) and fxPairData(slug), see above). A chart that holds no series of its own (the cards of both lists and the settings preview) gets them from lib/charts/comparisonSeries.ts, the one door:

Function Role comparisonTargetFromStore(asset) the asset's cached daily series as a ComparisonTarget, named with icon and type; null while the cache holds none ensureComparisonSeries(assets, range) loads what the cache lacks for the assets over range; never throws fxPairSlugsOf(configs, ownSlug?) the pairs the fx-pair signals name, once each, without the chart's own pair and without an empty one ensureSignalFxPairs(configs, ownSlug, range) loads those pairs' rates into the FX stores (ensureFxRangeLoaded); one pair failing does not stop the others; never throws
  • One request for the missing assets. ensureComparisonSeries asks POST /assets/prices/query once for all the assets whose cache has a gap in the range (in batches under the backend's caps, sendBulkBatches()), daily, include_events: false, with no conversion: the series is in the asset's own currency, as the FX detail page draws it. With nothing missing it sends nothing.
  • The cache is shared. The series are filed in assetPriceStoreRegistry, the cache of the asset detail page, so a visit there warms the lists and the reverse. A request that fails marks nothing as fetched, so the next call asks again; a 404 is final for the assets it carried.
  • The stores are not reactive. Neither the price stores nor the FX stores trigger a redraw. A page that loads series reads a version counter in its SignalDataSources and bumps it after the load: the FX list's comparisonSeriesVersion (bumped by fetchComparisonSeries(), which runs one load at a time, and asks the assets of the cards plus the one the open settings window draws) and the Assets list's fxRatesVersion (bumped by loadFxRateData(), which follows a change of period). Both lists already load every pair's rates, so they do not need ensureSignalFxPairs(); it is for a chart that loads only the pairs its signals name.
  • For all charts there is no asset to draw. The demo curve of the settings window for all charts has no real asset, so a comparison with an asset is not drawn there; the FX pairs are.
  • Contract for the detail pages (owned by another workstream, still to adopt): call ensureSignalFxPairs(signals, ownSlug, {start, end}) on open, on a period change and when a pair is chosen, then bump their overlay version. Until they do, a saved fx-pair comparison does not draw on a clean load of a detail page, only when the FX store is already warm.
  • Tests read the count, not the canvas. The cards (AssetCard, FxCard) and the settings preview (chart-settings-preview) publish data-overlay-count, the number of overlay lines they draw.

docs.title: Preview chart in the modal
docs.text:
The preview in ChartSettingsModal is PriceChartFull, the chart of the detail pages, not a bespoke LineChart. It is configured as follows:

Prop Value data the absolute series: the card's real data in pair mode, a synthetic curve in global mode externalViewMode the modal's view selector (Abs / % / Rolling Return, see Three views): the chart takes the percentage view itself externalChartType 'line' (no candlesticks) hideToolbar true chartHeight '220px' areaFill, colorByBaseline, showGridLines, showGradient the aesthetics being edited, not the saved ones yAxisMode / yAxisMin / yAxisMax, secondaryAxisScales the axis scales being edited, for the primary scale of the active view and for the secondary axes overlaySignals, overlaySignalInfoMap the preview signals and buildOverlaySignalInfoMap() of them, so a comparison shows its asset's icon and type in the tooltip like on the detail page

The modal passes no events, measure or edit props, so none of them is drawn. The mouse-wheel zoom is the chart's own inside dataZoom.

docs.title: Baseline colour on cards
docs.text:
The list cards (AssetCard, FxCard) pass colorByBaseline from the chart settings to PriceChartCompact, which forwards it to LineChart; before, compact charts ignored it. The series is green from the baseline up and red below it, with a dashed baseline line. The base is:

  • absolute view: the baselineValue prop when a page gives one, else the first non-missing point of the data the chart received. A card thins a dense series to weekly or monthly points inside LineChart, after this base is taken, so the base is the real start of the period and not the end of the first bucket;
  • percentage view: always 0, whatever baselineValue says.

baselineValue is an optional prop of LineChart, forwarded by PriceChartCompact, for a page that knows a better base than the first point of the data it hands over. No list page uses it today.

docs.title: Three views: Abs, % and Rolling Return
docs.text:
A chart's saved view is ChartSettings.primaryView (ChartPrimaryView: 'absolute' | 'percentage' | 'calendar-return', default 'percentage'), next to calendarReturnWindow and calendarReturnWindowAuto. The Assets list and the FX list use all three; the FX list opens on 'absolute' (scopeDefaultView('fx') in the store, as before), every other chart on 'percentage'. ChartSettingsModal offers the third view only when the page passes calendarPreviewResolver (otherwise it falls back to 'percentage' when a chart opens on 'calendar-return'); both lists pass it. STORAGE_VERSION is unchanged: a document saved before these fields existed is filled by the sanitiser (primaryView = 'percentage'; calendarReturnWindowAuto = true only when the stored window is the default one).

Function Role setScopePrimaryView(view, scope) the list's top bar: sets the scope default (__global_<scope>__) and resets every override of the scope to view, keeping their other fields; the other scope is untouched setItemPrimaryView(slug, view, scope?) one chart (a card's button, the detail page); an override it creates starts from the scope's settings nextCardPrimaryView(view) the card button's order: 'percentage' → 'calendar-return' → 'absolute' → 'percentage'; the button shows the view it goes to effectiveCalendarReturnWindow(settings, rangeDays) the window in force: the saved one, or, while calendarReturnWindowAuto is true, the preset chosen by largestCalendarReturnPresetFor(rangeDays) (calendarReturnWindow.ts: the largest preset whose days fit the range, the smallest when none does) detailModesForPrimaryView(view) / primaryViewForDetailModes(mode, viewMode) the mapping with the detail page's primaryMode and viewMode (below)

calendarReturnWindowAuto stays true until the user chooses a window. The rule is in the store: any save through setPairSettings or setGlobalSettings whose calendarReturnWindow differs from the one stored before sets it to false, whoever saves (modal, detail page). From then on the saved window is used as it is, whatever the period.

How the list asks for the rolling return. For a card whose view is 'calendar-return', the list (routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte) sends the card's item with a calendar signal (ASSET_CALENDAR_ROLLING_RETURN, window_days from effectiveCalendarReturnWindow() over the list's range) instead of the card's backend signals. buildReducedQuery() (lib/utils/reducedPriceQuery.ts), given the card's calendar option, adds one item for every comparison target — cached or not — as sample_like the card's item, with the same signal, include_price: false and target_currency = the card's currency, so every line has one window and one currency. The list keeps the answers per card in calendarByCard (the card's own view and its targets'), read with extractCalendarReturnView(). A card in this view draws the own points and renderCalendarComparisons(configs, views, target, fallbackName, selfAssetId) (chartSignalRendering.ts): the asset-comparison configs whose target view is ready or partial, each as a percentage line with the config's style, in the asset's name and icon; a comparison with the chart's own asset or without a ready view draws nothing. The other signals stay saved and are not requested. With no points, AssetCard shows the problem message (for example, less history than the window) instead of the chart.

The FX side. The FX list (routes/(app)/fx/+page.svelte) works the same way, with buildFxCalendarQuery() (lib/utils/reducedFxQuery.ts) over POST /fx/currencies/convert (sampling: backend FX architecture). For each card in the view it builds one conversion of 1 unit in the direction the card shows the pair (a flipped card asks the flipped rate), with the calendar signal, key fx:<slug> and max_points from the card's plot width. Every compared fx-pair signal adds a conversion of 1 unit in the direction its signal shows its pair, with the same signal and sample_like the card's key; the members of a card share a group, so bulkBatches.ts never cuts between them. The page reads the signals from signal_results, matched to its entries by request_index (local to the batch), into calendarBySlug (extractCalendarReturnView()); the rates of these conversions are never merged into the FX stores, and the cards' daily rates stay the stores' (not sampled). A card draws the own points and renderCalendarPairComparisons(configs, views) (chartSignalRendering.ts): each fx-pair signal whose view is ready or partial, as a percentage line with the signal's style; an asset comparison stays saved and is not drawn in this view (it is a percentage-return view of the pairs; the asset's line belongs to Abs and %, below). The modal's preview (resolveCalendarPreview) for one pair converts the same way; for all charts it posts the demo points to /signals/preview.

The detail page. The asset detail page opens in the view of its card: it reads primaryView with detailModesForPrimaryView(settings.primaryView) ('calendar-return' gives {primaryMode: 'calendar-return', viewMode: 'percentage'}, the two others give {primaryMode: 'price', viewMode: view}), and saves the user's change of mode or view as the card's view, primaryViewForDetailModes(primaryMode, viewMode). It saves it with setPairSettings() and the settings it holds, its signals included, not with setItemPrimaryView(), which rebuilds the override from the store's copy and would drop what the page writes into its signal configs (a comparison's _resolvedData). Its window is effectiveCalendarReturnWindow(settings, rangeDays), so the asset detail page uses the same window as the list, and a window chosen there is saved through the settings, which marks it as chosen.

docs.title: Responsive Date Axis
docs.text:
lib/components/charts/responsiveXAxis.ts (buildResponsiveXAxisPolicy()) decides how many date labels fit and how they read, in the interface locale (uiLocale()) unless a locale is passed. Two neighbouring labels never read the same (pinned in chartCoreHelpers.test.ts).

  • Compact or wide: the usable width is the chart width minus horizontalPadding, 64 px by default. The axis turns compact when that width is under 480 px, or leaves fewer than 24 px per point. A compact axis keeps 2 to 12 labels, one per 48 px on a time axis or per 56 px on a category axis: a time axis gets that count as splitNumber, a category axis with more points an interval that spreads them.
  • Compact labels: axisLabel turns on hideOverlap, showMinLabel and showMaxLabel, sets rotate: 0 and carries the formatter. A category axis also gets alignMaxLabel: 'right': the forced last label ends at its tick instead of spilling past the chart's right edge on a phone. A time axis does not: ECharts ranks time labels by tick level before hiding overlaps, so a month or year tick next to the edge would win, and the end label, pulled inward, would be the one hidden; its charts make room for the label instead (next bullet). The first label needs no alignment: it spills at most into the y-axis labels, inside the chart.
  • Zoom (category axis): an optional visibleCount, how many points a zoom leaves visible, replaces values.length in the compactness test and the interval; without it, every value counts. On the whole series, 365 daily points in 800 px get interval 33, which leaves a 34-point zoom only its edge labels; counted on that window, interval is 2. visiblePointCountFromZoom() reads the count from a dataZoom event or a {start, end} window, never from getOption(), which deep-clones the whole option. categoryAxisLabelPatch(), the axisLabel merged with setOption, puts interval: 'auto' first, so no merge keeps the previous window's step, and gives the compact keys back their ECharts defaults once the window is wide. LineChart and CandlestickChart merge it when a gesture pauses for ZOOM_LABEL_SETTLE_MS (120 ms), PriceChartFull in its 200 ms scheduleResolutionRecompute(); resizes and full renders count the visible window too. Time axes need none of it: ECharts spreads their splitNumber ticks over the visible extent.
  • Arrow markers (category axis): an overlay signal may end in an arrow (markerStart/markerEnd: 'arrow'), aimed along the line's on-screen slope, which a zoom, a pan or a resize can change. updateArrowRotations() (lineChartHelpers.ts) reads getOption(), so it re-aims them once a gesture or a resize pauses, in the settle that re-spaces the labels, which a dataZoom event or a ResizeObserver callback re-arms instead; a full render re-aims them at once, after restoring the zoom. It writes the series back only when an arrow turns by more than ARROW_ROTATE_EPSILON_DEG (0.01°), so the stability pass after a first draw and the settle after a redraw write nothing if no arrow moved. noteArrowMarkers(), called right after each full render (setOption(option, true)), records whether that option draws an arrow: on a chart without one (most charts), updateArrowRotations() returns before getOption(). It reads the option afresh on every call, so its write-back, which carries every series' colours, never brings back those from before a theme switch or a chart-colour change (pinned in LineChart.test.ts, PriceChartFull.test.ts, lineChartHelpers.test.ts and chartCoreHelpers.test.ts).
  • Right inset (time axis, compact or wide): the axis ends on the last day of the data or of the zoom, and ECharts centres that day's label on its tick, so half of it overhangs the plot's right edge. grid.containLabel: true reserves the labels' height, never that overhang, so on a phone the last label would be cut. timeAxisGridRight() takes the chart's width, the axis values, the locale, the grid's base right edge and a measure function, and returns the grid's right: half the widest label the axis can draw, rounded up, plus 2 px, when that is wider than base (px, or a percentage of width as ECharts reads it); otherwise base itself, so a desktop keeps its percentage and follows its own width. containLabel: true stays. ECharts 6's outerBoundsMode: 'same' with outerBoundsContain: 'axisLabel' was rejected: it estimates the label room once, before hideOverlap picks the ticks that survive, so on a narrower plot it cut labels that were whole and lost first labels (and containLabel: true ignores the outerBounds* keys). The price is a narrower plot on a phone (about 13–15 px in the dashboard charts, 4–5 px in LotComparisonChart), so sometimes one label fewer; hideOverlap may still hide the end label when the previous tick sits too close: a missing label, never a cut one.
  • Inset candidates (timeAxisLabelCandidates, cached for up to 16 locale-and-range keys): the widest label is taken over every text buildTimeAxisFormatter (below) can write, compact or wide, on an axis whose data runs from the first to the last of values. These are the two end days in the endpoint format (day and month, plus the two-digit year when the range crosses a calendar year), and the label of each local midnight from the day before the first to the day after the last, since zoom can put the axis edge on any day of the data and ECharts widens a one-day extent by a day on each side: 15 Jul on a day other than the 1st, 2026 on 1 January, both Aug and 1 Aug on another 1st (in en-GB). Past 366 days, every day of a leap year (2024) stands in for the calendar, except 1 January, which adds the year of each real one in range.
