docs.title: 📅 CalendarMonth
docs.text:
A monthly calendar grid component — the visual building block for date pickers.

  • Displays a single month with day cells
  • Highlights today, selected date, and date range
  • Keyboard navigation within the grid
  • Locale-aware (week starts on Monday for most locales)
  • The pending day (highlights.pending, the day of a first click in DateRangePicker) cannot be chosen again: it is a disabled button with the not-allowed cursor, as a future day is, while its colour and its data-state stay those of the pending day. The click handler refuses it as well, as it refuses disabledDates, because a dispatched click (what Testing Library's fireEvent.click sends in jsdom) still reaches a disabled button's handlers. SingleDatePicker never sets pending, so its grid is unaffected.

Used by: SingleDatePicker, DateRangePicker.

docs.title: 📆 SingleDatePicker
docs.text:
A single-date picker dropdown with calendar.

  • Opens a CalendarMonth in a dropdown
  • Manual text input with date parsing
  • Month/year navigation with arrows
  • Formats date according to locale

Used by:

  • DataEditor — the date of a newly added row; the dates already in the series are disabled
  • BrokerForm — Account Opened, never in the future
  • TransactionFormModal — the transaction date and, for a pair, the To side's own date
  • EventCreateMiniModal — the date of an asset event created inline from the transaction form
  • ScheduledInvestmentEditor — the date of each event row of the schedule
  • BoundaryDateModal — the boundary date(s) that ScheduledInvestmentEditor asks for when it deletes or splits a period

docs.title: 📅 DateRangePicker
docs.text:
A date range picker with start and end dates.

  • Two CalendarMonth grids side by side (current + next month)
  • Visual highlight of selected range
  • Quick presets: 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, YTD and MAX, plus a custom window (an amount and a granularity). 3Y, 5Y, 10Y, MTD, QTD and WTD fill the toolbar only when a JS measurement finds room to spare, never at the cost of an extra line (DateRangePicker.svelte:36,216-251)
  • Start and end date text inputs

Used by:

  • Page toolbars — the period of the Dashboard, broker detail, FX list, FX detail, Assets list and asset detail pages (Pages)
  • MeasurePanel — the two dates of a measure, without presets, while its row is expanded
  • DataTableColumnFilter — the filter of a date column, where either end may stay blank
  • CellDateRange — the Period cell of each row in ScheduledInvestmentEditor's period table (Scheduled Investment Provider)
  • L4Replay — the replay period, with quick ranges but no MAX

docs.title: 🚫 No range of a single day
docs.text:
A range always spans two different days (lot Y-N65, developer decision of 2026-10-19): every way into the picker refuses an end on the other end's day. The comparison is between real dates only: a blank end, or a min/max sentinel, never matches a date.

  • Calendar. The first click leaves its day pending (pendingDate, handed to both grids as highlights.pending, which disables it). handleDayClick ignores a second click on that day: nothing is published, the calendar stays open and the day stays pending. The next different day clicked closes the range, sorted. handleDayHover previews the range from the pending day to the day under the pointer, and nothing while the pointer is on the pending day itself.
  • Typed date. isAcceptableDate(which, iso) is the calendar's ceiling (isSelectableDate: no future day unless allowFuture) plus "not the other end's day". A date equal to the other end is refused like a typed future date: it stays in its field, turns red once armed (blur or Enter, data-invalid="true"), and nothing is published. It is applied as soon as the other end moves to another day: applyRangeDate takes the waiting date (waitingTypedDate) together with the new one, as a pair, and the usual swap orders the two dates the user wrote. Typing «From» as the old «To», then a new «To», applies both at once.
  • ↑/↓ on a field. A step that would land on the other end's day goes one day further in the same direction, and the swap still applies. When that further day is a future day the picker refuses, the step does nothing.

Open ends. A date typed while the other end is blank, or holds the min/max sentinel of MAX («All»), leaves that end as it is. Before Y-N65 the other end was filled with the same date, a range of one day.

Range before Date typed Published Meaning ('', '') «From» X (X, '') from X on ('', '') «To» X ('', X) up to X ('min', 'max') «From» X (X, 'max') from X to today ('min', 'max') «To» X ('min', X) from the first data up to X

A blank end is the open range of a date column filter. The pages resolve the sentinels as they always have, through resolveDateSentinel (lib/stores/dateRangeStore.svelte.ts), then the first date of their data for min.

Ranges of one day saved earlier still load and work as they are: the page period in sessionStorage (librefolio_dateRange) or in the URL (?start=&end=), a table filter in the URL, a scheduled-investment period. Only new ones can no longer be made.

The cases are pinned in DateRangePicker.test.ts and CalendarMonth.test.ts (their Y-N65 describes).

docs.title: 💬 Feedback & Notifications
docs.text: Components for user notifications, contextual information, loading states, and tooltips.

docs.title: 🔔 ToastContainer
docs.text:
Global container for toast notifications (success, error, info, warning). Components never mount it: they call the store toasts (lib/stores/app/toastStore.svelte.ts).

import {toasts} from '$lib/stores/app/toastStore.svelte';

toasts.success('Saved');
toasts.error('Sync failed', 20000); // custom duration in ms
  • Position: stacked at the top centre of the viewport (fixed top-4 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2, z-[9999]), newest last, each sliding in from above.
  • Auto-dismiss after a per-variant default — success and info 8 s, warning 10 s, error 15 s — or the duration passed to the call; a thin bar counts the time down. A duration of 0 keeps the toast until it is dismissed.
  • Dismiss: the ✕ button (toast-dismiss), which stays the keyboard- and screen-reader path, or a swipe of at least 60 px left, right or up (pointer events: finger, pen and mouse).
  • Color-coded by variant, with a matching icon; test ids toast-{variant}.
  • The store also offers show(variant, message, duration?), dismiss(id) and clear(); toasts are cleared when the signed-in account changes (client-session reset, e.g. logout).

docs.title: 🧼 HTML messages
docs.text:
A message may contain markup — flags, coloured badges, icons, links — and is rendered with {@html sanitizeHtml(message)} (lib/utils/core/sanitizeHtml.ts, DOMPurify): the markup is kept, event-handler attributes, <script> and javascript: URLs are dropped. Sanitising is the safety net, not a licence: escape any user or provider text you put into a message with escapeHtml.

Links inside a toast work like normal links. A press that starts on a link (or a button) never starts a swipe, so tapping it navigates instead of dragging the toast away. Build links to detail pages with entityDetailLinkHtml({kind: 'asset', id} | {kind: 'fx', slug}, label) (lib/utils/core/entityLink.ts): it accepts only those two routes and escapes the label. ToastContainer.test.ts covers both contracts.

Used by: mounted once in the authenticated layout, routes/(app)/+layout.svelte.

docs.title: ℹ️ InfoBanner
docs.text:
An inline banner for contextual information or warnings (ui/feedback/InfoBanner.svelte).

  • variant: info (default), warning, error, success — colours and default icon (showIcon, default true)
  • Content from message or from the children; with message, the banner hides itself when the value is empty or null
  • dismissible adds an ✕ that calls ondismiss
  • role="alert" for error, role="status" otherwise; test id info-banner-{variant}
  • Inline within page content (not a toast)

Used by: BrokerModal (validation errors), settings tabs, the sync and import modals, RegisterCard.

docs.title: 🛡️ DataQualityBanner
docs.text:
The unified data quality banner component for surfacing data warnings across the dashboard, asset detail, and forex detail pages. Replaces ad-hoc inline banners with a standardized DataQualityIssue model.

See DataQualityBanner Developer Manual for full documentation.

Modes:

  • grouped — dashboard: single container with all issues sorted by severity
  • flat — detail pages: one banner per issue

CTA: actions are emitted via onaction(action, target, issue) — the component does not navigate or open modals directly.

Used by: Dashboard (/dashboard), Asset detail (/assets/:id), FX detail (/fx/:pair), and the risk panels (RiskAnalysisPanel, AssetSetRiskPanel, RiskPanelHeader).

docs.title: ⏳ LoadingSpinner
docs.text:
A simple animated spinner for async loading states (ui/feedback/LoadingSpinner.svelte).

  • size: sm, md (default), lg — the vertical padding around it
  • text below the spinner, defaulting to the translated common.loading
  • role="status", aria-live="polite"

Used by: API calls, lazy-loaded content, search results.

docs.title: 💡 Tooltip
docs.text:
Hover/tap tooltip with automatic positioning (ui/feedback/Tooltip.svelte).

  • Content: text, or html (rendered through sanitizeHtml); math renders inline $…$ LaTeX with KaTeX
  • Positions: top (default), bottom, left, right — flips when it would leave the viewport; the tooltip is moved to document.body and drawn with fixed positioning, so a modal's overflow or a parent's opacity never affects it
  • Plain hover opens after showDelayMs (default 500 ms), so crossing the page does not flash tooltips; a click, a tap or Enter/Space on the focused trigger opens it at once and pins it
  • A pinned tooltip stays while the pointer is on the trigger or on the tooltip itself; it closes on a second click on the trigger, on a click outside, or 30 s after contact ends
  • interactiveChild: when the child is itself a button or a link, the wrapper does not add its own role="button" and tab stop

Used by: Toolbar buttons, icon-only buttons, info badges, DocsLink.

docs.title: 📤 File Upload & Media Components
docs.text: Status: Implemented and documented (Feb 2026)

docs.title: 📖 Overview
docs.text: Comprehensive file upload system with image editing, asset picking, and multi-file support.

docs.title: ⬆️ FileUploader (ui/media/FileUploader.svelte)
docs.text:
Multi-file uploader with:

  • Drag & drop support
  • Click to browse
  • File type & size validation
  • Edit (✏️) per pending file — on an image the button is titled Edit: it dispatches editImage and the host opens ImageEditModal. On any other file it is titled Rename: it dispatches editFile and the host opens FileEditModal. The edited file replaces the pending one (replaceFile()). Nothing opens on its own: on Upload the host receives the pending files as they are (the Files page's pendingImageFiles queue in routes/(app)/files/+page.svelte is never filled)
  • Restore original (↩️) on every edited file, cropped or renamed (editedIndices), Remove on every file
  • Preview for images via backend thumbnail API

Hosts:

  • Files page, Static Resources — on:upload sends each file through uploadFile(file, undefined, 'personal'): a file uploaded there is personal (see Scope of uploaded files).
  • Files page, Broker Reports (accept=".csv,.xlsx,.xls") — the selection opens the Assign Brokers dialog: one broker per file or Assign all to, pre-filled when the user can edit exactly one broker (Viewer brokers are left out), and Upload (n) enabled only once every file has a broker. All the files of one confirmation share a batch_id (generateUUID()), so they form one report set.
  • BrokerImportFilesModal — the report files of one broker.

docs.title: ✂️ ImageCropper (ui/media/ImageCropper.svelte)
docs.text:
cropperjs v2 based image cropper (Web Components):

  • Free crop with L-shaped corner handles
  • Zoom (overlay buttons and mouse wheel) works on the selection first: zoom-in shrinks it by 10% until it covers 50% of the image (MIN_SELECTION_COVERAGE), then zooms the image by 0.1; zoom-out enlarges it by 10% up to 90% (MAX_SELECTION_COVERAGE), then zooms the image out
  • Rotation (15° steps, −15° / +15°) relative to selection center
  • Flip horizontal/vertical
  • Aspect ratio given by the host (aspectRatio; 0 or NaN = free); the ratio buttons live in ImageEditModal
  • Selection clamped to canvas bounds
  • Middle-mouse-button drag for background translation

docs.title: 🖼️ ImageEditModal (ui/media/ImageEditModal.svelte)
docs.text:
Full image editing modal (extends ModalBase):

It opens only when a host asks: the ✏️ Edit button of FileUploader (Files page), or the upload path of ImagePickerWrapper (below) — never by itself when a file is picked.

  • Confirm button — Crop & Upload when uploadOnComplete is true (the default, used by ImagePickerWrapper); Crop when it is false, as on the Files page after ✏️, where the cropped file goes back to the pending list
  • Scope — the scope prop (default common) goes to uploadFile() on Crop & Upload. ImagePickerWrapper keeps the default, so an image uploaded through a picker is common; the Files page passes personal, though with uploadOnComplete false the modal uploads nothing itself
  • Presets (IMAGE_PRESETS in lib/utils/files/imageCrop.ts): buttons Avatar (200×200), Icon (broker-icon, 64×64) and Custom (free size), shown while allowPresetChange (default true). The asset-icon preset (256×256) has no button: only a host can set it
  • Round preview — a toggle for the ellipse overlay, on by default for Avatar and Icon
  • Ratio buttons 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, 3:4 and Free, shown only with Custom
  • Output — width and height are capped at the selection and keep its ratio; Scale goes from 0.01 to 1
  • Format — .png, .jpg or .webp, defaulting to the source file's type. Quality (JPEG and WebP only) moves with −/+ in 10-point steps from 10 to 100, default 90
  • Reset All (header) puts zoom, rotation and flip back and re-centres the selection (resetAll())
  • Closing with changes asks Discard changes? — Discard & Close

docs.title: 📄 FileEditModal (ui/media/FileEditModal.svelte)
docs.text:
Simple file rename modal (extends ModalBase):

  • Rename file before upload
  • Used for PDFs, CSVs, and other non-image files
  • Also available for BRIM import files
  • scope (default none: the backend's rule decides) goes to uploadFile() when uploadOnComplete is true. The Files page passes personal. With uploadOnComplete false — the Files page after ✏️, BrokerImportFilesModal — nothing is uploaded: the renamed file goes back to the pending list

docs.title: 🔎 AssetPickerModal (ui/media/AssetPickerModal.svelte)
docs.text:
3-tab asset picker modal (extends ModalBase):

  • Existing: Browse uploaded files with DataTable or FileGrid: the common files and the user's own personal ones, even for an administrator, whose GET /uploads lists every file. The list loads once per opening (existingLoaded). Confirming a personal file shares it first (D36-1, below)
  • URL: Enter a URL with live preview and circular overlay
  • Upload: dispatches upload with the picked image; the host (ImagePickerWrapper) opens ImageEditModal, which uploads it common

Used for: broker icons, user avatars, and any image URL field.

docs.title: 📸 ImagePickerWrapper (ui/media/ImagePickerWrapper.svelte)
docs.text:
(This component is an invisible logic wrapper and has no UI of its own) Wraps the full AssetPicker → ImageEdit flow:

  • Opens AssetPickerModal
  • If upload selected → opens ImageEditModal, with its default scope common
  • Returns final URL to parent

docs.title: 👤 UserAvatar (ui/media/UserAvatar.svelte)
docs.text:
An account's avatar in a 24 px circle, or its initial when it has none (lot N69-4, decision D8 a). Its one host today is the UserRow of the Users tab.

  • Props: username, avatarUrl (string | null, the account's avatar_url) and testId, the data-testid of its root. The root carries data-avatar="image" or data-avatar="initial".
  • An image uploaded to the app, an avatarUrl starting with /api/v1/uploads/, is asked for as its 48×48 preview, sharp on a 2× screen: img_preview=48x48 is appended after ?, or after & when the address already has a query. Any other address is used as it is. The image is a LazyImage (circle, placeholder="avatar", the username as alt), so the preview of an uploaded file goes through the preview cache (imagePreviewCache).
  • Without an avatar (null or empty): the first character of the trimmed username, upper-cased (? for an empty name), on a neutral disc: the scheme of the user pickers (UserSearchSelect), the roles bg-lf-neutral and text-lf-muted, with no colour of its own per user; the letter is aria-hidden.
  • Tests: lib/features/settings/users/UserRow.avatar.test.ts (URA-01 to URA-04, in ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit) mounts it through the row, with the real LazyImage and a fetch that never answers: the image asked for, the initial, and the toggle still opening its panel.

docs.title: 📁 FileGrid (files/FileGrid.svelte)
docs.text:
Shared grid view component used in both /files page and AssetPickerModal.

  • mode="browse" with showActions (the Files page): each card offers Download, Preview (when the file has one), Copy Link, the scope switch and Delete. The switch (file-grid-scope-<id>, with data-scope) needs the onscopechange prop and a file whose can_delete is not false; it calls onscopechange({file, scope}) with the opposite scope: the lock icon of a common file asks for personal, the users icon of a personal one for common. Delete (file-grid-delete-<id>, ondelete({id})) shows on the same can_delete condition. The cards carry no scope badge: the list view shows it
  • mode="select" (AssetPickerModal, showActions={false}): single selection, no actions

docs.title: 📋 FilesTable (files/FilesTable.svelte)
docs.text:
The DataTable of the Files page, both tabs, and of a broker's Uploaded Reports: type="static" or type="brim". The Report set badges of type="brim" are in Badges in FilesTable.

  • Visibility column (scope, type="static" only): a badge, info for a common file (Shared) and default for a personal one (Personal), with an enum filter on the two values, URL key scope
  • Row actions share and makePersonal (type="static", only with the onScopeChange prop): share on a personal file calls onScopeChange(file, 'common'), makePersonal on a common one onScopeChange(file, 'personal'); both only when the file's can_delete is not false
  • Delete row action: hidden when the row's can_delete is false, on both types (UploadFileInfo.can_delete; can_delete of the GET /brokers/import/files items). The bulk delete belongs to the host's SelectionBar: the Files page leaves those files out (below), BrokerImportFilesModal sends them and the server refuses them with 403

docs.title: 🔐 Scope of uploaded files
docs.text:
Every static upload is common (every signed-in user sees it) or personal (its uploader and the admins): developer decision 36. The backend rule, older files included, is in Uploaded Files: Common and Personal; the frontend chooses the scope of what it uploads, and lets the user change it.

Client — frontend/src/lib/utils/files/upload.ts, with the type UploadScope (UploadedFile['scope']: 'common' | 'personal') in frontend/src/lib/types/files.ts:

  • uploadFile(file, description?, scope?) — POST /api/v1/uploads, returns the file's URL. The multipart field scope is sent only when given; without it, the backend's rule decides (images common, the rest personal)
  • setUploadScope(fileId, scope) — PATCH /api/v1/uploads/{id} with {scope}, returns the UploadedFile as the backend now describes it. Only the uploader and the admins may: anyone else gets 403 or 404

Who uploads with which scope:

Upload scope sent Files page, Static Resources (handleUpload in routes/(app)/files/+page.svelte) personal An image picker: ImagePickerWrapper → ImageEditModal with its default scope (ProfileTab and WelcomePage avatars, BrokerForm icon, AssetModal icon) common ImageEditModal and FileEditModal on the Files page personal, though after ✏️ they upload nothing (uploadOnComplete false) FileEditModal at its default scope (BrokerImportFilesModal, which uploads nothing through it) none: the backend's rule

Files page (routes/(app)/files/+page.svelte):

  • FilesTable's onScopeChange and FileGrid's onscopechange both go to requestScopeChange(file, scope). common is applied at once; personal first opens a warning ConfirmModal (files-scope-confirm), since the other users lose the file, also where it serves as an icon or a photo. applyScopeChange() calls setUploadScope() and puts the returned file in place of the row
  • the scope URL filter (urlFilterColumns) also filters the grid view (staticGridColumns)
  • the bulk delete (handleBulkDeleteFiles, both tabs) deletes only the selected files whose can_delete is not false (deletableSelection()); the others stay, reported by file.delete.skipped with a warning toast

Image picker (AssetPickerModal). What a picker returns is shown to other users, so a personal image picked there becomes common, with a notice (D36-1):

  • the Existing tab keeps the common files and the user's own: scope === 'common', or uploaded_by_user_id equal to the id of currentUser (lib/stores/app/auth)
  • confirming a personal file, necessarily the user's own, first calls setUploadScope(id, 'common'), and dispatches select only once that succeeds, with file.scope.shared-on-pick and an info toast. On failure: file.scope.change.failed with an error toast, no select, and the picker stays open. Use Selected is disabled meanwhile (confirming)
  • a common file is handed back at once, its scope untouched

App events — through notify() (lib/stores/app/notify.svelte.ts), kept in window.__lf.events for the E2E; the toast is a field of the same call:

Event Emitted by detail Toast file.scope.changed Files page {fileId, scope} success: uploads.scope.nowShared or uploads.scope.nowPersonal file.scope.change.failed Files page; AssetPickerModal {fileId, scope, reason}; {fileId, scope: 'common'} error: uploads.scope.changeFailed file.scope.shared-on-pick AssetPickerModal {fileId} info: uploads.scope.sharedOnPick file.delete.skipped Files page, bulk delete {count, isBrim} warning: uploads.deleteSkipped

The page's other file events (file.uploaded, file.upload.failed, file.deleted, file.deleted.bulk, file.delete.failed) carry no toast. The texts are the uploads.scope.* keys of frontend/src/lib/i18n/files/<lang>.json.

docs.title: 🖥️ Backend Support
docs.text:
• Image preview API: GET /api/v1/uploads/file/{id}?img_preview=WxH, answered with Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600
  • File serving: GET /api/v1/uploads/file/{id} sends Content-Disposition: inline for the stored types of INLINE_SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES (PDF, JSON, plain text, CSV and the common images), so the PDF fallback of the preview, an <iframe>, displays instead of downloading; any other type and ?download=true are an attachment, and every response carries X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (H6-2, How a file is served)
  • Preview cache: Size-based (PREVIEW_CACHE_MAX_MB in .env, default 50MB), TTL 1h, invalidated on delete
  • No-op for small images: If requested size ≥ original, serves file directly without processing
  • Scope: every upload is common (every signed-in user sees it) or personal (its uploader and the admins). POST /api/v1/uploads takes an optional multipart field scope; without it, a file whose validated type (below) is image/* is stored common and any other file personal. PATCH /api/v1/uploads/{id} with {"scope": "common"} or {"scope": "personal"} changes it, for the uploader or an admin. Every UploadFileInfo carries scope and can_delete: whether the requesting user may delete the file and change its scope. The full rule, older files included: Uploaded Files: Common and Personal
  • Seed avatars: 30 default avatar PNGs copied to custom-uploads/ on first startup via seed_default_avatars(), with uploader 0 (the system): they are common
  • Off the event loop: the handlers of uploaded files (api/v1/uploads.py) run the service's synchronous disk work (save_upload, list_uploads, get_upload_info, get_upload_path, set_upload_scope, delete_upload) through asyncio.to_thread
  • Upload utility: uploadFile() in frontend/src/lib/utils/files/upload.ts — single FormData creation point; setUploadScope() sits beside it (see Scope of uploaded files)
  • Size formatting: Centralized i18n-aware formatBytes() in the same frontend/src/lib/utils/files/upload.ts

docs.title: ✅ Validation
docs.text:
Client side (FileUploader):

  • File type checking against accept prop
  • File size checking against global max_file_upload_mb setting

Server side:

  • Size — get_max_upload_mb() (max_file_upload_mb, default 10) is enforced on both POST /uploads and POST /brokers/import/upload: 413 above the limit.
  • Static files (validate_upload_security() in services/files/static_uploads.py) — the extension must not be in BLOCKED_EXTENSIONS (.exe, .dll, .sh, .py, .js, .jar, …); when python-magic (libmagic) loads, the content's detected type must not be in BLOCKED_MIME_TYPES, otherwise the type is guessed from the extension (mimetypes). A declared type that differs from the detected one is only logged. A refused file returns 400.
  • Static delete and scope change — DELETE and PATCH /uploads/{id} belong to the uploader or a superuser. Another user gets 403 on a common file (Cannot delete files uploaded by other users, Cannot change files uploaded by other users) and, on a personal one, the 404 of a file that does not exist. The UI offers delete and the scope switch only on a file whose can_delete is not false (FilesTable, FileGrid).
  • Broker reports — EDITOR or OWNER on the target broker (403), an empty file is refused (400), batch_id must be a UUID (422). There is no server-side extension check: only the uploader's accept limits them to CSV and Excel.

The two families differ deliberately: someone else's personal static file answers 404, so its existence is not revealed, while the broker report routes answer 403 to a user without access to the file's broker.

docs.title: 🏗️ ModalBase
docs.text: The foundation for all modals in LibreFolio. It renders nothing while open is false; when open it draws a backdrop (role="dialog", aria-modal="true") and the content box, and injects the caller's content as children.

docs.title: 📋 Props
docs.text: Prop Type Default Description open boolean false Shows the modal. onRequestClose () => void no-op Called when the user asks to close: backdrop click or Escape. The modal never closes itself — the parent decides and sets open to false. closeOnBackdropClick boolean true Whether a backdrop click calls onRequestClose. closeOnEscape boolean true Whether Escape calls onRequestClose. trapFocus boolean false Opt-in: focus moves to the first focusable control and Tab / Shift+Tab wrap inside the modal. restoreFocus boolean false Opt-in: focus returns to the element that had it when the modal opened, once it closes. labelledBy string — Id of the title element, set as aria-labelledby. zIndex number 50 Stacking level: 50 first-level, 60 second-level, 70 third-level. maxWidth string 'lg' A preset (sm…6xl, also as max-w-*, or none) or any CSS length. allowOverflow boolean false Lets the content box overflow, for dropdowns inside compact modals. noTransition boolean false Skips the fade (backdrop, 150 ms) and scale (content, 200 ms) transitions. contentClass string '' Extra classes on the content box. testId string '' data-testid of the backdrop element.

docs.title: ⚙️ Behaviour
docs.text:
• Backdrop click closes only when both the press and the release land on the backdrop, so a text selection dragged out of the content does not close the modal.
  • Escape is handled on the modal's own backdrop element and stops propagating: in a stack, only the topmost modal reacts.
  • Focus: on open the backdrop itself takes focus, so keyboard events reach the modal. Focus trapping and focus restoration are opt-in (trapFocus, restoreFocus), off by default for the existing callers; PlannerDialog (PAC planner) and SocialShareModal turn both on. ModalBase.test.ts pins the two behaviours.
  • Scroll lock: the page is frozen at its scroll position (position: fixed plus a negative top) while any modal is open. A counter on document.body.dataset.modalScrollLockCount makes stacked modals share one lock; the last one to close restores the scroll position. The app header watches the same counter to stay visible while a modal is open.
<ModalBase {open} onRequestClose={() => (open = false)} maxWidth="2xl" labelledBy="my-title" trapFocus restoreFocus>
    <h2 id="my-title">…</h2>
</ModalBase>

docs.title: ⚠️ ConfirmModal
docs.text: A confirmation dialog on ModalBase, for destructive actions, discard flows and operation results. It is exported from $lib/components/table as well.

docs.title: 🎨 Variants
docs.text:
The confirm button takes one of three colours; the header shows a warning icon in the same tone for the last two.

Props Confirm button Use it for default (danger={false}, warning={false}) Primary (brand green) Plain confirmations danger Red Destructive actions: deletions warning Amber Non-destructive but attention-worthy actions: discarding a draft

danger wins when both are set.

docs.title: 📋 Props
docs.text:
Prop Type Default Description open boolean Required Shows the modal. title, message string Required Header and body text. description string '' Secondary text under the message; descriptionItalic sets it in italics. items, itemsLabel string[], string [], '' Collapsible list of the affected items; a single item is always shown. confirmText, cancelText string common.confirm, common.cancel Button labels. danger, warning boolean false See Variants. onConfirm () => void Required Confirm button. onCancel () => void Required Cancel button, the ✕ in the header, Escape and backdrop click. zIndex number 60 Above a first-level modal. results {label, success, detail?, action?}[] [] Results mode, see below. testId string '' Identifies which confirmation is on screen (on the header).

The buttons carry stable test ids: confirm-modal-confirm, confirm-modal-cancel and, in results mode, confirm-modal-close.

docs.title: 📊 Results mode
docs.text:
When results is not empty, the body lists one row per item — ✅ or ❌, the label, then the detail — and the footer keeps a single Close button, which calls onCancel.

  • detail is rendered as text: markup coming from the backend stays inert.
  • action ({href, label, testId?}) adds a link at the end of the row. Deleting an asset that still has transactions uses it: the ❌ row links to the Transactions page filtered on that asset.

docs.title: 🗑️ Discard-draft flows
docs.text:
A modal or panel holding unsaved edits asks before throwing them away: it opens a ConfirmModal with warning (amber), and confirmText set to Discard. The global settings tab (lib/features/settings/tabs/GlobalSettingsTab.svelte) is the reference: locking the panel with pending edits opens the confirmation.

  • Confirm discards the draft and completes the action (closes the parent, locks the panel).
  • Cancel, ✕, Escape and backdrop click all reach onCancel, which only closes the confirmation: the draft is kept and the parent stays as it was. GlobalSettingsTab.test.ts checks the four paths, and that a second request still finds the same draft.

Implement onCancel as "close this dialog" and nothing else — never as "discard".

Used by: DataTable (row and bulk actions with requireConfirm), the discard confirmations of GlobalSettingsTab, BrokerSharingModal, FxPairAddModal, ChartSettingsModal, DataImportModal and ImportWizardModal, and the delete flows of the Assets and FX pages.

docs.title: 🔄 Sync modals
docs.text:
SyncModalBase.svelte is the shared shell of the provider-sync dialogs: header, date-range bar, timeout setting, progress bar with countdown, one result list per section, per-item and retry-all-failed actions, and a summary. Each specialization passes SyncSection[] with its own sync function and result-row snippet; sections without targets are hidden, and all sections run in parallel under one countdown. Closing the modal does not cancel the backend request, but each opening is a new session: a late answer from an abandoned run is not shown in the next one.

The Timeout field (default max(20, item count) s) drives the countdown and the limit of every request, retries included: syncRequestTimeoutMs() (utils/sync/syncHelpers.ts) hands each section's sync function max(120 s, field + 5 s), and the timeout message names that limit, which can be longer than the field.

Component Syncs Used by AssetSyncModal (components/assets/) Asset prices Assets list FxSyncModal (components/fx/) FX rates FX list, transaction form, PAC planner PageSyncModal (ui/modals/) Asset prices and the FX pairs they need, in parallel Asset detail, FX detail, risk panels

PageSyncModal reports onsynced({accepted}): accepted is true when at least one item of the current run came back ok or partial, so callers refresh only after a run that changed something. SyncResultRow.svelte renders one result line for the three modals.

The warning before the start (C-66). A sync replaces the stored rows of its period with the provider's values, manual edits included. A section's optional existingIds lists the targets whose shown data already holds a stored row in the period. Before Start, SyncModalBase shows one warning per active section whose targets meet it (data-testid="{testId}-overwrite-warning", with data-section, data-existing and data-total; the section title leads it only when several sections are active), and hides it once the run starts. The pages compute the ids from what they already show, with hasStoredPointInRange() (utils/sync/syncHelpers.ts): a point counts unless it was filled backward from an earlier date (extractDaysBack(), utils/assetPriceDerived.ts, the one home of that rule). AssetSyncModal and FxSyncModal take them as withDataInRange, PageSyncModal as assetsWithDataInRange and fxPairsWithDataInRange. The Assets and FX pages pass them, and so do the detail pages for their own asset or pair and their pairs. A compared asset is not counted, and the transaction form, the PAC planner and the risk panels pass none, so they show no warning.

docs.title: 🔽 Select & Dropdown Components
docs.text:
This section documents the reusable dropdown and select components in lib/components/ui/select/.

There is no shared base component: SimpleSelect, SearchSelect and TreeSelect each self-contain their open/close state, click-outside dismissal, keyboard navigation, and dropdown positioning (position: fixed, so the dropdown is never clipped by overflow parents). The shared logic that exists lives in plain TypeScript — optionFilter.ts (filtering, ranking and keyboard-step helpers: SearchSelect uses all of them, SimpleSelect the step helpers), types.ts (SelectOption) and treeSelect.ts (the tree shapes of TreeSelect). Every specialized select composes one of the generic ones — except FxProviderSelect, a self-contained route picker, and AssetPickerPanel, built on SelectPopover.

Generic selects, then domain-specific wrappers:
