  • Backend Sync: Most reference and domain stores wrap API calls, automatically fetching data on mount and pushing updates back to the Python backend.

Next Steps: Dive into the specific categories using the navigation menu to understand the internal structure of each subsystem.

docs.title: 📱 App & UI State
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (Feb 2026)

The App & UI State category contains stores responsible for the global user experience. These stores manage authentication, global preferences, localization, shell navigation, and the public configuration, notices and block state of the instance.

docs.title: 🗂️ Stores
docs.text: Store File Purpose Auth app/auth.ts Holds the session state — the current user (null when signed out) and the loading, error and initialized flags — through login(), logout() and checkAuth() (GET /auth/me). The session itself is the HttpOnly session cookie the backend sets: the frontend never sees the token. The user is the backend's AuthUserResponse, whats_new included: {since, release} while changelog chapters are left for the user to see after an update, null otherwise, which the What's new store reads. Settings app/settings.ts User-specific preferences (language, theme, base currency, avatar). Syncs with the backend. Global Settings app/globalSettings.ts Application-wide settings (admin-only writes), like max upload sizes, loaded by the app bootstrap. It no longer types enable_registration, and nothing reads the registration mode from it: the login page asks the instance configuration instead, which holds the mode in force, LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION included. Language app/language.ts The interface language. currentLanguage.set() also sets the svelte-i18n locale and saves the choice in this browser (librefolio-locale), which the next load starts from. Nothing listens to the Settings store: the language is set explicitly — by the auth store at login, from the user's settings in the login response, and by the UI: the Preferences tab and the Welcome page after their write, or the header selector (this browser only). Interface locale app/uiLocale.ts The locale every figure is written in: the interface language, plus the browser's region when the browser's primary tag is in that language. Derived from Language, so it follows every switch. Two faces: uiLocale() for runes code and as the default of every figure formatter; uiLocaleStore, read as $uiLocaleStore in a legacy template. See Numbers, amounts and dates. Theme app/themeStore.ts Manages dark/light mode toggling and system-preference detection. Privacy app/privacyStore.svelte.ts Device-local "hide amounts" flag, read inside the currency formatters. See Privacy masking. Navigation app/navigationStore.ts Controls the sidebar state (open/closed) and active page tracking. Toasts app/toastStore.svelte.ts Svelte 5 Rune-based store for displaying global notification messages. Page busy app/pageBusy.svelte.ts The «big» requests the page on screen has in flight, which its Refresh button waits for (busy). Scoped to the page: reset on a route change and when the client session ends. See Page busy. Instance configuration $lib/features/instance/instanceConfig.svelte.ts The public configuration of the instance (GET /api/v1/system/instance), read once per page load, before the sign-in. See Instance configuration. Instance notices $lib/features/instance/instanceNotices.svelte.ts The messages about the instance that features register, shown above every page of the app shell. See Instance notices. Instance block $lib/features/instance/instanceBlockState.ts, $lib/features/instance/instanceBlock.svelte.ts Whether the hosting provider blocked the instance: the first 423 instance_blocked from the API turns it on, and the (app) layout then shows the block page instead of the app. The plain module (no runes) holds the state, which the API client marks; the .svelte.ts module is its reactive face, which the layout reads. See Instance block. What's new $lib/features/changelog/whatsNewStore.svelte.ts Whether the «What's new» window is due (lot C-54): the signed-in user's whats_new names released chapters of the bundled changelog, and the window was not closed on this page load. dismiss() hides it and posts POST /auth/whats-new/seen. See What's new. Changelog window $lib/features/changelog/changelogModalStore.svelte.ts Whether the app's one changelog window is open (lot A-CL1). The Sidebar mounts the only ChangelogModal, bound to changelogModal.open; the sidebar's version and the version in Settings → About open it with show(), its close calls close(), and the Sidebar closes it when it unmounts, so it lives as long as the app shell. The chapters it shows come from localizedChangelog, whose cache of loaded translations is a SvelteMap: a window waiting for a language sees the load that fills it, its own or another's. Chart Settings chartSettingsStore.svelte.ts Chart preferences of the FX and Assets pages: line colouring, area fill, grid lines, stale-data gradient, axis scales, the asset Calendar Return window and overlay signals. Kept per user in localStorage (lf_{userId}_chartSettingsStore), never on the server, in two separate scopes, fx and assets: each has its own global settings plus per-item overrides (pair slug, asset-{id}), and applying a scope's global settings clears that scope's per-item overrides. The chart period is not stored here: it lives in sessionStorage (Date Range, below). Date Range dateRangeStore.svelte.ts The date range (start, end) shared by the Dashboard (through dateRangeController.svelte.ts), the broker detail page, and the Assets and FX pages, list and detail. It lives in sessionStorage (librefolio_dateRange), so it belongs to the browser tab and survives a reload; on a full page load, start and end in the URL win, and it falls back to the last three months when the account changes.

docs.title: 📐 Architecture & Flow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows how the stores are filled and who sets the language and the theme. Once the auth check succeeds, the (app) layout's appBootstrap.load() loads the stores in parallel (see Onboarding Guides); nothing listens to the settings store, so language and theme are set explicitly (items 2–3 below). Writes are dotted and go through the components (write first, item 4 below): a component sends the change to the API and, once it succeeds, copies the saved values into the store with setDirect(). No store writes to the API itself — their updateSetting() methods have no callers.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph TD
    API["🐍 Backend API"]

    Auth["🔐 authStore (Manages Login)"]
    Boot["🚪 (app)/+layout.svelte<br>appBootstrap.load(), in parallel"]
    Settings["⚙️ settingsStore (User Preferences)"]
    Onboarding["🧭 onboarding (Guide Progress)"]
    Global["🌍 globalSettingsStore (App Config)"]

    Lang["🗣️ languageStore"]
    Theme["🎨 themeStore"]

    UI["💻 Frontend UI Components"]

    API -->|Session / User Data| Auth
    Auth -->|"checkAuth() succeeded"| Boot
    Boot -->|"userSettings.load()"| Settings
    Boot -->|"onboarding.load(onboardingApi)"| Onboarding
    Boot -->|"globalSettings.load()"| Global
    Auth -->|"Login: setDirect(user_settings)"| Settings
    Auth -->|"Login: currentLanguage.set()"| Lang
    Auth -->|"Login: applyTheme()"| Theme

    UI -.->|"PUT /settings/user<br>first Welcome: POST /settings/onboarding/welcome/complete"| API
    UI -.->|"PATCH /settings/global/bulk (admin)"| API
    UI -.->|"setDirect() once the write succeeds"| Settings
    UI -.->|"setDirect() once the write succeeds"| Global

    UI -->|"currentLanguage.set(): after the write<br>(Preferences, Welcome) or header button"| Lang
    UI -->|"applyTheme(): after the write<br>(Preferences) or header button"| Theme

    Lang -->|Updates text| UI
    Theme -->|Updates CSS vars| UI
    Global -->|Enforces limits| UI

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication Flow
docs.text:
1. Mount: On app load, auth.checkAuth() verifies the existing cookie with the backend.
  2. Bootstrap: If authenticated, the (app) layout runs appBootstrap.load(), which loads the user settings (userSettings.load()), the onboarding progress (onboarding.load(onboardingApi)) and the global settings (globalSettings.load()) in parallel. Before them, as soon as it knows the user, it starts the open-registration warning (its dependency startOpenRegistrationNotice, see Onboarding Guides). The auth store loads nothing: at login it copies the login response's user_settings into the store with setDirect(), and applies their language and theme (item 3).
  3. Language and theme: nothing listens to the settings store; they are set explicitly — by the auth store at login, from the same response (currentLanguage.set(), applyTheme()); by the Preferences tab after its write; by the Welcome page after Continue (the language only: Welcome leaves the theme alone); and, for this browser only, by the header buttons (item 4).
  4. Write first: no settings screen updates the store before the server answers. The Preferences tab sends PUT /api/v1/settings/user (one field per request) and, only once it succeeds, applies the language or theme and calls userSettings.setDirect(); a failed write leaves the store as it was and shows an error toast. The Profile tab (avatar) and the Welcome page also write first; Welcome only previews a new language (the svelte-i18n locale) until Continue saves it. setDirect() itself never calls the API: it sets the store and its per-user localStorage cache (lf_{userId}_user_settings). The header's theme and language buttons change only this browser (librefolio-theme, librefolio-locale) and save nothing to the account.
  5. After a reload: language and theme come from this browser's librefolio-locale and librefolio-theme, so a change made on another device shows here only at the next login.

docs.title: 🏢 Instance configuration
docs.text:
instanceConfig (lib/features/instance/instanceConfig.svelte.ts, Svelte 5 runes) holds the public configuration of the instance: the answer of GET /api/v1/system/instance, the same for whoever asks and readable without a session (backend side: Public instance configuration).

  • When: the (app) layout calls void instanceConfig.load() at the top of its onMount, before the auth check, and does not wait for it. Pages outside the layout call it too: LoginCard on mount, the /invite page, which waits for it together with the inspection of its link (Account Link Pages), and AuthPageFrame on mount, so every sign-in page has it, /verify-email included.
  • One request per page load: concurrent and later calls share the same request; load({force: true}) asks again, and fetchConfig replaces the API call (tests). GlobalSettingsTab forces it after saving registration_mode, so the rest of the app follows the new mode.
  • Never blocking: config is always the configuration in force: DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CONFIG until the server answers, then its last answer. A failed request changes nothing but failed, and the next load() retries. Only the latest request writes its answer (a generation counter), so a forced reload outruns an older request.
  • The default: a self-hosted instance where anyone may register, {profile: 'selfhosted', accounts: {registration_mode: 'open', registration_locked: false}}, without the optional first_account_open and password_rules: LoginCard treats anything but true as false, and PasswordStrength checks DEFAULT_PASSWORD_RULES, the five rules of release 1.3. So until the answer, and when there is none, the login page offers Register here; a registration the server refuses gets its own message. On an instance that registers by invitation, the link shows for a moment, until the answer withdraws it (backlog A-19).
  • Getters: config; loaded, true once the server answered on this page load; failed, true when the last request failed.
  • Type: InstanceConfig is z.infer<typeof schemas.InstanceConfigResponse> from the generated client, so a field added to the backend response appears after ./dev.py api sync.
  • Readers of accounts: LoginCard (Register here while registration_mode is open or first_account_open is true), the /invite page (closed while it is disabled), GlobalSettingsTab (the select locked, showing the mode in force, while registration_locked), UsersTab (no invitation while registration_mode is disabled, and a reason that names the variable while registration_locked), the open-registration warning (registration_mode and registration_locked, read only once loaded is true: the default is open, and an invite-only instance would show the warning until the answer), and PasswordStrength under every new-password field (the checklist and its valid from password_rules, DEFAULT_PASSWORD_RULES while the list is absent or empty). PasswordStrength does not load the configuration itself: the page around it does. The /reset-password and /setup pages ask for it on mount without waiting for it, so the checklist switches to the server's rules when they arrive and a slow request never delays the form.
  • Readers of profile (F05, workstream A): one test, the helpers of lib/features/instance/profile.ts. selfHostedConfirmed() is true once the server has answered on this page load (loaded) and said selfhosted; managedConfirmed() is the same for managed. Until the answer both are false, although DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CONFIG says selfhosted, and a reload that fails after an answer leaves that answer confirmed. So what a hosting provider's customers must not get waits for selfHostedConfirmed(): a managed instance never shows it while its answer is in flight, nor after a request that failed before any answer. What only a managed instance shows waits for managedConfirmed(). The helpers are reactive, read in a template or a $derived, and live in a module of their own rather than on the store: they read only loaded and config, so the test files that replace the store with vi.mock keep working. The readers:
    • donationsVisible() (lib/features/support/donations.svelte.ts), which returns selfHostedConfirmed(), is the one rule of the coffee links in the Svelte app, reactive in a template or a $derived. Header (header-donate-link), HelpMenu (help-donate-link and the divider above it), AuthPageFrame (auth-donate-link) and SupportActions (the coffee and the «Or share» divider, in the About tab and in the donation popup) draw their coffee only while it is true; the share buttons of SupportActions stay. The popup itself never comes on a managed instance: the backend decides it (Deferred popups). The static offline page (frontend/static/offline.html, which the service worker serves when a navigation fails) reads no configuration: its coffee link shows on every instance, managed included.
    • checkForNewerRelease() (lib/features/update-check/updateCheck.ts), the administrators' check at sign-in, awaits instanceConfig.load(), then returns null unless selfHostedConfirmed(), with no request and no write to its cache: GitHub and the image registry are probed only once the answer says selfhosted (Container Image Check).
    • ForgotPasswordCard draws forgot-ask-admin while managedConfirmed(), the server commands once the answer is in and does not say managed, and neither while the request is pending. When the request failed before any answer (failed true, loaded false), it draws forgot-ask-admin, the advice that holds in both profiles, and still no command (FPM-08): that branch reads loaded and failed itself, beside managedConfirmed().
    • AssetSearchAutocomplete (workstream H) offers the GitHub fallback of «Let us know» only while selfHostedConfirmed() (Asset Search & Link-Finder).
    • ChangelogModal draws Check for updates (changelog-check-update) only while selfHostedConfirmed(): not before the answer, not on a managed instance, and not while no answer came on this page load, a failed request included, on a self-hosted instance too.
    • The gate: frontend/src/instanceProfile.gate.test.ts keeps profile.ts the only source that compares a profile with 'selfhosted' or 'managed'. It parses every product .ts and .svelte file under src — TypeScript's syntax tree for a module, Svelte's for a component, its scripts and every expression of its markup —, skipping the tests, the mocks and the generated API clients, and fails on any ===, !==, == or != between a profile (a member or a variable of that name) and one of the two values, in either order, or on a case of a switch on it. A comparison anywhere else is a copy of the rule: call a helper, or add one to profile.ts when neither says what the site needs. Its forms are a floor: it does not follow an alias, a constant holding the value, or a lookup keyed by the profile.
    • Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs profile.test.ts (PRF-01…08: both helpers false before any request, while it is in flight and after a first request that failed; true for the profile answered, kept after a reload that fails, following a reload that answers the other one; reactive inside an effect), the gate, donations.test.ts and updateCheck.managed.test.ts; ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit runs Header.managed.test.ts, HelpMenu.managed.test.ts, SupportActions.managed.test.ts and ChangelogModal.managed.test.ts, with those of AuthPageFrame and ForgotPasswordCard (Authentication Components): each before the answer, once it says selfhosted and once it says managed.
  • Readers of legal: the two components of the legal notice, LegalNotice and LegalLinks (Settings Components), draw each link only while its address is set. The default has no legal: until the answer, the notice shows without links.
  • Reader of client_log_level (H-60): the store itself. Each answer that lands sets how much the browser console says about failed API calls, setApiConsoleLevel(client_log_level ?? 'error') (lib/api/apiErrorConsole.ts); a failed or superseded request sets nothing, so the level is error until the first answer (The Browser Console).
import {instanceConfig} from '$lib/features/instance/instanceConfig.svelte';
import {managedConfirmed, selfHostedConfirmed} from '$lib/features/instance/profile';

await instanceConfig.load();
instanceConfig.config.profile; // 'selfhosted' | 'managed': never compared by hand (the gate), see the helpers
selfHostedConfirmed(); // true once the server answered on this page load, and said 'selfhosted'
managedConfirmed(); // the same for 'managed'; both false until the answer
instanceConfig.config.accounts.registration_mode; // 'open' | 'invite' | 'disabled'
instanceConfig.config.accounts.registration_locked; // true while LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION pins it
instanceConfig.config.accounts.first_account_open; // true while the instance has no account (optional: absent reads as false)
instanceConfig.config.accounts.password_rules; // [{code, value}]: the password rules (optional: absent or empty, PasswordStrength assumes DEFAULT_PASSWORD_RULES)
instanceConfig.config.legal?.terms_url; // the terms of service of the instance, or null (optional: absent until the answer)
instanceConfig.config.client_log_level; // 'error' | 'debug': how much the console says about failed API calls (optional: absent reads as 'error')

docs.title: 📢 Instance notices
docs.text:
instanceNotices (lib/features/instance/instanceNotices.svelte.ts) is the registry of the messages about the instance shown above every page of the app shell. A feature registers its notice; nobody edits the layout to add one. InstanceNotices.svelte (lib/features/instance/components/) shows the registry: routes/(app)/+layout.svelte renders it once, inside the shell's <main>, after the onboarding banner and before the page. The Welcome page, which has no shell, shows no notice.

Field of a notice Meaning id Stable and unique; it starts with the owner's area, such as assets.disallowedProviders severity info, warning or danger messageKey, params The i18n key of the message, and its ICU parameters dismissible The user may close it, until the next page load action An optional link after the message: {labelKey, href}, with href a path inside the app
  • show(notice) adds a notice, or replaces the one with the same id in place.
  • hide(id) removes it. A notice hidden and shown again is visible again, even if the user had closed it.
  • dismiss(id) is the user closing a dismissible notice: it stays closed until the next page load.
  • clear() removes every notice. It also runs when the signed-in account changes, signing out included (registerClientSessionReset('instanceNotices', clear)).
  • list holds the notices to show: not closed by the user, danger first, then warning, then info, and within a severity in the order they were first shown.

The feature that registers a notice decides who sees it, since it knows the user and their role, and hides it when the condition is gone. Two features register one today: the catch-up of the prices (Updating prices…, Updating prices…) and the open-registration warning (accounts.openRegistration, for administrators). For example (the assets keys are illustrative):

import {instanceNotices} from '$lib/features/instance/instanceNotices.svelte';

instanceNotices.show({
    id: 'assets.disallowedProviders',
    severity: 'warning',
    messageKey: 'assets.notices.disallowed',
    params: {count: 3},
    dismissible: true,
    action: {labelKey: 'assets.notices.review', href: '/assets'},
});

instanceNotices.hide('assets.disallowedProviders');

How InstanceNotices.svelte renders them:

  • Without notices it renders nothing. Otherwise a <section data-testid="instance-notices">, labelled by instance.notices.label, holds one instance-notice per notice, with data-notice-id and data-severity: role="alert" for danger, role="status" otherwise. The link is instance-notice-action, the close button instance-notice-dismiss, labelled by common.close.
  • Colours are colour roles only (frontend/src/lib/theme/tokens.css). For each severity X (info, warning, danger), the notice is bg-lf-X-soft border-lf-X-line text-lf-X-on-soft and its icon text-lf-X. The classes are written whole in NOTICE_CLASSES and ICON_CLASSES, so the colour gates see every class.

docs.title: 🔒 Instance block
docs.text:
The instance block is a flag: whether the hosting provider blocked this instance (backend side: Instance Block). Two modules of lib/features/instance/ hold it, so that the API client, which turns it on, imports no module with runes: the AI Export probe loads the client without Svelte's compiler, and a gate keeps the client rune-free (the probe's frontend bridge).

  • The state: instanceBlockState (instanceBlockState.ts), a plain module without runes. It holds blocked, which markBlocked() and clear() change, and subscribe(listener), which calls the listener synchronously after every change and returns the function that stops it. The module also exports isInstanceBlockedError(), INSTANCE_BLOCKED_STATUS and INSTANCE_BLOCKED_CODE, and imports nothing from the API, so the client imports it without a cycle.
  • The reactive face: instanceBlock (instanceBlock.svelte.ts, Svelte 5 runes), which the (app) layout reads. Its $state starts from instanceBlockState.blocked when the module loads — a block marked before the layout loaded shows at once — and only its subscription writes it afterwards, synchronously: a change shows in instanceBlock.blocked in the same tick. Its markBlocked() and clear() are the plain module's own, and it re-exports the two constants and isInstanceBlockedError(): a page or a feature may take all it needs from the face, while a module on the API client's import graph imports the plain module.
  • Who turns it on: the error interceptor of lib/api/zodios-client.ts calls instanceBlockState.markBlocked() when isInstanceBlockedError(status, data) is true: status 423 (INSTANCE_BLOCKED_STATUS) and detail.code instance_blocked (INSTANCE_BLOCKED_CODE). The error still reaches its caller.
  • Who reads it: in routes/(app)/+layout.svelte, the branch $isAuthenticated && instanceBlock.blocked comes before the bootstrap ones, so InstanceBlockedPage replaces the app and the app shell never starts: its requests never pile up refusals.
  • Who turns it off: clear(), which also runs when the signed-in account changes, signing out included: instanceBlockState.ts registers the reset (registerClientSessionReset('instanceBlock', …)), and the face, which follows the state, registers none. A page load starts with the flag off.
  • Getter: blocked, on both.

The backend answers 423 only to a signed-in user; anyone else gets the 401 of get_current_user(), which the interceptor turns into the login as usual — except on /, where the login already is, and on the anonymous pages of a link, which handle the 401 themselves (A 401 on a Link Page).

InstanceBlockedPage.svelte (lib/features/instance/components/) is the full-page block page:

  • On mount it reads GET /system/block (fetchBlock, a prop that tests replace). When blocked is false, the block was lifted meanwhile: it clears the flag and reloads the window. When the request fails, the page stays, without the date, the subscription link and the backup card, and does not ask again while it is mounted: a reload brings them back.
  • Its text depends on the role: instance.block.adminDescription for is_superuser, instance.block.userDescription for the other users, under the title instance.block.title.
  • instance.block.deletionDate shows deletion_date, written in the interface locale (uiLocale()). The ISO day is read at midnight UTC and formatted in UTC, so no time zone moves it.
  • An administrator (is_superuser) also gets the Manage subscription link (instance.block.manageSubscription) when billing_url is an http(s) address, checked again here; it opens in a new tab, rel="noopener noreferrer".
  • The block message is one <section role="alert">, which also holds the logout button: labelled by auth.logout, it calls the layout's logout(). There is no button to delete one's own account yet, though DELETE /auth/users/me stays allowed.
  • The backup card (decision 12). When the answer's backup_available is true, and only then, a second <section> under the alert, named by its <h2> (aria-labelledby, text instance.block.backupTitle), holds BackupDownloadCard (lib/features/backup/), the same card as Settings › Administration › Backup: start a backup of the whole instance, follow it, download the archive, delete it. The server decides who gets it (the administrators, today: see Instance Block); the page never guesses it from the role, so a false, a missing field, a pending or a failed request mean no card, for an administrator too. The section stays outside the role="alert" one, so a screen reader announces the block, not the card and its progress. The card's routes already answer on a blocked instance: the four of the backup, and GET /backup/instance/options, the rules of a secure backup's password (Instance Block).
  • The page mounts its own ToastContainer: the (app) layout mounts one only with the app shell, which this page replaces, and the card reports its errors and a backup with warnings by toast.
  • Colours are colour roles only. The test ids are instance-blocked, instance-blocked-description, instance-blocked-deletion-date, instance-blocked-billing, instance-blocked-logout and instance-blocked-backup; inside the last one, the card keeps its own (backup-download-card and the others).
// lib/api/zodios-client.ts marks the plain state: no runes on the API client's import graph
import {instanceBlockState, isInstanceBlockedError} from '$lib/features/instance/instanceBlockState';

if (isInstanceBlockedError(error.response?.status, error.response?.data)) instanceBlockState.markBlocked();

// a page or a component reads the reactive face
import {instanceBlock} from '$lib/features/instance/instanceBlock.svelte';

instanceBlock.blocked; // true, in the same tick: the (app) layout shows InstanceBlockedPage

Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit runs InstanceBlockedPage.test.ts, which mounts BackupDownloadCardStub (frontend/src/__tests__/harness/) in place of the card: it checks where the card goes and when, while lib/features/backup/BackupDownloadCard.test.ts covers what the card does. ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs instanceBlock.test.ts: isInstanceBlockedError(), the flag and its reset at a change of account, and the face — a change through instanceBlockState shows in instanceBlock.blocked with nothing awaited, a block marked before the face loads is on from its first read, and one session reset, the plain module's, clears both.

docs.title: 🙈 Privacy masking
docs.text: The header's eye button (lib/components/ui/PrivacyToggle.svelte) flips a single flag. Everything else is decided where a number becomes a string, so this section is the contract for any code that renders money. What the user sees is described in the Privacy mode section of User Preferences. Paths are relative to frontend/src/ unless they start with backend/.

docs.title: 🗄️ The store
docs.text:
lib/stores/app/privacyStore.svelte.ts holds one rune, hydrated synchronously at module init from localStorage['librefolio-privacy']: the currency formatters import the store, so it is initialized before the first amount is formatted. Only the exact value '1' means on; an absent key means off, so nothing is masked by default.

  • Device-local, bare key. The preference describes the screen being watched, not the account, so the key is not lf_{userId}_…. With a per-user key, switching account in front of a projector would adopt the other account's "off" and bring every value back.
  • Two guards. browser answers whether localStorage exists; try/catch answers whether the call can fail while existing (private modes, exceeded quota, denied storage). After a refused write isPrivacyPersisted() returns false: this session keeps masking, the next load will not. No component reads it today.
  • No cross-tab sync. There is no storage listener: another open tab follows on reload.
Export Use isPrivacyEnabled() Read the flag. Called inside a runes template or a $derived, the read registers the dependency — no subscription needed. setPrivacyEnabled(value), togglePrivacy() Write the flag and try to persist it. isPrivacyPersisted() false once a write has failed.

docs.title: 🧰 The masking channel
docs.text:
Masking is decided at formatter level: before the string exists, the formatter hands the caller either the figure or PRIVACY_PLACEHOLDER (•••). Where the resulting node lands is then irrelevant — a masked string is as safe in a table cell as in an ECharts tooltip or a title attribute. The placeholder is a constant and carries nothing derived from the value: no magnitude, no digit count, no sign.

Primitive File Use it for formatCurrencyAmountPlain, formatCurrencyAmountHtml lib/utils/currency/currencyFormat.ts Every money amount — the D8 primitives. Option sensitivity: 'personal' or 'public'; omitted means personal, i.e. masked. maskable(formatted, sensitivity?) lib/utils/privacy/maskable.ts A formatted amount without its sign, replaced whole. maskCurrencyParts(parts, sensitivity?) lib/utils/privacy/maskable.ts An Intl.NumberFormat with style: 'currency': pass its formatToParts(…). maskFormattedNumber(formatted, sensitivity?) lib/utils/privacy/maskable.ts A number with no currency, such as an axis tick. maskableQuantity(formatted) lib/utils/privacy/maskable.ts A quantity the user holds, where it sits next to a price. shouldMaskAmount(sensitivity?) lib/utils/privacy/maskable.ts The decision itself; public returns false before reading the store. CurrencyAmount.svelte lib/components/ui/display/ One D8 amount rendered from a legacy parent (below).

The rules the primitives carry:

  • personal or public. personal is wealth: values, cash, P&L, proceeds, fees, taxes. public is a number that does not let anyone infer what the user owns — market and unit prices, WAC, FX rates, the amounts of asset-level events (product owner, 2026-09-22). The default is personal on purpose: a public value left unclassified disappears, which the user reports; a personal value left in the clear by the opposite default would leak, which nobody sees.
  • The currency stays. The D8 primitives mask the absolute value and append symbol, flag and code afterwards: -••• € 🇪🇺 EUR. A formatter that lets Intl place the currency cannot append it, so maskCurrencyParts works on the parts: the run from the first to the last magnitude part (integer, group, decimal, fraction, compact, the exponent parts, nan, infinity), inner literals included, becomes one •••, while currency, the sign and the outer literals stay — -$1,234.50 gives -$•••, a compact 1,2 Mio. € gives ••• €. compact is inside the run on purpose: €•••K would still disclose the order of magnitude. Known limit: in pt-CV ICU types the escudo sign $ as a decimal part (and the currency part is a zero-width space), so the masked string loses the only visible symbol.
  • The sign stays (D8). The D8 primitives write + or - outside maskable. maskFormattedNumber and maskableQuantity keep the leading sign run exactly as the locale wrote it (/^[\p{Cf}+\-\u2212]*/u: U+2212 in sv-SE, a bidi mark before the minus in Arabic) rather than rebuilding an ASCII hyphen, which would change the unmasked output too. The cost is stated in the maskable docstring: where a site passes showSign: value !== 0, a prefix appears exactly when the amount is non-zero, so a masked column still shows which rows are zero. The product owner ruled with that objection on the table; do not move the sign back inside the mask.
  • Absence is the caller's job. Check for a missing, non-finite or unavailable value first and render —: masking an absence would claim a figure that does not exist, and an em-dash handed to maskFormattedNumber comes back masked.
  • A quantity's class is decided at the call site (D5′). The same number is masked in positions and lots, where quantity × public price rebuilds what the user owns, and stays visible in the Transactions list. So the rule cannot live in a shared quantity formatter: maskableQuantity is a separate, searchable name with no sensitivity, and a site that must stay visible — formatTxQuantity in lib/features/transactions/txDisplayHelpers.ts — simply does not call it. Its callers today are ExposureTable.svelte, unifiedLotsTableHelpers.ts, LotCustodyModal.svelte, LotGanttChart.svelte and LotWacPriceChart.svelte. Units and tickers stay outside the argument, as the currency does for money; a partially closed lot keeps its open share (formatLotQuantityCell renders ••• (60%)).

docs.title: 🚧 The anti-regression gate
docs.text:
lib/utils/privacy/moneyRenderSites.test.ts tests a premise, not behaviour: that the places rendering money are the places we know. It scans every .ts and .svelte file under frontend/src/ — test files and the node_modules, __mocks__ and __tests__ folders excluded — line by line for two forms:

  • Form A — style: 'currency', exact;
  • Form B — a template literal interpolating a currency token (currency or symbol) beside a numeric-looking one (toFixed, toLocaleString, amount, price, total, …), a heuristic.

Every hit must be registered in REGISTRY, keyed by file and whitespace-collapsed content rather than by line number, so an unrelated edit above a site does not turn the gate red. Each entry carries a status and a written reason:

Status Meaning masked Goes through the channel, at the site or at its function boundary. not-money Matches a form but renders no amount. public Real money in the clear by rule: a market price, an asset-level event, a rate. residual Real money outside the channel, deliberately not fixed yet. unmasked Real money outside the channel, found by the gate and not yet triaged.

The test fails on an unregistered hit and on an entry whose code no longer exists. It asserts the residual, unmasked and public lists by exact content, so fixing or reclassifying a site is a visible edit, and it carries a positive control — hits ≥ entries, both forms found, the risk helper found — because "no unregistered site" is also true of a scanner that reads nothing. It runs in ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit.

A line that matches SAFE_CALL — it names a D8 primitive, a currency-code formatter or the risk helpers' formatCurrencyAmount / formatScopedCurrencyAmount, or calls maskable( or maskFormattedNumber( — is not scanned for Form B. The skip is line-granular: a masked call on a line also hides an unmasked fallback written on the same line. Entry to SAFE_CALL has a price: the name must be an export pinned by unit tests that would break if its masking were removed.

What the gate cannot see:

  1. Money without a currency token — axis ticks and labels, such as the value axis of the lot comparison chart (formatAxisAmount in lib/features/brokers/lots/lotComparisonChartHelpers.ts). Only their own tests protect them.
  2. A public marking. {sensitivity: 'public'} sits on a SAFE_CALL line and is never a hit, and a public entry is not re-examined. Only the tests of that site protect the decision — for the Positions price and average cost, the D5′ block of ExposureTable.test.ts.
  3. Reactivity. A site can be registered, masked and green and still not follow the toggle: see the legacy freeze below.

docs.title: 🧊 Legacy components freeze masked output (R20)
docs.text:
In a legacy (non-runes) component, a function call inside a template expression is compiled into $.untrack(…), and only the values the expression names are tracked. The privacy flag, read inside the formatter, never becomes a dependency, so the output keeps the state it had at mount: turned on in place, privacy leaves the digits visible; turned off, ••• stays. The same {@html formatCurrencyAmountHtml(amount, code)}, compiled with the Svelte in frontend/node_modules (5.48.0) — excerpt:

// legacy parent: export let amount; export let code;
$.deep_read_state(amount()),
$.deep_read_state(code()),
$.untrack(() => formatCurrencyAmountHtml(amount(), code()))

// runes parent: let {amount, code} = $props();
$.html(node, () => formatCurrencyAmountHtml($$props.amount, $$props.code));

Neither the gate, which reads source text, nor a formatter unit test, which calls the formatter fresh, can see this. The remedy:

  • render the amount through a runes child — lib/components/ui/display/CurrencyAmount.svelte renders one D8 amount — or migrate the parent to runes when it is small;
  • cover the site with a component test that toggles privacy in place, in both directions, including a mount with privacy already on: lib/features/brokers/BrokerCard.test.ts, and lib/components/ui/display/CurrencyAmount.test.ts, which mounts the child under __tests__/harness/CurrencyAmountLegacyHost.svelte. That host is legacy by construction (export let) and also renders the same call inline, as a control that must stay frozen.

Today the legacy parents that render money are lib/features/brokers/BrokerCard.svelte and routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte; both render it through CurrencyAmount.

docs.title: 📈 ECharts formatters
docs.text:
ECharts calls formatter and renderItem callbacks itself, outside Svelte's effect tracking. They read the current flag whenever they run, but the read registers nothing, so a toggle does not redraw what is already painted: an axis keeps its ticks, a bar keeps its label, and an open tooltip keeps its text until it is shown again. The render $effect must read the flag itself — void isPrivacyEnabled();, beside its other void dependencies — so that a toggle re-runs it and the option is rebuilt with every formatter called again:

  • lib/features/brokers/lots/LotComparisonChart.svelte — axis formatters; each render replaces xAxis, yAxis and series (replaceMerge);
  • lib/features/brokers/lots/LotGanttChart.svelte — the lot quantity on each bar is built in renderItem.

The interface locale follows the same pattern: both effects also read void uiLocale();, so a language switch redraws the chart as a toggle does (see Numbers, amounts and dates).

Keep the formatter a pure exported helper, as formatAxisAmount and formatAxisCurrency in lotComparisonChartHelpers.ts are, so a unit test can pin it; the effect wiring itself is only exercised by a test that mounts the chart.

docs.title: 🧩 Contract for Tool renderers
docs.text:
A Tool's compiled renderer (see Tool plugins) presents results the backend computed from the user's own scenario, so it renders through the same channel:

  • money only through the D8 primitives, with an explicit sensitivity on every call, so the classification is read at the site rather than implied by the default;
  • quantities through maskableQuantity where they are holdings;
  • rates and percentages marked public explicitly wherever they pass through a masking primitive;
  • — for an empty, non-finite or unavailable value — checked before formatting, never masked;
  • runes mode for the component, and the ECharts rule above for any chart it draws.

The PAC allocator renders through lib/features/tools/pac-allocator/planner/format.ts, its only privacy adapter: every amount, quantity, price, rate and percentage the planner shows goes through it. An exact_ratio number — the ExactRatio branch of backend/app/schemas/pac_allocator/exact.py, whose authoritative value is its reduced numerator and denominator — is shown through the backend's display_decimal, a projection the schema marks non_authoritative, with ≈ in front unless that projection equals the ratio; an amount is rounded exactly from the ratio to its currency's minor unit instead, ≈ marking a rounding that changed it.

docs.title: ⏳ Page busy: the Refresh button
docs.text: Each page has one Refresh button in its own top bar. It spins, greyed and disabled, while the page's «big» requests are in flight — the ones the page decided to make to (re)build what it shows — and never for a reload the user did not ask for (developer decision 48, P3). lib/stores/app/pageBusy.svelte.ts (Svelte 5 runes) holds those requests as tokens; its header comment (pageBusy.svelte.ts:1-26) is the contract. Paths are relative to frontend/src/ unless they start with frontend/.

docs.title: 🧰 The API
docs.text:
Member Use track(label, work, options?) Holds a token while work() runs, resolves with its value, and ends the token in finally, on a rejection or a synchronous throw too (pageBusy.svelte.ts:89). What the pages call. begin(label, options?), end(token) The same by hand (l.71, l.85). end goes by token, not by label, and is idempotent: an unknown, expired or pre-reset() token touches nothing, since ids start at 1 and only grow (l.44). join(label, work, options?) A load that completes what the page is already doing (N55): track while a token is pending, work() alone on an idle page. Decided at the call (l.102). reset() Drops every token and clears its timer (l.107). busy Reactive: at least one token is pending. What the buttons read. labels The pending labels, in begin order: diagnostics and tests. PAGE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS 120_000, the default timeout of a token (l.36).

The pending list is a $state.raw replaced on every change, and the writers read it with untrack (l.45-50): track and join are called from $effects, and an effect that started depending on the list would run again at every token — or loop, when it begins one on each run.

docs.title: 📍 Where track and join go
docs.text:
On the trigger, never inside a load function. The same loadAll() (Dashboard) or loadOverview() (broker detail) also reloads the page in background, after a price catch-up or for a cache a portfolio mutation marked stale, and that reload must not spin the button. So the token wraps the call where the user's request arrives:

Trigger Examples The first load, in onMount dashboard-first-load (routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte:858), broker-first-load (routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:299), asset-first-load (routes/(app)/assets/[id]/+page.svelte:1145) The Refresh handler handleSync() → dashboard-refresh (dashboard/+page.svelte:734), handleRefresh() → broker-refresh (brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:468). On an asset's page the token sits on the button's onrefresh, asset-refresh (assets/[id]/+page.svelte:2316), because handleRefresh() also runs after a sync A change of period, currency, scope, filter or tab createDateRangeController(() => void pageBusy.track('dashboard-period', () => loadAll())) (dashboard/+page.svelte:176), dashboard-scope after the broker filter's debounce (dashboard/+page.svelte:729), broker-period in handleDateChange() (brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:465); on an asset's page asset-period, asset-currency, and the chart's view and calendar window, asset-mode and asset-calendar-window (assets/[id]/+page.svelte:1806, :1217, :393, :421) A reload after a save in a window assets-reload after a create, an edit or a merge on the Assets list (routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte:967, :1968, :1984); asset-reload after an edit, a new FX pair or the data editor's save on an asset's page (assets/[id]/+page.svelte:2795, :1785, :2679): the page rebuilds what the user just changed A panel that opens, changes its inputs, or follows the page's Refresh lib/features/brokers/lots/LotsAnalysisPanel.svelte:365-392 (lots-panel-load, lots-selection-load, and lots-*-refresh on refreshVersion); lib/features/risk/riskPanelController.svelte.ts (risk-load in applyBaseSignature(), l.594; risk-refresh on refreshVersion, l.658); on the Assets list's Correlation tab, AssetSetRiskPanel.reload() (lib/features/risk/AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:224) hands each section a new refreshVersion, so «Reload All» waits for their risk-refresh A load that completes what the page is doing: join The lazy loads a panel asks by itself: dashboard-pnl-candles, dashboard-contribution (dashboard/+page.svelte:1066, :1083); broker-pnl-candles, broker-contribution (brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:712, :741). The Δ over the range on an asset's or an FX pair's page (X-R59), from an $effect: asset-detail-range-delta (assets/[id]/+page.svelte:545), fx-detail-range-delta (routes/(app)/fx/[pair]/+page.svelte:327)

Inside an $effect, read the inputs tracked and start the load untracked, as the lots panel does:

$effect(() => {
    if (!(open && assetId != null && ready)) return;
    const [currentAssetId, currentBrokerIds, currentCurrency] = [assetId, brokerIds, currency];
    untrack(() => void pageBusy.track('lots-panel-load', () => loadMain(currentAssetId, currentBrokerIds, currentCurrency)));
});

Never for:

  • the live-price poller;
  • an action with an indicator of its own: price and FX sync, the PAC's «Calcola», the import wizard, a save in a modal;
  • per-card and per-row refreshes, and the small background reads;
  • a background reload. On {kind: 'prices'} from the portfolio bus (the end of a price catch-up, Z-13), reloadAfterPriceCatchUp() calls loadAll() or loadOverview() without a token (dashboard/+page.svelte:755, brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:486); the other views on screen (the risk controller, the lots panel, the Assets and FX pages) reload the same way through onPricesCaughtUp() (Y5-1), also without a token; and the risk controller's own sync, handleSynced() (l.612), reloads without a token too. See How a page uses the cache.
  • the reload after a sync on an asset's page: handlePageSyncComplete() and handleFxPairCreationSynced() call handleRefresh() without a token (assets/[id]/+page.svelte:1752, :1780). A sync can still make the button wait for a panel: the Dashboard's banner syncs bump refreshVersion (dashboard/+page.svelte:396, :472) and the asset page's handleRefresh() bumps riskRefreshVersion, so an open lots panel or Risk tab reloads under its own token.

join (N55). A new report drops the P&L candles of the growth chart and the contribution of the positions panel, and a panel left on that view asks for them again at once. After the user's period, currency, scope or Refresh the page is busy, so that load takes a token of its own and the button waits for it too; after a background reload the page is idle, the load runs without a token, and the button stays still. A retry after a failed load (Y-24, Lazy sections after a failure) calls the same join when it falls due, seconds after the failure, on a page normally idle by then: it takes no token, and the button does not spin for a request the user did not ask for (P3). The Δ over the range on an asset's or an FX pair's page (X-R59) joins too: handleRefresh() asks it again, and also runs after a sync without a token (above), so with join the Δ waits under the user's Refresh, a change of period and, on an asset's page, a change of asset or the first load, and runs without a token after a sync, where a track would spin the button (P3). One limit: in a flush its $effect runs before the effect that begins asset-currency on an asset's page, before onMount's fx-detail-first-load on an FX pair's page and, on a change of pair, before the one that begins fx-detail-orientation, so those three loads find the page idle and run without a token: the button may stop a moment before the figure lands.

The risk panels no longer have a refresh button of their own (Y11 step 3): the page's Refresh bumps refreshVersion, and the risk controller and the lots panel reload with force under their own tokens.

docs.title: 🧭 Page scope and timeout
docs.text:
• Scoped to the page. routes/(app)/+layout.svelte:61 calls pageBusy.reset() in onNavigate when the route id changes, before the new page mounts; a change of parameter on the same route (one asset to another) keeps the tokens. reset is also a client-session reset (pageBusy.svelte.ts:129): signing out or switching account drops every token. A request of the old page that lands later ends a token that is gone: nothing happens.
  • Timeout. A token that never ends is dropped after PAGE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS or its own timeoutMs (a positive, finite number; anything else falls back to the default, timeoutOf(), l.53), with one console.warn naming its label (l.79). The request is not cancelled: only the button stops waiting for it.

docs.title: 🔘 The button contract
docs.text:
Every Refresh button reads pageBusy.busy three times: disabled, data-busy, and the spin of its icon. Trimmed from the Dashboard's:

<button onclick={handleSync} disabled={pageBusy.busy} data-busy={pageBusy.busy ? 'true' : 'false'} data-testid="sync-button">
    <RefreshCw size={14} class={pageBusy.busy ? 'animate-spin' : ''} />
</button>
Page Test id Where Dashboard sync-button routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte:1023 Broker detail broker-refresh routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:661 Brokers list brokers-refresh routes/(app)/brokers/+page.svelte:384 Transactions tx-refresh-button routes/(app)/transactions/+page.svelte:768 Files files-refresh-button routes/(app)/files/+page.svelte:783 FX list fx-refresh-all-button routes/(app)/fx/+page.svelte:1178 FX detail fx-detail-refresh-btn routes/(app)/fx/[pair]/+page.svelte:1371 Asset detail asset-detail-refresh-btn lib/components/assets/detail/AssetDetailToolbarActions.svelte:92, with busy={pageBusy.busy} from routes/(app)/assets/[id]/+page.svelte:2315 Assets list assets-refresh-button routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte:1715 Assets list, Correlation tab risk-reload-button («Reload All») routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte:1665, in place of the list's button on that tab Tools hub tools-hub-refresh lib/features/tools/ToolsHub.svelte:162 Tool page tool-host-refresh lib/features/tools/ToolHost.svelte:263

The two Tools buttons are also disabled while their own load runs or the user is signed out.

The page root keeps its own data-busy (dashboard-page, brokers-page, files-page, …): it follows the page's own loading flags, not the tokens, and it is what waitForSettled() (frontend/e2e/fixtures/app-events.ts:68) waits on. After a price catch-up both stay false: the button because the reload holds no token, the root because the Dashboard runs it as loadAll(false, false, {background: true}) (Z-18, step 5 of How a page uses the cache). The broker detail page has no data-busy on its root.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing it
docs.text:
• The store: lib/stores/app/pageBusy.test.ts (Vitest, ./dev.py test front-portfolio store-unit) pins the tokens, the timeout under fake timers with its single warning, track on a rejection and on a synchronous throw, busy re-read by an effect, join on an idle and on a busy page, and that no writer called from an $effect makes that effect depend on the store. Its // @vitest-environment jsdom docblock is load-bearing: under node, $effect never runs and the «does not run again» cases would pass vacuously.
  • The pages: frontend/e2e/portfolio/page-busy.spec.ts (./dev.py test front-portfolio page-busy). A localhost answer lands before an assertion can look, so each case owns the busy state by holding the request that causes it:
    1. hold() (l.189) parks, through page.route, the request the trigger sends — picked by method, path and body — and lets every other one through. heldRequest() (l.225) fails by name when the trigger never reaches the network. release() lets the request go with route.fallback(), not continue(), so it still crosses the page's other routes; dispose() runs in finally.
    2. expectBusy() and expectIdle() (l.231, l.237) read only data-busy and disabled: never the spin class, a colour or a text.
    3. For a request the button must not wait for, recordBusy() (l.379) keeps every value the button's data-busy takes, through a MutationObserver in the page, so «it never waited» means never, not «not when the test looked». simulateCatchUp() (l.349) stubs the catch-up status so the tracker sends {kind: 'prices'}.
    4. Then the control, in the same page under the same recording: a period change (the 6M preset) must make the button wait, and the record must now contain true (l.690-702). Without it, the silence of step 3 proves nothing.
    5. The N55 cases also hold the cascaded P&L candles or contribution: after a background reload the button stays idle while they are held; after a period change it waits for them once the period's own report is back.
    6. The asset pages' cases (l.1243): an asset's Refresh and a period change hold the chart's price query; the reload after the page's own Sync — answered in the browser, nothing written — must leave the button idle, with a period change as its control; on the Correlation tab, «Reload All» holds the sections' base wave.

docs.title: 🛠️ Core Infrastructure
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (Mar 2026) · entityStore: Apr 2026 · TimeSeriesStore stale state: Oct 2026 · TimeSeriesStore generation: Oct 2026

The Core Infrastructure category contains the generic building blocks of the Store Client System. These modules hold no business data of their own: entityStore is the session cache behind brokerStore and assetStore, TimeSeriesStore the date-keyed cache behind the price and rate registries, and EditBuffer a buffer of pending time-series edits that no component uses yet — only its unit test does.

docs.title: 🗂️ Stores
docs.text:
All these modules are located in src/lib/stores/core/.

Module Purpose entityStore Factory (createEntityStore) of a generic session cache for a user's list of entities, looked up by ID from many components; brokerStore and assetStore (Reference State) are built on it. It loads the list once (concurrent callers share the request), normalizes each entry, merges partial payloads — for example, after a successful create or edit, the fields the frontend just sent, since the backend answers with little more than the ID — and invalidate makes the next load fetch again. EditBuffer Bidirectional edit buffer class for pending time-series modifications. Provides sync between chart click-to-edit, CSV textareas, and manual forms. TimeSeriesStore A specialized generic cache for managing historical data points (keyed by ISO date). Handles gap detection (getMissingIntervals, which skips the ranges already marked with markFetched) to minimize API calls and merges partial time-series datasets (merge). markStale(), which the price and rate registries call on every store after a price catch-up, keeps the points readable and drops the fetched marks (the read-only getter isStale says so until invalidateAll(), Y5-1): until invalidateAll(), getMissingIntervals returns every part of a range that no markFetched made since the last mark covers, points or not (Registries & Caches). generation is a number unique in the whole app (a module-level counter: never given twice, not even to a store made anew) that invalidateAll(), invalidateRange() and markStale() renew and merge(), markFetched() and the reads do not; whatever is computed from a store's data keeps the generation it was computed over and is dropped once it changes (Signal result cache).

docs.title: 📐 Architecture & Flow (EditBuffer Pattern)
docs.text:
EditBuffer<T> is a class designed to hold the edits of a time series that are not saved yet, for any point type with an ISO date (TimeSeriesPoint), whichever way each edit was made: a chart click, a line of a CSV textarea, or a form (EditSource: 'click', 'csv', 'form'). It keeps them in memory only: it has no network code and no UI.

Not used by the app yet

No component uses EditBuffer: in frontend/src, only its unit test, src/lib/stores/__tests__/EditBuffer.test.ts (run by ./dev.py test front-fx fx-unit), imports it, and git history shows no other file ever did. The FX and asset data editors that exist today, FxDataEditorSection and AssetDataEditorSection, are built on DataEditor (src/lib/components/ui/data-editor/), a table editor that tracks the status of each row itself (original, edited, deleted, appended) and imports CSV through DataImportModal.

Each pending edit is a PendingEdit<T>: a unique id, the point (new or modified), its csvLineNumber (1-based, header excluded), its source, and isNew (a point absent from the original data, rather than a change to an existing one).

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph TD
    Click["add(point, 'click')"]
    Form["add(point, 'form')"]
    CSV["replaceFromCsv(points)"]
    Change["update(id, point) · remove(id) · clear()"]

    Buffer["🛡️ EditBuffer: pending edits by ID, plus a date index"]

    Listeners["onChange listeners: getAll(), sorted by CSV line"]
    Lookups["getById(id) · getByDate(date) · getCsvLineForDate(date)"]
    Points["getAllPoints(): the points, sorted by date"]

    Click --> Buffer
    Form --> Buffer
    CSV --> Buffer
    Change --> Buffer
    Buffer -->|"after every change"| Listeners
    Buffer --> Lookups
    Buffer --> Points

docs.title: 🧠 How it Works
docs.text:
1. Adding: add(point, source, isNew = true) records an edit and returns it. An edit already pending for the same date is replaced by the new one, which gets a new id but keeps that edit's CSV line number.
  2. Changing: update(id, point) replaces the point of an edit, moving it in the date index if the date changed; remove(id) drops an edit. Both return false for an unknown id. clear() empties the buffer and restarts the line numbering — meant for a Cancel action.
  3. CSV synchronization: replaceFromCsv(points) takes the points already parsed from the CSV textarea, in order of appearance — the buffer does not parse CSV itself. It drops every edit whose source is 'csv', then numbers the points 1, 2, 3… in that order: a point on the date of a pending click or form edit updates that edit, which keeps its source; any other point becomes a new 'csv' edit.
  4. Reading: size and hasChanges; getById(id), getByDate(date) and getCsvLineForDate(date); getAll(), the edits sorted by CSV line number; getAllPoints(), their points sorted by date.
  5. Notifying: onChange(callback) registers a listener and returns the function that removes it. Every change — add, a successful update or remove, replaceFromCsv, clear — calls each listener with getAll().
  6. Saving is left to the caller: the buffer sends nothing. A caller would read getAllPoints(), send them in one bulk request, then clear() the buffer.

docs.title: 🧠 Domain & Feature State
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (Feb 2026) · portfolio page cache: Oct 2026

The Domain & Feature State houses the heavy computational stores that implement core business logic, such as the portfolio report cache, transaction ledgers, and foreign exchange (FX) graph routing. These stores often consume data from both Reference State and Registries.

docs.title: 🗂️ Stores
docs.text: Store Location Purpose portfolioStore portfolio/portfolioStore.svelte.ts Session cache of the unified portfolio report (POST /api/v1/portfolio/report). The backend engine computes holdings, performance, and allocations; the store keeps one answer per question, shares the requests in flight, and refreshes stale answers in background (stale-while-revalidate). portfolioMutation portfolio/portfolioMutation.ts The signal bus: tells the portfolio caches that a write changed what they show, that the user asked for a refresh, or that the server caught up on prices. lazyReportRetry portfolio/lazyReportRetry.svelte.ts When a page may ask again for a lazy section of the report — the P&L candles, the contribution — after a failure: 2, 4 and 8 s later, then not until the scope changes or the user's Refresh. One per section and page, from createLazyReportRetry(): see Lazy sections after a failure. lotsAnalysisStore $lib/features/brokers/lots/lotsAnalysisStore.svelte.ts Session cache of POST /api/v1/portfolio/lots/analysis (the FIFO lots panel), under the same stale-while-revalidate rule. dashboardViewStore $lib/features/dashboard/dashboardViewStore.ts The Dashboard's target currency and broker filter, per user, in sessionStorage. riskStore $lib/features/risk/riskStore.svelte.ts Session cache of the risk catalogs, of POST /api/v1/risk/query, and of the POST /api/v1/risk/eligibility verdicts. txStore $lib/features/transactions/txStore.svelte.ts The master ledger of user transactions. Supports infinite scrolling, complex filtering, and bulk operations. currencyGraphStore currencyGraphStore.ts Caches the multi-directed currency graph used by the DFS algorithm to find conversion routes (FX Chain Algorithm). fxCardInversionStore fx/fxCardInversionStore.ts UI-specific domain state tracking which FX pairs the user has "flipped" visually (e.g., viewing USD/EUR instead of EUR/USD).

docs.title: 📐 Architecture & Flow (Portfolio Page Cache)
docs.text:
The frontend does not compute the portfolio. One POST /api/v1/portfolio/report runs the backend engine and returns the summary, the daily history, the allocation history, the data-quality report, and whichever optional series the caller asked for. What the frontend decides is when to ask again. Every portfolio view keeps its answers for the session and follows one rule, stale-while-revalidate: a write marks the cached answers stale and keeps them; a page shows what it has at once, asks again in background, and moves to the fresh figures when they land. There is no time-based TTL.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph TD
    subgraph Signals ["Signals"]
        Axios["🌐 axios response interceptor (zodios-client.ts)"]
        Refresh["🔄 Refresh button (requestPortfolioRefresh)"]
        Prices["⏳ End of a price catch-up (notifyPricesCaughtUp)"]
    end

    Bus["📣 portfolioMutation.ts (isPortfolioAffectingMutation, dispatch)"]

    subgraph Caches ["Session caches: mark stale, keep the answer"]
        Report["🧠 portfolioStore (invalidate)"]
        Risk["🛡️ riskStore (markRiskStale)"]
        Lots["📦 lotsAnalysisStore (own mark)"]
        PriceStores["🏭 asset price and FX registries (markStale on every store)"]
    end

    subgraph Page ["Dashboard page"]
        Peek["peekReport: synchronous, at init"]
        Render["Render the cached report: no skeleton, tweens start at their value"]
        Fetch["fetchReport in background: only if stale, missing or forced"]
        Update["Apply the fresh report: tweens move from old to new"]
    end

    API["🐍 POST /api/v1/portfolio/report"]

    Axios -->|"method, URL, response body"| Bus
    Refresh -->|"kind: refresh"| Bus
    Prices -->|"kind: prices"| Bus
    Bus --> Report
    Bus --> Risk
    Bus --> Lots
    Bus -->|"kind: prices only"| PriceStores
    Bus -->|"kind: prices, after the dispatch"| Fetch
    Report -.->|"report + stale flag"| Peek
    Peek --> Render
    Render --> Fetch
    Fetch -->|"one request per key"| API
    API -->|"stored under the mark it was asked in"| Report
    Fetch --> Update

docs.title: 🧠 portfolioStore: the report cache
docs.text:
• One key per question (reportKey): user | broker ids sorted | dateFrom | dateTo | targetCurrency, followed by one suffix per include flag (contribution, breakdown, history, allocation history, broker P&L history, P&L candles, income, cost, deposit, and acquisition-funding series). fetchReport() and peekReport() build it the same way.
  • invalidate() moves the mark: every cached report becomes stale and stays in the cache.
  • peekReport(...) reads synchronously the key that fetchReport() would ask with the same arguments (without force): {report, stale}, or null when that question was never answered.
  • fetchReport(...):
    • serves a fresh entry without asking, unless force is set;
    • asks a stale, missing, or forced key once per key: a caller joins the request in flight, unless that request left before the last mark;
    • never discards an answer because of a mark — only a session change or resetPortfolioCache() does, and the promise then resolves null;
    • stores an answer asked before the last mark still stale, and never over a newer one;
    • resolves null when the request fails, with the message in portfolioError(), and keeps the stale entry for peekReport().
  • resetPortfolioCache() is the hard clear. Registered as a client-session reset, it forgets every report and every request in flight on logout or account change, so a page never shows another account's figures.

docs.title: 📣 portfolioMutation: the signal bus
docs.text:
The axios response interceptor (frontend/src/lib/api/zodios-client.ts) passes the method, the URL, and the response body of every successful response to notifyPortfolioMutation(). isPortfolioAffectingMutation() keeps the writes that change what a portfolio view shows, and the bus dispatches {kind: 'mutation', method, path} to every listener registered with registerPortfolioMutationListener(). The Refresh button goes through the same bus: requestPortfolioRefresh() dispatches {kind: 'refresh'}. So does the end of a price catch-up, with a signal of its own: notifyPricesCaughtUp() dispatches {kind: 'prices'}. The Updating prices… tracker (frontend/src/lib/features/price-refresh/priceRefresh.ts) sends it when a catch-up is over, if it saw one of the catch-up's jobs running and the catch-up brought something up to date (last_refreshed): see Updating prices…. The report, risk and lots caches mark their answers stale on any kind; the asset price and FX registries mark their stores stale on prices alone (The other listeners); the Dashboard and the broker detail page, while on screen, also reload on prices (How a page uses the cache). The bus never spins the Refresh button: it waits only for the requests its page tracks in pageBusy, and a reload on prices tracks none (Page busy).

Write (under /api/v1) Counts as a change POST /transactions/commit Always POST/DELETE /brokers, PATCH /brokers/{id}, PUT /brokers/{id}/access, PATCH/DELETE /brokers/{id}/access/me Always POST/PATCH/DELETE /assets Always POST /assets/merge Unless the answer says dry_run: true POST /assets/prices/sync When a result has points_changed > 0 or events_changed > 0 POST/DELETE on the other /assets/prices… paths, /prices/current included Always, except /prices/query and /prices/period-changes (reads) POST/DELETE on /assets/events… Always, except /events/query POST/DELETE on /assets/provider… Always, except /provider/probe POST /fx/currencies/sync When total_points_changed > 0; without a total, when a result has points_changed > 0 POST/DELETE /fx/currencies/rate, POST/DELETE /fx/providers/routes Always

Reads and failed requests count as nothing. An answer the rules cannot read (a sync without results, a merge without dry_run) counts as a write: a stale view nobody refreshes is worse than one request too many. POST /assets/prices/current is a write because it persists today's candle, so the live-price poll of the asset page marks every portfolio view stale. isPortfolioAffectingMutation() is the source of truth: a new endpoint that changes portfolio figures belongs there.

docs.title: 👂 The other listeners
docs.text:
Store On any signal: a mutation, a refresh, a price catch-up On a session change riskStore.svelte.ts markRiskStale(): query and eligibility answers are marked stale and kept, a remembered failure is dropped, nothing in flight is discarded. The catalogs describe the engine, not the portfolio, and are left alone. invalidateRisk(), the hard reset: forgets everything, catalogs included, and discards every answer in flight. lotsAnalysisStore.svelte.ts Moves its own mark: every lots analysis is stale and kept, so peekLotsAnalysis() still returns it while fetchLotsAnalysis() asks again. resetLotsAnalysisCache()

Both follow the report's rules — one request per key, an answer stored under the mark it was asked in and never over a newer one — with two differences. queryRisk() and fetchLotsAnalysis() reject on failure, leaving the previous answer cached. And a lots key is the user plus the request with its object keys sorted and its broker_ids, requested_analyses, and selected_lot_ids lists sorted, so the same question in any order shares one entry. getRiskQuerySnapshot() is the risk counterpart of peekReport(): {key, status, response, error, stale}.

The two price registries listen on prices alone. assetPriceStoreRegistry.ts and fxStoreRegistry.ts register when they are imported, under their own names, and on {kind: 'prices'} call markStale() on every TimeSeriesStore they hold: the points stay readable, and the next read of a range asks the server again, once, so a price or FX page loaded after the catch-up shows the prices and rates it brought. A mutation or a refresh leaves them alone: the live-price poll writes today's candle, a mutation, every 30 s on an asset's page, and would otherwise turn every cached series stale each time. See Registries & Caches.

One component listens too. AssetEventPicker.svelte, the Linked Event field of the transaction form, registers with registerPortfolioMutationListener() under a key of its own instance (asset-event-picker:<uid>, the uid random per picker, so two pickers never replace each other's listener) and unregisters in onDestroy. It reacts only to a mutation on /api/v1/assets/events… — a new event or Edit this from the form's mini modal, a data editor save — and ignores refresh and prices. It then clears its fetch key and reads the events around the transaction date again: fetchEvents() returns early on the same asset, date and range, so without this the field would keep showing an edited event's old values.

dashboardViewStore.ts is not on the bus. It keeps the Dashboard's targetCurrency and brokerIds per user in sessionStorage (librefolio_dashboardView:<userId>) through readDashboardView() and writeDashboardView(), so a return asks the key it left and the cache can serve it; resetDashboardView() forgets every user's view on logout or account change. The period already lasts the session in dateRangeStore.

docs.title: 🧮 How a page uses the cache
docs.text:
The Dashboard (frontend/src/routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte) is the reference:

  1. At init, before the first render. readDashboardView() restores the currency and the broker filter; the period comes from dateRangeStore. When the broker list is already in memory — any in-app return — the owned brokers are known at once (brokersReady), and hydrateFromCache() puts the peekReport() answer, and the cached contribution of the Period view, on screen. setTweenHydration(() => summary !== null) runs just before it, so a TweenedValue that mounts with a known figure starts at its value instead of counting up from 0. The cards of the Risk tab follow the context that RiskLevelsPanel sets itself, the nearest one (see Risk below).
  2. Owned brokers first. On a cold load the broker list arrives in onMount (ensureBrokersLoaded()), and nothing is asked before brokersReady: a request without broker_ids is widened by the backend to every broker the user can see, Editor and Viewer ones included. When the user owns at least one broker, the report, contribution, and lots requests then carry the owned set from getOwnedBrokers() (role OWNER, share unset or above 0), or the filter's subset of it; with none, loadAll() never runs and the overview stays empty.
  3. loadAll() peeks again, applies the cached report if it is not the one on screen, and calls fetchReport() only when the entry is missing, stale, or forced. The answer replaces the figures and the tweens move from the old values to the new ones. When the refresh fails with a cached report on screen, the figures stay and a toast reports the error. loadContribution() follows the same rule for the Period view: contributionRefreshing keeps the rows on screen instead of the skeleton of contributionLoading.
  4. Refresh (handleSync, data-testid="sync-button") calls requestPortfolioRefresh() — every cache marks its answers stale — bumps refreshVersion, which makes the risk and lots panels ask again with force, and runs loadAll(true).
  5. After a price catch-up the page reloads by itself (Updating prices…). It registers the bus listener dashboard:prices in onMount and removes it on destroy. On {kind: 'prices'} alone, the listener queues reloadAfterPriceCatchUp() with queueMicrotask(), so the reload runs after the dispatch, once every cache has marked its answers stale. The reload runs loadAll(false, false, {background: true}): without force, it asks again for the report the mark made stale, while the figures stay on screen. It touches neither refreshVersion nor requestPortfolioRefresh(), the signals of the user's Refresh, so no spinner turns on for it; the risk and lots panels reload on their own listener (see Risk and Lots below). Nor is it tracked by pageBusy (frontend/src/lib/stores/app/pageBusy.svelte.ts), whose busy the Refresh button follows (Y11), so the button neither waits nor spins for it. And with background the page does not say it is busy (Z-18): reportLoading does not turn on, and a stale cached contribution is asked again under contributionInBackground, a flag the root does not read, instead of contributionRefreshing, so the reload turns on neither aria-busy nor data-busy on the page's root (data-testid="dashboard-page"); a load the user asks for still does.

The panels and the broker detail page reuse the same pieces:

  • Risk — riskPanelController.svelte.ts: when the store holds every base wave the panel needs (fresh or stale), loadBase() puts the getRiskQuerySnapshot() responses on screen with initialLoading = false and refreshing = true, sets hydratedFromCache on a first load, and refreshes through queryRisk(). Its own sync (handleSynced()) marks the answers stale as well, instead of forgetting them.
    • After a price catch-up. An $effect of the controller calls onPricesCaughtUp(): when a base wave is on screen it runs loadBase(false, true), without force (the stale mark is what makes the store ask) and silent, so refreshing stays false and the figures stay as they are, outside pageBusy. With nothing on screen there is nothing to reload (the first load is its own), and the on-demand analyses the user ran (comparison, stress, replay, simulation) are left untouched.
    • Tweens. RiskLevelsPanel calls setTweenHydration(() => controller.hydratedFromCache), so the tweened L2 cards (numericValue + formatValue in L2Diversification.svelte) start at their value when the cache served them. It is the nearest context for the panel's cards: the host page's own getter (summary !== null on the Dashboard, portfolioSummary !== null on the broker page) does not reach them.
    • Failed refresh. RiskLevelsPanel wires onrefreshfailed to toasts.error($t('risk.states.loadFailed')). The controller calls it, and leaves the figures on screen, only when they answer the very question whose refresh failed: shownQuestion holds the request keys of the two base waves whose answer — fresh or from the cache — is on screen. When the inputs moved (another period or currency) and the new question fails before any answer to it is on screen, the controller sets loadError instead, which replaces the levels with the error message: a failure never leaves the figures of the old question under the new inputs. A host that passes no onrefreshfailed gets loadError in both cases.
    • Scope. The Dashboard passes scope={{kind: 'portfolio', broker_ids: ownedBrokerIds}}: every owned broker, never narrowed by the broker filter (the risk.dashboardFullPortfolio subtitle says so when a filter is on). It mounts the panel only under {#if canAsk}, so no risk request leaves without broker_ids — the backend would widen it to every broker the user can see, Editor and Viewer ones included. Once the brokers are known, a user who owns none gets common.noData and nothing is asked.
  • Lots — LotsAnalysisPanel.svelte shows peekLotsAnalysis() at once and calls fetchLotsAnalysis() only when the answer is stale, missing, or forced; a failed refresh keeps the lots on screen with a toast. Its ready prop holds every request until the host knows the broker scope (the Dashboard passes canAsk: the owned brokers are known and there is at least one), and refreshVersion forces both analyses again. After a price catch-up an $effect calls onPricesCaughtUp(): while the panel is open with an asset and ready, it asks the main analysis and the selection histories again, without force; the cache answers the stale ones, so the lots stay up with no loading state, and it is outside pageBusy.
  • Broker detail page — frontend/src/routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte does the same for its single-broker report: peekReport() then fetchReport() in loadOverview(), setTweenHydration(), and requestPortfolioRefresh() plus refreshVersion for its own refresh. After a price catch-up it reloads like the Dashboard's step 5, under the listener broker-page:<id>:prices: loadOverview() without force, and nothing else.

TweenedValue.svelte exports the hydration hook from its module script: setTweenHydration(isHydrated) sets TWEEN_HYDRATION_CONTEXT during a component's init, and every TweenedValue below it that mounts while isHydrated() is true starts at its value; later changes still tween.

docs.title: 🔔 Views that reload on a price catch-up
docs.text:
The Dashboard and the broker page have their own listener (step 5). The other views on screen use one helper, onPricesCaughtUp(reload) (frontend/src/lib/features/price-refresh/onPricesCaughtUp.ts): it listens for {kind: 'prices'} alone and calls reload in a microtask after the dispatch, so every cache has already marked itself stale. It never throws, and returns the function that stops it. The views: the risk controller and the lots panel (above), the Assets list and an asset's page, the FX list and an FX pair's page. The flow, with the bus and the marks, is drawn in Updating prices… — the reload.

flowchart LR
    Bus["portfolio bus: kind prices"] --> Marks["caches mark stale and keep:<br/>report, risk, lots, price and FX stores"]
    Bus -->|"microtask, after the dispatch"| Dash["Dashboard, broker page:<br/>reloadAfterPriceCatchUp"]
    Bus -->|"microtask, after the dispatch"| Helper["onPricesCaughtUp"]
    Helper --> Panels["risk controller, lots panel"]
    Helper --> Pages["Assets, asset, FX, FX pair pages"]
    Dash --> Silent["figures stay, no spinner, outside pageBusy"]
    Panels --> Silent
    Pages --> Silent
