docs.title: 📥  Crédit Agricole
docs.text:
Crédit Agricole is both your bank and your broker, and it shows the same operations in two lists: a coupon, a purchase, a fund redemption or a matured bond appears in the list of your securities and in the list of your account. To import them without counting anything twice, download both lists and upload them together: LibreFolio recognises that two rows are the same operation and imports it once, with the cash that really moved on your account.

Upload both files together

A single Crédit Agricole file uploaded alone is not imported. The wizard tells you which export is missing: add it in the same upload and carry on.

docs.title: 💳 Export the account movements
docs.text:
This is the list of your real cash — salary or pension, transfers, bills, taxes, fees, coupons and dividends — for the last two years.

Prefer the Excel file

SCARICA EXCEL adds, above the table, your Saldo Iniziale and Saldo Finale (the balance at the start and at the end of the period). LibreFolio uses them to start your cash from the right amount and to check it against the bank. The CSV has no balances.

docs.title: 📄 Step 1 — Open the movement list
docs.text: In online banking, open Conti in the top menu and choose Lista movimenti. If you have several accounts, pick yours in Seleziona rapporto.

docs.title: 🗓️ Step 2 — Choose the period
docs.text: Click Ricerca avanzata, set Data contabile (Dal) and Data contabile (Al) to the widest window the bank allows (two years), then click CERCA.

docs.title: 💾 Step 3 — Download the file
docs.text:
Below the list, click SCARICA EXCEL (better) or SCARICA CSV, and import the file without opening or editing it.

✂️ Export in blocks — when the bank shows only the first results

When the list says Stai visualizzando i primi … risultati, it has been cut and the oldest movements are missing. Export the period in blocks:

  1. Download the block as it is.
  2. Note the date of its oldest movement.
  3. Set Data contabile (Al) to that date, click CERCA and download again.
  4. Repeat until a block reaches the start of your period.

Upload all the blocks together with the securities file. You can download the same period more than once, and blocks may overlap: a row that is in two files counts once, and when two files cover the same day the one with more rows is used.

docs.title: 📂 Export the securities movements
docs.text: The list of what happened in your securities account: coupons, purchases, fund redemptions, matured bonds and securities transferred in from another dossier.

docs.title: 📂 Step 1 — Open the securities movements
docs.text: Open Portafoglio in the top menu and choose Lista Movimenti.

docs.title: 🗓️ Step 2 — Choose the period
docs.text: Set Data Operazione (Dal) and Data Operazione (Al) so that the period covers the one of your account export — a little wider is fine. Operations older than the start of the account export cannot be imported with their cash, because the cash of that time is not in the account list: they are listed in a warning so you can enter them by hand.

docs.title: 💾 Step 3 — Download the file
docs.text: Click CERCA, then SCARICA EXCEL or SCARICA CSV, and import the file as it is.

docs.title: 🧺 Upload the set
docs.text:
Upload the account file(s) and the securities file(s) in the same upload. The import wizard shows them as one set with the two exports, how many rows each has and the period it covers. If one is missing it says so (A file is missing) and offers Upload the missing file.

Then, in the analysis step, the Matching securities ↔ cash panel shows what LibreFolio did with every row:

  • pairs — an operation found in both lists, imported once;
  • standalone rows — rows imported on their own: everything of the account that has no counterpart in the securities list (salary, bills, fees…) and the securities moved in from another dossier;
  • excluded — rows that are not imported, each with its reason (below).

docs.title: 🔄 How a pair is imported
docs.text:
LibreFolio looks for the same kind of operation, the same amount (to the cent) and the same value date in the two lists. For example, with invented numbers:

Securities list Account list Imported CEDOLA, BTP Demo 2033, 87.50, value date 22/03 Coupon of BTP Demo 2033, 87.50 credited, withholding (RITENUTA) 12.50, value date 22/03 Interest 100.00, plus a Tax of −12.50 ACQ.CONT.SU MERC., BTP Demo 2033, 5,010.00, value date 10/03 Debit of 5,010.00, value date 10/03 Buy, with a cash amount of −5,010.00

The date of the transaction is always the operation date (the day the order was given or the coupon was booked), never the value date; the two can differ by days. The cash is the one of your account, so no automatic Deposit or Withdrawal is added.

LibreFolio never guesses: when two rows could be the same operation and there is no way to tell, it leaves them out and says so.

docs.title: 🚫 Rows that are left out
docs.text:
Left-out rows are listed in an amber warning with the rows in detail, so you can add them by hand if they are real movements:

Reason What it means What to do No counterpart A securities row with cash that has no matching row in the account list Check that the account export covers that day; otherwise enter the operation by hand Ambiguous Several rows could be the same operation Enter the real movements by hand Not settled yet The cash arrives after the last day of the account export Nothing: the row comes with your next import Settled before the cash statement starts No account file covers the day the cash moved Download the account list for that period, or enter it by hand Replaced by a newer file Another file for the same days has more rows Nothing Unknown type A securities operation that LibreFolio does not know Open an issue with the link under the warning

An account row is never left out for lack of a partner: it is real cash that moved, so it is always imported (only a row whose amount cannot be read is skipped, with a warning).

docs.title: 🕳️ A month with no account file
docs.text:
Imagine the account file ends on 30 June with a balance of 1,000.00 and the next one starts on 1 August with a starting balance of 900.00. Nothing says what happened in July: July is a hole. LibreFolio sees that the balances differ by −100.00 over a period that no file covers, tells you (No account export covers 01/07 – 31/07) and, in the Align with the bank step, proposes a cash correction of −100.00 on 31/07 (After the gap).

What to do:

  • If the bank still has July, download the account list for it and upload it with the others: the balances then add up, and the correction disappears by itself.
  • If you cannot, keep the correction: your cash will then match the bank.

The same step shows a Starting point — the cash and the positions at the beginning of the account export — and an End-of-period check with the bank's balance at the end of each file. A check that does not match is never corrected automatically: if the rows are all there, it usually means a movement is missing or was left out above.

Balances that do not add up

When the balances of two files differ although movements are present in between, LibreFolio does not correct anything: it warns you that the balances do not add up, and compares them only. Check that no export is missing a day, or was cut halfway.

Account file without balances

With only the CSV of the account (or an Excel without balances) LibreFolio cannot start or check your cash. In that case add the starting balance yourself: read Saldo Iniziale and Data dal in the bank's Excel export and add a Deposit of that amount on that date with the transaction form.

docs.title: 🔄 What gets imported
docs.text: In the exports Imported as Coupon found in both lists Interest, with a stated withholding (RITENUTA) as a separate Tax Purchase found in both lists (ACQ.CONT.SU MERC., SICAV: SOTTOSCR) Buy Fund redemption found in both lists (FONDI: RIMBORSO) Sell Matured bond found in both lists (TITOLI SCADUTI) Sell at par (100), plus Interest for any amount paid above par GIRO ALTRO DOSSIER, VERS.TITOLI Adjustment: securities moved in from another dossier, such as an inheritance, at their book price and without cash Salary or pension, card payments, bills, cash withdrawals, transfers Deposit or Withdrawal, by the sign of the amount Coupons and dividends with no securities row Interest or Dividend, linked to the security when the line gives its ISIN Account interest and the monthly fee (INTERESSI/COMPETENZE) Interest when credited, Fee when charged Commissions and charges Fee, or Tax for capital gains tax, stamp duty and withholdings Buys and sells of securities that have no securities row Buy or Sell when the coupons of the same bond give the quantity; otherwise a cash row for you to complete A fund redemption paid by bank transfer with no securities row A Deposit for you to complete: the bank states the money, not the units sold Any other operation Deposit or Withdrawal by sign, listed in a notice so you can check it

docs.title: ⚠️ Good to know
docs.text:
• Some rows ask for your help in the Corrections step of the wizard (how it works):
    • trades without a quantity, and fund redemptions: pick the type, the security and the quantity;
    • trades whose amount may include accrued interest and commissions: add them under Separate the price from the charges?, from your contract note (nota informativa);
    • charges that name no security: assign them, or keep them on the account.
  • Securities are matched by name. The securities export gives no ISIN: match each security in the Resolve Assets panel of Review.
  • Amounts as written, in the currency of each row, with no conversion. Dates are the operation dates.
  • Messages in Italian. Most of the importer's notices about these files are in Italian, like the report.

docs.title: 📥  Danske Bank
docs.text:
Alpha

This importer is in Alpha: it was built from the exports of a single account, shared in issue #26. If your files look different, or a row is imported in a way that looks wrong, please open a new issue and mention #26.

LibreFolio imports the equity savings account (osakesäästötili) of Danske Bank Finland. The bank splits it into two exports, and neither is enough on its own:

  • the securities transactions (XLSX): trades, dividends and demergers, with quantities and prices — but no deposits, withdrawals or balance;
  • the cash statement (CSV): every cash movement and the balance — but no quantities.

So you upload them together: LibreFolio reads them as one report set, matches each trade with its payment and checks its balances against the bank's.

docs.title: 📤 What to export
docs.text:
Export (name in LibreFolio) Where in eBanking Format How far back Securities transactions (Transactions.xlsx) Sijoitukset → Tapahtumat XLSX at most one year per export Cash statement the account transactions of your equity savings account's cash account CSV up to five years
  • Securities transactions: the whole year the bank allows.
  • Cash statement: the same period, from the day before it, and ideally a few days past its end — trades are paid a few business days after they are made.
  • Import the files as downloaded, without re-saving them in Excel.

docs.title: 🧺 Upload both files together
docs.text:
1. Open the Import Wizard, drop both files in Upload, assign them to your Danske Bank broker and click Next: Select Files.
  2. In Select Files, the two files form one card, already ticked: check that it reads Complete. A note on the card tells you what this import will do.
  3. Click Parse: LibreFolio merges the two files into one combined file and analyses it as one row. Its detail, Matching securities ↔ cash, shows how the trades were matched with their payments, and why any row was left out.
  4. Go on as usual up to Import N transactions.

Files uploaded together from the Files page or a broker's Uploaded Reports form a set too.

Exports uploaded with a LibreFolio version before 1.2 are in no set and cannot be read on their own: the wizard keeps Parse disabled while one of them is selected. Upload all the exports of the set again together, in one go, then select that set; the old copies can be deleted.

docs.title: 🧩 If one file is missing
docs.text:
• Dropped only one file? Next: Select Files keeps you on Upload, naming the missing export and its period: drop it there — it joins the same set — and click Next: Select Files again.
  • Going on without it? The card shows A file is missing and offers Upload the missing file. Meanwhile the ticked set blocks Parse: untick it to import your other files first.
  • Files uploaded at different times never join: upload the missing one again with Upload the missing file on the right card, then delete the earlier, lone copy.

docs.title: 🔀 How the set is read
docs.text:
Normally there is nothing to change: Read as, in the card's header, shows Danske Bank (detected). If a file does not belong in the set — say, a statement of another account uploaded by mistake — choose Remove from the set in its ⋮ menu: the file moves, without a plugin, under Other files of this broker, where you untick it. To put it back, choose Danske Bank in its Plugin column there (the choice appears once the file is ticked).

Read the files one by one is of no use here, since no other importer reads these exports: if you chose it, put each file back the same way. A set ticked only in part — its checkbox shows a dash — blocks Parse: click the checkbox once to untick the set, twice to tick it whole.

docs.title: 🗓️ Import at least once a year
docs.text:
The securities export only goes back one year, so import at least once a year, each new securities export reaching back to where the previous one ended. Overlaps are fine: what LibreFolio already holds is hidden in the Review (N already in LibreFolio (hidden)) or arrives deselected as a duplicate. Skipped more than a year? See Gaps.

Sets imported with LibreFolio 1.2

LibreFolio 1.2 recorded each trade on the day the money moved; it now records it on the day you made it, a few days earlier. Imported again, those trades would not be recognised as duplicates, and would count twice. So, once: delete all the Danske Bank transactions those imports created — the corrections tagged gap_fix too — and import the whole set again, or import only from the day after the last day you already imported: start the securities export there, and the cash statement the day before, as What to export says. From then on, overlaps are fine again.

docs.title: 📝 What is imported
docs.text:
In your files Imported as A purchase (positive Määrä) and its Osto … payment Buy A sale (negative Määrä) and its Myynti … payment Sell Tuotto and its credit Dividend Nosto osakesäästötililtä Withdrawal Vero osakesäästötililtä Tax Palvelumaksu… (service fees) Fee Korko… (interest) Interest Any other credit (only your own money can be paid in) Deposit — a notice lists them Jakautuminen, vanha / uusi (a demerger) Adjustments without cash — see Demergers
  • Each trade is recorded on the day you made it (Kauppapäivä, the trade date): a purchase made on the 27th is a purchase of the 27th, even though the bank moves the money a few business days later. Dividends and demergers take their day in the securities export too; deposits, withdrawals, taxes, fees and interest keep their date in the cash statement. Amounts are in euro, as the bank wrote them.
  • The files give no ISIN or ticker: confirm each security in the wizard's asset mapping.
  • Every row is accounted for: a row left out — a missing payment, a trade paid after the statement ends… — is still counted in the set's detail, with its reason, and listed in the importer's notices, in Finnish like the files. Two cases are handled differently:
    • Reservations (Varaus in the cash statement) are holds that the bank replaces with the booked movement, and that movement is the one imported. They are counted in the set's detail as reserved, not booked, but not listed in the notices: there is nothing to check.
    • A status LibreFolio does not know: a row whose Tila is anything but executed (Toteutettu) or booked (Toteutunut) — an order not executed, for instance — is left out with a warning and a link to open an issue on GitHub. Please open one, naming the Tila you see, so that the importer learns to handle it. Meanwhile, if one of those rows is a real movement, add it by hand.
  • Check the matched trades a notice flags because their names differ.

docs.title: 💶 Fees are included in the trade amounts
docs.text:
The files give one total per trade, commission included, so the Corrections step asks, for every purchase and sale:

  • Separate the price from the charges?, then Apply correction — for a security priced in euro, LibreFolio suggests the likely commission; the exact figure is on the trade confirmation in eBanking;
  • or Keep as recorded: the trade keeps its whole amount (your cash is right either way).

Each trade needs a choice; Keep the remaining N rows as read settles the rest in one click.

docs.title: ✂️ Demergers
docs.text: A demerger (Jakautuminen) arrives as adjustments without cash: the old line (vanha) removes your old shares, each new line (uusi) adds new ones. In the editor, each new line needs its cost per share (Save All waits for it): the cost of your old shares × the line's percentage published by the Finnish Tax Administration (vero.fi), divided by its number of shares.

docs.title: 🏁 First import: align with the bank
docs.text:
On the first import, everything before the first day of your securities export is summarised in a starting point at the end of the previous day; from then on, every movement is imported one by one. The set's card tells you the date.

After the Review, Import N transactions may open Align with the bank: it compares what LibreFolio will hold with what the bank states, and proposes what closes the difference — a Deposit or a Withdrawal that brings the cash to the balance of the cash statement, and an Adjustment for each position your files prove.

LibreFolio records a trade on the day you made it, while the bank's balance changes only when the trade is paid, a few business days later. So each comparison counts the imported trades already made but not yet paid on that day, and both sides speak of the same thing.

  1. Cards at the top show each point — the Starting point, an After the gap point per gap, the End-of-period check. Click one to see its comparison and only its corrections; click it again to see them all.
  2. The corrections, tagged gap_fix, are selected by default: untick those you don't want (or use Select All, Select visible, Deselect All), then click Continue.
  3. In the editor, enter the cost per share of each position marked cost to enter — the bank's website shows each holding's average purchase price. Save All waits for it.

The step opens only when there is something to show — usually not after a yearly import that overlaps the previous one. History you entered by hand counts: only the difference is proposed. If the comparison with the bank fails, you can Continue without corrections.

docs.title: 📅 If your cash statement starts later
docs.text:
If your cash statement starts after the first day of your securities export, the starting point still falls on the day before the securities export, and takes the balance your cash statement starts from.

  • A trade you made before the cash statement starts, and that was paid inside it, is imported as usual, on the day you made it.
  • A trade already paid before the cash statement starts is not in the statement, so it cannot be imported one by one: a notice lists it, and the set's detail counts it as settled before the cash statement starts. Its money is already in the balance the statement starts from, so it ends up in the starting point, a few days before the day you made it. Its shares too, when your files prove the holding — a dividend, for instance; otherwise check that security on the bank's website (see Limits).

To have every trade imported on its own day, export the cash statement from the day before the securities export, as What to export says.

docs.title: ✅ End-of-period check
docs.text: The last card compares your cash with the statement's balance at the end of the last securities period — counting, like the other points, the imported trades made but not yet paid that day: Matches or Does not match. It is never corrected: your next import brings the trades of the last days, missing from your cash until then. If it does not match, add by hand the movement the import left out (see the set's detail in Parse).

docs.title: 🕳️ Gaps between securities exports
docs.text:
A gap is a period that no securities export covers while the cash statement shows trades in it — you skipped more than a year, or left a hole between two securities exports. Without quantities, those trades cannot be rebuilt:

  • the gap's deposits, withdrawals, taxes, fees and interest are imported with their own date;
  • its trades are summarised in the After the gap corrections;
  • securities bought or sold in the gap must be checked on the bank's website and fixed by hand.

The set's card warns you about such a hole: if the bank still has that period, export it and upload it with the others.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limits
docs.text:
• Securities that never show up: positions are proven only by a dividend, a demerger's old line, or a sale of more shares than you bought (at least N). A security that did not move and paid no dividends cannot be seen: check your positions on the bank's website and add the missing ones by hand.
  • Invested capital: a negative position correction, or a demerger's old line, removes shares without lowering your invested capital.
  • No going back in time: a securities export older than the history LibreFolio holds for the broker is not imported; the set's card says so.
  • Earlier corrections: if a new set covers the date of a gap_fix correction imported before, delete that correction after the import, as the card asks — or the cash counts twice.

docs.title: 📥  Degiro
docs.text: LibreFolio imports DEGIRO's Account Statement: the CSV that records every movement of your account — trades, fees, dividends, interest, deposits, withdrawals and currency conversions — in any language DEGIRO offers.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
1. Log in to the Degiro Client Portal.
  2. Open Inbox in the left sidebar, then Account Statement.
  3. Choose the Start Date and End Date: from your first deposit to today for the full history.
  4. Click Export, choose CSV and save the file (usually Account.csv).

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
Account Statement, not Transactions

DEGIRO's Transactions export lists only your orders: no dividends, deposits, withdrawals or currency conversions. If you upload it, LibreFolio recognises it, imports nothing and asks you for the Account Statement.

  • Keep the file as exported. Any language works, as long as you do not add, remove or reorder columns, or change DEGIRO's day-month-year dates.
  • Warnings in the file's language. Import warnings are in the language of the statement, whatever language LibreFolio uses: English, Dutch, German, French or Spanish, and English for any other.

docs.title: 🔄 What Gets Imported
docs.text:
In the statement Imported as Buys and sells, such as Buy 5 APPLE INC@180,25 USD, in any language Buy or Sell: the sign of the amount gives the direction, the description gives the quantity Order fees (DEGIRO Transaction and/or third party fees) and exchange connection fees Fee Stamp duty and financial transaction taxes on an order Tax Dividends and their withholding tax (Dividend, Dividend Tax) Dividend and Tax, each in its own currency Deposits and withdrawals Deposit and Withdrawal Interest (Flatex Interest Income) Interest; interest charged to you becomes a Fee Promotional and courtesy credits (DEGIRO courtesy) Interest, keeping DEGIRO's description Currency conversions (FX Debit and FX Credit) One linked pair of FX conversions (see below)

Amounts are imported as DEGIRO reports them, each in the currency of its own row.

docs.title: 💱 Currency Conversions
docs.text: DEGIRO books a conversion as two rows: the money leaving one currency and the money arriving in the other. LibreFolio imports them as one linked pair: in the wizard's Review it is a single row showing From, To and the rate the two amounts imply, selected and imported whole. It counts as two transactions in Import N transactions. DEGIRO's AutoFX cost is already inside the debited amount, so no separate fee is added.

docs.title: 🚫 What Is Not Imported
docs.text:
Each kind below is listed in an amber warning during the import, with its original rows, so you can check them. Each warning has a link to open an issue on GitHub, in case the rows are real movements LibreFolio should read:

  • Corporate actions (product or ISIN changes, splits, mergers, stock dividends and their cash settlements), money market fund rows and capital returns: LibreFolio does not import them automatically — check the positions they affect.
  • flatex withdrawal rows (flatex Withdrawal): LibreFolio cannot tell whether money really left your account. If it did, add the withdrawal by hand.
  • Currency conversion rows without a partner: the other leg is missing from the file or cannot be identified.
  • Rows with an unexpected sign for their type, such as a negative dividend.
  • Trades whose quantity cannot be read from the description.
  • Unrecognised rows: anything else LibreFolio could not classify.

Skipped without a warning: information lines without an amount, DEGIRO's internal bookings (cash sweeps, transfers to or from flatexDEGIRO Bank, reservations) and zero-amount lines that name no product, such as an interest of zero.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text: LibreFolio supports both the CSV and XLSX (Excel) formats exported from Directa SIM. The screenshots below are from desktop, but the steps are similar on mobile.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the transaction list
docs.text: Log in to Directa and click the CONTO tab (❶). Then click the transactions filter icon on the left (❷) and select the time period you want — e.g. 6M (❸).

docs.title: Step 2 — Export as CSV or Excel
docs.text:
Click the export icon (the spreadsheet icon with the green X) at the top of the table. In the dialog that opens, select File separato da virgole (csv) (or the Excel option) and click ESTRAI.

Save the file and import it into LibreFolio. If you choose CSV, don't open or re-save it in Excel first, as that can alter the number formatting.

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• Supports stock, bond, and ETF trades, dividends, taxes (ritenute fiscali), and transaction fees.
  • Both CSV and XLSX (Excel) formats are supported — not ods.
  • Account operations are denominated in EUR.
  • Rows LibreFolio cannot read (too few columns, a date it cannot understand, a missing or unknown operation type) are not imported: they are listed in an amber warning during the import, with a link to open an issue on GitHub.
  • The export covers up to 3,000 rows per file. For longer histories, export multiple periods and import them in sequence.

docs.title: 📥  eToro
docs.text:
Beta

This plugin is in Beta — tested with sample files but edge cases may exist.

LibreFolio reads the Account Activity sheet of eToro's account statement, saved as CSV.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
1. Log in to your eToro account.
  2. Open Portfolio, then History (the clock icon).
  3. Click the settings icon at the top right and choose Account Statement.
  4. Choose the start and end dates, then click Create.
  5. Download the statement with the XLS icon.
  6. Open the file in a spreadsheet, go to the Account Activity sheet and save it as CSV, keeping the column names on the first line. LibreFolio does not read PDF or Excel files.

docs.title: 🔄 What Gets Imported
docs.text:
In Account Activity (Type) Imported as Open Position Buy Position closed Sell Dividend Dividend Interest Payment Interest Deposit Deposit Withdraw Request Withdrawal Withdraw Fee, Withdrawal Conversion Fee, Conversion Fee Fee, when the amount is not zero Overnight fee (CFD financing) Fee, when the amount is not zero: a cost of money, with no asset Overnight refund (CFD financing given back) Interest: money given back (positive amount), with no asset and the description Overnight refund SDRT (UK stamp duty) Tax, on the instrument of the row

The instrument comes from Details (for example NKE/USD) and the quantity from Units.

Any other type is skipped with a warning.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
Check the currency of instruments not quoted in USD

LibreFolio records each row in the currency after the slash in Details (KER/EUR in euro), and every other row in US dollars. eToro states its amounts in your account currency (usually USD): check the rows of instruments quoted in another currency before saving them.

  • Keep eToro's dates: day/month/year, with or without the time. A row whose date cannot be read is skipped with a warning.
  • Withdrawal conversion fees. A non-zero fee becomes a separate Fee, next to the full Withdraw Request. Compare both with your statement: if the fee was already taken out of the withdrawn money, untick it in Review.
  • CFDs become ordinary buys and sells of the instrument, like real shares. Their overnight fees are imported as separate Fee transactions, with no asset: check those positions and their costs against your statement.
  • Overnight fees and refunds. Fees are imported as Fee and refunds as Interest: the overnight cost you really paid, net of refunds, is the fees minus the refunds. A refund shows up as income, so a report of your income includes it.

docs.title: 🚧 Known limitations
docs.text:
• Amounts in your account currency. See the warning above: check the currency of instruments not quoted in USD before saving.
  • Something is off? Please open an issue with an anonymised example file.

docs.title: 📥  Fineco
docs.text:
LibreFolio imports FinecoBank's Ordini e contabili report (its Titoli list) — your securities operations (it carries the Dossier and Intestatario lines above the table) — saved as CSV.

This guide, and the fix to how commissions are counted, come from a real export shared by @Xgialippo in discussion #49: thank you!

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text: The screenshots below are from the Fineco website on desktop. Personal data is blurred.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open PORTAFOGLIO
docs.text: Log in to your FinecoBank account. In the menu at the top of the home page, click PORTAFOGLIO (the arrow).

docs.title: Step 2 — Open Reports
docs.text: In the left bar, click Reports (the arrow).

docs.title: Step 3 — Choose Ordini e contabili
docs.text: In the Reports menu, click Ordini e contabili (the arrow).

docs.title: Step 4 — Open the filter
docs.text: Stay on the Titoli tab. By default it shows only the last three months (Ultimi 3 mesi). Click the filter icon on the right (the arrow) to change the period.

docs.title: Step 5 — Choose the period
docs.text: Pick the period you want, for example Ultimo Anno (the circle), then click Cerca (the arrow).

docs.title: Step 6 — Export to Excel
docs.text:
At the bottom of the list, click Esporta excel (the arrow). Fineco downloads a file named Lista Titoli.xlsx.

Screenshots courtesy of @Xgialippo.

docs.title: Step 7 — Save it as CSV
docs.text: LibreFolio reads CSV files only, so open Lista Titoli.xlsx in Excel or LibreOffice and choose Save As → CSV (comma or semicolon separated: both work). Keep the lines above the table (Dossier, Intestazione or Intestatario) and the column names: LibreFolio recognises the report by them. Do not edit the numbers.

docs.title: 🔄 What Gets Imported
docs.text:
In the report (Descrizione) Imported as Compravendita titoli, with Segno A or V Buy or Sell Dividendo Dividend Stacco Cedole Interest (bond coupon) Rimborso Sell (redemption or maturity), with the amount as printed Aumento capitale Adjustment of the quantity, without cash Commission columns, when the report has them One separate Fee per row, of the same security, in euro. The commission columns of the row are summed, not one Fee for each kind

Any other operation is skipped with a warning.

Commissions. In Fineco's report the Controvalore (the settled amount) of a purchase already includes the commission, and the Controvalore of a sale already has it taken off. LibreFolio records the trade for the amount without commission and the commission as a separate Fee of the same security, so the two together are exactly the Controvalore. Two examples, with made-up numbers:

In the report Imported as Total Purchase of 40 shares, Controvalore 862.95, commission 2.95 Buy −860.00 and Fee −2.95 −862.95, what left your account Sale of 4 shares, Controvalore 246.65, commission 2.95 Sell +249.60 and Fee −2.95 +246.65, what reached your account

Rows without commission, dividends (already net of tax, as Fineco prints them) and the other operations are unchanged. So are reports without the commission columns.

Bonds repaid above par. When a bond is repaid above par (100) — a premio fedeltà or an inflation revaluation — the sale is recorded at par and the amount above it as a separate Interest, like a coupon, so your gain reflects the price alone. LibreFolio recognises bonds by their name (BTP, BOT, CCT…). Bonds repaid at or below par, and other redemptions, stay a single Sell.

docs.title: ⚠️ Good to know
docs.text:
• Both layouts work, with or without the commission columns: LibreFolio tells them apart on its own.
  • Capital gains tax. It is not in the report, so LibreFolio cannot import it: add it by hand if you want it tracked.
  • Amounts as written. Each row keeps its own currency (Divisa), with no conversion; the Cambio column is ignored.
  • Dates. Each operation is recorded on the day you made it (Operazione): a purchase you made on the 27th is a purchase of the 27th, even if the money moves a couple of days later. When Operazione is missing, LibreFolio uses the value date (Data valuta).
  • Only settled operations. An operation whose value date (Data valuta) is after today has not settled yet: typically one of the last one or two working days. It is not imported this time, commission included, and a blue note says how many. Nothing to do: it arrives with your next export, once settled, still on the day you made it.
  • Dates in files imported with LibreFolio 1.2 or earlier. Those versions recorded each operation on its value date. Imported again, the same operations now come with the day you made them, a day or two earlier, so LibreFolio does not recognise them as duplicates and they would count twice. So, once: delete the Fineco transactions those files created and import the files again, or import only the operations after the last day you already imported. From then on, importing a period again finds its duplicates as usual.
  • Commissions in files imported with LibreFolio 1.2 or earlier. Those versions counted the commission twice (the Controvalore plus a separate Fee), so the cash of those trades is off by the commission: buys too low, sales too high. The data already imported stays as it is. To correct it, delete the Fineco transactions created from that file and import the file again.
  • Rows with a missing number. If a row has no quantity or no amount, LibreFolio reads it as it is: a missing amount counts as 0, and an operation that needs a quantity cannot be imported without one. A blue note lists these rows and asks you to check them. If the file looks right to you, use the link in the note to open an issue on GitHub, and we will look into it.
  • Rows LibreFolio cannot read or does not know. A row with too few columns, no readable date or an empty description, or one whose operation LibreFolio does not map, is left out of the import. An amber warning lists these rows and has a link to open an issue on GitHub.

docs.title: 🚧 Known limitations
docs.text:
• Checked on one kind of account. The importer has been verified on a real export from an account in the regime amministrato (the broker withholds the tax), where the commission is in the Commissioni amministrato column.
  • Not seen yet on real exports: accounts in the regime dichiarativo (you pay the tax yourself at the end of the year), funds and BTP. Their columns or values may differ.
  • Not seen yet on real exports, either: a Rimborso (redemption) that carries a commission, a commission larger than the Controvalore of a purchase, and rows in a currency other than euro. LibreFolio imports them with the rules above, but they have not been checked against a real report, so look at them in the import preview.
  • Other column names. If your report has commission columns with different names, LibreFolio sums the commission columns it finds, so check the Fee of a few trades against your report.
  • Something is off? Please open an issue or write in discussion #49, with an anonymised example file.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
To export your transactions from Finpension:

  1. Log in to your Finpension account.
  2. Go to your active portfolio/account dashboard.
  3. Click on the Transactions (Transazioni / Transaktionen) tab.
  4. Click on the Export or download button and select CSV.
  5. Save the file to your computer.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
Do Not Modify Delimiters

Finpension exports use a semicolon ; as the column separator and German/Swiss formats. The BRIM parser detects these locales automatically. Avoid opening the file in spreadsheet editors (such as Excel) and saving it back, as this may change the CSV's raw structure.

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• Swiss pension platform.
  • Supports cash deposits, buys, sells, tax withholdings, and management fees.
  • Denominated in CHF.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
To export your transaction statement from Freetrade:

  1. Open the Freetrade app on your mobile device (or access the web portal if available).
  2. Tap on your Account icon in the top corner.
  3. Scroll down and select Activity.
  4. Tap the Export button (usually represented by a download or share icon in the top corner).
  5. Select CSV as the format, pick your date range, and export the file. Send it to your computer.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
Export Format

Make sure you request the raw CSV export. PDFs or screen-scrapes of transactions will not pass validation.

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• UK-based broker.
  • Supports equity and ETF trades, dividends, cash deposits, and withdrawals.
  • Full multi-currency support for GBP, EUR, and USD assets.

docs.title: Generic CSV
docs.text: The Generic CSV importer reads a CSV file you prepare yourself. Name its columns as in the column reference — date and type at least — and LibreFolio recognises them by their names: there is nothing to map by hand.

docs.title: 🎯 When to Use
docs.text:
• Your broker is not in the supported list.
  • Your broker changed its export and its importer does not read it yet.
  • You keep your own spreadsheet, or a script writes the CSV for you.

docs.title: ⚙️ How to Import It
docs.text:
1. Prepare the file. Save it as .csv (from Excel, save a copy as CSV). Its first row names the columns, as in the column reference; other columns are ignored.
  2. Upload it in the Import Wizard and assign it to its broker.
  3. Check the plugin in Select Files: if Generic CSV is not already chosen, pick it in the file's Plugin column.
  4. Parse and review. Each row becomes a transaction.

One file per broker — not one file per currency

Every row of a file is imported into the broker you assign to that file, so never mix two brokers in one CSV. Rows in different currencies can share the same file, as each row carries its own currency; you can also split a broker's history into several files, one per year for example, and import them together.

Several date columns? Use the operation date

LibreFolio reads one date column per file, never two. If the header holds several columns with an accepted date name (for example trade_date and settlement_date, see the column reference), it takes the first one, reading from left to right, and ignores the others. A column with another name, such as order date, is not read at all.

Put in the date column the operation date: the day the trade or the transaction was made, not the settlement or the booking day, which can come days later. This matters most when you write the CSV by hand or have another AI write it for you: tell it to use the operation date, and to leave the other dates out of the file.

docs.title: 🧯 If Something Goes Wrong
docs.text:
• "required column 'date' not found" (or type): the first row lacks that column, or names it differently. Add it, or rename the column to an accepted name, and upload the file again.
  • A row is missing: rows LibreFolio cannot read — an unknown type, a date in an unknown format, an empty currency — are skipped and listed among the warnings of the Parse step; rows with a wrong sign appear as validation issues. Fix them in the file and upload it again.
  • The bulk workspace asks for a cost on an ADJUSTMENT row: enter the cost of one unit, not the total value of the position. Only a row that adds units asks for it: one that removes units (a negative quantity) has no value.

docs.title: 📅 Date format
docs.text:
A date such as 03/04/2025 can mean 3 April or 4 March, and a year can be written with two digits (03/04/26). LibreFolio lets you choose how the Generic CSV importer reads the dates of your files. The choice is yours alone: other people of the same LibreFolio keep their own.

Open Settings › Plugins, find Broker imports, and set Date format. Each option shows the shape of the date and a complete example:

Option Example dd/mm/yyyy (the default) 03/04/2025 = 3 April 2025 mm/dd/yyyy 03/04/2025 = 4 March 2025, as written in the United States dd/mm/yy 03/04/26 = 3 April 2026 mm/dd/yy 03/04/26 = 4 March 2026 yy/mm/dd 26/04/03 = 3 April 2026 yyyy-mm-dd 2026-04-03 = 3 April 2026

dd/mm/yyyy is how LibreFolio always read the dates, so nothing changes if you never open the setting. With dd/mm/yyyy and mm/dd/yyyy, a date that only one order can read is always read right: 25/12/2025 is 25 December, because there is no month 25. With the two-digit-year options the order you chose is the only one used, and yy follows the usual rule: 00–68 are 2000–2068, 69–99 are 1969–1999. Dates written like 2025-12-25, 20251225 or 25 Dec 2025 have a single meaning and never move.

A row whose date cannot be read in the chosen format is left out, and the analysis says so for each row (Row 4: 25/12/26 is not a valid date in the format mm/dd/yy…), with where to fix it: correct the date in the file, or change the Date format in Settings › Plugins and press Re-parse all. After the twentieth such row one note counts the rest.

Parse the file again after changing it

A file you already parsed keeps the dates it was read with. After you change the setting, the file shows the notice that it must be parsed again: parse it again, then review the rows.

docs.title: 🔄 Converting a Custom Report
docs.text: If your data comes from another tool, a short script can turn it into a Generic CSV. The Generic CSV technical specification describes the format in full — signs, which type to use when, worked examples. You can paste it into an AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini…) with a few sample rows of your file and ask for the script.

docs.title: 📋 Column Reference
docs.text:
These are the columns LibreFolio recognises in a Generic CSV file. Column names are case-insensitive, and spaces around them are ignored.

Column Required? Accepted aliases Description date ✅ Always data, settlement_date, value_date, trade_date, fecha, datum, transaction_date, exec_date Transaction date type ✅ Always tipo, transaction_type, operation, operazione, action, azione, trans_type, op_type Transaction type — see values below quantity Required for BUY/SELL/ADJUSTMENT quantità, qty, shares, azioni, units, unità, amount_shares, num_shares Number of units. Negative for SELL, positive for BUY. amount Required for most types importo, value, cash, cash_amount, total, totale, net_amount, gross_amount, price Cash impact. Negative when cash leaves, positive when cash enters. Empty for ADJUSTMENT. currency Optional (defaults to EUR) valuta, ccy, curr, currency_code, divisa, währung ISO 4217 currency code. EUR applies only when the file has no currency column: if it has one, fill it on every row with an amount, or that row is skipped. asset Required for BUY/SELL/DIVIDEND/ADJUSTMENT symbol, ticker, isin, asset_id, instrument, strumento, security, titolo, name, nome Ticker, ISIN, or a consistent name string for unlisted assets description Optional descrizione, notes, memo, note, details, dettagli, comment, commento Free text notes

docs.title: 🏷️ Valid type values
docs.text:
BUY · SELL · DIVIDEND · INTEREST · DEPOSIT · WITHDRAWAL · FEE · TAX · ADJUSTMENT

Not supported: TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION, CASH_TRANSFER

These need two linked rows, which a CSV cannot express: such rows are skipped with a warning. Enter them by hand from the Transactions page, or use your broker's own importer.

docs.title: 🧙 How to Import Transactions
docs.text: The Import Wizard turns the reports you download from your broker into transactions. You check what it read and settle its doubts; nothing is saved until you press Save All.

docs.title: 🚀 Step-by-Step Guide
docs.text:
1. Export a transaction report from your broker: its page in Supported Brokers says which file.
  2. On the Transactions page, click Import ().
  3. Drop the report into the wizard, assign it to its broker and follow the steps below.
  4. Click Import N transactions: the rows open in the bulk workspace, not saved yet.
  5. Give them a last look and click Save All.

docs.title: 🧙 The Import Wizard Steps
docs.text:
Four steps are always there; the others appear only when your files need them, and the progress bar shows only the steps of the current import.

Step When you see it 1 · Upload Always 2 · Select Files Always 3 · Parse Always 🧬 Unify assets The same security appears under more than one name or code 🔧 Corrections The importer recorded rows it could not fully understand 🧹 Duplicates The same movement is in two of the files you import together 4 · Review Always ⚖️ Align with the bank Report sets only, when the bank's figures differ from LibreFolio's

docs.title: 📤 Step 1: Upload
docs.text:
Drag your reports into the wizard, or click to choose them (CSV or XLSX), and assign each one to its broker — or all at once with Assign broker for uploads. A missing broker can be created from the same list (Create new).

  • Every report you upload is kept: to reuse one, skip this step with Next: Select Files.
  • When one account comes in several exports (e.g. Danske Bank), upload them together: if one is missing, the wizard stays here and names it.

docs.title: 🧭 A file in the wrong broker
docs.text:
When you click Next: Select Files, the wizard checks each file you have just uploaded against its broker's Default Import Plugin. If that plugin cannot read a file, the file probably belongs to another broker, and the wizard asks you about it before going on (This file may belong to another broker). From top to bottom, it shows:

  • Assigned to — the broker the file is in, with its icon, and its default plugin, marked cannot read it;
  • Notes from the plugin — why that plugin cannot read the file, when it says why: in your language when a translation exists;
  • Move it to — the broker whose default plugin can read it. When the default plugins of several brokers read it, the prompt lists those brokers instead: choose one, the first is already selected.

Then choose:

  • Move, with the icon of the broker chosen under Move it to — the file is uploaded to that broker, in the same session, and removed from the wrong one. If the move fails, an error says so and the file stays where it was;
  • Keep it here — the file stays, and the wizard reads it with another plugin that can, as before: you see it in the Plugin column of Select Files;
  • Remove — the file is deleted.

One prompt per file, in turn (File 1 of 3); closing it keeps the file. If you remove every file you have just uploaded, the wizard stays on Upload, ready for others. When none of your brokers has a default plugin that reads the file, the prompt names the plugins that read it — or says that none can — and offers only to keep or remove it.

Brokers without a default import plugin are never questioned, and neither are the reports you reuse without uploading them again.

docs.title: 🗂️ Step 2: Select Files
docs.text:
Each broker's panel lists its stored reports, with the files you have just uploaded already ticked. Tick the files to read and click Parse (N).

The importer of each file is detected for you: change it in the Plugin column if it is wrong, and for a CSV you built yourself choose Generic CSV.

Report sets are one card, ticked as a whole. Read as, in its header, changes how the set is read, and each file's ⋮ menu can take it out of the set (Read alone with ‹plugin›, Remove from the set) — details.

Parse is disabled? A ticked file has no plugin, or a ticked set is incomplete or only partly ticked (a dash in its checkbox): choose the plugin, use Upload the missing file, or tick or untick the whole set.

docs.title: 🧠 Step 3: Parse
docs.text:
LibreFolio reads each file, checks it and sums it up in a table:

Column What it counts 📊 Transactions read 🏦 Securities found ✗ Securities not matched to your assets yet — you match them in Review 🔴 Validation issues: rows that could not become transactions 🔧 Fields to fill in before saving (red when one blocks the save) ⚠️ ℹ️ Two numbers: warnings (amber) need a look, such as skipped rows; notes (blue) explain a choice the importer made, with nothing to fix

The tiles below the table count what will really be imported; View All, or View Detail in a row's ⋮ menu, opens the details, with the warnings and the notes listed apart.

  • Warnings and notes: Continue lists the warnings first, then the notes; read them, then click Continue anyway. A warning about rows the importer left out, because it does not know or cannot read them, has a link to open an issue on GitHub.
  • A file failed: a banner says why. Fix its plugin in Select Files, then parse again. Re-parse all is in the analysis only once at least one file was read; if none was, go back to Select Files and click Parse (N).

docs.title: 🧩 Steps that appear only when needed
docs.text:
Depending on what Parse finds, up to three steps can come before Review, in this order. Open the one the wizard shows you:

🧬 Unify assets — when the same security appears under more than one name or code

Your files describe the same security more than once — under two names or codes, or in two files. Unify it here, or it becomes two assets with its transactions split between them.

Each card is one security: a solid green border means unified, dashed amber means to confirm, grey means nothing to decide.

  • Confirm or Split a proposal; merge or separate cards with ⋮ (Merge with…, Remove from group) or by drag and drop.
  • Click a code badge to make it the leading code (⭐) — pick the one prices are quoted on; the others stay as alternatives.
  • Rename with the pencil; a security already in your library (in archive) keeps its name.
  • Continue waits until no proposal is open: Confirm all (N) settles them at once, and Restore automatic grouping starts over.
🔧 Corrections — when the importer recorded rows it could not fully understand

The importer recorded rows it could not fully understand — today, rows from Crédit Agricole and Danske Bank reports.

Rows are grouped by question. Give each one an answer:

  • Correct it: pick the type and, where it applies, the security and the quantity, then Apply correction. A fee or tax may belong to No instrument (broker charge).
  • Split it: separate the price from the commissions, taxes or accrued interest shown on your contract note.
  • Keep as recorded: accept what the importer read.

Row N in the file shows the original line, and Restore undoes an answer. Continue waits for every answer; Keep the remaining N rows as read answers all the open ones.

🧹 Duplicates — when the same movement is in two of the files you import together

The same movement is in two of the files you import together, such as a yearly and a quarterly statement. Matches with transactions already saved do not open this step: Review flags them.

  • File priority: drag the files into the order you trust and click Recalculate by priority. Each group keeps the copy from the highest file — never one already saved or waiting in the bulk workspace.
  • Keep: tick the copies to import, row by row; Reset defaults restores the automatic choice.
  • Compare shows the copies side by side, differences highlighted.

Groups are listed under Total overlap (identical copies) and Partial overlap (something differs).

docs.title: 📦 Step 4: Review
docs.text: Every row to import in one grid — status, date, type, security, broker, quantity, cash and tags, plus the file when you import several.

docs.title: 🗂️ Match each security
docs.text:
The Resolve Assets panel above the grid lists the securities of your files. Match each one:

  • Search In this import and In the archive (your library) from one field. Likely matches come first, with a confidence badge (Exact to Low); a single match is already selected.
  • Create “…” opens the new-asset form, filled in with the name and codes from the report.
  • ✏️ Inspect / edit opens the chosen asset; Merge appears when two of your assets match.

If the report's code differs from the asset's or the price provider's, LibreFolio asks which one is the main one. The provider's code, the one with prices, is preselected; the others stay as alternatives. An amber note on a new asset, such as a possible maturity, is only advice.

docs.title: 🚦 Read the status badges
docs.text:
Badge Meaning Ticked at first? ✓ Unique Nothing similar is saved ✅ ℹ Possible dup A saved transaction has the same type, date, quantity and amount, but another description ✅ — check it ⚠ Likely dup A saved transaction matches, description included ⬜ ⧉ Duplicate in batch Exact copy of another row of this import, or of the bulk workspace ⬜ ≈ Possible batch dup The same, with another description ✅ — check it ✗ Unresolved Its security is not matched yet ✅ — match it or untick it ⛔ Before opening Dated before the broker's opening date Cannot be imported ⏮ Already in LibreFolio Report sets: older than the history LibreFolio holds; hidden behind a counter Cannot be imported

Click a duplicate badge to compare the row with its twin; a banner says why rows are unticked. A currency conversion is one row, imported whole.

docs.title: ⛔ Rows before the broker's opening date
docs.text: Rows dated before the broker's opening date cannot be imported (the opening day itself is fine). If the date is wrong, the banner offers Set opening to ‹date› — the earliest row date — and Edit broker date; the rows are then checked again.

docs.title: 📥 Import the rows
docs.text:
Import N transactions is enabled once at least one row is ticked and every ticked row has its security. A last duplicate check runs first: changed duplicates between files send you back to Duplicates, and a changed selection keeps you here with a message — check the ticks and click again.

⚖️ Align with the bank — after Review, only for a report set such as Danske Bank

For a report set such as Danske Bank, LibreFolio compares what it will hold with the bank's balances and positions. Cards show each point — Starting point, After the gap, End-of-period check — above the proposed corrections, all ticked. Untick those you do not want and click Continue; if the comparison failed, continue without them.

docs.title: 💾 Save in the bulk workspace
docs.text:
The rows arrive in the bulk workspace unsaved. Check or edit them, then click Save All: it waits for the rows listed in red, and asks before saving the values listed in amber that you have not verified (Save anyway). A row whose quantity has more than 10 decimal places, whose cash amount has more than 6, or whose per-unit cost basis has more than 12, is refused at Save All, with the maximum in the message (Quantity: At most 10 decimal places): LibreFolio never rounds it. Transaction dates can go back as far as the year 1 and up to tomorrow. A row dated before 1900 is marked amber in the review (a note above the table counts them) and the bulk workspace asks once to confirm them, since such a date is usually a typo; once confirmed it is saved like any other. A row dated after tomorrow is refused at Save All, with the last allowed day in the message (Date: Not after 2026-10-18 when today is 17 October 2026).

A row that brings units in — an Adjustment that adds units, or the receiving side of an Asset Transfer — keeps the cost written in the report, even 0, in Manual. If the report gives none, it starts in Auto (💡 in the Cost basis override column): Save All saves it at the average cost of the units already held, unless you switch it to Manual. If there is nothing to average, the row is refused: choose Manual and type its cost, 0 for a gift.

Rows whose missing cost the importer flags are the exception: a position added by Align with the bank, a new line of a Danske Bank demerger, an ADJUSTMENT row of a Generic CSV file that adds units without a cost. They are listed in red, and their form opens in Manual with the cost empty: type it by hand, even if it is 0 — choosing Auto does not take them off the list.

When the rows arrive, and after ⚡ Validate now or a refused Save All, the grid turns to the page of the first row whose Auto cost was refused, and highlights it: the oldest by date, as correcting it can let the later rows of the same asset at that broker pass. The automatic check that runs while you edit does not do this.

docs.title: 🧭 Guided First Import
docs.text:
The first time you open the wizard, a guide bubble walks you through it:

  • its Step N of M counts only the steps you see; the tips for optional steps wait for an import that needs them;
  • it only points: it never clicks, uploads or edits for you;
  • it ends by highlighting Save All, without pressing it;
  • X skips only the current tip.

To see it again, choose Replay at next trigger for the Import guide in Settings → Preferences → Onboarding and guides: it starts with your next import.

docs.title: Interactive Brokers (IBKR)
docs.text:
Beta

This plugin is in Beta — tested with sample files but edge cases may exist.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
LibreFolio reads the trades of an Activity Flex Query exported as CSV. The standard Activity Statement is not supported.

  1. Log in to the Interactive Brokers Client Portal and open Flex Queries, in the reports menu.
  2. Create an Activity Flex Query with only the Trades section, and select the fields that give these columns: Buy/Sell, TradeDate, ISIN, Quantity, TradeMoney, CurrencyPrimary, IBCommission, IBCommissionCurrency.
  3. Choose CSV as the format and yyyyMMdd as the date format (for example 20240315), then save the query.
  4. Run it for the period you want and download the file.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The first line must be the column names. LibreFolio recognises the file by the quoted Buy/Sell, TradeDate, ISIN and IBCommission headers on its first line: keep column headers on, and leave header and trailer records and section codes off.
  • CSV only: PDF and XML exports are not read.

docs.title: 📝 What Is Imported
docs.text:
• Buys and sells of instruments with an ISIN, in the trade's currency (CurrencyPrimary; USD when the column is empty).
  • Commissions, each as a separate Fee on the same asset and date, in IBCommissionCurrency (or the trade's currency when that column is empty).
  • Not imported: dividends, interest, taxes, deposits and withdrawals, currency conversions (the currency trades, which have no ISIN, are listed in an amber warning with a link to open an issue on GitHub) and corporate actions. Add them by hand, or with a Generic CSV file.

docs.title: 📥 Import from Broker (BRIM)
docs.text: BRIM (Broker Report Import Module) imports your transactions from the files your broker lets you download, so you do not have to type them. To run an import, follow the How to Import guide.

docs.title: 🏦 Supported Brokers
docs.text:
Pick your broker to see which file to export and what to watch out for. Importers that are still maturing carry a label:

  • 🔬 Alpha — new: expect rough edges and check every row;
  • 🧪 Beta — tested with sample files: unusual cases may be missed.

Importers without a label are well tested and reliable for the formats they support.

Interactive Brokers 🧪 Beta · CSV trade report from a Flex Query Degiro The Account Statement CSV export eToro 🧪 Beta · Account statement CSV Directa SIM Transaction history, CSV or XLSX Charles Schwab 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Revolut 🧪 Beta · Account statement CSV Coinbase 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history (crypto) Freetrade 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction statement Finpension 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Trading212 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Avanza 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history BUX 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Disnat 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history InvestEngine 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Rabobank 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Fineco The "Ordini e contabili" securities list, saved as CSV Intesa Sanpaolo 🧪 Beta · Movements or patrimonio snapshot, CSV or XLSX Crédit Agricole Account movements, CSV or XLSX, plus an optional securities export for history older than 2 years Danske Bank 🔬 Alpha · Finnish equity savings account: the securities XLSX and the cash CSV, uploaded together as one report set Scalable Capital Broker account (Scalable's CSV or the LibreFolio exporter) and overnight account (exporter), as two brokers Trade Republic 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history XTB 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Parqet 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Saxo 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Swissquote 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Bitvavo 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history (crypto) Crypto.com 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history (crypto) Relai 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history (crypto) CoinTracking 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history (crypto) Delta 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history (crypto) Investimental 🧪 Beta · CSV transaction history Generic CSV Your own CSV: columns recognised by their header names Request New Plugin Your broker is missing? Request a new plugin or contribute code!

Accented letters, the € sign and semicolons

Files written by banks or re-saved with Excel on Windows are read correctly: accented letters, the € sign and columns separated by semicolons included (LibreFolio understands the UTF-8, Windows-1252 and Latin-1 encodings). Still, upload your files as downloaded whenever you can: some broker pages, such as Danske Bank, ask for exactly that.

docs.title: 🗂️ Asset Mapping
docs.text: Each security in your report must be matched to an asset of your library. LibreFolio does it on its own when exactly one asset fits; for the others you pick the asset — or create it, filled in from the report — in the Resolve Assets panel of the Review step. Until then the row shows ✗ Unresolved and the import waits.

docs.title: ♻️ Duplicate Detection
docs.text:
LibreFolio compares every row with the transactions already saved for the same broker: same type, date, quantity and amount, small rounding differences ignored.

  • If the description matches too, the row is a ⚠ Likely dup and arrives unticked.
  • If the description differs, it is a ℹ Possible dup and stays ticked for you to check.

Copies between the files you import together are handled the same way, and the Duplicates step lets you choose which copy to keep. You can always tick or untick a row yourself.

docs.title: ⛔ Before the broker opening date
docs.text: If a broker has an opening date, rows dated before it cannot be imported; the opening day itself is fine. If the date is wrong, correct it from the Review step and the rows are checked again. Whatever the opening date, transaction dates can go back as far as the year 1 and up to tomorrow: a row dated before 1900 asks for a confirmation (it is usually a typo), a row dated after tomorrow is refused when you save the imported rows, with a message such as Date: Not after 2026-10-18, when today is 17 October 2026.

docs.title: 📥  Intesa Sanpaolo
docs.text:
Beta

This plugin is in Beta — tested with sample files but edge cases may exist.

LibreFolio reads two Intesa Sanpaolo exports, in CSV or Excel (XLSX), just as you download them:

  • the movements list — the coupons, dividends, fees and taxes of a period;
  • the portfolio snapshot (patrimonio) — your holdings at their fiscal cost, and your cash balance.

docs.title: 🧭 Which files should I import?
docs.text:
Brand-new accountAccount with history (recommended)

Import the movements list: it brings the coupons, dividends, fees and taxes. LibreFolio takes no buys or sells from it, so add your purchases by hand with the transaction form, or with a Generic CSV file.

Intesa exports about one year of movements, and LibreFolio takes no buys or sells from them. Start from the portfolio snapshot instead:

  1. Import the portfolio snapshot. It adds one Deposit for your cash balance and one Adjustment per holding, at its fiscal cost, all dated the snapshot date: the latest quote date in the report.
  2. Set the broker's Account Opened date to that day. Older movements are already counted in the snapshot: the wizard marks them Before opening and leaves them out (how it works).
  3. From then on, import the movements list for the new coupons, dividends, fees and taxes.

docs.title: 🔍 Step 1 — Open the advanced search
docs.text: On the home page of your online banking, click RICERCA AVANZATA, next to Ultime Operazioni.

docs.title: 🗓️ Step 2 — Filter and download the movements
docs.text: Set Tipologia Operazione to Operazioni titoli, choose the period in Da and A, click APPLICA, then SCARICA EXCEL.

docs.title: 📊 Step 3 — Download the portfolio snapshot
docs.text: For an account with history, open Patrimonio from the home page and download the holdings of your Deposito Amministrato.

docs.title: 🔄 What Gets Imported
docs.text:
In the movements list (Operazione) Imported as Cedole (coupons) Interest, linked to the security named in Dettagli Dividend… Dividend, linked the same way Commission… Fee Ritenut…, Imposta…, Bollo… Tax

Any other operation — buys, sells and everyday banking rows such as card payments or transfers included — is skipped with a warning: the import never fails because of it.

From the portfolio snapshot: one Adjustment per holding (its quantity, at its fiscal cost) and one Deposit for the cash balance when it is not zero, all on the snapshot date.

docs.title: ⚠️ Good to know
docs.text:
• Filter on Operazioni titoli. Without that filter, every card payment or transfer of the period shows up in the warnings as a skipped row.
  • The same security, two names. The movements list names a security only in free text, while the snapshot gives its ISIN. Match both to the same asset in the Resolve Assets panel of Review.
  • Amounts as written. Movements keep the currency of their Valuta column, and the snapshot is in euro: nothing is converted.
  • Messages in Italian. The import warnings are in Italian, like the report.

Beta

This plugin is in Beta — tested with sample files but edge cases may exist.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
To export your stock/crypto transaction history from Revolut:

  1. Open your Revolut mobile app or log in via the web client.
  2. Navigate to the Invest (or Stocks/Crypto) tab.
  3. Tap ... (More) next to your portfolio balance, then select Statements.
  4. Select the desired account (e.g. Stocks account) and tap Transaction Statement.
  5. Set the timeframe, choose CSV as the format, and export. Transfer the file to your computer.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
Trading Account vs Main Account

Ensure you export the statement from the Invest/Trading sub-account. The main Revolut debit card statement uses a completely different file format and cannot be parsed by this plugin.

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• Supports stock trades, crypto purchases, dividends paid, custody fees, and cash transfers.
  • Handles multi-currency amounts in the same file automatically.
  • Transfers between your own accounts are left out quietly, since they change nothing.

docs.title: 🔀 Stock Splits
docs.text:
In an Invest file, a STOCK SPLIT row with a positive Quantity is imported as an incoming Adjustment of the shares added (the Quantity of the row is the number of new shares, not the total after the split), at no cost.

The importer cannot tell a split from a gift or a spin-off, so it flags the row. The end of the import wizard (the Review step) tells you how many rows look like splits, and the Bulk editor shows a banner, N rows may be stock splits. For each row it lists the ticker, the shares added and the date. When the rows above it in the file show how many shares you held before the split, it also shows the ratio that results (for example 3 for a 3-for-1 split) and the shares held.

Two buttons let you settle it:

  • Create the SPLIT event and link opens the small event form with the type already set to Split and the ratio filled in with the suggested one. You can change it: type 3 for a 3-for-1 split, 0.25 for a 1-for-4 reverse split.
  • Link to an existing event lets you pick one of the asset's events, if you already created the split.

Once the row is linked, the banner entry goes away. If the row's asset is not chosen yet, the banner asks you to choose it first. For more on events, see Asset Events.

🔢 When the broker rounds the quantity

Brokers sometimes round the shares they write (for example 0.1643 instead of 0.16431924). If the quantity of the row differs from your holding times the ratio minus one, the banner says so and gives the difference in shares. The Lots view follows the ratio of the event, while the Dashboard and the average cost follow the quantity of the row. The gap is small, but after selling the whole position a tiny lot that cannot be sold may be left over.

Link the split to a Split event

Until the row is linked to a Split event, the new shares enter without cost and dilute the average cost of the asset. The Lots view shows a lot with a cost of 0. If you sell part of the position, LibreFolio first sells the old, expensive lots at the price after the split, so you see a loss, and later a gain when the zero-cost lot is used up. An asset without quotations also stays overvalued: the new shares count at full value, even though the price has not been divided. Linking the event makes the cost follow the old shares, which is right for a split. The file does not say whether the shares come from a split, a gift or a spin-off, so the choice stays with you.

docs.title: 🚧 Known limitations
docs.text:
• Reverse splits are not imported. A STOCK SPLIT row with a negative, zero or missing Quantity (or without a ticker) is listed in an amber warning, with a link to open an issue on GitHub: add it by hand.
  • Invest files only. Stock splits are read in Invest statements, not in Crypto ones.
  • Something is off? Please open an issue with an anonymised example file.

docs.title: 📥  Scalable Capital
docs.text: LibreFolio imports both accounts of Scalable Capital: the broker account and the overnight account (conto deposito). LibreFolio is not affiliated with Scalable Capital.

docs.title: 🏦 Two accounts, two brokers
docs.text:
Each account becomes a broker of its own in LibreFolio, read by its own importer. Create two brokers, one per account, and choose the Default Import Plugin of each:

Scalable account Default Import Plugin Files it reads Broker account Scalable Capital broker the LibreFolio exporter's broker file, or Scalable's own CSV Overnight account Scalable Capital overnight account the LibreFolio exporter's overnight account file

docs.title: ❓ Why two brokers?
docs.text:
• Each account has its own cash balance and its own IBAN.
  • The money you move between them is a Cash Transfer, which links two brokers.
  • With two brokers, each balance can be checked against Scalable's app, and each transfer becomes one linked pair.
  • Each importer refuses the other account's file and names the importer that reads it.

docs.title: 📤 How to export
docs.text:
As of October 2026, Scalable lets you download your transactions only on the PRIME and PRIME+ plans, and never those of the overnight account.

That is why a browser extension was built that exports your data as CSV files: the LibreFolio exporter. It works in Chrome, Edge, Brave and the other Chromium browsers, version 120 or later, and reads your transactions on Scalable's pages, in your browser.

We recommend our extension for the following reasons:

  • it works on every plan, FREE included;
  • it is the only way to export the overnight account;
  • it adds what Scalable's own CSV lacks: the transaction id and the exact type of each movement.

LibreFolio's import plugin for the broker account also reads Scalable's own CSV (PRIME); the overnight account's plugin reads only the exporter's file.

🧩 Install the exporter — once, before the first export

The up-to-date details are in the exporter's README, which also covers updating, privacy, and the risks of an extension that uses the internal interface of Scalable's web app: read it before you install. Here is a summary of the steps.

  1. Download the two files of the latest release, librefolio-exporter-<version>.zip and librefolio-exporter-<version>.zip.sha256, into the same folder — for example Downloads/chromePlugin.

  2. Check the ZIP from a terminal. The cd goes to that folder; the second command compares the ZIP with the fingerprint in its .sha256 file:

    macOSLinuxWindows 
    cd ~/Downloads/chromePlugin
shasum -a 256 -c librefolio-exporter-*.zip.sha256

    cd ~/Downloads/chromePlugin
sha256sum -c librefolio-exporter-*.zip.sha256

    Windows has no command that reads .sha256 files: use the PowerShell lines of the exporter's README.

    OK means the ZIP is exactly the one published. On any other answer, do not install it: download both files again.

  3. Unzip it in that folder: you get a librefolio-exporter folder. Leave it there, since the browser loads the extension from it.

  4. Open chrome://extensions (edge://extensions in Edge), turn on Developer mode, click Load unpacked and choose the librefolio-exporter folder.

Export:

  1. Log in to Scalable Capital: the LibreFolio button appears in the bottom-right corner of every page.
  2. Click it, choose the accounts and the period, then click Export CSV.
  3. You get scalable-broker_<date>_<time>.csv and scalable-deposit_<date>_<time>.csv — together in one ZIP when you export both accounts. Extract the ZIP: LibreFolio reads the CSV files.

The first export reads the whole history; the next ones start from the last export (Since last), so only new transactions are read. Rows that are already in LibreFolio come back as likely duplicates and arrive unticked. You can rename the files: LibreFolio recognises each one by its columns.

docs.title: 📥 Import
docs.text:
Import each file into its own broker, in the same import or at different times: in the Import Wizard, drop the CSV files and assign each one to its broker. Never import the same file into two brokers: its transactions would count twice.

Only executed orders are imported. Orders that are pending, cancelled, expired or rejected are left out quietly, without a note: an order executed later comes with the next export. A row with a status LibreFolio does not know is listed in an amber warning, with a link to open an issue on GitHub.

💡 A file in the wrong broker

If a broker has a Default Import Plugin, the wizard checks every file assigned to it right after the upload. When that plugin cannot read a file, the wizard says why, shows which broker can read it, and offers to move the file, keep it or remove it.

docs.title: 🔁 Transfers between your two accounts
docs.text:
Money you move between the broker account and the overnight account shows up in both files:

  1. the account the money leaves records a Withdrawal;
  2. the account it reaches records a Deposit, on the same day and for the same amount;
  3. you merge the two into one Cash Transfer: after the import, while the new rows wait for Save All, LibreFolio suggests the pairs, and asks before saving if you have not looked at them.
🔍 How the pairs are found, and how to fix them
  • Files imported together: the two halves arrive with the other new rows, and a green banner, Complementary transactions detected, offers to Merge each pair — or all of them at once, with Merge all (N).
  • Files imported at different times: when you import the second file, LibreFolio finds the halves already saved and shows the 💡 button: click it to add them, then Merge each pair from the banner. For transfers saved long ago, you can also tick the transfer rows of both brokers on the Transactions page and click Edit: the same banner appears.
  • By hand: tick the two rows of a pair on the Transactions page and click 🔗 Promote pair.
  • Descriptions: the two halves have different descriptions, since each carries its own transaction id. Keep the joined description that the merge proposes (in Merge all, the default choice: Combine): an export that overlaps a merged transfer then brings its halves back as likely duplicates, unticked.

  • The fee and tax columns (Kosten, Belasting) are not imported yet: the row itself is imported, and an amber warning lists the rows that have a fee or a tax, with a link to open an issue on GitHub. Add the fee or the tax by hand. The same warning lists the rows LibreFolio does not know or cannot read.
  • Not sure the net value is really net: see Check the net amount below.
